reviews.comment: I had Anna for a summer creative writing course and she was by far my favorite english professor. She is really passionate for her work and she doesn't ask much of students except to participate and engage. As long as you try with all your writing assignments, you will get a good grade.

Anna is SUCH an amazing professor! There were about four short writing assignments, typically ranging from 1-3 pages; a reading due almost every class; and one final paper, roughly 8 pages in length, due at the very end of the semester. Overall, the class was super fun and Anna made it such an enjoyable experience for all of us.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the most passionate and engaging professor I have ever had. She is very understanding and compassionate and welcomes feedback. Very nice and open, with plenty of energy, while still maintaining a good sense of professionalism. My only critique is that she makes you watch Hannah Gadsby, which is as pleasant as chewing a brick.

SUCH a cool person, I looked forward to class every single day. Only required a couple essays/papers so nothing crazy, but I left this class feeling a lot more capable and confident in my writing abilities.

Anna is one of the most caring, thoughtful people I know. On the last day of class, she gave us all a personalized note and a book suggestion! She really encouraged us to find our creative side and always found positives in our writing. Also has a wonderful British accent, big fan. Not too writing intensive, never overbearing, and class is fun!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures were occasionally confusing. HOWEVER, if you have questions she is always eager to answer and gives clear and detailed explanations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: bismillah get me out of here
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I've been a top student of math for years until this class. She absolutely never teaches, relies on smarter students, NEVER answers your questions and rather repeats your question, quiz/test every week without notes, study guides, or homework that relate to the quizzes. you are basically set for failure if you cant learn without being taught
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: might lowk be the worst teacher at hamilton, no joke. she is snarky and weird and doesnt teach. I HATE THIS CLASS
sucks at explaing math. did not need to hear someone talk about figure skating all day when i'm desperately trying to bring my grade back to an A
this class singlehanded made me hate math and stats. i regret not taking other classes instead of this. DONT TAKE HER CLASS!!

I do not trust this teacher to teach anything but foundational algebra, all we do in class is listen to the teacher talk about random and confusing things, I've also noticed that she places a huge emphasis on theorems but not into application, we are expected to learn from our smarter classmates rather than her or online assignments. Don't recommen
bad
Gives too much hw and is bad at explaining math
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice and very eager to help, but a bit awkward at times. The lectures are bit too focused on theorems and I think they could be explained in much shorter ways (plus her handwriting is hard to read sometimes). She did make a large effort to be available after class though...

Having already learned about most of the topics in the class, I felt extremely bad who came into Calculus fresh. She explained everything through definitions, never in plain language, and failed to make anything comprehensible. She's just an awkward math major that should never be teaching students.
She is very boring and is not very helpful when you have questions. I would suggest avoiding her class.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Güler seems intimidating at first but he's a great professor. He's very funny and it's clear that he truly cares about his job. He emphasizes hard work and active participation, which ultimately determine your grade, and provided a lot of extra credit, opportunities to fix quizzes, etc. If you do all this, you'll get an A.

Dropped after one week due to the instructor's rude and dismissive behavior. He disregarded documented disability accommodations, blamed students for his own mistakes, and offered no accountability or apology when errors were pointed out. Expectations were unclear and support was minimal. I strongly recommend avoiding this class

Guler is not good at communicating and really just throws material at us to understand on our own. He does have an accent but that's not the problem, it feels like he mumbles half the time. Genetics would be so much easier if the professors really taught the course better here. But be prepared to do the majority of studying on your own.
A good and caring professor’s proudness “must be” interaction with his/her students not the asking out of context questions.
Uncaring and bad at class management

He only teaches 25% of what is needed to do the projects, quizzes, and tests. Everything you need to know is in the book; sometimes, you must read over 60 pages to do the quizzes, and you only have ten minutes. In addition, there was unnecessary homework that was not related to the class at all. Took points off from the smallest of detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Apostolellis does a great job making the lectures engaging and enthusiastic although he often misunderstands questions/takes a while to answer what is actually being asked. Overall the programming assignments and quizzes aren't too hard but the in-class quizzes can feel quite a bit harder.

I loved the material in this class. Honestly, I think that this should be a required class if you want to get a computer science degree I took for 3 week class. It was too hard Professor speaks very bluntly. Does not mean he's uncaring Collab site layout is fairly unintuitive You should take this class. Prof wasn't best teacher but is trying
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Questions on exams and quizzes are always way beyond the scope of what you learned in class or in assignments. Hard to get a hold of outside of class. Not very lenient on grading even if the issue came from his end.
Great lectures Open note quizzes project is important Thursday lectures are fun
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: HCI with this professor is, in a word, painful. Firstly, if you've ever had issues with group work, don't even consider taking this course as it's 90% groupwork. He always tries to fit far more than he can teach in his lectures, but still quizzes us on what he had to skip over because of time. Overall, a poor teacher of what was once a good class.

Arohi is probably one of the best CS lecturers at UVA and I did learn a lot about coding through just coming to lecture and asking questions. HOWEVER 1112 with Basset is a lot easier in terms of grading because we get the CS 1111 (for ppl with prior experience) exams and they get their own + retakes, so take that into consideration when picking.

As a non-CS student, I took CS1110 for an elective as well as just to try out coding, which was brand new for me. This class was still unbelievably difficult - not initially, but more so in the 2nd half of the semester. Curriculum gets shoved in exponentially, and even my CS friends had difficulties. Khargonkar does try to help and listen.

Very nice, but TAs are way more helpful. Tests were pretty difficult and she moved quickly through lectures sometimes. Most of grade comes from assignments and labs, tests are only 10% of grade (final is 15%). Can definitely be hard when coding for first time, definitely need to put time in and do all the practice problems to do well.
explains coding in very understandable terms and goes super step by step, explaining everything along the way.

She's a great professor. She always provides time to ask questions and answers very thoroughly. Her stance on late credit for the weekly webassigns are strict. Otherwise, her stance on late credit for the inclass worksheets are pretty chill, I've submitted a few things late for negligible points off and when I emailed her it was no points off.
Absolutely loved her. She is the sweetest lady and cares about all her students. Explains topics well and will always answer questions. Textbooks available but not really required.

She's amazing. Just be courteous on your time submission, she doesn't tolerate late submission. If there's something you're going through she understands and most likely finds a way to compromise. 45% of your grade is 3 midterms 2nd mid-term is the hardest and 1 final which is 30%.

Monika is pretty straight-forward. Usually no trick questions and as long as you do your work, and TURN IT IN ON TIME, you will be fine. She has no tolerance for late work. Exam 2 is the hardest of them, so study for that one. Other than that, you'll be fine if you focus, take notes before class, and do the homework.

Professor Abramenko is a wonderful person and cares deeply about her students. She is always open to meet with you in office hours. She can be very blunt, especially in terms of how to be successful in her course. I wish she would give slightly better lecture notes, but I think she is the best choice for APMA 1110.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Abramenko, she is so sweet and will help you any way she can. This is the weed out class for STEM majors, but she explains things so well that you will never feel like you won't pass. I would recommend having her as your professor you will learn a lot.
Had her for Calc 2. I liked how she explains things & she was always really nice.
She's horrible. She rates herself. Avoid.

Although I did retake this class , I would like to say that she is a very helpful professor. Yes, she will always ask if you have read the textbook but it is seriously something you should do to do well in the class. If you read the textbook, stay on top of group work, and go to office hours when needed, expect a B+ or A-. It's hard but doable.

She has a very thick German accent which can make it difficult to understand her. She also has a tendency to get confused when students ask her questions in lecture, despite this she clearly knows her calculus very well and is excellent when helping students one on one.
Really excellent professor. She moves quickly through the material, but is always ready to go back and explain when there are questions.
She is the best APMA professor I have ever had

shes cool. nice lady. i took in summer school and she gives us at least a 10min break. she deducts grade for attendance which kinda sucks if ur smart and can just show up for the exams and get 100's without coming to class. but its only 10%. She's cool with turning in homework late too. You should take her MATH 1140 class. She got german accent.

Abramenko is one of the best professors I've had at UVA!She's personable and wants you to learn. Her office hours are very good when there aren't 100 people there. Linear Algebra is a difficult class to keep up with, the first few chapters can give a false sense of security. She's fun to listen to and really knows her stuff!
The best APMA professor I've had yet.

She's my favorite professor here- in all seriousness, she is very helpful and approachable and truly cares that her students do well.  I took her class once and failed it because I didn't try, and she let me take it a second time and I got an A, with her guidance and assistance.
Do not think that this is an easy class! Material is prety easy but test questions are not clearly worded so rather hard to figure out what exactly is being asked to calculate.

I agree, if you go to class and do your homework EVERY night you will prob. be able to pull off a B+ if you are not a math whiz.  However if you are looking for an easy, don't do alot of work type of class, do NOT take this. office hours are mandatory for clarity.  Teacher is very nice and understandin, she will NOT curve any tests, not matter what

Loved her!! She was really nice and made the class as easy as possible.  I hadn't taken math for 4 years, so I had a rough start, but after meeting with her for 15min I have been getting A's on everything since.  She helped me understand what I was doing wrong, which kept me on track for the rest of the semester.

Au contraire. I found this class VERY difficult. I struggled alot understanding the material and applying it on the exams. She is a very understanding and helpful professor though. If you like math, I would suggest it but be very careful from Day 1...ask for help!

Probably the nicest professor I've had.  This class is easy and applicable to the real world.  I'd definitely recommend it, and if you do the homework and study for the quizzes and tests, it's an easy A.

It is a great class. As long as you go to class, you will get an guaranteed A+. Half of the class doesn't show up and says it was not as easy as they thought; it's because they didn't go to the class!

The class was not as easy as I assumed it would be, but if you work hard, A's are definitely possible.  Attendance and homework were not mandatory, but to understand the material, highly recommended.  I recommend going to her office hours for understanding and also so she can see you're making effort.  The exams feature a lot of extra credit.

Didn't know what to think of the class before I took it, but I thought it might help me.  On the first day I realized she had an accent, and I didn't know if I would be able to understand everything, but I soon realized that she was actually a really good teacher.  If you just pay attention and do your work, you're fine.  She did a really good job.
The class wasn't easy, the teacher did have an accent, but she is very helpful if you go to office hours.  Nice lady.  If you honestly do the homework then you will do decently well.
German with terrible english. Says, "because I said so" to explain some answers.

I took this class in the Fall of 2025. Attendance was taken every class and tests were focused on both lectures and textbook. She lectured for the entire class with no major class engagement, but you're expected to participate in discussion. Certain parts curriculum are slower than others but lecture is only fifty minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is literally so amazing, and literally my favorite professor at UVA. She is reading heavy but she is always available to help and she even gives many extra credit opportunities and always tries to make sure everyone knows what is going on. Her classes are always so informational and she is very passionate about anthropology and archaeology.

Professor is clearly very passionate about her subject and I found many of the readings quite interesting. The readings are super hefty though and she does tend to ramble a lot in lecture. Make sure you have a good TA otherwise the labs can get pretty complicated (there aren't many though)

The class is easy but the lectures are BORING!! This class is dry and uninteresting. I would not recommend it unless you have to take it. There are so many other classes at UVa that are more interesting and still get you an easy A if that's what you're looking for.
She rambles on a fair amount in lecture, DO THE READINGS. I cannot stress this enough. Class is fairly challenging if you do not, and I speak from experience.
Prof very passionate and knowledgeable about subject. You must must must do the readings and study your notes for the exams. Recommend
Interesting topic and professor who loves what she teaches and knows what she is talking about but kind of boring which makes the lectures kind of tough.

Nice prof. The class wasn't bad, kinda boring though.  She's not the best lecturer and I feel like the class could have been a lot more interesting.  The tests are very detail oriented.  Know the textbook and the bolded vocab terms really well. That's where a lot of the test questions come from.

laviolette knows her stuff and it's obvious that she enjoys what she's teaching. it's important to do the readings and go over her power points. the tests ask really specific questions which make them tough but she tries really hard to give you as many points as she can. discussion sections are the saving grace for this class.

she's a really nice lady! she usually teaches anthro archeology classes, but i had her for a usem. it was on modern africa through film, so we watched an african movie every week and read a chapter and then wrote an essay about it. it was very fascinating because i am interested in africa. it's very possible to get an A if you just do the work.

LaViolette is very friendly and talkative. She is interested in her students and she cares a lot about Africa.  She spent time doing anthropological work in Africa and refers to that frequently.  She does not grade harshly.  Sometimes she rambles off topic.

Fantastic woman. Obviously knows/cares a lot. If archaeology is not your thing, maybe you won't enjoy it. But if you read the books and come to class you'll definitely do well. I was really sick the night before the first midterm and she told me to not even think about it til i was better, and let me do it 3 days later no prob. Lovely woman.

She is very clear in explaining terminology and how it is applied so technically you will get what you need out of taking this class from her.  Her personal work shown confused and bored some b/c it didn't get connected to what we read.  Otherwise, she is understanding and helps you.  Don't expect her to coddle you though. Overall a good teacher.
Should be an easy A if you do the readings thoroughly. She follows the class syllabus very well and you will know what she is talking about if you did your readings.

I really like her class!  Her teachign style is pretty simple and easy to follow.  Make sure you do the readings because a third of the exam needs them.  Her grading is fair and she makes sure the students are focused on the important things.  She brought in slideshows a couple times to show her own personal work in Africe to give us a beter sense of what the field is like.

Interesting teacher who cares about her subject and makes it interesting.  Helps if you area already interested, as it can get a little technical.  Really cool as a prof and a person.  Some people say she can be a bit harsh, but it's more that she's fair, which is good.
so awesome, she's excited about what she teaches and is great to talk to after class

I enjoyed the class but tests were far too long -- she expected tons of in depth material on all short answers -- attending lecture is a must, reading the book is beneficial but not nearly as much as good lecture notes  -- just write more than necessary on the tests and you should be okay
She's a nice enough lady, but her classes are a little dry. not too hard though.

very easy, go to class and take the hints she clearly gives you.  If you read the book and go to lecture there is no reason why you shouldn't get an A.  She is very understanding, when I broke my wrist before an exam, she gave it to me take home so i coul
I found the lectures interesting. She knows her stuff, and is always helpful.
Sarcastic, boring, unclear, and a know-it-all in the WORST way.  GET OUT of her class if you still have the chance!
Mean and not understanding

Professor Vaish is incredibly kind and makes Intro to Child Psych a breeze. The material is quite easy and the tests are incredibly straightforward. The homeworks are very easy and brief, and as long as you read the assigned reading before class and take lecture notes, you'll get an A. She is a funny lecturer and caring professor. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She was a decent professor, kind of boring but that could've just been me since I already knew a lot about the topic. Her tests aren't very difficult and if you read and pay attention in class you will do pretty good. She also had quizzes after most classes but they weren't too difficult.

Her child psychology class was phenomenal. I learned so much but the tests were straightforward and not at all difficult. Some of her classes go by fast, but if she feels she rushed too much she will go back to the material she rushed through. She assigns readings in the text book, but if you listen in class, all you need to look at is bold terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof. Vaish very clearly knows her stuff and does an amazing job explaining it. The slides are very clear and neatly organized, and she posts them online, which makes note-taking less stressful. The tests don't try to trick you, so learn the concepts and you'll be fine. She's enthusiastic and friendly, and reasonably no-nonsense. Recommended.

Looks can be deceiving... Upon first glance, he's a very sweet professor. His lectures are quite engaging; if you're asleep and dreaming about them, which is easy to do. He's a genuinely nice person, and it was very easy to get a good grade in his class. I did not because he refused to listen to reason about my final project. Beware of his grading!
He is an OK professor. Clearly passionate about monuments and the discussion around it. Lectures were very boring, though.

I loved Evan Brubaker so much, I learned so much in this class & the workload wasn't difficult at all. He  funny & very easygoing & understanding. There was a group project at the end that had clear guidelines & you could do pretty much whatever you wanted with it. Had a lot of friends take his other engagement and they said the same things!

Professor Brubaker, though he specializes in classics, was an incredible professor for Ethical Engagement "How do we remember?" He doesn't grade too harshly, and is very engaging as he facilitates discussions among students. He is an all-around smart but also kind person; you will learn a variety of things from him.
Class was easy, although quite heavy on the reading and lecture material. Professor is quite opinionated and makes frequent comments that I did not appreciate as a women pursuing higher education.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wilcox is extremely knowledgable and reasonable. He articulates his lectures with an abundance of evidence and makes it more directly applicable than most other classes. He's funny (though not goofy) and his lectures are compelling. Loved every second of this class and everything (even the homework readings) were worthwhile.

I cannot say enough good things about him. Out of all of the classes I have taken at UVA, his sociology of the family class is one that truly can be applied to the real world in the best way possible. I found myself looking forward going to lecture every class. The readings are great, and if you make an effort, you will likely get an A. 11/10.

i took soc of family to get a credit out of the way, and it was a pretty easy class. there is discussion, midterm and final, and an 8 pg paper but i did none of the reading and got an a. some of his politics are flawed but its an overall easy a

Sociology of the family is a great class. Very easy to get an A in, barely any homework. Like any class, participation matters. Material is interesting and extremely relevant. Anyone who gives Wilcox a poor rating is only kidding themselves and you. They probably just don't agree with his politics. But you don't have to in order to enjoy the class.

Lectures are incredibly repetitive and professor gives limited feedback on assignments that make up your grade (final exam, 8 pg paper). You have to memorize quotes from readings and hope they apply to essay questions on tests. Not the worst class ever, but not enjoyable. Definitely not the easy A I expected + a lot of pointless memorization.

Soc of the family is a super easy class. You don't need to do the reading, but you should know which ones go to which topic because you need to quote them on tests. Hands out mc answers in lectures. All the information you need will be in the lectures. Class is extremely interesting.

I took this expecting an easy A but was the only B I got. Tests are ridiculous because half is essays where you have to give specific facts and cite the exact readings they come from. Lecture is not an acceptable source (even though he cites his own books) No feedback on the 8 page essay. Wilcox is a fair guy but requires too much pointless effort.
I loved this class! The lectures can get long, and you show up to your discussion section because it helps clear up confusing subjects that are covered during lecture.

SOC 2052 was the easiest class that I've taken at UVA thus far. Professor Wilcox is very nice but very repetitive. The lectures are really boring and you are forced to go due to I-clicker participation questions but the class is very  easy. Lots of reading but I didn't do any of it and still managed to get an A in the class.
Dr. Wilcox was a fantastic teacher. He really knew the information, and, in fact, wrote many of the books we read in class. This is a must have class!

Wilcox seems to really dislike women and any person of color, according to his lectures. A professor like this would only be allowed to run rampant like this in a predominantly white, male-dominated school like UVA. I've really like sociology so far, but Wilcox's comments really offended me.

Dr. Wilcox is a nice man. I hated his class though. To put it diplomatically, I would say he has trouble seeing both sides of an issue and doesn't use very reliable statistics. He is very conservative and stubborn. Not a bad guy, but maybe not the best class for a liberal woman.

Best class I took at UVA. Didn't do any of the readings and still got an A. Just go to lecture and you'll be fine. The material is interesting and you can connect to it. Make sure to take the class with him. I heard the other lady that teaches it isn't as good
Wilcox is great. There is a lot of reading but he goes over much of it in lecture, so not all of it is necessary. Exams and papers are straightforward, if you attend lecture you will be fine.

He really is a great man and really invests in his students.  You can tell he knows his stuff and is really smart but lectures are little dry.  An insane amount of reading but can get by without doing it as long as you answer personal questions in class to get participation. Had us over for dinner and was so great!

Took this class thinking it would be a broad-based sociological perspective on marriage and the family. Instead, got a twice-weekly lecture about how women's rights have ruined our society and about how gay and black people just can't get it right. If you want to learn from someone who doesn't think the 50's were the Garden of Eden, look elsewhere.
he's the man
It is a good 400 or 500 level soc class for soc majors. Grades are mostly based on participation and weekly papers which are not difficult. A lot of reading, but interesting.

I loved this class!  Sometimes it could get a little repetitive, but I found almost all of the material very interesting.  It definitely opened up my eyes to a lot of things I had never thought of before!

I'm not religious and I thought this class would be an objective look at how religion affects people sociologically. It was very biased. Wilcox is very religious and 90% of the kids in the class were also very religious. I found the articles and readings to be selected for the sole purpose of making religion look good. He's nice though.
No Comments

Boring, monotone lecturer. Material is repetitive. Slideshow notes are online, so there is no need to go to class. Must attend discussion section though. Easy class to get an A. Know specific statistics. Midterm, final, paper, debate, and participation in discussion required.

Horrible lecturer, misogynist examples, think women deserve****if they drink. Also doens't really understand stats, just how to make his own research look valid. AVOID THIS CLASS! Take stats in another dept.

stats really wasn't very hard at all, and brad was always willing to help anyway he could.  sometimes the lectures aren't exactly thrilling, but then again it IS statistics, so i'd say he does a pretty good job overall--ESPECIALLY compared to other stats profs i've had in other departments..
he's friendly and his class isn't too hard if you keep up with the work. go to class b/c he calls on you randomly and marks off if you're not there.
Very boring lecturer, no need to go to class because the notes are online, learn statistics for the tests
not the most enthralling lecturer, but he uses lots of examples and makes it pretty clear. and puts the slides online, so you don't have to take notes frantically in class.

She can come across very hardcore and HATES when people are late to lecture. She will literally call you out in front of everyone if you come in late. But the TA's are super nice and chill and extremely lenient so the class is not hard (you won't actually be working with the professor herself much). Amazing lecturer, super passionate, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor this class. All assignments are easy as long as you show up to lecture (for the most part) and take brief notes on readings. There are weeks with a lot of readings but even when I didn't do them I was more than fine. She definitely likes ppl to share opinions in class so prepare to be cold-called on if no one's raising their hand.

Think Regina George Burn Book energy. This class was actual chaos. Prof was disorganized yet demanded perfection, shut down differing views, graded like it was the Olympics, and had ZERO chill. Workload? Brutal. Praise? Nonexistent. Only win? Her sad lil dog (who desperately needed rescuing too). I finessed her so hard. Oscar-worthy survival.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: i absolutely LOVED this class. you can really tell how passionate hagerman is about the subject and she enjoys engaging with students. there are TONS of readings but most of them are pretty interesting. i recommend, even if you just want to take it for fun.

While she is a very passionate lecturer, she is a very tough grader. On the pop quizzes, she knows exactly what she is looking for and if you don't get that, you don't get a good grade. I don't recommend this course for someone who doesn't already know a lot about WGS. The TA's were awesome though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a passionate lecturer who is very educated on her topic. We would have random writing assignments that were graded somewhat harshly by her, but the TAs did the grading for everything else so it evened out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Hagerman has the most engaging lectures I have seen at my time at UVa. She always wants to hear feedback from students so you have a chance to give your opinion as well as listen to those around you. She assigns a few readings for each week and a journal. The readings can be pretty hefty but nothing too bad. Take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken so many of Professor Hagerman's classes because I really love the way she teaches! Her lectures are really engaging and interesting. There's a lot of reading but I find them relevant and interesting. Her exam style can be frustrating but it's very fair. She's become more understanding about absence and mental health since the pandemic.
Very funny and engaging! Gives a lot of work though and could be more understanding about mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class and was super excited with the subject. However, that quickly changed. Two two hour movies a night plus 2 x 2-3 pages of writing and additional readings of most of the time 30+ pages. Every night. Then, a 36 page paper due at the end of the two weeks....I mean come on. Two days to complete this because I had no time with the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She seemed cool in the beginning of the semester, but she literally expects perfection w/ no human error. She expects you to prioritize her class ALWAYS and never miss or need help with anything. Also don't raise your hand bc she'll treat you like an idiot for having an opinion different from hers but class participation is part of your grade:)))
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bonnie seemed like a cool prof at the beginning of the semester until I missed one class and all hell broke loose. She has this in-class reactionary paper that she doesn't give any heads up for and if you miss that class, you get a 0. It's looking like I'll have to drop this class, one i otherwise liked. She has no sympathy for human error. Sad.

I took WGS 2100 with Bonnie Hagerman this summer. It was a very interesting class, and I enjoyed it overall. However, there are some drawbacks to the class. First, she is a very harsh grader overall in terms of essays. You need to be an extremely strong writer if you want to get an A. Work is randomly collected. Participating is part of your grade.

Hagerman is the laziest professor I've had. Most of her PowerPoints are made up of memes, and I didn't learn anything in this class that I hadn't already read on the internet. She relies almost entirely on class discussion to fill up lecture time. She also assigns busywork that is collected randomly, making it impossible to prioritize your time.

She is a great lecturer and class discussion was always so interesting, she's a tough grader so don't necessarily expect an easy A. I took 2100 and loved the format of the class and thought it was very insightful. Attend class, participate, and do the readings and you should be okay, though!

Dr. Hagerman is great to work with. She's very interesting, and willing to share her views. That being said, she doesn't force her opinions on the class or into the lectures. Unless you are adamantly anti-feminism, you will likely agree with most of what she says or suggests.

Great professor, extremely helpful, and very kind. I would highly recommend taking a class with her. I took WGS 2100 with her last semester and plan on taking another class with her next semester because she is just that good.
Passionate about the subject, grades papers like we're all English majors. Interesting class, but not an easy A.

Professor Bychkov is not really a professor so much as a researcher that was put into the position of a professor. All of the teaching and grading was delegated to his TAs, which were some really great people that helped me pass.  Professor Bychkov was just sort of there, and most days I couldn't tell you what he was doing behind his computer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you show fear he will prey on you, you have to be brave even if you don't know what you are doing, you musnt show fear

For a 1 credit class, the pre and post labs take way longer than they should. TA office hours were a lifesaver for them. TAs are the ones to run the class; in the first few days, Bychkov was nowhere to be seen. Granted, when he does teach, he does so passionately. Also, the ALEKS Skill Tests quite pointless-why are we doing a test for simple math?

Has a clear passion for physics and physics research. Very nice, personable guy. However, the worst lecturer I have ever had in my career. Unfortunately, it's not his strong suit. Hands-on activities are, however, where he shines. With that being said, I learned more than I realized and that's due to his teaching. He could be a great lecturer.

This was by far one of the worst classes and professors I took while at UVA. The lab is painful. I dreaded it every week. You can get by if your group is motivated and goes to office hours, but if not, seriously, good luck.

Utterly evil class. Maksim is completely unavailable and refuses to lift a finger to teach or help students. Everything is graded by a set of sadistic TAs that obviously are taking out some sort of complex on students. Can't think of any class that dissuades more people from going further in the subject than this. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is best represented by being a medieval peasant (you the student) and being shoved into a brazen bull. The lectures are worthless tangents that derive equations that you couldn't possibly understand nor derive yourself. Unclear grading criteria and borderline masochist exams. I would rather be shoved into a meat grinder than take max.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bychkov does not actually teach the class. It is all taught by TAs who are helpful but also do not grade your work. Your work is graded by a bunch of graduate buffoons who are arbitrary in their grading methods. Each report is limited to 1 page despite the shear amount of details that Bychkov demands on each report.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking PHYS 1429 and 2419 at the same time. Lab TAs tried and provided decent help, but there was an absurd amount of work for these *one-credit* classes. Some labs were especially vague/random. Questionable grading too which meant going to OH to add points back to your reports. Final grade really depends on the group you get.

In lab, grading was strict and sometimes graders took points off for things groups didn't even know they were expected to do, due to the fact lab manuals were sometimes vague. Also, labs could be a lot of work if your group doesn't do anything. Lastly, lab was based a good amount on the fact you had a strong understanding of physics already.

Dr. Bychov is the best professor I have had at this university. I had him for the lecture section and although it was very rigorous, Dr. Bychov was insanely helpful. Before exams he would hold office hours for 2-4 hours AT LEAST to make sure his students were comfortable with the content. I have not met a professor at UVA who cares as much as him.

He is very enthusiastic and passionate about what he teaches.Make sure to participate in class,he thrives off the engagement and the class is really what you make of it.He is very good at explaining things simply and then building off of that, and is super welcoming to questions.He works to make sure that everyone understands the content effective.

The lab is hit or miss, but Dr. Bychkov's lecture section was one of the most enjoyable classes I took. Hes highly knowledgeable, passionate, and is really invested in helping everyone in the class understand the material, even if it means lingering on a subject for longer than planned in order to make sure everyone is comfortable.

Max is a really tough proffessor but he is one of the most engaged proffesors I have ever had. He really cares about his students and he will work with you to make sure you understand the material. I took his lecture course and found it really rewarding, however the lab is a lot of work. As long as you put in effort, your grade will be fine.

If you're sick, still come to class and hide it otherwise you will get penalized, for being...sick.
Your only form of contact is email with a sprinkle of attitude, real life sightings are rare and should be bewared.

This one-credit lab has no right to take up the amount of time that it does. The uninspiring tasks and convoluted lab instructions are enough to dishearten the most obedient of students. It's a shame that physics credit does not exempt suffering from Bychkov. If God created pain so we can feel pleasure, Bychkov must be His proudest creation.

This was one of the worst lab professors I have ever had, he is so demanding and assigns so much work for a 1 credit class. I had more work in this class than my actual lecture class. If you can avoid him please save yourself.

Maksim Bychkov has been the worst Professor I have had so far. TA's who grade your reports are not the one's in class helping you out. I've been through several weeks of illnesses, anxiety, depression, ocd attacks, insomnia, hospital visits, and a medical leave. Maksim was not forgiving at all. He ignored my SDAC accommodations on several accounts.

Maksim Bychkov was the worst professor I ever had. Not only did I received a bad score due to an error on his end, but he was also not willing to correct it for me or 40 other students in his class. the TA graders were also harsh. I received assignments back and when I attended office hours, I was never given a clear answer. No one likes Maksim

Maksim Bychkov has been the worst professor I have EVER had. Not only is he not willing to accept errors HE made that affected my grade, but he also bullied me into accepting my fate. Not only this, but all of his TAs are harsh graders. I went to office hours to understand why I had so many points taken off for my labs and I never got a good answer
An alarming lack of compassion and sympathy from this guy. Tried to guilt trip me when I was sick and couldn't make a lab. Unbelievably miserable person.
This is the worst class at UVA. Easily 8 Hours of Homework a week for a 1 Credit Class.
He has specific "graders" that grade all the lab reports and they grade harshly and refuse the correct their grading even after they admit that they were wrong.

Harsh grader. Responds to essay length emails with just a few words. Ignorant and oblivious to the fact that students take classes other than a 1 credit physics lab. worst professor I have ever had at uva.

Good grades are attainable in this class but it often felt needlessly hard, especially for a 1-credit class. I put more time into this lab than I did the lecture. The postlab questions were harder than anything else in the class which was very frustrating. You won't fail if you work hard, but I don't plan on revisiting physics after this.

this physics lab is so hard for no reason, like dude, this is only a one credit class, why would you make us doing so much work, like what. And also we are doing this online, which makes it even worse.

The lab class was very tough online, and Professor Bychkov seems to really enjoy giving students way, way too much work for a 1 credit class and really seems to like making us suffer. Go to your TA office hours, it will probably raise your grade in the class by at least a couple of percentage points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Awful professor. Shocked that other people say he's helpful, he literally refuses to teach. If you ask a question he asks you to answer it. I wouldn't be asking if I knew. When I got it wrong, he randomly called on someone else in the office hours, who also didn't know. This continued for 30 minutes until someone looked it up online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is absolutely horrific. He doesn't explain anything, his workload is insane for a lab, and all of the work is extremely difficult. Do not take him under any circumstance.

This is coming from a student with an A in this class. This professor is terrible. He is blatantly disrespectful in any and every circumstance. His automatic answer is "that is not my job" and does not try to help in any way. What is he payed for? Terrible professor.

Professor Bychkov is brilliant, he puts a lot of effort into the labs so that students can learn the physics concepts step by step. People who hate this class are usually the people who haven't done any reading or ever tried to understand the material. These labs are set up for people to explore the concept and learn, not just be told the answers.

Get ready to WORK! Maksim is by far one of the most engaging professors that I have ever had. His labs are tough and he will specifically call on random people to answer questions. Most students get A-s or an A in the end, if they put the work in. Despite his bluntness, he truly cares about your learning so stop complaining and get back to work!

Literally the worst class I've taken at UVA to date. The labs are vague and uninteresting, the post-labs are barely related to what was done in the lab, Maxim isn't very helpful, and can randomly just decide that he thinks too many people are getting A's and change the grading criteria. Overall unenjoyable, avoid if at all possible.

The class isn't tough at all, but the TAs are there to unnecessarily tank your grade. Maksim isn't helpful at all, and he does absolutely nothing to help your grade, even if you work very hard to get it. Get 100s on quizzes and homework, don't worry, because the TAs will reduce your grade in the lab reports. Definitely a case of grade deflation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was tough, but very rewarding. Professor Bychkov takes the time to teach you things as long as you ask. Dont be intimidated! He is actually a really interesting person and very smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Feels very poorly planned. One lab will be straightforward and short, another you'll be trying to decipher the problem for an hour and a half before they just say what they actually wanted isn't indicated. One lab report could be half a page, another could be 3+. One prelab will be a video and 6 questions, another will be 50+ questions.
He's great. You have to put in the time and effort. He's great at explaining concepts when you ask him in person- take the time to do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very disrespectful to students. Try to ask any questions about make up labs or the lab itself and he brushes off your question and gives a very sarcastic and snide response
He's really hot. Makes you buy the text (because he has written it). Comes around during lab to help you out if you're having trouble with the equipment. Can be funny. Nice guy, also really hot.
He is useless. He only make sup rules for the course, the TAs do all the work. As well, they like to hurt your grade.
russian body builder.  Knows physics. Doesn't really run the class, but he will answer questions during lab if you ask him.
All he does it think we have too high of an average in lab, so he makes the TAs give us lower grades for no reason.
Super sweet and easy class! She wants you to do well.

Awesome prof; easy-to-understand lectures, plenty of resources, and very available for help outside of class. She is very caring and wants her students to succeed. Most lectures have a lab at the end of class, where attendance is recorded. Make sure to show up! Exams are not bad and the final is a group project which is very doable!
Loved her! Cares a lot about students and their success in class. Very accessible and more importantly very approachable. Kind, caring, and definitely recommend taking her for CS 2100.

amazing professor, i took cs 2100 and it was an insanely difficult class but basits lectures made sense and if you got lectures you should be fine. they had opportunities for retake quizzes and gave us extra credit opportunity at the end.

An Amazing professor who really cares for every student. Her lectures and slides are incredible and easy to follow, and she is extremely helpful and responds to emails pretty fast. No complains honestly! Highly recommend.

Professor Basit is one of the kindest professors I've had at UVA. She is very open and accessible to talk outside of class and genuinely seems invested in her students' success in class. Definitely recommend taking her for CS2100.

one of the best cs profs by far :) really cares ab u as a student and will set up time to explain concepts so u can feel confident in the class. she will literally listen to u talk ab whatever thats just how nice she is. shes also super accommodating, if something comes up and u cant make a deadline shell grant extensions and try to boost ur grade

Professor Krentz was one of my favorite professors! His lessons are thoughtfully planned and he cares about and engages with his students. I took disability in literature with him and liked it so much I signed up for his American lit class the following semester. Take anything he teaches! And yes, he has an adorable personality and is so kind.

If you're an ASL minor at UVA you'll find yourself taking one of CK's classes. What they don't warn you is how much of an English class these are rather than ASL classes. The grading is very specific, so missing even one thing can hurt you. CK is a cool person, but not a very lenient professor and sometimes lacks social cues. keep it professional!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic about the material and genuinely interested in his students' development and in-class comments. Useful feedback on papers; while Krentz's grading is fair, it's worth noting that he tends to be a bit meticulous.

This was the worst English class I have taken at the University. While the literature was great, he provided no useful extra information to enhance a student's initial evaluation. His grading was unfair because he had a grader so nothing was consistent. He didn't want analysis, he wanted you to tell him the "themes" he had noted in class.
I think he is the best professor i've ever had. he is so passionate about deaf culture and society so it shows when he teaches. AND he's so adorable, you can't not like the class! :)

This was such a great class. I took this course to fulfill my foreign language requirements and he made signing easy although it really isn't.  He made you realize that there really is a DEAF culture out there. Always looked forward to this class.
No Comments

Best professor ever. I am not a STEM person and was definitely not a fan of physics coming into this course, but Prof Neu is a wildly engaging lecturer and such a sweet guy. Learned a lot, always looked forward to class more than any others. Daily demonstrations (very cool, interactive and effective). Not crazy hw load. TAKE THIS COURSE.

(I took 1060 not 1050). Probably my favorite professor that I've had at UVA. I didn't have a huge interest in physics but took the class to fill the requirements. Easy to talk to, funny, and extremely passionate about teaching. All of the work except the final is online and open-note so it's easy to get a good grade if you do your work and study.

Chris Neu is easily the greatest professor I've ever had. I took PHYS 1050 as someone who does not like physics and this was my favorite class. Professor cares about each and every student and is willing to give extra credit opportunities. Midterms and quizzes are open note, and you have to put in work to get an A on exams, but 100% doable.

If youre taking PHYS 1050, please do not.  Professor Neu is very nice in person and has cool lectures, but the tests are actually impossible and he warns you at the beginning that only about 20-30% of people get an A.  The first midterm average was a C-, and it was open note if that tells you anything. Do not recommend at all. Youve been warned.

While I think Professor Neu is hilarious and has a lot of energy, he can get a little lost when explaining physics concepts. He will spend a lot of time on derivations when they really don't matter that much in the overall class. He is very helpful and will do anything he can to help a student and I respect that a lot.

An icon. An amazing professor and person. I had him for PHYS 1010. Super manageable course (with effort), but you still learn so much. Never was stressed. Lectures are entertaining have at least a couple demos from shooting someone on a rocket to throwing eggs on the wall. 10/10 every time. 10/10 recommend. Not even a physics fan but no regrets!

Professor Neu is hands-down the best science professor I've had. He genuinely seeks to get to know his students and is always willing to discuss improvements in class and offer additional extra credit opportunities. One of the best professors at UVA!
Prof. Neu is the best teacher I have ever had, he is super funny, very inspirational and gives great extra credit opportunities. Also he always ready to help.

Looking back, Fundamentals of Scientific Computing is one of the most important courses for a physics undergraduate. Learning to code for the first time is hard, as is learning Linux and how to interact with the OS using a terminal - but Neu does a great job.  I do wish we had done some scripting.

I HATE physics. It is incredibly difficult for me. Neu put extra time aside to help me, and his lectures were clear and engaging. I got my first and only A in physics from him. He uses clickers and homework to help boost your grade (significantly), so it really is possible to succeed. Go to his office hours!

Despite my never ending struggle with physics, Professor Neu's wit made me look forward to class everyday.  He made the material engaging and gave me a better understanding of physics than any other could. If you put effort into homework and go to tutorials you will get a 100% on homework which will help your grade if physics isnt your strong suit.

I can tell he is an expert in this area, but the course contains so much and he moves so fast that it is very challenging for me to catch up. He is good at teaching, though, very engaging and funny, and if not I was so gonna fall asleep every class.

Professor Neu is brilliant. He is hilarious, engaging, and loves to do demonstrations. All of his demos are interesting and really helpful in understanding course material. Tests are not too hard and you are allowed a "cheat sheet," but you really need to pay attention in lecture and prepare well for them.
Overall awesome professor, one of the best I've had at UVA. Very funny and clear during lectures, if you get a chance to take him for a physics course definetely recommend him!
Fun Lectures, teaches the material is an interesting and engaging way.

Young, excited, knowledgeable guy. He was nervous at first, but got the hang of the class, using engaging demos to draw in the class. Favorite part of the year? Using aquanet, a lighter, and a 2-liter soda bottle to make a rocket. DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT use much aquanet if you try this at home!
The learning environment is psychologically unsafe for students of color.
Do not take her course unless you are prepared to witness some performatively championing anti-racism without ever actually practicing it.
She is the Jill Lepore of UVA! Awful person! Should be retired!
Holds abusive power dynamic with students. Very difficult person with little to no character.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful person! Behind the mask of hypocrisy and obsessive virtue-signaling, there is a f* racist called Lawrie Balfour!
Her class is a re-enactment of the very power dynamics it pretends to analyze.
She is a colonizer.
Professor Balfour is a very strong teacher. She is extremely well-read and very caring. I'd suggest taking any class you can with her!

Politics Prof. Lawrie Balfour cosigned the opinion that "a simple mention of Jefferson is enough to undo progress" as it relates to race and higher education.  Yet, another SJW disguised as a professor. Please resign from UVA.

Indoctrination 101.  Tried to tell us that Jefferson has no place at the university he founded.  Clearly unable to understand people are complex and that we can appreciate what he did for us all without endorsing every aspect of his life.  But she keeps taking the paycheck, no surprise there.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. Course is interesting, readings good, but this Professor is so ANAL if she doesn't like you. She also borders on creepy. Avoid her classes. Really the worst polisci professor i have taken thus far as a politics major. AWFUL! her essay questions make no sense and her grading system is really subjective. Refuses all extensions!

Loved this class! The lectures were clear, structured, and interesting. The class went at a nice pace. We had 3 short papers and a final exam, which wasn't hard at all. She made it very easy to take notes and pay attention.
If you go to class, you will do well.  Pretty much everything on the exams and everything you need for papers she will go over in class.  Also, very willing to help at office hours.
Very interesting lectures, very helpful.  If you go to class and take notes, papers are very easy to write.

Very interesting selection of readings. I felt that she gave a diverse amount of writers so that one got a comprehensive view of political theory. If you speak to your TA regularly and take a pro-active approach to essays ( I did essay outlines, first paras) you can get As. Don't slack off on readings.

The first half of the class was easier to grasp than the second half. She does her best in lectures to clarify the readings. The readings are not bad, but you should be prepared to read actively and dilligently to understand the material. She is always up to discuss the readings during office hours. getting a helpful TA is also important to pass.

Boring.  Not a true intro course.  On the last day of class before the final she asked a sample exam question which she said was "easy."  No one could answer it.  Avoid her class, but if you must take it, avoid the TA James Patterson at all costs.  Worst TA at UVA by far.
Really interesting material and she is always very prepared and clear in lecture.  The grading is pretty hard though, but a very interesting class-especially if you are interested in politics.
African-American Political Theory. Maybe Balfour isn't great at the intro class, but she rocks her knowledge base in this class. Well versed, and teh work is interesting and not overwhelming.

AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!  The reading material is interesting stuff, but nothing you can't just read on your own; lectures are boring, but above all the TA's are HORRIFIC.  They do not grade whether you can write a good theory essay; they grade on the exact words/points they've got on their sheet.  I was disgusted and wish i had withdrawn.

"This class isn't 101 because it's easy-there's just no prereqs.  Last semester there were 4 As."  That scared the crap out of me... but guess what?! I got an A!  So advice: lecutre is interesting- just ignore the liberal overtures- so go (55% of class is exams taken straight from lecture) Write cogent papers and say cogent things & you'll be good!

WORST CLASS EVER! AVOID IT! Lecture was so boring hardly anybody came. And the TA's are boring and grade the essays RIDICUOUSLY hard. The average grade on the essays was like a C-/D+. Also Balfour is SO liberal and pushes her own agenda. Obsessed with the civil rights movement, which is pretty much all you read about. Don't take the class!
horrible TA's and they all follow her anal grading scale

Balfour is a nice lady but she is super liberal. She relies way to much on the outlines she puts up, this is probably because she has difficulty giving a lecture for 50 minutes so she uses the outline to jump around. As others have said your TA is really the important thing because they do all your grading. Papers are graded hard, test are easy.

The content is fun for people who enjoy political theory, but getting a good TA is essential. If you value your GPA, I suggest you stay away from this course.  Getting a bad TA, like I did, leads to frustrating paper/test grades with no comments to back them up.  I would not recommend this course.

Getting a good TA is crucial in this class, but the final exam was unbelievably easy! If you work decently hard you will do well -- as long as your TA is a good grader. Going to lecture was really important because she packed a ton of info into them.

Balfour's class was a shocking, disturbing disappointment.  Her lectures were sickeningly convoluted to the degree I could not find a feasible essay topic.  The writing was extravagant: for some, it qualified as a second writing requirement.  I would not recommend this class to my worst enemy.

Balfour has a great attitude.  She is open to different ideas, even if she disagrees, and cares enough to know all of her students' names.  Unfortunately, she is not always clear.  She is a brillant thinker-not always able to structure her classes to show
Balfour was inconsistent in her grading decisions, and was not able to express her thoughts clearly in lecture.
Too broad, does not make material very interesting

Professor Balfour is great professor.  She's not as fabulous as say Mr. Elzinga, Mr. Sabato, or Mr. Coppock, but she's definately good.  However, she's extremely liberal, but is fairly good job keeping the liberalism to a minimum excpet for a few classes.
The papers are graded pretty hard, but the class is interesting and Balfour is a good lecturer-though fast at times.
Hard grader, but awesome classes and material.
Talked too fast to take legit notes.  Good TA is key.
Early readings hard, good TA is important
No Comments
had to put in a good word--she's one of the best profs at uva--go to her office hours & talk--*really* helpful & nice!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Chong was awesome. The people giving her low ratings probably came in with their minds already made up. In American Cinema, she challenged us by giving us really intense and interesting movies to watch (Window Water Baby Moving especially) and made us ACTUALLY THINK about the material and challenged our preconceived notions.

Prfsr Chong is easily the worst professor I have had at the University. She refuses to hear and interupts opinions which aren't her own, is exceptionally rude to students, jokes at wildly inappropriate themes, such as genocide, casually insults students' intelligence, and grades inconstistently. I can't stress enough: Avoid. This. Professor.

The most insane professor at this whole University. She will discredit your opinion due to your "white privilege" and said that "all white people who adopt Vietnamese children do it because of their white guilt". She is a bizarre grader and only accepts opinions that align with her own. STAY AWAY

The class is fine but the way some liberal arts teachers grade papers is just bizarre to me, they give you no rubric or any real advice on what they're looking for and then give you just one shot to do well on something that makes up a large part of your grade. The material was interesting, but not to an incredible degree.

This teacher does not care for your input unless it reinforces her point . She has no interest in discussing an opinion in class which is not completely in line with hers. Will shut you down immediately if you start expressing your opinion. Class is not difficult and material is interesting. A shame she skews everything sometimes non factually.

She ruined my fourth year in college.She is extremely opinionated. Easy in sense that you just have to think and express the way she wants you to. Freedom of Speech is tolerated with severe grade deduction. I truly regret taking this course.

I?m sorry but there seems to be a major conflict of interest with this woman teaching in an English department.  She has outspoken contempt for English majors and English as an academic discipline and would be far better suited to another department.

The class was really easy, as long as you regurgitated her ideas and concepts on the papers and final exam. She assigns a lot of reading that is essentially useless to the class. I was extremely interested in the course material but found her intolerable and mean as a professor, especially during office hours. Overall, not worth it.

This is the worst professor I have ever had in my UVA experience. She is a favoritist and completely shuts student opinions down in class. She does make clear her expectations and requirements at all and then docks points without explanation.  I was extremely interested in the course material but it was ruined by a bad teacher.

Professor Chong challenges her students, she wants you to think deeply and have complex arguments rather than just getting by. She does give a lot of reading and has high expectations for her students. She can be intimidating but she has a sense of humor and appreciates different opinions. Recommended if you want a challenge.

She is a very intuitive and intelligent professor. The class teaches you how to think and analyze literary and visual works critically. She may appear intimidating, but she is very nice. Just make sure you think through your ideas comprehensively and avoid making assumptions. Even if she corrects you, take it as a learning experience.
Highly critical of papers, but also highly vague when you try to clarify what exactly she's looking for. Not a good combination.

Mandatory boring field trips where trans and accom. had to be arranged by students! she made me feel uncomfortable in class with personal questions, and was really mean when it came to discussing papers. she only left room for you to agree with her answers, not make your own. i hated this class. she thought she was cool and "on our level", but not.

Her classes are so interesting. The way she opens up a topic and then exposes every single nitty-gritty detail about what those little things could mean and stand for is just so mind boggling. I enjoyed learning how to analyze movies & texts, but the class can be very difficult. (weekly film responses, 2 papers, 1 final)

Flipping through the COD for an interesting, relevant, thought-provoking course, this class is what you're looking for. Chong leaves questions unanswered and indefinite but gives you the tools to answer them yourself. Afterwards, you can call yourself a pro at analyzing film and other visual text. The readings are enjoyable, lectures engaging.

Sylvia was a great teacher! Definetly take her ENMC355/AMST201 class. She's very smart and knows so much about Asian American Cultural History. She's also very willing to take time to help you with any paper topics. Highly recommended. :-)
Potentially great class ruined by bad teacher.

HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE! I love American Studies but could not stand the class. It was not about mainstream American Studies--it was about the obscure topics she wanted to push. Had no idea what she wanted on the essays--penalized students who weren't as weird as her. Sometimes there isn't a "deeper meaning"--things are just what they are.

Sylvia is relatively young and passionate about what she is teaching.  She always pushes you to think past what you're used to, and is willing to make a fool out of herself to do so.  She is incredibly willing to help if you need clarification, though personality-wise can be a bit blunt. She is a smart, smart woman, but don't let it intimidate you.

His homeworks are somewhat disconnected from the lectures he gives for the lab. It makes it required to go to Office Hours or Recitation, which were not always at a good time for me. He is also generally disrespectful, especially when answering questions, and almost mocking when you are doing something wrong in the lab.
So rude. Genuinely do not talk to him regarding any personal issues you may have because he does not care.

He was very rude; he always says that he will say what will be on the exams during his lectures, which he did in Orgo 1, but failed to do so in Orgo 2.  I would only take this class if you're taking basically nothing else.
Very nit-picky and passive aggressive.

Meh Professor. Jaguar XKR. Really slow at everything: grading, lecturing, even starting class. But at least there are JAGUAR XKRs

boring. lectures are unecessary. he puts his slides online. his examples are nothing like the problem sets or the tests. you're better off reading the textbook than going to class.

hes alright. whole grade is based off 5 exams (minus 1 for drop, so 4). course content was decent. he wasnt super nice but wasnt a total jerk. i literally skipped every lecture except the first one and got an A. All the notes you need are on google.

Exams are each 25% of grade, with the lowest regular exam dropped (3 of 4 regular exam grades, plus the final being 25%).

Prepare to spend a few hours per week reading the textbook. I went to every lecture, but had friends who skipped lectures and got As on exams. Depends on your personal learning style

He was usually good with giving points back

reviews.comment: the lectures are easy to follow and he covers the material well

Tests are multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank, and free-response. Almost all are terms or concepts straight from the textbook.

reviews.comment: You can tell that Mazurek is passionate about psychology, but he spends a lot of lecture time answering questions from students and doesn't cover a whole lot of content. The tests are really easy as long as you read the textbook, and he'll drop your lowest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire grade of the class is based on 4 tests. The vocab terms all contradict one another; if you don't use the exact one, you will not get credit. He was completely unreasonable and very passive-aggressive every time I spoke to him.

He's a nice guy and a fairly decent lecturer, but your grade is based solely on the 4 exams, with the cut-off for an A at 95%. If you're fine with an A- or B+, you can easily get it, but if you want an A make sure that you do the reading and review the slides before exams.

I went to the first couple of lectures before the first exam and then found out how unnecessary they really are. I have gotten an A on every exam from simply reading the textbook and reviewing the day before. He spends the first 30+ minutes in class answering questions from students about things that don't apply to the whole class.

Mazurek's social psych was worthwhile and not all that hard. If you do what you are supposed to do -- come to class and read the textbook -- it's very hard not to get an A-. Mazurek is passionate and organized, he makes lecture slides available. His exams are straightforward. He's sometimes boring in lecture, but it's not intolerable.

I took this class my first semester at UVA and I loved it! The content was interesting and Mazurek is a great lecturer. He's funny and charming and it helps that the material is cool to learn about. A good grade is very achievable in this class even though grades are only based on exams. If you take notes and do the readings you'll be just fine.

Prof. Mazurek was great, although I struggled because the class was test heavy and I don't excel at tests. He's been teaching for a long time, so he isn't so suceptible to feedback, but his experience means his lectures are refined and he knows how to connect. He focuses on a few things in lectures he will expect you to know on exams, but he tests you on things on the book he doesn't cover in class.

Prof Mazurek has sincerely been my favorite professor at UVA so far. His lectures are so interesting, and any questions asked during are met with well thought out, fascinating answers. reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I've never loved a professor like I love Christopher Mazurek. Not only is he an amazing lecturer, but his blue eyes are genuinely my favorite thing to look at. I. would take any class with this man. 10/10 would recommend.

Prof. Mazurek was SO funny during his lectures. You mostly teach yourself from the textbook, but exams were open note. He seems very nice, and I would 100% recommend taking this class with him.

Even though it was online, he made mini-lectures that were super entertaining. I loved the course honestly. There is a lot of reading and understanding on our own, especially since it is online, but it was pretty easy. He was super caring and entertaining in the lectures. Tests were open notes. You should def take it.

Mazurek is one of my favorite professors at UVA. You can tell he really cares about what he's teaching and he's always willing to help. You can tell that he truly cares and wants you to succeed. As long as you do the readings and attend his lectures, the exams are easy. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!

I love the energy he brought to lectures. If you pay attention to everything and DO THE READING, you will succeed.

Attendance is "optional" but most of the test has questions that are specific to what he says in class. He brings a lot of energy, so the class is never boring. I took him twice because I liked his energy so much and from the 1st semester to the 2nd I went from a B to a B+. The textbook is not optional - it is needed for the class.

reviews.comment: Skubby does not allow you to ask for lecture slides if you miss class. He has three exams, two midterms, and one final. You need to literally memorize his slides and if you reword things, he deducts points. He assigns so much homework for the almost two hour labs. He is also really boring.

Prof. Skubby is the BEST! Ive taken 2 of his classes and am about to take a third. He keeps class interesting + engaging, sticks to the syllabus (so no surprises!), and has open office hours 4-5x per week. Though it is a lot of reading (5-8, 100-300 pg books/semester), the books are applicable + entertaining. 1000% would recommend his classes.

Professor Skubby and his TA Heidi are both awesome. I found the course interesting, but there is a ton of reading and writing. It does count for the 2nd writing requirement, but it sure is a lot of work. All grading, though, is very, very fair.

Prof Skubby is the best - he's inspirational, kind, and accommodating. If you have lots of work for other classes, he will let you turn in assignments late. Class consists of reading summaries every few weeks, midterm/final, and a term paper. Daily class isn't challenging and is very interesting. Take this class if you're looking for an easy one.

Coppock is a great, engaging macro professor! He clearly cares about his students and the subject. Grading can be tough/nitpicky, but in my opinion it's very fair and clear if you read the textbook and pay attention in lecture. If you're going to take macro, do it with Coppock.

Mr. Coppock's Public Choice class is the best Econ elective at UVA. The midterm and final are worth 70% of your grade and you pretty much have to attend all lectures, but it was totally worth it imo. Mr. Coppock is my favorite professor, and the material is fascinating.

reviews.comment: Professor Coppock makes the lectures engaging, but the exams can be brutally tough, even for diligent students. Definitely read the textbook cover-to-cover and utilize resources like unstuckstudy to nail the small details. Overall, a challenging but rewarding class.
Lee Coppock was my favorite professor at UVA!

Lectures are entertaining, but you must read the whole textbook to do well. Final is purposely REALLY hard and based on very small details. Coppock is very animated but definitely hard to get the A. Grade is based almost entirely on 2 tests and final. He's a good teacher it's just a lot of material and tests are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coppock gives great, animated lectures. Avoid multitasking during them because the exams and clicker questions included stuff he casually said, like a book quote or a specific statistic. His exams can be tricky, but doing the questions at the end of the textbook chapters gives you a good idea of what you'll be tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid Professor, good at lecturing, and lecture attendance is graded by clicker questions, so you basically have to go to most lectures. I recommend reading the textbook and trying hard in this class, or your grade could slip very quickly. I wish he gave more practice problems for prep, but besides that, solid teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and loved his lectures, but I did not like how they tested you in this class. Also, he makes you buy his $120 textbook, and you have to read the whole thing if you want to at least pass. His tests are unfair as he tests on the smallest details, and the final is impossible. Honestly just wait a semester to take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Coppock is a fantastic lecturer. The problem with this course is the "checkpoints". They make no sense at all. Instead of testing your knowledge on the topic, the exams just test exact memorization. This means even if you can show that you understand the topic conceptually, the littlest thing can make you lose all points on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Coppock's class is one the largest at UVA, so naturally it's just a lecture and textbook class. It's very important to read the textbook to do well, but he wrote it himself so it's pretty easy to follow. He's a funny guy and likable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging and interesting despite 500+ kids in the class. Very straightforward on lectures and on exams. Don't understand why he doesn't have a higher average on here, def one of the better intro Econ profs at UVA
Makes Economics easy to understand. Also connects well with hus students. Would take hime for every class if I had the Oportunity

He is one of a kind professors who dare to speak about the truth. He loves talking about economics and its application in real life. Especially, he loves to relate topics with Trump and China, and other international phenomenon. One bad thing about him is that he asks everyone to buy his book, which cost me around $120. Attendance was mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Coppock is a passionate and engaging professor. His Public Choice class helped me gain a deeper understanding of our political structure and allowed me to dissect some of the most influential Economics papers of all time. My main complaint is that his grading on the exams in public choice is difficult to understand and thus hard to prep for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader
