ENGR 1520 is a dual enrollment class designed mostly for high schoolers. It's probably not what you expect it to be. Expect a lot of busy work with confusing instructions.
MSE is an interesting class and Professor Groves teaches it very well. Homework is by far the worst part but tests are open note and open internet and open book etc. Definitely recommend.
Great professor that will go out of his way to help students.
Dr. Groves is professional, knowledgeble, and respectable. He expects high-quality work but is a fair grader and easy to talk to.  One of my favorite professors; recommended.
Thought this class was gonna be horrible but it really wasn't that bad. Very helpful. Kept trying to get his point across even though his lectures were on the boring side. Fairest grader on campus.
Very helpful and extremely fair when it comes to grading.  He tried to make a boring subject more bearable.

Excellent. Professor Gray has a deep command of IT and business strategy and delivers clear, focused and engaging lectures. He is a tough but fair grader who provides direct, valuable feedback and pushes students to think critically. The deliverables mirror real-world, high-stakes strategy work, making the course demanding and highly valuable.

Gives direct and clear feedback which I prefer. Challenges your thinking so that you are always backing it up with data, comprehensive research and defensible rationale. He reminds me of tough CEOs I've worked with so it's good preparation for the real world. I'd take another Masters course with him to learn more about Business Strategy & Analysis.

Professor Gray's Business Strategy module at McIntire's Master's in Management of Information Technology program was a transformative experience. The curriculum is really challenging, but it offered invaluable insight into the considerations and feedback executives apply when evaluating technology presentations and proposals.

Professor Gray is tough but fair, pushing students to reach their potential. He's always available outside of class to offer guidance. His commitment to student success and the direction of the course is evident. You'll leave with a solid grasp of the material and a sense of accomplishment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Gray is exceptional. His deep knowledge and clear explanations make complex concepts understandable. He sets high expectations but is fair and provides helpful feedback. Prepare to be challenged and grow academically, and grow in strategic thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Gray is truly committed to his students' success, going above and beyond to support their growth. His class was instrumental in rapidly developing my strategic skills. Setting high yet achievable standards, he challenges students to reach their full potential, creating an environment where they can excel academically and professionally.

Professor Gray pushed and challenged me more than I've ever been pushed in all my academic career. His belief in the potential of our MSMIT capstone project drove him to push us harder. The knowledge I gained from his guidance is truly priceless and has completely transformed my understanding of competitive business strategy.

The lessons I learned from Prof. Gray will stay with me forever and will continue to add value to my career. He meticulously prepares the course and sets students up for success. While yes the material is tough but Prof. Gray truly wants to teach the skill of analysis to his students. The course is highly challenging and rewarding at the same time.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Gray challenged the class to apply business strategy concepts to real-world scenarios. Lectures were full of deep conceptual discussions, enabling individual & team efforts to apply those concepts. Questions & open discussions were constantly encouraged. He is an excellent coach, pushing you to hone practical skills to utilize in your career.

Professor Gray offers real-world insights that elevate learning at UVA's McIntire School of Commerce. His teaching pushes you to achieve C-suite level skills, with a focus on growth and practical knowledge. If you thrive on challenge and a rich curriculum, his courses will be immensely rewarding.

Prof Gray did a fantastic job as the Mod 4 coordinator. He makes difficult strategy topics accessible using real-world corporate examples. He creates an environment where students are encouraged to think critically during the group project. Yes, he will challenge you, but he wants each group to create an amazing final project (which we all did).

Treats graduate students like undergrads and expects them to work around his schedule. He made students regret joining the MSMIT program because of how rude he was on top of being extremely unavailable and an unnecessarily tough grader. The program would be better off with a different professor leading module four like Grazioli
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Gray provided me with a solid theoretical foundation and taught me how to think strategically. I am convinced I would not have been nearly as successful without the time, thoughtfulness, and care that he put into our development as students and IT professionals. His passion for teaching is palpable and immediately apparent in all lectures.

Peter Gray's facilitation of the Capstone Project provided the MSMIT program's most realistic simulation of real-world experience. Peter challenged us to think logically and dig deeper to create a compelling strategic business case and an effective presentation. I truly benefitted from his coaching and could immediately apply the skills at work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Peter led the strategic management module of the MS MIT program. I would definitely take any course that Professor Gray offered - he clearly has a firm grasp on the material and has plenty of examples for how it is applied in the "real world." He also takes the time to provide substantive feedback and answer ?s both during and outside of class.

I had Prof Gray for Fall 2020/Spring 2021 ICE. Systems was challenging at times, but also the most helpful for future classes/jobs (process mapping, tableau, big data). I appreciated Prof Gray's clear communication style and ability to explain the most of complex topics. His pushback and feedback definitely made me a sharper thinker.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Gray is difficult and hard to please. He hates almost every idea from students and will find problems in anything. He is not helpful and I learned very little from his class. He also is in charge of the block and makes ICE pretty miserable. You better hope you are not in his block!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Gray taught & managed the Capstone Proj. for MS in MIT. He gave excellent lectures on Innovation & Tech. Mgmt. He also managed & supervised all student teams that spent 4 months on the Proj. His regular feedback was detailed, highly relevant, & motivational. He wanted all students to succeed. You have to work for him, but it is worth it.

The best professors are the ones who push you beyond your comfort zone because they believe in your ability to achieve great things. Peter believes each of his students has the ability to do great things both in and outside the classroom, and he creates an incredible learning environment that brings out the best in every MSMIT graduate. 5 stars!
Professor Gray is really intelligent. However, when asks for clarifications and answers he rejects the students when they ask question. Other professors are welcoming compared to Gray.

Peter Gray communicates well with students, but he's not up to the standard of other professors at his dept at least. The class is easy enough, but you will feel like you are wasting your time, which you are. I wish I could have dropped this for another, more useful course.

Peter had a deep knowledge of his subject matter, enterprise strategy.  He was always available and helpful with ideas and commentary to help the class improve.  The course was tough, but a ton of fun and applicable in the real world.

Peter provides clear expectations, a readiness to support you, and active communication.  His instruction and enthusiasm for the material on business strategy helped me appreciate the content and be successful in one of the most difficult classes of the MS MIT program.

Professor Gray was one of the most knowledgeable and effective instructors of the MSMIT program. His enthusiasm & experience in the subject areas of business strategy and innovation are outstanding. He surely urges students to dive deeper into their research which results in a more profound understanding of the material covered in in the program.

Peter easily intertwines business strategy concepts & complexities with relevant case studies that create a robust and enduring foundation of knowledge. His expertise extends beyond a linear comprehension of strategy and reveals the impacts and dependencies of business networks and behaviors. His classroom is engaged, interactive and energizing.

Peter Gray is an excellent instructor. He is crystal clear in making his expectations known. His lectures are interesting and on point, providing very useful guidance for formulating and discussing business strategy. This was one of the most valuable of all the grad classes I have taken. He is not "easy", but you will learn a lot from him.

Excellent professor.  Brilliant and engaging.  One of the best professors I had in graduate school. Whenever I think about strategy in my career Peter Gray's lectures always come to mind and they are very useful.

Peter Gray is an excellent professor and I highly recommend him and the MSMIT program at UVa's McIntire School of Commerce. He has a good sense of humor and his classes are very enjoyable. He communicates business strategy very well, and is very accessible and willing to help. I learned a lot from him that is definitely improving my career.

Dr. Rosenblith is a very knowledgeable professor in her field. Her lectures and tours are very interesting, and it isn't hard to do well as long as you show up and participate. She is very understanding and approachable.
Gillet is very caring and passionate about public housing. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

Class is the easiest A: you're only graded by weekly 1 page reflections and a group project at the end that you work on in class. Dr. G is so nice, caring and passionate. You just go on weekly walks around Grounds and learn about UVA's history. Very political, but informative. In-class lectures definitely get boring, though.

This was a great EGMT course to take (both enjoyable and easy). You are expected to show up to class, which consists of a lecture/discussion once a week and a walking tour around Grounds to better understand the history learned in the previous lecture the other day of the week. I thought that she was incredibly kind and helpful. Great first class.

Professor Rosenblith, though I only had her for seven weeks, is someone I can assuredly call an excellent professor. Her lecture style and personality were very engaging, and the work she assigned was simple, reasonable, and purposeful. Her knowledge of the subject matter was also observably extensive and allowed me to learn a great deal.
I've taken 2 classes with her and she is notably kind and supportive. She allows extensions when students need and very good at emailing and response times. Would recommend to anyone!
Amazing lecturer! Honestly one of the most engaging Ive had at UVA!
Keara is a fantastic lecturer!! She does a great job of making them engaging and actually interesting. Shes also a fair grader and as long you do the readings, you should be fine.

Such an unnecessarily tough grader. If your social beliefs don't 100% align with hers, don't expect a good grade on anything. Doesn't make her expectations completely clear, and grades as if you're in a grad school level course. Don't take her class unless you're able to completely dedicate your time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He was honestly really mean and raised his voice in a completely inappropriate way when a student disagreed with his politics and didn't make students with other perspectives or viewpoints feel welcomed in his class. Not a super approachable guy
Terrible teacher. Lectures were long and boring and he wasn't accessible outside of class. He wasn't helpful at all and it seemed like he didn't really care for his students.

Alexander is the worst professor I had in all 4 years at UVA. Make sure you don't get sick (I had to spend a week in the hospital for a severe infection when I took his class), because he will not provide any accommodations. He even asked for medical documentation to prove my illness which my dean later told me he was should not be asking for.

I would not recommend taking a class with him if you receive SDAC accommodations. He was ableist when I met with him over Zoom to discuss my accommodations with him, saying they wouldn't be valid for his class.
Amazing professor. The reading is dense, but really ties in with the lecture. Grade was based on two papers (with REALLY long, confusing prompts) and one final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor! His lectures are incredibly fascinating and he explains his stuff really well. He's not easy and the class has a ton of dense reading, but he does a great job of explaining it and bringing it to life. I really learned a ton in his class. Found him very inspiring. Definitely a must if you're willing to work.

I thought Alexander was a great lecturer. He has a narrative style, which is helpful to understand the aggregate material. But the professor himself is arrogant. I went into his office hours three times, and each time was traumatized by his rude behavior. I you plan to remain anonymous to him, it's a good one. And useful for a focus in CP.

Take this class if you are a FOOL. Hated every single minute of this class (lectures are boring/talks too fast/only he knows what he's talking about), readings are too dense, structure of class is horrid. Worst class and worst professor in the Politics Dep. Do yourself a huge favor and AVOID THIS CLASS!!!!

Really really good class. He makes the subject matter clear. You have to study and read, but you have to do that to excel in any class. Took this class as a first year without any previous politics courses and i'd recommend this class/professor. Engaging lecturer, interesting subject matter. No trick questions, information is straightforward.
Strident and sarcastic.  Rarely permits or respects other points of view in the classroom

He?s an awesome professor, but if you?re not willing to work hard don?t take his class. Readings can be long and often require serious thinking. Weekly essays are a challenge. Prof. Alexander expects a lot from his students, but if you put in the work you?ll get more out of his class than any other at UVA. Think about it.
Not a great lecturer.  Just go to section.  Fair grading.  Do the readings and you will be ok.

Alexander is incredible! Fun guy, and great material. This course is reading intensive, but 6 2-page essays with exception of 15-page final are easy to get A- on. Word of caution, if you are Jewish, this course has material and students, that defend offensive theories of the Holocaust.
Great teacher. Take his class. Lots of work, but worth it

Requires a well-thought argument and if you put time into papers, it works.  Not all readings are necessary, just those mentioned in class and TAs do expect a lot.  Overall, an interestign course but make sure you have the time to put into it.

Hands down one of my favorite professors at UVA. I was impressed in lecture and even more impressed when I spoke with him outside of class. He absolutely does demand excellence from his students. I disagree that he refuses to change his viewpoint; the trick is that you have to have a valid and supported point. Take the class, be ready to work.
Really cares about the subject.  A great class but lots of readings.

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS! I dont know if he has high ratings or not but he is a horrible teacher. He only listens to his own opinions and if he doesn't agree with you you might as well throw in the towel. Essay assignments are hard. TA's grade hard. Class is uninteresting and has too many readings.

Half of the readings are beyond the grasp of the average undergrad, while the other half seem to relate to the material only after careful explanation.  Lectures are interesting enough and extremely clear.

Argued today, 15 minutes, why forming group study guide was like stealing music off Napster. Papers graded harshly by TAs. Very extensive tedious readings. Makes very few people chuckle. His minor lisp on G, CH, and SH comes from trying to speak too hard and fast. Bring a laptop and type fast. If you don't accept his ideology you might not do well.

The readings are long and dense.  Reading responses are expected weekly on most of these readings.  Papers are short, but graded harshly.  Passionate lecturer, but speaks a mile per minute.  I went from typing 25-30 wpm to probably 35-40.  Proceed with caution...

The high recommendations for this guy are absolutely wrong.  I don't know anyone in my class this semester who thinks he is a good teacher.  Repeats himself way too much, gets way behind in the lecture schedule.  Readings are overly intellectual and there are way too many of them.  Unless you want to bang your head against a wall, don't take him.

Amazing professor!  Really engages students in the material.  A lot of reading but definitely doable.  Papers are short and graded harshly because he's looking for a very specific answer in them (but if he sees you improving over the semester he grades up!) Highly recommended!

He is a very fast speaker, but his lectures help in clarifying the readings.  The readings are very long and extensive, but they are not all necessary.  The papers are not too difficult to write but are graded very harshly.

It's true that he's a very energetic speaker. if by energetic you mean it sounds like the man is running on doses of speed at all times... he speaks faster than you'll be able to write unless you bring your laptop with you. EXTENSIVE reading. Essays are graded harshly, beware.
signs off on paperwork - but not helpfull as an adviser...

Really excited and interesting teacher. Makes politics come alive. Cracks jokes, runs around, bashes France now and then. There is a lot of reading but its not all necessary. His papers are kind of hard but they dont take a lot of time and he is available to help.
No Comments
Very riviting teacher
He rawks.  Very energetic and gets you motivated
He is an amazing professor.  Always willing to help sutdents out, funny lectures, really smart man... take his class!!
Awesome professor who is extremely clear and knowledgable.  His class is actually fun to go to and is never boring.  Be prepared to work really hard on the 2 essays during the semester.
LOVE this guy.  He's my advisor (chose him after I took this class).  He's great - interesting, knows his stuff, awesome, highly reccomended!
No Comments
Politics of Advanced Industrialized Nations. Good course, funny guy, knows his stuff, energetic. Boo-ya.
Funny, only 2 papers, graded by the TA so get a good TA, European politics rocks my world, I kind of want to have Thatchers babies. Take the class, FOOL
Also took GFCP/PLCP 311.  A somewhat aloof guy, but he knows his stuff.  Doesn't require too much writing for these courses.

honestly, I had to create a rmp account just to rate this guy. genuinely half his lectures are so off-topic and nobody understands what hes trying to say. the only reason his "grade point average" is higher than the other professor is because nobody attends the others lecture. this guys exams are also nothing like the topic
Not a good professor. None of the topics are extremely relevant and expects you to know things outside of the notes he teaches in his exams. Also very stingy on like every little detail.
Barley an elective.

Professor Hott is a great professor, despite being a little bit awkward. He teaches material well and gives assignments that really enforce your understanding. For this specific class, however, those assignments were non-stop, and took actual days to complete. I definitely feel like I learned a ton though.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Robbie is a very kind person, and a pretty decent lecturer. He obviously cares a lot about his students, but man, he really expects a lot out of them. Overall, I'd say he's fair over anything.

Hott is a gigachad. Excellent lecturer, caring, reasonable. Grading expectations are clear, tests fair (entirely stuff covered in lecture). Generous w/deadlines. Grades WILL be tight if you're weak in a 40% area, so do your best. People complaining about either exams or the hw is a skill issue imo... it's all uphill from bit fiddling!

Be aware, you will spend 10+ hours a week on your homework assignments because the difficulty between the lecture material and homework is so, so vast that you will sit in office hours to get through each problem. Good luck.

Robbie Hott was a great professor, he had a rough semester along with all of us and was very considerate and easy-going with some of our assignments and deadlines in order to make things as stress-free as possible. His lectures were sometimes hard to follow, but the website gave a lot of explanations. His blog is dope too.

I really enjoyed my experience in ECON 2010. The class if co-taught by Elzinga and MacKay, who both give great lectures, but I found the textbook really helpful. As long as I kept up with the readings, this class wasn't too stressful for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elzinga, while very well-known and has been at UVA for an eternity, would blab about things that weren't specifically related to the content. He kept talking about setting us up for the future/how it's important to be knowledgeable in economics but he was so off-topic and boring. He seemed like a super nice guy but maybe not the best to understand.
He is the GOAT. My dad also had him

Professor Elzinga is a knowledgeable and engaging lecturer, but the class requires a lot of work. Definitely use unstuckstudy ai, ChatGPT, and the textbook to supplement the lectures and nail the exams.

This guy is considered a legend and for good reason. The lectures are informative and helpful, however it is necessary to read the textbook and study it as well to receive a high grade in the class. I would highly recommend taking Elzinga's class as long as you are ready to read a little bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The Lectures were not too bad but went off topic very often and I had a hard time keeping focused in the lectures. They became so mundane to the point where I didn't even need to come to class. This class all depends on the quality of your TA. My TA was not very helpful and gave us no practice problems to do. This class is dependent on the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Elzinga is a good professor, but what makes or breaks your grade in the class is a TA. My TA was great; he provided all the materials the discussion section needed to succeed in the class, which is not what some other TAs do. The final is a bit annoying since there are a lot of niche textbook questions that we didn't go over in lectures.

If you're gonna take Econ201, do it with Elzinga. Knowledgeable, lovable guy who you'll learn a lot about econ from. Pray for a good TA, it really makes a difference. Tons of textbook readings which you just have to grind through. Lectures get boring but material isn't that difficult. Going to office hours & working with others really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Elzinga is clearly knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. Lectures, while often boring, do help you understand the material and only last an hour. He seems like a genuine person who wants the best for his students. My TA was AWFUL and I felt like I was at a disadvantage because of it. Still, this class wasn't crazy difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elzinga was great but the TAs are really a hit or miss which really can influence how well you do on tests.
If you are not good with economics and have never taken it, you will struggle. If you're gifted and find economic type things easy, you'll be fine.

Prof Elzinga has an interesting personality; the only reason I went to lecture. Often went off-topic and random scenarios to explain concepts. Read the textbook and do the practice problems!!! Hopefully get a good TA and then go to all discussions. This class is VERY HARD to get an A in. Do not rely on Dutch Knockout, work hard throughout semester.

Amazing teacher - easy to drift off during lectures tho. The final can kick your ass if you're not careful. Don't rely on the dutch knockout. 
Getting a solid grade is easy so long as you read + pay attention + work w/ your TA. You'll do well. 
The curve at the end is insane - this could help if you're not doing well. HARD to get an A/A+

Taking Econ 201 with Elzinga is like a right of passage at UVA. If you take the class seriously, do some reading, go to lectures, and study, you will be fine and get a good grade. It isn't the easiest class ever, but if you put in a little bit of time before the exams you will be fine.

Kenneth needs to retire. His lectures are pointless, boring, and full of random stuff that no one cares about but him. His final is impossible and is not even worth taking cause he expects us to know stuff that we NEVER LEARNED. Wtf. Im saving you future pain... DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!

Attending his lectures is not enough to do well on the exams, so you must read the assigned chapters from the textbook as well.  Also, watch his Econ Minutes as soon as they are released because they're time-sensitive, and you'll miss out on easy points on the exams if you forget. Overall, he's a funny professor but a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He really is a great guy and you can tell he's super knowledgeable about economics. However, his class is not easy at all, and the exams are terrible. I would not recommend this class with Elzinga to anybody. 

In terms of "the experience of taking econ with elzinga," highly overrated. No one cares about the "experience" if it means your GPA tanks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Lectures are interesting, but painfully useless. The two midterm exams are difficult, but doable. Good luck getting above a 75 on your final exam. 

If you get a good TA, you might make it out alive. If you get an average or subpar TA, drop and take ECON2010 with someone else. Do not take it with Elzinga if you care about your GPA at all.

If there's one mistake you're going to make at UVA that you will regret forever, it's taking ECON 2010 with Elzinga. 

It is RIDICULOUS how much of a difference there is between taking it with Elzinga vs Doyle/Santugini. Elzinga's final is impossible, has terms that never were taught, and his two midterms are graded so partially it's hilarious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Elzinga is caring but beyond that, I don't see any redeeming qualities about this class.The final is worth either 50 or 100% of your grade and doesn't even test conceptual knowledge but instead obscure details from somewhere in a 500 page textbook. The lectures are dry and pointless also. I am considering changing my major because of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elzinga is a legend at UVA. He is clearly experienced in economics, and his jokes in lectures always land. HOWEVER, I would not recommend this class to anyone who is not required to take it. The lectures are useless and the tests are written in riddles. He preaches principles only and then makes super-specific test questions. Not worth it at all.

Lectures are useless. He rambles on about an amount of information you could learn from reading a page of the textbook. Most classes have iClicker questions, but you can answer them from anywhere. Test content varies and are overall pretty difficult even having read text. Pray you get a good TA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elzinga was a dry speaker, but a very caring man; You could tell he loved teaching, but staying awake was very hard. The material he teaches is very difficult and you better have a good TA to re-explain the material for you because you will definitely need it. Each textbook chapter took me at least 2 hours or more to read, they were so long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class twice, once with Elzinga and once with Doyle. When I took it with Doyle, everything made sense and was so much easier/far less time-consuming. I got an A+ in the class and learned a lot. Elzinga's final included references and questions/math that were never addressed/taught in class. Do yourself a favor and take it with Doyle.

Elzinga is very knowledgeable about Econ, but his lectures are painfully boring and don't really go in-depth into the topics he tests on. If you get a good TA, his class isn't too bad, but if you have a bad one prepare to read your textbook and get study materials from other people. He's a nice guy, but not the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Elzinga teaches the most popular course at UVA like a professional. Micro is interesting but the lectures are nothing spectacular, and he doesn't cover everything in class. Exams (most of your grade) are easy enough if you pay attention and go to discussion. Beware, though, Elzinga likes to talk politics even when he promises not to.
lectures are useless and the final is unnecessarily hard and also worth either 50% or 100% of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the lectures and Elzinga in general. I didn't like the way he simplified everything in lecture and then makes the tests so difficult. He says and I quote "the tests aren't meant to trick you" and then there are so many deliberately tricky questions, especially on the final. Good guy, terribly structured class.

Elzinga is an amazing professor who could properly teach economics to someone with no understanding of society. His lectures were insightful and fun, and his teachings were allowed me to fully understand some immensely complicated concepts.

Worst professor at UVA. Last semester, I contracted COVID-19 as an immunocompromised individual and lost my taste and smell for months, and was knocked in bed for weeks. I had to take an exam during my illness given that Elzinga gives no opportunities to make up exams. Elzinga should follow what he preaches because he did not show any sympathy.

Professor Elzingas lectures just dont seem to be in depth enough to prepare you for the exams without reading or having a good discussion TA. I really loved hearing his stories/experiences though. This class had almost no homework- 80% of the overall grade was from 3 exams and the final was worth almost 50%. Head TA can really make or break class
Don't take his class unless you want to lower your GPA.
This class is great for someone who knows nothing about economics. It's a really great class, but be ready to work. If you don't do the readings or participate, the exams will be hard.

Professor Elzinga is great guy. He is super nice and respectful, and is really, really, passionate about economics. He is super knowledgeable and his experiences in anti-trust cases are mind blowing. However, his lectures aren't very detailed, so to get a good grade in class you must read the textbook and take good notes. The tests are tricky too.
Terrible professor

A lot of these ratings claim that Elzinga isn't "all that" and that the course is too difficult; I suspect that's more a result of the exams' focus on critical thinking (as opposed to memorization) than anything else. Elzinga is a true expert in economics and his lectures are enjoyable as well as engaging -- even with hundreds of students.

Lots of stories and tangents in lecture, but it keeps them interesting. Very far from a textbook approach to microeconomics, is has the feel of a liberal arts course. You might never need to open the textbook if you go to class take good notes. Your TA really matters, they grade your tests (which are almost all of class grade). STUDY. ovr not 2hard
I studied and studied for this course, but could never seem to hit the nail on exams of exactly what he wanted to see.
Avoid this man
He isnt all that, like at all. Ive had better professors than him. Also if you have an awful TA youre probably gonna struggle.

I have no idea why he is so famous. He legit sucks. Why is he so terrible?? Unclear. UVA needs to do SO MUCH better. He is a terrible lecturer and kinda annoying. He makes you buy his own book that he wrote under a different name so you don't know it is his.

Professor Elzinga is one of the best teachers I have had the pleasure of learning from. His lectures are entertaining and engaging, and he encourages students to think about not just the nuts and bolts, but the application of Economic thinking to their lives. Very compelling, a legend of a professor.
I DON'T LIKE HIM

Elzinga is legend here at Mr. Jefferson's University. Fantastic lectures, both interesting and informative. Tests are a combination of lecture material and reading material, so going to class and doing readings are both very important. Class was not overly challenging, even though I had an abysmal TA. Highly recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I found the concepts within the course to be quite interesting and I will probably end up becoming an ECON major. However, Professor Elzinga is simply a bad professor. I did not learn a single thing from any of his lectures and the course was basically learn it yourself. Luckily, I had a very good TA who helped me. Elzinga is famous, but he sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Elzinga is widely respected, but he did not explained concepts in clear and concise ways. His lectures were long and pretty unnecessary, and the way he sets up his discussion sections and TA's are what I hear the biggest complaints from. Lectures and discussion are both unhelpful. Read the textbook and try learning it on your own.

He doesn't really upload his notes anywhere and leaves a lot of material for the TAs to clear up in discussion. The TAs all vary in quality, so much of what you get out of the course depends on the TA. His lectures are funny, but he takes the long way to get to the actual point. The class is huge too, so it may be hard to focus.

The lectures are amazing, but that's all I can say about his teaching. The lectures go over all the easy stuff, with little to no math involved, and the tests are really hard. I don't know how you can teach this way. If you take the test based on how he presents lectures, you will FAIL badly. Cool guy, bad teacher.
Well respected and my mom took his class. Everybody loves him but I didn't. His lectures are a little too simplified for the level of difficulty of the tests.

Elzinga is pretty famous at UVA (and in general). He teaches Econ well but reading the textbook is somewhat necessary to do well. His lectures are a bit more airy than the technical work you need to know how to do. The grading is really difficult/specific and some of the questions seem to come out of nowhere. Worth taking with the legend though
Prof. Elzinga is an amazing professor. He is a real gem and going to his office hours were one of my favorite memories of UVA so far.
Makes Econ applicable to the real world. You need to do a decent amount of reading and there are clicker questions in most classes.

Tests are pretty tough, and you definitely have to work for a good grade in the class, but there's a good curve at the end. Elzinga is a good lecturer, incredibly interesting and humble, and extremely accomplished. A must-take before you graduate from UVa.

I did not do well in this class, but I am not going to blame Elzinga for that. I think that for a 500 person lecture, he commands attention pretty well. The one thing I will say is that his tests are very hard. Make sure you know every detail and know how to clearly explain all terms and ideas.

Great person, loved to talk to students. I went in with high expectations of his teaching because everyone told me Elzinga was God. His reputation is a little overrated. Didn't usually understand the concept fully in his lectures, so do background reading too and actively attend discussion sections, you should be fine! Test questions from guide.

Elzinga is a cool guy who knows a lot about Econ though I did prefer Macro with Coppock.  He uses metaphors and stories to make his points and doesn't use powerpoints (lectures at the podium with an occasional transparency). Go to class his econ minutes are on the exams. Read the book! Grading is fair and DO NOT rely on the dutch knockout

I really liked Professor Elzinga. Sure, his lectures may have been a little on the boring side occasionally, but he's very passionate about teaching ECON 2010. He offers tons of advice. His final was not particularly difficult, if you attend class (you'll need to pretty regularly) and studied you're fine. Overall, great class!

He is not all he is cracked up to be. His tests are extremely tricky and he only has the TAs grade them, who are harsh. He rambles in lecture about nonsense and then will ask a deeply specific question on a test about nonsense whether or not it has to do with the standard microeconomics course material.

He is one of the worst lecturers here at UVA. He rambles on about nonsense and gives unreasonably hard tests just to trick us. Also, he allows inexperienced undergraduates to grade our hard tests and they are harsh. I would avoid this at all costs.
He is super hard and his TAs are just students who grade too tough. He is overrated and does not deserve the high reputation  he somehow holds.

DO NOT TAKE.  Everyone who says he is a great teacher LIES. The tests are graded insanely tough. In office hours he can be almost condescending, which contradicts his general nice attitude. Take the other guy.
I took this class in the Fall of 1975.  It changed my major, my career and the way I think to this day.  Best professor ever.
Prof. Elzinga is an excellent lecturer (although he failed to keep my attention sometimes). He is readily available outside of class to answer questions about class or anything else.

Elzinga does a great illustrating Econ & ensuring everyone has an opportunity to understand it. Although the material can be dull at times, his side stories and examples are funny and keep you interested.

Don't let yourself be fooled by the seemingly easy material. In a class of 1000 students, the exams have to be hard. I went in with a lot of confidence and then ended up with a B even though I liked Econ, did all the readings and understood it.

Everyone says that this is a class everyone should take. It. Is. Not. Not only are the lectures and discussions pointless but the exams are extremely difficult. Elzinga tries to make the lectures interesting but never gets his point across. The best lecture of the year was given by the head TA.

His lectures are fun and informative, you will enjoy the class until you reach the midterms. They are not easy at all. The final is just something else, even if you think you did well because it's multiple choice, you probably didn't. If you are a pre-comm student, I advise you to take micro from a TA so that you can prevent your gpa from falling.

People RAVE about this professor.. BUT: his lectures are pointless, he takes 35 minutes to get to the point, you need to teach yourself, the curve it terrible, and he really is not as kind as everyone says. I sent him multiple emails never to have a reply. Do yourself a favor and stay out of his class.

Elzinga is fantastic, I thought his lectures were fascinating. People complain b/c they "didn't relate to the material" but that's what the discussion is for. His lectures take the material & make it applicable to everyday life. Tests are really challenging, especially his final. Go to lecture and really utilize your disc & TA and you'll do fine.

While his reputation precedes him, the class itself is lacking in that it is large and lectures focus almost entirely on small cases studies rather than spent working through the material in detail.  While it would be admittedly difficult to dissect material in a class this size, considerable time and effort on the part of the student is required

Elzinga is a super sweet guy - I'd love for him to be my grandpa. That being said, I think his lectures are overrated. I learned most things from my TA (Ben Leyden, who's amazing) and from the text. Sometimes lectures help teach textbook material, but he usually spends the first 25 minutes talking about useless things.

Elzinga really isn't a great lecturer. It seems that he is able to keep teaching based on his reputation as a professor rather than on his actual skill. His lectures sometimes have nothing to do with what you are learning, and his tests are unreasonably difficult. You have to read the book on your own, because he doesn't go over it at all.

This is the best professor in UVa. I have no interest in econ but his lectures were very entertaining, I had no problem staying awake. (I normally sleep thru other classes). Take the class, you will not regret it.

The rumors are true; this is definitely a class everyone at UVA should take. As far as grades go, he offers his signature "dutch knockout" which is great if you are like me and do better with multiple choice exams since that's how the final is. Genius professor!

If you've already studies and understand 90% of what the textbook said, they you'll find the lectures interesting. If you didn't, then like me you may not understand what the prof. said. This class requires passion on ECON and a lot of self-teaching.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! Especially if you've NEVER taken Econ before! You'll have to teach yourself everything - DO NOT TAKE IT. If you really need econ for a requirement take it with a smaller class not a 1000-PERSON LECTURE!!!!!!!! You have been warned.

Elzinga is the most helpful and amazing guy out there. He teaches his lectures very clearly and makes it interesting for a person with any major. His classes are only 50 minutes long. I truly enjoyed this class and suggest this for anyone no matter if you are interested in Economics or not.

Elzinga is such a nice guy, and Microeconomics with Elzinga is a class that everyone takes a UVa because Elzinga is legendary! Don't expect this class to be easy though. I never had Econ in high school, and I had to study hours and hours before exams and then I got B's. TA's don't speak good English which is annoying.

Elzinga is probably the best micro teacher at uva, mostly because the ta's rarely speak english as their first language, but I didn't really enjoy the class too much. He has gigantic lectures and repeats himself alot... and then he repeats himself alot... but he is definitely the best here, so take his class. Its pretty hard tho, so be wary.

Mr. Elzinga is a living legend. 201 is one of those quintesential UVa courses you need to take to get the full experience here. Amazing lectures. Final is tricky but there is a generous curve. Take this class before graduating no matter your major
Not as good as everyone thinks. He's a funny guy and his lectures are entertaining, but frankly, microecon is about the most useless subject, which nobody seems to recognize.

Classes are not that bad, the topic is really interesting and the midterms are extremely easy. The final is really really hard, is worth 50% of your grade, and is nothing like the midterms. Make sure your TA knows how to speak English fluently! I got really disappointed of this class and professor Elzinga after the final.
As has been said, Elzinga's the man. Take Micro with no one else.

Elzinga is wonderful. Final is abysmal. You must do well on the first two tests in order to buffer your grade. If you do poorly on the final it will drop at least a letter grade. This class is not for those who just get by with minimal reading.
He is nice and fun. But unfortunately, I'm still not interested in econ...

Elzinga is an absolutely fantastic professor who is passionate about the material, able to bring real-world experience to his lectures, and personable enough to make you forget that there are 500 other people in the lecture hall with you. Not an easy A though. He'l make you work for it. And watch out, the final is notoriously difficult

This class was awesome!  Elzinga is a wonderful lecturer who makes a topic like economics seem fun.  He jokes in class and is wonderful at office hours.  He loves teaching and it is obvious through his performance in the classroom.  Don't take microeconomics with anyone else!  You'll regret it later!

Definitely THE professor to take ECON 201 with. Lectures are often funny which makes class enjoyable. Micro is not really my thing and sometimes I left class without feeling like I learned a whole lot, but that might be expected from a principles class. Still, Elzinga is a really nice guy and great at what he does so I definitely recommend!

Elzinga is the King of ECON 201. He's a wonderful guy and has a good sense of humor. His lectures are organized, interesting and very enjoyable. He is very enthusiastic and cares a lot about his students. The class itself is pretty easy. Definitely take this class!!

I took introductory economics with Elzinga in 1975.  He is one of the 5 best teachers (kindergarten through law school) whose class I've had the pleasure of taking.  He lectured on antitrust at a CLE program I attended four years ago.  Still superb!

I love Elzinga!  He managed to make a topic that would otherwise bore me into something fun and interesting!  I learned a lot in his class, and overall it wasn't too much work.  I highly recommend that everyone take ECON 201 with Elzinga.

I really enjoyed this class. The first two exams are really easy but don't let that fool you into thinking the final is. It's worth 50% of your grade and the class average this semester was a mid-C. Elzinga is such a good professor though, definitely take his class.
very nice man but the exam is impossible! go into the exam with an A and expect to come out with a B or B-.  just warning you.

Elzinga is the man. I went to every lecture even though they are optional, and enjoyed them all. He is also a superhero and most likely lives in a batcave underneath the chem building. Join the clicker club. Love it.

If you take Economics, take it with Elzinga. He knows his stuff. He is VERY important in the economics world -- he's a powerful guy. He's funny, a good lecturer, and his tests really are not that hard. Study for like 1-2 hours and you'll be fine.

READ!!! READ!!! READ!!! Although Elzinga is a great lecturer and just over all cool guy you will be COMPLETELY lost if you dont do the reading. Luckily the textbook isnt THAT rough, and once it clicks it clicks. Elzinga- totally awesome guy. I recommend this class but remember that a little effort goes a long way.
Everyone should take his class. He is just a great professor with lots of experience. Knows what he's talking about and gives excellent lectures.
The man is God. Legit teacher and a cool guy. Take this course!

Everyone knows him and he lives up to the hype. Great professor, no one else can make ECON 201 clearer. Clicker questions aren't hard to come by and the majority of the final grade comes from the two midterms and one final. Take notes during lecture and maybe look over the book before tests and B+ or above is almost gaurenteed.

Well, I got an F in this class even though I am otherwise a solid B+/A- student. Moral of the story: you need to go to every lecture, and do not rely on his "double-dutch" deal to save your grade. Clicker questions add up, the final is tough.
Elzinga is very clear and the actual class is not that difficult, however be sure to study hard for the final because it was more difficult than people expected it to be!
Great class, great proff. Take econ w him if you have the chance

You don't realize how good Elzinga is until you watch your TA lecture, or you try to read the book and learn it on your own.  It's not really anything spectacular, but he teaches and does it well.  Tests and the final were not easy, but if you keep up, it's not all that bad.

I really enjoyed class and Professor Elzinga, especially b/c the class is not strictly lecture.  It's a little relaxed.  That said though!  Tests were awful.  I never got enough practice to be able to apply lecture material.  I took this class "for fun" b/c everyone knows about Elzinga, but with my final grade, I should have waited.

Professor Elzinga is amazing. His class makes you look at the world in a whole new (economic) way. Pay attention to the clicker questions...they tend to mimick the final. His unit tests are purely applications to the principles of economics and can be occasionally vague, but they're not that bad. The examples from the lectures help you understand t
very nice, but sincerely too many tangents... too little class... BORING

Take ECON 201 at UVa, and unless you've heard something great about one of the smaller sections (I hear they can be gems, if with the right teacher), Elzinga is a great choice!  Bit of a hard curve though.
The UVa. experience is incomplete without Elzinga.

He is an amazing teacher! I love him! Attendance is not mandatory but exams are based mostly on the lecture so you need to go if you wanna do well on the exams. He manages 500-students incredibly well and gives very interesting, well organized lectures. He is just unbelievably amazing!

He is an amazing teacher and really loves his subject! He is really concerned about the status of his students.  He will make time for his students and has office hours and offers Pepsi and cookies.  His class is really interesting and has a lot to do with everyday life.  I highly encourage every student to take this class at some point in time.

Kenneth Elzinga is god. He teaches in a way that everyone can relate to. This is one teacher that almost everyone will have something good to say about. He is very comical and the tests arent too bad. Make sure you study hard for hte final because it is difficult. This man is so dedicated to his students, he will offer you to come over to his house

Absolutely wonderful! His lectures are always entertaining and give you valuable information that everybody should know. Mr. Elzinga genuinely cares about his students and is more than willing to help you outside of class. His tests aren't that bad, but watch out for his final!

I don't really care how intersting this man's lectures are. What I care about is the grade. So watch out, his tests are different from what you would expect. And the final is nothing like the previous tests, nor is it similar to the way he taught the class. Sure he is funny and a seemingly good Christian, but don't be caught off guard. Beware.
Incredible

Elzinga is an amazing professor that makes econ so interesting. His lectures are always engaging and he goes above and beyond to make himself available to his students. Definitely take his class while you're at UVA.

Absolutely great.  Highly recommended.  Go to class and do the reading (there is not too much outside work) and you will do fine.  Elzinga is an incredibly engaging professor who is open to his students even though he teaches two 500-person classes.  He actually lives up to all the hype.
awesome.thats all.

strongly recommended. you may not learn too much about economics but elzinga is a very inspiring lecturer and he really teaches you what he calls "the economic way of thinking". his exams are not that hard as most people say. test materials are usu in the text, apart from the part after the 2nd test (income)

OK, this was an amazing class. Elzinga is a great lecturer. He cares immensely about his students and genuinely loves teaching this class. He could be making millions elsewhere, but he loves his students and even invites you to thanksgiving dinner at his house. His passion shows through in class. Take it, you will definitely learn A LOT!

Elzinga is awesome.  advice:  LISTEN to what he was saying..I regret going to class and just taking notes.  If you sit and LISTEN, it's soo much better and you understand the material better.  he's a great lecturer and he presents the material with much knowledge.  If you're lucky, you'll get some free bee's in class!

Wonderful professor.  He explains everything very clearly.  Although you can get by without attending lecture, you really should go all the time because tests are almost entirely out of lecture.  Reading the text helps also.  If you take Econ 201, definitely do it with Elzinga.
AMAZING TEACHER! Everyone should take this class regardless of major, it changes your life and the way you see the world!

Although he'll say his lectures dont parret the readings in the textbook its pretty much the exact same thing, just 3 tests all semester so don't mess one up. Also he'll let you take the final exam grade as your grade for the class which is really cool and he may be one of the best public speakers I have ever seen. Very knowledgeable and nice and y

Though it's too big of a class and doesn't really suit my way of learning, Elzinga's lectures are really interesting, and is always willing to help after lecture and during office hours. If you know the key concepts really well, then the class won't be so hard at all, despite what some of the other comments might say.

This class is really easy.  There are a few key concepts you need to know (supply demand, marginal cost, etc) and that's it.  There's very little homework.  Elzinga is a pretty good lecturer, and usually dwells on topics for a few weeks, so you can afford to miss a lot of class.  Make sure you know the key concepts though, otherwise you're sunk.
this is a great class to see how college should be...interesting, demanding, thought provoking... great guy who cares about his students if they care enough to ask for advice and help...
No Comments
very tough classes... too many students... get noticed through office hours and study like a banchee...

very nice guy--get free soda and cookies if you go to office hours.  explains material very well.  there are only a few grades though so if you mess up on the first exam you should probably drop because you will probably do the same on the second and on the final (which is relatively difficult no matter how hard you study). recommend smaller class

I love Elzinga! He had the most interesting lectures...tests were really hard, but if you kept up with the material in class they were'nt too bad because they were curved.  I also felt like it was my only useful class i have taken thus far, and that the subject matter was very relevant and interesting.

Genuinley good professor..but nevertheless, the most challenging course I took this semester. Don't depend on lectures to help on exams, read and fully understand concepts in the text. If you do not do well on first two exams, final exam grade replaces entire semester grade for class (great option). However, do not be fooled..the final is no joke!

Elzinga is the man!  He really cares about the students and is willing to take the time nessecary to explain the material and in so doing, cultivate a love of economics in his students!  I love Elzinga!

I loved this class. Elzinga is a great professor.  He always makes jokes when you aren't expecting it.  He knows the subject very well and tries to be as clear as possible in lecture. My TA was decent and helpful, Peggy Huang.  The midterms are not easy by any means but it is possible to do well, but the final wasn't too bad.  Awesome class!!

An institution at UVA and rightly so.  Instead of piling on even more praise for Mr. Elzinga (which he deserves)I give this advice: don't be afraid to keep switching discussion sections until you find a TA you like.  The importance of the TA is a bit overstated (because the final can make up your entire grade and its MC) but find a good one.
He is a great lecturer and can keep a listener enthralled in his lectures, but the TA's are all horrible, making the class harder than it should be.

GREAT teacher! Best one I had all semester. He was easy to understand and taught a large lecture class well.  He was intresting and just an all around great guy. even if you are not planning to take any econ classes take his class. he is a great teacher and his class is very worth your time.
great teacher, hard class
Saving grace was the final exam. TAs were overly picky with taking points off of the midterms. Elzinga is a good man.
Professor Elzinga is AMAZING.  ECON 201 with him is exactly the must-take course everybody says it is...take it, and do yourself a favor.  He is a brilliant, kind, and wonderful professor.

Good speaker, great guy, but kind of overrated as a professor. I didn't follow follow his lectures very well, and they definitely din't stimulate my interested in econ. Don't expect too much from the TAs.

Elzinga is good, but not as great as everyone says.  The structure of the class is horrible, no discussion leaders speak english, and your first two tests show it through the grading.  I would take a smaller econ to avoid the ambiguity of grading
Elzinga is my favorite teacher ever! I'm so sad that Econ 201 is over! His lectures changed my outlook on life.

Mr. Elzinga is fantastic and his lectures are awesome; by far my favorite class so far.  I've never taken Econ or a business class and I'm doing pretty well.  Keep up with your reading, study, and come to lectures-- it's a great class and very worth while!!

SOOOO dreamy. From the first time i stepped into the room i realized that i had found my true love. I am doing pretty well in his class but i would be doing SO much better if i could just help myself from getting lost in his beautiful, soulful eyes. AWESOME TEACH! VERY HOT! VERY FUNNY!  <33

pretty much what you hear is right. awesome professor, and I predict he will end up being my favorite throughout my educational career, no joke.  tests aren't bad even though that one commetn suggests you ought to have done well on AP.  I've never touched business or econ and am doing very well. go to lecture, do some of the reading and you are set
Mr. Elzinga is the mam, pure and simple.

Was explecting alot more from elzinga...Test are hard (with very open ended question, but just one specific answer), As a teacher he's terrible, lecture is a waste of time since the book teaches you everything he does and alot more, As for the TAs...good luck trying to understand them (I still cant pronounce my TA's name)
Tests are challenging.  Those who get A's probably got 5's on AP exams.  If you're one of those people, the class is no sweat.  Very little work and very little reading.
funny, interesting, knowledgeable, has major credentials
Antitrust Policy is the single most useful class you can take at UVA.  Believe the hype, Elzinga is a top-5 UVA professor hands down

Elzinga is the most overrated professor I had at UVA. He's not an engaging lecturer. You can tell he uses stock jokes every semester. On a personal level, I lost respect for him after juxtaposing his frequent proselytizing with his career defending Wal-Mart, Du Pont and other corporations that defile the environment and consistantly violate human rights. Regardless of his Christian and Corporate Right values, I think he was only an average professor.
absolutely one of THE best professors at UVa
overrated. really. i bet he's a nice guy, but not that great of a teacher, does not live up to the hype
No Comments

While he is definitely an econ expert, and a very entertaining lecturer, his tests were really difficult. Anyone who is just taking this class because they heard Elzinga is cool should try auditing or doing credit/no credit if not an econ genius.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Elzinga is fabulous- a great lecturer, knowledgeable economist, and really sweet old man :) you will gain alot of useful daily knowledge from his class, and always be entertained. his tests are hard, esp. the final... make sure your TA is good.

Elzinga is a great lecturer, definitely fun to listen to. However, his tests were really really hard. I was told to take him by so many people, but I found out later that the smaller classes seemed to learn things alot better...I would go with a small class if possible.

He is an amazing person. Go to office hours and get to know him. It will be worth your time. He cares so much about students, and anyone who has anything bad to say about him either never really went to class or got the chance to know him, or is bitter because they did badly in the class.

Highly overrated. Having struggled through what should have been an introductory course, I know now to warn others before they make the same mistake. His lecturer can be interesting, but know that his class doesn't really prepare you for upper level Econ, despite what you hear.
Totally nerdy, yet totally cool.
talks slow, but that is the only complaint. a fun guy.

Elzinga is amzing- makes economics as fun as it ever will be in my opinion. Anyways, if you need to fill 3 extra credits, even if you have no desire to take multiple econ classes, I would recommend taking 201 with Elzinga

Great Teacher, but he loves making money.  Brags about being the economic consultant for Wal-Mart, Microsoft and every other big company.  I liked his class, but when I went to his office hours, he kicked me out only because Show Girls was playing on HBO.
Very intertaining, good overall guy.  You don't need to read the book if you take good notes at the lectures.

Elzinga is just about as good as they come.  Great speaker and very clear, the class is easy if you show up and listen.  Take good notes and ask questions in your discussion and reading the text isnt even needed.  Elzinga covers everything in an hour twice a week.  Bravo.
I loved the class.  It was a lot of fun.  Some of the lectures will be very useful in everyday life :)

Great Class! I loved it. I didn't realize that Economics could actually be interesting before I took this class! Elzinga is very down to earth and approachable.  Don't let the large class size scare you away, I barely noticed there were 500 of us in the class (of course I sat in the front...)
One of the best classes to take, Elzinga's lectures are enjoyable and interesting.
Undoubtedly one of the best lecturers I have ever encountered. It was a pleasure to take his class. I definitely learned a great deal, and would very much like to take another course with him.
Elzinga is the man!!!!

Great teacher, tells lots of funny stories and has an awesome dry wit. While this class is a must take, it is not an easy A. Expect a B or so if you do the readings and go to lecture. Good, english-speaking TA is a must.

Best teacher ever. He rocks. If he asks for a volunteer, raise your hand, he might give you money. The only class I would reccomend attending lecture. You won't need the book if you pay attention to him.
Very interesting teacher.  Keeps lecture pretty interesting.  Tests are hard.

ECON is okay.  Elzinga's lectures are pretty hit or miss, with him hitting about 70% of the time.  Occasionally a lecture is just a series of graphs that is shuffled through too fast to comprehend.  You had better hope you don't have an international TA, too!

Elzenga's definetly one of the best professors at UVa. His lectures are simply amazing and he has so much experience! He really teaches you all you need to know about econ. And he gives really good advice and is friendly and approachable.
I think his lectures are nice, he makes them fun, still I also dont know what the hype is about.His tests are difficult!
great sense of humor...loves and knows a great deal about sybject.

He is a great guy.  The lectures are big, but pay attention and keep up with the reading and you'll be fine.  Go to his office hours! He will help anyone with academic advising.  You will appreciate him even more after talking to him.  Go to discussion to understand topics not covered in class.
Good lecturer, but not a great teacher. Very enthusiastic despite a class of 500+ students. Pray you have a good TA or the class can be pretty challenging.
The GOLD standard!

He is the man: a man of extreme intelligence, passion for his subject, and a willingness to serve every student that comes to his room.  An amazing person, in and out of class.  God bless you, Professor Elzinga.
I have no idea what the hype is all about.
love the dry sense of humor
Elzinga is the man! He's totally brilliant and is a great lecturer. The class is large, but worth the experience.
good lecturer-- never made me miss econ 201 more than 5 times but hard exams... and NO i am not stupid.
Best professor ever!
not as good as everyone makes him out to be...hes a super nice guy...but his big room lectures are awful....can someone explain why his "pegs" don't organize his lecture at all?
The class is not that hard, but you get lost with all the other 500 students. The key is getting a good TA because Elzinga isn't that accessible. He tries the best he can, is very enthusiastic.
this guy below me is absolutely correct. HE IS THE MAN. HE IS THE MAN. His tests can be tricky, but that's because you are dumb/stupid.

elzing-zing is the man.....incredible speaker, funny lectures, best professor at the university.....tests can be hard, but they're manageable and worth it.....and dont forget about the good old dutch knock out

The Dutch Knock Out: Your grade is made up of two midterms, your discussion section, and the final exam.....OR.....Your final exam alone will be your final grade if it is higher. The final exam is usually multi-choice, which compensates for the difficulty
Amazing. Take it before he retires.
Awsome Class, Funny, great lecturer
One of the best professors in the nation.
He's Incredible.
great lectures
He's pretty clear and helpful.  He has the lectures down like he's reading a script.
Great Lectures.  Funny and approachable.

best lecturer!!! uses lots of examples and material isn't hard. tests are weird (don't really cover material well...ambigious questions....) but material can be absorbed just from lectures. study for the final.

Although I am merely a first-year, Dr. Elzinga is far and away the best professor I have. He's articulate, funny, and has every one of his lectures down to a science. I recommend this class to everyone.
lives up to the hype...great lecturer.  make sure to get a good TA though, because a bad one can make the class a lot more stressful.

Elzinga is perhaps one the nicest and most approachable person you'll ever meet; his lectures are always captivating; however, his tests are extremely hard and in a large class setting, it is often difficult to fully understand the material
Professor Elzinga is a great guy any way you cut it.  An amazing person and teacher, and his lectures are not only thought provoking, but fascinating as well.  Everyone should take his class.
GREAT class, enjoyable lectures! The tests are intresting, however, but the class is still enjoyable, just the same!

Prof. Elzinga is simply amazing.  His class just cheers you up, no matter what your day's been like, and he's possibly the best teacher I've ever encountered.  This class should be required for every student at UVA.

Elzinga is the man.  If you are going to take ECON201, you should take it with Mr. Elzinga.  Great lectures and very willing to helo students understand the material.  He goes above and beyond for his students, for whom he cares deeply about.
Elzinga is the man. Plain and simple, he is brilliant and he does one of the few lectures that is always entertaining as well as informative. Again, the man.

I had Dr. Elzinga 25 years ago for Micro.  He made a lasting impression on my life.  He is certainly one of the most well-rounded, impressive people I have ever met.  Ken Elzinga motivated me.  I have gone on to teach College Econ myself. I recommend him.
nice guy, goes way and above and byond for his students.  he is also the head economist of microsft so he knows what he is talking about

The best Prof I have ever had.  The only reason some idiots say bad things about Mr. Elzinga is because they didn't study for the final and it caught up with them.  He is great and everyone should take this class.  There is a reason he teaches 1000+/year!
Nice guy and good lecturer. Test questions are sometimes ambiguous.
Definitely a nice guy, but I don't understand what all the hype is about.
Incredible teacher, everyone should take his class.
The best! His lectures provide very good examples that are great for the material
201 is overfilled and over-rated.  To be fair, he's really good in anti-trust
Great teacher
Anyone who thinks Elzinga is a bad teacher is an idiot.  The best prof I know!
BS's during lectures, won't take questions or see you in office. Ambiguous tests
No Comments
pretty good lecturer, tests are tricky and a bit unfair
No Comments
Elzinga is a beast, take  him
Great Lecture and great guy.  Tests can be tricky
yay
No Comments
No Comments
Great guy, good teacher, but don't take expect a gut.
No Comments
come on, Elzinga, everyone at UVA should take his class, it's tradition
Though he seems like a passionate professor, he is very disorganized and an unfair, harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a law student, Professor Halliday presided over the most ridiculous class I took during my time as a student. Dig this. For 3 credits, you read 12 books, present for 45 minutes on of those books, write a response essay on another book, and have a final exam. Thousands of pages of reading with almost no knowledge gained. COMPLETE FAILURE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Halliday is a smart guy and seems to know the answer to any question you ask. Class time is used for large-group discussion, which brings out the key parts of the reading. Halliday can come off as condescending to students at times, although you can tell its not his intention so shake it off and keep going. Hes a captivating prof and makes it fun
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really dedicated, and makes an enormous effort to provide guidance and feedback. Gives a lot of work, but has a lot of constructive criticism and is always fair.
I had Professor Warren for the engagement of 'God and Nature in America" and it was a super chill class. All you need to do is show up and say something and you'll most likely get an A.

I had Professor Warren for my engagement, and she was incredible. To be completely honest, I was a little intimidated by her at first, but after several conversations, I realized how funny and kind she is. She really cares about what students have to say, and I loved how she handwrote feedback at the bottom of assignments.

I took this class for an easy credit 2nd-semester 1st year. While the class material as a whole was fairly easy, and Heather Warren's lectures were interesting, the TA graded exams somewhat harshly, and it wasn't the "easy A" type of class that I was expecting. Prof Warren also requires students to handwrite notes fervently while she lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: test questions were pulled directly from study guide-completely possible to get a perfect 100 in the class if you are good at memorization. Going to lecture and taking notes is definitely helpful, but u could probably skip every lecture and cram for exams and still do well. Warren is funny and endearing, really cares about her students, love her.

Didn't go to lecture other than to take tests, you don't really need to. Attendance at the discussion section is mandatory, though. She gives a study guide before tests and most answers are on Quizlet or you'll go over them in your discussion section. Easy grade with little effort compared to other courses.

As long as you study, you will get an A in this class. Gives a "study guide" ahead of time and pulls all exam questions from the study guide. If you have any questions and ask her through email, she will usually respond immediately with great amount of detail.

Professor Warren's class isn't too difficult as long as you do the work. All exam material is on a study guide given about a week and a half ahead of time and she is responsive to questions. Exams are entirely written (with IDs, quote IDs, and an essay) and are very memorization heavy - do not put studying off. Solid choice for gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Heather Warren is a great professor. I have taken her for 3 classes at UVA and she sets very clear expectations, and prepares you well for the tests which are not too difficult. Go to lecture, use her study guides and you'll be set!

Gives a study before exams, and then all exam material is pulled from the study guide. Exams are handwritten in blue books, and have vocab/quotes/essay sections. Decent bit of writing but easy to study for. Go to lecture though and take good notes! That's where you get info for study guide. I didn't read much, but readings obviously help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Warren is an amazing lecturer: there is so much substance in her lectures (which sometimes makes it hard to keep up but if you collaborate on notes and study in groups, you'll be fine) and I learned so much every class. Amazing class for a Religion major: she packs so much clear, relevant information into this course. She's very cool.

A MUST TAKE COLA if you have interest in god/ nature. The readings are inspiring. No exams and all you need to do is showing up and joining the discussion. Prof Warren is one of my FAVORITE in UVa. She's extremely humorous and really cares about her students. Great advising part. We also had wonderful time in tea party and Shenandoah hiking trip.

I am HORRIBLE at religion and Christian religions always confused me. However, I got an A in this class. Even if you suck at religion as long as you're good at memorizing, you're set. If you work on the reviews she gives out before each test, you are literally set. She's also a pretty entertaining lecturer. Not too dry.

Clearly the best class of my first semester.  Heather Warren is an amazing professor!  Lectures cover a lot of material each day, so be prepared to write. (no computers allowed)  I only read the primary sources, not the extra textbook readings, and did fine.  Make sure to ask questions to your TA about the study guide-- they are very helpful.
The grading for this class is unrealistic. No matter how much you study, you will get a B at best. I studied so much and ended up with a B. The professor is fantastic though. She is very funny.

Heather is amazing. Incredibly brilliant (she was a Rhodes Scholar) yet so kind, humble, and wants to help her students do well in school and life. She's a professor, priest, and she spends her summers on the Appalachian trail...coolest prof I've ever had.

an awesome professor and class--i highly recommend it, even if you arent interested in religion as a major. i took two of her classes my first year and now i am a relg major. Lecture is always interesting and there are no papers, several exams which you can do well on if u do the studyguide she provides. one of the best teachers ive had a uva.

So nice and caring!  Gives study guides before every test and obviously wants students to do well.  Lots of knowledge on the subject matter, presents it in a clear, fun way.  By far the least boring and has the most personality of any history teacher I've had yet.

Pretty easy class. Like everyone said she gives you all the possible questions ahead of time, and doesn't put all of them on the actual test. There are basically a few key words they are looking to check off while grading the tests, so it's important to put the right words. Didn't do most of the readings, still did well.  Take the class!

This class is an easy class.  All you have to do is go to class and take notes from her lectures.  She sends out wat is going to be on the exam word for word.  I hardly did the readings because my discussion was based on the lectures not the readings.  She is a very nice and approachable professor.  I recommend everyone take her class; its a easy A

This is an interesting class.  Attendance to discussion is mandatory and as well as lectures. Her tests come right from her lectures.  Test are easy because she gives you it ahead of time, you just have to memorize it. Overall, an easy class as long as you study and take good notes.

Professor Warren is great! She is an entertaining lecture and keeps things interesting, even if the assigned readings about them aren't. She gives a great review sheet for the exam but, because of this, she expects concise answers on the test and the grading is tough. So go to lecture, go to discussion and join a study group. You'll enjoy it!

I loved this class, its what made me want to be a religious studies major.  It is a great overview of religious life in America with just enough detail but not too much on any one focus.  Lectures are interspersed with film and songs performed by Warren herself. Warren is very clear lecturer.  She gives you an outline of exactly what to study.

Lectures were very interesting. LOTs of readinng material but you dont REALLY need to read it all except if you want to do well in disc section. disc section was horrible, but tests were easy as long as you prepared answers to the questions that warren gives on the study guide...which is basically the test.
