Stay away unless you love Computer Science and are ready to dedicate a lot of time and work. I had zero knowledge about coding when going in and the programs we had to write were definitely NOT intro-level. First 2 weeks might seem easy because he only teaches concepts but the material from lectures isn't helpful for HW. Use the book, it helps.
Even though the professor is super smart he teaches at way too fast of a pace and gives too much work. Avoid this class.
Class is super hard and involves a lot of math. If you are not good at math, stay away! He lectures at a breathtaking speed so if you don't understand something once, seek help immediately.
Always helpful at office hours and answers all questions. Great lectures but workload was high.

Very entertaining in a nerdy, quirky kind of way. Goes through lecture material very quickly. He's hyper intelligent and really helpful outside of class so I highly encourage going to his office hours if you're stuck. Recommended only if you're a CS major and interested in the topic he's teaching though because he does expect a lot of work.

Too much work given. Does not realize that the students have other courses/a social life to take part in. His homeworks make you build a graphics engine from scratch forcing you to use his arbitrary input syntax while there not being any online resources that are helpful for the homework - probably because no other graphics class is as tedious.
He may be all energetic and enthusiastic, but he is totally useless. I can never understand a single thing in this class. His quizzes are stupid multiple choice that are just trick questions.

best professor for CS 2110! He goes through the material somewhat quickly, but if you're the kind of person that understands concepts easily then this class should be a breeze. Tycho. is a very quirky guy, but nonetheless energetic and VERY enthusiastic. he might go a kinda fast if you're looking to have him for CS1110, but he taught CS2110 well.

Very energetic and quirky but in a good way. He is very knowledgeable in his field. Attendance is not mandatory but his lectures are always engaging: so much so that I feel as if I've missed out if I miss a class. UVA needs more professors like Tychonievich.
That previous review was clearly written by Tychonievich. That said, he was pretty much on-point with his assessment of his  class.

Fantastic, energetic professor. Codes super fast, so pay attention in class, but will take time to explain any tough concepts. Class isn't tough; just keep up with homework. Entertaining lectures, with original poems and jokes.

I am so sorry I tried my hardest to like this guy but i just couldnt, lectures are messy, unorganized, and confusing, He confuses himself so often and just assumes we understand everything. Would not recommend.

NL is a really nice person who cares about his students, but not the best lecturer. Basically talks for the entire lecture without stopping to make sure everybody is on the same page. He has a relatively forgiving grading policy, though, which is nice.

This man is extremely kind and he seems to care, but honestly I don't see why he has such amazing reviews. His lectures are not helpful and unclear. He speaks at a lightning pace.I would choose to skip class everyday almost except there are clicker questions that count as part of your grade, therefore, I attend.

This class was pretty easy and Prof Liyanage had some great demonstrations to go with his lecture. He also posts all his notes online (and they're up on or the day after that lecture). The homework problems given as well as the examples from class help prepare you for his exams (there were only 2 plus a take home final).

Very smart teacher and class does not require much effort - just be sure to turn in your homework problems and do them well. There are 2 papers due, the first is pretty easy, work hard on the second one (due during finals) - it's not impossible.
AMAZING teacher. I have never had a more helpful and caring teacher in all of undergrad. He is very approachable, always willing to help, and his lectures are very clear.
good teacher

Physics is a hard subject, but Liyanage is very good at explaining the material and I think he makes it as comprehensible as it can be.  He has fun demonstrations, which are nice breaks and are helpful to understanding the concepts.  He is nice, devoted to the subject, and is very helpful during his office hours.  Good teacher.
Liyanage is a great professor and really does everything he possibly can to keep physics interesting and help you understand it.....His demonstrations are the best!

I hate how this class was run. It's basically skimming over a bunch of random topics (beware the "intro" classes). And the curve is a nerve racking experience. BUT in terms of having the most painless experience, Liyanage is certainly the way to go. He's a great lecturer, even for the pace of the course, and he's very approachable in the office.

Good professor - does interesting demonstrations and tries to keep things interesting.  Also very cute and funny.  Has an accent but you'll get used to it after a few classes.  The exams are very very hard, though, but Professor Liyanage seemed willing to help out.

He is the better of the two professors. Reasoning: better lecturer, performs experiments in class, he's funny/cute. Just pay attention in class, and make sure your equation sheet for tests is filled. He talks kinda funny though

This man is a great teacher. Its hard, but its physics and he can mostly turn it into something understanable. There are clicker questions (so you have to go to class) and a weekly discussion with a quiz and weekly homework. If you can deal with this is isnt a bad class and a bad prof. Way better than louca (the other teacher).

Cool teacher. a little bit of accent but very funny man. Very good with demonstration and engaging lectures. Absolutely helpful and I actually learned something. As long as you follow his lectures, you can learn physics like you have never learnt before.Definitely first recommendation!!!
entertaining and good lecturer!

He's really genuine and really does try to be the best professor he can be. He really does want you to pass and you can tell he cares about each and every student in the room, even if they're in the corner and never talk which is rare for most professors. Super chill and understanding guy as well, 100% recommend.

Great professor! His notes are a genuine lifesaver if you're willing to learn from them and you can tell from his teaching that he enjoys math a lot. Don't listen to the haters who tell you that he's the worst professor for Calc II, you just need to be willing to put in some effort and you'll be fine.

Definitely a lot of work/studying, and a good bit of figuring it out yourself. Grading is mostly fair, but he does like his grade distributions where they are. Overall a good course if you're a capable learner.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is pretty funny. Great guy, loves Leibniz. Unfortunately, you'll need to be locked in 24/7.

Prof. Morkowchuk's lectures are great and her exams are pretty fair. TopHat is used, and I suggest using it to review for the exams, especially the Bringing It Together (BITs) and Looking Back Looking Ahead (LBLAs). Also, make sure to be part of the Expos! Great professor overall, and the TAs are awesome also.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: CHEM2120 is an second writing requirement ethics class, so it worked a lot differently than her other classes, but I'd definitely recommend taking it. There were no exams, just a lot of writing, which she always took time to give useful comments on. Lecture was interesting, and there was a fair amount of class participation.

People always conplain about intro chem lab 2, but I honestly loved it. Yes pre and postlabs get annoying but I found the labs fun to do and I also had a good TA (which REALLY influences your happiness in this class). Lisa pops in time to time, but never spoke to her lol. Regardless, quizzes were okay and chem lab wasn't much of an issue.

I enjoyed CHEM 1411, but it had almost everything to do with my TAs and groupmates. Prof. M posted videos on Canvas explaining assignments, which were very helpful, but you won't see her in class. The experiments can get confusing at times, so definitely put in the work, and if you're with people who contribute equally, you're set for the semester.

Loved this lab. Honestly, the only thing that got me an A- was the fact that I'm a bad test taker and didn't satisfy the 1/3 try-again quizzes. This curriculum is quiz heavy, by which I mean, if you don't pass one you're stuck with a B (unless you master everything else). Overall, loved my lab experience and the experiments weren't difficult.
CHEM 1411 is a joke. It's literally impossible to not get an A

The first thing people need to understand is that this lab is run and graded by TAs, not Morkowchuk so don't get mad at her. My TA (Paolo) was clearly uninterested and didn't want to be there, but an easy grader. Overall, the lab can be annoying because you can fail an assignment by just a little bit and how to then use a token to redo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her! She is so nice and is beyond helpful at office hours. I think her lecture style (go over the major topics and most missed from chapter compared to every tiny thing) fit the class very well. The textbook and homework are slightly annoying but overall helpful because they strongly resemble the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The exams in this class are HARD and they are partially group exams, which can be really good or really bad depending on the group you are assigned. All assignments are done on TopHat, including chapter readings, LBLA, BIT, and Expo assignments. The lecture is actually good, just does not provide help on the content that is tested on the exams.

This class is very easy because it is graded by mastery, rather than by correctness. That being said, some of the work is time consuming for only 1 credit. She sent out a weekly update for each section that was extremely helpful. Your experience in the lab and workshop depend on the TAs you have. There are unclear guidelines for the plans and labs.

Content-wise it was easy, even without taking lecture. The class is lenient on grading, since everything is essentially pass or fail. This professor makes the class pretty straightforward in terms of knowing what's due. 

Workshop was difficult though if you didn't have good TAs, since you are given little guidance on how to plan experiments

I love her.

Great experience overall.

Teammates are important, this is a group-project based class.

Do not be the one who takes a free-ride!

I loved having Prof. Morkowchuk! As someone who did IB Chem in high school, the content wasn't too difficult and much of our coursework was done online. She is extremely friendly, approachable, and easy to reach. I was lucky to have her for expo as well. All lectures are recorded so I barely showed up and still passed :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I can't grade Lisa because I never saw her during the lab. The lab itself was awful, the experiments are either boring or confusing and the grading is totally dependent on your TA. Lisa gave videos to provide background on the lab work which were never helpful. If you don't have to take this lab, don't. It sucks way too much for a 1 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Morkowchuk for 1410 Fall 2019, and she was such a good lecturer that I took her again for 1420. She's very clear with her expectations. If you've taken Chemistry before and are good at it, chances are you will do very well in her class. A little bit more work is required if you're not strong in Chemistry but she lets you know what to review.

I mean she's good but she spends way too much time on her job. You know that one teacher that made you do arts and crafts in like the 7th grade. She reminds me of that teacher. She's just over the top and its kinda annoying. Sad part is she's the second best Chem prof at UVA. Stains is EASILY #1. She's new so she's not well known but she's the best
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Morkowchuk for CHEM1411 Lab, but she also did a couple of the video lectures for CHEM1410. Those recorded lectures were on the longer side, but the readings for the lab component were very reasonable. Quizzes are mostly straightforward; not too much homework & plenty of time to do it, but some assignments can be graded somewhat harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lab was easy and straight forward. I took the physics lab online during COVID and it was absolutely hell compared to this. This lab is so much better I literally cannot express how good it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire lab was online due to COVID, which was super lame. The entire thing was run by TAs and I never even met Professor Morkowchuk. I thought the content was super boring and the labs weren't engaging or interesting at all.
The class was run by TAs- I never once had Morkowchuk pop in and say hello or anything. The grading is very harsh on Postlab assessments, but the other grades aren't awful.

I took 1610 with Professor Welch and his teaching style was very different than what I was used to I suggest Morkowchuk who teaches more traditionally as I took her for 1620. Pretty good lectures, engaging in such a large class and good notes.

Lecture can be a little boring and she covers a lot of material in a short amount of time. The tests are challenging if you do not the homework or go to office hours, and even then they can be quite hard. My advice: Get a study group early, do practice from the textbook, don't slack off. She's a nice person at heart though, kinda funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lisa is not as bad as everyone says. Her tests are easy if you study hard and know the material. She explains things well. There are also other opportunities to boost your grade besides tests such as homework, participation, and mini quizzes which are fairly easy. Final is much harder than the midterms though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful. Do not take it with her... she will ruin your grade. Take it with Columbus or Welch. She does not know how to teach and her exams are ridiculously difficult. If you want your GPA to be 0.1 points lower than what you are hoping for, then take Morkowchuk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took CHEM 1410 and 1420 from her during the summer session. It was difficult but also proved to be excellent prep for Orgo and Biochem. Grading was fair and consistent, and the professor was readily available to go over difficult topics in office hours. Put in the work and you'll be thankful during later chem courses.

This lab class was run by TAs and Lisa just planned the experiments. It may have been a 1-credit class but felt more like 3. The quizzes are unreasonably difficult and there were a couple nobody did well on due to poorly written questions. Some TAs are alright but they can be very hit or miss. Postlabs are very harshly graded and coding is a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An okay class, lectures are somewhat boring but usually concepts are fairly well explained. Textbook is engaging enough and the amount of reading per class is very reasonable. The once-a-week online assignments are quite time consuming and I'm not sure how helpful they are. The assessments are challenging because they have relatively few questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you don't have a strong background in Chemistry be careful with this class. I didn't take AP Chemistry and felt behind in the class. It's fast pace her tests are short and challenging. She also doesn't curve at all.

Awful, awful, awful. Hated this prof and the way she taught. As a student who used to enjoy chem, Lisa managed to ruin it entirely for me. I'm pretty sure she was ordered by the Dpt. to make this a weed out class- everyone I knew thought this class was atrociously taught and graded incredibly unfairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: At first, I really enjoyed this class. Morkowchuk seems fairly sweet from her lectures, and I didn't mind going until the first test. It focused so little on what we focused on in class. 30% of one of the tests was on a subject that we spend 5 minutes on in class, which was ridiculous. Overall, her tests relate nothing to what she actually teaches

Uninspiring, heartless professor who teaches like a robot and creates ruthless exams with only 25-26 points each meant to weed out those pursuing pre-med. Teaches using a scribbled note of paper she projects on the screen, and talks in a daunting, pessimistic tone as to give her students no hope in improving and enjoying chem. Avoid at all costs...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took this class during the Summer, so it was a lot of work with an exam every Friday. Professor Morkowchuk was very prepared and methodical with her lectures which made them easy to follow. She is also incredibly beautiful.

There are plenty of UVA chem professors who structure their tests and quizzes in a way that lets students demonstrate what they know. Morkowchuk isn't one of them.  Save you energy and take gen chem with a prof who is going to make chem interesting and (somewhat ) enjoyable, not a professor who designs assessments to trick you.

Lectures didn't prepare you for homework. Tests didn't reflect a most of the homework and most test questions had some twist. Tests were out of 26 points tops (miss 2 and out of A- range) and 5 question quizzes (15% of grade) had no partial credit. Never knew what to expect on tests/quizzes. Think like her and do every practice problem you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my class with Prof. Morkowchuk. She is a very caring professor and truly wants you to pass her class. Although the class is a typical pre-med course, she makes the necessary topics easy to understand and retain. The textbook is VERY important. If you want to do well on the tests, definitely reinforce the notes from class by reading
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She was enthusiastic and changed the level of the tests based on how the students did on the tests.

Alison is so lovely and funny. Hoos Connected is a fantastic program and she is so passionate about teaching facilitators-to-be about social psych and group dynamics. She is always so joyous and light-hearted. This course has a funny schedule, so you will only see her about half the semester, but she makes the schedule easy to understand.
I cannot overemphasize how compassionate and enlightening she is. So funny and such a good lecturer. I feel very well prepared for facilitating.

Although Prof. Nagel is in charge, the facilitators are the ones you get to know and meet. They are your peers at UVA, and the curriculum for Hoos Connected is nice. I made nice connections in the class, but this class did cost me from being on Deans List. It's okay though, I made countless memories in this class that I wouldn't trade.

Weekly readings that are long, but really not necessary as he explains them in detail during lecture. Writing is all graded by your TA so hope you have a lenient one. Professor Adams is a great professor and amazing speaker though, such an interesting class if you put in the effort.

Not much feedback from Prof Adams directly, almost everything graded by TAs. that said, lectures are engaging and crucial to understanding the content. Be prepared for lots of reading every week, some are worse than others, nothing unmanageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was tight-lipped and inaccessible as an advisor. Withheld information until after tuition payments were made. I dont think he had bad intentions, but I wouldnt recommend.

This was the first philosophy class I've taken, but I LOVED it. Both lecture and discussion with the TA were so useful and the readings were useful too. I 100% recommend going to office hours so you can clarify the readings because they'll be useful for the papers! As long as you participate and try, it'll be a really interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Intro to Moral and Political Philosophy was a great introductory philosophy course. I went in knowing absolutely nothing about philosophy and ended the semester having felt like I learned a lot. Dr. Adams assigned really interesting readings and the semester's writing project, midterm, and final were very fair. Would definitely reccomend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the best class and the best professor I've ever had. Philosophy is a hard subject but Dr. Adams is incredibly good at explaining things and is so accessible and kind. I want to be his best friend. This class specifically is also really interesting. TAKE HIS CLASSES
I loved her so much. Genuinely the best professor I've ever had. She cares about her students and if they are actually learning the material. She makes class interesting and is very fun overall.

This is the perfect intro class to a language. The class was very textbook centered and class discussions mirrored the book. The homework is easy and as long as you do it you will receive a good grade. Grading for tests/assignments is also very generous. As long as you study her lecture slides you will do fine.
Best SPAN professor ever: clear and funny. The course is pretty demanding, but I totally recommend taking it with her.

This was a cool course on art, literature, and migration. We wrote and read comics, we had people coming to class, and the final exam was a paper. We had to choose a work of art and a literary work. It was one of the best courses I have even taken. Prof. Bonino is awesome. This class was on Zoom, but it could be in person now.

Profesora Bonino was very accommodating and understanding of the challenges of online classes and the realities and stresses of living in a pandemic. Going into the semester, I was very stressed about this course being online but she was very reassuring and was accessible for all students who needed her. She genuinely cares for her students.

Profesora Bonino was a fenomenal teacher. She is extremely approachable and is always willing to help. She makes class discussion fun and inviting. No one in the class was afraid to participate because she was so helpful in and outside of class. The best Spanish teachers I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bonino is absolutely the best teacher I have ever had. She is funny, intelligent , and engaging. Her explanations are super clear and interesting. I have learned a whole lot in her class. She is super prepared. I definitely recommend her.
Nicole is the best Professor I have ever had. Very fun and smart. She is available outside of class and makes everything easy to understand and relaxing.

He's a kind professor who encourages many upbeat discussions in class. The class is very relaxed, and everyone jokes around. He is truly passionate about the topic and can answer pretty much anything, or is willing to go through the research to provide an answer. It is not lecture heavy, and the readings are easily digestible.

I would be extremely wary of taking any of Professor Nair's classes. He gets super behind and by the end of the semester you've got all the work that has been pushed back from the start of the semester. He also doesn't return grades on time, and is very late with them. Unless you  like writing paper on paper on paper, DO NOT take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Classical Islam and it was wonderful! He is very insightful and the lectures were interesting. There were no weekly discussion posts, or small tedious assignments. our grades are compiled from 4-5 total assignments, but aren't too bad. If you need any extensions or help with any course work, he'll definitely help you out!!

I learned a lot in this class. Professor Nair is a really intelligent, friendly guy. However, he can sometimes be long-winded in his lectures and tends to get sidetracked, which can make things a little confusing. There's quite a bit of reading assigned, but the overall workload is pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Louis Nelson is a wonderful professor. I am a STEM major who took his 3701 class for a requirement and thought it would be a bore. I was very wrong. He is an amazing and enthusiastic lecturer who is very invested in what he does. I highly recommend that anybody who is interested in ARCH or HIS or needs a requirement takes his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Nelson knows what he's talking about and is a pretty good lecturer. That being said, he structures his classes horribly, only have 4 assessments, making the midterm weigh a lot, and only have 1 grade in before the final had to be taken. Also he uses norm-reference curved grading in a subjective class which absolutely makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Seriously, jump at any opportunity to learn from or work with Professor Nelson. The way that he structures his courses is clearly masterful -- you'll learn heaps from lecture alone because this man knows how to TEACH. Be prepared for one of those rare classes that truly reminds you why educational institutions are sacred and indispensable things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's really charismatic and he's not afraid to joke around. There are very few assignments (three short papers, a midterm, and a final) so you NEED to put time into studying for them. We analyzed all sides of Thomas Jefferson and I'm glad that Nelson didn't make TJ out to be a saint. Moral of the class was that TJ was a complex hypocrite.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: HE is the best professor i have ever had

Amazing professor. Make sure to do all the reading and take notes during the lectures. The individual portion of the main group project for the class I took (ARTH 2753) was very stressful and difficult, but if you seek the right guidance and work hard in the class its possible to get an A. Great lecturer and great course!
Great Class
Great Professor!
Stone cold pedagogical excellence.

Louis is easily the best professor I've had so far at UVA (4 semesters). You can tell he's passionate about the course material and  the lectures are amazing! That being said, the readings are pretty intense (although no textbook!) and you really get out of the class what you put into it.

Professor Nelson is one of my favorite professors I have had so far in college. I am not an architecture major, but found his class engaging and his talks very interesting. He is a fair but tough grader. There was a lot of reading and writing in my class, but he gives you plenty of useful feedback on papers. He is particularly a stickler on prose.

Professor Nelson is a really interesting guy. His lectures are great - very engaging and easy to follow. It's obvious he has a true passion for what he's doing as well as an excellent understanding of it. I would really recommend his Arts&Cultures of the Slave South class with Professor McInnis. The two really teach well together!
Great lecturer.  Even if you aren't interested in the class, you will be by the end of it.  Lectures are very organized and tests are very straightforward with no tricks.
Louis Nelson is a great guy and a great teacher.  His lectures are interesting and well organized. Also, he is reeeeeeeeally hot.
Louis Nelson = AMAZING!!!! I could not have asked for better!

Professor Nelson's class was well organized, entertaining, and very interesting.  His lectures are awesome, and he tells you the exact information that you need to know.  The term paper was a challenge, but if you study hard and follow the directions on all tests, quizzes, and assignments, an A is definitely attainable.
Nelson is a great professor.  The paper is tricky, so you must be creative. DO NOT MISS LECTURE, ever. I loved this class so much that Arch. History is going to be my minor.  Take this class!

I absolutely loved this class! Professor Nelson's lectures were the easiest to pay attention to and very well organized. And he tells you exactly what he wants on tests, quizzes, and papers which is so helpful. Also, he has a great sense of humor which always helps makes things more interesting. Take this class!!!
... he's great!
really nice...well spoken  good sense of humor and sense of how to help his students. very approachable.

i definitely recommend this class...nelson is a great teacher and knows the material.  he makes the lectures really fun, and has really corny jokes.  the material is kinda hard but he tells you exactly what he is looking for. make sure you attend lectures
No Comments
Lectures became less informative towards the end of the semester. Not an easy grader but not unfair. Interesting readings.

An engaging, phenomenal lecturer. His passionate for literature is infectious, and he makes sure you have a solid understanding of works even if you didnt read all of them. Hes genuinely invested in students success. Hes also great at making class relevant and fun, often making jokes and allusions to current media. Overall, a great person.

He is so kind, he really cares about his students and their work and is actually interested in helping his students learn, which shouldn't be a novelty at a University but it is. Definitely recommend his class.

This is really great class because of the digital project, which is interesting and a great way to cushion your grade. O'Brien makes sure to give you more than enough time on even the smallest tasks. He is an expert on Samuel Johnson, so class discussions are always interesting. He's an easy grader if you follow his instructions.

O'Brien is a nice guy.  The class, however, is a topic I'm not very interested in and took it only for a requirement.  If you're interested in 18th century theater, he's your man.  However, it's quite a bore in my opinion.  I did most of the reading and took little of value away.  Forgettable, but otherwise not too bad.

Lectures are a bit boring but overall he's a nice guy who really loves this stuff! Just do the reading. one performance (not a big deal tho) Midterm is easy. two papers...he's kindof a tough grader. You learn alot though and it is pretty interesting! I reccomend him
Smart man who just doesn't lecture enough.  Class is missing out on a lot because of his teaching style--class discussion.  He has a lot more to offer than the students get.
No Comments

He's very much an old-fashioned type of professor who gives long lectures mostly from his memory--maybe not for everyone, but a really good experience in my opinion. He cares a lot about getting students to engage with the world around them and will like you if you're chatty.

I had the misfortune of having Opere for two classes this semester, and so far it has been awful. Not only are his expectations totally unclear, he clearly does not care at all about his students. Because he had to travel, he insisted that we make up a class on a Friday evening. He is also making us purchase our own tickets to a flamenco recital.

I really didn't like Opere at the beginning of the course and had a lot of trouble understanding his accent. By the end of the course, Opere became one of my favorite professors. My Spanish improved immensely, especially my accent and my ability to comprehend a fast-paced genuine Spanish accent. He's passionate and knowledgeable. Take his class!

We did a lot of reading of texts from before 1800, which is hard when you're a native speaker of Spanish, let alone someone trying to learn it. The midterm was ridiculous. None of the terms were things we'd discussed more than once.

This class had the potential to be interesting but he is quite arrogant and unhelpful, so much that it made me uninterested in it. He also likes to assign incredibly hard long and boring readings and then would call on people at random. fun. His test was a horrible way to judge our knowledge on the subject.

He is an intelligent man, but his teaching style is bogus. He assigns 70+ pp. of Renaissance Spanish a night, then cold-calls on people and expects them to know all the answers; if they don't, he gives them a '0' for the day. People sit in class nervous the entire time, praying not to get called on. I will NEVER take him again.
I cannot understand how this guy manages to teach graduate students. Bored me to death. Funny tricks to charm the crowd, no depth whatsoever. Not your usual UVA scholar. Great gut course.
By far one of the best, most inspirational teachers you'll ever have. I feel very lucky to have had class with him.

Opere is the greatest. Somehow he took a subject I thought I would hate (business Spanish) and turned it into one of my favorite and most memorable classes, incorporating personal stories, energy and cultural teaching to what could have easily been a stale class.
No Comments
He is nice.  Class is easy.  Gut course.

Great, energetic, funny professor.  Book is a little boring but he brings material to life.  Boring business letters you write each week, but he provides a good background for doing business in latin american countries. Highly reccomend the prof.

Extremely knowledgable about the business spanish curriculum and business customs in spanish speaking countries. Very good accent that prepares you for listening to and keeping up with natives. Leanient grader considering new material to most.
She wants you to do well. Participate and go to office hours! Work according to her rubrics and plans very precisely. Quizzes are hard, papers are better because they are longer term.

Prof Ogden loves the language and wants you to succeed. She is strict and has expectations that you must follow. She used specifications grading for this class which means for each project there's criteria that you have to hit, and then you'll get full credit for the assignment. Easy to do well: MUST participate and come to all classes.

Ogden is a brilliant professor who studies medieval French manuscripts and uses this class to show students the connections between medieval legends and modern ideas of heroism. She pays extraordinary care to the health and wellbeing of her students.

Ogden is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's my advisor, and I couldn't have a better one. I thought the class was going to be boring, but I was fascinated. The class discussion is sometimes less than scintillating, but the readings are interesting and the assignments make you learn a surprising amount. Excellent!

Mme. Ogden is an incredible professor! She really loves the language, she's incredibly encouraging, and she is extremely helpful. She knows the matierial is difficult but she does her best to make sure you understand every nuance. She's a really good grader too. If you're going into high-level French, take her class!!!
yes, very boring
yea, the professor is boring.
She is really nice and really knows her stuff. She's also really helpful. If you put effort into the homework and make an effort to discuss in class, you'll be fine
Easy to talk to, intersting class.  Grade hard.

She is very knowledgeable about the subject matter. She is accessible and gives a lot of help on papers if you ask for it. She does not give a lot of homework, but when she asks for writing assignments, she expects them to be well-polished. I would recommend you take this class, or with Bargach
Extremely boring, seems nervous speaking in front of class. She definitly knows what she is talking about but it is so hard to stay awake especially when there is no discussion created in class.

One of the kindest professors I have ever taken a class with. Anyone should do so if they are able, as I have learnt so much under her guidance. An absolute delight who is so passionate about her subject and always there for her students.
Marie was a very fair grader and was always willing to her students get better. She kept class as interesting as it could be for an ENWR

This class has been really great. The books we've read are interesting, and Marie is good at picking-up common themes amongst them. She is also a very fair grader and is very helpful when it comes to writing papers for the Second Writing Requirement. However, enthusiasm is a must for this class, or you will probably hate it.
Marie is a very nice, helpful person. She does not assign too much work and keeps discussions very interesting and engaging.
Marie is a really cool professor. She doesn't give a lot of work, keeps the reading reasonable, and is really nice. Usually in the English department but offered class in MESA this semester.

Super down to earth professor who always makes sure to get to know students and always shared funny/interesting personal stories. Very understanding of students' workloads. Thought it was amazing how in touch the professor was with their word choices to make sure all students were respected and through providing insight into the professional world.
Great Professor, highly recommend

Learned a lot about computer networks. I was surprised and impressed by the hands on labs. I wasn't expecting to learn real world skills, but I really enjoyed it. I also really like the course long network design project. I was able to put what I learned to use.
I knew nothing about security and I learned a ton. Labs are really well done. Best final exam ever!

This was by far my favorite class so far. I actually learned things that I put on my resume and talked about in interviews. Professor Orebaugh is was always available to help me with the labs and provide career advice. She brings such a great energy to the lectures and I love hearing her stories about all of the things she has done in industry.

I would also say the professor is Respected, Gives good feedback, has amazing lectures, and so on. It is truly a privilege to take this class with the professor as the labs are fun and applicable to the real world. Being limited in what I can put here I would say a lot more good about the professor, but overall I would say take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved the Smart Cities Enabling Sustainability course. I took it because I had previously taken Principles of Sustainability with Dr. Orebaugh and LOVED IT. She is very inspirational about the topic of sustainability. Everything she teaches in class can be related to the individual or where the individual lives.

I changed my career because of this class! I was kind of interested in sustainability, but I had no idea the impact I could have. Dr. Orebaugh is so inspirational and shows us all that we can make a difference in our own cities. Smart Cities Enabling Sustainability is a must take elective! I just wish BIS had a sustainability concentration.

I took BUS 5120 Securing the Internet of Things as an elective. I wasn't sure what to expect, but I loved this course! Dr. Orebaugh gives great lectures and didn't make the material too complicated for me to understand (like others often do!). I learned impacts, attacks, and mitigations for the IoT and cyber physical systems. Great class!

We had a course long project where the class performed like a consulting firm to create a security architecture for each of our "clients". I've never had a class like this and it was really creative and helpful to prepare me for a job in security consulting. The professor guided us through every step and provided a lot of support along the way.

I was extremely disappointed in the lack of respect Akemi has for her students. She is jaded/ gives inflexible technical explanations, once, with no real connection to printmaking history. Her comments on technique and content were unhelpful or even confrontational. She is there to answer questions, but will give minimal or redundant information.

This professor is one of the most amazing people I have ever met. Sure, if you do not work, then she won't be happy but, why are you at UVA if not to work hard and produce results? She takes time, she is understanding, she is brilliant-knows her techniques through and through. She is a shoulder to lean on and will get you through the hard times.

Do not take this class if you are a female athlete. No point in reading textbook- she doesn't understand the techniques in it. Also stay away from office hours... she had weird conversations with me about her personal life and likes to hear herself talk.

So helpful. THE BEST. the most helpful professor I have had at UVA. Do NOT pay attention to other comments about being a perfectionist, yes she likes clean borders, but when you get a certain kind of project that requires borders, any professor will want they clean, its embarrassing for you if they are not. I have had her for three semesters.
She's tough, but you'll learn tons.
Akemi is a wonderful teacher. She is fair and understanding.  She helped my a lot and I loved that we used multiple different mediums.  I loved this class and she is very nice and lots of fun.

This woman's idea of learning to draw is to spend every minute of your life drawing so that you have no option but to get good at it. She doesn't give much instruction and is very vague when she attempts to. Definitely not an easy A, and requires a huge amount of time because the work can be slow and tedious.

Strict on attendence, but if you made an effort to be there on time and didn't make excuses for lateness, she was tolerant. She was helpful with technique advice, but was really looking for the student to solve their own visual problems and over come the challenges of the medium and subject matter.  Great class.

she expects really good drawings. she has high standards. a strict grader, dont expect this art class to be a slack. Not recommended if you haven't been a good drawer before or know how to draw well already. a good teacher but i think she's too perfectionist
Very helpful and has excellent comments. Strict on attendance, but not strict in general.
No Comments
Bad teacher who doesn't teach.  Her idea of teaching is telling you to take out your supplies and start drawing.  Also, many projects are boring compared to what other Arts 161 students do.

Prof. Johannessen was the best part of this class. A great professor, super knowledgable in the topic and an overall nice guy. The class content itself was incredibly dry, and lectures were extremely fast paced, but he does post slides and recordings can be requested. Your TA will make or break your grade in this class.

Johannessen lectures in a very straight-forward way. Readings are so optional I did none of them. Getting a good TA matters for writing your memo. Prof is very kind and knowledgeable. Class can be a bit dry sometimes but not hard to get the A if you put in the work. All tests are open-note.

I took Professor Johannessen's Intro to Public Policy in Fall 2020 and he was compassionate and flexible, especially during COVID. His lectures were engaging and all of the important terminology was color-coded so note-taking was easy. The workload was somewhat heavy, but nothing out of line with similar classes at UVA.
Really nice and caring prof, especially during COVID. Very clear expectations with clear lectures with lots of examples. Definitely worth taking.

It appears opinions on Padron go either to love or hate, but here's my take. Our course code isn't available, but I took him for Quijote. Prof. Padron cares about how you think about the work. Occasionally he might tear down your argument, but he's approachable and will help you understand why. If you care about learning, he's your guy.

This professor is supposed to be an expert, but he seemed more petty than anything. He appeared to be satisfied if he thought he had managed to dismiss you or your questions. He had much greater respect for men than women. If you enjoy being treated with basic decency, do not register for any of his courses.

For any student of Spanish interested primarily in language or literature it is important to note that Professor Padrón is a respected academic in Transatlantic and Transpacific Studies which combine the methodologies of history, philosophy, and literature. If you lack an interdisciplinary background his class will be tough but very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: worst professor i have ever  had. do not take any classes with him. unfair grader and extremely unhelpful during office hours. will give you feedback and  recommendations and then grade you negatively for following those recommendations. he is excited about the topics he teaches but not worth taking any class taught by him at all.
Amazing professor-- brilliant, funny, and so passionate!
Really good professor. Makes everything interesting. He is incredibly smart and easy to relate to. Overall, Ricardo is an awesome teacher.

Ricardo Padron is one of the University's best professors - he brings the best to each class and his students respond with much of their best thinking. It is one of the only classes at UVa that is "hard and rewarding.". Also an outstanding academic and genuinely good human. The University is lucky to have this talented and hard-working professor.

wonderful teacher. very passionate about literature and knows his subject well. he's also just a hilarious person, and makes this small class very inviting. i was intimidated as a first year in this class, but sr. padron is very clear and lets the class guide discussion so i wasn't too intimidated to participate

He is very passionate about his subject, despite having taught the same short stories many, many times. He really wants you to understand the nuances of the text. 330 is required to take upper-lvel spanish classes, but he makes it fun. definitely try to get him!

He's a fantastic professor.  He's very engaging and always has time for students in office hours.  He seems to genuinely want kids to learn and his class objectives are very clear.  Take him for any class possible.

A great teacher.  He's obviously really into what he's doing, but doesn't overburden students with his enthusiasm. The class isn't the most interesting in the world, and there's not a lot of motivation to do the reading, but even without it, you'll be fine so long as you pay attention in lecture.
No Comments
No Comments

A top-notch professor: he knows the subject well and obviously likes teaching; he cares about students and takes the time to answer questions or explain concepts clearly; his lectures are interesting and informative; and he grades fairly, though you have to work for a good grade. Highly recommended!

He is very knowledgeable and welcomed all questions during class, which he answered very thoroughly. He is not accessible to students, even when extenuating circumstances exist. There were no rubrics, so overall grades did not seem to match individual assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and experienced but sometimes came off as quite cocky
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zelikow is one of my favorite professors at UVA. His lectures are amazing. Only two take-home exams. As professor Zelikow puts it: it's an easy class.

Professor Zelikow loves to answer questions, but be ready for a super long response and tangent. Overall a lot of reading and you better do it because he has daily quizzes. He is a great lecturer and knows his stuff. He has great experiences and stories to share. If you love history and foreign affairs, this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Phenomenal.

Zelikow is an absolutely phenomenal lecturer. This, mixed with the interesting subject matter of WWII, his insightful nature, and a bit of comic relief, has made him by far the best professor I've had. The catch is that there are really only two grades (both papers). However, if you have gone to class and are able to write well, you should be fine.
As long as you do the readings, this class is a breeze, but Zelikow's lectures are some of the best at UVA

Incredibly knowledgeable about the stuff he teaches. Phenomenal lecturer and in discussion (seminars). I've taken both a 15 person seminar on The Rise of Liberalism and the much larger History of American War from WWI on with him and both were amazing. It's a good amount of writing, but you don't need to memorize any tedious stuff for tests.

Zelikow is one of the most interesting professors I have had. He has served several high level positions in the government and uses his experiences in the lectures. This class requires about 100-150 pages worth of reading each class, with a weekly quiz on it. The midterm and final are both 12 page papers. The discussion section was engaging as well

He is very knowledgeable and clearly loves to teach history. The class is demanding with one 75 min lecture and then a few hours a week of watching lecture videos and then a few hours of reading. There are weekly online quizzes & class quizzes based on videos & readings. Several papers and grades depend on your TA. Exams are written to confuse you.
very smart! relatively approachable. Love the online lectures.
He is a gorgeous teacher!
He is an excellent MOOC professor: clear, suggestive and engaging
Prof Zelikow is one of the most respected authors about history and American politics. He´s class is a must, even if you are online or only in internship
Very Smart

Tests are very very tough and requires you to read or skim over all readings since that is what they are based on. I didn't have study much (or at all) for the exams because I did the readings.He is a good lecturer but lectured on things I was not interested in. I did well but would not take this again.

This is the first time Zelikow has done this class, and it's... challenging. There is a TON of reading for each class and supplementary reading quizzes. You MUST read for the two Midterms. Lectures are neither bad or good. If you're in love  with History, I suppose it wouldn't be awful, but otherwise the readings are overwhelming.

If you like history, all aspects from economics to politics, specifically in the 20th century, then this is the best class that you can take. It was very interesting and changed my perception of many key events and people in the early 20th century. There is a decent amount of reading that needs to be done, but it is easily managed.
i would never miss his class. if you like history this is where it's at.

Very good teacher. His lectures are clear and easy to follow. There can be a lot of reading each week, but it can be done. Make sure to get an enthusiastic TA. Two midterms and a final, no papers, pretty specific, but if you've done the readings and go to lecture you'll be fine.

This class is very dry and Professor Zelikow's lectures are not interesting.  The exams require you to regurgitate the opinions of Zelikow and are not open to discussion.  I would not recommend this class to anyone unless you have a lot of background knowledge and are willing to learn a lot on your own.

Extremely knowledgeable and sometimes really hilarious. His lectures are extremely well-organized and clear. A lot of reading to do, but not a lot of work in the way of papers. Tests are fairly difficult, but not unmanageable. Definitely recommended.

Professor Zelikow is a big shot on Capitol Hill and was the Executive Director of the 9/11 Commission.  He is extraordinarily intelligent and his lectures are crystal clear and exhilerating.  He respects students and dedicates ten minutes of every lecture to questions, but he is often inaccesible.
A very clear and interesting lecturer.  Lots of reading and not necessarily easy, but definitely worth taking.

he was on the 9/11 commission.  runs miller center.  get ready to read your ass off, but good lectures.  TA's are actually more arrogant than he is, which if you know him, is hard to believe.  He deserves to be, the TA's are b/c he chose them.  He is an amazing resource.  In a word, imminent.
I took his WW2 class. Extremly smart, excellent lecturer, very difficult to approach. His excellent lecturing style allows the class to be easy.
I took several of his courses over the years and he always came across as overly pleased with his own smarminess (like how he got kicked out of Japan) and an obvious political shill...
Very Intelligent, Best Professor I have had here at UVA
Not approachable at all and seems more into research than teaching
Most intelligent professor I have ever had.
Very intelligent and knowledgable. Not approachable.
No Comments
Probably the smartest professor I have ever had.
good communicator, likes to teach
very interesting, excellent lecturer

This class was fairly easy given you complete the weekly assignments. The exams are all open note and most answers can be found directly from the textbook. Lecture slides were taken straight from the textbook and can quickly become very redundant. However I highly recommend for a GPA boost with little effort.
Taking SOC1010 with Prof Polillo is one of the best choice I made last year.

He did not lecture at all.  The students ran each lecture by being divided into groups at the beginning of the semester and then being assigned weeks to present for both Monday and Wednesday for an hour and 15 minutes. Midterm assignment was unclear which resulted in a ton of low grades but he gave us a second chance to bring up those grades.

The lectures are incredibly boring and the readings are very dry. The tests are rather easy, he gives the prompt the class before and you can bring a sheet of notes to write the essay on the prompt the day of. I wouldn't take this class again but I did learn some interesting things.

I only took this class because the course description made it seem really interesting. It's basically a philosophy class though and he's a terrible teacher. Not engaging at all. Powerpoints are black text on a white background. People sign into attendance and ultimately get up and leave during the class. No tests-just papers,but he's a picky grader

Goofy and quirky, but grades based on engagement with the material and original thoughts, not necessarily accuracy. Probably wouldn't take the class again, but I did learn some interesting things in this class.

This class is one of the most boring, useless classes I've ever take. The professor attempts to make this 2000 level class harder than it needs to be by making four assignments each week that don't actually help you learn the material, but is judged solely on whether you can schedule to do them. He has an accent and rambles quickly through lecture.

This class was just okay.  I pretty much hated it at the beginning because the lecture style was unorganized and the slides were bad, but things got much, much better after the midterm.  He's a really nice guy and does want you to do well, but it's not a class I would go out of my way to recommend to anyone.

I took Economy and Society with him and it was an interesting class.He's not the most exciting lecturer especially that early in the morning, but lectures were very clear and organized and really helped with understanding the readings.Midterm was pretty easy,straight from the slides,and weekly exercises weren't too bad.Overall,I'm glad I took it.

Daniel Quinn was a great professor. For fluid mechanics, be prepared for the course to be front loaded, as in you'll have more homework the first few weeks before it tapers. It's also largely due to the learning curve of completing his assignments. The first exam will teach you how todo the rest. The final, said to be cumulative, was mostlylast ch.

Dan is an awesome dude! He's really excited about what he's teaching, which will make's fluid mechanics all the better. Homeworks are fair, and he's not opposed to helping you with them if you get a little stuck. The tests are also fair, but be prepared to study a fair amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: He is so good at teaching. I became interested in Fluid Mechanics due to so many interesting facts. He teaches enthusiastically and passionately which makes you engrossed to the subject. He is very well-behaved and respectful. Not hard to get a good grade. HWs are very educating rather than just challenging.

Course material is hardcore math by nature, but Dan does a great job making the problems and examples interesting and inspiring. Incredibly available outside of class and puts students first. Helpful balance of computer visuals/videos and old-school chalk boarding.

Lectures are well prepared and cover the essentials of fluid mechanics. Homeworks are based on lectures, but also ask you to be creative and do some research on your own. Overall, this is a worthwhile class and I highly recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was very well-structured and Professor Quinn did a wonderful job of explaining the material in a clear manner.  The homework really helped nail down the main concepts used throughout the course and was challenging and engaging. He is also accessible out of standard hours. I got way more out of the course than I expected to.
This is a class you don't want to miss, especially if Dan is around. Great well-rounded course.

As a introductory fluid course in graduate school, Dan gave a very broad picture to student like me who does not have much fluid background and did a good job about it. He is very keen in teaching and deliver the course structure in a very smooth manner so that every one can understand it.

The class lectures were well structured overall and were easy to follow. Though there were some gaps in the connecting some of the material, further discussions with the professor helped filled those gaps. The homeworks were completely manageable and forced you to think outside of the basics that  you learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best graduate professor in Mechanical/Aerospace engineering. Should to be nominated for a teacher award for this class. Clear lectures, accessible outside of class, gives homework that teaches you important concepts and challenges you, prepares you not just with the theory but also the tools (Mathematica) to apply new concepts in your research.
Dan is a very nice professor who has a lot of passion in what he is doing. I think this is a very early stage in his career in terms of teaching but he did a good job.

In class, she kinda isn't the best. (often elaborates on parts you understand, shows you something but then immediately the answer without giving you a change to think it through. small scribbly handwriting on chalk, etc.) BUT: She is VERY outgoing and very willing to help you out. Has deadlines but will give credit if your willing to work for it.

CS 1113 with professor Asma was a nightmare. This class was filled with many unnecessarily hard homeworks/classworks/tests, she didn't teach us what we needed to complete labs (TA's had to teach us), and she did not know how to lecture. Office hours are helpful and she is knowledgeable/a nice person, just a bad teacher. Extra credit helped a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Prof Asma is a really awesome professor once you get to know her. Go to office hours and she will help you with anything. Such a sweet and genuine lady!

AVOID ASMA FOR ENGR 1620! Look, she's nice one-on-one. However, that alone is not enough to make a class. Much more busywork than other 1620 sections with draconian high-school rules: no phones, mandatory attendance, no talking. Yes, she'll dock your grade. Endless group work (not hard, just way too much of it). In the end, frustrating and futile.

Dr. Q is a great professor, but she has very high standards. She provides a lot of material for you to work with and it very helpful in office hours. That said, she goes into a lot of pure math and isn't super generous with partial credit. Her lectures are awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: hard, unclear, too smart to teach.

She is really an awesome teacher. She explains everything well with a lot of details and really wants you to do well. She is really flexible with her office hours and will do whatever she can to help you out. The class itself is a lot of work but she really did a great job teaching it. you can tell she loves it.

Katie is an amazing teacher! She is great help when you go to her office hours, she is clearly very excited about her material, and I feel she does an excellent job preparing you for the exams. Try to get into her section!
No Comments
One of the greatest professors at UVa. I would recommend taking any of his classes, but sadly Fall 2012 was his last semester. His substitute, Professor Schulhofer-Wohl is rather good too.

He's had a very interesting life, working under the Nixon administration and others, and that gives a personal flare to some of his lectures which makes them engaging.  Clear and consistent.  He is very understanding; he'll let you reschedule an exam if you're too busy, provided you stick to the honor code.
BEST PROFESSOR I've had at UVA.  He is so knowledgable and really wants you to do well-doesn't try to trick you.  Do the readings, at least skim them, and go to class.  Totally worth the effort.

He-Is-A-Baller.  I love him and am going to take every class he teaches at UVA. I've already taken two. Do the readings (there are a lot, but there is always a question on the exam on a random article.)  But for the rest of the exam/material... everything is verbatim in lecture - SO GO!
Good class. If you're interested in the Middle East you should definitely take it.

Quandt is the foremost Middle Eastern scholar at Virginia and arguably one of the top minds on the subject in the country.  His expertise brings first hand accounts to lectures, which makes them worth attending.  His tests are fairly difficult but completely predictable.  One of the top teachers at UVA.

loved him and loved the class. just take it. it expands your knowledge of an area of the world the US is so involved in. Quandt knows what he is saying, he's been there, he's seen things. my favorite professor. last day of classes he gave special ME desserts to the whole lecture room!

Quandt was extremely clear in his presentations-you don't realize this until you go back through your notes-TAKE GOOD NOTES! The reading load was overwhelming, but he mainly asks about key themes and points in the readings, unless he's discussed specifics in class. Going to class is extremely helpful, since all of the ID's come from class notes.

Quandt is a great teacher. I feel like I can intelligently discuss the ME now. The class is not easy there is a ton of reading and like others have said the ID's on the test are stupid for a class where you more talk about themes. Overall I would totally recommend this class.
quandt is clear, helpful and interesting! class is hard but worth it if you're interested in the ME!
very knowledgeable and approachable, but I do not like how he includes IDs on tests- too narrow a focus on details while largely not testing on major themes and dynamics
Another one of these UVa Government Profs who likes to toot his own horn.  However, his class is really very good, but seriously, do we need to be graded on a competitive scale?
No Comments
excellent teaching

I have never hated a class more, I stopped attending lectures almost immediately because I learned nothing from Professor Pandya on top of her being so condescending and rude to people participating. I hated even studying for the class because the concepts just reminded me of her and it made me want to give up. It's not a hard class I just hated it

CORRECTION: don't know how on earth it changed my rating to a 5. should be a double 1 if possible

Her lectures and personality hinge on trying to sound smart by asking questions and leaving us to teach ourselves anything we actually want to know about trade. I have never had a worse professor or lecturer. Rude, self-absorbed, and unhelpful.

Prof needs  some public speaking training. I find that her lectures are very jargon heavy and mumble jumble, and it's hard to stay engaged because she is rambling and not making things clear most of the time. Also at the end of her sentences she doesn't speak loudly and it makes it very difficult to understand. Not a UVA quality class

yes!! I remember thinking the same. Why is she treating students as competitors? She should be educating and facilitating debate. this is a classic sign of someone not comfortable with herself. I didn't see a lot of intellectual depth. maybe she has it but i certainly did not see it in class.

Dr Pandya relies too much on her academic qualifications and isn't a flexible thinker. She can't absorb knowledge that conflicts with her preconceived notions. She often gets defensive and starts arguing with students who have a different perspective instead of engaging in a dialogue. It's very weird. These other reviews are mostly accurate

I have been told by countless industry experts that her ideas are garbage. Professor Pandya has interesting theories but sometimes her lack of experience shows. She has never really held a job outside of the college environment. She basically lectures to teenagers for a living, and is rarely invited to engage people outside of her bubble.

Her class is tolerable but not her personality. The reviews are mostly correct. She's socially awkward, cold, insecure, and petty. She has academic credentials but is not really an astute thinker. She gets threatened when students develop intelligent counterarguments to her favorite theories. Some say it's ego but I think it's insecurity.

Wow some people actually liked her? They must have sucked up to her or saved the life of her cat or something. Most found her strange and unlikeable. I breezed through the course. But I found her ego and personality to be very annoying. Just ignore it, don't get your hopes up that you will find a mentor in her or a recommendation letter

The other reviews are slightly over the top but they are not far off from the truth. She's not a friendly professor and does not manage conversations well. I can also understand the social awkwardness angle. I see that in her. At the same time, she's not batshit crazy either. Her class was just okay and you'll learn something by taking it.

These reviews are making it out to be worse than it was. While I would not take a class with Pandya again, it was not the end of the world. The readings are dense but not necessary all of the time- the study guide terms she gives are a good guide to learn the course content. She is very stingy on giving details about the exams though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She didn't seem to enjoy engaging students. I always got the impression it was a chore to her unless you had interests that aligned with hers. Maybe that's where these other reviews are talking about. The class was nothing more, nothing less than what I expected. If you wanted something more from her, I can see why you'd be disappointed.

I think it's clear that the overwhelming majority of her students thought she was odd and socially awkward. She also gets nasty if you disagree with her. I've been in large gatherings with people that knew her and they all say the same thing. Like I said, there are some students who like her but they are typically people who think exactly like her.

She was a clear and knowledgeable lecturer, though sometimes the lectures moved fast. I really enjoyed writing the essay. The only major critique I had was the lack of guidance before the first exam. I probably learned the most in this class out of all my classes. The other reviews are ridiculous. She was a perfectly sane and normal professor.

She is not very intelligent. No question. I agree that being well educated is not the same as being smart. Being intelligent requires flexibility and humility as the world changes. She may have been smart at one point in her career but she's a joke at the present moment. Everyone else agrees, except for a handful of people who think like her

She acts nice if you agree with her. If you take opposing positions her face starts to look like a demon possessed her. She is never mean openly but is subtle, but it is definitely there. Good thing she has tenure. She would win the prize for the fat girl who gets voted off the island in any other organization. That's how toxic her personality is.

villainous. The entire course is a mystery, you will not know your final grade unless you assume and calculate, i dont even know my grade on my final. She avoids answering any questions regarding the test. Her ego is through the roof. Why is she competing against her students?! Her voice is like a lullaby. If you want to sleep go to her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's the classic example of someone who is well educated but not very smart. She sticks to her viewpoints and is not capable or even interested in reexamining her views in light of new information. That's indoctrination not education. She also lacks people skills and emotional intelligence. Total weirdo. She prefers students who think like her.

Ask around about Pandya before doing any work for her or if you're trying to identify professors for letters of recommendation. Taking a class with her is okay because you're in a larger group. But she's awful 1-on-1. Very socially awkward. No ability to advise students. I really think she has psychological issues. I never met someone like this

She says some crazy stuff. When I talk to other people who don't lecture to 18 year olds for living, they tell me to ignore what Dr. Pandya says. Her ideas sound good in the isolated world of a college classroom but not outside of that. I don't think she has personality to interact with other experts so I'm not surprised.
Is it just me or did you gain a ton of weight? looks like 50 pounds at least.

She hold back in her critiques but you can tell when she's dissatisfied if she makes a odd face. Best way to describe it is as a lost beaver. She will look at you cluelessly and make the face. Ugliest face ever. It gets annoying because she's being negative without being transparent.

She has no social skills and is an unpleasant human being. Someone please send her courses on how to behave in a civilized society. I'm fairly certain she eats with her hands at restaurants. It's debatable if she showers before class
Her reputation is well deserved!!  (that's not a compliment)

She's must be the most unpopular professor ever. There's no way students would find her personality acceptable. She's better on some days than others but she's consistently an unlikeable person. I enjoyed the substance of the class but not her.
Wow, the stories about her are true! I met with her recently.
We all laughed at her after class.

haha she not all that bad. It's true that she's socially awkward, narrow minded and probably has some kind of personality disorder like others have said. But she does her job of teaching what she knows. this sounds mean but it is true. Everyone knows about it. but don't let that prevent you from taking her class if it can be relevant to you.

I always felt she was a little outdated in her thinking. She likes to discuss political economy in isolation which is not realistic in the modern world. Partly this is because I don't think she knows anything other than the small IPE literature. Take her class but make sure you supplement it with other opinions. She has a lot of critics.

Take feedback from her with a grain of salt. Consult other professors or outside experts. If you do that and just understand that she has certain pet peeves, you'll be fine in her class. If you're interested in IPE, her class has value, even with her quirky demeanor and emotional baggage.

She tried too hard to prove she was smart, which was strange because we were all undergraduates. It's like: get over yourself. She makes comments on papers for some ego trip. About half of them were just wrong. You could tell she got emotional and really wanted to make certain critiques haha. They were not geared towards helping students

She knows a lot about international political econ which is my passion. She is a little rigid and inflexible in her thinking but you can compensate for that. Just talk to other faculty and mentors for balance. She has some blind spots and doesn't know much outside of political econ, so just prepare to work around that. Work with what u got

I had a lot of problems dealing with her nasty personality and I'm not the only one. I don't think she is comfortable in her own skin. It probably has something to do with her having a narrow focus and being drowned out by IR scholars and students who have wider interests. It doesn't take a shrink to make this observation, it is very obvious.
Pandya is a weird gal. Her own colleagues do not even like her.

She said something that sounded off in class so I later discussed it with experts during a summer internship. Nearly everyone agreed what Professor Pandya said was total crap and they showed me evidence. They explained that it sounded like Panya was trying too hard to protect her favorite theories in the field. The truth can be inconvenient I guess

She has annoying habits in class and office hours. She is very hard to like as a person. Some students claim to like her, but they only tolerate her because of her niche expertise. Most students have wider interests but she isn't smart enough to think outside of her little world. She's sheltered. That's obvious right as you meet her

Has legit academic accomplishments, but she is not a sharp thinker and is not articulate. Poor interpersonal skills and doesn't really engage well with others. I got the impression she feels that she doesn't need to explain herself because she looks down on students. Not sure how much weight her work has in policy circles. my guess is very little

The feedback on assignments are basically a way for her to vent frustrations. She has certain pet peeves. She hates it when students challenge authors using evidence outside of the IPE field. Instead of engaging competing views she will try to be critical. But she does it in a way that is not useful, she makes generic statements that are abrasive.

She narrowly specializes in political economy so be aware of that going in. She gets frustrated when asked about things outside of her narrow interest. Sometimes she will lash out. HUGE sign of insecurity. Other professors are a lot more well read on the full range of IR topics. She is the odd one of the faculty who is super specialized.

I found her helpful if you put in the work. Yes, she isn't well rounded in her knowledge. She is a little too specialized. But she's willing to put in the work to help you if you also put in the work. I have seen some of the negative sides to her that others have mentioned, but I can live with that as long as the course is productive.
Is she still fat and weird?? That's all I remember about her. A lot of people used to talk about her.

Stay away!!  Seriously. She has trouble interacting with different types of students and people with different scholarly interests. The people that love her all tend to be IPE-focused students. The students who dislike her tend to be non-IPE students. That's not a coincidence. She is polarizing. She has some serious issues!

The most awkward and unfriendly professor I have experienced at UVA!! It got uncomfortable sometimes in class when she would stare at us awkwardly and try to hide her annoyance that students would dare criticize articles published by her friends. HAHA! We would all just hope time would fly by so we can gossip about it afterward.

She has no clue on certain areas of IR. There were a couple of times when we asked her some questions on an important issue, and she gave completely erroneous answers (it was clear they were made up). On other occassions she seemed hesitant and unsure of herself. She is not well-rounded. She has parochial interests. Don't expect much from her.

She is not a people-person and it shows. Be prepared to learn completely on your own. I got the impression she enjoys being harsh in her critiques of papers because it makes her feel smarter. It's one thing if her critiques were actually helpful, but they're often not. She's there to just collect a paycheck and feel smart around undergrads.
Class discussions can get stale and unpleasant because she is socially awkward. They were always rushed and limited in scope. I did not feel like I get everything I wanted to out of the class.

She sets a very different classroom tone than most other professors. Academic discussion requires an openness to new ideas and an encouraging environment that lets all opinions come out. Dr. Pandya would verbally encourage this, but her demeanor and conduct suggested the opposite. She's condescending, rude, and defensive. Avoid her at all cost!

She encourages everyone to challenge the readings but you could tell it bothers her when students criticize certain authors. She's not open to new ideas. That was the most frustrating thing about her. She also does not give useful advice. She likes to criticize without providing any practical suggestion. It doesn't help she contradicts herself!
