Professor Pandya focuses on political economy. She didn't appear knowledgeable in other areas of IR. Her lectures were decent, but she wasn't the most objective person. She had her favorite authors in the field and you could tell. She also wasn't very helpful in advising me of my career opportunities. Major disappointment.

I guess I'm one of the few who enjoyed her classes. I can see how some could dislike her. She can be too much in some ways. She's not the warmest person in the world, but you have to consider your goals. Are you looking for a friend, or someone who will provide you with knowledge?

She's "smart," but not smart. She has a narrow lens for viewing the world and was never able to show intellectual flexibility and curiosity. That's her biggest weakness. I always left meetings with her unimpressed. A more genuine and personable attitude would have helped, but only so much.

She takes pride in her students' work. But she shows it through her own way. With that said, she has a personality defect and probably is not someone who is accustomed to interacting with people or managing relationships. She's your stereotypical academic book worm with lackluster social skills.

Try talking to her about global issues outside of her favorite pol econ topics. She can barely put together a coherent sentence. I've moved on from my undergrad days. When I talk to experts in the private sector, they ask who filled me certain nonsensical ideas. Guess what my answer is, lol

She is frustrating to talk to because she doesn't take time to explain. Her answers to my questions were short and incomplete as if she enjoyed keeping students in the dark as some kind of hazing ritual. Not the most eloquent of lecturers. Stay away unless the course is required or you really love political econ!

I'm glad others are acknowledging things many of us have felt in her classes. We all talk about this. You should definitely take her class if you are interested in political economy. Just be aware that Dr. Pandya can get a little defensive and seems to take things personally if you are overly critical of her peers in the field.

She said some things in lectures that were questionable in terms of accuracy. Her lectures were kind of bland and lacked the "spark" I was expecting. She seems unknown outside of academia, so she wasn't a real help when seeking guidance on post-UVA career searches.

Her class is hit or miss. You love it or hate it. I think her teaching style is the same way. I personally enjoyed her style, but I know others had issues with it. She is an IPE specialist who isn't well versed on all political science matters. This is well known, because a lot of students who have broader interests talk about it.

Intro to Financial Accounting is *not* an easy class. However, I think Martin did a good job of explaining the material in a very digestible way. He's a really caring guy and wants you to succeed. There's definitely a lot of resources out there to help. To study, I would recommend reviewing readings and doing lots of practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: incredibly ass professor who isn't very intelleigent or a good professor. is more of an annoyance than anything

This review is for COMM1800 but Mr. Martin is a funny guy and if taking 1800, I definitely recommend taking it with him. Material is very interesting and all expectations are set day one.  Assignments are relatively easy and tests are fair (will drop questions if majority of class got it wrong) The only con is that he doesn't accept any late work.

One of the worst classes, probably followed by COM2010 also by Roger. This class was in enjoyable in every definition of the word. He lectured maybe 45 mins the entire semester. You would have a better time buying McGraw hill on your own dime.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good class and Professor Martin's end of unit reviews for Intro to Financial Accounting are super useful. Sends emails to congratulate students who significantly improve their test scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gets paid to just make the students read the textbook while doing absolutely no work. I'm sure he's a smart guy but I haven't learned a single thing from him this semester and have the same style course with him again next semester because these are requirements to get into the UVA school of Commerce.

He is an incredibly unforgiving Professor. I had three deans send him an email for my extenuating circumstances due to very serious personal issues in order to grant me an extension on the exam and assignments and he did not respect it. Instead he asked me to prioritise his class over my everything in an email and refused to grant any extensions.

This course was by far the worse one I have ever taken at UVA. I am unaware of why he even gets paid to instruct the course when in reality our teacher is the online software and textbook. This class made me reconsider why one would pay so much for a UVA education only to be taught accounting from a computer-automated program.

Online class this semester. No actual lectures- did not teach anything. Left all learning to smartbook reading and questions and did really minimal if any work himself. Did not have any leniency with bumping grades and grading scale he used makes a typical grade percentage wise a whole mark lower. Strict on this after doing no work himself
Beware of tricky homework, for they take time and practice to receive some ideal credit.

This guy is very hot if you like suede buck shoes.  Hopefully he has upgraded from the polyester pants he showed up in a freshman at the University of Kansas.  he appears to have overcome the handicap of growing up in Topeka, KS.
Very Helpful, always available

AWESOME professor! Very well prepared for class... is available to help you when you need it. Research exams are a little hard but not if you put in a some effort. Best professor Ive had at UVA until now! Oh and really funny too!!
INCREDIBLE! Without a doubt the best professor I have had at UVA. Grading is fair and he actually makes accounting enjoyable. Take this class or find a class with him!!

Awesome professor! Without a doubt one of the best accounting professors i've had. He makes you think and challenges you. Very good class. A bit time consuming expecially with hydromaint but Prof. Martin actually can make accounting fun!!
Great teacher. Very patient. Open office hours are wonderful. The only thing holding him back is Hydromaint!

Stolz is a very passionate and knowledgeable professor; I learned a lot in this class and deeply enhanced my writing skills. However, he assigns around 100+ pages of reading a week, so while attendance is not mandatory, lectures explain the readings. Stolz is kind, but he does not answer emails, nor does he put in grades in Canvas until the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unlike many English teachers, Stolz is very encouraging when students share their interpretations, even if they are not on the mark. We spent most classes slowly working through the text that was assigned for homework, which was an excellent way to learn if you didn't understand at first. He loves what he teaches and knows the material inside out.

He clearly enjoys and is passionate about the topics. There is a lot of discussion involved and he challenges the class to think about the material. All around extrememly knowledgable and conveys the information in an effective and entertaining way. The class is challenging but not hard as long as you do the reading and keep up with the themes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This isn’t a history class. It’s a political and economic theoretical class with bits of historical information. If you want to read 5+ thick books with only 4 big essays throughout the course then you’ll like this class if not then you’ll hate it. This format of teaching applies to most of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stolz is a lot more focused on political-philosophy and the relation between nation-states and capital (socialist background) than the actual history of modern Japan in his lectures. You will have to do a lot of your own reading and research outside of class to get a base understanding of what's going on. You MUST answer questions his way
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very, very, very focused on political philosophy and the nation-state form. Assignments had more to do with these philosophies than with actual history. Some assignments were rather unclear. If you want to learn more political philosophy than history, you may enjoy this course.

Not your typical approach to a history subject but if you get past trying to view it through this lens you will realize how fascinating of a lecturer professor Stolz.  Not a super difficult class but you have to do the readings - the weekly reading quizzes definitely help.

HIST 3281 (Genocide) was a genuinely interesting course. Regarding reading, I only really did the ones for the weeks that I had to do write ups for, but I would recommend doing them. Shoutout to Ethan-he was an absolutely phenomenal TA and really helped me prepare for the exams. The final is worth a bit too much IMO (40%).

took russian history w/ rossman & while there was a LOT of reading (both textbook and packet readings) it was very rewarding. not too much work outside of the reading- three 2pg papers due throughout semester which weren't too hard + midterm and final. grading was pretty lenient. lectures very fast-paced & contained a lot of info so don't skip

hist of russia since 1917 is a great class. rossman is a fantastic lecturer and very knowledgeable. lots of reading but not unmanageable. the essays are annoying but you can basically write them in one sitting. he seems grumpy when you ask questions but still answers them well. participate in section and read the class packets and u will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rossman is a great lecturer and handles this difficult subject in good taste. You don't have to read the textbook to do well but you should at least read the supplementary readings that are assigned in order to be prepared for discussion and they will show up on the midterm and final which are short answer and essay questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My first ever college course as a visiting student in Summer 2015. His material really opened my eyes & the professor was certainly knowledgeable & competent, but after attending several years of community college he seems pretty average in retrospect, don't fall behind on readings or lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Final exam is 50% final grade. Best lecturer I've ever had to date. This class makes you work for it but it's worth it; you come out of this class a more perceptive and empathetic person. The subject matter is of course extremely heavy, and was really hard emotionally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: V3ry hard grader
My favorite professor this semester.
Very into what he's teaching. His voice draws you in and you can't help but pay attention. Only 3 papers and one midterm. Very manageable.

The class was pretty easy as long as you kept up with the reading (there was kind of a lot of it, but not unmanageable). Professor Rossman is really knowledgeable and passionate about the subject and I think that both of the TA's in my class seemed really nice. They didn't grade very hard at all.

His lectures are pretty interesting. His knowledge on Russian history truly is extensive and impressive. And you really don't have to read the textbook if you attend his lectures and read the packets.

Tons and tons of reading, prepare for 90+ pages of PDF files every other night. It was a shame that the readings were so redundant. Also, your TA  grades your exams and your papers, and also participation grade. The class was worthwhile, but I would definitely not take it with a very full courseload.

this was a great class. Rossman is one of those people who you listen to and just feel yourself getting smarter. He knows a lot about the subject and the class is always interesting. I would DEFINITELY recommend it! it's worth the work
Awesome class. Great prof. Tons of reading. Go to class take good notes and you should be good for exams. You have to write several short papers. TA's are anal so watch out for them.

Prof. Rossman definately knows what he is teaching, there is no doubt about that whatsoever. However, he made this class very dull. I was a little disappointed, especially because the readings for the class were very engaging, yet he talked about the topics with no enthusiasm/passion.

Great Class. If you go to class, you dont need to read the textbook because through the review sheet and class notes, youll be fine for exams. Lectures did get a little dull later in the semester, but I learned so much about Russian history.

This class was awesome. Rossman did a great job keeping the subject from getting too depressing without losing any of its seriousness. Readings were helpful.(There is A LOT though!) TOTALLY RECOMMEND!
awesome class! rossman is extremely knowledgeable on the subject! just do the study guide.. i never opened the books at all (or saw the movies). GREAT CLASS!
This guy is awesome. Clear lecturer, gives a review sheet, and extremely knowledgable on the subject. Take this class!

Ask him to give the final review sheet out earlier, cause its an assload, you will learn about Russian History and he knows his stuff, just attend lecutre and pray to god you can write for three hours cuz that final is like woah !
you can ace this class without going to lecture or reading the books..all you have to do is memorize the study guide.

he was a very helpful professor, gave out study guides before exams and it was not entirely necessary to read the material, just go to lectures.  they are pretty interesting because he's very knowledgeable and is pretty interested in russian history and all that...
rossman knows his stuff. goes along well with powerpoints. you can still do well without attending all lectures.

Great lecturer and reall knowledgeable about the subject. His enthusiasm diminished later in the class, but still more interesting than a lot of professors. Not too harsh on grading and his sweaters in 90 degree weather kept me amused.

Very very good professor at the first half of the semester, then once we left Stalin and Khrushchev he began reading from a sheet that he prepared before class.  Became very boring and monotonous and seemed as though he stopped caring.  Good introduction to modern politics of Russia. but by the end lecture became very very tedious.
No Comments
Definitely an expert on subject. Clear, interesting, organized lectures with powerpoint outlines.
Prof. Rossman's lectures are clear and concise, and he teaches with enthusiasm and finesse.
knows his stuff, very enthusiastic about russian history, class is moderately easy if you attend class
If you are interested in Russia, this is your man, he really knows his stuff and will present more than one side of the argument.  Overall a very good teacher.

First of all I do not suggest taking math 1190 if you have not already taken pre-calc or calc!!! Professor Rolf was nice and I liked him but honestly he was disorganized, made many errors, and just seemed like he was always a mess. Also UVA does experimental grading for this class so if you are placed in “growth based grading” I suggest you drop.

Dr. Rolf is extremely knowledgeable and charismatic. He makes fun prep videos for you to watch before class to understand concepts and then goes into more detail during lecture. There are 2-3 homework assignments and 1 quiz per week, but your grade is weighted heavily in the 2 midterms and a final. Exams are difficult, so be ready to work hard.

Prof Rolf is one of the most personable and charismatic profs you will ever meet. He does not teach the way i'm used to- someone just lecturing at you while writing examples on the board. you really have to do the pre class video/web assign problems or you will not know what is happening in class. go to office hours as much as possible!!

Prof is good. The class runs on a checkpoint system which can be annoying at times just because it's difficult to not fall behind. However when you make it through, if you perform well on the checkpts the final can't hurt your grade much. From all of the checkpoints you shouldn't need to study much. They also took a long time to grade some checkpts

Overall just an ok experience. The material is not easy, especially if math is not your strong suit, and Ryals doesn't do a lot to help with that. Taught as a reversed classroom, so you watch recorded lectures outside of class and do practice with a group during class. Hw on webwork could be tough sometimes and the tests are pretty hard.

She is a lovely person, very understanding and always on time for her office hours; I know I am not the best critical thinker, but I always study hard to make up for it. Everything was fine for me until the first exam, open-note, it was nothing like the homework. If you are fast at solving new problems, I think this class might suit you well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach any of the content herself, uses "hands-on" worksheets and expects TAs (half of which don't know what they're doing) to pick up the slack for her. Takes forever to grade work and has typos in nearly every assignment, many of which change the problems themselves, resulting in an "incorrect" answer for a question you weren't asked.

There's a couple awful things about this professor, firstly: for ODE she does not teach at all. Its a "flipped classroom", but instead of providing material for us to learn with she just assigns a worksheet every class and a pre-class without any instruction on how to do it. Also, she gave an exam at 6:30pm on valentine's day, who does that???

I am a second year mech-e student and I have just started APMA 2120 with Julie Spencer. Recently they have redesigned this course to be more "hands-on" which is "better for learning", but it is not. Julie literally doesn't teach. We are all lost with 7+ hours of homework a week. And it is only the 4th week of school. I have not learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Spencer is super unorganized: consistently comes to class late, almost never comes on time, makes excuses (ADD, covid, etc). Tests are difficult (department-wide average on first test was 64%). But, she is very understanding and kind to students. She is a good person but has too much going on, and it burdens her students.

Professor Sicoli is very accommodating to his students and you can tell he is really enthusiastic about anth. Class attendance isn't mandatory, weekly discussions are. Classes can be attended on Zoom. Discussion is really easy. Material can be dense and readings are pretty heavy but if you skim them you should be fine for the take home exams!

sicoli is absolutely fantastic. took language in human evolution with him (ANTH 2415)- one of the most rewarding classes i've taken. very easy- not much reading + all lectures offered on zoom. discussion was easy & interesting. lectures made me think about things i'd never thought about before. highly recommend this class/any class taught by him.
LOVE Sicoli, such a good lecturer. ANTH 2415 Language in Human Evolution is one of the best classes I've taken here--super interesting and easy. would love to take another of his classes

Professor Sicoli was a wonderful instructor when I had him. He clearly cares very deeply about the subject of linguistic anthropology. If you're like me, you might think that subject to be too nebulous to care about, but honestly, I'm now more fascinated in language than ever, all thanks to Mark.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Sicoli had three tests and discussion sections were 28%. He offered a few extra credits and that was nice. His lectures were specific and he had good PowerPoints with them. You only use two books and they are both interesting.

Prof. Sicoli is extremely knowledgeable and a great professor. The texts in this class are pretty easy to understand and his tests are a breeze. He is also extremely caring and considerate toward the needs of his students. I learned so much from this class which I was not looking forward to at first. I highly recommend it to everyone.
She doesn't really listen, and once she decides she's right, that's the end of it. Why teach something you don't even practice?
RIP if you are in the MAT program and have to take her. Long Tuesday nights ahead.

Hands down the worst professor I have had at UVA. She is nice enough during office hours and did try to adapt the course to the online form. Still, she provides information contradictory to that given in readings and lectures. Despite teaching assessment it seems that she does not understand how it is used in real-world applications.

I have never had a worse professor in my 5 years at UVA. Preaches grading and assessment practice but doesn't follow good grading or assessment practice herself. Very subjective grader, if she doesn't like what you have to say you won't get a good grade, even if you meet all criteria on the rubric. Is not open to discussion, it's her way or the hwy

The sentiment that Santugini's ECON3010 is math-focused is absolutely correct; there is virtually no economic concepts taught other than mathematical approaches. Exams are difficult but fair, if you do all the homework/additional practice you'll be fine. Very accessible outside of class and friendly, always has extra credit opportunities.

This class is certainly hard and requires a significant amount of dedication and work. However, if you are willing to work hard, meet with TAs, go to office hours, and stay on track with assignments, you will succeed. Prof Santiguini is an amazing person and truly cares about his students and their education.

If you are not religious and you have to take this class then please pick a religion and start praying. If you are an econ major and need this then take another professor. This class is absolutely ridiculous how much work it is and how difficult the exams are. Marc is funny but does not want to help his students do well or succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Santugini's class is hard but inspiring at the same time. You have to put a lot of efforts in it (lecture quiz, homework, practice problems and tests) to earn yourself an A. However, he's also there to help when you need him. Overall, if you are a first-year who wants to take this class, get ready before the first lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If not comfortable with math, you will suffer, and please take it with Troyan or Westerfield. This course is extremely math-heavy and has more of a graphing approach. Homework and weekly quizzes are relatively difficult, you can't solve it without consulting him or TA. The exams are 8-9 FRQ questions, impossible to complete in time.

As most UVA students are aware, Marc Santugini is one of the worst professors for Intermediate Micro (ECON 3010). His exams are much more practical and challenging than other professors teaching the same course. As opposed to relying on graphs, he teaches complex formulas which must be mastered perfectly for a decent score.

If you are struggling, go to lecture and/or discussion. The class isn't difficult if you pay attention. Prof. Santugini is super nice and he is more than willing to take time outside of class to help you out!

Santugini is a very engaging lecturer, you can really tell how much he loves economics. I didn't find the course content difficult, he gives you lots of practice problems and is easy to reach outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm reviewing for ECON 4095 (Dynamic Economics with Applications) but that wasn't an option. The lectures seemed overwhelming at first, but everything was manageable. He posts the slides and recorded practice problems and has tons of office hours. Exams were all take home and a grind, but actually pretty easy As if you put the time in. So rewarding

The tests were a big portion of the grade, but they were fairly difficult. The final exam was also fairly difficult. There were a lot of tiny assignments every week, about 3 or so and you need to stay on top of them as those small assignments add up in points. He was a great lecturer and I enjoyed being in the lectures.
My homie

Santugini makes 3010 manageable. He is super organized, posting lecture slides, solutions, practice problems, and hours of additional videos. He also is super accessible, I would message him and he would always respond the same day. He cares about his students and is an expert on Econ beyond just micro. I am looking forward to take him again.

Professor Santugini is a great guy who does whatever he can to make us feel welcome in class. He didn't use a textbook, which has its benefits and drawbacks. Sometimes I had problems understanding the content and the slides didn't help me. I didn't reach out as much as I should've, which is my fault. Teams made it easy to reach out to him. 

10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take Santugini he's amazing and the kindest person ever! He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. We didn't use a textbook. You basically only learn by attending lecture, so you have to do a lot of learning outside of class. The course is very test-heavy. The first 2 midterms aren't bad, while the final is hard and worth 50%.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: > than Elzinga and Doyle. Bros elite.

You will have no idea how you did on the homework going into the exams, which is the only thing he gives you or tells you to study off. The expectation is to fail and he will curve everyone up. The class average last year was a 61 from what I understand and even lower this year.

Santugini is awesome. Very personal teacher and makes every student feel welcome. Walks up and down the lecture hall before class talking to every student. There is no textbook and everything is based on lectures so I highly recommend you go. Test heavy class. Mid terms aren't too bad, but the final is harder so prepare for it. Overall great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Santugini is nice , but don't take his class for this reason. If you're not super quick with calculus and a fast-paced learner, don't do ECON 3010 with him. Told me this class has to be one of your priorities or it won't go well. Goes super fast and gives no theoretical background, only numbers and graphs. Made me not want to be an econ major
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Santguini stands about because he actually cares about his students and he wants his students to do well (unlike many of ECON professors at UVa who couldn't care less). You have to show up to lectures and he goes over material quickly. He is passionate about ECON and it made me interested in the content as well. Test heavy

Professor Santugini is a really great guy. That being said, his course is a mess. There is no textbook, so if you fall behind in the lectures, good luck trying to catch up. The course material is almost entirely math-based and I feel like I barely learned any economic concepts whatsoever. On top of that, my TA couldn't have been less helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Santugini is awesome. He is super approachable, and his lectures go by fast. You can get as many "TA points" as possible so definitely do all of the HW because when you go past 25 it is extra credit. The first two tests are 1/2 take home, 1/2 in class, and they are easy if you pay attention. The final is hard, but the class is very fair.

Santugini understands the concepts of rigor and truly treats economics as a science -- a fun, exciting science. Classwork is beautifully objective and if you try you will do great. Take a course with Santugini!!!

Santugini is always available and his class is one of the most informative I've ever taken. If you aren't doing well in the class, reach out to him. He will do his uttermost to make sure the students who are trying to succeed will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Santugini Is an amazing professor and his excitement about econ is contagious. He is willing to do whatever it takes to help his students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Santugini is easily one of my top three Econ professors at UVA. His lectures are fun to come to and he's very approachable outside of class. If you go to his office hours, he helps a lot with some of the math, which is helpful when you haven't taken a calculus class since first year. I would highly recommend taking at least one class with him!
Pretty good lectures, good guy
Test heavy
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Santugini is such a gem. You definitely need to attend his lectures, but this isn't a negative thing. If anything, its good to know that the professor is doing the actual teaching, not the textbook (which is totally optional). He's energized in class and is so passionate about Econ. Always available outside of class!! One of UVA's best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: COME TO THE LECTURE. The class and tests are heavily based on graphs and numbers so if you find yourself a person who runs away from both, then I advise to take the class with another professor. Professor Santugini keeps several office hours and makes himself very available to all students. His TAs are also very helpful and nice
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Santugini!!! His teaching is interesting and if you attend all lectures then you will not fail. His tests are sectioned by his lectures NOT TEXTBOOK CHAPTERS. The TA's aren't that much help, but his office hours are very helpful and he really cares for his students.  The lectures aren't mandatory, but there are clicker questions.

I had such high hopes for this class because I got a 100 on his first test, but then he through a complete curveball at us for the second test. This class really should be accompanied with a set of homework problems, definitely go find practice problems for yourself because he does not give you enough. Also, most of the TAs suck.

Marc Santugini is a decent lecturer but his notes are incomprehensible. He writes on a sheet of paper which he projects onto a screen. His handwriting is messy and all over the page, so most notes taken during lectures are useless. Nice guy but not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Marc is a nice guy and all, but he does not provide adequate practice problems. What I mean by that is that the ones he does provide are not like the ones on his exams. And he never posts solutions to the problems he does provide. The only way to get the solutions is to go to his office hours or his TA. I would not take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love him

The professor is fairly easy as well as his lecture. The most important thing about him is that he teaches really slowly, by which I mean two weeks behind compared to the other lecturer who teaches with the same schedule. But the good side is that his tests are not hard at all, and if you don't skip lots of lectures, you will probably get a A-.

Marc's just a fantastic lecturer. He makes things very clear, even if he may go faster than he should at times (although he's very good at further explaining concepts during office hours). He's funny, straight to the point, doesn't waste a minute of class, prepares you VERY well for exams, and is very understanding. You definitely should take him.
Really nice and helpful, very willing to help students after or outside of class if you need help but doesn't offer many practice problems which makes studying for exams difficult.

Fantastic...no textbook, gets a bit confusing at times, but he is really nice and will answer and clarify any questions you have...he wants you to learn the stuff and do well on the exams...wish he gave more practice problems/exams, though...otherwise, great teacher

This guy is pretty cool. He gives you literally everything you need to do well in the class. He doesn't use a txtbook, but he's got all his notes and writes them ALL out on the blackboard for you to copy. A bit fast, but it's an easy class to ace if you go to classes. Didn't go for the beret this year I guess. Small group. Take the class with him!

"DUTCH KNOCKOUT" RULES!!!!!!  (For those of you who don't know what that means, it means that if you score really high on just the final exam, he will erase ALL the other bad grades of the semester and just use that single one final grade for the overall grade.)  Isn't that sweet or what!?  Thanks Mr. Santugini!  (Your ratings are up.)
"Dutch Knockout."  If Mr. Santugini gives me an "A" through this, he is the coolest professor ever.

I think Marc is a pretty great teacher. All these other guys must be jealous of his sexy French accent. Although it is a little freaky that he ALWAYS wears a beret to class. And he always eating croissants. Come on, you're in America, try a donut for a change!
He is terrible.  The only way this class could be worse is if juan carlos taught it.

Ridiculous teacher.  CHOOSE JUAN CARLOS BISSO INSTEAD OF MARC STANTUGINI!!!  marc treats this class like a toy... only 2 scanty hw assignments and 1 midterm (whats there to learn?) when theres only like 20 days left in the semester (hint: other normal classes at least use a real book...)

hmm... this french t.a. grad student, who teaches this class by himself, is hard to describe.  Truly a one-in-a-million teaching style he uses... he writes everything he says on the board.  Literally... everything.  I guess you can't ever miss a single note, sometimes a bit boring, but nonetheless, his style makes it easier to do well.

Thought this would be an introductory class. Boy was I wrong. "Go to office hours" they say. I go, she tells me all these things that I need to do that are unrealistic. She tells you mistakes are welcomed. Half of my assignments got heIIa points off because of mistakes but I thought mistakes were welcomed....??? She is nice and sometimes funny

Don't take this course 

1) class is discussion based. You won't improve when everyone knows nothing about the language but are speaking in incomplete Japanese.
2) class has insane workload. You get two homework everyday and 3 quizzes every two weeks and 3 test a semester AND a final exam except for the quizzes everything is graded harshly.

The class had to really work with her about the workload. It gets ridiculous, so often we have to let her know when we can't keep up. She is nice and open to feedback which is good, but she isn't clear on grading whatsoever. I feel like she overestimates our retention of material. Don't take unless you really love Japanese; but tbh I'm burned out.

This class gets really intense in the higher levels as well! Beware this class!!! It's extremely time-consuming and difficult. If you are not 100% serious about Japanese do not take this class. Take something easier and save your GPA. Memorize the vocabulary VERBATIM. Go to her office hours every chance you. She is very nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sato Sensei is very respective and caring. Although her class is tough and you have to work very hard to fully master Japanese, you will indeed learn more than you expected. try to be friend with her and she will give you basically everything advice you want. Sometimes the workload might be too much, but it's never impossible to be accomplished.

She sincerely care about all her students and tries to set up the class so that we're all close with each other. Expect to speak a lot (you get graded on your participation), but it's fun to interact in Japanese with your classmates. There is, however, a bit of a harsh grading scale. Prepare to practice daily and work on time consuming projects.

Sato-sensei is amazing. We came in knowing very little or nothing about the Japanese language and at the end of the semester, she had us write paragraphs using all 3 of the alphabet systems. We sat back and realized how much we had learned. So much work, but so worth it. Often I would think, why am I taking this class?? But I loved it all. :)

Best teacher I ever had. Hardest class I've ever taken. She has no idea how long her homework takes her students to complete it (hours and hours and hours). If you don't really, really love Japanese, this course isn't for you.

I had Sato-sensei since my first-year Japanese. And now she's teaching 200-level. This is a must-take course if you are interested in learning Japanese. The only thing needs to be aware of - you need to make sure you have enough time(>10 hrs/week)to devote in this class since Sato-sensei always keeps a high standard.

She's one of the best professors I've been taught by.  She's a bit (actually, very) scary at first, but once you give her a chance, you'll see she's a sweetheart.  She's readily available in her office hours and, of the four Japanese professors I had, I'd say she was the one I learned the most with.  Cheers for Sato sensei!

Satou-sensei is simply AMAZING. She is scary and harsh. You won't get an excused absence from her except when you get hospitalized. Her teaching method is really effective and she is basically in her office all the time. Don't be afraid to make mistakes or ask questions. You'll find that you love her and this class so much!

This class takes up more than half of your time every day. BUT Sato Sensee is amazing. I learnt SO MUCH from this class since it is so intense. It's a lot of fun doing the skits too. She doesn't have much sympathy and can be VERY harsh (she tends to favor certain students) so make sure she likes you!

Sato sensei is simply AMAZING. She's had years of teaching experience and she's just a great teacher, in fact she's in her office all the time-not really but you got the idea. UVa has the best Japanese language program on the east coast. Any wahoo intrested in learning Japanese should totally take the advantage.
She's the best language teacher I've ever had. She knows how to teach an introductory level language course very well. You will learn a lot in this class.

Participation is important in the class. Don't afraid to make mistakes, if you speak up, you will get the grade. she is a little bit scary in the class but really nice and helpful during her office hour. Fun class but required hard work!

Sato sensei is awesome.  She looks very serious when expressionless, but her smiles are warm and brilliant.  This class requires a lot of work.  However, as long as you try hard, you'll succeed.  The skits are always hilarious!

Personally, I found her *very* intimidating at first, but she sincerely wants to help you learn.  There is at *least* 1.5 hours of outside work a day if you want to be prepared.  A very structured schedule, which helps.  My most challenging class by far, but I enjoy it a lot and find it very interesting, which makes it worth the effort.

Sato-sensei teaches very well, but is a little scary. The class takes a lot of work, 10+ hours a week, but it is worthwhile. As long as you do the homework and participate in class, you'll get a pretty good grade.

Follows a strick and thorough schedule, so you must make sure not to fall behind.  You will learn a lot of material, but this leads to a greater amount of outside class studying than other language classes might.  Be sure to do all work and review every day.  Don't let Sato Sensei scare you, she truly wants to help you learn.

Strict and exact. However, she's also a very effective teacher who'll make sure that you'll grasp the material. The drills in class are very fast-paced. One should definitely at least review the material for the day before each class. This is a demanding class; be prepared to work for your grades.

Very fast paced class, lots of worksheets and outside class studying and work. However, very good teacher, very willing to meet with students if necessary. Enjoyable and efficient teacher, if just a little scary at times.
Fast-paced, though well-structured.  Expect plenty of work outside of class.  Helpful in a one-on-one setting.
3 Total Grades --> All EXAMS. He's a nice professor, but unfortunately a senile old man who gives conflicting information which is tough when the calls is all exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Two recommendations for success in this challenging class: 1) Attend every lecture and take good notes. 2) Recruit three or four fellow students to form a study/exam review group. Do this before the first exam! I only did this for the subsequent exams, and my first exam sunk my grade. We all take notes differently, and comparing them is invaluable.

Absolutely phenomenal lectures. He's a great storyteller and makes all the topics he covers surprisingly accessible. Get ready to be really stressed about his three exams, but it's worth it for the lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't go to every class you'll be in a pretty tough spot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Mr. Thomas. He is the greatest teacher of all time. I never went to class, and he would send me recordings of his lectures. He was always concerned with our well-being. I highly recommend this easy, fun, and useful.

I took American Economic History with him during Fall 2022 and I will say I didn't feel prepared enough for the class. This professor really knows his history but THIS IS A HISTORY CLASS. I am a double Econ major and I took this class seing Econ 2060, but you only need to know supply and demand curves for this course. Take if you like history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Thomas is a REALLY great lecturer and his class was very interesting. However, taking this class as a first year who only had some interest in American Economic History was a huge mistake. His tests are incredibly difficult and can cover a huge amount of material, so you never know what is on them. It is really challenging to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is more of a history class than an economics class, though Mr. Thomas is well versed in both. There are four exams, but the third exam and the final are taken back-to-back during the final exam period. There is quite a bit of reading, and skipping lectures is not advised. Exams are tough and strictly graded, but the lectures are fascinating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas gives the greatest lectures of any professor I've ever had. The entire class is graded by three exams and a lot is covered in the lectures so you don't want to miss a single one. Tough class with a ton of reading but the professor makes all of it worth it. Can't recommend this class enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in a class that should have put even his colleagues to sleep. Prof. Thomas was interesting and had good humor in his lectures. However, the entire grade for the class is based on written exams that he grades somewhat harshly. Don't expect an A or A-plus without a LOT of work- my B+ cost me lots of reading and note-taking.

DO NOT take this class if you do not have to. The whole grade is based off of just 3 exams and the final is worth 50% of your grade. The TAs grade rather harshly as well. If you want to do well in this class it will require A LOT of time each, and that is time that you will probably end up using for more important classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thomas is a very approachable professor and his lectures are quite interesting. However, he has no power points, dose not record lectures, and bases your grade only on THREE tests, with a final worth 50%. The amount of reading is immense and the textbook is REQUIRED. Grading criteria is tough and is very subjective to the grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Thomas is a really good lecturer/story teller and this was probably one of my favorite classes this semester. That being said, there were a few issues: 1) Our entire grade is based off of 3 tests 2) You have to do A LOT of reading 3) He didn't give us any info on the final until one week before 4) this is def a history course, not an econ one
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at UVA. Incredibly intelligent and guides discussion well. Very well respected. Has a wonderful sense of humor and interacts with students on a personal level. I was comfortable talking to Professor Thomas and considered him as close to a friend as any professor I've had.
Amazing lecturer and super interesting class though the he grades the tests extremely hard.  Certainly must do the outside readings extremely in detail if you want a good grade on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer.  Class is challenging, but if you pay attention in class, understand the grading criteria and study your notes you can do well. I would not take this class to fill requirements because only a genuine interest and analytic mind will allow you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really not a hard class at all except for the fact that if you aren't interested in history it will absolutely lull you to sleep. If you are able to pay attention for 50 minutes and summarize the main points of what he says you'll easily get a high mark in his class. I personally found it impossible to pay attention to the subject and still got a B

Mark Thomas is a fantastic lecturer. He is very passionate about economic history and gives dynamic lectures featuring both in depth historical analysis and story telling to put the information in context. You need to pay close attention in lecture to do well but I enjoyed his lectures immensely so that was never an issue.

Mark Thomas is a great lecturer that you can tell really cares about the subject. However, the tests were incredibly difficult, and graded harshly. Definitely not a class to take if you want to save, keep, or improve your GPA.
Way too hard in my opinion.  I wouldn't recommend unless you really have a love for history and plan on majoring in it.  My main problem was just how tough the  grading was for the tests.
I cannot recommend this class highly enough. Mark Thomas is absolutely fantastic; a very notes-intensive course that requires a lot of reading. I looked forward to his lectures every other day.
American Economic History- very interesting course, sparked my interest in economics. Mark Thomas is a great professor, good sense of humor too, funny.

Each lecture is like a story. Mr. Thomas is a great lecturer and is also extremely helpful in office hours. He cares about his students, and will remember your name! Definitely take History of the U.S. Economy.
An excellent lecturer. I learned so much from every class. The tests were difficult and you really had to study.
Best lecturer at UVA.

I took History of U.S. Economy, found the class very interesting and Mark was very helpful. If I go history major he'll be one of the main reasons why. Go to his office hours, for clarification and just to get to know him cuz he is a nice guy and very cool. The class is not easy- reading is important and grading is tough- but its worthwhile.
bearded wonder
Mr Thomas is a great professor, definitely not an easy A class but completely worth it. Just pay attention in lecture and you'll do fine.

Mr Thomas is a great teacher, very clear and you feel like you're listening to a story. The readings are VERY IMPORTANT and there is lots of reading. He's very kind, and wants his students to do well. Once you're introduced (I ran into him at the mall) he never forgets you. It's not an easy class but it's a good class.

He is a great teacher. Very knowledgeable and friendly. He knew a lot about Australia and  really encouraged the students to want to learn more. Very cool, approachable, and disarming. Also, he has a great beard.

Really great instructor! Very entertaining, drew diagrams and gave funny stories a very interactive professor. I learned alot in his class, i hadn't taken an American econ/history and Prof. Thomas really made the facts still in your brain. This is a class that I would take a second time if given the opportunty

Mark Thomas is hilarious, an awesome guy, leads discussion well. Sometimes class is awesome other times it's so boring. there's a lot of reading, but you soon figure out you can get away without doing it or at least not all of it.

This class is hard.  He has a roundabout way of lecturing where he will give a theory, explain it in detail, and then tell you it's wrong.  He runs past 50 min every day and his tests are all essay.  Tough class but very interesting.

Really good, clear lecturer. Plus, British accent makes it more fun to listen to. I didn't think I'd be interested in this class but I was. Don't even both buying the textbook it's useless. Just go to lecture and take notes and you'll be fine.

I took this class during the Spring '06 semester.  I really liked the professor and his lectures, but found the subject very dry.  Reading the material is a MUST, but it is also dry.  It was an ok class overall, but can be tough (i.e. don't take it if you're looking to bump up your gpa).
This is not a class I recommend. The class is really hard and not interesting.

I was really interested in this class at first, but professor Thomas did nothing to maintain that interest.  I was very disappointed in this class.  He was more boring than I expected, he always ran over the time limit, and the exams were much too hard and didn't effectively test what we knew.  He tested us on nitpicky details.

I'm not saying there was never a dull moment, but Mr. Thomas is a great lecturer and you are gauranteed to learn a great deal in this class. IT IS A TOUGH CLASS, but if you are interested in history and or economics it is entirely worth it. Exams are mostly essays. Would reccomend taking ECON 201 first or at the same time, will help you!

GREAT CLASS!  Definitely not easy.  It lets you see how the principles you learn in Econ 201 apply to American history - it might sound dull, but he's a GREAT lecuturer and will keep you interested 90% of the time.  Don't expect an A, but expect to learn A LOT.

professor thomas is absolutely brilliant.  he manages to make his lectures interesting most of the time, and all in all he is awesome.  this is a good class to take to complement econ 201 (which is all theory) because this class is about application of econ.  HOWEVER, it is not easy to get an A in this class, so dont expect one.  definitely READ!

HIUS/ECON 206- I was really looking forward to taking this class and it started out well, but I lost interest. The  material is boring and he would sometimes drag on.  He was never on time and always ran over the time limit.  The tests are hard but do the readings and attend lecture and you should do well.
Australia USEM not really what I expected. Funny guy who had a good sense of humor. Class tended to get boring (2 hours is just too long). Lots of reading that tends to get repetitive quickly.

seemed to have a hidden agenda.  summer in oxford program seemed to have some mysterious importance to him.  did not seem to be very open-minded and did not encourage independent thought, critical thinking.

His usem about Australia was sometimes interesting, sometimes not . . . there was a lot of reading.  He's a great guy, I really liked him, and he led discussion well.  I definitely feel like I know more about Australia, but it wasn't always the most enjoyable class.  Cool professor though.
amazing lectures. highly knowledgable and very personable as well.  highly recommended.
Really great lecturer, almost made me care about the subject. Tests are kind of hard, make sure you do the readings and attend lectures and you should be ok.

Take notes on everything in class because that's what the tests (all built around an in-class essay) are on. You'll need to read the course packet, but the book is absolutely useless. Thomas is a great teacher, but the subject matter can get dry. Still, it's a fairly easy class that doesn't require writing any papers.
Great Great Class

Move over Elzinga, Mark Thomas should take the title of "great econ lecturer." He presents the imformation (topic is similar to AP US history) in such an interesting way that you enjoy going to lecture. You need to study for the tests that are essay/short answer and require thorough reading of the material.  Not too hard but not too easy.
Awesome.
this guy is very interesting and very likable.  this australia class was two hours long at the end of the day every week but he still managed to keep us engaged.

Prof. Thomas is always enthusiastic; the lectures are intense. There's WAY too much reading, so I mainly studied my notes. Going to class is very important. Colonial economies & the 1800s are pretty boring, but it picks up.

Excellent Lecturer, probably the most under-rated at UVa. Very engaging lectures, well organized, if a little too long for the syllabus. (For Econ 206) In general, very apporachable, and extremely eccentric
No Comments

Although she is highly educated and respected, I would not recommend this class to anyone. The lectures are boring and she is no help. You will most likely receive more help from the TA. She's also a very tough grader. You pretty much have to get all the questions on the multiple choice part of the exams right in order to get a passing score.

This class is a wonderful opportunity to learn about what economists actually do: in class you discuss real-world problems and look at leading economists' research on the topic (students not responsible for technical content).  Turner is a very good economist and a compelling teacher.  Not difficult.
Pretty easy for a 300-econ. Turner's expectations are pretty clear, material is fairly interesting. But why is there a discussion for this class? My TA sucks, discussion is worthless
very nice

Horribly boring class, but there are a few redeeming topics.  The articles are completely useless.  Turner is very intelligent, but just really boring.  Tests aren't hard per se, but require a fair amount of BS.

Good class. There's no textbook, and the readings are numerous, but you can get by just reading the abstracts. Attending class is important; she also makes the PPT slides available online, which is crucial. She's always enthusiastic and helpful.
Boring, very very boring.

This class is extremely difficult and will take up the majority of your time. STRICT GRADING. She likes to say there is no final exam, but fails to mention that the last week is only quizzes and tests, which is so much more work than a 3-hour final. She is nice, but expects this class to be your number one priority, and WILL call on you. 0/10.

This professor is awesome, a little tough at times, but actually made me engaged in the class. After a semester of this class I am able to decipher Japanese relatively easily with no prior experience at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Marshall-sensei is super energetic and caring. Right from the first day, she made everyone feel welcome. Classes are MTWThF and hw is due every night. This can get overwhelming if you can't keep track of everything, so I definitely recommend looking at collab at least twice every day. Overall, this class is an amazing intro to Japanese.

Marshall sensei is an incredible professor. If there is any way for her to help you understand the material more easily, she will do it. Tests are hard, but there are opportunities to improve your grade. She goes above and beyond for her students, her feedback is detailed, and she is extremely organized. Easily one of the best professors at UVA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Marshall Sensei is one of the best professors I've ever had at UVA. She is genuinely so caring, and wants to see students succeed. This is reflected in the way the class is graded, it's heavily participation and homework based. However, if you don't put in effort in the beginning and fall behind, your grade will suffer. Don't skip class, either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was insanely hard in amount of work. I had almost no time to do any other homework around this, especially since it was 5 days a week. Not for the faint of heart or the inexperienced!

She is a great teacher. Her class is a lot of work, and you will have to spend some hours on it per day, but you learn a lot in the process. If you need help go to her office hours and she will help you with anything you need. She might seem intimidating but she is really nice once you get to know her.

Marhall-sensei is fair, funny and a very effective professor.  She intimidates me greatly, but is helpful in office hours. I was very relieved to find out that she makes all of the red marks on everyone's papers and not just mine.  I enjoyed that there were a lot of grades in the class and it wasn't solely weighted upon tests.  Better than Sato.
SHE IS NICE AND FUNNY

Marshall-Sensei is a really good teacher, but scary sometimes. Compared to the other language teachers, she's the best and the least scary, but she's really hard core about attendance and turning things in on time. Unfortunately, she's good at weeding people out of the Japanese program that are in it just for a lang. req. Super Fun projects though!

Tough, but fair.  She's good at explaining concepts and the "why" behind the labrynthine grammar of the Japanese language.  Her classes will eat your life and your brain, though, so you probably won't do well unless you're *really* interested in Japanese.
You have to get used to her at first, but after u get to know her, shes real nice and helpful and very fair. she challenges you and helps you and really wants u to get better :)
No Comments

Such an interesting guy, passionate about what he's teaching & not afraid to share his opinions/get real which makes class so much more engaging. Both midterm & final were multiple choice and the final was non-cumulative (because he asked what we'd prefer). Definitely come to class right before an exam because he basically gives all the answers.

I've been in university for 6 years and in all my 6 years I've never taken the time out of my day to rate a professor. This is a special case. Baris Unlu is the best professor I've ever had, hands down. He cares about his work, wants to see you succeed, and is the clearest example of passion in education.

Professor Unlu is awesome. He is one of those people who is really invested in teaching you in order to help you create a different perspective on the world and to help you reach your personal goals, rather than just teaching you information for the sake of an exam. You can tell that he genuinely cares about the education of his students.

Alright professor. Most learning came from books and not the lectures. Professor is nice and does want you to get a good grade in his class, however I believe his lectures could be better paced as it often felt like there was no time to take notes as we went one slide to the other. Provides good resources on canvas too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not that big into physics, especially E&M, but Chatterjee is the man to take if you're going through PHYS 2415. Pretty funny guy and cares a lot about his students. He repeats over and over that everything is going to be fine, even when people are struggling a bit (a lot) in the course. Everything turned out fine in the end - surprisingly got an A.

I really enjoyed taking this class with Prof. Chatterjee. Yes, the lectures in Physics 2 can be very information heavy but Dr. Chatterjee is very accessible outside of class and is very devoted to making sure his students understand concepts both within and outside of class.

Gennady is not for the weak. If you are weaker in abstract math, I would consider a different professor. However, if you want to be challenged and learn on a deep level (as good mathematicians should) then he is always readily available to discuss advanced topics and get help from.

I LOVE gennady as a person, extremely charismatic and understanding. However, the assignments and approach to teaching calc 3 skills was extremely confusing. His lectures were always messy, using examples we never finish. Open homework assignments take almost 5 hours to complete and his tests... so hard. Would be wary of this class.

Gennady is really smart. He's also quite funny; there were a few moments where he cracked a joke that made me laugh. That being said, though, Gennady is not a great teacher. This class is going to take up your time more than anything else. This class alone accounted for more than half of my total homework. And that final, jesus. Hardest test ever.

Gennady is the nicest & worst math teacher I have ever had. Although he is smart he is also over qualitied for his position teaching calc 3 and is hard to understand. If you have taken mulitvariable before it is still confusing. His only grades are tests and homework and his homework are unsolvable without office hours. Do not take this class
Not my favorite

class is easy if you are ok at math (aka parsing things out.) It's a math class... She's actually a good professor, I don't know why the idiot above wrote that. She shows all the steps to solutions, aka she shows ya math. Idk how much more you're going to ask for a math teacher. Only thing that was annoying is that the class is mandatory attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst math instructor I have ever had in my entire life. I had to attend the same classes taught my another professor in order to understand what was going on. Not accommodating, not caring, and just interacting with her is a headache. Should not be a professor at UVA. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, find a different professor.

Professor Uzzell is one of the most troublesome individuals I have encountered in my academic career. Not only does she give harsh, critical feedback, but purely on an ideological basis rather than a structured one. I believe there is a fine line between constructive criticism and ad hominem, baseless attacks. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. Professor Uzzell is a fantastic lecturer who will make you will leave each class feeling smarter than when you entered. BY FAR the best professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Uzzell made an introductory course miserable and difficult. Her expectations surpassed what was expected fo typical introductory students to the subject, which often left students disinterested and unmotivated. Very displeased with the way this course was taught.

For context, POL 100 is an intro-level government class. Professor Uzzell was an incredibly hard grader and expected students to write papers as if they had her level of understanding. She does give substantial comments on rough drafts but they are harsh and often condescending. Coursework is heavy. Not pleased with my decision to take this class.

Professor Uzzell is great. You read a ton for each class but the discussions are incredibly valuable. The class size is small which allows for you to really get to know her and the rest of your classmates.

Dr. Uzzell is an great teacher. She had a way of making a potentially boring subject ("American Political Tradition") very interesting and engaging through in-class discussion and activities. She  is an excellent lecturer, and is very helpful with essay comments and feedback. You WILL have to do all the readings, or risk making a fool of yourself.

A very interesting class that requires a lot of thought and a fair bit of reading. I got a lot out of it--it aided in my understanding American Politics and I thought the paper topics provoked thought. She's harsh on papers, so support your argument, and reading is pretty crucial for the actual discussion.

Notes are extremely clear, very organized. She does have an accent, but she writes everything on the board, so it shouldn't be a problem. Quizzes are taken straight from practice problems online, and midterms/the final are definitely harder, but not insane.

Do not be fooled. Her notes are super organized and she is always willing to help. If you look at the online questions she posts then you are set to ace the quizzes. However, most of your grade depends on her midterms and final, which is dead-on difficult to the borderline impossible. If you care about your grade, don't take this class.
She definitely knows what she is doing. She is very nice and can explain the subject very well.

Good class and great professor. Econ is a dry topic but she actually makes it quite interesting (to me). Midterms/finals are hard, but is not impossible. She is a fair and to an extent, lenient grader. Take her class.
Interesting, funny, and cute!

I had her in summer school and I am glad she was the instructor. She is extremely good at explaining things and always willing to help you if you have problems. She tries to make the class interesting by showing movies, giving real life examples etc. Her exams are challenging, but if you study the lecture notes you will be fine. She is also hot!
Smelled bad.
Super knowledgeable and willing to help students

A prime example of what happens when you make a research professor teach. He's got the enthusiasm, he's got the knowledge, but he really doesn't have time to prepare for the class and it's rather difficult to get space in the office hours. The TAs are of limited use since they refer to Venkat for most questions about the projects. A huge struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard and confusing

This was a wonderful class contrary to what I've heard from last year. I came in not wanting to learn about the subject, but ended up enjoying this class a lot. Venkat is very knowledgeable and his enthusiasm about the subject really shows in lectures. The cache attacks project were very interesting. Exams are on the tough side but not too bad.
If you could only read course forums or surf reddit about this dude on r/UVA

Professor Urbanovich is an experienced man from Soviet Georgia, and many provocative topics can be discussed during the class PLCP2600. The reading is informative and relatively easy for students from other majors.

Is this guy a professor or a bard? Took this course way back in Summer 2015, you sit down, & he just starts telling you stories from his life. Wanna explain late stage USSR corruption? Story where he was annoyed at a loud person in a Baltic state restaurant who the establishment wouldn't shush because they were literal mafia. A gem of a course.
TOUGH GRADER!!!! BEWARE!!!! you have been warned so my job here is done.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: YURI IS THE BEST! If you have the chance to take one of his classes, do it. He's such a kind, sweet man and as long as you at least try, you won't come out with anything lower than a B+. Show up to office hours and you'll get bonus points. There are few assignments but they're graded easily. Guaranteed you'll learn a lot AND enjoy the class.

I love this professor! Class readings are completely optional. As a professor, he tends to have very long lectures instead of discussions but he obviously very much cares about what he is teaching! You won't get a good grade on the exam but everyone comes out of the course with an A. He is one of those professors who doesn't care about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Fascinating man and interesting class.  His lectures can get somewhat rambling and dull at points but he really is a fascinating man to listen to, especially near the end of the course when he teaches about the fall of the USSR by telling stories about his time growing up and living there.  Lots of outside reading that is kinda dull
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took The Rise and Fall of the  Soviet Union. Professor Urbanovich's lectures are fascinating. He has amazing stories about his life in the USSR. Readings can be very long and boring but his lectures make up for it. As long as you participate, you should get an A. Very easy grader. He cares more about how much you learn than grades. Great class!

He makes the lectures interesting. Prepare your presentationgroup work EARNESTLY and don't miss class (you can miss one but no more than two). Readings are interesting but sometimes gets overwhelming.
Great Professor, very helpful, and very knowledge, Highly recommended!! He is a great lecturer, very clear, and very passionate about the course.

Fantastic Professor! Book readings aren't always necessary, but definitely do the collab readings. Tests are easy if you study and the final isn't bad either. Urbanovich wants his students to understand and entertains any questions, anytime. He is great!
Great professor. I recommend to anyone interested in russian history.

He is the best professor in UVA.  He genuinely wants his students to understand the material.  I liked him so much, i took another class with him the next semester.  TAKE THIS CLASS!  He is so nice!  No need to read the material. Go to class, pay attention and def. take notes.

1 midterm, 1 final, and participation grade. Yuri gives a crystal clear image of Soviet history. Exams are fair as it consists of mostly core material that we talked about in class or read in the exam; only a few obscure facts are asked. Most important is still to note every single word Yuri says in class!

Professor Urbanovich is an extremely knowledgeable and caring professor.  This class really helped me understand the Soviet and post-Soviet periods of history.  Not only that, but I looked forward to the class each week because Prof Urbanovich was funny and engaging.  I would definitely take another course from Prof Urbanovich!

Ok, he's a nice guy, but beware: this is not a typical USEM.  It is a lecture, not a discussion.  If it is a discussion he tends to take over and suddenly we (the class) were wrong about something.  He's really opinionated and assigns an unearthly amount of reading.  Class was mostly made fun by Facebooking each other about the funny things he says

Prof. Urbanovich has a wonderful lecturing style, telling stories about Russian politics and the history of foreign policy in the USSR and Russia.  He gives quizzes and tests requiring you know dates and have read the chapters assigned.  He is a very fair professor.
Great professor, easy to understand and takes a real interest in his students.

This class is amazing-- even if it is really early in the morning. Urbanovich is a great professor and lectures are very interesting. If you have any interest in the USSR, or just foreign affairs in general, take this class!

My friends, I would say that Yuri is one of UVA's finest assets. His classes are worth it for the anecdotes alone. Tests are manageable, and if you want to understand what life in the Soviet Union was really like, he's your man.

OMG!!! I can honnestly say that he is the best prof. teaching at UVa right now.  I had 0 interest in Soviet/Post-soviet history and politics before taking his class.  Mind you it was J-term and we had to be in class for 5 hours a day, yet I looked forward to hearing him talk everyday.  He is highly knowledgeable, VERY engaging, caring, kind, funny.

A self-motivated class -- students have to do the reading and participate, or they won't get anything out of it. Readings are excellent, lectures are long and sometimes unfocused. Very little class participation most of the time -- "seminar" becomes 2.5-hour lecture.
This is a great class to take- just not on Monday mornings for 2 1/2 hours. Lectures can go on, but the material is easy

Urbanovich is the man. I had no clue about Soviet politics/Russian history before taking his class and now feel like I can have an informed conversation about anything to do with Russia. He was a weapons control diplomat before becoming a professor so he has incredible stories and class always fly by. TAKE IT

This was a jterm class, so inevitably there was a different feel (i.e. stress-wise); however, prof. Urbanovich is very fair, funny and will make 5 hours of class worthwhile. I had no interest in his subject prior to this class, but i am considering the concentration in FA for this region now. Great class, very knowledgeable!!!

Yuri is one of the best professors I've had at uva.  His adorable accent and good looks along with his lectures, film screenings, helpfulness, and eastern europe experiences makes this class enjoyable.  He makes you want to go to class and learn.  In the end, he wants Americans to be familiar with russia and eastern europe!
Great professor, take this class if you have any interest in the rise and fall of the Soviet Union.
No Comments

this man really knows his stuff. his lectures are always engaging and his personal anecdotes are always amusing. having studied (and taught) international relations at a prestigious Moscow university, there's no better professor to take.

HE IS AMAZING. he is very cute the way your grandpa is. has the best accent ever. laughs a lot. anectodes from Russia where he studied during the Soviet regime. very helpful and outreaching. even though it had been 2 years since I've taken his class it is the first techer i'm rating! take his class.
If you're interested in learning anything about Russia or the Soviet Union don't pass up a chance to take his class!  He is AMAZING!
He's the man, coolest prof in the university, always nice, funny, smart, and interesting.  Big ups to the juggernaut from Georgia.

He's adorable!  Prof. Urbanovich is an extremely interesting and engaging speaker, and he has first-hand knowledge of many of the most interesting times in Russian history.  You will learn a lot from him, particularly through his own anecdotes.  Take this class for an enlightening experience!

Great class, great teacher who really know swhat he's talking about. He goes out of your way to help you and make sure everyone knows what's going on. Cutest russian man with the cutest accent. One of the best professors I've had.
easy class, quizzes are graded easily (10/10 = A+, 9/10 = A, 8/10 = A-, etc), movie review & essay are easy too.  Readings are sometimes dry.
It was an okay usem.  Quizzes are harder than I expected but he graded relatively easily.  He's a very nice man with a great accent.
fun to listen to. very engaging and helpful. very enlightening. one of my favorites. I highly recommend him to anyone that doesnt know much about russia
Awesome class. Yuri is a ****.
Great class, although the room gets hot.  Interesting, powerful speaker.  Textbook is wordy, but he is interesting and good.
Take this class, Yuri has a great understanding of USSR and Russian politics and has great anecdotes, plus a great Russian accent.

Dr. Urbanovich is the best professor at UVA without tenure.  If you want to learn Russian/Soviet politics from an insider's perspective, you MUST take one of his courses.  The work wasn't too difficult, and if you stay engaged in the class, you will be rewarded.
cant go wrong with this class.  he goes the extra mile, constantly has extra review sessions and reaches out to interested students.  very interesting material as well.  great professor
He's very nice and likes lots of discussion. Sometimes lecturing can get slow, though. Almost no work and relatively easy tests. But it's still good if he knows you and likes you!
Great prof! Really knows what he is talking about but goes off at a tangent A LOT and cannot stay on schedule
Likeable teacher, definitely a harder USEM though.
No Comments
No Comments
Him talking about his own like experiences was always more interesting class

Class is boring, it's SO theoretical - you're just studying theories and methods of thinking about media the whole time. Half of classes were on Zoom, easy if your TA is an easy grader. Exams are take home essays with no time limit. Not hard to get an A, just made me not want to study media studies anymore. Must show up to all discussions.

If you like straightforward answers, this isn't the class for you. Siva takes a nuanced approach to the topics which I appreciated. Though the multiple choice exams are subjective, they encourage critical thinking. The extra credit from completing all the in-class essays really helped my grade. Readings were boring but he's an amazing lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures
