This class is very hard to get a good grade in, and I don't think I'd recommend it to non-psych majors. I took it in my first semester of my first year and it was honestly a mistake. HOWEVER! I've got to admitI really liked this class. I really learned a lot from Williams, and though he's tough on your grade, he's worth considering.

DO NOT take this class, unless you absolutely have to. I worked as hard as I possibly could and I did not even come close to doing well in this class. Not helpful, Doesn't care about your grade. Only talks about sections of the brain and the tests are basically straight memorization. Not a conceptual class in any way
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Williams as a person, but he was the toughest professor I have ever had. He is hilarious, kind, caring, and his lectures are interesting. However, he packs so much information into every single lecture that if you look away for even a second its like you're now a couple slides behind. SO MUCH MEMORIZATION
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Terrible. horrible. Do NOT take this class. The only way you can hope to get even a B is if you memorize everything from lectures, pointless diagrams, and the book. Seriously memorize EVERYTHING or you are screwed. Williams knows his stuff but doesn't know how to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hard and unhelpful.  Would not take again.

This class was VERY difficult. Unless you enjoy detailed behavioral sciences, I would not take this class. Lectures are long and information PACKED; I found every lecture session to be very overwhelming. You have to memorize EVERYTHING for the tests.

He's really funny and I enjoyed the class. I am the type of student that would never miss a class and would always do HW. but this class was extremely impossible to get an A on. IT WAS HARD!  He's a great person and a professor but ID NEVER want to take this class again. 2000+ level? More like 4000 : Oh and theres 4 long papers :(

Professor Williams was incredibly interesting and funny. I was never bored in his class. He had review sessions before tests where he'd answer any questions.  Still, the tests were impossible to get an A on. There were five papers that were graded very easily. You really don't have to read the book at all. I loved this class!

His style of teaching is useless. He tries to incorporate elements of learning psychology into his ppts but doesn't include really any info he says in lecture on them. He puts pictures of his slides on exams and expects answers exactly as he says them in lecture. Just make sure you go above and beyond on homework. ALSO, YOU HAVE TO GO TO CLASS!

Dr. Williams is a great professor and very invested in his work, but this class is close-to-impossible. The material is really interesting, but even if you attend every class and take vigorous notes, you're by no means guaranteed to do well whatsoever. This is a lot more medical-based Psych than Social, so I struggled a lot.

Quite literally one of the best professors I've had at UVa so far. I took this class my first semester at UVa, and if you go to class, do your homework, go to office hours and don't wait to get help, you're GUARANTEED an A. It does have some neurobiology, but nothing that can't be handled. Also makes himself available on appointment. Amazing class!

Pretty cool teacher and at first I thought the info would be boring, but if you pay attention, it's really neat. He goes really fast so you have to keep up. Tests are multiple choice and short answer, which can be tough, depending on how much you study. But I liked it and pretty well.

Way too hard for 200 level.  I took neurobiology and it was cake compared to this class.  Trick exam questions, book questions that only someone who does nothing but read that book all semester would get right.  Slides not that helpful.

Williams attempts to make the material as clear as possible, though his slides are more distracting than helpful. Short answer questions on the test are killer so make sure you MEMORIZE a good portion of the material.
Prof. Williams is a great teacher, and I would recommend him to anyone. He's great in class and during office hours - just do the readings and study for the tests and you'll be fine.
Good professor. Random bits of neural biology that isn't very well explained. The rest of the course was very clear with notes posted on the internet. Great course.

This class is fairly easy but not worth taking unless you're a psych major. Class is worthless as he posts lecture slides online and tests come almost directly from study guides that he provides. Less testing on concepts than on pointless details.

Great professor! He does post notes online, but you really need to go to class to understand them. Clear and easy study guides for every test and VERY minimal homework.  One of my favorite classes this semester!

He is a very engaging profesor and is always out to make you laugh. He teaches learning and so obviously know what it takes to get you to learn the material. His slides are a little distracting w/ lots of colors and differnet fonts but his tests are EASY as long as you read and take good notes. HW for every test.

One of the best psych classes Ive taken. Williams is engaging and makes the lectures relatively interesting. The tests are HARD! You HAVE to study to do well, but as long as you go over his review sheets and do the reading, you're fine. Failed the first test, but did well on the rest once i figured out how to study for them. know minute details.

Prof Williams is one of my favorite professors. He explains things well, is more than willing to help you outside of class, and genuinely wants you to do well in his class. If you create your powerpoints for the presentations ahead of time, he will go through the whole thing with you and point out what to do to make it better. Excellent class.

Nothing says neuroscience like a man who can pull off wearing purple, talk about trashy romance novels and being in a frat, and still have his students respect him. Prof. Williams teaches one of the best classes at UVA. It is HARD WORK but rewarding when you realize how much you've learned to do. Take this class if you have a genuine interest.

Williams is tough, but is more than willing to help.  Go to his office hours!  He genuinely cares about his students' success.  I hated him at first but now he is one of my favorite professors.  He explains how the material is applicable to real-life situations and is willing to explain anything you don't understand in class or during office hours.

I don't know what all the whining is about. People come to UVA and then complain when a professor gives a little work. Cheez. I commute 2 hours each way to this school and work 30 hours a week and have a 3 year old and I have a 98 average in this class.  Just do exactly what he suggests and you will do well. Not to mention the guy is harry-lariou

Like it has been said previously, I found this to be a very different course, especially for a 200 level class.  It was the hardest class I had.  The homeworks were long and tedious.  The tests draw on a lot of comprehensive material rather than brushing the surface to provoke an interest.  Williams is willing to help but at what cost to you?

The best professor I've had at UVA. Yes, there is a lot of material covered in his class - but why are the people who complain about that even in school if not to learn? The class will require work on your part but you will learn a great deal if you put for the effort. Williams is extremely personable and helpful.

I found this class to be way to difficult for a 200 level psych class.  The homework was long and tedious.  It seemed disorganized.  Once I got a test back w/ no grade.  Professor Williams wasn't helpful in this at all, he regraded it by tougher standards than the TAs.  Over all the class was too hard considering I didn't even learn anything.

YES the material is very hard and he goes quickly through lecture but if you go to his office hours he takes time to explain until you have fully understood everything.  uses many examples and tries to keep you engaged.  Great professor USE HIS OFFICE HOURS

Extremely difficult and tedious class.  Take good notes.  Review every days lecture.  Most of the test material came from days when he knew everyone was going to be absent, like the day before thanksgiving break, etc.

Seemingly gratuitous details during his lectures would appear on tests as fill in the blank questions. His homework assignments were mostly busy work that weren't particulary thought-provoking yet time consuming. I was interested in psychology until I took this course. I guess at times he was funny.

i took psyc210 in fall 2003 with Prof. Cedric Williams. he's a superbly engaging lecturer, BUT yes, his homeworks are pretty demanding. a lot of writing to do for a 200-level class where the other typical classes just have MCQs. and you REALLY REALLY REALLY have to read the textbook!!

This class requires an obscene amount of work considering that it a. doesn't fulfill the 2nd writing requirement, and b. is 200-level.  I wrote in excess of 25 pages for his homework assignements!  He also goes at such a furious pace that he isn't able to make clear what will be on exams.

he got great reviews on here, but didnt live up to them during the semester. he's really pretty hard, one of teh harder classes ive had. i managed to pull out a B- but it was an accomplishment for me. pretty interesting class, but don't take it if you havent had a psych class before (i hadnt).

this was the hardest psyc class i've taken at uva.  the tests are on very specific material that is not in the book, only gone over very quickly in lecture. if memorizing neural pathways and charts of slugs for hours while barely passing the class is your cup of tea this MIGHT be the class for you
I concur with the previous rating. The earlier ratings fooled me into taking this class.

WHO ARE YOU PEOPLE???? I think the earlier reviews were totally fake. Class is really fast and its hard to get notes on everything. The tests are practically impossible. On the most recent on only 5 people in the class got A-s. There were no As. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. There are probably easier ones.
Very personable, but very rushed class.  The test were harder than expected especially with a fill-in-the-blank section
He is a good teacher, very clear and helpful.  But he tends to rush things and the tests are all close together, so if you don't mind a little stress come exam time, this class shouldn't be too bad.
Williams is the best professor I had this semester.  He really cares about students and is willing to help.  He makes lectures interesting and easy to understand.  Great teacher!
Very good teaching technique.  Very helpful, especially if the whole class is involved in good discussion.  I highly recommend.

Great teacher. Will always answer questions or go over material during class. Definitely recommend his Intro to Learning class. Study hard for the tests, but he makes it easy for you if you participate in class.

GREAT professor!  He is very friendly and really makes the class enjoyable to take.  Gets very into the subject - you can tell that he loves what he does.  His enthusiasm projects over to his students.
He is a great teacher. His class is easy if you do all the work that he assigns.

This guy is boring beyond belief. He stands at the front of the room and rambles with no slides and no chalkboard. Getting a good TA is vital to make this class not take way more effort than a 1010 class should because god knows the lectures are not going to help you.

I wasn't sure what to expect with Professor Ceaser going into PLAP 1010, but I was pleasantly surprised. He did go off on tangents during lectures, but his demeanor makes lectures feel like you're listening to your grandfather talking. 

I had a great TA, and I'm unsure of how the other TA was. This was an enjoyable class, I recommend it and Ceaser
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I got a B- in a 1010 intro to American politics class. How? This should be one of the easiest classes you could take. Prof. Ceaser is terrible, I would leave his lectures with maybe 3 bullet points of notes because the lectures have nothing to do with the material. He goes on random tangents for what seems like hours. Awful lecturer.

Ceasar's lectures are extremely boring and tangential, and often have little to do with the readings. I often find it hard to take notes because he simply stands in the corner of the room and rambles with seemingly no direction. I have yet to see him write anything on the chalkboard or use any form of presentation.

Professor Ceaser is a great lecturer. He sometimes goes on tangents, but he always talks about current politics and tries to keep the mood light while lecturing. There was a lot of reading per week that was necessary for the discussion. Both primary sources and textbook readings were needed for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He does tend to ramble in lecture but throws in funny tidbits. He's very knowledgeable. Reading is easy. It's an easy class because it's material you learn in high school civics or just by being aware of your own political system. Overall I enjoyed the class. Some people describe him as a "cute old man". I missed 50% of lectures and received an A

Professor Ceaser's lectures are incredibly boring, but that's okay because the material is so basic you won't learn anything from them. It's an easy A if you know anything about American politics. Most students skip lecture, and only attend sections which are mostly a review the readings.

I think I went to a total of 3 lectures and still managed to get by with a B. The class should be easy; it's essentially just a review of high school Civ/AP Gov, but the readings are dry and lengthy and Ceaser is getting too old and distracted to keep up each lecture engaged and interesting. Only 2 exams with a lot of specific multiple choice Qs.

Interesting class, and Ceaser is hilarious. He tends to ramble, but if you listen, you'll still hear the desired main points of the lecture. Not the most difficult with two papers, two exams, and weekly discussion sections(go, they help). Overall, would recommend.

Lectures are boring, unfocused and clearly supporting his own right wing ideology. If you know anything at all about American politics, do not take his class. The lecture hall is almost empty because so many students skip class

Endeavoring to follow the 50-minute "ramble" is worth the effort--it normally goes somewhere interesting and, if not, you'll learn something just by being in the same room with Ceaser. VERY good one-on-one and when he's especially into the topic, e.g. the Founding Fathers and Tocqueville.
He smiles the whole time! Which makes me smile lol

Ceaser is a wonderful professor who is truly passionate about what he is teaching. Though his lectures may seem boring to others, those who actually pay attention will appreciate his sense of humor and stunning good looks. This class is sure to be the highlight of your semester, for more reasons than one.
I really liked this class. I learned a lot and Ceaser always managed to make things interesting. It was one of the oddest classes I've ever been in at times, but I gained a lot from it.

I feel compelled to say- do NOT take this class! Lecture was absolutely worthless...even though I only skipped one class I still learned nothing at all from lecture.  Some days I sat through the whole class and had no notes to show for it.  Want to like him bc he seems nice but only the TA/outside readings helped in any way.

never before have i taken a class where i could simply not pay attention in lecture whatsoever.  I would hear the first few words and immediately zone out and forget where i was for about half an hour.  smart guy but his lectures are disorganized with tons of tangents and no outline.  the TA is the only way you will succeed. beware!

A brilliant mind...those seeking entertainment should take Sabato's 101, where everyone gets spoonfed a series of sound bites about the nature of American politics. Listening to Ceaser's lectures IS actually work but yields ten times the dividends....
Seems lazy, class is painfully boring, so your TA makes it or breaks it for you.

Ceaser is a horrible lecturer and absolutely useless to listen to. He rambles and goes off on so many tangents its impossible to follow his points. Very good class if you like to zone out on facebook, but if you want to learn, find another professor.

i really like this class. he lets his ideology show through in lecture, but as long as you recognize that its ok. some people complain he rambles, but i think he is relatively amusing. he is overshadowed by sabato, but i would rather take plap from him. his tests are hard, but its nothing you cant prepare for. good class overall!
mediocre guy

Makes American politics about as boring as possible. I went to every single lecture and found less than a handful of them helpful on the midterm/final. The text is overly detailed and monotonous. TAs were the only saving grace of this course. Last 101 I'll ever take

Disorganized and rambles.  That said, he is very interesting.  You either "get" him or you don't.  He is VERY good one on one.  Interested in students.  Some people like the lectures and some don't.  Not a hard grader.

If you have any background in politics, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  I hated lectures because it was all useless rambling about his obsession with Toqueville and the Founding Fathers.  Going to class is very unnecessary.  I really enjoyed the outside readings, though they were hardly discussed.

Ceaser while somewhat odd was great.  Yeah the book is a bit redundant if you go to lecture but it really enforces what he talks about and you need to read to do well on the two reading quizes.  Material is pretty interesting and he presents it well.

Overall he's a nice guy and seems very interested in the stuff he teaches, but there's really no structure to the class.  Either attend lecture or read the book, you don't need to do both since they're basically the same.

What are these people talking about?  Ceaser's lectures are completely useless; he only rambles, leaving you wondering why you attended in the first place.  You better have a good TA in discussion, because that is where you learn everything.  Take Sabato's class.
His textbook and lectures follow very closely with one another because he is the one who wrote the book. He is sometimes boring but a lot of times he makes the lecture interesting.
an interesting character.  Test really aren't that tough. Lectures kinda sporadic, most of what you need to know is in your book.
No Comments

Clearly one of the best instructors at UVA.  Great sense of humor, brillant handling of material.  Respects students and learning process.  Do whatever you can to take get Professor Ceaser before you leave UVA.
one word, BORING!
Take Sabadot instead
a theorist but not a thinker, stopped developing in grad school in new jersey decades ago
Great Professor. Has very clear lectures and is engaging.
Ceaser is one of the finest profesors at UVA, and one of the finest theorists in America. Sabato wishes he possessed Ceaser's accumen.
No Comments

One of the oddest professors at UVA. He wore black the entire time that Clinton was in office. Black shoes, black suit, black shirt, and black tie. He was mourning for the country when Clinton was President.
Great teacher, brilliant mind, eccentric, funny, helpful and disorganized. Just sitting in his class you can learn so much. Cannot miss this clance if you are at UVA.
No Comments
Great teacher, sarcastic, witty.  Be prepared for a seirous class
Provides great overview of founding principles. Eccentric, but in good way!
Very historical background on politics.  Almost like broad US Hist. course.

The lectures can be interesting, but more often than not, they're a bit dry. Regardless, there are some interesting elements to the course, and Cesaretti is a very nice, invested professor that I would recommend to everyone.
A truly incredible professor to learn from
One of the kindest professors I have ever had, he cares about his students and works with you. Take him!!!
Il migliore! Professor Cesaretti is a master with his material and quite the looker as well. Both my mind and eyes were thoroughly sated by the end of the semester.

Prof. Cesaretti's class on the Novella made me fall in love with Italian literature. Most of his insights are downright enlightening, yet I never felt intimidated to offer my own opinions, even if they sometimes contradicted his.  He's very nice (I had bad luck and got sick 2ce this semester, and he was very understanding about work)Take his class!
Interesting teacher, keeps learning fun by not requiring a lot of outside work aside from reading Italian newspapers and some essays.  Good teacher, nice guy.

nice guy...interesting topic (Utopias)...but difficult and absurd readings (such as about a man trying to overthrow pasta)...the course is quite confusing and he usually does all the talking..just add in a few comments every now and then and u'll be fine. i enjoyed the class but regret taking it due to my grade...definitely needs more guidelines
he's SOOOO hot...i almost got a B in his class because of his looks...he's like one of those italian guys that all girls dream about!
Prof. Cesaretti is so wonderful.  He is a great professor, and just an overall nice guy.  Take a class with him, it will not only help you Italian, but also get you more interested in it.

Dr. Reiner was an absolutely AMAZING professor. There were never any surprises regarding when quizzes were, what they covered- and likewise with exams. He knew what he was lecturing about and provided VERY thorough and informative powerpoints. He really cared and was always available and enthusiast to answer questions, and answered emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Horrible at life. His children know more psychology then he does.
Class with Cedar was lots of fun.  I recommend him highly.
He's fabulous!  He knows his stuff, he somehow makes it fun, he let us leave class early almost every day...and he's adorable!
No Comments
man he's HOTT
really cool guy, laid back, buys donuts for his students

CELESTE IS MY WORLD! She's sassy, brillant, and full of poetic expertise. You will not only grow as a poet but as a person! this seminar of 15 people became my favorite one I've ever taken at UVA, and I came into it actually hating poetry. You learn so much, and you won't regret your decision. Say yes to Celeste.

Celeste is an incredibly smart teacher and very helpful both in and out of class. She made the whole class comfortable with each other during workshop. This class was a positive experience especially thanks to Celeste. She is wonderful.
Best class ever!!!! Celeste is awesome! You are missing out if you don't take this class!
Best class taken so far at UVa! Celeste's got it all. Disclaimer: don't take the class if you don't have a sense of humor--it would go wasted on you.

You'll finally find out what poetry is. Celeste is an amazing person who makes everyone in class feel like they belong there. If you lack depth, humor, or sassiness in life, DEFINITELY take this class. If you don't, couldn't you use more anyway?

LOVED LOVED LOVED this class. If I could take it again, I would. Celeste is such an amazing teacher, and she's always available for help. If you love witty, sassy, hilarious, and funny comments - take a class that Celeste teaches.
Celeste is amazing! She always makes herself available for extra help and is really invested in her students' work. Highly recommend.
Take this class for an easy A and an unintentionally hilarious professor.
No Comments

The most knowledgeable prof about all things Physics/astr including current developments.  Easy weekly hw assns.  Easy end of semester presentations.  You can learn a LOT if you feel like it.  Can learn nothing if you feel like it (no tests/quizzes).  He puts a lot of effort into the class, into looking over your hw and answering any questions!  :)

Yikes. DON'T take origin of the universe unless you are reeeally interested. Prof. Celli rambles on and on in class, and even if you understand the words he is saying through his thick Italian accent you still have to decipher the physics mumbo-jumbo. But, it's also incredibly easy, even if you never pay attention in class.

I almost cried the last day of class because I didn't want it to end. This class was super fun and interesting. You could get away with skimming the readings. Weekly online posts were pretty simple; tests were easy; discussion was boring. Lecture was awesome, though. She showed great videos and really taught me some useful things.

Really nice professor! The course is interesting and fun, especially when you get to the later topics which are less theoretical. Attendance isn't mandatory at lectures (but participation is part of your grade for discussions so you have to go to those) but the tests are based off her powerpoints. Definitely recommend!
LC is super nice, and care for student's performance. Her class is interesting and not that hard. You can learn a lot from both her sociology experience and class

Used to teach at W&L. Super nice. Easy to follow powerpoints. Material is straight forward. You have to go to discussion and class. Discussion is part of your grade, and she doesn't post powerpoints on collab. Make sure to do all the readings. It's kind of a lot, but she uses all class material for the tests. Tests are predictable and reasonable
She's nice and tries hard, with good French (she's not a native English speaker).  She just seems tired all the time.  The TA I had last semester (Mr. James) was more fun and relaxed.
Great Prof, she is willing to help.  Dont take the night class though, 2 1/2 hours is a long time.
She is extremely helpful and nice.  The class may have been a long 2.5 hours, but she found ways to keep it interesting.  Very fair grader.  My favorite professor during my first semester!
Great professor, clear, helpful. Class moves fast, but it has to to cover 2 semesters worth of material in one. Study for the quizzes that are about every other week and you'll be fine.

Mme. Ciudin is excellent.  She is enthusiastic, which is important for the 2.5 hour, twice a week section.  The class moves fast, but that's to be expected in intensive French.  I highly recommend her.  She is skilled at explaining tough concepts and willing to help students having difficulty.  Generous grader.  Very fair.

She is a good teacher but moves a little fast. SHe is not very good at explaining grammer and if you take the 2.5 hour class(trice a week) prepare to be bored. Class is nevertheless fun but she is an extremely strict grader adn classes do not prepare you for her tests.
Madame Ciudin is amazing!  She is one of the best professors I have had at UVA!
This proffesor is amazing..and so hot!!!
Awesome teacher! Great pronunciation and very understanding and approachable. You won't be disappointed.
She is great! I adore her and will miss her when I have a different french teacher. She is very sweet and an easy grader.
The best language teacher I've had in six years of foreign language studies.  Very helpful and willing.
one of the nicest french teacher ever!!!! she can be unclear sometimes especially when it comes to grammar, but she's definitely willing to help always.
super respected and driven and intelligent - would take her again!
I heart her Queer Novel course. So so good! I wish there were more classes like this at UVA.
Prof. is THE G.O.A.T. Enuf said.

What a waste of three credits. I hardly learned anything! She mostly lets students talk, and rarely offers more than vague suggestions of deeper meaning in the texts. Her lectures sound sourced by Wikipedia. She also makes you turn in drawings of monsters from the texts, so get ready for that. She is a harsh grader though- plan your papers y'all.

I took the Dystopian Novel with Professor Chakravorty during the elections.  It's the most eye-opening and relevant course I have taken at UVA.  Chakravorty is unsettling but in a good way.  I haven't stopped thinking about the books and lectures from the course!  More English classes need to be like this.

Chakravorty's great. Despite not having separate lecturediscussion class periods, she's really good at being able to balance the two in class. There weren't any tests, and she's a relatively tough but definitely fair grader. Gives LOTS of helpful feedback on papers and makes herself very approachable. Lectures were really interesting too.

Prof. C is a strange cookie. You're never sure if she's way ahead of her time, very timely, or just timeless. Turns out she's all three and that's cool. Her lectures are genius. Just dazzling. Who would've thought monsters--fascinating as they are--symbolize capitalism's dead labor?  But they do! Take any class with her. Sure to open your eyes.
Prof. Chakravorty is incredible. Her class is challenging and engaging, and she really pushes you to look beyond the obvious when crafting an argument. I highly recommend any class she teaches.

Professor Chakravorty will challenge you to the point of insanity, but she is definitely worth it. She's brilliant to listen to in class, and she's helpful in Office Hours for papers. I highly, highly recommend her class, but not if you're not willing to work your tail off (loads of reading & long papers). More classes at UVA should be like this.

Chakravorty is most definitely difficult to follow at times: you really need to ask questions and concentrate if there's something you want answered. Occasionally thick accent aside, she was quite passionate and knowledgeable on the subject matter (migrant fictions) and helpful in office hours when it came to papers.

i had a passing interest in the topic; not anymore. i am a huge convert.  the books are smart, and prof. chakravorty is smarter!  she makes post-col. the hottest topic around.  i'm onboard.  imperialism must be subverted.

I love this class!  It's not super easy, but it's definitely worth the challenge.  The readings are really intense, and she gets you to think in totally new ways.  This class has really made me think much more deeply about things happening in the world today.
So incredibly boring... lectures way too fast, and is often difficult to understand. She is really tough on papers, and sometimes her comments make no sense. BEWARE
Great professor and great class!

Professor Harold is a fantastic and inspirational speaker. She may appear frazzled at times, but that is because she is so passionate about what she teaches that she shares it in an authentic manner. One of the best professors or teachers that I have ever had, hands down!

i didn't really think that i was going to like this class at first, but it turned out to be one of the best i have taken at UVA. she is an excellent professor and her passion is obvious. it was a lot of reading at first, but she said she would limit it for future classes. i definitely recommend this class!

She is really passionate about the subject and cares a lot about student achievement, she wants you to do well in the class. She offers extra credit papers and sometimes gives pop quizes that she counts as extra credit. My only critique is that there is A LOT of reading, but most of it is interesting! I highly recommend this class!

WAY too much reading. We cover a WIDE variety of topics that differ EVERY class. The material is very broad. Granted, she's a great professor with an appealing personality. But if I had the option again, I wouldn't take this class.

I took Black Nationalism in the Fall 2005 and I really enjoyed this class; at first I was a bit skeptical about taking this class based on the title because I thought it would primarily be about black militancy.  But, it proved to be a very enriching course, and Prof. Harold is VERY helpful, always available to talk or discuss and very approachable

She is an amazing teacher! She genuinely cares about all her students and will work with them to ensure that they receive grades. She makes you think and question how society operates, yet the course is not structured to be extremely difficult. Its like she talks to you and not AT you. Amazing class and I would take ANY other class she was teaching

Great professor. Nice balance of work/reading as well as fair test,quizzes, and grading.  Take advantage of office hours especially if  you want to build on material outside of class. Nice to talk to. Take anything she teaches b/c it's bound to be good.
;) TRUST ME, YOU'LL LOVE THIS CLASS
Great teacher, take her American Labor class. If we had more teachers here at UVA like Prof. Harold, UVA would never need to fire any professors. Very helpful and understanding.

Prof. Harold is a great teacher. I had no idea what to expect for this class, but I've definitely learned a lot. The essays on the exams take a toll on your hand, but they are fair and straightforward. Not too too much reading. Also, some movies here and there. If you've never taken a history course at 300 level, I'd recommend her first.
No Comments

I cannot explain how boring and awful her class is. She is very old school and doesn't allow any phones or computers. She thinks that she's above all. She will try to constantly correct you even though you gave the right answer just didn't word it the way she wants you to. The only B I will have this semester. Boring and snobby, do not recommend

This class is not hard if you pay attention in class and do most of the reading. Prof. Clowes is super nice, just beware that the tests require a good amount of memorization (like specific dates and artists). There are two tests and a good amount of small assignments to boost your grade.

Professor Clowes is a very considerate professor who knows a great deal on the subject of Russian culture. She assigns a decent amount of reading, but she's very realistic and doesn't expect you to necessarily finish it all. The classes can be a bit dull at times, but that's more of a question of taste and how interested one is in the material.

I think that Professor Clowes is an incredibly caring professor and really wants the best for her students. However, it is important to be warned that this is a CULTURE class, not a HISTORY class. Also, while all of the reading is super interesting, it isn't always worth it to do all of it, but it is all very interesting if you have the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I took this thinking it was modern Russian culture. This class is ONLY Russian history, so be forewarned. It's not that hard; study guides for the midterm and final, and no other tests or quizzes. One project at the end, group or solo, but there are basically mini essays due every day. A lot of reading but I skip a lot of it and I have an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof.Lyu is very kind and cares a lot about her students. She gives many challenging assignments at once and can make things overly complicated. Felt frustrated and annoyed with the challenge until we'd talk in class and then she was so likeable I forgave her. Difficulty of the French often felt beyond the scope of the class. Nice grader, so doable
Professor Lyu is such a kind and caring professor. She gives amazing feedback on papers and genuinely wants to help you get better with your French. I would highly recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is very nice but her class is difficult
extremely caring and well-spoken. her french is impeccable and she always offers the best insights. this class/madame lyu have made me fall in love with french poetry and literature!
She is one of the best professor I've ever had. She can be tough sometimes but show her effort and improvements, you'll get a lot out of her course.
i write a rough draft. she gives it a terrible grade.  i go to see her in office hours, and she tells me i'm terrible in french and don't understand how an essay works.  thanks for the encouragement.
I took two upper-level French classes with Mme Lyu and wish I could've taken more.  Her passion for poetry is evident and contagious.
If you're into poetry, this is a good class.  Lyu is nice, and you'll still learn some stuff.
No Comments

wonderful and very knowledgeable! She emphasizes the process of learning, not the answers. The key to success w/ her is showing how much you've improved. Lots of work in beginning of semester with poetry, less with plays and novels.
Simply awesome. Really pushes you to succeed, and gives you plenty opportunity to do so. Recommended!
She is wonderful. Very sweet. Highly recommended.

I took PSYC 2200 and PSYC 4500 with Dr. Clabough. I enjoyed her teaching, but her exams are very, very memorization intensive. You will learn a great deal, but for 2200 make sure to memorize all the lectures and readings. Don't take her J-term, there were 2 sets of daily assignments and 3 projects for 4500, and I finished it fine, but it was a lot!

Dr. Clabough is a nice person, but her class structure isn't conducive to learning the material. Get ready to sit through dense, dull readings compounded by rambling lectures. It's unclear what you need to know for tests as she gives little guidance - EVERYTHING is fair game. Don't take this class unless you're a Psych major - not worth the stress.

Pretty cool class, same knowledge base as BIOL 3050. If you passed AP Psych, this will be the next level. Great class if you have a lot of time - she posts her lectures online to watch (2 lec / week, 1 hr each) alongside online textbook readings (usually take 30 min - 1hr), and in class, we do active learning aka the coolest group projects ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Grading is really clear. She drops the lowest grade out of all categories: active learning, knowledge checks, tests. There's also a mediation assignment to replace a test grade. Her lectures are all online. Active learning is fun. Unclear what you need to know for the test - ascpets of textbook in it. Don't worry - if you study you can get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Grading and expectations were very clear. Exams were based mostly on lectures with a few additional details from the textbook. Attendance was not mandatory when I took the class during covid season.
Professor Clabough seems like a really nice person but her lectures were unorganized and the material did not always agree with the associated textbook readings. TA's were no help at all either.

Clabough is a cool professor. The material is super interesting. Her exams are ridiculously hard. Not open book or open notes, but if they were it would still be really hard. The reading is a bit tough as well. I still recommend the course just because of the material alone. She's not a bad teacher at all, but the tests averaged at about 75%

I had her for neural basis during covid. all tests were closed book. I think the class in general is hard, but the way she explains things can be really confusing. material is not intuitive to me and I often had zero clue what I was expected to know. tests are the only grades we get, and no study guide or clarification on what we need to know

I had Prof Clabough for a lab class during covid, and thought she did a great job transitioning the class to an online format. Asynchronous lectures, open-note quizzes, and lab papers on easy-to-understand experiments. I wish the class didn't have to be online because normally you get to do cool stuff like dissect brains. Nice & smart professor.

Worst professor I have had at UVA. When I had him last fall he would refuse to post lecture notes so if you missed class even for an emergency he would not share them. If you asked he'd instead say to "ask a friend". Class was not interesting.  He was not good at explaining the material, also not helpful or sympathetic to students. Don't take him.

How this guy became a professor is beyond me. He got mad at me for taking this class because I've taken a stats class before. THIS IS A REQUIREMENT FOR THE PSYCH MAJOR SO I NEED TO TAKE IT. Was never helpful during office hours, you're lucky if he even shows up. Reads straight off powerpoints during class and goes off topic a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He should not be a professors. Doesn't respond to emails, cancel office hours at the last minute, doesn't provide and practice problems or resources for studying, and says something bad about UVA every class. Stay away from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory since he gives random quizzes for your participation grade (15%). He has fill in the blank notes/powerpoints and literally just reads them verbatim during class. Every time I've raised my hand and said I was confused and asked him to explain again, he read the slide again and made me feel dumb. Also rambles off topic a lot

He doesn't give ANY practice problems to study with despite the fact that this is a math class. He wouldn't let me see my past exams because it's his "intellectual property" and was not accommodating whatsoever when I had COVID. I obviously couldn't come to class so my participation grade tanked even though I had a legit reason.
He is quite literally a mess. Also he never answers emails.
He is very disorganized. If you can, take this class with any other available professor.

very disorganized but u can cram the night before the exam and do fine, u don't have to pay attention in lectures u just have to complete fill in the blank notes and then teach yourself, also no hw and 85% of the grade is based on 4 exams then 15% is participation

The professor makes the class as easy as possible for the students. It is clear that he truly wants to see us succeed. He makes an effort to answer any questions during class and also encourages office hours. The material is not tough to learn and tests are directly translated from the lectures. If you work for this class, you can do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: As someone who usually struggles with math, I found this class VERY frustrating. Options for study materials are useless- he recommends you do the questions from the textbook, but the test questions look nothing like that. Lectures are posted incomplete and you can't see what test questions you got wrong because it's his "intellectual property."

It is very clear that he wants everyone to pass his class. He basically makes the class idiot proof with fill in the blank notes. He is very clearly knowledgable and experienced in the field. Despite his effort students seemed to be very disrespectful towards him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Poor lecturer overall and needlessly confusing. A lot of emphasis on a growth structure that just isn't that helpful. Class was dual taught with another professor and whenever it was Professor Columbus's turn to lecture, I consistently understood way less. Required chem class for me so it was fine, but I wouldn't recommend if you don't have to.

Had her for CHEM 4410. The code wasn't an available option to press because she chose to teach 4410 as a last minute course to prove to the chemistry department that she can do it. Takes forever responding to emails. And her lectures? She stutters and is physically incapable of finishing a sentence. My advice? Take any other professor BUT her.

I'm not sure if these are specifically issues with Professor Columbus or just the Chemistry department as a whole, but the amount of homework is insane. I'm required to take Chemistry despite it not relating to my major and even though it is my least important class, it by far gives the most reading and outside work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: LC is so underrated! She emphasizes understanding the material rather than memorizing trends, which is admittedly harder, but pays off in the end. Her lectures serve as a supplement rather than a review of the reading, so make sure to put in the work to understand basic concepts before lecture and you'll get a lot of this course.
Walked into lectures feeling good, walked out feeling more confused then when I walked in. The best lecture we had was when we had a substitute professor come in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Linda was not great at explaining things. The overall setup of the class sucked and she constantly made mistakes with the logistics.

I stopped attending her optional lectures because there was nothing fruitful happening during them. The workload is heavy and confusing for this course, and they make things hard to understand for no reason. I really disliked the structure of this class.

I took this class with Columbus because I heard amazing things about her, but I was wrong. Whenever we don't understand something, she quickly looks it up on Google. Common things she says are "this answer looks like goobly gook" if its incorrect rather than a complete explanation, annoying laughs if we have a question, and never responds to emails

Columbus truly provides an environment where she wants to see each student reach their full potential. She is a visionary that has rebuilt the framework for this class using an active-learning method, and it is fabulous. Even more, Professor Columbus is a highly regarded individual within the academic community and is an advocate for each student.

Took both the 1410 & 1420 course with Columbus. Class is setup differently from traditional college classes; online reading/questions before lectures and then group assignments following lecture. Basically flipped classroom - not a bad thing. The difficulty is nothing too bad as long as you keep up with the weekly reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Field is just the best. Pushes students to engage on a complex level with the material and participate actively in discussion, but in such an encouraging way that it doesn't feel like a burden. Genuinely cares about her students' success AND wellbeing, which is rare. If you show up and try your best, you can't lose with her. She rocks.

Professor Field is a great person with a lot of insight into WGS! Make sure you actually put in the work in the class and develop a relationship with her by going to office hours and the experience will be very pleasant. She doesn't tolerate slacking, so this is a must. She is a very caring and even motherly figure in lecture!

Professor Field is amazing. She's incredibly passionate and cares for her students and tries to make things as clear as possible. She is always willing to help you, whether it's after class or in office hours. She's also incredibly nice. Tough grader with papers, but she makes the criteria clear and helps you do better with each paper.

This was an incredible class mostly because of the professor. Cori was very reasonable and organized--assignments and readings were well selected and very thought-provoking. Made me rethink a lot of things.

Field is a knowledgeable professor who's skilled at teaching many perspectives and really utilizing an intersectional outlook. She gives credit to everyone's ideas but uses her extensive historical knowledge to support her claims. Lectures are interesting, tho reading journals can be annoying and student presentations take up a lot of class time.

Such a good professor, her lectures were always so interesting and engaging.  NOT a droning history professor by any means.  Reading and coursework was different and interesting as well, lots of room for exploring own topics!  Highly recommend her!

Cori Field is the BEST professor I have ever had at UVA. She truly cares about her students and is always more than willing to meet outside of class to discuss or clarify anything. Her passion for history makes her an interesting and engaging lecturer. She even comes to discussion sections to hear the ideas of her students. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

I really enjoyed this class. Professor's Kinney is quite harsh in terms of marking your work and her tests, especially the final, are worth a lot of your final grade. That said, you do learn a lot, and if you do the reading and the assignments you can get an A without too much stress.

Lots of awkward silences in class. Asks very specific questions and expects you to guess what she's thinking. Terrible for discussion. Avoid! (My number rating came out wrong below: this is the right one.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of awkward silences in class. Asks very specific questions and expects you to guess what she's thinking. Terrible for discussion. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Kinney is an incredibly intelligent woman and I enjoyed her class even if there were times that I felt it dragged on a little bit -- if you love English, though, you should definitely consider taking one of her classes.

I LOVED this class. Clare Kinney is absolutely amazing. She solidified in my mind my desire to become an English major at UVA. There are pretty hefty readings assigned before each lecture, but I thought the material was interesting so it was never painful. She posts lecture outlines on Collab so note-taking is really easy.

Prof. Kinney is the only prof I've ever had who doesn't just make you think critically about the material - her lectures make you FEEL it. Elocution is simply in her blood and she can give you chills. Her critiques WILL improve your work if you're actually smart enough to listen to her. If not, you're losing out on a wonderful learning experience.

Agree with the rhymes with rich comment. If you are taking the independent study, hope you get Levenson. She is a mean spirited and sad person. She has to put down others to prop herself up. If she doesnt like you, watch out! But its k, she'll be reading my books in a year  :) her attempts at discouragement go nowhere !

If you want constructive criticism like this: ?Your paper gives the impression of a ?Monster Download? effect,? ?you go off on tangents,? ?And the 100s of footnotes are a real giveaway,? ?In the end, this is a huge jigsaw puzzle of data??take Clare Kinney. She picks her favorites and is as irrational as they come. PLAIN BAD PROF. just sayn!
Class was interesting at first but soon became a chore and a little overwhelming. Good class to take, but whether or not you'll enjoy it is questionable.

I was pretty disappointed with Kinney's lectures. She likes to read/act out the Shakespeare dialogue: really promising the first class but got old when there was absolutely nothing substantial in lecture material. She basically reads quotes and rehashes what happened in play you just read. don't recommend for those looking for engaging classes

She politicizes graduate classrooms and only acknowledges her super-acolytes. I saw her demean a Rhodes scholar during class. She lectures runners on running, Germans on Germany, physicists on physics. She affects expertise in everything. Acknowledges questions on nothing. Dishonest, mean, hyperpolitical.
How to put this in polite terms? It rhymes with rich.

Her lectures are prepared down to the word, making every sentence a gem of information. The reading happens in manageable slices so long as you do the assignments when they are due. Her tests are fair. She and others will call them nit picky, but overall they are manageable. Also, there are many bonus point opportunities.
Prof. Kinney was, hands down, one of the best professors I've ever had.  Yes, you will work hard, but she makes you think and inspires great work.  Take her as soon as you can.

Kinney is the reason I am an English major! She is extremely intelligent and draws out connections that really bring the works she teaches together in a way I never would think of.  She makes herself very accessible and works with you to help you improve as a student.  I have taken four classes with her and would gladly take more! Love her!!

Although I thought most of the formal aspects of the class were okay--organized, not excessively heavy coursework, etc--the professor personalized more than most. Given that fact,the class was weird, and she displaced her anger against students, especially unusual students.
I attended the lectures and did all of the reading but I did worse than I expected (hoped).
Enjoyed the class but not easy by any means. Midterm can be tricky... meticulous notes are necessary for success.
Great professor! Her tests are not ridiculously hard but if you want a good grade, do read the material and attend all lectures and discussions.

I don't know if it was just a bad semester for her or what, but every time I interacted with Kinney, she was really rude!  Her tests are unnecessarily detail-driven and don't really promote critical thinking, which is sort of what being an English major is all about. Lectures are okay. She's funny and knows the material. But this class is a pain.

GREAT PROF! Organized clear lectures, funny as heck, doesn't suffer fools, but fair. Kind of hard but not impossible on tests and papers. Class is very useful for the major and with her you actually learn a ton.
Great lecturer and manifestly all-around brilliant woman!
Great lecturer, funny too.  Pay attention and you will be fine.  Her accent is awesome.  Take any class that she is teaching.
She's a great lecturer, very passionate and knowledged. The final is a nightmare though, and Shakespeare gets old after a while.

prof kinney is AWESOME.  i don't know what these people are complaining about - if you have a half a thought you could pass the midterm without studying.  all you have to do is pay attention in lecture (which is not hard at all).  highly recommend this class

Highly recommend - even if you're not an English major (like me). If you're going to take Shakespeare, take it with Kinney. She's a lot of fun, and her lectures are brilliant, well-organized, and insightful.

GREAT professor! She's so intelligent and witty, and her lectures are always well-organized and interesting. The midterm was fair - I studied only a little and did really well. All you have to do is do the reading and go to lecture and discussion. Anyone who says they didn't like this class probably should have put more effort into it.

Yes, easy and helpful, but she is the most boring & irritating professor I have EVER had. I fall asleep EVERY class. Midterm was just bad-didn't test intelligence, but only the ability to remember small details. I feel dumber for having been in this class. Shakespeare is rolling in his grave. Her accent is also horribly annoying.

Amazing wonderful challenging prof. Knows everything but is witty and puts it together for you. Do not try to slide by, she will zap you, but go in there and give it everything you have and have the best experience you'll ever have in a college class.
One of the best professors I have ever had in my life and I am now in graduate school. Incredible lecturer.
She's amazing!  Knowledgeable, engaging, clear; she cares about her students, and you will be a better person for taking anything with her!  ... Plus, the Brits are hilarious.
Very engaging and very funny professor.

Awesome professor-- she really cares about all her students and will push you to do your absolute best.  She is very willing to meet you outside of class to discuss papers or other issues you may be having.  Although her grading may seem hard, she is really just trying to get you to do your best.

She is so brilliant, so eloquent, so poised, and so funny.  Her readings of Shakespeare alone were enough to make the class worthwhile - she could easily be a professional stage actress.  Instead of proposing a single analysis, she usually offers several alternate interpretations, and let you decide

Kinney is brilliant!  Her lectures were entertaining, well structured, easy to follow, etc.  We had TA's b/c it was so large, but she was more than willing to discuss papers and readings during office hours.  She's just a warm, good humored Brit :)
Be warned...if you don't accept her theoretical stance on the material, you're asking for a poor grade.  She has no patience for alternative points of view.
Most excellent.  Smart and courageous.  No patience for the lazies.
Very engaging lecturer.  Very articulate, and her British accent works well with the material.
awesome lecturer

Disappointed and upset prof could not be bothered to show up on time, and would often leave early. The "lectures" are just quotes from readings copied and pasted on a PowerPoint. She was inaccessible,NEVER offered constructive help, and syllabus wasn't followed at all. The grades were done at the end of the year and I can't believe I paid for this.

Class was great. Professor clearly knows her stuff. Very encouraging. She is big on discussion so be sure to read and be ready to talk. I took her as a senior, wish I could have taken more classes with her.

I took my COLA 1500 with Dean Smith fall 2018. Her background is in English and writing, so this is the flavor all her classes will have. She values class discussion more than anything else, and most of class was spent with open conversation. She is pretty set in her views and mostly wants to hear her own words regurgitated back in papers.
Professor Crane is such a kind person and clearly passionate about the course material. This class was not very difficult, but I still felt like I learned so much.

I enjoyed Professor Crane's class. The class meetings were her lecturing, and there were weekly readings and assignments. Overall, the lecture part of this course was generally pretty good; participation does matter (at least it's strongly encouraged). Grades are determined by TAs, so it can depend a little bit on the luck of the draw.
Prof. Crane is a great scholar. I think she might be better in directing researching than lecturing. She is smart and patient with students. I think her class was challenging but I did learn a lot!

Professor Crane is an excellent speaker and is very knowledgeable about what she teaches. The lectures can get somewhat boring, but she tries to make the topics intriguing and interesting. The weekly assignment questions were annoying and the readings were dull. However, the class was ultimately pretty easy.
Professor Crane is a very good scholar. She is very knowledgable and helpful. This class is a high level class and it is challenging.
She's really passionate about the subject and is really personable one-on-one!

Sheila is an amazing professor, who truly cares about presenting herself as a standout educator. She is always available for discussions either through email or office hours, allowing students easy access. She is so organized and clearly defines her expectations for tests and assignments. All of her course materials are on Collab. A great class!

Hardly anyone goes to class.. I feel bad for her because she is such a horrible public speaker.  I think she knows what she's talking about, she just can't explain it.  She seems like a really nice lady! I guess it's a good class if you want to skip all of the lectures and wing it in discussion.  Midterm, paper, final

Awful teacher. Gesticulates far too much and is distracting with her overuse of subjunctive clauses and qualifiers. AND "um." By the end of the class, barely anyone showed up and those who were there were playing tetris.
She sucks
I took AR H101 with her, and really enjoyed it.  AR H203 was a different story.  She is very knowledgeable, but her lectures are often difficult to follow.
She is horrible.  I never make comments here, but for her, I'm making an exception.  I hope for your sake you take my advice and avoid her at all costs.
Great teacher, great scholar.
I can see how she got where she is....it's obvious stat.
her first class was fine, but near the end it get really boring ---i felt like a prisoner in that class avoid taking her class ---one of the worst teacher at the A-school
the worst teacher by far ----i didn't enjoy her class at all

Professor Griffin is extremely kind and easygoing. She will happily work with you to find a solution to any problem you may be experiencing. The course readings were incredibly interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you have a chance to take a class with Cristina, DO IT. She is so welcoming, encouraging, and absolutely hilarious. Discussions were always insightful and she's a great advisor too! I am someone who has always hesitated to participate in seminars, yet I found myself raising my hand lots in this class because of the environment Cristina fosters.

REALLY loved this class. ENWR on "One Great Book" and it was so insightful and fun, especially as someone who shares Cristina's passion for literature. We had so many great discussions and she was wonderfully accommodating when some personal issues came up and I couldn't attend class. Super easy and fun class!

Her ENWR on Writing about Television was so fun and a really great way to teach writing. She is extremely caring for all of her students and if you have completed a certain threshold of assignments by the end of the semester, you get an A. If this class is offered, TAKE IT!
Really great teacher and fun class!

Cristina is an amazing professor who gives every student the chance to succeed and works to make sure that all students achieve their goal. Cristina hypes up students when you do things well and is very communicative and easy to talk to. She makes every student feel important and like they belong in her class and she is very funny.

Cristina is amazing. Her class for my ENWR was easy (gender and gothic), but I felt like I was really getting something done. She spaces out assignments well, gives extensions, supports all the arguments you make no matter how half baked. Easily one of my favorite professors so far.

Just such a wonderful, kind human! Facilitates meaningful discussions where everyone feels like their opinion matters. Respects your time and is flexible when you have issues/need an extension. So kind and easy to talk to!

Cristina is warm, funny, and extremely intelligent. She's got a fantastic memory and makes a strong effort to know every student inside and outside the classroom. One of the kindest, most brilliant and articulate professors I've had the pleasure of getting to know. Ask her about her love for the Great British Baking Show!
Absolutely great professor! Always looked forward to his lectures and I learned a lot through his assignments. Loved his class and hope to take more with him in the future!

Professor Dill is nice and enthusiastic about CS, but his classes are somewhat bare-bones. Often times, you can get the same information he brings to lectures from texts and slides. People who prefer hands-on learning will likely do better by reading through the texts and practicing the examples. Nevertheless, his classes are easy and digestible.

Craig Dill is well-meaning, but is simply not a good professor. There is absolutely no point in going to lecture because you won't learn anything and his voice puts you to sleep. There are many much better professors in the CS department so please take one of them instead.
Loved this class.  Learned a lot in Latin that I had lost in high school.
She's spunky  and clear

Prof. C. is wonderful. She's funny and friendly. She loves to go on interesting tangents about her dog, Roman festivals and Classics events. Rest assured, she still stays on target. It's a great class. I recommend everyone who is in need of a fun, interesting and meaningful class to take it! :)
Hard class, I wouldn't advise taking Latin if you're not good with languages. Take French or Spanish to meet college reqs. Class basically depends on which TA is the best and if you have that TA.

Crawford is the coolest person. Very easy to understand if you pay attention. Always do the homework it is a free 10 points! Lots of small quizzes, and 3 one hour long tests. Really knows her stuff and is very helpful, but expects you to try. Definately take this class!
funny

A seminar class with her was hell.She must have thought that we all regarded are GPAs as jokes, because the midterm was so ridiculous that maybe three kids finished it-and her response was "if you don't like your grade, make it up somehow." She could also make unconstructive and downright rude comments during class discussion.

You HAVE to take at least a thousand classes with Prof Crawford. She's hilarious and adorable and brings cookies and muffins to class sometimes. At least an hour of work a night, but if you put that much into it, the quizzes and tests will be very easy. Plus, I mean, this is a language...what were you expecting?

I started college when she came to uva and even in her first semester here, she just got it! awesome teacher, awesome person...she wrote me a nursing school recommendation and it was by far the best in my batch!  get to know her!  shes a really nice lady and great teacher who loves classics

This class was awesome. You learn something interesting every lecture, and Prof. Crawford is always so full of energy. Quizzes and tests are easy if you put in a consistent level of hard work throughout the semester. Expect to do about an hour a day of Latin in order to do well. A bonus of the class is you get cookies on Roman and Greek holidays:)
She is my sunshine.
HILARIOUS! her sense of humour rox my sox
She did a great job with our intro level latin class. She's also hilarious, I would recommend her.
She is awesome--and absolute blast. You will love her jokes and cheer from day one.

She is a good teacher and is quite perky (which can get annoying since you have some form of Latin in the first level everyday!) but she is nice and definately wants her students to succeed. You've got to keep up with the class but that is how it is with any language!
Professor that wants to see her students succeed. She provides so many points in the class that if you mess up a couple of times, it's just fine
No Comments

Makes the class interesting and actually seems to care about engaging with students. Querky sense of humor makes having class everyday pass faster. Tests aren't bad either and she reschedules them around football games...which is amazing!!

If you have the opportunity to take Age of Augustus with her, TAKE IT! She obviously knows exactly what she's talking about and communicates it clearly to the class.  She's a bit quirky, but in an interesting way! Her tests can be tricky, but she;sthe nicest prof you'll ever meet!

Professor Cushman is by far the best professor I have had in four years of undergrad. He wants to see every single one of his students succeed and is willing to support you in any way possible. He comes to class with so much enthusiasm and creates an environment where you actually enjoy learning. Truly a one of a kind professor!

Absolutely incredible professor. I took Professor Cushman's class on the recommendation of another professor at UVA and it turned out to be my favorite of the semester (by far). He's engaging, insightful, and brilliant. His feedback and attention to students is thoughtful and thorough. Take any class you can from himyou won't regret it.

One of the best professors in UVA's much-famed English department - and that's saying something. Extremely well read, outgoing, funny, and brilliant. I noticed that he would be mid-sentence in seminar, but if he saw a hand of a student, would stop and call on them. Take a class with him before he retires. I bet you'll love it.

Prof. Cushman is hands-down the best professor I've ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable (he has a PhD from Yale) but also humble & kind. I once took a law school class that was mostly about the environment, just because he co-taught it. Don't expect an easy A, go to as many office hours as you  can, listen to his advice. You won't regret it.
I love prof. Cushman.

Professor Cushman is one of the most brilliant, insightful, and engaging professors I've ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable about the material, and presents it in fascinating, well organized lectures. I absolutely loved being in his class. He's also extremely helpful and welcoming in office hours, and is so easy to talk to!

I had Cushman for World Short Story on Semester at Sea and he was absolutely amazing.  He challenges you to be better by not adhering to standardized grading devices.  By far one of those unique teachers that blends knowledge with personality. Lots of knowledge, and great personality.

What a pompous, overyly prescious egomaniac! Couldn't stand him, found his lectures uninspiring, and his knowledge and enthusiasm the material very limited. Any energy or effort he exerted was to make us think he was cool or clever, of which he is neither. Avoid, unless you want your love for criticism stabbed in the heart.

Professor Cushman may be the greatest professor I've ever had. He really turns a small class into a community (I was lucky enough to have him as a section leader) and I learned a LOT in his class. Definitely get to know him in a smaller class. He's really a fantastic guy.

I disagree with people's ratings of Cushman. I thought he did an excellent work explaining the prose and poetry we read for class. He taught the class with Levenson and was every bit as charming as he was (in his own way....they were quite the duo actually). It was apparent that he had a lot of passion for the material and made class exciting!

I was lucky enough to have Cushman as my wonderful discussion leader! He was enlightening, funny, and completely personable. He is willing to help all students and genuinely cares about our lives outside the class (many discussions centered around our well-being overall and what he could do to help us). I highly recommend taking a class with him!

i disagree WHOLEHEARTEDLY! Cushman is amazing, my favorite professor at UVA. He is engaging as a section leader, really wants to hear everyone's voice, allows us to talk in colloquial language, using pop culture references to all texts we study. Most comfortable and engaging discussion i've EVER had!! He's so cool and funny, too. LOVE HIM.
boring lecturer. huge ego.
boring, arrogant, and a lackluster poet.
Superb!
A rotten, boring poet.  He should stick to criticism.
No Comments
awesome  (and do the summer London program as well; you won't regret it!!!!)
Great professor!!!!
not very interesting professor. kind of bland. I think he's more interested in his own writing and in his family.
She is a harsh grader and expects an unnecessary amount of understanding of genetics for an engagement. She loves group projects and unnecessary busy work. Do not take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Genetics is not an easy class; it has a lot of busy work, which means you will ALWAYS have some sort of work to do, and the exams are extremely difficult, mainly because there's no partial credit. CC is a really entertaining professor who cares about her students but you should read the textbook and do practice problems and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Genetics is hard. You biology majors have to take it. The memorization portion of the class isn't that daunting; it's the ability to integrate the endless amount of concepts learned throughout the course (and discussion sections) that is the real challenge. BUY THE SOLUTIONS MANUAL. DO THE HOMEWORK. AND EMAIL HER REGULARLY. You'll thank me later.

Great professor, always easy to get in touch with, made class interesting. Genetics is inevitably a tough subject but by the end of this class if you put in the work/effort she can help you get a good grade and better yet an excellent grasp of the material.

She could improve as a teacher if she didn't waste so much time writing songs and raps designed for 3rd graders and instead covered more relevant & applicable information that relates textbook info to real-life genetic issues. Even studying the book and problems inside and out will not prepare you for her fantastical & made-up scenarios on tests.
good professor and very helpful

horrible teacher. condescending and belittles student answers. takes an interesting subject and makes you hate it by the end of the course. tests are manageable but completely out of left field. Like in lecture, she asks questions, she expects answers on the tests that cover material she fails at covering herself. too bad u need it for the major.

Her first 3 tests weren't really hard but the final was hard as hell. She ended up curving the class average down even though it was at a B- like she "promised". Even if you end up study hard be prepared to end up disappointed.

She kept the classes very interesting but the questions on the tests had nothing to do with what we had done in class. Be prepared to study A LOT. It is a very difficult class but still very interesting. I studied my ass off and still got a B+ when I deserved an A.

Professor Cronmiller was great!  The class is hard but doable if you stay on track with reading/practice problems, and she really tries to make it fun!  Even did a self-written "genetics rap" for our class!
She's a great professor! She's very nice and dedicated to making sure her students understand the subject. Her exams were difficult, but not impossible.

Cronmiller is TERRIBLE. Seriously, stay away unless you have a strange desire to be talked down to by someone who has no clue how to teach genetics. Her tests are ridiculously hard and the TAs are absolutely zero help whatsoever. She responds to emails quickly. That's about it.

Tests are impossible, huge curve at the end, discussion session helps your grade, but not your comprehension of the test material. Worst professor I've had, take Wormington instead. Avoid this abomination of a class and teach yourself genetics without the pressure! There is no support in this class...Lectures/ Office hrs./TA's not helpful.

Tests were nearly impossible and the questions were sometimes pretty ambiguous even if you understood the material. Everything is curved pretty well at the end of the semester though. VERY approachable outside of class.

This professor is one of the worst I've had. She does not explain the material, and going to lecture to listen to her ramble about topics not on the test is almost useless. The tests are extremely difficult and she does not give partial credit in most cases. Do not take this class unless you have to!
interesting class. but NOT worth all the trouble
Good professor but tough tests. Be sure to work out the practice problems and go to office hours. Tests are free response math questions.

Amazing. Compared to the other two professors for the class she is absolutely fantastic. She explains everything clearly and its obvious that she not only enjoys the material but really loves teaching. Her tests aren't hard if you listen in class and study. Even though they're not multiple choice they're muchhh easier than Hirsh and Adler's tests.
She's a great professor!  She's very nice and dedicated to making sure her students understand the subject.  Her exams were difficult, but not impossible.
friendly, but ridiculously hard

Awesome teacher! She puts biology ideas to contemporary songs/raps to keep up class interest. Her tests are difficult but fair because she only tests on material that she teaches in class. She is very easy to get in touch with (email!) and office hours are definitely a good place to go to clarify on ideas from class.

Cronmiller is an absolutely fantastic professor.  She is so clear in lecture--the book was definitely helpful but she only tested on the material that she covered in class.  She is very helpful outside of class, too (e-mail her!).  Her tests are challenging but not tricky, so if you get it you'll do well.  Made me want to learn.
engaging and enthusiastic professor who sings and raps. however, i still found it difficult to absorb everthing in lecture so textbook is pretty mandatory.
Ok
agreed, atrocious teacher
No Comments

She is absolutely the worse teacher I have ever had. I actually feel like I am unlearning everything I properly learned in fluid mechanics. She has no clue about what is going on. Her notes are terrible, she makes countless mistakes, she nervously laughs about worthless stuff and her homework is literally impossible because she can't teach. AVOID.

Prof Curran is the worst teacher I have had at UVa. She is absolutely terrible. She is extremely disorganized and makes countless mistakes in lecture. Homework assignments are impossible because she is so unclear. The book is usless as well so you need to go to class to get notes, but it is such a waste of time to go because she cant keep on topic.

Dusan is great. He teaches to the book, his exams are challenging but not out of left field. Econ is difficult in general. Just because you don't understand it doesn't mean that the professor is bad. Dusan is helpful and his teaching style is super clear.

Professor Curcic is very nice and extremely helpful to students who seek his help. It's helpful to do all the practice problems he suggests because they may appear later in the course. I personally struggled at the beginning of the class but with his encouragement I was able to tuen my grade around. I also found his lectures fun, but math based.

Dusan doesn't want to teach and it's obvious. He teaches all theory and then the exam is almost entirely math-based. The text book is helpful, but only really helps with theory-based concepts. Definitely avoid taking his section.

The class wasn't too hard, but Dusan's teaching didn't match up with the exams very well.  The midterms were mostly math based, when Dusan taught a lot of the theory but not so much the math of economics.  It doesn't help that the textbook doesn't go over a single math problem.  This class was frustrating because it's easy but the prof made it hard

Exams are basically identical from previous sections... get your hands on them and you will ace the class.  I would not recommend him to learn from.  The book is much more useful.  He acts like he doesn't care, and it shows in his effort.
My favorite class.

Shaun is an interesting character. I really like him as a person, he was unnecessarily nit-picky on paper and exam grading, and quite lenient on quizzes.
