I liked him a lot more at the start of the semester than I did at the end. I don't know that I would seek him out as a TA, but definitely don't be disappointed if you get him.
Very intelligent and willing to accept multiple opinions as long as you are not a complete dumbass. great sense of humor but still managed to keep classes on topic.
awesome teacher- a little off the wall but you'll definitely want to come to class.  very funny!

I had Shaun at 8am for discussion section. If you know what 8am in college feels like, it is NOT GOOD. But Shaun was always ready to go--very enthusiastic and kept things interesting. He does make everyone participate, so don't expect to sit back and fall asleep. Funny, helpful, and crazy! Take him if you can!

I took his class at Cal state Los Angeles this was his first quarter teaching there. He assigned a lot of reading for each class and gave a quiz at each class meating. If you are taking this class make sure you have time deticated for all the reading (usually a chapter a class and some additional articles) He gives these quizes daily, one self eval
decent prof i learned some
Seminar has been fun and interesting.  I've learned a ton and had a good time doing it.  Great class, great prof.
Class is interesting and entertaining and you dont realize how much you learn. Highly recommend taking enwr with Gar - he's great
Pretty good prof.  Grading's a bit tough.
A lot of fun and very helpful.  You learn a lot of useful things in his class.
really a lot of fun, and you learn a lot.  this is impressive for an ENWR

Gar was a great professor.  I learned so much from his class. I thought I knew how to write going into his class, but after leaving it I can really see how much I learned.  He also is very good about office hours and helps you out if you have trouble.  I would definetly recommend him.
A great class, and a great instructor.
I've never enjoyed a politics class as much as I enjoyed this one.  I actually looked forward to coming to class each day.  The course was really hard, but still really fun.
Funny and helpful.  A very good instructor.
I can't imagine a better instructor.
I did not want to take this class. It's a requirement.  But I ended up enjoying it and never missed a day because the instructor made it fun, interesting, and worthwhile.

He makes himself available to try to clarify what he fails to explain well in the first place. The style of writing that he tries to teach is utterly ineffective and useless. The worst part is that no matter what you do, you won't write like he wants. Expect to spend hours many days editting your papers. Even if you write well, this still applies.
A tough class to teach, but he made it good.

I feel like my writing has digressed in this class.  It might be a good topic, but you'll soon find out that the teacher is always unpleasant and lacks office hours.  He does not seem to want to help.

Professor Hoehler-Fatton co-taught this course with Professor Paul Jones and I took it when it was first offered. There is a lot of reading to do each week, but each text was always discussed together in class. She seemed a bit unapproachable at the beginning of the semester, but really warmed up to everyone by the end!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so helpful when it comes to questions about the course, the material, or the department. She helped me switch to a religious studies major and became my advisor because of how helpful she was outside the classroom :) Does grades grammatical and structural problems somewhat seriously but not badly. Took RELG 1500 (wasn't an option)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was definitely my favorite class of the semester-Prof. Hoehler-Fatton is a really engaging lecturer and the material is really interesting.  She really does care about her students success and she was a pretty easy grader.  We did have reading quizzes, but she dropped your two lowest if you did the course evaluation.

LOVED this class, and I'm not even a religious studies major. Prof. Hoehler-Fatton is very knowledgeable and one of the most approachable professors I've ever had. An extremely nice woman. You had to know the material, though, no faking it. She posts a lot of study guides and those really help.

AWESOME CLASS! She is a wonderful prof. who will introduce you to a whole new world. Talk with her outside of class if you can - she is incredibly friendly and has tons of field experience with the Luo people. The work load is not bad, and class + exam are pretty straight forward. Oh! And WATCH the movies - they are well worth it!

This was my favorite class as a first year. There are several readings so you have to pace yourself, but it should not be difficult.  If you take it, be sure to take note of foreign words and their definitions.  It'll open your mind to so many incredible beliefs and customs.  Yep, hope my pitch was good

great readings, lectures parrot the readings a little bit but very interesting class, hard tests, study that**** real good, but besides reading, class is not too intense, i took it as a first-year without any of the prereqs and got a b-, its funny too the readings are kinda feminine-biased
The course is very interesting and the lectures are extremely informative!!
Interesting class, sometimes she can be alittle boring but the material makes up for it, fairly easy class.
she advised a friend and i for a trip to africa and totally made it happen for us.  she's awesome!
She is way too old to be teaching ICE. Super inefficient. The class is a repeat of Stat 2120. Complete waste of my time.

Professor Fraser is, without a doubt, the worst professor or teacher I have had during my academic career. I've never submitted anything to RMP before, but Fraser's incompetence, lack of presence, and overwhelming lack of both communication skills and empathy make her a nightmare. I have had a great experience at UVA but she is the exception.
Really useful/ important class. Hands on andcareer relevant, unlike other stat classes that I've been forced to take. Fraser is helpful in office hours and really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor, really knowledgeable, a marketing expert. Great credentials, an honor to study with her.

Doesnt care about students. Schedules office hours during the universal ice block class session; demonstrating a lack of care to her availability. Notes are incomplete, her book has errors. She will see your hand raised and blow you off. She has now sent a mass email to her students saying she will no longer answer her email (its finals week). Lazy
Prof Fraser is nice and always willing to help.  Go to office hours, and the class isn't that hard.
Course is manageable if you pay attention. Fraser is quirky and nice. Go to office hours.

Professor Wall is a very sweet woman who is really passionate about literature. She leads great discussions every class. There was only a one page commentary due once a week and three papers which she gives you very personal feedback about. She is the kindest woman who knows what she's talking about and is happy to share her time with anyone.

Dr. Wall is a most delightful woman who makes a high level class essentially like a relaxed book club where you share whatever you want with the group. She is brilliant and witty, so if you're interested in the 18th Century this is a must take. Lots of reading and fairly standard papers.

I seriously LOVE this woman. Her enthusiasm, dry wit, and love of learning make it so enjoyable to watch her speak, but she's also great about keeping discussions very interactive even in a larger class. Yes there's a lot of reading, but even the less glamorous stuff becomes infinitely more meaningful when she brings it to life. Huge fan!!
Awesome prof.   She know her stuff and is very supportive.  I would definitely take another class from her!

She is an amazing teacher. I kind of signed up for her class by accident, but it became one of my favorites! There's a lot of reading and most of it is boring, but she is able to take would-be boring material and make it incredibly fun and interesting. Take her class!
Shy at first, but very knowledgable and supportive of student's insight. She likes to choose really long novels for her classes though!
No Comments
One of the best UVa English has!  Cynthia Wall not only knows her material, she knows how to TEACH.  Her class was never dull, and she was supportive of student research.
Avoid her lectures!  I hear she's better in seminar, but her 382 lectures were unbearable.  Some of my friends actually came to class to see who was lecturing, and left if it was her turn!
QA is not the most interesting topic, but Gasman explains things well and is always willing to help.
QA is an important topic but it is soooooooooo boring. She's a very nice woman but I had serious trouble staying awake. She is great at answering e-mails quickly.. though sometimes you're not clear.

Gasman is interesting...She's a great lady, but really can't teach.  Try and get on her good side, which will at least make the class bearable.  Be prepared to spend a LOT of time on homework assignments, and to get frustrated.  There's no way of avoiding this class- just try to enjoy her sense of humor if you can :)

She doesn't teach the topics very well, but the class is very easy to get an A in, mainly because she will give you the answers if you just go to office hours. She's a very easy grader and just wants you to show enthusiasm about the subject. QA assignments take FOREVER but they aren't necessarily difficult.
i have nothing positive to say. just awful
She is not the most organized, but she is very nice and willing to help.  Most complaints are due to the SPSS program, but it really isn't that difficult to learn if you are decent with computers.
She is a very nice person. The only problem is she doens't know how to teach.
She grades inconsistently and arbitrarily. She is confusing and makes no sense. Everyone works in the lab all night trying to make sense of her assignments. Stay away if you can.
the most confused professor ever! Very often does not make any sense. Is amusing at times because of her quirkiness but that isnt incentive enough to take the class. Avoid of possible.

terrible, makes mistakes all the time in class and usually looks confused; if you know anything about statistics you can do cicles around her and the material - most difficult part is getting to know the software
Avoid at all costs.

Kinney isn't winning any teaching awards. I heard good things, but I wish I'd dropped after the first day. His class is a place for him to talk. He gives no feedback and doesn't seem to care about the material we're supposed to be studying. If you can handle sitting through him rambling, give it a shot, but don't expect to learn anything.

I truly hated this course despite loving reading and writing. The prof has unclear grading standards and only graded one of the three assignments. The assignments were weighted 25, 50, 25. The lectures consisted of the prof rambling on about the book, with no clear organization, no connection to any assignment, and no relevance to the student.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is brilliant, but you need to be well-read and intelligent to keep up with him. He can be hard to follow, but he is the smartest person I've ever met. His classes are absolutely worth taking. He is also incredibly helpful one on one. Thought-provoking, astounding--the perfect absent-minded professor.

Prof. Kinney's lectures are impossible to follow due to his heavy use of unnecessary use of "educated" language.  Also, he starts on a point and then completely jumps to another subject without completing his initial claim.  AVOID!!!

If you cna fight through the the fog of flowery language you might learn something.  Very disorganized, lectures jump from one topic to another without following any coherent sequence.  Very nice man, however.

Seemingly disorganized as a professor. You really, really have to pay attention to get the two or three true kernels of insight from each lecture. Doesn't use the text much. Very open to helping students, though, and very thorough...

I do not recommend taking a class from Mr. Kinney.  While he is a very nice person, his lectures are usually extremely difficult to follow.  He arrives late to class every day and also runs at least 5 minutes over.  There are 2 weeks left in the semester and he hasn't returned one graded paper to anyone in the class.

I agree with everything the person before me said. There was not enough discussion- his response to every comment was "[pause] I think that's useful..." and then moving on to more lecturing. He's a really good guy though, understanding and helpful.

His classes were hard to stay awake in. He has a hard time engaging the class, and talks more than he lets other talk. We read too many books in too short a time, and we did very few close readings.  However, he is lenient if you need to turn in a late paper.

This course is definitely as hard as you make it. Devin Donovan uses specifications grading instead of a "normal grading" system. I really feel that this helped me become less stressed over my writing and performance in this course. I highly recommend this course to fulfill your ENWR requirement, or to just take for fun!

Prof. Donovan is one of the best professors I've had. He is very passionate about what he does and he is willing to go the extra mile to see you succeed. It's one few writing courses I've genuinely enjoyed. Our final project was to create a video out of something we enjoy doing (+ a few other things of course). It doesn't get better than that!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you get the chance, Professor Donovan is definitely the best Professor to take an ENWR class with. Even for a student who isn't specifically passionate about writing, Professor Donovan's genuine passion and care for his students and sharing his love of writing makes this class extremely inspiring. An absolutely incredible Professor!

I really love Professor Donovan. He is so understanding and he will understand if you need an extra day or two to turn in your essays, just let him know beforehand. He doesn't grade harshly in my opinion, but even if he does, he allows you to rewrite essays to get a better grade and it does work. He's very caring a kind professor. Take his class.

Prof Donovan is great. He truly wants you to have a takeaway from his class and become a better writer- to which I did. The class can be tedious in the topics you talk about, but he is still worth taking. You don't exactly know your grade throughout the semester, just a general idea w certain feedback. It really depends on your final portfolio.

Professor Donovan was a fantastic First Writing prof. Genuinely felt like he cared about every student in the class, and he was super receptive to whatever manner in which you wanted to approach an assignment. I took Contemplative Writing and would absolutely take his class again if I could. A fair amount of writing but it never felt like too much.

I cant say enough about how caring Donovan is. His transfer ENWR class was truly inspirational and helped me learn so much about myself despite me not taking the class seriously at first. Theres a strong focus on revision and growing as a learner and the class isnt difficult in the traditional sense because theres so much freedom in the assignments

The class topic was Writing as Mindful Practice. It was a lot of BSing your way through the class at the beginning but less as it went on. Papers were interesting to write once you understood the prompt but fairly difficult to get to that point. If you're looking for an easy A for your First Writing Requirement, look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: His topics for his ENWRs are really applicable to every day life and writing - not super specific topics like some other ENWRs. Donovan really stresses discussion and making every student feel valued in class. Great guy who has a vision of how he wants his students to improve.

Prof. Donovan's class does provide inspirations for writing. However, if your intention of having a writing course is to fulfill requirement, I do not recommend you to take his course for the workload is heavy. Also, discussions are usually tedious and sometimes become arguments between two and three students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's a decent instructor. Could be worse. On the other hand, could be much better. Lectures are painfully boring at times. He's not very good at posting assignments at least three assignments were posted very late the night before they were due. Overall, I would stay away from him unless you really need a writing requirement.

Professor Donovan was awesome! He was very flexible and accommodating to what the class' needs were, and he was totally open to new ideas. He was very invested in us and wanted everyone to do well, and loved hearing about people's opinions. He was always prepared with new, interesting readers and is a great at paper feedback. Would recommend!

Topic: The Art of Persuasion This class  will make you think. It isn't as easy as writing a boring and traditional English essay. He wants you to understand why you're arguing what you're arguing; why anyone should care.  Class discussions can be a bit hard to grasp, but they always tie back to how to authors can make an effective paper.

Don't take this course! She is overly serious about an Engagement topic; must complete assignments (long readings and movie) before every class to write a response. She grades your responses very strictly. She DOES watch you if you participate or not. At the end, you must make a zine including 5 entries with a group AND a final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. McGrady is likeable personality-wise, but in relation to the class I did not really enjoy her. The material was quite abstract and she did not explain it very well. Also, SO MUCH of what she yaps about in class is a lie. She would reference historical and current events and I'd fact check them for them to be wrong! Her political bias is clear
Great Joan of Arc class, passionate professor! Would take again, not too difficult and the professor does not believe in exams.

Deborah is my absolute queen, the class was always exciting and heavy with discussion in the best way. There was always a lot of reading, but if you are clever enough you can get by without it. Very generous, forgiving, and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my time with her!! She never made me dread coming to class & is definitely a very enthusiastic, knowledgable woman about Joan of Arc & medieval history. The class itself wasn't difficult, just participate, share your opinion & you'll be fine. The history part is probably the larger portion which I really liked! 100% recommend
Really hard on grading. Have certain kind of favaritism towards certain students. especially for females.

Deep is a good and responsive professor. He teaches Probstat in a way that makes the subject easy to understand. The class is quite easy if you take extra time to do practice problems. He also responds to emails quickly and is generally accommodating.

Deep clearly has a passion for this work and clearly tries to help students in every way he can. However, the class structure is completely jumbled. One day he's giving a meaningless lecture, the next you're in a random group with a week to do a project together, then there's a guest speaker, etc.. More homework than expected, but not unmanageable.

Two main things that made this class difficult: the subject and this professor. You have to give 100% of your undivided attention (as you should). However, you have to constantly ask for 1-on-1 help. Lecturing a class is clearly not what he's good at. Barely anyone could understand what he's trying to teach us. Better to go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He is definitely one of the most brilliant people on grounds. He is also very helpful during in-class activities and WeBWork (weekly online homework). However, keeping in mind this was his first time teaching an APMA course, his lecture style had little to no effectiveness. Barely a third of the class came. APMA 3110 tests were extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I have mixed feeling for this instructor. On the one hand, I was introduced to a wide range of topics and learned some useful skills. However, he could improve his explanations of new topics. Sometimes he expects us to self-teach, but when we ask questions he looks at us like he thinks we aren't trying.

I don't even know how to describe this class other than unorganized, unhelpful, and one of my least favorite classes I've ever taken. Maiti seems to have little clue to how to actually teach, and have no classroom management skills. He yells at us for not asking questions, but then yells at us for not knowing the answer to the questions we do ask.

Outstanding professor. Homework is not too heavy, and classes are entertaining. Materials are well-covered during class time. Although I'm not a music major, it is an enjoyable experience to take his class.

Professor DeVeaux is an entertaining guy, and the textbook (that he wrote) is beautifully done. It's definitely not an easy A, though. The listening portions for the midterm and final exam are tricky, especially if you don't have a musical background. DO NOT wait until the last minute to listen to the material - it takes time to absorb what's

Professor Deveaux is by far the kindest professor I've met at UVA. Go to him if you have any problem, even if it doesn't have to do with class. He actively looks out for you. Go to his office hours for help with assignments- readings aren't always clear but he is. Make him your best friend if you're a music major! He's the music DUP (look it up).

Deveaux is by far the best professor I have had at UVA. His lectures are very entertaining and he is hilarious. He mixes in lecturing with playing music himself in order to keep you interested. The tests are not too difficult but you do need to read the chapter outlines and go to lecture. Definitely take this class!

I had History of Jazz with Dr. DeVeaux 23 years ago, and it still stands out as one of the best classes I took at UVA.  I'm rating him now because RMP did not exist when I was in school, and the music I learned about in his class was life-changing for me, even though I was not a music major.  Thank you, Dr. D., for making the last 23 years richer!

Deveaux teaches with his old powerpoints he's very familiar with. He gives cool piano examples to help the class understand what he's saying better. Read the textbook (which is basically all his powerpoints are on) & you'll do fine. Listening can be a bit tricky for beginners but not impossible if you keep up with them too. I enjoyed this class!

Deveaux plays the piano during class and gives tons of musical examples. The tests have a listening and history portion. The history is easy if you memorize his powerpoint. The listening wasn't too bad either and my highest musical experience is middle school orchestra. You also have 2 papers, but I also had some help from the TA, so it's not bad.

This class was easy if you studied hard. I enjoyed listening to the jazz music and the discussions were helpful and not too bad. The papers were a little difficult but the tests were not very hard. Good class overall. I recommend it if you are at all interested in music.

DeVeaux is remarkable. He has incredible passion, energy, and knowledge that he always brings to lecture. His tests are not too difficult; a few of the listening questions can be a bit ridiculous, but overall they were fair. He is truly one of the best professors at the University.
Proessor Deveaux is the bomb.  Go to lectures and you'll learn everything you need.
Hard class, the description saying musical background is unnecessary is false.  He has unfair grading, and unfair tests.

Interesting class.  a little difficult if you dont know anything about jazz or music, and requires a lot more studying.  tests can be difficult.  great professor, really goofy and plays the keyboard a lot during class to explain things.  essays and concert reports definitely boost your grade because the exams are somewhat hard.  overall , loved it.

Deveaux is great at teaching you the material without it ever getting boring. He includes tons of videos and sound clips throughout his presentations that really make them fun and interesting. he is also funny when he plays the piano for you.

DeVeaux is a funny, enjoyable professor. He knows the material well and is brilliant at teaching. I recommend this class to anyone remotely interested in jazz...it takes in-depth exploration through the history of jazz, from New Orleans Jazz to Avant-Garde Jazz and Fusion. You'll learn about many different artists and songs.

Prior musical experience is needed or, at the very least, makes the class much easier as listening examples are on each test. Great lecturer. Obvious he loves his topic. I thoroughly enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Took this class to knock out some requirements, was way better than what I was expecting.  Deveaux is very clear about what he wants, and he tries to make things as clear easy as possible.  Definitely take this class.  Obviously some musical background will be helpful, but not at all necessary to appreciate what is being taught.

great class for people with musical backgrounds and an ear for different scales, individuals' tonality, and eras of jazz.  Don't have to come to class or even read the text book consistently.  beware if you don't have a good ear for music patterns or identifying particular instruments amongst the mess.

Obviously, there's an advantage to people with a good ear for music, but a lot of the material is still based purely on the history and facts. Overall, if you put in a solid amount of work into this class, you'll do fine. I love jazz, so I got a lot out of it, but I was admittedly lazy at times and didn't do as well as I'd liked because of that.

Deveaux is a decent professor, considering I had no previous knowledge in jazz.  However, don't expect to not work, especially if you're not familiar with musical terms.  The class overall was quite interesting and instructful in basic music.  The material becomes dry later in the semester, but Deveaux has good power points.

funny guy and always available to help, even via email. it takes an effort to familiarize yourself with different jazz styles, but you end up learning a lot just by listening. even the professor recommends taking it as credit/no credit, unless it is to fulfill a requirement, i would definitely do so.

I would DEFINITELY NOT recommend this class if you have no musical experience or a good ear for distinct music styles.  LIstening on exams count as 40%, and all exams are cummulative.  I would say jazz-lovers would enjoy this class, but I completely regret it, and it turned out to be my lowest grade - total GPA downer.

Great class overall He is passionate about the subject matter, sometimes brings live bands into class for demonstrations. There are 2 midterms and a Final, and 2 papers. All three are MC and are EXACTLY from the powerpoints. The only difficult part were the listenting portions (about 40% ) of each exam. TAs make or break the class--get Joe or Sara!

I was pleasantly surprised by this class.  I only took it to fulfill two requirements, but it was much better than I was expecting.  The exams were straightforward and easy, lectures weren't too boring, the professor was nice and sometimes funny, and I really learned a lot about a genre of music I previously had no interest in.

Scott DeVeaux single-handedly reawakened my interest in music, and turned me on to a genre that I had previously ignored.  His lectures are fairly by-the-book, but he still makes the material interesting.  The hardest part on the tests are the listening examples.  As said before, I would not take this class unless you have some musical background.

If you have no music background, the class seems somewhat overwhelming at first. But his exams are fair, they're taken straight from his powerpoints. If you are good at memorization or just sweet like me, you'll find it easy to pick up even if you know nothing about music. The papers are tougher than the exams mainly because the TA's grade them tou
one of the classes I've enjoyed the most so far. Deveaux is such a cool guy! a must take if u're interested in jazz

I loved this class - Deveaux is a little out there sometimes, but always hilarious. Coursework is light (if you come to lecture you don't need to do the lecture readings), and the tests come right from his ppts - its basically memorization. However, if you have no music background, you might find it hard
something about talking while playing music made it difficult for me to understand a single thing he was saying.  More interested in name dropping all the legends he's had the priviledge to meet.

Probably one of the best classes I've taken at U.Va. Deveaux knows so much about the subject and it really shows when he plays random examples during class to help you understand the underlying technical aspects of the music.  I DEFINITELY recommend this class to anyone interested in jazz! So good, SO easy!

this class is definitely perfect for you if you have taken at least band is middle school and remember what notes are.  otherwise, if you read you should do fine. easiest class test-wise I've had so far... just do the reading and remember it well- you should get a good grade.  don't listen to anyone who said this class was bad.  it's awesome!!

If you know anything about music and especially jazz the class should be a breeze. Go to 2 concerts and write a page on them and 2 other short papers. Exams are easy though and all the info from class he puts up on the website as power point slides. You really don't need more than the slides. Readings are short and only important for discussion.
amazing class.  i recommend it highly.

Don't take the class. He's an odd and weird guy who in recent year, has made it his purpose to make the class difficult instead of intersting.  People worry about this class likes its Organic Cheminstry instead of enjoying the music like they should be.
didn't lie but didn't tell the whole story
Class could be boring, especially since we found out later he would post all of the slideshows, but material was fairly interesting and tests were alright.  Easy non-western perspective though.

I had some prior musical technical knowledge but no real knowledge of jazz, and I'm looking at a probable B in the class. It isn't too hard, but requires a lot of out of class work to learn the musical styles and textures.
prof. deveaux makes jazz inaccessible and incomprehensible to the non-musician.  Two five-page papers and concert reports don't help either.

Deveaux is aweful.  His crusade to make History of Jazz a hard class ruins the appeal of jazz music.  Spends first 3 weeks solely on technical terminology.  I can't understand how he relates to jazz -- he's old and stuffy; nothing like the dynamic musicians he decribes.

This class is not hard if you spend any time studying at all. Lectures are sometimes boring but his quirky personality and passion for jazz add interest. So, he has a few problems with organization and technology. It was an intersting class and he is a helpful professor.
Great professor--he's not a teacher who the average student will understand or relate to, but for the more quirky student, I definitely recommend this course and professor.

Think it's easy, guess again.  I took this 3 years ago now and he has made a lot of changes since then, but this class was my worst grade at UVA and really just turned my interest in jazz into hatred.

like everyone has said before, you have to have music experience or be very interested in jazz, b/c it is very difficult to try and listening and determine which kind of jazz it is if you have no prior knowledge.  he doesnt really attempt to teach you the difference either.
not good
As the last person says, if you have any musical knowledge, it's easy.  If you don't it's hard as all get out.  But then again, I have a little knowledge of music, and it's still hard as all get out.

this class is an Easy A if u know ANYTHING about jazz.  wouldnt recommend it to ppl who dont have any prior musical knowledge.  notes are clearly displayed on powerpt, test questions taken right from them.  listening selections also on tests, again, not hard at all if u know anything about music.
Not a good professor. Stay clear of him. His teaching style is one of the worst. Its basically 50 minutes of straight note taking. Cant explain stuff any.

Despite having difficulties with computers, Deveaux is a great professor.  Each lecture was worth my time in one way or another, either for educational value, entertainment, or both.  The course can be a little more difficult if you don't have music exp. but it's still a great one to take.
My favorite class.

The man is a nut.  Spends the first 10 minutes of class trying to get the "technology" to work--the TAs get frustrated and end up doing it for him.  Kind of makes class funny.  Lectures are nebulous and circuitous.   Despite common belief, the class is NOT EASY!

Deveaux circles the airport in his teaching method.  I cannot determine whether his complete ineptitude at powerpoint or the useless course packet was his greatest flaw.  Musical experience is a huge benefit to this course; this made this course one of the easiest 'A's I've ever received at UVA.

I would NOT recommend this course to other students.  Upon enrolling in this course, I was under the impression that "no prior musical knowledge/experience" was needed as a prerequisite for the course.  I was sadly misled, as nearly 50% of the exams are listening (which immediately presents a disadv

Ok, this man was obciously born before computers.  He has serious issues with powerpoint and finds the best method of fixing them to be talking to himself.  Overall, everybody thinks this class is easy, I think no.  However, excellent way to do nonwestern perspectives.
AWESOME
turned borderline jazz fan into bonafide jazz lover. he really loves what he teaches and it shows; he's also funny without even realizing. Great TAs (especially Jeff Decker) and good class overall.
Easy and interesting. Take for Nonwestern perspectives req.
Very good teacher, very interesting (and easy) course.
Yes, this class is easy. Very worth it. It is not difficult to prepare for the tests at all. READ HIS WEBSITE NOTES. The course packet is of minimal importance.

Good teacher, knows his stuff and subject is interesting. Class isnt that hard, tests very straight forward. It's worth taking for the non-western persp. and fine arts requirements, or just credit/no credit.
No Comments
I'm not a big fan of jazz, but Deveaux managed to make the class fairly interesting. The tests are pretty straight forward, and the class has ample resources online to aid in studying.

I loved Harman. I had him for 1810 and it was the best chemistry class I've ever taken. The content was difficult and some of it he didn't have time to cover in class, so we had to do it outside of class. Other than that, there was no homework outside of class. The class is heavily curved, I ended with around a 70 on all exams and ended with an A!
Professor Harman's chemistry class is challenging but rewarding. His infectious enthusiasm makes the lectures lively and engaging, even at 8am. Attend class, use Unstuckstudy, and you'll excel.

Dare I say overrated. Look, he's a polite man. Yes, his office hours are extremely helpful. Unless you have another class at that time. In that case, you'll miss critical information. Did I mention there's no powerpoint, so if you don't write your notes fast enough, the information might as well be gone with the wind. [80s series still worth it].
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
My favorite class I've ever taken. Material is very tough but Harman provides plenty of resources and generous ways to get points back on tests with corrections for 1/2 points back. Office hours are very useful and accessible (save time right after lecture to go).

Beware of lab 1811!! It is very difficult and tedious, take 1411 lab w/ 1810 lecture

Amazing class. I have no interest in majoring in chem (am premed) but this has me leaning heavily toward a minor or taking more intricate classes. As an engineering major, I am also very happy i decided for the 1411 lab with this, I've heard brutal things.

Harman has influenced me to a degree where I aspire to be as excited to talk about a topic as he talks about chemistry. He speaks with such enthusiasm for the topic and inspired me to major in chemistry. If you are invested in chemistry and want to have a great time learning it with an easy-to-approach and reasonable professor, take his classes.
This class almost made me want to become a chemist.

Chemistry at 8am might not be the preferred, prof. Harman is so passionate about chemistry. Although you might be very interested in chemistry, beware, it is an extremely difficult class for those with an advanced chemistry background (ap chem or the equivalent). So if you don't have that chemistry background, you're up for a challenge.

Professor Harman is the most gifted instructor I have met through all of my years in school. While the course content is admittedly extraordinarily difficult, his incredible teaching ability makes the class worth its rigor. He truly cares about his students and has a genuine love for teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Harman is just awesome! He is freakishly knowledgable and a very gifted lecturer; the fact that I was fully awake and tuned in during the 8am lectures speaks volumes. His tests are very difficult and they get progressively harder, so maximize points on the first two exams because the final will be brutal. Curves are generous, though!

I strongly recommend this for Engineering students who only need 1 semester of chemistry. 1810 was awesome, but I really would not want to take 1820 next semester. You will love Dean Harman and honestly it's hard not to get a B+ to an A in this class if you try. BEWARE of 1811 (Lab section). If you're in engineering take 1810 with 1411 lab.
Great professor who is passionate and wants to help you! Lectures are fairly interesting too for 8 ams! Key to doing well in this class is attending lectures AND consistently going to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Harman is a great teacher, but the style may not be for everyone. Lectures are fascinating, but tend to be about the theory behind something rather than how to use it on an exam. You only go over how to do the questions as homework/with TAs in discussion, unless you go to office hours. However, if you work/study hard, you'll be rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Harman is a god among men.1810 is a very difficult class but the material is fascinating and Harman shows he cares about his students. 3 tests at 25% each, but you get half points back for corrections and he curves the grades at the end. Definitely one of the best professors I've had so far, and NO you don't need to take AP Chem to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Harman is hands down the nicest professor you'll have in college; he takes time to teach you, whether individually or in a group. If you did really well in AP or IB Chem, then this class isn't a bad idea. It's fast paced, but TAs or the professor will help you. Warning: test average 60-70%, but he offers corrections for half credit back.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely phenomenal, do not be scared to take this class, you will get a B+ if you just try. But if you care about GPA, beware of 1811 lab and Professor Sen Zhang

NOTE FOR INCOMING FIRST YEARS
This post is NOT for Professor Harman (he is good), rather I want to warn you before entering the course. Please check out the 1/5 rating for Professor Serbulea for additional information (I am on a character limit here).You should not take the 1800 sequence. The 1800 sequence community is very snobbish and elite. ...

You could never miss a day of Harman's lectures or you would be so hopelessly lost. However, if you put in the work, take notes, rewrite the notes like he says, you will be fine. Going to the discussion groups was helpful because a lot of what was there was also on the test in some way or another. I was a hard class. if you work you will be ok

Harman is great! Class is hard and you better work hard, but if you're at all interested in chemistry, I highly recommend. He also curves the grades at the end, so it's not *that* bad at the end of the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very difficult with only 3 exams, but he does offer test corrections.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Online 1810 was still a great class! Professor Harman is super knowledgeable and his office hours were very very helpful. Difficult tests but prepares you well for future chem classes.

Professor Harman's class is largely graded on effort. Homework and test corrections are graded on completion which gives you an advantage in grading. However, his lectures and presentation of information are disorganized. I had credit for gen chem and took this as a refresher and I do not think it really prepares you for organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Harman is a fantastic person and teacher! Chem 1810 was as engaging as it could be online, and Harman worked hard to make it fun for first-years this fall. The class is not a walk in the park, but Harman is there to help out and you get corrections on the exams which is a lifesaver. 1230982/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Harman is amazing. Lectures were tough at 8 am, but always engaging and he cares so much about each student. Office hours are great. Exams are VERY challenging, but usually, a 65% will be an A/A- due to corrections/curve. This proves that he really wants students to attempt to apply what they learned on the exams. Work hard, you'll get an A.

Honestly, such a genuinely nice guy. His class is very difficult, but he is so caring about his students and his office hours are incredibly helpful. The tests are like nothing you've ever seen but he does allow for test corrections, so if you go to lectures and ask for help you'll probably do fine. Taking his class is definitely worth taking 1810.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Greatest chem prof I've had here. HIs office hours were like a second lecture

Harman is a fantastic teacher, especially since he rarely teaches other classes besides advanced intro chem, but this class is hard unless you want to major in chem. It's doable, but not for the lazy or faint of heart.

Harman is awesome! This class is not easy, and the tests definitely require studying, but you will come out of this with the best chemistry understanding in the world. He is such a clear lecturer and is totally invested in making sure everybody understands the concepts. He sends out plenty of practice tests and review sheets to help. Great class!

Prof. Harman is awesome. He devotes half of his lecture days to teaching & helping students afterwards. Expert in his field, really smart guy. Has high expectations, evidenced by the exam. The course is as challenging as it's said to be but also very rewarding. If you don't understand something (sometimes everything) it's your job to ASK QUESTIONS.

Professor Harman really does care about students, but you still need to work hard in the class. The best thing you can do for yourself is to ask questions and attend office hours if you are stuck. It is not an easy course, but If you put effort in, you will attain great results.

This was the greatest class I have taken just because of the professor. It was definitely a tough class, but no problem with dedication. If you are choosing between the 800 series or the 400 series for chemistry, this class is a must, even if you choose to drop to the 400 series afterwards. Take this professor's class. You won't get another chance.

He's an excellent teacher. He's clear and is very willing to help you with anything you're struggling with. However, the class is really difficult. Although he's great, I would still recommend getting supplementary help. I used clutch prep and ended up with an A. But I really had to be dedicated.
The class is hard, but the professor explains everything very clearly. He has made Chemistry fun. Definitely should take the class.

This class is VERY difficult. It is fast paced and the first month consists of learning that everything you ever knew about Chemistry was a lie; however, Harman is an amazing professor. He makes himself available and explains things as clearly as possible. This class was definitely worth it.
This class is by no means easy, but Harman is one of the best teachers out there. He has a deep understanding of the topic and his passion for it makes the class so much more interesting.
One of the best teachers I have ever had! He really knows how to present a topic in a way that everyone will understand. Hard material, but phenomenal professor!

Fantastic! All grades are curved, so if you work hard, it is easy to get an A. I'm a science person, but didn't think I'd like chem and he made it one of my favorite classes. He is the best professor I have had at UVA!

This was a very hard class, and very competitive, but I would still take it again just because Harman was such a great professor. He is very clear in his lectures, so clear in fact that you don't even need the book. The tests are very hard, but if you put in a lot of time, you can expect an ok grade.
Incredibly helpful, probably THE best chem prof on the face of the earth!
Best teacher ever!!!1

Harman genuinely cares about every student doing well in the class. His lectures are so clear that you never have to read the textbook. I took good notes during lectures, went to office hours, and ended up with an A.
Extremely Helpful professor. The number of times I have not understood something he has explained can be counted on one hand.  It was his birthday yesterday and we all sang him happy birthday.

Extremely difficult class, but extremely helpful&interesting teacher. Grading based on take home problem sets (group work), and hour-tests (solo). Great lecturer, covers all of material in class, available in office hours. Could not have done it without him. Grades curved, B+=average, b/c honors.

Best chemistry professor in the whole university; will spend hours discussing research and advising students for which he has no obligation to do so (i.e. not his major advisees, etc.).  His lectures are crystal clear -- he should write his own textbook.

Professor Harman is a very genuine professor who truly wants all of his students to succeed. He is the reason why I am so in love with chemistry. Even thought it is honors chem, he makes it all worth it.

Lectures aren't strictly "mandatory", but might as well be.  Harman can (and will) explain anything better than any textbook.  I literally didn't open mine the whole semester.  One of the most dedicated, knowledgeable and dare I say fun professors, especially for a high level class.  If you make it to the end of the 80 series, a very welcome reward

Harman is an awesome chemistry teacher; he really does everything he can to make difficult material understandable. Exams are challenging, but I'm not a chem person, and even with that Harman made it so much easier. Definitely take chem with him!
HESSSSS AWESOMMMMEE! he's a really nice guy:-)

Harman was awesome!  I loved going to his class, even though I didn't do very well.  He is very enthusiastic, and a fun lecturer.  He doesn't have a lot of notes to copy down, which was both great and slightly unhelpful.  His quizzes weren't too hard; Chemistry is.

Amazing teacher and his lectures are very interesting. I really reccomend chemistry with him.His lectures along with reading the book will get you the A. His quizes arent hard if you know the material. Most of the questions are direct.

Due to popular belief, he is not ACTUALLY a DEAN(that's his name). Anyways, I prayed to not get Metcalf for CHEM and I got Harman. Harman is one of my favorite professors at UVA so far. He uses funny and useful annecdotes to help explain his topic. It is a very difficult class if you have not taken AP CHEM before.

Professor Harman was awesome.  Quizzes and final were both lecture-based, so go to class!  I learned a lot using the textbook and watching Thinkwell recreationally too.  Take chemistry with Harman because he is always enthusiastic and makes the subject fun.

Absolutely wonderful teacher who  is genuinely interested in the material. If you take this class, you might spend hours thinking about problem set questions but somehow they will never become boring or tedious. Get a study group! PS: This class along with 181L will definitely consume your life. The curve helps everyone; 40% of the class got an A!

Probably the best lecturer I've ever seen at UVA.  He teaches the material such that any reasonably intelligent human could understand, and he's genuinely excited about the topic.  He's generous with office hours, and if you stick with him as you go, there's really no way you can't do well.  Harman's the way to go.

Harman is the nicest professor I've ever met. If you ever go to office hours he makes a real effort to help you understand the material, and he takes even the most asinine questions sincerely. His tests are more conceptual than math based, so make sure to get that comprehension down.

Prof. Harman is one of the best science teachers at UVA! He loves what he's teaching and after a semester, so will you. Tests are challenging but relevant and he tells you exactly what to study. Thinkwell is really helpful as well

By far, the best professor i have ever had.  If you have the chance and you like chemistry, DEFINITELY take this class. His lectures are very clear and he only tests you on what he's explained to you. He can answers any and all of your questions and no one leaves the lecture not understanding the material.

The class is difficult, but that comes with taking chem 181.  Genuinely interested in teaching the subject, and will try his best to make sure you get a good grade.  Grades with a fairly good curve.  Nobody rocks the stache like Harman.
If you have to take chem, definitely make sure you get Harman. The material is difficult but he provides a million different study tools for the students. Thinkwell is GOOD!
Great professor... take this class if you have to take chemistry.
not so good

Chemistry in itself isn't an easy subject, but his lectures are engaging and even funny sometimes; he is definitely the best lecturer for 141.   His quizzes are hard and even tricky though, so its a give and take.  Overall a really nice guy, and approachable
Harman is AMAZING and by far the best in the Chemistry department. Take his class if you have the chance!
Harman is a great professor that explains everything very clearly. He's approachable and is really helpful. Be sure to study and prepare for the quizzes because they can be challenging.

Professor Harman is the best!  He makes chemistry really interesting and he is one of the best teachers I have ever had.  He really cares about his students.  Chem itself is pretty hard, but he does his best to make it understandable for everyone.
He explains things well. His voice is sooo nice sounding too so its hard to be mad when you get a bad grade.
hardest class of my life. i cried after every quiz. chem is most def not my thing. harman is all about CONCEPTS. and everything is from effing thinkwell.
UGH - chemistry at uva is ridiculous. It's not even right. Harman was alright - he knew what he was doing - but i still didn't learn much. Uva pretty much sucks. steer clear.

Although I got a C in his class, he is one of the best professors, pound for pound, that I have had at UVA.  He explains concepts clearly, which is good, but can lull you into a false sense of security sometimes.  Go to his office hours!  His quizzes can catch you by surprise sometimes, but if you prepare & you're good at science it's not too bad.

I loved this class.  Despite his challenging tests and the heartache one caused me, I enjoyed every second of it.  Lectures are never dull, and for the most part, he's easy to understand. The tests are definitely not easy, however.  He LOVES conceptual, analytical questions, so you really have to know your material like the back of your hand.  I wo

hated chem. LOVED HARMAN. He was SOOOOOOO FABULOUS at office hours. I was struggling, went in for help, and got a B on the final (better than the C- i was used to) Anyways...he totally loves his job. HIGHLY RECCOMENDED

He's so cute! You can tell he loves what he does and wants you to care also. He blows hydrogen balloons up in class and poors liquid nitrogen on the floor (my favorite)!! Take his class... I only wish he taught 142

Harman is MONEY and he's sexy.  Don't get anyone else.  I thought the class was easy but lots of other people struggled and I already had credit from AP Chem.  If you study, watch the thinkwell videos and pay attention you should do well.

Very intelligent teacher, Ph.D. in Chemistry from Stanford. He also is a producer of the book's tutorial cds (thinkwell).  A very funny and helpful teacher, he deserves 5/5 stars. Class is not easy as it is a weed-out class for premeds, but he's willing to help you as much as he can.
Great professor.  Quizzes are tough, but he does a lot to make sure that everyone understands the material.  Will meet in office at almost anytime.
This man is the greatest teacher I've ever met.
He is a fatherly and gifted teacher.

Harman makes chemistry really interesting.  He relates material to stories, and he does experiments in class.  He's also concerned most with concepts rather than the boring math part of chemistry.  Definitely get a class with Harman if you can!!!

TAKE HARMAN!!! You will absolutely love him!  He makes Chemistry interesting and fun, even if you are just wanting to get through it. He explains everything with helpful examples in an exciting way (sometimes blowing things up). He was awesome! I only wish he taught CHEM142. You will not regret taking him!!
his class was fun and he had great stories. quizes are tough, but they are the easiest of all the other chem teachers
Harman IS a great guy, and tries to make lectures fun and interesting, but by no means was the class easy... quizzes do not always follow what you've learned in lecture.
Best chem professor i have ever had. He makes class fun and offers a lot of help. Take Harman
Phenomenal professor. Very clear. Given the other options, Harman is DEFINITELY your best bet!

Harman's specialty is clarity: he uses examples to make sure everyone is on the same page all the time.  The class is pretty easy, and it's also fun: he'll do experiments or tell a joke or a story just to entertain.  Definitely a great teacher.

Harman is a good teacher.  A bit too easy though.  You can study the night before the exam or do homeworks the night before, and still earn an A.  Great teacher, nice guy, but not much of a challenge.

Excellent teacher! By far the best lecturer I've ever had. Clear, concise, funny, and interesting. Cares about students, nice person as well as awesome teacher. Other teachers guest taught our class, so trust me, IF AT ALL POSSIBLE, TAKE HARMEN!!!!

OMG, Professor Harman is absolutely wonderful! He wants nothing more than for everyone to get a 100% on each and every test, and does everything within his power to get you there. And he's funny. And clear. And concise. HARMAN ROCKS!!

Imagine witnessing the full brilliance of one thousand simultaneously exploding supernovas.  Dean Harman is that spectacle in the form of a jolly, mustachioed man.  He will make you see the world for the first time.
He is amazing. Before his class I was afraid of chemistry, and now I love it!  If you need to take chemistry, take it from him.

He is an amazing teacher! I didn't have a good background at all in chem before i came and i haven't had much trouble in his class. Don't mistake good for easy though. His test are challenging and require studying but he makes the material much easier to understand.
No Comments
Gives as much help as possible for tests, interacts with class during lecture and makes sure as many people understand as possible  GO THINKWELL!
You don't know what a blessing this guy is until you have McGarvey. Harman's very clear, very helpful, and thoroughly cares about his students.

I LOVE HARMAN! he is an AMAZING professor, and he actually takes time out of his VERY busy schedule to hold review sessions- in addition to his office hours! most professors just leave it to the TA's, but harman actually holds the review sessions! & if u need extra help, he's in thinkwell!!!
No Comments

This was the best class I took this semester.  He is an amazing man that actually wants to teach, something hard to find at a research-based institution.  There is no point in taking the 40s series if you can have a class with Harman.  Also, its almost impossible to get lower than a C.
awesome teacher, awesome class
Harman is money!
best teacher ever
Smokin.

One of the best proffs I've had in my life.  He comes across as very interested in your sucess in his class and he definitely makes you feel comfortable asking questions.  I highly recommend him, if you are willing to work hard. 80's series is difficult

Harman is a great professor.  Definetely the best I've ever had, although I haven't had many yet.  I would recommend his class to anyone, even if you just have a passing interest in chemistry (like me).  He explains it so well you can't help but love it.
Prof. Harman is the best professor I have ever had.
His teaching is super-duper.  Makes excruciatingly hard things suddenly appear easy.  Looks like Gene Weingarten...the mustache is a plus.

I never understand why anyone would take Chem 141 and not have Harman.  He is able to make the most difficult topics perfectly clear, and is by far my favorite teacher (and I am taking Econ with Elzinga).
Super hot in a Tom Selleck kind of way!
Looks like the Beastie Boys in the video for "Sabotage." Like he's wearing a disguise. Unbelievable teacher. Taught me to see the world in terms of chemistry.
I love him!
A teacher that actually keeps things interesting.  Grades generously too.
No Comments
His direction, enthusiasm, motivation & charisma are reason enough to attend UVa

The subject matter taught was important. However, the lectures were boring, in-person quiz questions were required daily, and she was very disorganized. I took this class in 2021, when masks were still required, and she was not accommodating for any illnesses (I took an exam with a fever and positive flu result). Not helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher, very knowledgeable, passionate about subject matter. Just put effort into this course and you'll be fine.

Taken during covid, where tests were open note. Super easy, but tbh wouldn't have been hard even if closed note. Lots of other chances for points too--only 50% of your grade was exams, others included participation stuff, quizzes on chapter readings (easiest textbook ever), & a short easy blog post. Prof is super nice and passionate. No final.

I loved Prof Lawrence. To do well, make sure to read the textbook before tests, you have to stay on top of lectures (they are pre recorded) you have a 30 minute discussion during one of the class times, there are three exams and a project. You have a bunch of opportunities to do well. I think this was the best online course Ive taken.
Brutal lectures but attendance is enforced with Learning Catalytics questions. Tests are heavy on arbitrary details. Not nearly as interesting of a course as it appears. Definitely avoid.

Professor Lawrence is absolutely amazing. You can tell that she actually cares about the lectures she gives. The class super informative about climate change, and I've learned a lot. You get graded for participation in class by answering questions on Learning Catalytics. There are 4 exams (final isn't cumulative) and a blog post. Not much homework.

Professor Lawrence is a really engaging lecturer that made Climate, You & CO2 an awesome class! You do have to show up to answer learning catalytics questions and read the textbook, but if you do both of those it's almost impossible not to get an A.

easy A/B+! yes you need to go to class, but the tests are generally fair and theres no final for EVSC 1450. She's super enthusiastic about climate change and i liked listening to her. she assigns a lot of homework, but its just busy work like short easy quizzes and forum posts to get you participation points. definitely recommend. dont buy the book

By far my favorite professor at UVA. She is ALWAYS available and quick to email back. Obviously wants to work with students and learn from them, too. If you like environmental science, she would be a great advisor!

The class appears to be easy, and the subject matter is not difficult, but the tests are tested on insignificant details. The lectures tend to be boring, but the guest lecturers are usually great. The curve is AMAZING!

Easy. Professor is the BEST professor I have had here. She is very easy to understand and very kind. She truly loves the subject, and makes class interesting. She is always willing to help you. As long as you come to class and take notes during the lectures you will get a good grade. book helps solidify your understanding but isn't necessary

She's a really nice person and is always there during office hours. You have to go to class to get notes she doesn't put on the powerpoints. Lectures are structured and tests are long but straightforward. I'd recommend this class.

How do I begin to explain the terribleness of this class?  She made you come to lecutre by including stuff on the test that wasn't in the book.  Sleeping, however was the only option in lecture. The tests were SO hard witnessed by the 65-70 averages.  Scoring above the average is impossible if you are not hardcore about the material.  stay away!

This class looked like it could've been a fun and interesting class, but I was definitely wrong.  This teacher is horrible, and her lectures have nothing to do with the tests.  Please save yourself the time and energy of taking this class.  I wish I would've known about her before I signed up!
AVOID THIS CLASS!!! Terrible teacher, she is better at confusing herself than teaching you. Tests are ridiculous

Deborah is a difficult grader, but makes it up by curving.  She is much better in a small class setting rather than the larger ecology lecture.  If you're interested in ecology, her work is interesting and she'll go out of her way to help you.  If you are not really interested in ecology, I would recommend Smith for 320.

Deborah is nice and helps answer questions in office hours- COOL!  However, her tests were incredibly long and difficult.  She is confused herself when teaching which confuses you.  I studied my butt off, went to office hours & someone who never came to class got the same grade mysteriously.
Didn't really like her teaching style, but she was always around if you needed help.
Read the other frown face comments. I hate to be repetitive. The comments on the difficulty of tests and the amount of reading are quite true.

This is the worst teacher I have had yet.  Is pregnant yet cancels class for several days due to having baby.  Tests are bs and material is unexpectedly pointless.  Prepare yourself for some horrible lectures.

nice teacher, but definitely a lot of reading and the midterms cover a lot of material. if youre not an ecology/science person, definitely NOT recommended because its pretty hard to do well on the midterms

Whoa, this class is horrible,boring,hard,unfair AND confusing grading,etc.I expected to learn about conservation tactics,movements,public policy,rather I learned about dirt and the carbon cycle.I studied so much too,but all/non of the above questio suck.

Boring and its the worst class I have ever taken in 3 years at UVa. Tests are inherently unfair in nature, and test what you dont know, rather than what you do know. There is a reason AP tests no longer use all of the above questions. this class=pain.

this is not an easy class...contrary to popular belief, ecology is not a gut class.  the test are outrageous and they are not what is covered in class...and all the questions are in the form of "all of the above, none of the above...")avoid this
Very boring and uninspiring.
Was easy, but not a gut.
No Comments

This is for CS 1110:

Professor stone is a super nice guy who clearly cares about me. I think he would be a great teacher in a smaller setting. In a lecture hall with 100 + students, he's useless. He spends most of class typing stuff into the coding software. He tries to do class discussions, and it doesn't work in a large lecture hall.

Prof Stone is simply not good at giving lectures. He seems to know a lot about coding, but he has a hard time teaching it to others. Lectures are basically him going over the slides and giving confusing explanations. He also didn't record the coding portion of lectures. If you were absent, you couldn't get that information, adding to the confusion.
Hardly teaches and lectures consist of him coding in silence without explaining what's going on
Very difficult. Professors do not answer emails. Office hours are congested. Homework is very vague and exams are very, very difficult.

Stone is a nice man but a little clueless sometimes. He actually does know his stuff quite well; hes just not a very good lecturer. I completely stopped going to lecture about a month into the semester and still ended up with an A+. If you dont mind teaching yourself this course, he's perfectly fine. Otherwise go for Basit or Hott.

This professor is a solid choice. If you do not understand the material he is willing to work with you and give help. The lectures go along well with the reading that is assigned. There are in class activities that are assigned that also help with understanding the material. Overall, he cares very much about students mastery of the material.

I had Professor Stone for CS 2110 and he really takes it upon himself to make sure his students fully comprehend the course material. He differs from all of the lecturers I've had in the extent to which he encourages in-class discussions which was incredibly beneficial to my understanding of the topics and made me genuinely enjoy the class.

Professor Stone gave clear explanations of the material and worked with students in class to make sure they understood challenging concepts. He was accessible outside of class and would even agree to meet with students outside of office hours. He helped students to make sure that they were fairly graded on tests and in-class assignments.

The course itself might sound hard but once you attend his lectures, you can explore the whole new aspect of CS field. The class is engaging and the professor is always ready to answer students' questions. He is certainly one of the best CS teachers I've met

I had Prof. Stone his first semester teaching and I'm so glad I did. Prof. Stone really cares about his students and is interested in their projects inside and outside the classroom. He will advocate for students and takes feedback seriously. If you are struggling, he will do anything he can to help out. I wish I could have him again next semester.
Dean Dass killed my love for creating art.
Best professor I've had at UVA.  Brilliant but abstract thinker--sometimes its hard to decipher what he's trying to tell you.  You end up learning a lot more than printmaking in his classes.
Dean is wonderful.  It's up and down with him, but just have confidence in yourself, take his criticism, and learn from the experience.  Go visit his office hours.
Excellent instructor and mentor
Dass is odd but thorough.

this teacher is extrememly dedicated; he offers plenty of criticism but in a very helpful and diplomatic manner. his enthusiasm is infectious. he takes enormous and unselfish pride in the acheivements of his students. he's outstanding!
No Comments
awesome. nuff said.

Overall pretty good professor. He has a bit of a thick accent and poor handwriting which can be tricky at times. Nonetheless, he's a great teacher and I haven't had any trouble with him at all. His teaching system is also super predictable which is a godsend being able to know exactly the amount of calc work I'll have every week.

Heavy accent but understandable. Easy to reach outside of class. The tests and exams took major part of your scores. Basically, 80% of your grade is based on those. So if you screw up a test, drop it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took ODE course with him and he's one of the best professors I've had and you can tell he loves teaching and educating. I'd recommend him to anyone interested in learning ODEs, as this has been a great positive experience.

Farzad was completely inclusive and welcoming to every person regardless of any status. He was a kind teacher that offered me opportunities to give feedback in class as well as helping during class while his lectures provided thorough examples.

Never expected to like this material and this was my fav class. Dillery is the most passionate guy so he gave great lectures- important material is crystal clear. Super reading heavy, but readings are needed for tests not lectures- you can catch up later. If you're not a history buff, CHOOSE to be engaged in this class and you may really enjoy it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class knowing nothing about Greek history, and am now totally hooked! It should be a literature class, in my opinion, but still amazing. LOTS of reading, but you don't need to do it all so long as you show up to lecture and take good notes. He will always tell you everything you need to know!! Overall, great & entertaining

Professor Dillery highly values attendance and participation (i.e. skipping is a BAD idea in his class). However, for the effort I have put into his class, he has put in exponentially more to make the course material come to life. He is highly respected, immensely knowledgeable, and I am going into my third semester taking a class with him.

Dillery is extremely passionate and knowledgeable, but this can lead to him teaching the information at a level beyond what a 2000 level course should be. Two exams, two essays, and a lot of reading inbetween. You'll do best if you have a real interest in Greek literature, which is all this class is. That being said, if you are interested it's fun.

Great professor! Very knowledgeable about the subject and is very straightforward in lecture (almost always got out about 10 minutes early). Lot's of reading but he goes over the important passages in class. Good class for a literature credit or to learn interesting things about the ancient Greek world

Amazing professor. He's very passionate about it and his explanations are great. There's a lot of reading (but it's a clas course), but most of it is really interesting. One major thing that stands out is that when the TA was sick he did the discussion sections himself, which i've never had that happen before. Love it and had no interest before.

very good teacher, he likes his subject and makes it interesting. A LOT of reading!! 90 pages  to read the day before the exam (that will be on the exam). write down all the quotes he reads in class ( you will have to know them for the exam).

great class and professor. try to get into his discussion! because everything he puts on the exams are from lecture/discussion. reading is extensive but not necessary as long as you take good notes and pay attention. the material can get a bit boring but hes pretty enthusiastic which helps. only grades are 2 papers and 2 exams

Initially I liked Dillery b/c he was so enthusiastic and really interested in helping me at office hours.  My test and paper grades don't reflect this though.  I never really found what he was exactly looking for in papers.  The tests were beasts and the IDs could be random and unpredictable.  A LOT of reading, skip The Histories.
Dillery is a great lecturer, really enthusiastic. the readings may be long sometimes, but as you get used to greek literature more the readings get more interesting. great class, really recommend it
No Comments

This class should be called Greek Literature, not Greek Civilization.  If you are going to take it, be prepared to do a lot of reading.  However, Dillery is extremely enthusiastic and makes a lot of interesting points.  Go to class, get the handouts, and pay attention to every passage he remarks on, because the tests are all passage identification.
energetic professor, willing to look over drafts for papers, very helpful

I really enjoyed this class!  I wasn't interested in Greek Civ at all before but he is so excited about it and made me excited about it too.  There is a LOT of reading but if you go to class and take notes, you don't have to do all of it.  The TA is super-sweet and energetic too and grades pretty nicely.  Overall, lots of reading but GREAT!!!

could have cared less about greek civ b4, and i still dont, but he did a good job at making it interesting.  to do well, underline every quote he reads from the books and know them for the tests.  go to lecture to get the handouts, they make life much easier.  for the discussion, make sure you get him and not some TA. lotta tedious reading though
He's so incredibly passionate about the class - it's impossible to fall asleep. BUT in all seriousness, a wonderful professor! Lots of reading but he makes it interesting!

This class was amazing!  I went into it not interested in greek history or mythology at all, but Dillery made me want to know more.  He taught my discussion section himself, which really helped.  He took a vasted interest in my grades and made sure I was on the right track.  Overall, he's a GREAT PROF!!

he is an amazing teacher..really helps A LOT..i recommend this class to everyone..a lot of reading..but it's very rewarding to study the classics..going to class and taking notes helps more than the readings themselves..also highlite any quotes he goes over in class(they will beo n the test)

more difficult than a 200 level class should be, but if you attend lecture and pay attention, it really isn't as difficult as everyone makes it out to be. subject matter can be boring, even though dillery is very enthusiastic.

Very enthusiasic professor but assigned much much much more reading than I expected for a 200-level class; the tests tend to have rather obscure characters so it's not even an option to surface-read the assignments, it's an exhausting course.

This guy thinks that he's teaching something like CLAS 401 instead of CLAS 201.  I heard great things about him going in but instead got to experience 250+ pgs of mind-numbingly boring reading per week along with a challenging paper due five days before his final exam.  Would def. NOT recommend.
COD didnt reflect what his course was about...lots and lots of reading...goofy yet intertaining
He is extremely well-versed in Greek lit and seems to enjoy espousing on it, but he assigns too much of it to read in a 200-level class.  Going to lecture and discussion is absoultely key.

Dillery enjoys a zeal for classics, which is greatly appreciated on my part.  However, he seems to specialize more in Greek than Latin, making his translation discussions somewhat convoluted.  He assigns above average amounts of reading for a 300-level class, which can lead to difficulty on exams.
The classes are interesting and easy, if you go to lecture, he goes over all the readings in class, so you dont really have to do the readings.
HE's great!!! Best professor i've had so far...he's so enthusiastic about what he lectures...it makes class sooo interesting.  Try to get into his lectures.
he's a huge geek. but lovable.
Quirky, but VERY excited about the topic, so he's very interesting.  Always ends class early.  Hard, in-depth tests.  Interesting material.
Quirky, but interesting even early in the morning.
Wonderful professor, really excited about Greek history, a little quirky though and tests are in depth.  But overall very nice and helpful.
best greek class ever
such an awesome teacher; very passionate; try to get into his discussion- very helpful
more theory than story time.... but still pretty good
Take any upper level Latin with Prof. Dillery.  He's great.
Very sweet, want's you to suceed!
He's an awesome teacher, he's really passionate about what he teaches
Best professor I have! Take anything he teaches
She knows all of our names and is very helpful.
The most amazing professor! I hated ODE so I was nervous about PDE but she made it my favorite class I've taken at UVA. She's so funny and really cares about the students
She is the best
Professor Morris is just all-around awesome. She makes every lecture engaging with her humor and speaking manner. She makes sure there are plenty of chances to get the grade you want.

This is a change your schedule professor. It takes so much talent to explain complicated material, and somehow she does this in a way that makes the material clear and almost easy. UVA is lucky to have her.

Prof. Morris is the best math teacher I have ever had. I was very worried about taking diff eq but she explained everything in a way that it was almost harder not to understand it. Plus, she is always available in office hours and amazingly helpful. She never makes you feel stupid for asking questions or getting an answer wrong. Take her class!
