Lilian is a super sweet lady. She is a bit disorganized, but she always makes up for it and makes sure that everyone participates in class. Her tests are easy and straightforward; as long as you pay attention you'll get an A.
Prof Feitosa really cares about her students.  Lots of homework but not difficult.  She makes her requirements very clear and as long as you put in the work you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is SO nice and happy and a very lenient grader. If you're really there to learn, you'll get an A.  There are oral exams and one group project. There is a lot of online homework, (normal for UVA languages) and it isn't hard, just time consuming and due whenever you have a test. She speaks really fast, but I highly recommend this class.
Professor Fatton is an excellent teacher who is passionate about the topics he teaches and conveys that passion well. Would take his class again

Any questions of Prof. Fatton are met with his incredulity and annoyance. He is very hands off and focuses more on hearing himself speak than engaging intellectually curious students. He very often ignores questions during lecture. His GA was not good and was often very scattered during section. Reported concerns about GAs are not taken seriously.

Fantastic class. Professor Fatton is an engaging lecturer, and the material is fascinating. Coursework includes a midterm, research paper, final exam, and discussion participation. There is an overwhelming amount of reading assigned, but your TA should be able to help you navigate it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very smart guy, but the lectures consist of him ranting at you for the entire time. The group projects were boring too. Not hard, but would not recommend if you want to be interested in the class you're taking.
Professor Fatton is an amazing lecturer. His class was really informative and was not too difficult as long as you do the readings and really work on the paper.

The material in this class is very interesting, but the lectures were so boring. He just talks, he doesn't use a power-point or any kind of visual so it was easy to lose focus. He assigns lots of readings, but I only did like half and still got a B. You have to come to class though. Grading depends on your TA. Mine personally was insanely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The readings and discussion aspect of this class will be the make or break your grade  A passionate teacher with very interesting material and insight, Prof Fatton's lectures can sometimes be unnecessary or just simpler reiterations of the weeks readings.  That being said every other lecture is insightful and fun.  Good teacher, funny dude.

Great class, great lecturer. Professor Fatton is Haitian born and can bring a personal perspective to global development and life under a dictatorship. He also brings intelligent academic study of the politics of development.
I have a tremendous amount of respect for Professor Fatton. The lecture was very inspiring and he is truly a brilliant man and scholar on the topic of Development.
Professor is awesome and knows his stuff but sometimes his accent is incomprehensible. He needs to use a mic. 2 exams: 50-minutes. 1 10-pg paper. I learned a lot. Just focus on Easterly and Sachs.
really great lecturer. this class is very interesting, though it's at 9 AM.

Very interesting class. He's a great lecturer and it's easy to take notes on. There is a lot of reading but not all of it is necessary. I learned a lot but it's definitely not an easy A. You need to know what you're talking about for the exams and paper.

This class is a great combo of case studies and theory.  Don't let Fatton's even-toned voice scare you on the first day.  He's a very compelling lecturer.  The course is very interesting, and isn't difficult.  Make sure to shop around for a good TA during the first weeks, though.  Some are terrible.

Great class, especially the first half. Towards the end, too much reading that was technical and dry. learned a lot, but very tricky midterm-ouch, and very generalized final-easy. 10pg paper on anything you want. quite an easy A and a superb history/roots/explanation of world's poverty trap. take it if you care about more than your own backyard.

really interesting class... great lecturer... most of the reading gets a bit repetitive, and not all of it is necessary.... I'd definitely recommend this course to anyone who has the chance to take it!

Lectures not really illuminating; broad generalizations without using specific examples.  Grading is pretty easy, but if you take the class in the fall, be prepared to turn in a 10 pg paper the day you get back from Thanksgiving Break.  Decent amount of reading, but you are never tested on it and everybody eventually stopped doing it.

This class inspired me to go into global development.  Although dry at times, Fatton was very approachable and has a great sense of humor.  He certainly knows his materials, too.  Take this class! Easy A!

Fatton knows his stuff and he's a really nice guy. He sometimes drones on and on, and lectures feel worthless. Readings often feel irrelevant. Walked away from this class feeling like I had learned very little.

Professor Fatton is a great lecturer. He's very knowledgeable about the subject matter (imperialism and globalization). I highly recommend taking this professor. Plus, he's funny; and as you all know, at U.Va. we can always use a good laugh!
great class. reading a bit repetitive at times which makes them a bit boring but overall, good class.

The course gives a great overview of the historical and current topics concerning development. Clear and easy to follow lectures, highly highly recommend it for anyone interested in this area or would like to learn more!

GREAT CLASS!!  I learned so much about developing countries... it truly changes your opinion about the world.  You don't have to do the reading, but if you want to do well, I suggest you do it... 2 tests (essay-based) and 1 10-page paper... manageable!

Fun class... lectures (unless he's taking attendance now) are optional but interesting to go to. Your experience will be heavily based on who is your TA. He comes off a bit arrogant at times, but he's not tragically flawed. Hint Hint: Try to pick up his political ideologies and where he stands on the topic. Helps a lot on exams and papers.

Great class. Intersting readings for the most part. Very interesting about the world outside US and Europe. If you live in a bubble and think that everything in the planet will be fine is going to be fine w/o doing anything or knowing about it. You're in for a treat. Prepare yourself for the future, take this class.
Everyone should take this class, at least to fulfil a rqmt.;very much worth it. readings not that heavy and very interesting.
Great lectures. Readings are repetitive but interesting nontheless. If you believe the world is and will be a beautiful place, Professor Fatton will change your mind and make you care.
His accent really isn't that bad...you get used to it almost immeditely.  Fatton is awesome...surprisingly funny...cares about the future of the world.  Great class, not hard.

Fatton's lectures are extremely organized which  makes them easy to follow but the endless lists get a little tedious sometimes. Overall the material is extremely interesting and he is very knowledgeable.

The class is pretty interesting, sometimes Fatton is difficult to understand, but you quickly get used to his accent.  He seems like a pretty nice guy, willing to answer questions during lecture and here alternative views. I think you should take this class only if you are interested in the topic.

He taught politics of developing countries. You could not ask for a better prof, kind, funny, very liberal but open to other ideas... super easy to talk to, actually very very accesible, during the class he was eager to abandon the lecture notes and discuss any questions that inquiring minds have.
fatton is hard to understand sometimes but really into it and dramatic. he's funny, such a cute little old man.
fatton is a total jerk and really high up on himself. seems to care less about the students and teaching. did i mention he's a jerk?

Feldman is one of the worst professors I've ever had. She knows her stuff, but is obviously more interested in teaching students who share her knowledge, i.e. if you don't know as much as her, then you probably won't do well in her courses. I have taken 2 of her classes and wish I had never had the misfortune.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professors like Feldman are the reason that the humanities are hemorraghing jobs and students. They have a lot to say but prefer destructive criticism to constructive criticism whenever possible.

Professor Feldman is one of my favorite professors at UVa. She is very engaging and really pushes you to think more deeply about poetry. She's fantastic to meet with outside of class, too. Definitely take her class!!!

Feldman inspired me *not* to become an English teacher. She disregarded my original comments, but made a lot of my less sophisticated prose. She silenced me a few times during class and didn't stop another student from making ad hominem attacks towards me.

Feldman damned me with faint praise on a letter of recommendation that has been questionably cited to me by several interviewers after I had put in a lot of hard honest work for her course. I gave her a resume and she couldn't believe I did several of the things I actually did on my resume. Small imagination.

Professor Feldman helped me decide to switch from Neuroscience to an English major! The woman is incredible, leads great discussions, really knows her poetry, and is always open to new ideas and interpretations. Can grade a little hard, but is not out to KILL you -- put in the time and effort and you'll love her!

Ms. Feldman knows her poetry. Although she assigned a lot of writing, the work load was not unbearable, and as long as you made a good effort you will be fine. She is also extremely willing to help you outside of class, in particular on papers and such. Overall, she is a very nice woman. I would take a class of hers again.

Very knowledgeable about poetry and literature in general. However, sometimes she can make you feel a little dumb, although she doesn't mean to. Class discussions are really deep and thought-provoking, but all the writing is murderous. Take this class only if you're really into poetry and are seriously contemplating majoring in English.

I was ready to learn all about Leonardo Da Vinci but did not expect Fiorani to be such a tough grader! I am a math major who took this class for fun, but it turned out to be just the opposite. Fiorani gives such touch grades on what seems to be subjective responses from writing assignments. She also does not give any feedback or study resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable about Leonardo and interesting to learn from. She grades harshly, however - on one paper, she said my only issue was that my grammar was occasionally unclear, but the content was excellent and accurate, and I got a B+. You can get away with never reading the textbook, but you should buy it anyways because it's very helpful.
Hard class. Alot of studying. Very hard grader. Not very fair about it either. No real reasoning behind  why she gives you what she does.
Don't take this course unless your an Art History major. You won't get an A unless you really know your stuff. The reading isn't really necessary... just show up to lecture.
best professor at UVA: she is inspiring. take the class, but be ready to work and attend section- you won't regret it.

Love her.Really understanding and passionate about material. Didnt have prior ARTH experience which was a little tough but definitely do-able. a lot of reading but relatively easy to not do. class attendance important.  SO MUCH STUDYING is required for the two exams, but i'm overall so glad i took this class and have this worldly knowledge.
The professor's lectures were a little choppy sometimes, but that may have been due to the nature of the course material... otherwise, I'd definitely recommend it... overall, very enjoyable class.

She went over important slides several times, so we reviewed things over and over; it was really helpful for making information stick.  It was cool to learn about Italian art in and Italian accent!  Her class inspired me; I need to go to Italy and see everything we talked about someday.  There were a lot of texts to read, but I've kept them.
If you love hearing someone say "um" 3000 times a class with an Italian accent and consistently mess up the slides, then this class is for you!

I learned so much in this class about Italian Art, and it was very interesting. There are just 4 assignments: 2 papers, a midterm, and final, so mainly there's just reading and notetaking for work. Fiorani is a great teacher and very knowledgable and fair.
she was mean to me
Very helpful and interested in students. Great knowledge of subject matter and loves sharing her knowledge with others. Terrific teaching style.
lectures could be repetitive, and assigns plenty of reading, but you learn tons.  really kind, too
She has an Italian accent, but you get used to it. Tests and papers are fair. Great lectures and she loves the topic! Very knowledgable, great teacher.
Very fun and knowledgeable.  Italian accent, but you get used to it fast.  Very helpful, and keeps mandatory lectures fast-paced and fun.

He's a good man, that cares about each student he comes to meet that shows him that same respect. Give him grace and he will give you grace. Do the bare minium and show up and youll do good. Hes a good guy.

Loncke is one of these cool older profs at UVa who just does his thing and if you're into his thing he's happy to share. His exams are not hard at all, so I wouldn't have gone to lecture if it weren't for iClicker points because they get a little boring, but he's a sweet guy and makes them as funny as he can. He likes learning students' names.
Professor Loncke is a nice and approachable person. Class was easy and chill, though kind of boring to me.

Prof Loncke is so helpful and excited about speech science, it makes this ridiculous 3-hour long class bearable because he is such a great professor.  The midterm and final are moderately easy if you study the powerpoints and come to class.

I was extremely disappointed by this class. Class time was never used to hear student ideas on the books. Simply, he stood and spoke. Jewish Humor is such a great topic. Yet I found class time boring. If you're looking for a second writing requirement, I do not recommend this class. Perhaps his other classes are better.

Absolutely my favorite professor. I've taken 4 classes with him. He's so kind and is committed to having students understand the material (even topics I didn't think I would like became interesting). He's always happy to meet outside of class, if only to chat. Definitely take any of his classes if you're interested in history and/or Judaism.

Finder is an awesome teacher and an awesome person.  So glad to have taken this class with him, and I highly recommend any of his classes.  Very personable, not overly difficult, but does a good job keeping a class engaged.

Definitely my favorite teacher at UVA. I took his German Jewish Culture and History class in the Fall, and his new class, Jewish Humor class this spring. He is unbelievably nice, very funny, and very helpful. If you go to his office you will definitely end up sitting and talking for at least an hour and he gives you really good advice for papers.

Professor Finder is very, very kind and passionate about his teachings. I took his first year seminar, "The Nuremberg Trial" and he was very knowledgeable about the topic. Though there were times it kind of got repetitive, he kept the class alive and well.
Professor Finder is extremely nice and well-organized. He could answer your questions even before you ask them!

Very nice guy, cares a lot about his subject, lectures can get a little boring but but you can bring your laptop and distract yourself while taking notes. It is a 300 level class so it requires in depth analysis but all in all im very glad I took his class.

Finder is definitely my favorite professor at UVa. He is very helpful and engaging in his lectures. It's easy to understand what he's saying and the material is especially interesting. He makes himself available pretty much whenever you need to talk with him and his advice is always helpful. Lots of reading, but you don't really need to do it all.
Finder is a great professor and is extremely nice.  Very fair grader, although it may be a little difficult to get an A he's not out to make people fail at all.

Very biased about the material.  Class was three quizzes (he grades hard on) and a final paper.  LOTS of reading assigned, but you don't really have to do it.  Unless you love the topic, I would not take the class.
He is very nice and easy to understand.  Lots of reading but it's not really necessary.  Easy quizes if you come to class he basically tells you all the terms.
Sooo nice! Quizzes aren't bad if you study the terms. You can tell he really loves the subject.

Finder is a nice guy and he is not that hard but he is very bias and extremely pro-Jewish.  This is a hard subject to discuss; I am not **** but I can easily detect that he teaches with an extreme bias and assigns readings that are similiar.  He is a great person if you ever talk to him, always willing to help, but the class is very slanted.

Professor Finder is a great Professor if you are looking to learn more about the Jewish experience during WWII.  He knows his stuff and is very open to different paper topics (class consists of 3 papers that increase in length).  Paper topics ranged from the Jewish underground to concentration camp Kommandants.
Finder is a great professor. Really cares about subject matter and students. In Eastern European Jewish history, he was able to balance tragic and humorous topics.
He is laidback, friendly, and sooo nice.

His lectures are very clear though sometimes boring. I dont think people will ever fail that class, but dont expect an easy A. Good: No exams only papers. Bad: High level of analysis for papers is expected and sometimes it is hard to know what he expects.
Best proffesor at UVA

Good, charismatic lecturer! Everything is quite straightforward in the class, but the material itself is inherently difficult. Lecture is good, but I would say the textbook carried me in this class. One thing I wasn't a fan of was that the exam grades made up the majority of our grade and the grading on those tests was a bit harsh.

Floryan is legendary, actually one of the coolest and most laid back CS professors at UVA. He is full of humor and is happy to make the class burst out into laughter on many occasions. He is also happy to adjust the course based on how the semester is going (due dates were extended when a lot of people were lagging behind).

No Tests, No Finals. Weekly Quizzes (60%) and Homework (40%) compose the whole grade. Those quizzes can be HARD! Just took the priority queue quiz, didn't have a clue what to do. There are retake options around every three weeks. And you can make up any one of them during "final"

Homework are Implementation (Wed) and Analysis (Fri). Not too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are recorded and optional, but they are really helpful for labs and exams. The labs are tough but the office hours are useful and theres usually lots of TAs there to help. Overall the workload isn't terrible.

Floryan is an exceptional lecturer who does the course material justice. CS 2150 covers a lot of ground, even though the course is relatively easy. Floryan can explain concepts well to newcomers and is pretty entertaining.
CS 2150 is the hardest class I have ever taken, but Floryan is also a fantastic teacher. Hilarious and you can just tell he's legit.
Tough class, but an amazing professor. He's funny, engaging, down to earth, and really knows the material. It's a lot of work, but Floryan is a great teacher.
2150 was one of the hardest classes I've taken, and though Floryan tends to be a tough grader, he is a fantastic lecturer who really cares about the students learning and doing well.

I would not have taken this class if it wasn't with Floryan. Great professor. That being said, his classes are super difficult. Be prepared to work forever on Algo homework and still not feel prepared for the exams. It's a tough class, he makes it tough, but he's such a great lecturer and you do really learn in classes he teaches.

Floryan is awesome!! I've taken Algorithms and HCI and I have enjoyed both of them. He really wants to teach the students and is really understanding of what the students need! For HCI, he even extended the deadline of a homework assignment and push backed a test to make it easier on us.

Floryan is a good lecturer and the material is interesting but... The assignments' instructions are unclear, and the one programming homework given was absurd and more about nonsensical implementations in Java than it is about HCI. Grading is often very subjective and harsh. You'll get random points deducted for formatting. Poorly organized class.
Floryan was the best professor I've had at UVA.  He is the most clear and organized teacher I've had, and he's really good at helping students get through tough patches in the semester.
Floryan is the man. Take all of his classes. Explains the material well, gives interesting lectures, and is very approachable and understanding. Makes a fun class even more fun.
Professor Floyd's classes are informative and entertaining. He facilitates class discussion based on the week's reading and prerecorded mini-lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Professor Floyd in the Spring for another class that was held asynchronously and it was really good. He has clear expectations and asks you questions to push you to think outside the box. I am taking this class with him again as I like the subject matter. As long as you try, he will help you.

Great lectures and lots of fun "tidbits" in class that will make for an enjoyable and rich semester! However, he seems to be book enthusiast (what good Historian wouldn't be?) so get ready to read a LOT! Each submissions is returned with great feedback and he works with you as long as you want to keep learning! Take at least one of his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's probably the best professor I've had - and I'm in my last semester (in BIS).  He's not an easy grader, but if you have a legitimate issue during the semester, he's extremely kind and understanding.  Definitely always knows what he's talking about and clearly spends a lot of time prepping for class. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor. Not the easiest class, but Prof. Floyd was always available for office hours. Very helpful and always willing to go the extra mile for his students. Even if you're not a history major, I would highly recommend taking one of his classes.
Excellent professor. Lectures are clear and he's very helpful outside of class as well. Highly recommended. This was my favorite class this semester.
Fantastic professor who kept me engaged with both interesting lectures and assignments; I would highly recommend the class to anyone with an interest in European History.
Jane Austen - great class, great readings, interesting assignments, great professor.

Floyd is great. I took this class and I'm in a seminar with him this semester. Not an excessive amount of reading, class isn't too hard, and learned a lot. He's really clear and keeps class from getting too boring.The only bad thing about this class was the 9am MWF slot.

Prof. Kondyli is the best prof I had this past semester! I'm not sure where the claims of her "poor English" are coming from but she is an extremely engaging and comprehensible lecturer.  She also doesn't give any exams, which is really nice when taking lots of other exam heavy courses.  She also always gives time to work on assignments in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Kondyli is a good teacher and she is passionate about what she does, but her class has a lot of reading compared to other egmts (>50 pages/class, 2x week!) Had 2 hw assignments due every Sunday, one w max of 1000 words. Classes spent discussing the readings, and participation is important. Easy A if you do what's assigned & participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Kondyli is one of my favorite professors at UVa. Her lectures are consistently interesting. She makes an effort to improve the educational process, often implementing new, helpful techniques. Expect to read extensively. Also, as a 3000-level course, considerable writing is required. Overall, she's very helpful and quite understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Hard to understand, expects a lot for an entry level Art history class, and is a pretty tough grader
Good office hours (in fact, all but requires that students drop by at least once to talk), and is generally available if you really need help.

I loved her class, although there were some people who didn't have enough of a background on the subject and might have gotten over their heads, plus some people who may have been expecting an easy A. (Protip: if you're taking a class on Byzantine art, don't complain about your teacher's accent or the abundance of Greek names in the material!)

Very difficult to understand as her English is poor and tests are not related to much of the material.  Extremely inconsistent with classroom lectures and  hard to follow.  Not a quality professor and moreover,  extremely unaccommodating and forgetful.

Had Professor Foutz for two Marketing classes. She is kind of eccentric and goofy, but nice. Her Marketing sessions as part of ICE were pretty fun, and the content / readings she provided were interesting. She tends to pick favorites in the class, and will often invite these students to serve as research assistants / tutors for her kid.

I have not taken a class with Professor Foutz. I have, however, worked with her as a graduate assistant. Professor Foutz really cares about people and will go well out of her way to help if she can. That being said, she's the kind of person you want to be around. She is clearly knowledgeable in marketing and I'm sure a great Professor.
Great teacher!  Made me really interested in marketing.  Has fun research projects and gives great examples of what to and not to do in real life. A+++

Fowler is one of the best professors in the English department because her compassion for students steers her teaching. She is kind and patient, and she bends over backwards to help every student learn something and feel good about the semester. She is especially helpful to students who are not English majors, patiently teaching everyone new terms.
Fowler is totally disorganized. Class discussions are rambling and unplanned and it's not clear what you're supposed to get from them. Class is almost entirely digression. Horribly unstructured.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: An incredibly gifted lecturer who assigns an inclusive set of readings. Lectures usually connect pre-1800 writing to recent events while establishing the context in which authors were writing. A surprising number of guest lecturers to introduce students to the department. Participation is 40 percent of the grade but includes weekly written work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Fowler's class is very interesting and fairly easy as long as you read and show up to discussion. Passage ID's are huge, but aside from that she is very straightforward and offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. Also a very nice person who loves when students come to office hours.

Professor Fowler was quirky and always interesting.  I had no interest in Chaucer prior to signing up for this class, and just did it to knock out a pre 1800 requirement.  Now I absolutely love Chaucer.  She was very helpful and I definitely recommend this class to anyone.
Fantastic, enthusiastic professor with high standards. Makes you want to do well in class.
Incredible professor. So knowledgeable and so willing to help! She really made Chaucer attainable, and I now I absolutely adore him, even in middle english!

I started out incredibly disgusted and discouraged by Prof Fowler's unclear, rambling style.  However, after a few weeks I got the hang of it, and the material wasn't that hard.  About 30 of us  got A+'s on the midterm, and who knows how many got A's.  You'll do fine, just read everything for the passage IDs and get a helpful TA!

Her lectures are unfocused and you MUST go to class in order to get the information needed to pass. She is enthusiastic about it, but her voice tends to be monotone/soothing so try not to fall asleep...Good luck....

Prof. Fowler is great! While her lectures are usually unfocused, she bubbles over with enthusiasm about her subject. Prof. Fowler has also been really    accessible outside of class; she visited nearly every section before the exam. It is tough, but a little studying and you can ace it!

She loves the material which is endearing but her lectures are completely pointless and very poorly organized--I skipped at least once a week.  However, she does test on rather obscure material, so there is some benefit in going.  Overall, I just can't wait for this class to end.
DONT TAKE IT WITH FOWLE..SHE DISCOURAGE YOU FROM BEING AN ENGLISH MAJOR!

Fowler is such a smart woman and it is apparent in her lectures. she is so enthusiastic about the material, it's hard not to be interested. her lectures were sometimes unfocused, but fun none the less. with an awesome ta, this class is great and engaging. (and you learn a ton)

Fowler is a very smart individual with lots to say even if its not clear what she wants you to take away from lecture. I agree that the fall 04 final was a total ****. I went in with a B+ and came out with a C+, ouch.

Fowler is an interesting lecturer (animated and energetic) BUT it's really hard to understand what one is supposed to take away from her lectures.  The final for Fall 04 was KILLER.  If you take this class know EVERYTHING for the final b/c she tests on really obscure poems that we didn't discuss.

Fowler is a fine, quirky professor. I personally enjoyed her class, but some people found her lectures to be cloudy and non-topical. All in all, she is a great professor for those who are confident with the abilities of their TA.

She is incredibly knowledgable about the topics she lectures on, but because she has so much to share and teach, the course moves pretty quickly.  She is animated and fun, and you can really tell that she enjoys teaching.
If you are trying to knock off your pre 1800 requirement, look for a class taught by Fowler. I loved her Chaucer class. She is animated and interesting, and very interested in her students.

Congratulations on 40+ great years, to the Best Professor that has been on the University of Virginia faculty in my lifetime. Please enjoy your retirement, Sir:   you are well deserving of every accolade for your genuine and generous heart.
A great professor

Fr Fogarty is one of the BEST professors at UVA. He genuinely wants each of his students to succeed and will work with you to understand material.  You're a fool if you don't attend his office hours. Go to the BBQ that he has at his house and become besties with him. G. Fogs is best!!!!

Father Fogarty is a very knowledgeable man, but because he knows SO much he often goes off on to tangents not related to the point of the lecture.  Lots of times the lecture is not chronological so it can be confusing. The class started strong, but then got harder and harder to follow as the semester went on.

A very nice man and excellent priest-the worst professor. His lectures often digress into personal anecdotes. The class is definitely biased towards Catholics. The essay questions on exams are overwhelming and the multiple choice questions are designed to trip you up. When note-taking, stick to his outlines (provided on collab)!
Father Fogarty is one of the best professors I have ever had.

Prof. Fogarty is one of the best professors I have had at UVA.  He is incredibly knowledgeable and cares deeply about his students. He is a tough grader on exams, but if you get to know him, he will remember that when it comes time to give grades.  There is a reason he has taught here for over 30 years...because no one is more qualified than he is.

I learned a great deal from Fogarty and his class on Catholicism even when I though I knew my faith!Fogarty might be hard to follow at some points, but he's more than willing to answer questions and clarify.He is very smart. Do the reading- it adds significantly to the class and helps with your understanding.

Father Fogarty is extremely knowledgeable and fun to listen to if you're interested in the subject, and he's definitely easier to understand if you have a background in Christianity. The lectures and notes are very disorganized and he's often unprepared, so be ready for anything.

Bascaically, everyone who has previously written a comment...they are all catholic or christian.  If you are not, then dont take this class, b/c it is exremely biased against you.  I have taken many religion courses, and this has been the only one that has had an underlying assumption that you are of the religion being taught.

Class pace is painfully slow.  He’s a well-intentioned man with a good heart, but the class was incredibly boring and disjointed.  Often forgot the materials he needed in order to effectively lead the class and it crippled the discussion.  Overall extremely frustrating and a class I dreaded going to.

Prof. Fogarty is an amazing person, and probably the smartest man I have ever known.  Sitting down and having conversations with him is fascinating, so definitely go to his office hours.  He loves getting to know his students.  The class is no joke, and the rading is kind of boring most of the time.  He can be a bit unclear during lecture too.

the readings are massive but the class is well worth it. Fr. Fogarty is everything a professor should be. though he can be a bit confusing sometimes, he's very open to talk with students in clarifying abstract topics or just about anything else.

Father Fogarty is great. Although his class is hard, you can tell he really knows his stuff and is passionate about Catholicism, which is important in a professor. I learnt a lot from this class although i found it really hard at times. but it was worth it.

Fr. Fogarty is great. His class is always interesting, peppered with amusing anecdotes, and he is very available outside of class.  He is concerned about his students and overall, is just an awesome man.  I'd definitely recommend this class.  Although there is a lot of reading, it is worth it.

He's awesome! Sometimes confusing, but if you do the readings before class, you'll understand. He knows so much, it's unbelieveable. He really cares about the students and is there for anyone who wants help or just wants to talk. He is exactly what I think a professor should be and I learned so much

Father Fogarty is awesome! Some people say the readings of Rahner, etc. can be challenging, and he sometimes is confusing in lecture (which can be true) but even they like his class a lot. He is really high up with Church leaders and is the smartest professor at UVA.
He's a really nice guy, and I learned a lot about Catholicism, but his classes get somewhat boring and a lot of concepts are abstract and hard to clarify.

If you are picking your ENWR class and enjoy reading ghost stories, this class is definitely your best choice! Eliza is AMAZING. She is very passionate about the topic and gives detailed feedback on every paper. She is always there when her students need help!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Eliza is probably the most patient and approachable professor at UVA. Take this class if you are interested in ghost story! The reading is so much fun, and our homework is sometimes watching a horror movie. I highly recommend this class, even if you've already fulfilled first year writing requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Eliza is the best! She is a difficult grader, but she is one of the nicest and most helpful teachers out there.  I highly recommend meeting with her about papers because she really knows her stuff and will help you succeed. Take any class Eliza is teaching and you won't regret it.

Eliza was incredible. She is a really tough grader but puts in a ton of effort to help her students improve. She literally creates a color coded outline of your first paper and goes over it with you to improve your critical writing and organization skills. She also brought food to class and was the most passionate TA I've ever had at UVA.

Ghost stories ENWR is one of the best classes. The readings are really fun and she's always there to help students do better. The attendance is mandatory but I never regretted going to class. There are five papers for the whole semester. The grading is little harsh but there are lot of other ways to make up for a bad grade. Definitely recommend!

Eliza is the best TA that I have ever had at UVa.  She expects a lot, but she puts tons of time and effort into helping her students to do well in return. She is always available to help and constantly provides helpful resources. This class helped me to improve my writing & critical reading skills and deepened my love for the Bard. Take her class!!

Great guy, good lecture, horrible readings.  The readings are extremely dense and long (sometimes 60+ pages to read  for a class) and you have to pay attention to all the words he says because he does not write words on his PPT slides.  If you are looking for a good segway into Art History, this is not it.  Not recommended for other majors.

Fordham is a great Professor and it's obvious how interested he is in the subject matter. My only problem was actually getting to the class, as it was a 9:30, but despite this he is a very engaging teacher and at times very witty and entertaining. His class isn't necessarily difficult, but you do need to do the readings and study to get an A.

Fordham is adorable, knowledgeable, and very engaging! Attendance was not mandatory, but you definitely need to go because there is no textbook. The readings were a little tough for the level of the class, but you only need general ideas from them. Not much work besides memorizing slides for the midterm/final. Besides that just a 5-10 pg paper!

One of the best teachers I've had at UVA. He is very interesting, cute, extremely knowledgeable, and good at leading classroom discussion (even in a larger lecture setting). I want to take more of his classes!

Fordham is a young professor who got very interested in the subject matter of the course I took - British Art History. He has cute nerdy moments that make him endearing and for the most part the lectures are interesting. He pulls a lot from the articles so take good notes on the themes and main points of those as well as recording lecture notes!
Amazing teacher, great class. He really gets you excited about art, and you can tell he's very passionate and very knowledgeable.
Fordham is awesome. He's a pretty good lecturer and is a really nice guy.
Really interesting class, most of the reading is articles on toolkit so probably not really worth it to buy the textbook except maybe for the images but you can google those.
Great professor who makes the subject really interesting. Has a lot of energy.

This was easily my favorite class, but also my hardest. The tests were very straight forward, but there was a TON of memorization required. Fordham's lectures were fascinating, and he really cares about his students. I'd definitely recommend him as a professor, just be prepared to devote a lot of time to his class.
Doug rocks, he's adorable and funny and his lectures are very clear. The tests are very straightforward as long as you know the material and pretty easy to do well on.

This is an absolutely fantastic class.  He is a brillant and eloquent lecturer, very passionate about the subject.   Best class I've taken at uva...and I'm a 4th year.     Warning - tons of memorization required so be willing to spend long nights in the library.
Great class. Lectures rarely dry but Prof. Fordham keeps it entertaining regardless. Important to keep up with the readings and go to lectures if you want to all the material on the exams.

prof fordham is very clear, engaging, and incredibly nice. he's been extremely helpful and encourages class participation. i enjoy going to his lectures, and make a point not to miss them. he's a fair grader, and the memorization wasn't excessive. i highly recommend his class for anyone, even with no art history background.

I initally only took this class to fill my humanities requirement, since I couldn't take studio art. But it really ended up being one of my most favorite classes so far, and I never felt bored in that class even though it's mainly lecture. There are lots of readings to do, but otherwise, it's a great class!

I signed up for British Art History as a random course of interest, and now it's one of my favorite classes this semester.  Professor Fordham is an engaging lecturer, the subject matter is interesting, and it's made me want to take more art history classes.  There's a steady flow of important reading, but it's managable.  Really good class.

It's a fun class and gives a interesting take on history and how it effected art during this time.  The text to read are up and down for interest; you have to be sure to keep up on them.  But, Fordham is great, helpful, funny, and hot.  Also, the lectures help with getting through some confusing parts of the text.
This is a pretty easy class, not a lot of reading and the tests aren't too bad.  The class can get boring but Prof Fordham makes up for it because he has a good sense of humor and is hot.
No Comments

Before considering taking this professor, don't. She was consistently late to classes, would constantly have errors in lecture slides, including misspellings and formatting errors, or just wrong information. Discussion section was what made this class passable. Material was easy, but her teaching abilities are abhorrent, UVA should reevaluate.

I think the subject matter was absolutely wonderful, but her teaching lowered the quality of this class. This class had wasted potential, due to her being late on numerous occasions to class, several typos in the syllabus and other assignment, grades being put in days before they are due, and her rambling and not making much sense a lot of times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was very clear that she did not put the time or effort in to teaching. There were numerous typos in every lecture, study guide, rubric, and test. This made it incredibly hard to learn and felt disrespectful of our time and money. She rambles a lot and the lectures are not very helpful. All of the tests are based solely on the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rambles a lot and has lectures that are really hard to follow because they don't have a clear structure. Most of the assignments are unclear and we are 80% done with the semester and we have no grades in the gradebook. She's often late to class and going to class just feels like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was the most disorganized, unprofessional conglomeration of nothing I have ever sat through. Prof is very intelligent but conveys this in no way through her lectures. Grading is harsh and unjustified given the lack of clarity, construction, and specificity.

Probably one of the worst, most incompetent people to work at this University. She does not teach, but rather just wanders around talking to herself about irrelevant and incomprehensible things. There are few assignments and they are graded incredibly harshly. Do not take under any circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Fraser didn't even know what she was talking about half the time, she would refer questions asked by students back to other students because she was constantly unsure.  She seemed to be learning along WITH the class versus teaching it, while the exams were extremely specific and harsh grading.

Professor Fraser would come in to class and would forget what the reading was about and have to ask students. Her powerpoints are full of misspellings and look very thrown together and the assignments she gives are unhelpful in learning the material. She seems to be learning it along with us.
Professor Francesca Calamita is an amazing engagement prof. Very easy!

Prof. Calamita is an absolutely amazing professor!! She is so sweet and does a great job teaching Italian. My Italian improved so much as a result of taking her class, and she inspired me to be an Italian minor! Would highly recommend taking this class with her.

Francesca is a great Italian teacher. She definitely knows the language since she's a native. The class usually has a lot of assignments, so make sure you stay on top of everything. Fair grader. Show up to class and study and you will be fine! Attendance definitely matters!
Italian was her first language, so she has no problem understanding the class.

FOR EGMT 1540....Plastic Everywhere
Cool class, awful professor. She was beyond disorganized and never had anything prepared for class. It was so boring and she was always changing up what we were doing, but if you stick with the class it is an overall esay A. make sure to put effort into your written responses because she is kind of a harsh grader

Professor Fraser and the TAs made this class not only tolerable but truly enjoyable. It was an incredibly challenging year, but despite it all I feel that the work I put in was valuable and the class was worthwhile.   This class will be HARD WORK especially 2nd semester. Choose easier classes alongside it. I  worked 15 hours on just Orgo some weeks

The benefit of taking orgo with Professor Fraser is that she pushes you to understand the concepts and not just memorize. Her class has a lot of components (weekly homework, reading questions etc.) so be organized. Discussions and office hours are SUPER important- go every week! Tests are the hardest part, so take advantage of the regrade.

Fraser requires a lot of work, but is very understanding and extremely kind. She has an amazing mind and really helps you get excited and interested in Chemistry. I've had a lot of horrible Chemistry professors, but I would major in it if I had a chance to be taught by Fraser every time. 1010 Would recommend!

Fraser is one of the most caring professors I've had so far at UVa. The work load is rough, but it's all for the better. Organic chemistry requires a lot of work and having her guidance is a huge plus. Tests are hard and comments are not too helpful. TA's grade everything and are used as direct references for help. Fraser has good office hours too.

I had Dr. Fraser in for Orgo II in 1996 (her first year at UVA, I believe).  Her class was challenging, but I learned a lot, including the importance of hard work.  I am a professor of chem now as well and remember that she seemed to care a lot about making sure that we learned.  This meant a lot.  Thank you, Dr. Fraser.

Fraser is the worst. She's not helpful - I'm the sort who really loves to go to office hours, but after the first few I stopped going. The tests are impossible and in lecture she's a mess. Read the textbook, though, and you'll do okay in the class.

Prof. Fraser is a very nice and pleasant person to talk to. However, her Inorganic Chemistry class is very difficult - mostly due to a serious lack of organization and a big difficulty gap between what's taught in class and what's asked on tests. Teaches basic concepts only to test you on details and extreme cases.

Not a terrible lecturer, but not very interesting. Her exams are ridiculously hard which she intends because there is a big curve. She teaches you the basic concepts, but expects you to be able to apply them at a much higher level making the book a necessity. Probably one of the most difficult chem classes I've taken so far.
pure hell

This class is by far THE hardest class at UVA.  Proceeding through the chemistry major I have found that the class focused too heavily on the details; much of which we never have seen again in other classes.  Life was hell in that class.  The only things that keeps you going are the friends you have.  Be prepared to get beaten into the ground!

Thoroughly agree with the guy who said "prepare to fail your other classes". Chem literally becomes your life. That said, she's an awesome person - very nice, dedicated, and makes you learn A LOT. The class has really made me appreciate orgo. Plus you become great friends with your classmates. Very worthwhile class if you enjoy chem.

Fraser's lectures are very useful, she presents information clearly and orderly. She is very excited about the subject and is a nice person, the only reason the class is so hard is because that's how you'll learn best. This class made my life hell, I'm not gonna lie, it was rough, but I learned so much. I loved it.

Hardest class at UVA I don't care what anyone says.  Youur life will be chemistry. Our second midterm average was a 28%.  But, if you do the work you'll have at LEAST a B.  You will learn stuff in class, but it will have little or nothing to do with the homework you're doing. Prepare to fail all other classes though, you will have to ignore them.
ridiculous!

This is the class with the 38% exam average.  Fraser's a nice lady, but she's not very good at explaining things -- and neither was the TA the year I took it.  It IS possible to get an A, but be prepared to work 30 hours a week on the problem sets.

I have nothing good to say about this class. I love science but I hated this class with a passion. The work load is rediculous. She could have taught us more, better without it. You will not learn much that you didn't learn in 182. You will hurt. You will hate your life. You've been warned.
Exams are hard. She really knows her stuff, but is vague in answering questions.  Prepare to work in this course.
No Comments
Great class..She sets very high standards.
It's the hardest class I've taken at UVA. She's horribly vague at answering questions but she's okay with the lectures.
Frasier is a really nice lady to get to know, but this lady is HARD.  She can be very vague with answering questions.  Lectures are pretty clear though.
Very very very very very extremely hard class, feels great when you're done though
bad than ever
Hardest course at UVa, but worthwhile!!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

I like Professor Furia- he's down to earth and a great lecturer. The actual IR theories are just a small portion of the class and he focuses more on issues surrounding different regions of the world. There is just too. much. reading. A textbook is read within a week. They don't relate enough to lecture to make it worth being assigned that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There was a ton of reading for the class, but they were interesting and easy to find PDFs of online. The reading quizzes are simple, but specific, so be sure to read carefully. As long as you put in effort you should get an A. Prepare for TONS of reading though.
Furia is a nice guy but a very slow talker and sometimes hard to listen to. He is not very engaging - not a fan.

This class was interesting. You read a book every week and talk about it in discussion sections. He also has two lectures about the books every week. Our TA said it wasn't book club, but it felt like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Furia is a great professor who really tries to make seemingly hard topics easy. He genuinely cares that his students learn the material but he is not afraid to make you pay for it with your GPA. Class wasn't hard, neither was the final but you will have to work a little for it.
Great class, super smart teacher! Took PLIR 3500 Special topics-- learned a lot. Definitely a fair grader

Very broad basic intro to IR like most other classes. However, he needs to communicate with his TA's. My TA graded our sections much harder and she could never explain why anyone got the grades they got. She would try to help with papers, but never provided useful information.

His are very vague; the only reason to attend them are the partner exercises which are graded. 2 papers and 2 exams require you only to get the terms out of the textbook and do the outside readings (which the class is based around). Good, if sometimes too basic, intro to IR.

Furia's lectures are rambling and easy to zone out of, which is fine because you could probably skip the lectures and still get an A. The only thing that really matters are the outside readings on collab, I only had to use the textbook to look up terms before the two exams. All around, unimpressed with the class; doesn't take the material very far.

Furia is obviously really interested in the material and tries (and fails) to get the class excited as well.  2 essays and 2 exams are not terribly hard, although the essays definitely are easier.  Read the assigned readings instead of textbook and you'll be fine.  Good intro to IR.

The course is based on textbook reading, online resources (which I think is the most important part ) and lectures. It covers 1-2 topics in PLIR selected by the prof. You will need to write two two-page papers and take two exams. I do think this class enhanced my interest in PLIR a lot and the prof.'s lecture is clear. In sum I enjoyed this class.
Often unclear. Very basic and surface. Does not go in depth into many issues. Average professor.

This is your sign to become an ETP major. PLEASE do ETP as your second major you will not regret it I promise! Professor Freedman is literally one of the most thoughtful and caring professors at UVA. You will learn so much from him! Very energetic and upbeat - makes my day going to his class. Quizzes in class are reasonably fair and open note.

Prof Freedman is a great lecturer and readings are interesting. PLAP 3140 gets a bit repetitive so sometimes lectures are eh, but he makes it fun. He doesn't post his slides or recordings which is annoying, but lectures are worth it. Recommend his classes if you want to take a PLAP, the best politics lecturer I've had thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Freedman is so wonderful! He's very enigmatic and clearly passionate about his work. Awesome guy, awesome class!

Prof Freedman is the bomb!! He is so funny, quick and inspirational. I was always excited for class (despite being at 9am)- Mass Media Am Politics was such a cool, eye-opening course esp. during the election. Freedman is so passionate and has published his own studies. Careful, he will include very specific details from lecture in the quizzes.

Took this course during May Term at UVa's Morven Farm. Really enjoyed this interesting course and the chance to interact with Prof Freedman in a smaller class setting. Although this class is somewhat intense because it meets for five hours a day for ten days, it was fun and very worthwhile.

Professor Freedman is wonderful. His lectures are always interesting and animated. Although the class I took with him was 5 hours per day for 10 days, I was never bored. He is very accessible and happy to help with paper topics, reading questions, etc. I highly recommend taking any of the courses he teaches.
Freedman is entertaining and funny. I hope to take one of his classes again. First A I ever received in college!
It was AWESOME!!
Amazing Professor. Really nice guy. Kept class interesting and fun. Really great in a small group. Genuinely interested in your life and your success.

I took Freedman's summer Political Advertising course. Freedman is an amazing lecturer, and he's pretty funny. His class is easy if you skim the required books, participate, and pay attention in class. He does not try to trick you on the midterm/final; the questions are VERY straight-forward. Overall, the class was pretty easy. I received an A.

THE WORST CLASS I HAVE TAKEN INT HE POLITICS DEPARTMENT AND I AM A MAJOR! Tried to get into this class FOREVER. When I finally did, I was completely disappointed. Grading is based completely on the TA. Freedman is a good, engaging lecturer but the paper topics were AWFUL and there was a lot of reading (which was repetitive at that).

awesome professor! if you care at all about the media in america you will absolutely love this class - readings are always interesting and actually enjoyable (excluding the boring textbook which i dont think even he likes) and if you honestly go to every lecture and listen carefully even if you don't do the readings you'll get an A.

A fantastic professor! Interesting, funny, great lecturer, and very smart. Readings and lectures can be a little repetitive, but that makes the quizzes really easy. No tricks here, just wants to teach his students about the media and politics.
my favorite class ever at uva. go to class, take notes, and get an A! also, i loved going to class and the readings were not bad either but not necessary to even do

Great professor, really nice and outgoing, tries to get the class interested in topic.  Tests are easy and straightforward.  He doesnt try to trick you at all. Emphasizes the main points from lectures and readings.  There's no need to take extensive notes, just pay attention during lectures and understand the main findings of the authors. Only criticism is that he's somewhat repetitive.

Freedman rocks!  Class is enjoyable, especially if you take it in a small section over the summer.  Tests are fairly simple, he's not a fan of the 'long essay', and your best bet is to study the syllabus to see what authors wrote on what topics. :)
funny, nice, and very down-to-earth...loves what he teaches and keeps things fairly simple
He is very funny and a good lecturer, but the class is pretty repetitive. The tests are very easy.

freedman funny/nice but somewhat repetitive. easier, most material intuitive. lectures interesting but full of fluff. grade all on TA. paper topics easy and interesting. he is experienced in the media field and has a lot to teach. didnt do readings but it definitely hurt me come finals. just need to know basic outlines tho! most Qs from lecture.
This class sucks. What's with all the hype? Material is nothing insightful, painfully boring, and Freedman is not funny.

I would recommend him for f---ing anything!!  I just love him.  One of the best profs I've ever had.  Plus this class was during the summer so he really got to know us as individuals, which is cool because this class is taught during the semester in huge lecture halls.  There were about 35 of us.  Take this class during the summer if possible!!

Typical UVA politics professor: witty, engaging, and brilliant.  Freedman will respect you and treat you like an adult, provided that you do the same.  Tests are pretty easy if you've gone to class and taken good notes (the reading is required, but most test material came from lectures).  Definitely would recommend him to anyone.

I totally agree that he basically kicks ass. We were stuck in a very poorly a/c-ed room in Cabell for more than 10 hrs per week and he really did make every efforts to make us laugh/stay awake/absorb the material, which showed that he really cares about his students. Excellent lectures and easy tests too.

He basically kicks ass. One of my favourite teachers. This is a summer class and he's making every effort to make us smile/laugh at all times which is how he keeps us focused into the material. He knows perfectly what he's talking about and besides has a very effective way of speaking.
Accessible for newbies, still interesting for those who have some knowledge. Freedman's totally nice, and the work is very handleable.
lectures are great, not too much reading, tests are very easy if you go to class and are familiar with the readings. your grade depends on what TA you get

Class topics are interesting. Professor is very engaging and entertaining. I actually enjoyed going to lectures. However, I do believe that whichever TA you get will make or break your experience in the class.

Freedman is a top 5 UVA professor.  Tests are easy if you go to class.  Papers, you wont get anything higher than an A-.  So basically it depends on your TA as to whether or not you get an A in the class.  Make sure to go to his office hours a couple times
over-rated.  it all depends on the TAs.  lectures are entertaining.  he is charismatic.  over-rated.
excellent professor. very animated and involoved! you can't go wrong with a class of his, even if you aren't interested in the class!

Hmm. The ratings seem to be a bit inflated. Granted, he is an engaging professor and the tests are not difficult. However, it is obvious that he doesn't like to give out As on papers. The lectures are always interesting, but they simply provide a political term to what you could have learned on CNN.

He is the best prof at uva without a doubt. super nice, very funny, so smart you think he'd be more high on himself.. but he's so accessible and really wants the students to learn. Without a doubt one of the best profs i've ever had.
good class and teacher
Rawks.
Very animated and makes the class come alive.
No Comments
Awesome professor.  Clear with expecatations, reasonable with expectations, able to meet with students, great at relating information. Sense of humor is unparalleled.  Take any class with him.
and PLAP 227... One of best profs I've had at UVA.

Great lecturer and guy, especially since a lot of the material is so boring. If you're a non-politics class, just wanting to sample the politics department, don't take this class...its more of a stat class. peace.
If all the professors were as engaging UVA would be turning applicants away in droves!
Professor Freedman is easy to talk to, very supportive and encouraging. He is continually willing to meet with his students and always helpful.
Decent professor, pretty good lecturer.
really great prof., very accessible in office hours, good lecturer, take any class you can get into with Mr. Freedman
No Comments
No Comments
Awesome prof, courses tend to be # driven, very helpful

When people say this man is a genius, they are not kidding.  The profundity of the ideas expressed by Fuchs is staggering, and they are delivered without notes via a Hungarian-accented monologue.  He speaks slowly enough that you can get a transcript, word for word, which you can use on midterms/finals.  This class is a must-take for A&S students.
This is probably one of the very few classes at UVA Arts and Sciences where a student will learn to think. This classes lays a foundation for understanding the world.
Professor Fuchs is the best Professor I have ever had. He explains extremly well and the material is also very intresting. Best class I have taken at UVA by far. This man is a genuis.

Both Fuchs and his teaching style are a little unorthodox, and frankly, his monotonous Eastern European accent can make things dry.  However, he inserts some dry humor when you least expect it and the workload is generally light.  Short (1-2pg) essays that are open-note and minimal reading required.  You learn a lot though - the man is brilliant.

It's impossible not to get an A if you take copious notes and do the readings. Books are useless for everything but pulling citations for the essay portion of tests. The lectures are astonishingly boring, so multitask (sudoku?) to keep yourself from drifting off. Non-Soc majors have no reason to be in this class.

Everyday professor fuchs comes in with no notes or outline and goes on a 1.5 hour highgly abstract monotonous ideological rant in his world war 2 like eastern european accent. Expect several ackward pauses, exaggerated facial expressions, accented mispronounced unintelligble sociological keywords, and a joke or two.  TAKE GOOD NOTES.

He could deploy his massive intellect to crush students' souls, but instead kicks back and gives rambling lectures on classical social theory in its most digested and understandable form. With good notes and a grasp of the texts it's impossible to get a bad grade in this class.
He is a genius and knows everything which makes lecture very abstract. 2 tests open note/book. Be prepared to take lots of notes.
The best professor at UVA.  I loved his class and got more out of it than all of my other classes combined!

A serious intellectual. I think his self-acclaimed status as a thinker results in easy tests (open notes). The material is fascinating and his presentation is excellent. Without question, a class worth taking.
easiest class ever.  his accent is entertaining, but he talks soooooooo slooooooowly that it gets on your nerves after a while.
Fuchs is awesome.  I love his accent.  Easy class.

Fuchs is really great. Once you get passed the fact that he's hungarian, he's really witty and even more knowledgeable. As everyone has said, tests are open note so make sure you go to EVERY one of them (or at least come up with some sort of buddy system).

This class is amazing. Prof. Fuchs is a funny and extraordinarily intelligent man who knows Social Theory like the back of his hand.  Comes into class with no written material and is able to lecture clearly and with enthusiasm. This class was my favorite at U.Va., and it's not too tough, either.
he's so smart it's ridiculous. its awesome just to listen to him talk, plus the exams are open-ended and open notes.

the easiest class i've taken at uva! tests were open notes. fuchs is the kind of teacher you enjoy listening to. he knows his stuff like the back of his hand and to top it off, he's a really nice guy with a good sense of humor.
you must attend class and take good notes; the test is simply copying your notes

While not thrilling, Furstenberg was a clear, pretty patient lecturer.  With a little work outside of class, Furstenberg's teaching was good enough to get you a solid grade.  The material was EXTREMELY useful in my later economics classes, especially the 400-level topical classes.  Every serious econ major must take 372.

Furstenberg is really difficult. He sticks to material covered in the book but his class examples do not accurately represent the book. Good news is that he is always readily available to help you with your HW and will even tell you what you're doing wrong BEFORE grading.

Stay away from this professor. His tests have nothing to do with lecture, even though lecture attendence is mandatory; hw problems are not indicative of exam problems; TAs are worthless; and above all, the textbook is clearly not up to par with the difficulty of Furstenberg's tests. He does not give us relaistic examples in class.

Avoid this professor. His tests are close to impossible; hw problems are not indicative of problems likely to appear on exams; TAs are worthless; and above all, the textbook is clearly not up to par with the difficulty of Furstenberg's tests. He does not give us relaistic examples in class.

Avoid this professor. His tests are close to impossible; hw problems are not indicative of problems likely to appear on exams; TAs are worthless; and above all, the textbook is clearly not up to par with the difficulty of Furstenberg's tests. He does not give us relaistic examples in class and is not good at showing us what the "big picture" is.

Avoid at all costs. He was horrible in 301 and worse in 372.  His tests are rediculously hard. Also, the mandatory discussion sessions are useless, unless you like hearing a pompous grad student (Sean Sullivan) talk about how bad Furstenberg is as a teacher.
his lectures are clear but there is a huge difference between what we do in class and HW/exams. His exams are hard and better do as many exercises as possible
No Comments
good teacher...likes the material but the material is hard to like..wish the class was a little more applied less theoretical
Great Class

Prof. Garner is a good man and a good teacher. He was my undergrad academic adviser, and I took both of his mechatronics and another 4th-year class, the number of which i don't quite remember. He is one of the few professors who actually prepares you for industry, and gives you both scholarly and applicable examples. All around a great human being

Garner is the best professor in the department. He puts so much effort into making his lectures & labs interesting, practical, and also enjoyable. Take advantage of the time you have with him and learn as much as you can because you won't find many profs who care as much about students. He will challenge you but in the end you will be grateful!

Best Professor in MAE. Him and Thacker genuinely care about their classes, but Thacker has lost his edge. Garner often speaks of a lack of useful classes in the MAE dept. He is a teacher first and a researcher second (Unlike Knospe). Do well in this class and take Adv Mechatronics. He restored my faith in uva MAE.

This was my all time favorite class in the Mech major.  He teaches you things you will actually use in a fun/practical way.  He really cares about his students and loves to get involved in extracurricular projects.   He devotes a ton of time and effort in making this class a great and useful experience.
greatest teacher ever! he is so nice and learns everyone's names and he puts more effort into his class than i have seen before.
My favorite professor at UVa.  He is great at explaining everything you have to do.  This course is just plain fun and extremely practical to the field of Mechanical Engineering.

He is very good at explaining electronics to students unfamiliar with electronics. He is very knowledgeable in electronics and computer control. He is excited and dedicated to his classes. he can seem ornary at times but that is usually because he was in the lab all night working on something for class.

A great Professor. The class was very difficult. I would say that the textbook by McQuarrie and Simon was MANDATORY and so was the Problems and Solutions textbook. If you practice the problems in it, you will pass the class. Additionally, the class has a pretty heavy curve, so try not to stress too much. He genuinely doesn't want you to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He relies on the TAs to create the biweekly problem sets and exams, so the difficulty of the class really depends on them. The final grade is curved though, so as long you're about average in the class you should be fine. One in class exam and one take home, then an in class final. Gahlmann is very nice and very good at answering questions, too.

Though the course material is exceptionally tough, Professor Gahlmann was good at working through it slowly, allowing for and answering student questions in effective ways. Office hours and individual meetings with him were helpful, and I wish that I had attended more of the lectures.

It was his first semester teaching, so he made a few mistakes, but overall he really presented difficult material in a way that was understandable. He made me appreciate the subject much more. I think he has a lot of potential.

This was by far the worst prof. I have ever had. He reads off the textbook for 20 mins and the last 35 mins give a worksheet and puts you in a breakout room. His test are extremely difficult and are not like the problems that he gives on the worksheet or study guide. He mumbles through the lectures and isn't helpful at ALL. Avoid him if you can.

Prof. Fulgham spends a lot of time explaining the basics of topics. Then on the worksheets and tests the questions are way more advanced application problems that you feel prepared for. The tests look absolutely nothing like any of the study guides. Look at the chapter reviews and difficult webAssign/worksheet problems. GO TO THE TA OFFICE HOURS!

Attendance isn't mandatory but class is very lecture-based and although the notes are posted online the lectures help. There's a lot of work: worksheets and webwork every week and a few projects throughout the semester. I didn't understand the material super well, his teaching style was boring and made me want to zone out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hardest and worst class I've ever taken. not entirely professor Fulghams fault. He always had office hours and worked with you, but the material and tests felt impossible. I never wanted to participate in class because if I got something wrong in this class it would be beyond embarrassing. Classmates are very competitive in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Fulgham is a wonderful person, but the weightage of the class really throws you off. The exams are the most difficult thing you can expect, but they take up 70% (including final) of your grade, and there is no best way to study for them. They are a hit or miss, I got a 75% on the one I barely studied for and a 53% on the one I grinded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely love the guy but this class is very hard. If you dont know what youre doing on day 1 you will fail this class easily.
he is not a teacher i would recommend

I took this class online because of the pandemic. I would have class for 15 minutes and the rest of the class time was working in groups on the worksheet. The test are not the same on what was given on the worksheets. He finds the most hardest questions possible to put on the quizzes. He stubbles a lot and gets off topic when teaching lectures.

I took this class online due to COVID-19 and it was more challenging than expected. He takes off points on tests for minuscule details and if you do not show all your work (even work that seems unnecessary) you will score lower. It is definitely possible to do well in this class but make sure that you practice a lot before tests and pay atttention

Professor Fulgham is a really nice guy and I thought his lectures were easy to follow, if a little boring. He gave me a couple extensions on homework and classwork when I emailed asking, which was very nice of him. He has test review days that are very helpful and he's good at answering questions. The tests are tough but it's doable.

Diff eq. is a pretty tough class, but his office hours were unbelievably helpful. He taught in a pretty clear manner, but I wasn't a fan of his style. He lectures for about 15 - 20 minutes, and then has you work on group worksheets that walk you through learning to do the problems. American with no accent, perfectly understandable
Class was definitley required but if you keep up on the work tests are pretty straight forward.  Good guy, a little weird but a good teacher.

Mr. Fulgham is very confusing and unclear when he presents his material. He teaches his class for about 15 minutes then gives out a worksheet that you complete as a group. This may or may not work for you but be warned this class isn't taught traditionally.

Fulgham is a quirky guy. You can tell he is brilliant in the field, struggles teaching the material clearly. He would use simple examples in class and put ridiculously hard problems on the tests. I love math, but this class was not enjoyable.

I've been great at math up until this class. Fulgham explains the simple concepts you already know when going through complex problems, and moves too fast through the hard part. I went to office hours and was just as confused. I can tell he is a brilliant man, but that doesn't mean he is a brilliant teacher.

He is rather boring and dull. He is one of those teachers that discovered powerpoint after it had been made passe, but embraced it anyway. Good thing is that he puts all his slides online, so that's good. His tests are ridiculous though: he picks every tricky, challenging problem he can find, but in class the examples he does are super easy.

Fulgham is a good teacher in the sense that he is clear in his explanations, but he is extremely boring and awkward. I had a hard time keeping focus in that class because he has absolutely no enthusiasm and has a monotone voice. Don't take this class in the morning or you'll fall asleep.

He is very helpful and clear. If you do the homework, stay engaged in class, and put in a little time, you should get way above average on the tests. He is willing to help after class as well, and will give you personal attention at the discussion section.

Professor Fulgham is absolutely a great one to take with for your APMA courses. He is clear about his lectures, and quite approachable after class. His tests were a little bit hard but not as hard as the homework problems assigned.
The test is nothing like the homework.

Overall confusing and awkward. He mumbles to himself during lectures, and gets frustrated when people do not understand the material. His tests and quizes have low averages, and he picks the unique, hard questions to put on them.  The rewiew sessions are much more helpful than his office hours, 1 on 1 talking is awkward and unhelpful.

Very poor at teaching calculus to beginners. Often slows down his work on simple algebra then skips ahead through fundamental calculus operations, that beginners are obviously unfamiliar with. Decent and patient 1 on 1 help but its not worth having to go to every office to make up for his lackluster teaching.
Terrible, did not see his face the entire semester.  He simply re writes his notes on the blackboard for 50 min.  Most boring and pathetic atempts at teaching I have ever seen.
he rocks my socks! he is such a nice guy!
One of a few classes that I enjoy going to.

An extremely good professor.  He knows his subject, and can relay it well to others.  It seems like he's almost always available, and he's a really approachable guy.
