So this is a very hard class, you need to really prepare yourself to read the textbook every night, do ALEKS, attend every lecture, and go to office hours. The average grade for the first test was a 60, and quizzes range from 50% to 70% averages. Leung genuinely cares about chemistry and his students though so he will do anything to help out.
seriously horrible

Despite all of the negative feedback, I think he's a great professor who cares about preparing students to understand chemistry, not preparing students to "copy and paste" information verbatim so for quizzes. If you read carefully and understand concepts/where they come from you will see that the class/assessments are very clear-cut.

Leung is useless to say the least. He is in love with ALEKS which in my opinion is a giant waste of time. Don't get me wrong, he is a very nice person, he just extremely difficult to understand and his questions don't tests the concepts; they test extraneous tricks that are inaccurate reflections of your actual knolwedge

Makes you do a lot of busy-work; this is what will end up saving your grade, his quiz and test questions are all about reading carefully, as long as you do that and have a basic understanding, you should be fine

Honestly the worst professor at the University. He can't explain any of the concepts effectively, and then he spends the majority of every lecture telling us how bad we are all doing in chemistry. The questions on his tests are EXTREMELY unclear (because he actually can't speak English). Don't take chem with him. Take it with anyone else.

He means well but his lectures don't prepare you for the tests or quizzes. The averages throughout the year so far have been 60's on everything. ALEKS is a ok homework program but you learn through your mistakes rather than the actual problem process. He doesn't realize that almost all of the students who actually do well have taken AP Chem before.

He doesn't explain things well. He uses strange teaching strategies like the useless item-writing. ALEKS is a pain. He watches 20% get the LearningCatalytics questions right then starts lecturing us about how we don't study etc..attributes the success of his teaching strategies to the top 1% who is doing well. dont take chem with him

Leung is not a bad guy. He really cares about teaching, and tries to be innovative with his teaching style. That style, however, did not work out this semester; every chem student I know laments taking chem this semester, and is struggling just to pass. Take chem if it is your passion; if not, stay away.

The class was not easy to say the least. He believes in challenging you at every step and trying to get you to improve. He really cares about all of his students (I mean he has open office hours, he even sleeps there sometimes!)He also believes in teaching the concepts more than the equations(which I really liked). Overall a worth while professor.

I am speechless after taking this course.  He wants his students to succeed so much, and he is always there for us.  He has open office hours (name one other professor at UVA that does that).  Says that he sees on average of 50 students before a test and will learn every students name.He says he is not a genius, but I beg to differ. Must have prof!

During the first lecture he said, "I will never give up on my students." I didn't really knew what to take from this, but throughout the semester he proved he meant that statement. He is ALWAYS available for help and he cares about his students. He has made me learn chemistry rather than memorize it. Definitely take Leung. No questions asked.

FINALLY a teacher that cares about learning. At a big University it is often difficult to find the quality of education that is necessary to succeed later on.  Self-admittedly not the most "natural smarts", but promotes value of work ethic and complete understanding. Compared to the caliber of other professors at the university, superior
Leung really cares about you, although his teaching methods are a little different, you have to do a little learning on your own else you will do terrible.

Quiz averages were consistent with other professors but that is not important. The important thing is this professor's dedication to promoting learning not only of the material, but of how to think beyond the stated. Take the time to do your work and attend office hours. excellent teacher with a thorough understanding of chemistry.

Great teacher. Invested in his students. Expectations are high, but that is only because he recognizes in order to do well, not only does he have to deliver a meaningful lecture, but you must give of your own time to understand the material. Open office hours, always available, pushes students to become critical thinkers and not just memorize

Leung's lectures make the content seem simple, but his quizzes are very challenging. In fact, I didn't learn how to do some of the problems that were on the quizzes. He is a funny guy, but was very rude with the students in my section over several emails. Mastering chem assignments are much longer than the other professors teaching the class.

Class was fairly easy. He was the best professor I have ever had. I would highly recommend him over any Intro to Chem professor. Attend class and work hard on the homework and it should be easy. He also responds to emails very quickly, regardless of time of day.

He cared about his students, but was not an effective teacher. Whenever I visited him in his office hours I was belittled and was told that I may have a learning disability. I do not recommend taking Chem with Leung.

Leung is a very nice guy and really devotes a lot of time towards helping his students.  However, his lectures are not all that helpful.  They are not very well planned out and hard to follow.  His quiz averages were much lower than all the other intro to Chem professors.

Really cares about teaching and learning, very well thought-out lectures, quizzes/tests have a good mix of questions (easy/ hard). Pay attention to the questions asked closely, there are some tricky ones.

Funny teacher who really wants to help his students.  He has open office hours which is really nice to! Overall, I think he grades fairly even though his tests are difficult (I would say around the same difficulty as Metcalf).
I had him for my past 4 semesters he is a great straight forward professor.

Heavily reliant on spreadsheets, formulas, and wksheet links. Had to create Income Statement, BalSheet, Cash Flow without accting s/w, and had to tie together. Very labor intensive. If calculation error  found near the end, it was too late to revise. No advise from Prof along the way, though he did fist pump  thruout. Must have team participation!

Business concentrators are silently boycotting him. Seems to favor young male conservatives, and to have an attitudinal edge against others based on political views and status. Not friendly. Nearly everyone complains. The group homework projects are insane. Some in the program are hoping for a new professor, but feel it isn't safe to say so.
I would rather change majors or even schools than to take another class from this guy.

I can't believe UVA would allow a teacher like him. He is very difficult to talk to and has almost zero understanding of what it is like to be a student. He doesn't understand the material himself which is why he only present materials that came with the teachers edition of the textbook. I feel bad for anyone having to take a class from him.

Horrible horrible class. This guy doesn't teach as much as he reads slides. He demands way too much work and doesn't give proper or timely feedback. You should avoid him at all costs. Even if you have to change your concentration, you should not take this class.

This guy does not teach, he reads the slides that come with the book and requires you to do group assignments at the same time as 10 page papers at the same time as personal projects. He is the worst teacher ever and I hope he gets fired soon.
AVOID THIS GUY!!! This is the worst teacher I have ever had. He assigned 20-30 hours worth of work every week. He doesn't explain things very well and is at time rude.

Professor Hunter made this class interesting. His style of lecture is easy to take notes on. One key thing about the class is how important the lectures actually are. Tests are straight from lecture rather than the readings. The textbook for the class was not helpful, The readings would have been extremely tedious and time consuming.

The only readings you need are from the book of compiled articles, not the textbook. My TA wasn't a super easy grader but if you take good notes and just repeat everything you're told you'll do fine. It's a great class that opens your eyes to the ways of the world. Take it is you get a chance, Hunter is really great :)

Professor Hunter has been one of the best professors I've met in UVA. His lectures are really good because he puts the material in an interesting way and explains it clearly. I see the world differently after taking this class, as cheesy as that sounds... TAKE THIS CLASS
Even though professor hunter is my father, I actually really enjoyed his class and thought it was one of the most relevant classes I've taken at U.Va.

He was exactly what I would expect from an introductory level professor. He gave a lot of insight during lectures but if you skipped class it wasn't the end of the world. I would definitely recommend taking this class

Make sure you go to lecture! His entire tests are straight off lecture, and his multiple choice likes to make you think.  He is a great lecturer and really engaged you in the topic. He is also very easy going and funny.  I definitely recommend it.

Professor Hunter is amazing, he knows what he is talking about and teaches it very clearly. He is able to captivate his audience in a way that you don't feel time passing by. Make sure to go to every class and take notes all the exams are based on his lectures.
Professor Hunter is great!  All exam material will be right off his lectures, so attending class and taking clear notes is mandatory.  I thoroughly enjoyed this class.

If you are taking Hunter's SOC101 class, the most important thing to succeed is to go to his lectures and take good notes.  His tests are long and will take the entire amount of allotted time, but you can do well if you study the notes A LOT.  Also, grade depends a lot on TA, and mine was not so nice.  There is 1 3-5 paper, and it's not bad at all.

If you can get into this class, take it. Professor Hunter is hilarious, helpful and knows his stuff. He is very well respected in the sociological world and for good reason. Very available for office hours and loves to answer any questions about sociology, life, whatever.
Hunter is a great speaker, hands down, but I just hate the subject. Easy class, since the subject is common sense, but exams are pretty long. Grades depend heavily on your TA.

The only class at UVA that I have gotten an A+.  That said, I attended every class and studied long and hard for tests.  If you do this, you will get a good grade, but if you don't, you won't.  It's that simple.  The class contained more abstract concepts than I'd thought, but I would take the class if I were you.  Good guy, good prof.
the man? I don't think there's much more to say...probably the most approachable prof at uva, very kind, very enlightening..

This was my favorite class my first semester.  Every lecture is amazing and makes you want to come-and do because most of the material for the LENGTHY tests is discussed in lecture. Not difficult...Also cancels class occassionally:)

Overall a great class. His lectures are interesting and relevant.  It's a great introductory class to sociology and not hard at all.  However, this class is not a joke, you'll need to take notes every class and study for the tests, which can be long.

Hunter's lectures are epic.  They leave you feeling enlighted on the human condition.  This class tied in to all of my classes, none of which were blatantly related to sociology.  This was my favorite class my first semester, I highly recommend it.

I really enjoyed every single lecture. Hunter did a good job in telling the grand narrative of sociology. Overall, it is a very worthwhile class. It made me to consider minoring/majoring in soc. Just a note, this is not an easy intro class.
He was very clear

The topics are interesting but Prof. Hunter teaches in a very "preachy" manner, it sounds as though he is reading off an essay he wrote years ago. It's hard to sit through his lectures when he constantly repeats himself in every way possible. Discussions are good if you find the right TA
No Comments
great class, interesting lectures on interesting topics

He is a good teacher. I do not understand these bad reviews? LIke yes you need to go to class, but that is the same with every other Spanish Class. Pop Quizzes happen in every Spanish Class. Blame the Department , not the professor. Hes very funny and brings in activities outside of the normal textbook.
He didn't seem to care about us or the class at all. Not a fair grader and takes him literally months to return work. Does not promote an environment of learning at all.
he is disorganized and unprofessional and doesn't care about teaching

He is undeniably an intelligent man whose teaching quality is above average, but his PHIL 2340 was one of the most boring classes I've ever taken. I don't know how someone manages to make topics like world-destroying AI boring, but Mr. Humphreys definitely knows how to. Readings are jargon-laden and dull.

I took his Phil. of science class. I learned an astronomical amount in the class, but nearly all of it was self taught. Humphrey's is clearly an expert in his field, but he illustrates example after example without really explaining anything. He presupposes both a scientific and philosophical knowledge, with was fine for me, but may be problematic.
Exceptionally clear and precise. Very friendly and fair.
Humphreys great. Funny guy, awesome British accent, extremely intelligent. If you show up to class and let him know you're interested and taking his class seriously, you'll do well.

Easy class if you do all the readings and coming to every class.  Homeworks are great because you can check to make sure they're correct before you submit, and that's 40% of your grade.  Needs to make sure his mic is on before lecturing with his back to the audience.  My TA was great and explained things well, so that also helped.
Tough course, but getting an A is possible.  Not the best lecturer, but not the worst.  Overall, I felt like he would rather be somewhere else.
Lectures not all that helpful occasionally actually just puts the book on the projector...TAs a little weak
Not worth it if you are looking for an easy A.  His tests can be from pretty obscure lecture notes.

Not the most helpful/encouraging professor--crams many questions into a 45-minute exam that it makes it difficult to finish tests. Homework is assigned weekly & some sets can take up to 6-8 to complete. T.A. Kristina doesn’t know subject well and stumbles in explaining core concepts. Without determination, this class can get pretty tough.
loved this class! good lectures, and his responses to bad questions are funny. have to do the work but it is a great class, very smart teacher. highly recommended.

Not really a difficult class in terms of material, Humphreys packs in about two hours worth of material into a 50 min. exam, in which a few math/logic oriented people do well, and the vast majority do a mediocre job. You get to teach yourself because his lectures don't help. Also, one goof-up will turn your A exam to a B-. Take only if interested.

You do need a science background.  The readings are dense and jargon-laden.  Such is philosophy of science.  There's also too much reading; the class moves fast.  Stay away unless you're really interested in science--doesn't feel like a philosophy class at all.

If he didn't have a cool British accent, I would have never gone to class.  Don't take this class unless you're already interested in logic because you end up teaching all the material to yourself.  If you like the subject, the class ends up being pretty easy.  Get Clint as your ta!! He's awesome.
If you dont do well in this course then you're just lazy.  Do the reading (don't just skim, either), do the homework, go to class (pay attention).  Very straightforward, easy once you try.
Simply wouldn't reccomend

It is very difficult to perform in strict 50 min. tests and your grade often does not reflect your knowledge. The class material itself is not all that hard, he makes it so. Is not really very helpfull in office hours and his lectures consist of example after example with minimal clarification.

Humphreys is all right, but the homework is a pain, the class is boring and mundane, and how to study for the tests is unclear.  Humphreys doesn't do a good job of helping you to study, doesn't supply strategies for solving the problems in general.  You'll have to teach yourself.
philosophy of science was awesome -- he has contributed to the field but is modest. he likes class participation.

Humphreys does a good job of making a boring subject like symbolic logic seem fairly interesting. Anyone taking his class will probably dig his British accent and his sense of humor. The tests are straight forward, and the material is fairly easy.
great class.  helps to have a math background, but i didn't and i did fine
This class is a hit or miss you could get an A or a C by doing the same amount of work so honestly just ball out and take your chances the lab reports and then go off on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Undoubtedly absolutely brilliant and an equally terrible professor. The entire grade is the final, and that final is the most ridiculous test I've ever taken. Doing well in this class requires ignoring all other work and solely working on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is incredibly interesting. However, you need to be ready to really commit 10+ hours to it each week. Go to the Head TA's Recitations. Go to your Lab TA's office hours. Go to lab lecture, even though it might be your only class on Friday. And most importantly, attend the final review session by the Head TA. Work hard, do well.

Donald Hunt is a tough professor, and organic lab is a hard class.  Your TA points seem arbitrary, your lab reports don't necessarily determine your final grade (instead it's a really hard final), BUT Hunt wants everyone to do well and is incredibly patient and helpful in person.  Tough class, but a great guy.
The worst instructor ever. Got my worse grade ever. Incomprehensible and random grading. Never know what your final grade until its over.

Many say Hunt is cruel. Let's face it guys, Orgo lab is hard on its own. If you take the effort to go to Hunt's office, he is more than willing to help you. The bottom line though is if you're willing to spend LOTS of time working on reports, studying & understanding concepts, etc. then there is no reason why you shouldn't get a high rank & an A.
He is the worst professor I've ever had, and an even worse person as a whole. He is unfriendly, unhelpful, and not respectful whatsoever.

I earned an A in the Orgo lecture and put more than 12 hours per week into this lab course. The final was like a foreign language in that the material was nothing like either the lecture or the lab notes/book. One has to wonder about this guy when on the first day he happily announced that he failed his own daughter. Avoid him at all costs!

Hardest Class I've taken. If you're not 100% sure you're pre-med don't take it. The disparities between different T.A.'s is absurd. The only redeeming quality is that Hunt is very helpful if you go to see him.

Hardest class I have ever taken.  Grading seems unfair + the final was ridiculous.  I received an A and my tips are to go to lecture, since sometimes he answers lab questions in class + browse the assigned reading if something is unclear b/c the explanations there can be clearer. Class= tolerable if you figure it out, work hard + you can do it!

I had a question about the material and was terrified to talk to him because he puts up a very unapproachable front, but once we started talking he was very nice, and even insisted on giving me back points on my lab (which I didn't even ask for).  Tough course, but it really got me interested in organic chemistry!

Seems unapproachable, but not necessarily true. Very modest about his intelligence. Course is the hardest I have ever taken.  Spent 12-20 hours a week in the class.  Final exam is nearly everything. Study or find yourself with a C or lower. That said, got an A last time, expecting another A.  That said: be ready to commit hours to this class.

Nosferatu teaching chemistry, but works very, very hard to make lab happen for all 400+ students. The weight is basically backloaded to the final exam. I was first in my lab with a B for the course due to my exam grade. Memorize those mechanisms or end up a shell of a man like me, doomed to wander the cursed earth in search of n-Butyl bromide. :}
A very disappointing class.  Grades definitely don't reflect amount of work required.  Ends up ruining a subject I actually find interesting.

A very bizarre sort of class in the long run. First of all, let me state that I've never tried harder for a grade, pulling 12+ hour lab reports on a regular basis. That doesn't really matter for this course, however, as your grade boils down to your place on the final exam distribution. This is a game of chance, as everyone fails. Questionable.

Very difficult and time-intensive course.  Most students spent 8+ hours on lab reports and post labs weekly.  The final is exhausting, and the payoff for hard work is minimal.  GO TO YOUR T.A.'s OFFICE HOURS EVERY SINGLE WEEK.  Lab lecture was boring and not well-attended, but it was useful for retaining information for the final.
GET OUT WHILE YOU CAN! TAKE IT OVER THE SUMMER! do not make the same mistake that all of us here have made

Pretty much everyone in this class dislikes Hunt.  He is a tough professor.  The material he covers is difficult and is crammed into a 1 hour lab lecture section.  It is essential that you work hard to understand each lab as it comes for the final exam (your entire grade).  See a TA each week; APRIL RICHARDSON IS THE BEST!

Lab lecture was a complete waste of time, with Hunt doing nothing more than reading over the notes we already had in a monotonous voice.  The grading system is completely convoluted, and I would recommend avoiding the course until he retires, if at all possible

He is a tough teacher because he wants to prepare his students for any future lab/research work in chemistry. Most of your grade pends on the final exam. I would recommend recording his lectures because he talks fast and the recordings will also help you with your lab reports. Makes you apply material rather than memorizing;memorizing=F on  final.

Absolutely awful. completely unapproachable. 0 personality. grade determination is absurd: you are ranked in your section by your lab report grades, then everyone takes the final, and if 5 ppl in ur section got As, the top 5 ranked ppl will get As -- even if they failed the final. take over summer!!!!

evil sociopath, could care less is this class ruins your gpa & future. i thought i could get a decent grade, although friends told me to take it over the summer, definitely got a big fat C although i worked my a** off. postlabs make no sense. if he was stranded in a desert without water and i had a bottle, i would rather water a cactus

Hunt knows what he is talking about, but he's not very approchable.  If you make sure u understand every lab as you go, instead of crammin at the last minute, u'll be ok..because ur grade is almost entirely dependent on the final.  Just remember: Everyone fails the final, just be sure u don't fail it too badly, and u'll be saved by the curve!!
Grades really did all rest on the final, which was pretty ridiculous and all on specific details from the lab- not even general concepts.

If you wanna call youself premed at UVA, this is your gauntlent. Its hard but better than gen chem lab. Lab report format allows mistakes in procedure that dont affect your lab grade in a major way. BUT, its all about the final. So study. You can teach this stuff to yourself. Also depends on how good your TA is. Like all labs.
Terrible teacher.  Total d-bag.  Worst professor I've had at UVA.

Prof. Hunt is the most unapproachable professor I have encountered at the University.  I had to give him my testing accomodation and he just stared at me and then tried to argue with me about it.  He thinks we have graduate level knowledge of organic chemistry.  This class is rediculous.  Even the TAs hate Hunt and dont understand some of the labs.
His grading system is completely unfair. Please save yourself the exhaustion that goes into trying your best and take this course elsewhere!

he goes really fast in lectures and he doesnt really seem to give a crap about his students. I asked him early in the semester if I could change my exam date because it interferred with another class and he goes "well that's just not my problem".

The whole grade rests on the final. The person that said you need to study more is exactly correct because Hunt will not teach it to you. You will be hard pressed to find one person that walks out of the lectures getting something out of them. I could've studied for ten hours per day the whole semester and still barely passed the test.  Ridiculous.
he's not so bad.  the labs are interesting second semester and his lectures notes are really clear.  he has review sessions before the exams, so that helps a lot.  you people just need to study more!

This is ABSOLUTELY the WORST class at this University. You have to put a ton of work into it, and it doesn't pay off at ALL. It is graded EXTREMELY unfairly, and your entire grade rests on the final. Take it at another school, and save yourself and your gpa.
Quite possibly the worst professor at the university.  Unhelpful, deathly boring.

He's a pain, difficult to follow in lecture, only at the end of the year did it get slighlty interesting. Watch the attendance drop from weeks 1 and 2 to weeks 8 and 9. Everybody shows up the last two weeks to cram for the exam, and honestly those are the only classes worth attending.

Dr Hunt has been teaching for longer than I've been alive, and he knows his stuff. Chemistry, biochemistry, biology, immunology, pathology- he knows them all. The class IS hard and time consuming, especially the final, but if you study and really understand the experiments, you'll do ok. TAs are helpful; so is Dr Hunt if you go and seek him out.
evil, evil man
he's a drone
Hunt is sooooo boring in lecture it's not worth your time.  The TA's help a lot more.  The tests are ridiculously hard and confusing but you just have to gut it out.  Not fun and I'm glad it's over.

scared the living daylights out of me on the 1st day. flies through lectures in a drone, never pausing to let you catch up. impossible final. arrogant and condescending view on the students. very smart guy, but it doesnt make him a good teacher.
i love this man he's so funny and brilliant he knows every single thing in the world..bio, orgo...he DOES deserve the nobel prize...CELLS CHASE BACTERIA!!!! that is so amazing

Though it may seem odd, I have found this man quite helpful and clear. I do not know why he is dreaded soo much. If you go to his office hours, be yourself (if you like laughing, then laugh), this man will help you. He has helped me so much, even as to give me research positions in medical school!!

by far the worst and most horrible teacher on the surface of the earth. please do yourself a favor and stay away from this class. go to another school and take the course. it is very much worth it. only the wise listens.
Treats everyone like grad students. Doesn't even put effort into simple things, such as getting attention; he will just whine.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had.  Horrible teacher, lectures were monotonous and unhelpful, yet you have to go to get the postlab questions and if you just leave you'll look like a retard, so you're kind of stuck there.  And he's a ****bag.  Honestly, if you don't have to take him, don't.

By far one of the worst professors ever.  Lectures are incredibly boring, and the final is just ridiculous.  He makes every experiment sound impossible.  The only upside to this class were the TAs, most of whom sympathized with the students and helped out a lot.
poopyhead-sooooooooo mean.  Wants you to understand chemistry he probably doesn't even understand.  Expects too much from beginning orgo students-scary.  I'm terrified for the final-TERRIFIED

Horrible human being. Makes me sick to look at his face. Doesn't say anything helpful, just drones on the the most monotonous voice ever. Sometimes made class 2 hours long. (It's scheduled for 1 hour a week.) Rescheduled final exam because he thought he could. Deserved not to win the nobel prize.

he is a hunter. although he was a nobel prize nominee, he is not a good instructur. first thing he does is scaring his students and making them understand that they are not going to be able to pass the course. don't risk it, don't take the course with him..

Lectures seem helpful at the time. Then you try to write the lab report and postlab question and realize it was worthless.  Expects you to be able to understand the innerworkings of the labs you perform, without him explaining them at all. He'll ask for quantitative analysis when he has only done
No Comments
Sucks sucks sucks sucks sucks.  Very mean, very unhelpful, final was a killer.

Ignacio is not a good teacher, he does not make the material easy to understand. We ended up taking the final way earlier than we were supposed to because he was too busy applying for other jobs to actually teach the full semester. Economics is an important class, but don't take it with him if possible.
He lectures very fast, and his tests are wordy and tough. He doesn't require a text book, but you're going to need it to understand.
Great guy. sometimes hard to understand but it was never a real issue

He goes fast but the tests are fairly easy given the complexity of the material. He'll tell you that you WON'T need the book but I am telling you that if you want to do well YOU HAVE TO USE AND READ THE BOOK!!!!!
Best prof

Topic was Stereotypes. Make her like you early and you'll do better on papers. Class didn't teach much new information, but the topic was interesting. She's a little hard to understand sometimes, but not too bad. I got an A-, papers were easy. No exam. good for ENWR
My class was on stereotypes. The class was really interesting with a lot of discussion about topics. We have a total of four papers that are pretty easy. Plus she's super hot.
Very nice and approachable.

I think we learned more about Latin America because this prof. had the experience of being an immigrant exile who knew the hardships refugees go through when they flee their countries of origin. Learning English and adaptation are two of the major challenges that people from impoverished Central and South America countries go through.

I think that students have been unfair with this prof. They have not realized that she has contributed to the understanding of Latin American trends in culture and lit. We know more about exiles and refugees and the hardships in the host country. If you see what's going on in Central and South America, you will understand this prof's struggle

It is good to maintain a public forum where students can express their opinions about profs. While it is true that Ms. Lagos has improved a little, it is no guarantee that she will keep a fair grading criteria, and moreover, that she will improve her English skills. If she is so demanding, she should offer a model of acculturation--at a minimum.

Literally what is everyone complaining about, this class is a breeze. Read the text, take an easy quiz to make sure you read, discuss text as a class, reproduce what we say about the text on the exam. Two short papers where you give your specific opinion. BUT be forewarned- she won't let you get by on poor Spanish, which is completely fair for 3430
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If I were paid to take another class with this prof. I would decline the offer because what you thought you have learned you later have to de-learn.
She does not give good feedback, she is not accessible outside class, she does not deliver amazing lectures, and she does not speak English, but is critical of students who don't speak Spanish.
She is extremely critical of students who make mistakes, but she does not see her own limitations, primarily her archaic teaching style, that is, she's the only one who talks with no leading thread.

I cannot understand why she's still there pretending that she teaches. She should be ready to go. She is not a model to anyone. Her English is horrrendous but she demands too much from students who struggle with Spanish.

Like many of these teachers, Ms. Lagos is tired of teaching. It happens as teachers get older and bored with their own students. Everything is really easy but useless if you are serious and want to have a career in Spanish. Time to retire before you discourge more and more students.
She's a very nice teacher, the reading load is really light, but she is really strict on attendance, so make sure you come to class. She grades easy and the tests are emailed to you and done at home.

while the class is relatively easy (three one to two page papers and two tests), she teaches as if we are still in high school. there is lots of group work where you really don't learn anything and her lectures are inconclusive.
Very helpful and accomodating, super sweet, I loved her, and she's very knowledgeable
She's unclear and kind of mean in class.  Her expectations are not known and she's very forgetful.  If I were you, I'd just wait till another professor was teaching that class.
Awesome teacher and incredibly sweet.

Absolutely amazing. I dreaded taking my last CH class, but that dread disappeared after the first day. He made all the readings accessible online, but there are a lot of readings and sparknotes won't help. He's very passionate about his subject matter in the best of ways and is a hilarious person. Super caring. 12/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really enthusiastic about the material, sometimes to the point that he jumps up and down. Speak up in discussions and you will be fine.
Great professor. A bit out of the ordinary, but his class is very entertaining.  Make sure you read and take notes, and there should be no issue. Would take again.

Callum was my TA for Bird's course. He was great. His expectations are very clear & he's so helpful. Do the reading & be prepared for lecture - help out your classmates & don't look foolish. He really wants everyone to do well. Plus, he's cute.

Prof Ingram is clearly passionate about her subject matter and is a clear and concise lecturer. I only bought 1 textbook and only needed it for citation in the papers - if you listen and take detailed notes during her lectures, you'll have more than enough material for the papers/exams. Attendance and participation matter, thorough notes help.

Don't get fooled by the title. The class has little to do with demonology or ritual and is mostly focused on Russian culture, folklore, and history. Class is easy, just show up and study lecture notes for exams.

Class was pretty boring and did not feel relevant or relatable. Readings were dry and redundant, and it was not made clear what should be studied for exams, as they were based mostly on your ability to cite examples of folklore from text and lecture to back up an argument.

I learned more from reading the nutritional facts of a Pepsi bottle than I did in this class. It's about forgotten holidays and folkloric mysticism, with the weak explanation that a couple freaks still believe in bigfoot as justification for its continued relevance. Teacher reads from a powerpoint, arbitrary grading, conclusion: don't bother.

This woman is ridiculous. Half the time she isn't even talking about anything relevant. Notes are straight from powerpoint. Class not hard, but she refuses to give A's. She is the most off topic lecturer, you'll probably learn more if you don't go to class. Her "examples" are long winded and repetitive. You will learn almost NOTHING.

I can't believe it's possible to make this material boring, but this class manages it. Ingram spends half the class summarizing the last class, and the rest going over the reading almost verbatim. TA was a pain, and comprehension of the material does not = A unless you've stopped yourself from any attempt at interpretation.

you never saw in the same sentence during the lecture or readings and give lots of examples. Plus, open books/notes does not help because you don?t have time to look anywhere in ½ hr. Thus, you can never really write a solid A essay, so Ingram is the one who decides who deserves an A.

The class was extremely boring. Also, Ingram ?specializes? in Ukraine and has not been in Russia since the collapse of USSR, so half the time she is off on the Russian stuff. The exams are graded very subjectively, and it isn?t an easy A class if you?re not one of the favorites. In ½ hr of exam you have to write a whole essay connecting two topics
Everything the person before me said. I didn't get less than an A on anything all year. Interesting class as well.

She is an awesome lecturer - I rarely got bored during class. She knows her stuff and is so passionate about it. It's also super easy...an open book/notes midterm and final and a couple short papers. Get Stan as your TA if possible - he's hilarious and a really easy grader. This is a good class to get your Non-Western Perspectives out of the way.

Cool subject. She is a really good lecturer. keeps you awake.The customs r interesting and keep u attentive. Even disc sections are fun *highly recommend Eric Kenneda* u take a field trip & watch a movie in disc.Openbook/note midterm.only 3 essays 2 write which r simple.Basically if u put effort into this class ur grade will reflect that.
Very easy class! Interesting lectures, easy, short assignments, and an open note, open book mid-term! I'd highly recommend it for people who need their non-western.

Prof. Ingram is so nice.  She is really interested in the subject, and even if you're not, it's still funny to read about goofy slavic customs.  Also, she doesn't expect you to learn nitpicky details which is way-good.
No Comments
Very good professor. Easy to understand and high quality education. Has over 40 years of experience - he's been teaching for two times longer than some of you have been alive! Think about it!
Professor Herbst is a smart man, and he wants to make sure you know that.

I am not the only one who hates this man's teaching. Everyone I have spoken to is terrified of failing this class, and he is NOT AT ALL afraid to fail people. His expectations are wholly unrealistic. His lectures make no sense, and he's cocky and unhelpful. Do everything in your power to avoid his class, even overloading later. DO IT, DEAR GOD.

In class, he runs through incomprehensible and messy proofs. At home, the homework has nothing to do with what was done in class. Wayward and difficult to understand. Makes many errors during class, expects you to have an great understanding already of the class that he's supposed to be teaching, so he is completely unhelpful when asked for help.
The test was much easier than the homeworks which I always appreciate.
No Comments

"A unique sense of humor made him bearable. A lot of derivations and conceptual ideas instead of straightforward problems. Exams were always easier than pratice problems. Always available for office hours."                                               ---Thank you for your objective contribution, Prof herbst.
He stunk for e-school, simple as that. He didn't explain anything or help me at all.

Way better than Thomas who I had for 132.  Herbst explains problems in class so you can do the homework and tests.  Notice only the engineers are complaining...maybe he's better for the college version of the class.

Comes to class with just his sunglasses and a piece of chalk.  Impossible to follow in class.  Everything he wrote on the board was pretty useless.  A lot of students dropped the class.  Unfortunately I tried to stick it out and ended up withdrawing...
AWFUL!  Spends majority of class time trying to convince you he's a math god.  BEWARE!

the worst professor i've ever had...he has terrible methods of delivery, and merely regurgitates the conceptual ideas from the book that you wouldn't read anyway...oh, and his bizarre mannerisms only detract from his rating

This the worst class I have ever taken. Professor Herbst is by far the worst teacher that I've had in the math department, since he can't teach. The other person that gave him a good rating is totally lying. My only advice is to not take his class.

A unique sense of humor made him bearable.  A lot of derivations and conceptual ideas instead of straightforward problems.  Exams were always easier than pratice problems.  Always available for office hours.

I liked calculus until taking 212 with this professor.  He only cares about a few select students, leaving the rest of us to struggle.  This class hurt my gpa more than any other e-school course.  Try to find another professor!
He doesn't prepare lectures and just wings it in class.  He doesn't want to help you succeed.  The tests are killers.  Avoid this teacher unless you don't plan on learning anything.
terrible teacher, uses a lot hand motions when talking about 3-D objects, which are helpless. i don't go class anymore because of his teaching method

She is so kind.  She makes little jokes in class and genuinely wants you to succeed.  Grades very generously, even made our final exam optional. Weekly homework from the textbook which isn't too difficult, weekly quiz in discussion which is made up of problems directly from the homework, 3 exams, and a final. She speaks quietly so sit in the front!

Dr. Lasiecka along with Dr. Wang were two of my best proffessors at UVA ever. Not only they were great but as human beings they are angels sent from heaven. I loved both of them dearly. If you ever have to take MATH 331 or MATH 354 take them with one of them. I promise you that you will do good.

She's so lovely. Be warned, she does speak softly. But she makes up for that with her clarity. She does a lot of hw problems for you during the course. This is a very clear, easy math course. I just took care to study a little and I got a 499/500 for both midterms combined. Really nice class.
She cares what you learnt in this class. And she makes abstract thoerems extremely clear.
She is a really nice professor. Her lectures are very clear and helpful, which is of great importance for a course like MATH331.

Yes, she speaks softly but she is a great teacher. if you have to take MATH 331, definitely take it with her. I took it with someone else first and dropped it because it was impossible, but after taking it with Lasiecka I expect to get an A. she genuinely cares and wants you to do well, unlike a lot of teachers in the department.
Her lectures are unclear and boring. Don't take her for MATH 331.
her accent is pretty easy to get use to and understand. she's very patient and helpful.

she does speak softly and has some accent, but she is a very nice lady who wants students to do well in her class.going to her office hours is very helpful. her grading is relatively easy.she teaches via expamples (LOVED IT!).if u review notes and the examples she gives, u will do well in the class.
I could not understand her all semester. She is very quiet and has an accent. Easy grading criteria on tests though. She is also helpful if you go to her office hours.

she's real cool.  you'll appreciate her lingo as she goes through the examples.  however, she is fairly soft spoken, and has a heavy accent. diff eq requires endless hours of homework no matter who you have...

Very hard to understand, ONLY teaches with examples and doesn't explain what she is actually doing.  Unless you read material beforehand, it will take the entire class to simply figure out what your trying to solve, let alone why.
excellent teacher because she teaches via examples. if you understand the homework you will do well in the class.  the tuesday hour is essential so do attend
She is a helpful teacher if you can hear her.  She speaks softly and moves quickly. If you take good notes on what she writes on the board, you'll be set for homeworks and tests.
She explains things really well if you can get used to her accent. From what I hear, she's better than the other diff-eq teachers out there.
If you do the homework and understand it, you'll do fine on the tests. Overall Good lecturer, sometimes the definitions get technical and hard to understand, but that's math I guess.
If you do the homework, the test won't be impossible. She is very generous with the curve. If you try, you'll do well.
nice person and good lecturer, but has a accent u need to get used to.
The homework took 4-5.5 hours every week. Tests are too long for the amount of time we have and she'll ask you things we never did in class or on the homework. Overall she is a good lecturer.
hard class, but if you do the hw, u'll get at least a b+ on the test

Absolutely awful. His lectures are monotone, but there was no textbook and his notes were terrible. He taught in a deliberately obtuse way to 'make you think' (a senior level class). Then he would not share homework solutions or respond to questions. I could handle his distain for students if he was a useful professor. As is I had to teach myself.

Lark is one of my favorite professors that I have had. He is likely the smartest person I have taken a class from and he is good at explaining things. Assignments were designed to make sure that you knew and understood the material rather than make you fail. Also go to office hours! Enjoyable to talk to and has lots of cool stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a fine professor. Nothing special. His lectures are hella boring and I got annoyed that so many were for "cultural edification" that we weren't graded on when I had actual questions about the real material. But, he's not terrible. He has his policies and he sticks to them. He says attendance is mandatory, but do what you want.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No reason to go to class half the time, class is very dry and boring anyway. Other half is quizzes and turning in homework. Two tests & a final, 1 project.

The worst teacher I have ever had at UVA. He is slow and boring. Most students took a nap in his class. He hates being challenged and he wont like you after that. Very eregant man. I had to teach everything I know about that class. I got a B but I strongly believe I would of got an A if I was a girl. My girlfriend got an A!!!!!! I thought her every
QUite interesting to talk to.  He doesnt think his class is the only class we have, very considerate. NO TESTS, just projects and is very easy with his grading
James Lark is the man! Great lecturer, had SYS 201 and APMA 312 with him, and he really knows his stuff.  Would recommend him for any class.

He is meticulously thorough in everything he does. Some classes get longwinded and there is no such thing as a short stop by office hours. He is very bright and very fair on tests and grading. Great professor.
No reason to go to class at all, 3 projects, no work at all - no grades- VERY EASY!  Really nice guy, but the class is just pointless... take it!
3 projects, no other work.
interesting lectures, 3 large projects no other work, nice guy
No Comments
Very interestin lectures and minimal workload
Professor Lark helped make 1st year bearable.  Wonderful professor.
No Comments
Great Professor; his projects are interesting and his lectures are helpful
3 big projects but besides that almost zero workload

She was very caring, but she went on rants during lectures and was unclear about the syllabus, grading, timing, and did not submit our grades until the end of the semester. If you are ready to read, this is a great class, but not easy. She sprung a final on us after not communicating in the syllabus that there was one. Must participate once a class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely one of my favorite professors ever. She is incredibly knowledgeable and thoughtful in her lectures. I genuinely looked forward to her class every time. As a person, you can tell she cares that people learn and is less strict about measuring it by grades. She is very personable and the way that she teaches is inspiring. Just the best.

Class is all over the place and hard to follow. I only took this class because it was required, but while it was supposed to be an engagement, I instead got her political views and ideals forced upon me. If you don't write and respond with opinions that match hers, you will not do well.

Prof. Schmidt was very kind and inspiring, but so disorganized that the class became difficult to follow. Her assignments weren't hard but sometimes seemed trivial with unclear instructions. There was a lot of trouble with due dates, and again the class was extremely confusing and chaotic. Definitely interesting, just wish it was better executed.

Prof. Schmidt cares a lot about activism and the community at UVA, and this engagement class is her passion project. However, the assignments/expectations are often unclear and her lectures tend to stumble and wander. As a political person, I had hoped to learn more but most knowledge was very surface-level. Grading was lenient and group-based.
Very inspirational invidual.
She is wonderful. She is the wind beneath my wings, as it were. She took me on an ethnic journey I didn't know I needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: There is so much reading. If you don't do it, and you're gonna have a REALLY tough time.

I enrolled in this class primarily because all other classes fulfilling the non-western requirement were full. I ended up loving the class. As a chem major with taking mostly science courses, this class was wonderful. She is a great lecturer, and the readings are interesting. Must say she is a tough grader. One paper,  midterm/final are all essays.

This class is different. Lots of emphasis on historiography and learning about an often overlooked aspect of history. LOTS of reading (via collab or books on reserve...~30 to read for each class session). Kind of rambles on in class talking about lots of things. Only 2 tests, 1 paper (easy). You get what you put into this class.
She is very abstract and confusing. Tends to be very theatrical but it makes her point hard to understand.

I took Orgo I with Professor Samonina somewhat by chance. I am an international student, English is not my native language, and I am not on a pre-health track. Despite these challenges, I earned an A in the course, and I honestly believe Professor Samonina is the best Orgo I instructor among all available options.

I took her engagement class which was very lovely. Fun topics, interesting final project, easy enough assignments, and lots of discussion within table groups. Willing to work with students on extenuating circumstances, and a fun person in general. This was an easy and entertaining engagement course that I would recommend.

(Pt.2 review below). The grade is spread out between HW, iclicker questions, quizzes, and extra credit that she adds to your final grade (this really makes a difference!) She gives cold exams as practice for the tests and they are 95% like the exam. Study based on those and you will be fine. She dropped 1 exam, 1 quiz and 1 HW.

Dr. S. is overall a great professor. She knows the material and can explain things in different ways if you are having a hard time understanding it. She is available to be a mentor if you need and when I thought I was failing she told me to go to her office so we could work things out. She is there to help if you need and truly want to learn Ochem.

Super nice professor! She was a great teacher and presented the material clearly. The tests grades were padded with homework, participation, and extra credit grades and she drops the lowest quiz grades. Not flexible with grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rubenstein is honestly probably my favorite professor I've had. I took politics of emergencies with her and she has a really interesting way of teaching class. In true seminar fashion, we have discussions to learn, rather than a lecture, which is a great way to explore how you think, though I wish I got to hear her genius and thoughts more lol!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Truly one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of learning from at UVA. In her politics of emergencies seminar, she allows students to take control of the conversations to build their own ideas and thoughts surrounding class content, instead of lecturing and teaching her own perspective. She is a joy to learn from! Take her if you can!!
Unclear grading criteria, conflicting feedback. Often left impression that she did not do the readings she assigned to students for class and seemed unfamiliar with common interpretations of them.
She's very caring and clearly wants students to succeed. Ask questions and take advantage of office hours, and you'll do fine.

I have never met a professor so full of love and care. Her class is well taught as she puts so much effort into doing demos and makes herself so accessible for office hours (she has them nearly every weekday). She breaks down topics as best she can. Great pace. I wish there could be an award for her. She is so caring and makes me feel like family.

She is the kindest physics professor ever and cares for her students success. The best STEM professor I have had at UVA and truly wants you to understand physics and make a required class for pre-health enjoyable. She has extra credit on exams and also prepares you very well for the types of questions on her exams through review and practice tests
She is a great professor. She cares more about you success than any other professor ever will.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Marcel is one of the funniest and most insightful professors I've had the joy to have at UVA. His lectures were entertaining and thought provoking. He will always challenge your ideas but will never make you feel bad about any inconsistencies or for being "wrong." Really nice guy, I highly recommend him!

Professor Marcel communicates the material well, but his introverted nature tends to rub students the wrong way. Not the most inviting of professors, but he does a good job of teaching the material. I personally appreciated his down to earth teaching style. Does a good job of refining students' answers in class without telling them they are wrong.

Marcel is a great professor.  He teaches you a lot of material in a short amount of time, and is very down to earth.  He jokes around a lot and doesn't take the subject too seriously, which is refreshing.  Definitely do your reading before class!

Jerk. unclear and terrible teacher. thinks hes better than everyone else. has no interest in students work at all. skips major presentations. inconsistent grading highlighted by a complete lack of interest in student's performance
Strategy professor. Funny laid back guy, but he can be very frustrating. Difficult to please- most people think he doesnt like them. Ive had him for a year and hes still a big mystery.

This class is a grind, just like 2020. Mitchell is very caring and accessible, but since it's asynchronous you just won't come in contact with her often. Class is hard: please use TAs/office hours/study groups, etc. Too hard to try to figure it out on your own. Just as rough as financial in my opinion.

Mitchell is very accessible, cares about her students succeeding, and is very knowledgeable. However, accounting is brutal - you have to put in the work and GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU DO NOT UNDERSTAND IT. Too hard to try to teach yourself. Use the TAs & Mitchell. Tons of homework and it's a huge time suck but you just gotta grind through.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Mitchell is amazing! COMM 2010 was my first accounting class ever, and I loved it. Professor Mitchell makes the class feel as synchronous as it can be! She responds to individual and class questions in Teams quickly and thoroughly, and you can tell she really cares about her students. I would recommend stopping by her office hours.
The worst teacher I have ever had. Absolutely no empathy for students, even if you have an extenuating circumstances. She made me want to transfer.

First and foremost there was no syllabus or schedule for this class. He made his own separate website where we have to do everything there. He did not teach clearly and stutters when to explain something in detail. He's TA had to do all the work, all we did was watch her type and copy what she wrote. There was no in class assignments.

Insanely easy course. Pay attention during lectures and you'll do fine. Really likes questions and participation. There's a lot of homework, but they take like 5min and can be completed before even attending lecture most the time. If you have complicated questions/ concerns, TA's are usually more helpful than prof.

I found that this class was very easy personally, however I do not believe that this professor is the most clear concerning the course material.  He often stumbled when asked to explain something in further detail.
Very unclear. Speaks with weird accent. Seems very confident but doesn't really know what he himself is talking about. Wouldn't recommend him.

Professor is very nice, easygoing, and patient. This course is not very hard but requires you to attend classes regularly cos everything in the exam will be related to what he taught in class. It's easy to get an A if you follow him in class. Strongly recommended if you want to take 302 and want to learn some serious stuff while still getting an A.
Tests are easy if study the notes and practice exams.
His lectures are well organized
Not organized. Hard to understand. Doesn't care about the class whatsoever. Just avoid!!!!!

He doesn't care about this class. Read from slides and explain common sense for 30 minutes. Final paper was 15 pages with single space. Don't think he actually read my paper because it was absolutely horrible. He is not that terrible because he still gave me nice grade. However, if you want to learn something with that much tuition, avoid!
was really thorough and explained all the proofs well.
Once I spent an entire class trying to figure out that he meant "bias" and "association" when he said "bears" and "a social issue."

Don't waste your time going to class because you won't anything. A graphing calculator will literally give you almost all the answers so if you learn how to use it and read the book for content understanding you will do fine.  This is probably the worst class I will ever have to take at UVa

3 exams and assignment. Zhou's explanation is very bad. 95% of my understanding came from reading the textbook and reading his slides from my room. Exam is pretty hard, though is quite fair because few obscure material. Need to put extra effort in this class. I will get a B+ or A depending if he curves.
I don't the the professor helped understanding the materials, and I ended up study all by myself.
Worst professor I have ever had.  Nice guy...terrible teacher.  If you take his class you'll spend most of your time teaching yourself the material.

This professor is clearly very smart and knows what he is doing, however he does a really poor job of making sure the students know what they are doing.  This class sucks. Do not take unless absolutely necessary.

Seems like a nice guy, but is very hard to understand. The TA's are helpful though. Does nothing to help students actually work out the problems on either the calculator or excel. In short, you will end up having to teach yourself. It helps immensely to have taken this class in high school.

Jing is hilarious. There is a language barrier at times, but she will explain information repeatedly until it is completely clear to the entire class. She teaches to the test and there will be very few surprises overall. I am not a math person at all, but found her class entertaining and easy because of the way she taught.
Funniest teacher ever. Are you happy with result? ARE YOU HAPPY? Hilarious. Fantastic teacher. If you get her be sure to give her a high five at some point. It'll be the best experience of your life.

Her accent makes her difficult to understand at times, and theres often a language barrier in asking questions.  She mostly teaches through examples on the board, and makes rather frequent mistakes.  The class isnt really hard, but unless youve taken calc before, try to get into a different section
She tries to explain everything so that everyone and i mean EVERYONE in the class understands. Also her office hours were really helpful.
Even though english is her second language, it doesn't really get in the way of her teaching although sometimes there are some funny awkward moments with communication. Jing's accent is adorable.

Jing's lectures are a complete waste of time, because she only goes over the examples in the book - you can do that yourself. She also moves very fast, and her accent makes her difficult to understand. She also tended to make mistakes on the board. The homework that she gives from the textbook is easy to do; however, the webassign that she gives me

I felt respected as a student by Prof. Rini. He explained the Spanish language to us in a beautiful, non-patronizing way. He understood we are learning and took his time during lectures, emphasizing our understanding over everything else. Great man, I'm honored to have taken his class.

Professor Rini is easily my favorite professor at UVA. He is hilarious and makes the 1:15 lectures really entertaining and funny. He is so chill and cool and makes this class really interesting. I definitely suggest him!

Rini is, overall one of the best professors I've had at UVa (I am 4th year). He is a genuinely good person- kind, funny, crude, brilliant, inappropriate, suave as all he*l; he rocks a sweet slicked-back haircut and taught me a ton of Spanish. I freckin' loved the guy. I wish I could hang out with him on weekends.

I'm a 4th year and this was my favorite class/professor at UVA. It's super easy as long as you pay attention. Prof. Rini is kind and hilarious. Always helpful &will explain any question patiently. We have laughed A LOT in this class (and no cursing). I've never seen him get mad. 4 Exams (1 oral) not cumulative. Everything straight from notes.

Prof. Rini makes a very technical class seem like a fun conversation. There is a lot to handle but he makes it interesting, and his tests are straightforward. He sets up his classes to be low-pressure, though you can't afford to slack. He is a kind, and interesting person (and I never noticed any "constant cursing"!!)

Professor Rini is definitely one of the best! He's very knowledgeable, enthusiastic, and helpful. Phonetics is definitely one of my all time favorite classes I've taken at UVA. It's unlike any Spanish class I've taken before! I highly recommend it (especially for Spanish majors)!

Professor Rini was such a fun professor, always making jokes and laughing. He made a subject matter that could have been really dry, very interesting. There are 3 exams (the last being the final which is not cumulative) and an oral; there was homework 2 times throughout the semester. He's such a great professor, by far one of my favorites at UVA!
He was very interesting and knowledgeable on the subject. We didn't have homework or a book, which was great at first, but I think doing some work outside of class would have helped me on the exams.
Profesor Rini is my favorite teacher so far.  The class has no work outside of class and is really easy if you go to class.  He wants everyone to do well.  Great guy!

GREAT guy!!  He wants everyone to do well, and he takes the time in class to make sure everyone can pronounce the sounds correctly.  Phonetic transcriptions are kind of tricky, but the class is fun nonetheless.

i genuinely adore this guy. he is so whimsical and very witty, but more importantly he is extraordinarily knowledgable and a joy to hear lecture. if you're willing to put in the work of showing up, paying attention, and preparing before class (yes, you have to read---this is a philosophy course, what else were you planning to do?) he'll reward you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just a solid meh. Technically lectures are required, but I would usually skip and just get the info from discussion. Entire grade based on quizzes and tests, which are taken home paragraphs answering questions. Lectures were very hard to follow. Still finished with an A- minus though, so not too bad.

Your grade depends entirely on your TA and their grading. You get graded on maybe 3 quizzes and a final paper, it's very hard to get an A with how some philosophy TAs grade. IMO take another philosophy class - this one is a snoozer with the exception of Socrates and Descartes, the class is very repetitive but prof is cool

A very disorganized course. The discussion section doesn't match the lectures at all. The Professor just rambles on. He spends way too much time on Descartes which results in us rushing through other philosophers. He barely gives any direction for class. Some people might enjoy his class, but not me.

Prof. Secada is a super nice man. I took his class on medieval philosophy and it was really neat to learn about the history and the thinking back then. The lectures do require a bit of coffee but are super interesting. The reading is also a bit dense, but it's usually short enough that it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures can be confusing, but its mostly because he tries to cover so much in such a sort amount of time. Bring coffeetea with you and open up your brain to new things. There are whole semester classes for what he tries to get through in 4-5 weeks. Overall, the TAs will help you if you're not into office hours, but he's a helpful nice guy.

I attended almost every lecture but I have no idea why because there is absolutely no need  to go. I could never follow anything he was saying. The only reason I was bale to even know what was going on was from my discussion section.
He's a very interesting guy and knows a lot about a variety of areas in philosophy.  He is considered one of the smartest professors on grounds.
Horribly organized class. No sense of what we're doing at any given time
Native Spanish speaker and often rambles; not really a good teacher overall; tries to go way more in depth in the intro class than he should; TAs often complained as well
Boring lectures. Boring material. No use of powerpoint (or equivalent) what so ever. About 50% dropped out after the first class. I was dumb enough to stay.
Not a very gifted pedagogue.  I wasn't very interested in the primary texts at first, and I wasn't afterward.

Secada clearly knows a lot about philosophy but he does not teach it well for an introductory class. I skipped lectures a lot and learned most of my information from discussion sections. The content of the course was worth it though. Don't be afraid of how he comes across the first lecture day, he makes the class seem much harder than it really is.

Professor Secada is a very intelligent prof on philosophy, going to lectures is your best bet to do well, but ALSO have to learn to listen and write down notes. Do well by writing down notes, his ramblings are interesting tho. Gives you a good spectrum of philosophy and topics in it. Interesting, just listening and note-taking in class tho. Smart p
He is difficult to follow during lecture.  He rambles often.  I only stuck with the class because of my TA Matt Tirrigan.

Not a bad professor, but don't take unless you're really really into metaphysics and Descartes, Spinoza, and Liebniz. Reading the primary texts is not half as important as reading the secondary literature and going to lecture. You have to learn how to listen to him, but it's worth it to try.
He's a rambler. Really smart though, but hard to follow. But, I think he knows it, so he makes up for it by making the tests easy.

This man is brilliant, but let's say he's just on a different plane from the rest of us. Lectures usually ramble on and he takes sporadic attendance. It's not too important to come to class although I'm pretty sure he favors you during grading if he's seen you. You'll basically be guaranteed a B-/B just for breathing.

His class is not very well structured, and I found it very difficult to follow along in lecture since they were almost never related to the assigned readings at the time.  If you love philosophy, go ahead, but not for someone who isnt in love  with it.  Also, "The Ethics of Conquest" is misleading.  The class is more about...well, i couldnt tell yo
bored me, but if youre interested in phil, not a bad class

White is a really nice professor and really cares about her students. It's not her fault the class is terrible, it's the way UVA requires language courses to be run. She makes the best out of their system though, the class is easy.

Prof. White is excellent in SPAN 2010! The course is much more discussion-based than 1060, but she made sure to review difficult concepts in lecture. Also, she was very helpful with composition and project corrections. The biggest downfall in 2010 is the level of work enforced by the department, but White did everything she could to help us succeed
There is a good amount  of work, but she's really nice and willing to help.

Mrs. White is a nice teacher. The online homework in accelerated Spanish is excessive though. The Syllabus says about 8 hours a week for online homework. The tests are ok and there is a video project and a cultural paper. She talks as fast as native speakers that I know, but you get used to it. Would take again if it wasn't accelerated.

I loved Senorita White. She was a really great instructor. She does talk really fast, so it's kind of difficult when taking notes. If you don't understand something, tell her!!! She will help you until you get it. The homework on Connect can be long & difficult. So don't put it off. ALWAYS have your book because you WILL use it every class!!!
He's incredible. Would take again.

I took this class my first semester and loved it. There are just two 3-page papers and two take-home closed-book exams (pretty much short essays which you're allowed to type). Professor Connolly loves what he teaches and brings a lot of depth to discussion. It's a lot of reading, but a pretty easy A/A- if you do read!

Professor Connolly is one of my favorite professors at UVA. This was my second class with him, I loved the first one so much, I had to take another. He is extremely passionate about the subject and makes Russian literature (which can be a little dark and dry) come to life in his lectures. Papers aren't hard if you attend lectures.
Great professor, incredibly knowledgeable and enthusiastic
AmazingggggG!

Connolly is hilarious, energetic and extremely knowledgable. Although he doesn't take attendance, he goes over important themes and info from the books in detail in lecture so going definitely helps on the exams. His class was my favorite last semester--I wish he could teach all my classes!

Lots of reading, but worthwhile. Connolly is super smart and an excellent lecturer. He's very passionate about what he does, and it's contagious! Great class, a painless way to learn Russian Literature.
Knows what he teaches.
So helpful. One of the nicest people I know. OVERWHELMINGLY reminds me of Shaggy from Scooby Doo.   Take any of his classes
No Comments

awesome teacher -- so into it! he knows his stuff, and makes it interesting. very willing to listen to anyone's interpretations, answer questions in and outside of class. very funny and nice and charasmatic. i learned a great deal in this class.
Awesome lectures, interesting teacher. A lot of reading, but not that hard of a class.
His lectures are very clear and he makes some good insights, a definite A++!

To be honest, if you've already taken Calculus 1 (IB/AP/DE) this class is fairly easy. Spencer is very nice and understanding, however, this class can be incredibly confusing if its your first time in a Calc class. If this is your first time in Calc 1, I don't think this professor would be best, but if you took Calc 1 before, it'll be a breeze.

Don't listen to the other reviews, trust, this woman is God sent. Shes so understanding and you can tell she actually cares about her students. Math doesn't come to me easily but she helped sooo much. She makes getting help so easy and accessible I love this woman.

Prof Spencer is great. I had her for APMA 1090. She is chill and not strict on attendance. She takes time to teach each class and is extremely approachable and very kind. I was nervous going into her class because of reviews but I am so glad she is my professor. There are checkpoints instead of exams which you get multiple attempts for as well.

The class had a unique teaching method but was overall very nice. While the constant assignments did get inconvenient at times, I would take this class any day over constant lectures. Spencer is a joy to be around and did well to guide us through the work. My one complaint was the vaguely worded questions on many assignments.

My experience with this class was horrible. The professor is awful and doesn't know how to teach. The tests are absurdly hard compared to what is taught in class. It should not be this time-consuming for a 4 credit class, the whole course needs a new director
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Completely misunderstands the role of a teacher as someone who needs to convince students of the truth rather than simply offering it. The kind smile gives way to hurtful social tactics and extreme lack of professionalism when her teaching style and grading is challenged. Typos in every worksheet. Disorganized. Disappointed.

Her attitude was always very positive and charismatic, but the class is completely structured on learning with groups and with explorative worksheets--the organization of material wasn't great. Also, I would consider her a harsh grader, as she is particular about math/answer formatting.

** Eng Math 1 APMA 6410 **
Avoid her at all costs. She is literally the worst. So disorganized, awful at lecturing, takes forever to grade. Final grades are due in 45 minutes, and we still don't have a grade (received grades for a midterm and hw 3 days ago). She makes stupid mistakes in class, but is still a really harsh grader on hw/exams.

Prof Spencer is a great lecturer, but falls short in every other aspect as a teacher. She was very disorganized- constantly would forget to upload assignments, respond to emails, and grade tests among other things. She also gave a lot of work, a preclass and inclass assignment 4 times a week on top of a webwork problem set.
the worst teacher I've ever had

I took her class during coivd. Her style of teaching leaves a lot to the student to figure out, I guess she thinks we learn more that way. Before our first test I had to spend about 2 full days studying (free) online math notes to understand the material and I got an A. The class average was a 69. This shows that free material is better than her.

I really enjoyed my time with Prof Spencer- she was a great teacher for differential equations (although I know some people who said she was not good for prob/stat. She was always very kind and willing to explain anything further. Tests are hard, but not impossible if you pay attention during class and put in the work! Would recommend her!

Easily one of the best professors I've had, her notes are clear and concise, and she really cares about teaching students and helping them become better math students. Some of the earlier negative ratings probably reflect her teaching when she first started.

Best applied math professor I've had here! Lecture is easy to understand and the worksheets make understanding it before doing the HW much easier. Love that she let us vote for 3 or 6 exams. Having 6 has made retaining information and understanding concepts much easier. Also very nice that 1 is dropped. Would 100% try to take another class with her

Prof. Spencer is great! Her lessons are clear, well-structured, and balanced with practice material (which she provides in abundance). She's also super sweet and approachable. Tests are also very fair, and we never need a curve. I wish she taught more math courses!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the most engaged profs I've had here. Her lecture style, which is a little lecture and then the rest of the class on worksheet problems, isn't for everyone. She made herself very available in office hours and is good at explaining things one-on-one. Willing to help, friendly. Gives as much HW as everyone else.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS She doesn't like lecturing, so instead of teaching she hands out groupwork worksheets to "give you practice with the material" except she hasn't taught the material so its groupwork figure out how the thing works. And the sheets are graded. Occasionally clears things up the next day, but then its too late
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Spencer can be difficult to follow and seemed unsure of herself sometimes, but I think this was because it was her first semester teaching at UVA, and as the semester went on she got better at teaching in lectures. She made herself very available during office hours, during which she proved she genuinely wants her students to do well.

Spencer was kind of hard to get used to at the beginning of the semester, but she definitely improved a lot as a teacher. I think that's because it was her first time teaching the course.
