It's also really evident that she cares about her students because she does whatever possible to help us. Also her quizzes are easier than the other professors'.

Very bad teacher she doesn't care if you don't understand the material she moves on. When you email her about the material a week before the quiz she respond the day before the next class she is just a terrible teacher and she do not know how to teach at all. She talk about irrelevant things in class like her cat. Transfer out if you in he class

Really, one of the worst teachers I have ever had. Unclear, disorganized, and doesn't even know how to send an email properly. She always has lower averages than every other teacher simply because of her incompetence and the fact she doesn't write the tests herself. She tries her best, and seems smart, but some people were not meant to teach

Julia is a horrible teacher. I was in her class for two days and realized i would likely fail the course if i continued. Most would say I am a talented math student. I talked to my RA after my second day of class about any good Calc 2 professors and he specifically said to avoid Julia Spencer. He failed when he took it with her. I would agree.

By far the worst teacher I have ever had. Does not teach in class and instead forces you to watch 30-45 minute lectures outside of class. Gives unreasonable amounts of homework that far exceeds the difficulty of Calc 3 or other Calc 2 classes. Incredibly disorganized. If you get her, change immediately.
doesnt teach well at all but really wants to help
She was very disorganized and hard to understand.  She often would get really frazzled and have trouble explaining things.  Don't recommend

She is a grad student, just like the rest of the calc II teachers.  Was not an easy class.  You'll have weekly quizzes, online homework, two midterms and a final. The quizzes and homework actually helped me learn the material even if it wasn't always easy to keep up.  The best advice I have is to GO TO OFFICE HOURS.  Helped me get an A in the class
She was very disorganized and lectures were hard to follow since she would repeatedly erase all the work she had done. She's a nice person but not a great teacher. I really don't recommend

Really nice guy, the tests are legit copy and paste the study guide so if you go to lecture and do the study guides its an easy A, plus the content is interesting. The only thing is the TA grades the essays a little hard so I would recommend going to his office hours to go over your essays. Other than that great class!

Great professor and great class! The material is really fascinating. The professor explains things clearly, and the tests are outlined with a study guide so they're straightforward. Class doesn't require much work either. Only thing is, I felt like some of the readings were oddly specific and might not be representative of the historical era.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My GOAT great guy chill class interesting content what more can a girl ask

Karl is so kind and genuinely cares for his students. He made the environment so welcoming for us and the class itself super low stress. There are only 3 short writing assignments, one presentation (super laid back), and a reading or episode due each week. If you like The Good Place, philosophy, or religion, TAKE THIS.

I want to take all of his classes, that's how good he is! Presents everything clearly, follows the syllabus, and offers help whenever possible. The class doesn't require too much work. He's also really funny and kind, which is a plus!

Very kind guy. Midterm and final are outlined by a study guide so there are no tricks. There are 3 short papers, a midterm, a final, and weekly quizzes posted online. Attendance is not mandatory at all nor is the weekly reading. Just take notes in class and you'll pass.
He's an interesting guy and a very reasonable professor, grading and attendance-wise.
Such a wonderful man and a great teacher! Loved being in his class, even though I didn't find the material particularly interesting! I definitely recommend taking classes with him.
Clear outlines and helpful lecturer, always available for office hours.

Unreasonably harsh grading. I had a 97 but got an A- because of nitpicking on citations in a dance class. Expectations changed last minute, and the final was graded like a research seminar. Rigid, unforgiving, and disconnected from the course's actual focus.

one of my favorite profs ever. she's so nice and willing to help you with anything. she is a tough grader though- i thought this class was going to be an easy A but you really have to write well, do all the readings, and participate in class. we did a lot of fun movement experiences in the theaters which everybody seemed to enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not be fooled by this 1000 level Drama class. This professor makes you work and I would only recommend this class for people serious about the Dance minor. The few assignments we have are graded strictly and seriously for both content and form. Quite often, homework would consist of a 10+ page reading and a 30+ minute long dance piece.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: LOVE LOVE LOVE HER! Amazing teacher who wants to help us do well. Available outside of class. Tests are 75% (3 midterms, no final) but they're all very fair and you will do well if you study. Doesn't follow UVA grading scale (90 = A, 85 = A-, etc.) so class wasn't super stressful. Loved her, will take any other classes she teaches in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lab course was straightforward and relatively easy. Definitely take if you take the lecture as it will complement learning.

This class was difficult conceptually, but Schiro gives you exams to help you learn the material and to see where her students are at in terms of understanding. The course was "curved." Asides from the grade, I came out of this class having learned so much. 10/10 take Tropical Meteorology if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Schiro is amazing. Def take this and her other Meteorology course. Get to know her during office hours. one of the few professors I have had that cares about her student's success.

Professor Schiro was incredibly passionate while lecturing, which was really great. She was definitely more invested in the material than any other professor I've had. Make sure you read the textbook and do the extra credit, but an A is very attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly Professor Neff is an angel, she is so understanding and an amazing professor. I loved her class so much and she was always accommodating (for sickness, mental health, etc)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you are going to take SPAN 2010 at UVA, you should take it with Professor Neff. She is very caring and wants students to challenge themselves in class by talking. She is a very fair grader and the class is not too difficult. Attendance is mandatory and will ensure success in the class.

Best spanish teacher I've had and a great person. Class was fun, she really cares about her students and it shows. My class was 9 AM M,W,F and I honestly was not upset about it because of how great she was. I can't recommend enough.
I loved professor Neff she was great and made online learning really fun.

Professor Neff is the best professor for anyone who is taking Spanish for the first time. She is very patient and pushes her students to speak in Spanish in class. She is a sweetheart and always makes herself available to students outside of the classroom. She is very understanding and tries to make the lectures fun at times for the students. AMAZI

Very talented professor who has an ability to be understandable to someone who has never learned a word of Spanish. She is gifted in this sense and it allowed me to be able to pick up on so many parts of the language simply from paying attention to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Neff really taught the introductory course extremely well. She comes to class very prepared and creates a welcoming environment that allows everybody to feel comfortable. Learning a new language can be difficult, but she really helps and allows students the chance to learn. I'm excited to take the next semester with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Neff is by far my favorite professor at UVA. Not only is she extremely passionate about teaching Spanish, she truly wants all of her students to learn and be successful. If you put the effort in and do the assignments, you will get a good grade, both in 1010 and 1020.

She was absolutely amazing for both SPAN 1010 and SPAN 1020.  She goes above and beyond the rest of the intro level teachers to help you understand what she's trying to convey if you're not quite getting the Spanish. She gives excellent feedback and has a variety of in-class activities to make the material more relevant.

I kind of liked this class but I took it on MWF at 8 am which is not  good idea. It's a spanish requirement so it's pretty easy. She will bring your grade down if you miss more than 3 classes so be aware of that. Other than that she's a pretty cool professor.

I had Professor Neff while she was at Longwood University, and I felt she was very good with the class, and understood that not every gets the material all at once or right when its taught. She was helpful and was always willing to work anything out if there was a problem. Extremely friendly, I do not regret having her

It was alright. She's not about to speak to you in English but ever so often she doesn't mind if the entire class is clueless. Doesn't spend too much time on grammar althought she's gotten better as the semester went on. It's just another spanish class. Keep in mind I had to get up for the class because it was early.
Great Professor and is extremely helpful when you need it. Would 100% recommend taking her class!

Professor Kallivayalil is literally my hero. I loved her class. Easy enough to not feel like you're selling your soul to pass a random elective, but challenging enough to be at the very least interesting. She's super kind and super accessible, and she can make any impossible astronomical subject sound simple.

Prof K is super kind and so passionate about Astronomy. The class itself was very easy, which made it a lot easier to enjoy the content. Your grade consists of weekly homework assignments, 3 quizzes, 2 labs, and class participation (answering questions online). Definitely recommend taking this course if you're looking for an easy A.

Professor Kallivayalil is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. Her class is super easy and interesting, and the labs are awesome (you even get to go to the observatory and look through the telescope!). Overall, if you're looking for an easy, fun class to fulfill your science credit, look no further.

Grade based on 2 pass/fail labs that are impossible to mess up, 3 open note/book tests (final is non-cumulative), weekly homework which helps a ton for the tests, and answering questions in real time during class (which is how she takes attendance). She is incredibly caring and sweet, which was especially apparent after the events of November 13.

Because of the large class size, it can sometimes be difficult to engage with her, but she lets you know that she's available if you need her. Attendance is taken through Learning Catalytics. She assigns homework reviews once a week and there are two quizzes and two labs. Pretty low-stress class that provides good information on astronomy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I got a bad grade so take the review with a grain of salt. Regardless, my main issue with this prof. is his personality. Don't be fooled by his "nice old man" persona -- he doesn't quite listen if you need something. He will answer a question you didn't ask, and assert he's correct. (happened to students a few times).
Almost a stereotype for the perfect college bio professor.

Professor Kozminski is extremely caring. His lectures are very detailed. Participation is very important as the slides have no words. He makes everything very understandable as long as you pay attention to each piece. The test require application rather than memorization, but I have never come across an unfair question. Class was very interesting.

Professor Kozminkski uses slides that are useless if you are to miss class. They are full of diagrams and studies, not the take-home points. The course has 4 exams, each worth 25% of your grade. The questions on the exam are difficult and don't come from the material presented in class or the text.

Take it in the Fall with Wormington if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kozminski can come off as slightly odd at first, but he is intensely passionate about cellular and synthetic biology which is more than can be said about the usual type of professor that are his professional equivalents. You will learn more with him, but it will require more attention to detail to achieve a high grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kozminski is an amazing professor. He gets a lot of bad reviews, but thats just a reflection of the difficulty and heavy nature of the material. He is very thorough and very talented at explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He seems to be a nice guy, but his lectures are super heavy, and he does not care about your individual grade. I went to him several times and told him that I don't do well with tests, which sucks because he only gives exams, no homework. I would recommend Wormington if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests include small side notes from the text that seem important and tricky critical thinking. He does not curve, offer corrections, or have any other assignments to buffer the test grades. He assigns readings from the textbook every class, which is normal except for the fact that each chapter of reading requires several hours to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awful person and awful teacher. Chronic liar. Doesn't have clear expectations or a real gradebook. Is not knowledgeable on the subject and is very boring. Messes up a lot in class and expects students to miraculously know things he's never talked about. I don't thinking teaching is the right profession for him, let alone science.
Not an awful lecturer, but goes in to a ton of detail. Tests are extremely difficult. I wish I had waited until this semester to take the class with Wormington.
Lectures were clear and somewhat entertaining, but Kozminski expects a lot from his students.
Kozminski's lectures were very disorganized--people often looked around the classroom to see if they were the only ones not understanding--they weren't!

Horrible class. He curves to a C after giving tests where the averages are in the 50's. The class was disorganized and didn't flow together well.  The book sucked.Overall, this class has made me regret declaring a biology major.It's damn near impossible to get a decent grade in here bc even if you do better than average, you can get  C+. :<
smug & bizarre, but funny jokes... seems to hate and love teaching biology (at the same time). thought he was great and his teaching was good-- dont miss lectures, though!
Very smart, but not good at relating difficult material to students.  You will have to work a lot with the TA.
A smart man, but his tests are hard and he has no reservations in failing students or giving them low grades.
Professor Khan is a wonderfully caring and also extremely knowledgeable, and fair, professor. Very passionate.

Professor Khan is actually a great professor. There is a lot of reading assigned, but a student can get away with skimming. His lectures are very interesting and his grading criteria is very clear. Honestly, show up and participate in discussions and you will be fine. (Only problem is he does not believe in giving A+)
He really knows his stuff. Taught me a lot about Pakistani Tablighis. Really moving information about a culture.

The class emphasizes on self-study and self-motivation. The class meeting is lengthy and does not value so much as off-class reading. If you do the reading and really think about the issues Mr. Khare brings up in class, the paper-writing and the study process would be pretty joyful.

The class was kind of boring. He really does have a monotone voice, even though he speaks very slow and clearly. I feel that while I did learn some things about India, I didn't really learn as much as I wished I had because of the class structure.
very boring, monotone speaker.. dont have to really do the reading.. only two papers in the class, but you have to choose your own topic.. basically its up to the class to make the class interesting
She gives you so much individual attention. I felt like she cared about helping me with my specific issues. I should have gone to office hours more.

She is kind and makes class fun. The assignments and homework and more boring assignments are fun and we get to talk about them in class and she makes sure everyone understands what is going on without leaving anyone behind but it isn't boring even if you are really good at it. She makes herself really available and really wants us to succeed.

This is the best class I have ever taken. She is fun and kind and smart and funny. I would totally recommend it. She makes it easy if you are willing to do the work and sometimes she brings her puppies to class.

Absolutely the worst class available at UVA. The professor is incredibly rude, puts down those who have varying opinions, is an especially tough grader, and is overall completely unworthy to be considered a professor. Avoid this class if you have any dignity.

Give the course a chance. It was very enjoyable, though she grades a bit critically. The workload was fair, just about as much as I'd expect from a second writing requirement course. Professor Kim is very eloquent and knowledgeable, and honestly wants her students to do well and succeed not only in the course but in life as well.
Didn't learn anything in the class. Grades way too harsh and the workload was crazy for an elective class.

Dr. Kim is great! She's very articulate and passionate about the material presented in the course and always does her best to make students understand everything. She'll even look at your paper topics ahead of time and give you suggestions on how to improve it. Her classes were some of the coolest at UVA so be sure to try some of them out!

She is very articulate, and substance of the course is phenomenal and eye-opening. She is extremely helpful and kind with students, and I have high hopes for her as the new director for Korean studies in UVa. She is what UVa has been waiting for, and my semester with her was one of the best I have spent with a professor. All my classmates agree.
Okay. 2 tests. 1 page weekly papers. Exams are hard.

Professor Klein is kind of awesome. Makes all his lectures conversational and seems to get his point across without any difficult language or concepts. Encourages class discussion which you have to write a single-page paper on once a week. Tests aren't that difficult. Open-book, and as long as you take good notes or have a friend it's fine.

If you are interested in the material, Klein is not difficult at all. If you do the work and show up to class, you will be in great shape. Not a particularly hard grader either. Beware, Klein may bore those non politics majors, though.

I went into the final with a B, and came out with a D+. When I went to see him about the final, he just said that there was nothing right, when I know that my I had correct answers. I loved going to class, and would have taken another class - not now. If you agree with him and can defend that position, you should be fine. Otherwise, you're screwed.

Good one on one.  Lectures can be boring sometimes but the material is very interesting.  He is good at attacking opinions/articles if you listen to him.  Can be critical in his comments on your ideas.  Not an easy class and not for everyone but worth it if you are interested in the judiciary.
The material itself is interesting but he is not a dynamic lecturer.  He is helpful one on one though.  The tests are tricky.
He's great.  Very helpful, go to office hours.  Great TA's.  Hard tests because they are nuanced, but just a nice guy, knows his stuff, and a great resource.
depends on the class.  he tries, don't hold it against him. make sure its not statistics
This guy is full of practical insight which is very useful in a class like discrete where many students don't understand the course's foundation relevance in CS

Knight is a bit boring, but if you're interested in the material, every once and a while there will be a fantastic lecture. The class is not hard, just do the assignments on time. The tests are much harder than the class suggests.

Don't take this class unless you have to. Knight clearly is not interested in teaching it. Lectures are agonizingly boring and completely unrelated to what is covered on tests. Homework is a little better, but still doesn't give a very clear picture of what exams will be like. Knight was definitely more helpful outside of class, though.
The guy is highly disliked by most students. Comes off as an ass and his "humor" gets really old, really fast. He's also an extremely boring lecturer. That being said, the class is really easy.
Nice guy, sincerely interested in the subject matter. The lectures can be a bit dry, but he definitely knows his stuff. Also full of that dry British wit.

Fair amount of work, not impossible but requires some thought and some time. I learned a lot! Definitely attend lectures, review the slides, do the homework, and use the Brooks surgical method for the group project.

My advise is to follow the Brook's surgical method to programming in groups:  Find the best coder in your group and let him/her take the lead with coding and have the second-best coder help out.  Have the other two people work on the documents and website.  Trust me, my team won the Robot Games and all of my group members did fine in the class.

Can someone make a class harder? His CS340 is ridiculously time consuming and he doesn't help people at all. He just loves criticizing but that's it. If you are not a CS major, stay away from CS340 with Prof. Knight.
Knight is deffinitelly a character. Lectures are frightfully boring and he will tear you apart if you don't follow directions in lab.
Extremely boring lectures. Bluntly insults ppl sometimes.

I think Professor Knight wants to come across as mean or British or something, but he wasnt bad. His slides and lectures are very well done, but often times boring. He did a good job of teaching important material, and a decent job evaluating us. Takes some work, but should be an A class.
Relatively good professor for the CS Dept. but he tries to be a hard a$$.  He's decent.
No Comments
He lectures but the lectures are easy to follow and understand.
Tim's humor kept a dry subject interesting and he sure looks good in a tight pair of khakis!
He has a lottttttttttt of patience, probably too much, even with rude students, and teaches verrrry slowly so that everyone understands.  Couldn't ask for a better professor.
No Comments

This class is so chill. The discussions once a week are just so you can sit back and watch a movie, which you'll spend the next couple lectures going over and re-watching clips from. Prof. Korte is clearly passionate about film and is adorable in an old-person kind of way. Only 2 exams throughout the whole year, and definitely doable.

Very animated and interesting for such an old guy. Definitely knows his stuff and is able to present it clearly. Don't expect a film anthology - the class focuses on just a handful of directors (Welles, Hitchcock, Kubrick, Scorsese), but they are spread over a variety of techniques. Loved this class even as a science major.

Great class, shows the films that are the "classics" for those who study or love film (not movies). Very clear in what he wants the student to walk away from the class knowing. Visit office hours to chat him up/ask questions. Awesome one on one. DO attend class...info for exams is all presented there and DO see all the films, clips, etc GREAT CLASS

I honestly didn't like the class.  Yes it was relatively easy but I don't feel like I learned anything.  The class is Cinema as an Art Form yet well over half of the films are by Martin Scorsesse which doesn't give you a good overview of an art form in my opinion.  Lectures are boring and get very very repetitive.

Not my area of study but Walter really grabbed my interest in the class. Easily my favorite teacher at UVa. Medium difficulty first test then two essay exams that unless you are a moron AND don't go to any classes you will get a B or above.

This was a great class! It was very interesting and not hard at all. You have a multiole choice text test which you must do the reading for. Luckily this test doesnt count for too much ( got a D but still got an A- for the class). There is also two essay tests (2 essays/ test) which are graded pretty easily. The TA's and the professor are also grea

Having taken two separate classes with Korte, I can say the the vast majority of the films he selects are awful.  What they also have in common are overtly sexual themes and undertones.  It's like watching bad**** without the freedom to ****.  You can score an easy "A," but you won't learn anything useful.

AMAZING CLASS!! Korte is SO knowledgeable! It may seem easy to skip the lectures, but they are so interesting - and if you pay attention you are guaranteed a good grade in the class. Plus, the movies are awesome as well. If you do the readings and go to lecture you will come out with an A ... and be a movie buff!

Very interesting and knowledgeable professor. Gives a few non mandatory lectures per week, along with 1 required movie screening. Only two grades in the entire class, a midterm and a final. Good class if you like movies and care enough to figure out exactly what the graders are looking for.

TAKE THIS CLASS! It is really interesting, especially if you like movies. Porf. Korte really knows his stuff and makes the class really interesting. If you go to class and do the readings you are bound to get a really good grade.

This class was very interesting and the movies were great.  The textbook is pretty much useless except on the multiple choice exam.  The essays are much easier if you think of topics beforehand and outline the scenes so you have some idea of what to write on.

Prof Korte is a very knowledgeable about the movies, but he never sees a singlemidterm anf final ( and those are the only grades you receive) The class is easy if you keep up with going to class and reading... then you can write up a storm and adhere to their formula...He spells things out SEVERAL times in a lecture period... seems like a cool guy.

OK, easy class, but so much fun and very interesting...I actually took away a lot info that makes me look at movies differently....see him during office hours to chat...very helpful to organize all the info that he presents....

Maybe I'm artistically retarded, but I don't like the way this guy teaches. Exams are essay tests where you have to write about things that he's never mentioned in class and have nothing to do with movies. On the first exam, he asked us to relate cinematic devices to feminism. Turn on director commentary on DVDs if you want to learn about movies :(

Amazing lecturer who spells out most of his points. He knows his movies and shares many interesting views on the films watched in class. We focused on Scorsese, which was a cinematic wet-dream as his passion was incredible. You WILL look at movies in a different light after the class and will finally realize how crappy movies like The Notebook are.

my attendance rate was around 10%... and i still got a B+. nearly everything this man says is redundant. the reading is unneccesary. his more ambitious points are clouded by his inability to speak. one cool thing -- he has alright movie taste, and the free screenings make for good dates.

This was my most enjoyable class of the semester. We watched citizen kane, psycho, the usual suspects and 7 other great movies - one unit on Orson Welles/Alfred Hitchcock and one on film noir. Only two tests - a midterm and a final. Lectures are easy to sit through and the class is about movies!

Korte may be a dry lecturer but he loves movies and his tests are not bad. Hint: Prepare ahead of time your scenes & listen because he might hint similar TQ's.  If you love movies you will probably enjoy this class. More reading than I expected but Korte is cool!

Knows what he's talking about, says "Uh, um, err..." when he's trying to think up a word, which is very entertaining. Go to the weekend movie reviews!!!  Reading only necessary before taking midterm, for cinematographic terms.

Prof. Korte isn't the best lecturer at the University, but the material is certainly interesting and he has a definite love of film.  Easy course if you prepare for the tests and come to class.  I wouldn't recommend this to someone not already interested in film, but I loved it!

could he be any uh uh uh um ummmm ummm more ughhhhhhh...boring!  Be more boring!  if you ummmm uhhhhuuuuuhhhh uhhhhhhh, think that, that this entry is uhhhhhhhh, ummmm, hard to, hard to read, then, you may no ummmm, uhhh, want to, want to take...this class because uh, this is exactly how he lectures
Korte's lectures are circuitous but he eventually gets to the point. Study the glossary for the objective because it's incredibly hard, but the essays are easy.
korte's lectures are for the most part engaging and the reading for the class is very managable. the objective test is fairly hard but the essay-format tests are much easier.

I have taken several Korte classes over the years, and if you are interested in film, then you will find his courses both interesting and engaging. He is extremely animated in his smaller classes and definitely knows his stuff. Definitely one of the few g
I enjoyed this class very much, but beware, the lectures are quite boring, but Korte knows his stuff and the movies are fantastic.

Korte looks like Hitchcock.  He does tend to blather on and on, but the movies are interesting and if you just reguritate what he's said, and try to apply it a little to specific scenes within the movie, you'll ace the class.

I would not recommend this class.  I find him an unneccesarily verbose prof who loves the sound of his own voice. In, my opinion the subject matter is fairly interesting, but the presentation is pitiful and not worth the difficult midterm.
1 very hard multiple choice test & 2 easy essay tests, watch movies/great lectur
Very effort and participation-based. Professors super friendly and makes class engaging. Work loads pretty light

I learned so much with Mme. Krueger. The content was particularly engaging and distinctive -- I probably wouldn't have learned what I did with another professor. The writing could be challenging but she gave great corrections that paid off with the final paper. She clearly cares about her students, and she's incredibly intelligent.

Cheryl is by far the reason I decided to major in French. She not only is very passionate about her topics, but is genuinely a caring person. She makes herself very available outside of class and gives specific comments and provides areas for improvement on assignments. I have taken four classes with her now and am still amazed at her dedication
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kind and reasonable. I was never afraid to ask questions, but her lack of organization had me worried all semester. She relies on Collab (which is prone to crashing) a lot, so be sure to save your documents. I definitely learned a lot in this course - in writing and speaking - and enjoyed the positive, interactive atmosphere.

This course is well worthwhile. Preparation is a must because we discuss films in class you need to have seen prior; however, all of the films are interesting to watch. There are not too many text readings, and the professor is amazing! She is also available during office hours and willing to help you. This course is amazing... just take it. :)

The class is the history of French Cinema. I meak what could possibly be better then watching French movies for a class? Well, not only that but also discussing them in class. In terms of the workload this class is very light, and you learn so much! Definitelly worth taking!

Prof Krushkal is a kind guy. He is hard to understand at times though and sometimes feels like he is talking through what is in his mind as he lectures instead of teaching a group of college students. 2310 is conquerable, just do the weekly WebAssigns and hw, go to discussion, and step up on the 1 midterm and 1 final. Best of luck!

The only problem I have with him is that he is at least 3 minutes late to each lecture, which comes off as disrespectful. That being said, his lectures clearly explain the material and in-class examples reinforce it well. The grade came from weekly homework, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. The TA who ran the discussion section was entirely unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very, very good professor. Professor Krushkal always answers emails in a timely fashion. He clearly loves math and knows it very, very well. Goes the extra mile if you need any extra help. Highly recommended.
Very helpful in office hours and shows a genuine interest in students' success. He also always has a smirk on his face which makes for interesting classes.
Good math teacher. Go to class, do the homework, and ask questions if you don't understand something, and there's no reason you shouldn't get an A.

this guy's so smart you'll practically feel the brain waves emanating from him.. and he has a funny little grin that makes it seem like he always has an inside joke with the chalkboard... slava's awesome
one of the nicest profesors in the math department, aside from being a little shy he's an excellent teacher and its very clear that he wants to be as helpful as possible
He rocks.
Extremely nice professor.  His Russian accent is soothing somehow.  Took extra time to hold extremely helpful office hours, even answered questions in email in timely manner.  Great guy.
Besides his persistant coughing and clearing of throat, he's a great teacher.
He goes slowly and reviews alot. If you do the homework, and had a decent AB/I teacher you will be fine.
Very disorganized and unhelpful.  It is clear he does not care about teaching.

I had Marianne for the Art of Collaboration engagement, and the class was so fun and chill. We did 5 assignments max, and she gave the whole class A's. She is easy to talk to, fun, and makes the classes engaging and super interesting. Would definitely recommend to anyone who likes to move around during class and is looking for a chill engagement.
Marianne Kubik is an incredible professor who is passionate about the course content.  She goes out of her way to meet with students outside of class.

Marianne is a fantastic teacher, incredibly gifted and a true lover of theatre, and despite her slightly stoic demeanor she is a caring, vivacious person. I was fortunate to take multiple classes with her and do an independent study, and even when she's crazy busy she is a great resource. I cannot imagine the UVa Drama functioning without her.

Marianne is a kind person who is an expert in her field.  She is rarely negative in critiquing a student's work and offers great lifelong advice to every actor.  So long as you put forth your best effort in the class, you will gain a lot.

Marianne is an authority on what she teaches in the country. She genuinely cares about her students' growth and strives to challenge them constantly. She has high standards, which are fitting for such a highly accomplished individual.

My advice would be to read the textbook, but use the slides he gives in lecture to pick and choose what information you can expect to see on exams. Learn the diagrams and be able to explain functionality. Kopeny is a really sweet professor who wants you to learn, so definitely seek him out for office hours. I might just take 3420 to have him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The lecture and exams on lecture material in this class aren't too bad. Lectures can make material seem worse than it actually is, just read the book. But the lab for the class is certifiably awful. It counts for 40% of the grade and is just a 3 hours long cram session where your TA will just sit back and watch. By far the worst lab I've ever taken

If you're taking this class, be prepared for terrible/hard to understand lectures. Also, be ready to make your textbook your Bible because you have to know every little detail about every page of that book; the tests are very specific. I was disappointed in this course because I was looking forward to the material but it was not delivered well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I seemed to really struggle in Kopeny's class, but many of my friends did well. GET THE TEXTBOOK!! I found labs to be super easy, but I also took anatomy in high school. You really need to spend time studying for the exams because they're application and interpretation based. Office hours are really helpful and he does care to help you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. In lecture he is quite bland, he tries really hard to not read off the slides but then actually just pauses a lot and reads them directly anyway.  I went to every lecture to keep my mind in the subject but I only studied  the book. If you understand what everything on each page means & how they connect, you'll do well on the test.
Kopeny is a really nice, sweet professor. Sure, his lectures aren't the most interesting, but they help clarify textbook stuff. Also, the textbook is your best friend in this class.

Professor Kopeny seemed boring at first, but it turned out to be one of my favorite classes! Go to office hours cause he kind of pokes at what's going to be on the exams, also it's really helpful in general. If you take lab, then it'll parallel with the lecture material. Don't judge a book by its cover - trust me, this is better than 2010.

Though he isn't the most interesting person, he is there for you if you have questions. The labs that you participate in are actually more fun that BIOL 2030. It's a good class, not a burden. I learned a lot.

I fell asleep mostly every day in this class. You don't really have to show up, all you have to do is read the textbook. The lectures do help though. It also helps to go to office hours and ask questions.

The other reviews of Kopeny are pretty harsh.  He's a very nice guy who really does want you to understand the material.  His lectures and exams are straight from the book so if you read attending lecture is not always essential and vice versa.  He also provides practice exams before each test which are very helpful for assessing your preparedness.

The other reviews of Kopeny are way to harsh. He's a really nice guy and will definitely take the time to answer any questions you have if you go to his office hours. He does reads off the slides in his lecture but tries to make them interesting. He also definitely puts a lot of time into his slides which are really helpful for studying.
He's a terrible lecturer: speaks slowly, repeats mostly what's on the slides, and not engaging at all. Nice guy though. Tests are mostly based on textbook materials, so reading the text is mandatory.
Terrible teacher.  butchers the material.  leave class with less understanding than came in with

Although he may have a grasp on the material himself, he is in no way capable of explaining it to a class of 300 + students. Doesn't put time into  lectures that would promote a greater understanding of in-depth knowledge. Instead, essentially reads from a powerpoint without connecting important ideas or drawing important general conclusions

Kopeny is irrelevant, boring, and terrible at communicating information.  His lab lecture is nigh useless, with him frequently pausing and turning his back to his students in order to figure out whether he forgot to read anything off the powerpoint.  If it weren't for the scale I would've given Kopeny a 0 for usefulness.

A lab should be focused on improving microscopy and guided exploration skills while developing a further passion for the field of science. This lab course does neither of these as the investigations are random, unorganized, and filled with meaningless knowledge. Unhelpful and not a good course to further develop biological understanding

Terrible class and terrible teacher. To anyone with a passion for learning or a desire to pursue the sciences, I recommend finding a way out of this lab course. The work done in the lab is irrelevant to the "tests" given, the material is unorganized and poorly taught. Spent more time reorganizing his lectures than learning

Had him for lecture, then lab. Lecture was dry, teaches straight out of the book. Taking lab now; he makes you buy an expensive lab manual (THAT YOU DO NOT USE) then makes you print out the worksheets you turn in (again, the MANDATORY LAB MANUAL you BUY you do NOT USE. Instead, you have to print out the stuff you turn in.)

At first glance, Kopeny is boring because he is monotone  during his lectures. However, if you get to know him, he's genuinely nice. His tests are fair & his slides are pretty comprehensive in terms of what to get out of the textbook readings. Clickers are required but he stops using them eventually. Gives out readings, most are optional though.

For BIOL 340, lab quizzes are worth the most of your grade so it's important you do well on them (however, questions can be difficult and really specific). Labs are fun; Kopeny even brought his hawk in! Lectures are often hard to follow. Dr. Kopeny is very enthusiastic when he speaks and is willing to help if you need it. Received a B-.

Lectures? Pointless and BORING. Pre-lab reading? Somewhat pointless. Focus on the random facts the TAs toss at you during lab and you'll pass the quizzes. As for the professor himself.. he's really pushy in emails and at times even rude. Definitely not the nicest person.

Although Kopeny really cares about the success of his students and his exams are mostly about memorization, his lectures are very unclear. He tends to repeat himself when saying something, and then saying something that was opposite of his original statement. I had a hard time in this class this summer because of his uncertainty about what he said.

I enjoyed BIOL 204 much more than BIOL 203. At pre-lab lecture, Kopeny provides you w/a lot of useful information that you need for that week's lab. Lab quizzes are difficult but completion of the worksheets are valued the same. TA I had was Kilkenny. Received a B+ in the class.

Same as with the lecture portion of the class, but even more pointless.  Puts way too much weight on the pre-lab quizzes (of which you're at the mercy of the TAs) which don't really measure your preparedness.  Cram before each lab session and hope you get quizzed on the random facts you happen to memorize, because that's this class in a nutshell.

Wow.  One of the worst lecturers I've had at UVA (even for a 500 person lecture like intro bio).  Seemingly incapable of maintaining a constant stream of thought, lectures are pointless except for the extra credit clicker questions.  Show up for that, do sudoku/crossword/watch DVDs in the meantime, study the day before each exam and still get a A.

I'd try to say something more uplifting, but I really can't. Lectures are basically what's said in the text, just less clear, and exams are more incomprehensible than the lectures. Perhaps the one upside is that you're forced to suffer through the material here, which you'll have to do for the MCAT anyway. Overall a step down from 201.

Ugh.  I'm sorry if you have to take this class as a requirement.  I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who doesn't have to take it.  He makes you learn so much on your own that it is basically two classes worth of material in one semester.
Overall, a very intelligent professor who could not teach.  He leaves most of the material up to you, is unorganized, and the tests are extremely hard with nit-picky details.

"I don't have to teach this, you'll have to read about it on your own" is the phrase I've heard most this semester. He usually posts about 35 slides per day and gets through, oh, about 20. All in all, unorganized, unhelpful and quite the boring lecturer. If the subject matter wasn't so easy it would be an unbearable course.

BIOL 203 overally covers the evolution of organisms. The materials are boring compared to BIOL 201, and too many boring memorization. And his tests include considerate deep synthesis questions a lot. His tests are about 50-57 questions whici is painful. His lecture with slides were not organized at all.

The subject matter really isn't that hard. He just asks very tricky questions. Test averages are in the mid 70's. He rambles in class about unimportant things. He picks the most random things to put on the test, too. If you did well in BIO 201, don't think you'll do well here. He's a completely different teacher. Watch out.
different teaching style from Kittlesen. If you did well in Biol 201, don't take it for granted that you will do well in BIOL 202 also.

Tests are tricky and very detailed. Pay attention to every word he said even if he seems to go through it casually. Read the book in its entirety and pay attention to details, even though he said "I don't really want you to memorize this or that". Memorization is important! TA (Dexter)is helpful. Go ask him if you need help

Adores the sound of his own voice. I went to his office hours 3 days in a row, and he had no recollection of who I was or what we had talked about. Pathetic. Though he is passionate about the subject, he does not care AT ALL about students. If you can bear it, he focuses on lecture material  for exams, so go to class.

Terrible lecturer. Extremely unorganized and uncaring about his students. His powerpoints are impossible to understand during class and are a pain to look at for 20 minutes while he rambles on about some incomprehensable point. Expects you to get everything he says the first time he says it. My least favorite teacher at The University
Lectures were hard to follow and the powerpoint slides did not pinpoint the important material.  IMHO, Kittlesen is the better lecturer.

absolutely horrible. terrible teacher. doesnt know how to teach so he just rambles on and on. should just use the book but he feels like he is too good for it. only half the class goes to lecture because he confuses more than helps.
He speaks too fast during lectures, his slides are not very organized. listen carefully to what he says in class for the exam. overall: average teacher
Very good teacher! Very thorough, which was fantastic, and nicely energetic! A pleasure to go to lectures even though I'm not so keen on the material!
Dr. Kopeny was awesome! He was my advisor and he was so passionate about his subject and was just a pleasant person to be around.

This guy loves the sound of his own voice.  this class was so easy, but I hated waking up for an 8 am lab lecture.  I hated even more having to listen to him.  His lectures are disorganized and he lectures poorly.

1 word - BORING. he can NEVER stop talking and often overruns...only able to go through half his powerpoint slides everytime due to his longwinded-ness. very unclear and you can see a good number of people arriving 5 minutes before class ends everytime just for the clicker question. tests are not as hard as 201. the book'll be your best friend.

This guy needs to reevaluate his whole life.  His lectures are way too detailed and boring, 3/4 of the class is asleep or on their laptops.  I got an A in this class but i'm still bitter that he wasted my thursday mornings for nothing.Checks attendence with iclicker so u have to go for 5% of grade.  He messed up the grades last semester.

He is a great guy and wants to help his students a lot. His tests are midline difficulty. Tends to be repetitive in his lectures, and can be borning. He TAKES ATTENDANCE with iclickers. Very detailed and helpful powerpoint slides.
Nice guy but not a good lecturer. He tends to ramble and lectures are very scattered. Often late to class.

i LOVE Dr. Kopeny.  One of the few professors i've met who actually care about how the student is doing in the class and is ALWAYS willing to offer help in any way whatsoever....Go to office hours.   Exams are ok if you prepare accordingly!!
kinda scattered
Not the greatest speaker in the world...I usually fell asleep in lecture. Tests were not too bad if you studied well enough. He seemed really nice, but I found the content of his class boring.
Know his power point slides front to back, even the small details-this is where he gets most of his test questions.
random lecturer, extremely unclear

I took vertebrates with Dr. K and he's amazingly cool- the man has a hawk!  That class was great and I learned so much during that semester.  For intro bio lab, he did his best to make the class fair for everyone, and as long as you did your work and studied the slides, the test ought to have been easy. Bottom line- Dr. K is cool!
this man doesn't teach. he simply reads badly written slides. have fun
going to lecture is pointless because he reads directly from the slides and then posts them on toolkit afterwards.  just read the chapters and look over the slides and the tests are easy

Kopeny needs to learn how to teach intro bio from Kittleson.  Slides are incredibly wordy, and exams have very poorly worded test questions.  Class isn't hard, just frustrating because the lectures are so boring.

Kopeny is a teacher with a tremendous sense of passion for the study of LIFE!  Take good notes during lectures, read the book....and attend on a regular basis.  Random attendance checks are a guarantee.....

never have i felt so defeated after taking a test-- the tests didn't test lecture knowledge, there were obscure and ridiculous questions. i hated this class with a passion. kopeny needs to take it down a notch on the caffeine, then maybe his lectures would be more coherent.
ridiculous tests. wordy slides. have to read the book to even think about getting above a 50 on the exam.

Frankly, avoiding this class is worth forgoing a career in medicine.  okay maybe it wasn't that bad, but it was horrifically boring and the tests were completely ridiculous.  he tested obscure, useless knowledge.  don't bother going to lecture, just go to review once or twice and read the slides.
Just reads his slides so the lecture isnt worth attending.  Also terrible at responding to e-mail.  Accused an entire class of 400 of cheating and wont appologize.

he's an alright guy, really shows he's into the material. however his lectures are boring, i soon decided to never pay attention because all he does is read off of the slides and nothing more. tests are alright, the difficulty comes from your competetive students, not the test. curves to a high B-

Very bad at lecturing, reads off his overwhelmingly wordy slides (which he desperately need to proofread), very anal exams (I could care less what specific arms on a squid are called; they're all tentacles to me)
Good guy, but as for his biology expertice............

CANNOT give a lecture worth attending. Reads off his 500 word slides, which do NOT help. Uses lots of pictures from the book. Exams are badly worded, making them very tricky, and they need revision (too many typos). TA is much better.. Did well in 201 but struggling in 202, even tho I study more...

The guy needs to take a course in "public speaking" and "Lecturing". He can't give a lecture. He reads of off slides (50 in one .ppt file) full of text while studdering -- that is all, no examples or full explanations of concepts. The tests are full of tricky questions. (Nice guy in person tho)

nice guy, hard class.  His lectures are hard to follow as well... slides are completely full but don't need to know a lot of what's on them.  TA was a better lecturer.  He stutters a lot and doesn't sound like he really prepared, even though he knows the material.
No Comments

not a terribly difficult class, keep up with the readings... hyper little guy, moves around a lot, probably from all the coffee he drinks, which by the way, don't sit in the front row or you'll smell his coffee breath through the whole class... yuck! random attendance checks so beware
Dr. Kopeny is sooo sooo nice and the material he teaches is really interesting, but the course is also very hard!  I reccomend keeping up with the reading if you can, because he goes fast in lecture.
I love Dr. Kopeny! He is the best science teacher I have ever had! And he is soo nice!!!!

I graduated from UVA several years ago and Dr. Kopeny was by far one of the best professors I had in biology. His classes were challenging but your hard work will pay off.  He is very approachable, so if you have questions don't be afraid to talk to him.

very nice dude, attendance wasn't mandatory and he always made it very clear what would be on the test and what you needed to study. also pretty interesting if you pay attention. never added stress to my workload.
Hated his boring lectures.
Fun class. The grading is a lot harder than I expected, but the TAs grade the exams. Schaeffer is a great professor, so I definitely recommend his class to anyone interested in Buddhism or Tibet.

Professor Schaeffer is passionate, helpful and always engaged. His class was fascinating, he is funny, loves to get to know students and is very encouraging to all those to talk to him. Highly recommend.

His class seemed fairly laid-back. Basically he'd tell people to come in with questions about the reading, and then he'd spend the period answering the questions. It made it REALLY obvious if you didn't do the reading, though, and there was a lot of it for every week (200pg).  50% participation, 50% final paper (12 page summary of the book we read)

Class is kind of boring. The reading/film schedule was very disorganized and unclear. Tons of reading. My advice is to always finish the book a week before the film is shown, so that you don't get stuck doing too much at once. A single-spaced response paper for every work and a 12 page final is required. However, he is pretty lenient about grades and as long as you participate and turn in your work you will get a high grade.

EGMT.....You were born a scientist

Awesome professor, she was so knowledgeable and made a kind of dull topic so interesting. The class is overall pretty easy as long as you do the work, and I actually enjoyed the journal entries and they kind of did change my prospective. No final, just a easy group project

You can do well in this class without reading the book but you have to attend class - type your notes because you will not be able to keep up by hand. Lectures are amazing, and Professor Kucenas is always willing to help in office hours. You also learn how to read papers, which is a valuable skill. Good partners for the paper reports will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is amazing! I highly recommend her Developmental Biology class. It was honestly the best biology classes I have taken at UVA. I wish other professors would teach like her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher! Spends lots of time explaining concepts and making sure students understand. Is very excited and interested in the concepts shes teaching. Makes it easy to succeed because she offers a lot of opportunities to have things graded.

Awesome teacher - highly recommend taking a class with Dr. K. She is passionate about biology. I would also recommend taking this before taking the MCAT (if you plan on taking it). This is a pretty reading intensive course, so make sure you keep up with the reading or you're toast. You learn a ton. The last few lectures she let us pick the topics.

A lot of moaners in these comments. So many who did not learn how to study saying 'he's hard' or 'he's unreasonable.' Kuhn has been one of the best profs I had at UVA. Reasonable, approachable, with fair tests. Know your discussion Qs, homeworks, and lectures inside and out. Go to office hours. I got 95+ on every exam. Fair guy who cares A LOT.

Easily the worst professor I have had at UVA concerning anything biology related, which says a lot. Theres no curve for the class, and aside from offering minimal extra resources outside of weekly discussion (useless, btw), hes just downright rude; the rumors that he was a last minute sub-in for an actual biochem professor are probably true.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever seen. Disorganized, clueless, and outright disrespectful to students. Don't recommend this class unless you have a death wish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great Professor & very interesting lectures. This course is not too hard; you just need a decent grasp of the material for the exams. I usually don't like history classes, but the way Professor Kumar taught made it very interesting and easy to learn.
Incredible Professor!  The best Professor ever!  Awesome Professor! You will learn a lot, but need to work hard. Fair grader.
Kumar is awesome! This was my first Sociology course ever and he made everything so easy to understand. Take notes in lecture and you'll be good to go. He's terrific.
One of my favorite professors. Hes really passionate about what he does, and it makes the class more interesting and easy, the accent helps too..i just lvoe listening to him talk
He's a great guy. The class was interesting, the material was ridiculously thick, but he was more than charitable on the grading so the class ended up being highly enjoyable.
I have absolutely no clue what that class was about or what he was saying, but I got an A so I can't complain.  I'm not sure he bothered reading my final paper.

Good professor, hot accent. Also, a very clear presentation of the feild of Sociology as a whole. It will help you decide pretty quickly whether or not to pursue the discipline. Either way, its a good class.

Kumar oozed knowledge of sociology, from the British accent to his very dress.  He was very clear on his lectures, while he was not afraid to point out his expectations about exams.  If you attend lectures and do most of the reading, the exams are not a problem.  The paper seems a little too much.
yo dogg this man has it together you gots ta get up in his class if you want the grade boy.  he assigned reading on my dogg michael jordan so you know he's got it together.
easy class, cool accent
awesome british accent.  Good lectures

Professor Kuhn is really inspirational and let you visualize. Although he is not really strict about proofs, he actually gives you a very good intuition about analysis, which is significant for following studies in math.
Professor Kuhn is very good, he teaches clearly and gives easy tests.

Professor Kuhn is kind of hard to understand at times and seems to ramble, but he does know what he's talking about.  Homework takes about 5-6 pages and is due every week, I usually split it between Sunday and Monday night and am fine.  Test are harder than the homework, so be ready for that, homework and tests are both graded fairly.

Professor Kuhn is not very clear, often confusing. The workload is huge. 9-10 pages of homework each week, graded on accuracy. The grader is also very tough. On top of that, there are projects, 1 each 2-3 weeks. They take a while too. If I were to go back, I would still take calc 3 but with a different professor.
Do not take a class with Professor Lawless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took one class with Prof. Lawless's which was a disaster. She was combative, condescending, and dismissive to students and her co-professor. Exams emphasized irrelevant trivia over substance, and the poorly designed final project was harshly graded without feedback. Avoid poorly taught, and frustrating courses with Lawless—not worth your time.

Lawless is extremely unapproachable and judgemental towards students, she frequently acts defensive in class and through email and is not receptive to critique and questions. There is very little room for dialogue with her, creating a discouraging classroom environment. Quizzes and exams are very picky and are excessively difficult to study for.

Do not take this class. Lawless is extremely knowledgeable in her field, but is a terrible teacher. She is intentionally trying to trip you up. The exams ask you about THE MOST SPECIFIC stuff that they said as an afterthought during lectures. Readings dense & lengthy. Lawless strict & thinks she knows everything. Learned a lot but not worth my time

Professor Lawless is the best professor I have ever had at UVA and I loved this class.  The quizzes were very detailed but open-note/unlimited time, so not too hard. Every lecture was very engaging and I loved the guest speakers.  Professor Lawless always made time to meet outside of class to go over questions and she was always very kind/helpful

Avoid taking a class with Professor Lawless if you can. She's rude, unapproachable, and lacks any semblance of warmth or understanding toward her students. Her multiple-choice questions are infuriatingly subjective and designed to trip you up. Overall, she's not nice, and the learning environment she creates is discouraging at best.

Worst professor I've ever had. Always speaks of how she ran for Congress and lost, to the point where she added a question on our closed-note midterm asking which state she ran for Congress in. Brings in amazing guest speakers then asks other useless test questions such as whether they studied abroad or not. Would not recommend.

Professor Lawless is knowledgeable about politics but weaponizes her knowledge. She acts like she knows everything and expects that everyone in her class is a political junkie as well. I never write reviews but honestly, her classes are insufferable. The tests consist of the most specific details in the whole world. I DO NOT RECOMMEND.

Lawless is indicative of the larger problem with the politics department at UVA and its divestment from legal-centric courses. Tests are needlessly specific and material is unfocused, centering around her expensive book that reads at an 8th grade level and extended anecdotes. Not surprising that she was unsuccessful in her Congressional bid.

She expects you to remember every graph and picture she has shown in class as well as every anecdote and will test you one it a month and half later. She has quizzes almost every class as well as outside participation but it is the tests that are the worst. She is a great lecturer but her tests are brutal and so specific that its ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I just finished my last class of my college career with Lana and felt moved to post this. This is the second class I've taken with her. I would have taken more if I could. Her classes are so interesting a relevant. She is genuinely an inspirational woman who makes you look at the world in a new way, and she cares about students.

I've taken 2 classes with her and she is the best professor I've had at UVA. She's the reason I majored in media studies. The people claiming 2000 was too hard or that she's mean probably shouldn't be going to UVA in the first place. 2000 was truly NOT a difficult class AT ALL and it was definitely the most interesting lower level class I've taken.

Extremely condescending. Allowing10 mins to do 12 select all that apply questions is not appropriate for an intro class. When criticisms were presented, rather than listening, she blamed us insinuating we didn't read the textbook. Pretends to be relatable but is does not treat her students with respect and as equals to her.Horrible, don't take her.

She is not respectful or kind. I'm taking her class right now and she can't take constructive feedback and will weaponize your grade against you as a response. Her teaching method is basically using the textbook as a prop during class and provides no new content so it's not even worth going to lecture.
She is awful, do not take her
The material is not appropriate for an intro to media studies class, it's grad school level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Swartz is really a great professor. Her lectures are always interesting and relevant. Oh, and she's super funny! She makes discussion really fun. I definitely recommend her!
Lana is amazing. I don't look at payment systems or any social media in the same way. She is really entertaining, like little young white Oprah. She's super fashionable and cute, which is fun.

As an Environmental Science major, I had to take this course. While the subject is interesting, the teaching made it frustrating. Lectures aren't mandatory, but there are pop quizzes. Exams are take-home, easy, but poorly aligned with lectures, and the professor was often rude and dismissive during office hours, which made learning discouraging.

Do not take this class if you think it will be easy. Yes there is no final and there are only 6 tests which are take home but they are very tricky. The material isnt hard but the tests questions are confusing and will have questions about the color of his favorite bird. (Im serious) Even if you know the bird and color you may still get it wrong.

He is very disorganized and tests on very specific topics from lecture. Often used pop quizzes to curb low attendance to class. Only reason students took the class was the fact the grade was made up of six take-home exams. Overall, I do not suggest this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lerdau is a lovely, entertaining, and goofy person. His class is less great. He is disorganized, and grades only on tests. His tests are confusing, but you eventually get the hang of his wording and it gets easier. Take notes on the slides ahead of time because he flies through them in lecture. Don't take this if you are looking for an easy class.

The class is easy (I took EVSC 1010), but the one thing that you should know is he is quite literally the MOST disorganized man. He would mess up the quiz scoring banks, send out the most broken announcements that left everyone confused, and would NEVER respond to an email that you sent out. He's like an emotionally unavailable boyfriend.

I didn't find Professor Lerdau's lectures particularly engaging or informative--I was often confused about which information was necessary and which was supplemental, making it difficult to take effective notes, and his visual aids did not help much. However, he seems like a nice guy who is clearly passionate and knowledgeable in his field.

Honestly the most boring lectures about topics that do not have to be that boring. He admits to trying to trick you on the quizzes and your entire grade is made up of a midterm and a final. He is not helpful during office hours either. At best, he makes jokes sometimes but generally does not try and help his students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take the class. Don't do it. I also read reviews and didn't think it would be THAT bad--but it was. The ENTIRE course was based on 2 exams; exams that weren't based on the course material that we discussed...just random facts. Unfortunately, there's not other great intro cons ecology class, but whatever you do, dont take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good professor, there are very difficult tests, boring lectures. Helps to read the textbook.
I think this guy is actually a pretty good professor and lecturer. He makes the topic interesting and easy to learn, but the tests can be tricky.

This professor was one of the worst I've had at UVa. He is a very non-engaging professor and expects you to memorize his powerpoints for the exams. His exams are nothing you've seen before and he is a very tough grader. There were only two grades for the semester (2 exams). He is also very snarky and unhelpful in office hours. Avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There isn't a textbook, so he expects you to rely entirely upon his lectures. There were only 2 grades (a midterm and a final). Very unorganized and unclear lecturer. Doesn't write test questions that gauge students' understanding. For the most part they are either trick questions or extremely obscure. Readings are arbitrary.

Awful professor. Extremely disorganized. Readings unnecessary. You must be in class because the powerpoints are not helpful at all; take notes on what he says. Cheerful guy, but he is not fit for teaching, nor writing tests. He is delusional in his expectations; it took a month to get midterms back because they were free response and he has 0 TAs.

Very unclear, ramble-y lecture style. Minimalistic slides do not aid comprehension. Snarky and unhelpful during office hours. Would avoid class with Lerdau if possible. Nice guy but terribly boring and unorganized professor.

Professor Lerdau is an extremely unclear lecturer. He thinks that you come to the class already with a good understanding of difficult topics when in reality, most people have not taken an EnviSci class since high school. Consequently, he explains things rather poorly. He is also a tough grader, you essentially need to memorize his lectures.

He loves what he does which makes it worth taking. Not all that easy. But most of the tests are short response. He is lenient when grading them and if you understand anything about what you are saying he'll give you a good grade.

Professor Lerdau makes an easy class difficult.  His exams either consisted of memorizing every detail off of his lecture slides or "what if" type questions that did not correlate to what he lectured in class.  On our final test he wrote questions that he later admitted were unclear and poorly written.  Avoid taking Lerdau if possible.

The material that he is teaching is not all that difficult to grasp, but his method of teaching is more complicated than it should be. He focuses a lot on the specific equations that define the concepts, which turn out not to be very important. Also, he has not told us our grade on either of the first two tests and its been at least two months.
Lectures are essential to understanding context. The rest of the semester will be focused around group presentations. I highly recommend taking this class. Lecture is fun and engaging.

Prof. Schoppa encourages class participation, but when the wrong take or interpretation of a text is taken, direct feedback is given in front of the class. It would be helpful if the class EGMT 1520 accepted multiple perspectives  on required readings rather than a single correct answer. This is something that is reflected in grading as well.

He's got to be the most frustrating and shallow-minded professor I've ever come across. He asks you to critically think and make up a hypothesis, then shuts it down because when he's the one who isn't understanding the ideas you come up with. He's nitpicky in the worst way, like he's purposely trying to make his class relevant enough to care.

Professor Schoppa clearly loves teaching and I think he gets the material across quite well. There seems to be a bit of a disconnect between who he actually is and what his grading says. His essay rubrics are weirdly specific about certain things and he can be a stickler for minor errors. Overall a good professor

Schoppa is incredibly condescending and passive aggressive when responding to assignments, in emails, and even in class discussions. He takes points off for interpretation that he didn't get and doesn't allow for credit back or explain why an answer is wrong. He also words questions incorrectly from what he wants you to actually answer. Terrible.

I understand that this was Prof. Schoppa's first semester of teaching online, however, if this class is the same format next semester, I do not recommend that you take it. Your grade depends on the TA . The grade structure is 30% midterm, 20% discussion, 50% final. The exams require that you do ALL of the readings. ALL OF THEM. Asian historydull.

Professor Schoppa's PLIR 2030 course was very intriguing. It inspired me to pursue a career in foreign affairs, and I know have a great background in east asian politics. The midterm was a lot to study for, but only was 5 IDs and an essay. Your TA decides your fate - make sure you don't have daily reading quizzes. Go to office hours! Inside scoop
Interesting intro class, he is a very funny guy you can relate to.  Make sure to do the reading for the essay-style exam.

Currently in Comparative politics with Schoppa and I love it. I knew nothing about the subject when I started but I've learned a LOT. His lectures are interesting and very clear cut. Definitely attend class b/c his online notes are choppy. Don't buy w/the textbook, you'll never use it. DEFINITELY BY THE ARTICLE PACKET you'll need it for everything!

The class itself is alright. There are days where it can be very boring though. The required readings were the longest, driest readings I have ever attempted and I quickly lost interest on them all. Good guy, but could make the class more enjoyable.

This professor is absolutely the worst I have ever had. I took his class on semester at sea. Even though it was a mandatory class for all participants (even those who had no prior knowledge in political science), the exams covered upper level material. 100/300 people failed and he unfairly curved the failing half because he "couldnt fail 100 people

There's lot of reading, but this is a pretty good class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but try to keep up with the readings. JOIN STUDY GROUPS: they will save you when it comes to the midterm and the paper. Intensity of the class really depends on the TA. Some are MUCH more intense/hard than others, but you learn more.

Such a nice and happy man! His first few lectures were very captivating, but the difficulty and sheer volume of the reading really brought down my enthusiasm. I would not recommend this course for first years who have never taken a politics or international relations course. TAs make you or break you.

If you are interested by any means in east asian international affairs then this is a great class to take.  There is a lot of reading but Schoppa does a good job in conveying course material and is a good lecturer.  I knew quite a bit before coming into the class but I learned so much more.  I really enjoyed the class.

i've never seen a happier man. expects students to participate (i took a class w/ about 20 some people). he's very helpful and interested in your success in his class. assignments were not difficult for a grad level class. big assignment is a paper which you have the whole semester to do--the final was take home.
Grades seem very arbitrary - picked out of a hat almost.

I liked how to tried to present a balanced view. He is a liberal/constructivist, but at least he makes an honest *attempt* to be fair to the realist views in his lectures and gives them merits as well.
Lots and lots of reading for a 200 level class but depends entirely on your TA. Powerpoint slides are pretty important and lectures are pretty clear.

Very interesting course material, but lots of variation in lectures.  UK, France and Brazil sections are great, but China and Japan (especially Japan) get pretty boring, mostly because Schoppa is a Japan specialist and dives into minutae.  All in all, however, a very worthwhile course.

DO NOT take this class, especially if you have no background. Taught like a 400 level, readings are too hard, monotone, boring lectures, exams are too hard for material concepts. TA's are good. This class will lower your GPA b/c grading is Tough.

I really liked this class. Yes, it's a 101, so a lot of material is covered, but he does a good job of blending theory and information. His style of lecture can be a little awkward. At least he's clear, and the material is awesome.

Schoppa is very monotone and sometimes i get lost in his words because he doesnt seem to be excited about his subject matter.  He is very lively but I wouldnt recommend taking this course if you dont have an undying love for politics.

Schoppa does a great job of making the class interesting and delves deep into the countries we discuss.  The only problem is that the tests are not graded loosely at ALL like one would think a 100 level course would, and there is not grade adjustment at the end, making one wonder WHY?????

It's a 101. The material is basic, dense, and somewhat topical. Weekly readings for section are more interesting. Schoppa does his best wiht this intro course. 15 pg paper wipes out 2nd writing req. pretty easily. Exam/paper/grading isn't bad if you know your TA, he/she is grading you, duh.

What should have been an interesting lecture comparing government and institutions was turned into a complete disaster. The tests are too hard for a 101 level course. The midterm average was below 80 and there is no grade adjustment.

the teacher is not very lively but knows his subject. it's a very intersting class if you love international politics. the exams are not so bad and TAs (at least shebnem ) are always available. by the way, there is a 15pages minimum term paper.
The material was really interesting, and he did a good job of presenting it clearly. I liked this class a lot! There is a good amount of writing, but nothing you can't handle.
