Taking good notes and paying attention to every detail of any postulate/theory is key to doing well.

Merricks is a fantastic professor. He takes a difficult subject like religion and clearly applies logical arguments to the topic. The readings are not necessary, as he explains everything in lecture. Also, his study guides are key, and cover exactly what will be on the examinations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His personal religious views really come out during class. Did not feel respected as an atheist. Awful professor.

This was the BEST class I've ever taken and Professor Merricks is an absolute genius! He goes through the material very quickly  but if you take good notes, study in groups, and go to every lecture, you'll do well in the class. My mind was blown every single lecture: take Philosophy of Religion if it's the only thing you do at UVa.
Merricks is a fantastic professor. He takes a lecture on what many students might consider boring and difficult to understand and makes it interesting and very clear. Also gives a massive curve

My favorite professor at UVA. Funny, engaging, and passionate about the subject. Phil 266 is also a great course, and taking it really helps for 331 in my opinion. The material is tough, but he gives you everything you need to do well if you put in the time. By the end, you'll feel accomplished. He was great about helping me clarify my paper too.

I took his class while on Semester at Sea, during the summer of 2012.  Truly challenged me to elevate my perceptions of the world.  Kind of a mind-blowing professor.  Take his class, if you have the chance.  He's one of the good ones.

Best professor I've had at UVA hands down. Teaches an excellent, unbiased course in philosophy. 3 tests based solely on what is covered in lectures, can be difficult if you don't take notes. Take this class, it'll change the way you look at the world.

Philosophy of Religion fundamentally changed my thought process, and Merricks is by far the best professor I  have had at UVA. Merricks is engaging, funny, and thorough.  Tests are tough, but Merricks is fair, just take good notes and you will do great. No papers, just 3 tests. Warning: this is a philosophy class, not a religion course.

Amazing class, everyone should take it. Merricks explains even the most complicated concepts brilliantly and clearly. No textbook, only weekly (if not every other week) readings available on collab. 3 Tests total. You DO NOT need a Philosophy background to do well in this class! Just pay attention and make sure you understand the material.

Great lecturer. Approachable and not socially awkward or intimidating, which is rare for a philosophy professor. also cool finding him cited in stanford encyclopedia of philosophy. Not easy but an A is possible, he doesnt lie about the tests essentially coming from the study questions. Extremely entertaining prof. Kinda hot too.
Best philosophy prof I've had, and I'm a philosophy major.  Fantastic class, even if you don't find metaphysics that interesting.  Fair, tough grader.  Will make you a better philosophy student.

Merricks is an extremely engaging professor--he's often funny and almost always clear and consistently helpful. Tests can be hard but not tricky, just be sure to be very thorough. Highly recommend this class and professor.

Professor Merricks is an awesome lecturer. Very clear, and super helpful if you a further explanation on anything.  No needed philosphy background, tests are challending, but an A is definitely possible - esp. with his helpful study guides.  He does talk fairly quickly, but make sure you take very accurate notes, it'll help alot - GREAT PROFESSOR!!

Merricks is a really dynamic and interesting lecturer. If you go to class, take awesome notes, and do the study questions, you will do well. Not a lot of reading. Definitely reccommend Merricks, even if you're a phil novice.
best philosophy teacher i had, and i'm a philosophy major
Great class for the hardcore philosophy types.
Great class, with an outstanding professor.  Classes are usually small, Socratic method.  Difficult material and hard grader.  Everyone in my class liked him.

Professor Megill is a gift to the world. Took 3802 then 3812, both incredible. As long as you read, he will teach you how to read again independently and in a way that completely alters your worldview. You will learn how to think for the second time if you engage with the coursework and with professor Megill. What a privilege, take advantage of it.

Most intellectually stimulated I've ever been. Professor Megill has the remarkable ability to help his engaged students find their intellectual stride independently of his own. Reached intellectual heights I didn't know were there. Like scrubbing a life's worth of rust from my brain. A complete gift to take, one of the best decisions of my life.

You will never forget taking a class with Allan Megill. He is the most intense person I've ever met. His all-encompassing passion for understanding Nietzsche, Freud Marx, and other vital thinkers of our age is genuine. When I was 18, it was a mind-blowing, scary, dorky thrill to dive into his course. Thank you, Prof Megill, for the opportunity!

In my experience, Megill's class can be transformative if you really dive into it. Brilliant and quirky are understatements, and Megill places an unusual emphasis on precision for what is basically a philosophy class. But you can emerge from the class with (A) an exciting new understanding of some great thinkers, and (B) improved analytical rigor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was one of the most intense, difficult, and rewarding courses I've ever taken. Megill is a brilliant professor, and goes out of his way to help his students understand difficult material. I never wanted to miss a lecture. If you dedicate the time this course deserves, you will work harder and learn more than you ever have.

Megill is a fantastic professor, but his classes present some very difficult material. If you are willing to keep up with the reading and pay close attention in lecture, you will be rewarded with a highly enjoyable semester filled with intellectual expansion.

Not for the faint of heart, his Marx class involves a lot of dense reading.  While it is advertised as needing merely a poly-sci philosophy class, the people who did best in the course had at least a genuine phil101 class.  Also, I found I did better NOT listening to his advice on how to answer his questions.  Oddly, I still recommend the course.
Undoubtedly, one of the most inspiring intellectuals I have ever encountered.
Excellent professor. Can be unclear at times. Don't take this class lightly. Most useful class I've taken at UVA.

Professor Megill is a one in a million type of professor. While he is hard to understand at time, because he is very intelligent (and knows it), he does a great job of putting great thinkers in today's spotlight. For those who think he is too hard, go to his office and he will talk and explain for hours. History majors should take his Marx course
Certified Canadian Genius

Megill is a superb lecturer. I would almost venture to say he is electrifying-one of the best I've had. Make sure to do the readings. They're hard, but Megill's book is helpful to clarify the readings. He's actually pretty nice during office hours. He's intimidating during lecture. Just make sure to spend a lot of time on the term-paper and study.

Megill is a genius. He knows he is a genius. He also knows you are not a genius. He makes this very clear at several points throughout the course. Take it if you're interested in philosophy, but if you're looking for history you have come to the wrong place.

Don't be deceived by the great reading list for this class. The prof. makes or breaks the class, and Megill breaks it. He takes each of the great thinkers you read and fits them into his own box. If you don't see the world as Megill does, you'll find the class dull and frustrating. I got an A, but it's a waste of time. Also, his ego is absurd.

Megill enjoys parading around his great big brain, and it is pretty entertaining overall. BUT BE WARNED:  The kind of abstract thinking necessary for this class is not something we all have. It is tough to get.  Not sure what the previous entry means by the comment, but I am a history major, Dean's List, and got a C in this class.  Damn lucky too.

It's pretty easy to get a B in Megill's class but very difficult to get an A. If you aren't a hist. major, you probably won't have enough time to get an A  in this class because the reading is heavy and dense. However, he's a good lecturer and the subject matter is extremely interesting.

As a first-year I decided to take this class; Prof. Megil is extraordinarily knowledgeable and demanding, so it's intimidating at first.  But he loves what he does and is damn good at it- if you want to challenge yourself and learn something, he's your man.  Despite his authoritative demeanor in class, is actually easy to talk to. Thumbs way up.

Megill is an amazing teacher.  I was a little scared at first to take the class, and it was definitely hard at the begining of the semester.  But he really gives amazing and funny lectures, and by the middle of the semester everything started to fit together. I think it's also important to be geuinely interested in the topic though.

The material is amazing and Megill is smart as hell, but his ego gets in the way of making anything enjoyable.  His grading on the midterm and final is fair, but his expectations for the term paper are unreasonable and are not clearly articulated until after you've turned it in

The coursewill change your life and the material will blow your mind! Lecture range: mediocre to amazing; Megill makes up for off days b/c he's passionate, insanely knowledgeable, and (if you'll put in the effort) he'll do anything to help you along the way! If you thirst for knowledge, TAKE HIM!
No Comments

Professor milkis has given me a new lease of life. I went from drinking skim milk to whole milk within the night. He asked me to his office after class and he took an interest in more than my student life. I've never had such an invested teacher. I only got a D because I deserved it due to the milk shortage in my village but he turned it around.

Milkis is the man. When I was a first year, he invited me to his office hours without skipping a beat, just to talk to him about what I was interested in. Take a class with him if you get the chance, he's really passionate about the presidency and American politics.

This class one was of my favorite at UVA! Milkis is a great professor.  He is passionate about the presidency and really wants his students to learn.  There were a lot of readings but most of them were interesting and there's not much other work in the class.  If you work hard, it can reshape your perspective of presidential influence in history.

HARD grader.  A- is the best grade he gives.  Great lecturer.  Very interesting.  Very busy, however, now that he is Chair he doesn't have a lot of time.  Is nice to students but doesn't have a lot of free time.  You will get a lot out of the class but the grading might be tough for some to take.  You will have to work hard.

hard to get into this class for a reason.  Great TA's.  He does not give out A's unless you earn it.  Be creative in your papers and link it to the bigger picture.  He doesn't give Reagan the love he deserves, but he is fair.  A different perspective on the presidency.  Jefferson would be proud.

Milkis is a fabulous professor- he has utmost respect for his students and he is highly entertaining. He really makes you want to attend class, and treats students as though they are his equals. Awesome.

Professor Milkis is perhaps one of the most enthusiastic additions to the UVA Politics Department. It is rare to find someone with so much passion for subject matter and concern for students.  Readings can be numerous, but well worth it.
This class is pretty sweet...easy readings, and interesting material. Definitely take this, but oh wait, its nearly impossible to get into. Fun Fun.

not worth an a- in an engagement bringing down my gpa. good lectures and interesting class but an engagement should be an easy A when you do all the work.

Milov is cool, her lectures are somewhat difficult to follow, she moves quickly and sounds as if she's reading from a research paper. She assigns SO MUCH READING, but you do not have to do it all. You can get a B+ without doing any of the weekly readings. The TA Lauren is AWESOME but SUCH a hard grader, beware!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Milov is a great modern professor. The grade was  only based on papers, however, she is so helpful throughout the whole process. If you go to office hours and ask for helpshow that you are trying, she will definitely provide you with great sources! Also, I worried about my participation grade but don't stress it as long as you try and prepare!

Lecture is all random tangents. Concepts are never clear. The questions on hw are never on tests. Class is online in summer, super quick, and tests are impossible so most cheat to pass (barely). This class will consume your life - beware. Buy the solutions manual and be prepared for a class where no one understands anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Metcalf is very knowledgeable about pchem but is not very good about explaining concepts to students and glosses over fundamental concepts that are still difficult to understand. This was a summer class, so not a lot of time to really go in depth, but each session was 2hr15min long so I feel like he could have definitely spared a few minutes.

I came into Metcalf's class with no prior experience in Chemistry. The class difficulty was rather difficult but the tests were definitely possible to do well in. His lectures usually do not reflect what you need to master for the test. I recommend doing the recommended practice problems that are on the syllabus and the homework. STUDY AND PRACTICE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Metcalf is not a good professor at all. His lectures do not clearly explain the material well. He teaches as if the students already know the material and doesn't go in depth enough. His exams are also incredibly hard for no reason. Instead of preparing us well for the exams, he spends more time telling us what to know , instead of explaining it.

Nobody actually pays attention in this class. Paying attention to him and taking notes will honestly just confuse you more. Most topics he talks about aren't important and aren't on the tests. Even the TAs acknowledge he's the worst and can't even do some of the problems he expects us to do. Other professors have test avgs of 15-20 points higher

While Professor Metcalf clearly knows what he's talking about, he simply does not convey ideas in a way students understand. Compared to other General Chemistry professors at UVA, he just does not seem to teach to the student's level or take as much care to help students understand. Most students only go to his class to get participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Doesn't prepare you at all for the tests and the lectures don't make sense. He teaches random, unimportant things in class then expects you to know the things he barely mentioned inside andHe said a test average of 65 was good. The other teachers that teach this course have averages in the 80s. Save yourself the tears and don't take his class :(

If you have a choice, please don't take Metcalf's chem section. If it's unavoidable, you can still pass, but it will be harder than the other profs. His lectures can be funny but he tends to assume that we all remember high school chem and therefore just rushes through concepts I find confusing. I failed the first test. Prepare to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the single worst class I have ever taken in my life. You could study two weeks in advance for a test and still get a 60. Said he "aimed for an average in the 60s." This class will ruin your life and gpa.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor. Chemistry is not my best subject, but Metcalf was interested and easier to understand than most. Encourages questions and was really helpful during office hours.

Most ridiculous class I've ever taken. I'll admit I didn't like Chemistry to begin with, but Metcalf is the worst professor ever and I never even had a chance to get a good grade with his lecture style. He goes too fast and hardly ever answers questions students raise. He is perfectly happy with test averages around 62 - 67 %.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Confusing, with a teaching style described as "stream of consciousness". Difficult tests and general confusion abound

4 quizzes, get to drop lowest; each quiz 20% ,final 40%.  Attendance not mandatory.  class is useless. If youre smart/good at science, as good as it gets.   Quiz avg 70, meaning 1 s.d. for an A is around 83-85.  Got 100/100/95 on the first 3--went to see him to verify could skip last .  He confirmed.  Loved class.  Put in 4 days of work whole sems

Professor Metcalf seemed to want to teach what he felt was interesting but not necessarily was important for test, very boring lecture, everyone seemed to be checking Facebook. Definitely a "weed out" course for Pre-med so unless you're on that track, it's not really like a cool science class to take.
Wanders off on tangents about chemistry that aren't helpful and don't prepare you for the quizes

I actually really didn't mind Gen Chem and thought Metcalf was a good professor for a lecture hall class. His materials were clear and organized, and he even did some interesting demonstrations. He's kind of goofy, but really knows Chem inside out and does a good job showing how concepts interweave and build on each other.
He's at least phonetically accurate in English... more than you can say about Leung.  Other than that nothing special he is ok.

Took this class my 4th year and loved it. PChem uses equations and relations to derive meaning out of the material. Metcalf understands this and does a great job playing with the mathematics to explain what's going on. One of the better teachers at UVA's CHEM department
Terrible teacher, simply reads slides and then seems to enjoy killing students with the difficulty of his tests

Metcalf is not a bad guy, but as a teacher he is not great. He most of the time reads right from the slides, and class has gotten to be a bore.By the end of the semester he pretty much is so tired of teaching, you have to read from the book to even understand the slides. I would not take him unless you have to.

Absolute worst Chem professor. He is terrible at teaching, and downright mean. He obviously doesn't care about students and actually wants them to do poorly, he seems to enjoy it. Do not take him if you can avoid it.

Really nice guy. Outstanding chem teacher. Best I had at UVA. Problem sets come every 2 weeks but aren't bad. The tests are hard, but he's a really reasonable grader. Don't consider taking p-chem with anyone but him. I promise you'll regret it

Metcalf is definitely underrated. Took class Summer 2012 and thoroughly enjoyed it. P-chem is not a good subject or enjoyable by any means, mind you, but Metcalf made it bearable and was a good lecturer and did not try to cram a bunch of information down your throat without explaining it first.

He likes to engage students which is nice. His tests are very tricky though. Nothing on there is straight forward. You have to know your stuff inside and out. Knowing your stuff 50% will get you a 25%. You definitely have to put a fair amount of time outside of class studying to get a good grade. It's a little harder than it has to be but it's fair

Defintiely the best Chem professor at UVa. His quizzes are fair based on the information he teaches and also compared to other professors seem somewhat easier. He also gives the least amount of homework.

Metcalf is the best Chem professor at UVa (for intro chem). The quizzes were alright as long as you take them slow. He helped explain things very well and is very efficient with the grading. Homework is easy. He was very funny and easy to listen to. But don't take chem as an elective, after all its a weed out course.

He does a really good job of explaining the subject and he is pretty animated in his lectures. Seems like an all around nice guy. Never went to his office hours but seems the type to be helpful if I needed too. The tests are challenging but not impossible if you use all of the practice problems and study materials he gives you.
He's a great guy -- pretty funny too. Is interested in making sure you understand the material, and willing to help you if needed.
Professor Metcalf made PCHEM wonderful. He has very high expectations of his students, seen by the questions asked on problem sets and exams, but overall, he made PCHEM a breeze. Highly suggest him.
Great professor, really cares about his students and is always ready to answer a question. He is really hard, but he doesn't try to trick you on tests like some of the other teachers.
This is the worse teacher ever!!! if you want a good gpa, don't take this teacher!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Run while you still can!!!

Metcalf is only good if you already know what's going on, which is probably why the ratings are so bad for his intro level classes. In any event, this class was effectively run by TAs, since 95% of the grade is lab reports, which are a pain, but you should be used to this by now after 2 semesters of hell in organic. Not great but not horrible.
You can have a social life and still get an A in this class.  Maybe if students weren't such failures at life (like the person writing on 5/8) they would make A's too.

Not too bad (I had him for lab only, apparently disregard if you're in his lecture), like most labs its TA driven, but he didn't curve the final grade.  Which sucks if you're in the 35 person 80s series class.

For any normal person who likes to go out AT ALL and have a life, his class is near impossible. unless you're brilliant or have no life (person below), don't expect to get good grades. lectures are pointless. I did better when I just taught myself straight from the book. His tests are meant to trick you in cruel ways, be ware. get a tutor.seriously

His class is pretty difficult and I definitely had to spend a lot of time with the material. He doesn't make much sense in lecture so it's almost pointles... but he tells you what sections in the book are going to be on the test so you don't have to do unnecessary studying. overall, this class isn't impossible..but it IS hard work

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. "IT'S A TRAP!" (Akbar) Easily the worst teacher I have ever had, and I've had some bad ones. You MUST teach yourself. During class, try pick up hints from his inane rambling and awful handwriting while you: read your textbook; do all the practice problems multiple times; and try to glean what you can from old quizzes. Good luck!

He's honestly not a bad teacher. His class is about what I expected college chemistry to be like: he gives you basic notes but you learn the most from reading the text. His quizzes aren't that hard if you spend a little time studying & he tells you what's going to be on them. His class is definitely fair, I don't understand all the criticism.
You must attend class, as he uses alot of examples not found in the textbook or in the slides which he posts to the web.  He is a great guy and an easy teacher to learn from.

Choosing Metcalf's class is the most horrible choice i've ever made in my life; He's basically ruined my chances of getting into medical school. His tests are ridiculously hard unlike other professors.

I didn't really like Chem to begin with, but the tests are 15 questions (so missing 5 is a bummer). The final was much easier pulling my C+ to a B-. But it wasn't too bad, just the tests were more than I could do.

Don't be intimidated by peoples' reviews of Metcalf. He's a pretty good teacher--albeit unclear at times--who expects you to have read at least some of the chapter prior to coming to class. His tests aren't as impossible as people make them out to be and the weekly homework sets are pretty easy.

Despite all the complaining I heard about Metcalf, I really did not think he was a bad teacher. Sure, it's a hard class, but what did you expect? The other two professors (Garrans and Harmon) both put me to sleep during lab lecture, but Metcalf teaches it so you understand it, even if it may seem confusing at first. Easy online homework (1x/wk).
You won't understand him in class he teaches like you already know it....use thinkwell, go to his office hours, and be sure u can do the questions on the old test...that'll help u pass the class
He stinks. TRY TO GET SOMEONE ELSE! Tests are harder than the other classes. He's confusing in class, doesn't explain things too clearly. My high school teacher was better than him.

Please, i repeat, please do not take this buggers class. He will kill all our attempts to premed, bio major, or any prospect of getting good grades for the whole semester. His teaching technique, well he doesnt have one, and his tests are so hard that anyone who has just been studying from his notes will probably fail every single test!.. HEs bad
Umm... It's better to study by yourself. Tests: some questions are tricky! Attend the TA's review session - they're soooooo helpful! You'll find questions very helpful for the exams

this man is a waste of the carbon he talks about..boring, useless, and seems to enjoy you struggling. i pulled an a- both semesters but you hate every minute youre in class and you will learn to hate him. he is so dry you will fall asleep every class. he has now interest in teaching well. do yourself a  favor and take any other section besides his.

Please please do not take his class... he will ruin ur life and ur grades and ur prospects for GRAD school.. i took him this semester and believe me, it has been thw worst semester of my life.. i worked the most for this class and got the worst grade.. he cant teach, cant make tests. he can everything other than ramble bout useless crap..

Wow.  This class was a PAIN.  I put so much time into it, understood everything, and the tests were NOTHING like what had been discussed in class.  The class itself isn't awfully boring, but the tests are disgusting.  If you learn, it's due to the countless hours you have to put in to contend for decent grades.

nice guy, terrible prof. dont bother going to class because his lectures are unclear and the lecture notes dont help. you basically have to teach the material to yourself. do go to the TAs reviews sessions before the tests though, because those often cover questions very similar to the ones on the tests
Blech!!! Take Harman or Gerrands!
His lectures are worthless. Better off reading the book on your own instead of wasting time in lecture. Tests and the final are all multiple choice, which is a plus.

Metcalf is one of the least understanding people I've ever met. He was unable to explain the answer key to a lab or why my report was wrong, but refused to fix it, then insulted me because I didn't match the key, so he decided I must be wrong, even though me, him, my TA, and Jan down the hall all got a different answer then the key.
One of the worst professors I have ever had. He simply doesn't know a lot about the topic and going to his class made me lose my interest in chemistry.

The man simply cannot convey chemistry concepts well when he lectures.  His explanations are not well formed.  Reading the textbook is a better use of time than attending the lecture is.  (If you choose that path, just make sure you actually do read the textbook!)  Get Harmon instead.

Metcalf is a terrible lecturer, and there's really no point of going to class (maybe every now and then because he would give lil' hints about the tests). For the most part if you read on your own your better off. I do advise going to his office hours because he will gladly go through problems with you. Your better off taking another teacher

don't even bother going to class.  metcalf is a terrible lecturer and you're better off reading the book by yourself than going.  his tests are much harder than the other 141/151 teacher's tests.  take someone else.

People don't like him, but I thought he was fine. The tests aren't tricky, they're just hard and you have to know your stuff.  He sends out emails before every test on what you have to know which is helpful. You don't really need to go to class, you could learn everything from the textbook, but it does help to get a sense of whats on the test.

he gives very difficult quizzes because he tries to trick you and the material is occasionally stuff he does not review in class.  Go to lectures but study the book not your notes, half the time your notes wont make since, he rambles too much about nothing.

Metcalf is not helpful and he likes to try to trick students on the tests, however if you read the book, or had a good highschool chemistry class you will do well. If you are good at Chem, you will get a good grade because the rest of the class will be completely lost

This man and Dan Keenan are professors you do not want to have.  Absolutely the dumbest professors ever.  They both earn 200K for teaching and you learn nothing.  You can learn everything there is under the sun, and he would still make the test impossible.  Don't take this classsss ever.  Get Harmon or Gerrands, trust me!

Lectures don't help much, I used my book to figure most of the subject out. His homework is fairly easy. He always sends out an email containing what is going to be on the test, but his class is still hard. Would suggest Garrans or Harman over Metcalf.
Metcalf ruined my life!

Metcalf does not teach anything. His lectures are on things that have nothing to do with the actual material. If you get stuck with him, dont bother going to lecture with him. Just read the book during class and watch thinkwell. Good luck staying awake during lectures...

Metcalf is a joke.. All he does is ramble on in class about 50 thousand different equations and reactions that which end up meaningless b/c he dosent explain what the heck he's talking about. No point in attending his class, you'll only be more confused. Take gerrans.. Def NOT metcalf.. ridiculous tests

i got a B in 141 but its gonna be iffy for 142. basically talks to the blackboard the whole time. doesnt test on things he emphasizes in class. instead of just one question that asks you to apply info in an absurd circumstance, his entire test is like that. def take someone else...

He is a horrible lecturer who spends most of his time deriving formulas instead of actually explaining what they mean and how to use them. None of what he does in class appears on the quizzes, which are random and usually very very difficult. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS
141 is easy... 142 not so much, but if you read the book and go over the emails he sends before each quiz, you should do decent

Lectures are really boring and not very helpful. If you bother going to office hours, he'll give a round about answer to any question you ask. Avoid him if you can for the 141/142 class, but in lab try to get a good TA.

Terrible lecturer--regardless of his expertise on the subject, he cannot teach even simple concepts in a comprehensible manner.  He also will often introduce a concept with mathematical scribble rather than a simple example linked to informative lecture.

boring lecturer, and the book was bad. Completely uninteresting. Go to Gerrans or Harman if at all possible.
wat's up with the quotas??? GET OUT NOW
chem 151

I dont know what everyone is complaining about. Metcalf is a fine teacher, and it is possible to get a fine grade as long as you work hard and read the book. Quizzes are fair (my average is a 14 out of 15), and you just need to study to do fine. Lectures do not help at all though
He makes no sense
141: not awful, b/c most ppl already know the material 142: AWFUL..random ass questions...

The average for one quiz was a 57.4  I went to every single lecture and studied... what kind of professor is he?, you ask...

don't waste your time going to class. if you don't go every day, it's pointless. he writes on the chalkboard, which is impossible to read unless you're in the front 5 rows. the tests are deceivingly hard, however, he will drop questions if no one gets them right.
He's a pretty good teacher...easy to understand in lectures...if you can stay awake.  The class is hard by its nature but you won't regret taking it with him

He is an extremely smart man, but he really cant teach the material. You pretty much have to teach yourself and do all of the reading. switch to gerrans if you want easier tests and a much better lecturer.

Skipped class for 2 months (wish i went more though) & put in minimal effort...managed a C. He's a nice guy but lectures can become boring. Quizzes were fair and he returns grades quickly.  When i went to class, he was funny and approachable.  Go to his school website...he raises llamas!!

Horrible.  Lectures are almost useless because he cannot explain anything clearly.  Tests are pretty fair.  If you want to succeed without having to teach yourself the material then I would recomment Gerrans.

Does a decent job explaining the material, if you can read his writing and actually go to class in the auditorium.  Reading the book is a suitable alternative to lectures, as demonstrated by the many empty seats in the auditorium.  Sometimes funny, overall a fairly good teacher. Returns grades fast.

Illegible handwriting aside, he is not as bad as people make him out to be. Knows his stuff. The tests are possible if you read the book and read your notes for a couple of hours. Posts old tests online, which he takes questions from, so they are really helpful. Will take him again for Chem142.

Metcaf's lectures might have been out of the book, but some people learn better having it explained to them.  I loved this class, because I needed to do no work day to day, study a few hours for each test, and still get an A or B. Thats because I went to the lectures though!Funny guy and fair tests.
As the year goes on, he makes more sense!
i admit he knows chem, but he might as quit teaching, just assign the readings, and tell to teach ourselves and show up for test days.  real boring too.
teaches pretty much from the book. the policy of dropping the low quiz grade was nice. lectures were ok
I often find myself saying "What the hell is that on the board." Might as well Just read the book because you're  likely to fall asleep in class anyway. That is, if you go.
One word,sucks.
corny/weird sense of humor, unclear in class. don't go like everyone else and just read the book, because that's what he teaches from.

I can't work with the way he teaches; he writes on the board in an all-over-the-place kind of way, and his handwriting is illegible. I find it hard to stay awake in class. Some people can work with him better than others.
In my opinion the best of the intro chem instructors.  I enjoyed this class.
Teaches directly from the book. Really weird sense of humor. Most students don't go to class and just read the book. I suggest you do the same. Tests are difficult and graded on a bell curve.

Metcalf is a very good professor.  He has lame jokes, but that makes him funny.  I consider him neutral in terms of his personality.  He is neither positive, nor negative.  I would recommend him for any chem students
REALLY REALLY Boring!!  I learned more by skipping lectures and reading the book.

BORING, BORING, BORING.  I have fallen asleep several times so far this year.  He lectures right out of the book, which is kind of frustrating, but his quizzes aren't all that bad.  Supposedly he is helpful outside of class, but i havn't gone to see him y

better of the intro chem lecture profs., follows book close, read everything

He returns papers/tests incredibly quickly, and with very useful feedback. I found his course well structured, and every paper he assigned helped my understanding. He is the sort of classicist who likes grammar a lot (I am not) - you'll need to be able to explain why words are in certain cases/moods, bc it makes up a lot of his exams.
Really great teacher. Very patient, clear, not excessively demanding, and a really nice guy. Best Latin class I've ever taken.

Best class ever. If you are interested in Greek Mythology at all, you should take this class. Very funny. It's pretty much a comedy riot in his class all the time. Even discussion sections are not miserable bc the TAs know their stuff. Tests are easy if you listen to him at all.

I loved this class, it was so interesting.  Lectures were like story time where we got to listen to the soap opera of the gods/goddesses.  Tests are easy if you go to class.  TAs are helpful and good.  Definitely a wonderful class!
One of my favorite Classics professors, and very helpful with advice about classes, etc.

This is the only class that has ever pushed me to write a review on here. Questions on problem sets and tests are extremely vague, instructions are counter-intuitive, and no matter what you will be graded extremely harshly. Very little feedback is given for where you went wrong. Professor Skrutskie is great, but this class is simply not worth it.

I took ASTR 2110 in the fall of 2022, and I feel it is necessary that I post this review after seeing all of the recent 1/5 reviews. I do not understand where they are coming from. Professor Skrutskie was the best professor I have ever had. He was engaging and genuinely cared about his students. Don't be dissuaded by the recent negative reviews.

AST 2110 left much to be desired. The grading system was cryptic, lacking clear criteria and transparent instructions. Students struggled to understand how their efforts were being evaluated, creating a frustrating and confusing learning experience. Approach with caution if you value a straightforward approach to assessments.

I got 100% on every assignment except for the exams, which were confusingly graded and much more difficult than lecture material. We were given 2 hours to complete them, but honestly the questions asked would take 5+.
Overally disorganized and it was a very exhausting class. Problem sets were very confusing, not well explained, and TA was not insightful even though they wrote the problem set.

Not ever clear with how to solve problems or actually do the math behind the equations, covers extraneous components for the class period, then tests you on stuff never actually covered.

The best way I would describe it: He shows you how to get from A to B and the K to J and then he expects you to know A to Z.

Is not clear on expectations when grading, could say he wants you to be precise, but then will take off points if you don't write enough/exactly what he says- very frustrating especially when exams are worth 55% of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If he says write briefly, write a lot. If he says make crude approximations, you need to show every step in that process while not ever using sig figs as those will get points taken off. If you don't use sig figs sometimes, he will also mark you off. According to him, and literally no one else in the department, Pi is 3 and e is just Pi.

Exams are 55% of your grade, so if you mess those up, you have no chance getting an A. Very unclear on why so many points are deducted on exams. If you don't write enough to his satisfaction, he will mark you off, but answers should be very brief. The whole course was very conflicted as he asks for one thing, then expects the opposite.

ASTR 2110:
Overall dull class. Horrible grading and exams. Says to make crude calculations and approximations, but then marks you off heavily for doing so or marks you off for using too many sig figs. No clear grading rubric for assignments and exams, you just submit and pray most of the time. I left every discussion feeling more confused.

Very unclear grading parameters, tests worth a disproportionately large chunk of the final grade. Problem sets often are beyond the scope of things explained in the lecture, their difficulty largely depends on how good the discussion section TA is. Overall disconnect between the lectures and the graded assignments.
Nice guy, great demonstrations, loves astronomy, interesting stuff. Take this guy if your in 1210 intro to sky and solar system.
Awesome professor! He is very clear and interesting in his lectures in which he does experiments, and he posts all his powerpoints online.
THIS DUDE IS AWESOME! his lectures are very clear and posts everything online.

Skrutskie is an excellent lecturer - one of the most engaging I've had. This is not a hard class. He's excited about the subject matter and his online notes and resources are extensive. He posts enough on his class site that you wouldn't need the book at all for studying for tests. Very enjoyable course.

lectures can be boring but attendance pads your final grade. reread the online notes and go to the review sessions and it shouldn't be too hard. he knows his stuff and will take extra time with you. i facebooked through class and still ended with an A just from cramming before test days. i wouldn't buy the textbook; just borrow if truly necessary.
Extremely boring

Once again this class was much more difficult than I expected(I am NOT a science person). I love skrutskie though-he'll really try to help you out if you're struggling and he's incredibly smart. Do NOT buy the textbook.

Enthusiastic, knowledgeable, etc. etc. Lectures posted, but I went to (almost)every one. Some were great, some were sleep-inducing. Note on the book: DON'T BUY it for his class. He gives you all the material in lecture and it's reallllly expensive. BEWARE: Tests are tricky, even with studying! Yet he curves them a bit. Overall: not a bad class.

This class is ridiculously hard, especially for a math and science handicapped person like myself. Skrutskie is a good lecturer but his exams which are based on what seem to be "simple" lecture notes are very tricky and extremely difficult. If you want to fill a requirement don't take this class!! If you are a Astronomy or Science major, go ahead.

really nice professor, really engaging and accesible to students. i dont really have an interest in astronomy, so i found the class hard to stay awake in, but i think that was the material more than the professor. It helps to go to class for wildcards. reading the book isnt really necessary. if you take astr, take him, but dont be fooled, astr=hard

His class isn't too hard, but tests can be tricky. Take advantage of extra credit(!) and review sessions. Lectures can be dull, but he makes up for it with hilarious demonstrations. Be sure to visit during office hours or after class if you need help or just want to chat with a great prof. who's VERY passionate about astronomy. I love this guy!
good

Professor Skrutskie is AMAZING!!!! If you are just looking for a fun class to fill science credits, this is it! He makes astronomy fun and interesting and easy to understand. His in class demonstrations are awesome and the observing labs can be tedious, but they are an easy grade. Also, he gives extra credit....so take his Astronomy 121 class!!!!!!

Prof. Skrutskie is awesome! For a history major trying to fill her last science requirement and be done with that stuff forever, I really enjoyed the class. Go to lecture, part of the grade are "quizzes" that are for completion. I recommend printing the notes before class/bringing laptop. Reading is light, but keep up with it! Best astronomy prof!

Wonderful teacher. Very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter. ASTR 121 is not a gut class, but it requires as light an amount of work as you will find at UVa. Very interesting subject, if you attend class and read online notes you will recieve and A/B. His review sessions are very usefull. I would recomend them.

Wonderful astronomy teacher! I learned a lot and want to take his class again. Demonstrations and lecture topics are fascinating and he does a great job of debunking common astronomy misconceptions.  Class is an easy B NOT an easy A.  You will have to work very hard to do well on the 3 tests and the final.  There is extra credit available, though.
Best astronomy teacher ever.  If you are looking for an intro astron class, TAKE SKRUTSKIE!!!
Easy class, though lectures can be boring. Nice guy who knows his stuff though.

Skrutskie is an awesome teacher who teaches with passion about astronomy. He does lots of ish outside of class dealing with astronomy and his knowledge seems limitless--just try him with a question. Always willing to help and loves to spark interest in astronomical ideas
Great teacher, makes lectures somewhat interesting, just spend some time studying for the tests youll be fine

Prof. Skrutskie really loves what he does and his passion spills into his lectures. This class is not by any means easy though; you must study and do the readings. Keep your old tests, the final is composed of questions nearly word-for-word from the three midterms.

Prof Skrutskie is an amazing teacher, and he is truly passionate about astronomy and will do plenty to get you excited about it too. Be warned that this class is NOT an easy A. His tests are difficult, but you can easily get a B from the class work and 2 labs. Also, he reuses old test questions on the final, nearly word for word.
Early part of the semester was awesome. Later on it got a little boring. The class is an easy B, NOT an easy A.

Very interesting and friendly man who always lectures with a smile. His lectures are clear yet detailed. His tests may be difficult, but he gives a very generous curve. Overall, it's a very interesting course that is an easy A, albeit not an automatic A. The book is expensive, but it's not necessary at all.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS CLASS if you are just taking it to fulfill the math/science credit. it is very hard if you aren't interested in physics and the complexities of the solar system. the tests are very difficult. I am a smart person and I am doing very poorly in this class. TRUST ME it's a hard class! and it's boring!

Great lecturer who knows a lot about astronomy, and loves his job.  I have learned a tremendous amount in his class, but you wouldn't know it from my grade.  His tests are very hard, but I wouldn't take astronomy with any other professor

I didn't find this class as easy as everyone else on here says it is.  The lectures, though boring, were clear, but the tests were very challenging.  He's a nice and helpful guy, but I'd recommend taking one of the many other astr 121 profs.
Very entertaining, funny, and intelligable professor.  Great class!

Almost all the girls say he is hot, so... Best lecture I've had in UVA. Has cool demostrations. Extremely enthusiastic. In my class 2 years ago people clap like crazy for his demos (hint: he does not like the applause) and it shows we like him. Very very easy class. I never read the book for the A. I almost majored in ASTR because of him.

I had mixed feelings about this class.  The lectures are good, but not in comparison to other professors of the same class.  Reading the book helps if you do it before lecture, but if you fall behind it's not a big deal.  The greatest thing to remember is to do the extra labs.  He also uses another book in addition to the standard astronomy text.

I thought his lectures had mood swings. Some parts would be interesting while others would put you to sleep. I read the first chapter of the book and nothing after that so personally I think that you don't really need the book because of his online notes. Tests appear easy but are kinda challenging.

He's a really interesting teacher and tries to liven up the lectures with brief and fun demonstrations. Tests are easy if you read through the online notes and skim the book, review sheet helps only if you understand the answers on your own. He is INCREDIBLY cute and enthusiastic, I loved this class!

He is a great professor and the class is really easy. All you have to do is go to lecture and skim the book and you're sure to get an A. The lectures can be a little boring sometimes, but he has cool demonstrations that help to keep you awake. Overall an interesting and very easy class.

An absolutely wonderful lecturer who clearly loves his work. But be warned that the tests are pretty hard, even though the lectures are clear. The review sheets are not as helpful as they seem! Overall, though, I really enjoyed the class. And he is, hands down, one of the cutest profs at UVA ;)
taking him this sem. very enthusiastic guy and loves the subject really much. anyone has some comments about his exam? only study the notes or wut?

great class to take, just study the outlines and go over the notes (he posts them online), a few assignments...nothing hard..you just have to do it..i never used the book..and if you go to the review session before the test your fine! :o)ps hes so nice!!!

This class is deceptive! As a teacher, Skrutskie is really interesting because he really loves this subject. But his tests are difficult. The review sheets lure you into a false sense of security...BEWARE!!!

this class is very INTERESTING. the only DIFFICULT thing is learning how to spell his NAME! you can tell that he loves what he does..teaches very well...he's always talking (and fast too). really knows his subject. also has demonstrations, very funny. you'll love him and astronomy...trust me.
No Comments
pretty clear, easy class. prof. skrutskie tries v. hard to make the subject entertaining and easy to understand.

Excellent, excellent, excellent.  He makes it his goal to teach, not trick students, and he clearly enjoys what he does.  Relatively easy class in that the information is clear and tests are straightforward - one of the best professors I've had here.

This class is 100% tests. Moore is fantastic, hilarious, engaging, you'll learn a lot. CL2 is definitely harder than CL1. My section's final was hard for no reason and she put stuff on there I'm positive she never taught us, so that was a bummer. You must attend every class or get the notes from someone else. The whole class is lectures & tests.

PHENOMENAL class. No reading/HW, literally just go to lecture and take notes - she will literally tell you what to write down. Content is fascinating, she is HILARIOUS. An A is hard b/c of weighting but put in the work. You get cheat sheets for the tests even though they're hand-written. Sherri is accomplished, knowledgeable, and SO engaging.

Professor Moore's COMM 3410 is one of the classes that you will tell your children about. She is passionate and truly cares for her students' success. There are no readings and no work outside of lecture, other than studying for exams. Her exams are multiple choice and her grading system is very fair. I recommend this class to everyone.

This class was hard - yes. You have to put in the effort. Prioritize taking notes on what she teaches in class. Study for the weekly quizzes. I did not get an A but I still enjoyed it. Professor Moore is a very compelling lecturer. She is a good professor and she deserves the praise - she is also a genuinely nice human being.

Professor Moore's class is probably the most overrated at UVA. If you are looking for an easy class, thi is not for you. You are graded on very few things. a 40% final which is cumulatitive and the hardest exam ever. 2/10 recommend
The class material can get slow at times but this class made learning the law fun and interesting! Professor Moore is also such a wonderful lecturer and person.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sherri has been doing this for a long time and knows what shes doing. She is a very dynamic lecturer and makes going to class fun. Be prepared to take notes fast because she can talk quickly, but her exams are always straightforward. An A might be hard to achieve, but an A- is very doable.
Overall great teacher. Note-taking in her class Comm Law 1 is a grind but there is zero reading or anything outside of the class. Genuinely a great and interesting person as well.

Sherri is the greatest professor I have had. She makes Law interesting and applicable to a students life. The class is not difficult and you do not need to get the book. Go to lecture and pay attention and you will get a good grade in the class.

Professor Moore is very friendly and a good Professor. You really need to be able to apply the concepts to real situations if you want to get an A on her tests. I know that sounds simple, but she makes you work for it.

No longer an easy A but attend lecture, take it somewhat seriously and you're golden. You'll start to love Pr Moore and subconsciously work to not let her down. The material is sometimes dense but honestly everyone should take this course (lots of information about leases, contracts, your rights as an individual). Weekly quiz, extra fred, 3 exams.

To students who will take it in the future: this class is no longer an easy A class! You may find that from 2011-2012, people were saying that this class was very easy as long as you listen to her and take good notes...But, it is definitely not easy anymore! The test questions are tricky, and you have to have some background knowledge!!!

Great Professor, tries hard to make law relevant and interesting to students and is incredibly helpful during office hours. Students can use up to two pages of notes on the midterm and final, and almost all the material is covered well lecture. Tests are relatively easy as well. She uses clickers a lot though, so attendance is required.
Great professor who is super approachable and so so hot!

Amazing interesting and funny teacher. I came in expecting commercial law to be bored but her class made me like the material so much. Her tests are open note so as long as you took really good notes and paid attention in class you'll get a A!

Prof Moore is awesome! Her Comm Law class is always interesting and definitely useful in the real world. She is very approachable and helpful. Reading from the textbook isn't necessary as long as you understand your class notes. Definitely recommend this class!!!

Great teacher who is very friendly and approachable. She makes the class interesting and you learn very valuable real-world lessons. Reading was usually unnecessary as long as you took notes and paid attention in class.

Mokoko is wonderful and UVA is incredibly lucky to have him. It's uncommon I come across a Professor that cares so much about his students, and it's the reason he spends hours after class walking with students. His positive energy and respect is easily recognized across grounds. His curriculum is meaningful and healing, 100% recommend.
horrible prof
This guy is wrong on so many levels.

I am beyond thankful I got to have Professor Mokoko. I wouldn't call the class easy, but if you make a meaningful attempt Mokoko will guarantee that your grade in the class works out. He is incredibly insightful, motivating, wise, and more than anything kind. If you're considering his course, absolutely take it, and try to get to know him
It was his first time teaching undergrad, and he did really well! He explained things very thoroughly and was always available if you needed help.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class isn't as bad as many have written on here. Just show up, take down everything he writes on the board, and do the homework. For the midterm, just do all of the homework again and definitely do the practice midterm, since the real midterm is pretty much the same thing. As for the final, it's not hard, if you showed up for class.

One of the best ECON professors! He introduces the topics very clearly and systematically. Very useful analytical skills covered in the materials.Students are free to interrupt and ask questions and he'll answer them promptly. Materials covered are totally manageable. Especially if you like BOTH math & econ,you'll be very comfortable in this class.
Not a hard class. Just make sure you go to all of the lectures and write down everything he writes down. If you know how to do the homeworks before the tests you will do fine.

Believe what you read, he's the worst professor I've ever had. Can't understand him, his notes make no sense, his final is insanely difficult, and he prances around the room like a lunatic while he teaches. If you get stuck with him, go to class and copy down all the graphs, but read EVERYTHING relevant in the book if you want to survive.
Absolutely miserable professor.  Not only does the class border on physically painful, but I came out of it having learned NOTHING about macro.
Worst Econ Professor.  Don't take this class.

What everyone else has said is entirely true.  Lectures come word-for-word from the textbook, classes are extremely boring, and the second midterm was ridiculously hard.  But on the plus side, homeworks are graded on completion, and there must be a huge curve at the end because my final graded ended up being okay.

My advice: buy the textbook, show up only on the days of the midterms and final, or, better yet, DON'T TAKE A CLASS W/ THIS PROF! His lectures are useless, the tests are fairly straight-forward but hard considering the dearth of teaching, and he is thoroughly unhelpful. Didn't bother showing up on the day of the final. He shouldn't be teaching.

Awful Teacher. Can barely speak English and cannot pronounce the letter "r." I ended up being my own teacher with the textbook. First test, easy, then the second one is hard. Going to class will give you a headache and alot of time to read the cav daily. Oh, and the discussion teachers are worthless too.

Without a doubt the worst econ class and professor i have taken while at this school.  He does nothing but give lectures right out of the book and still doesn't manage to teach it clearly.  Its also almost impossible to sit through an entire class without dying from boredom.  Avoid if possible.

ludicrously easy first midterm, IMPOSSIBLE second one. class in super repetitive, less than half of the people attend, most do sudoku, barely anyone takes notes... i dont know of a single person who enjoys 302. the lectures are readings of the book, and the examples are straight from the book, class is "textbook storytime" terrible, just terrible.

Possibly the nicest prof in the econ department. He tries very hard to make the concepts clear, which sometimes results in repetitiveness. Also, he spends a lot of the class reviewing 202 and 301 - the actual macro stuff doesn't start till after the first midterm. There's sporadic homework, graded on effort, and two midterms - nothing too intense.

Great teacher, but extremely intimidating. Best advice is to get to know him one-on-one (after which he tends to go easier on you) and work really hard. His 100 and 300 level classes are difficult, but his dialect class is really laid back, especially for him. Also, take note of his hilarious expressions, idioms, and syntax.

He was by far the worst teacher I had at UVA. I've heard he's great in Arabic 101 but I had him for 301 (I was a transfer) and because of him, I withdrew. He's childishly mean and needs to be reminded that he doesn't rule the world. He's probably a great teacher if he doesn't decide to treat you like scum.
best professor
Do not take this class if you are not willing to put in the work!
Really nice out of the classroom but sort of intimidating in the class. He likes to call on people and put them on the spot - but overall the class is not that difficult and you will learn arabic!

He's a fun teacher, but the class is hard because Arabic is a hard language. Only take it if you plan to truly stay on top of the material. Do all your homework, it really helps your grade and prepare for the tests and quizzes. He likes students who are dedicated and really put in an effort. And he makes the class pretty interesting.

Put the work in. Very harsh to people who aren't on top of the material, but it's usually when we've heard it 5 times already. Difficult to memorize vocab with different characters. COME TO CLASS. He says things in that droning voice so you will repeat them how he's saying it. I'm in 201 now, and Arabic is not for the easily intimidated.

I've taken French and Arabic here and abroad and this is by far the best language teacher I've ever had.  He can be intimidating, especially if you get on his bad side by showing that you don't take the class seriously.  Work really hard in first year Arabic.  It will pay off

Sawaie is fun and interesting. He can be intimidating, but as long as you don't come to class unprepared, or at least pay attention and don't look like a ****bag he goes pretty easy on you, and he is awesome if he likes you.

Sawaie's a complex guy. Whats bad:He's nuts about public humiliation and is totally intimidating in office hrs.He wrote the only grammar textbook for the class is full of typos(every page conspicuously says "rough draft")which makes learning one of the hardest languages even harder.Whats good:he's funny as hell,and public humiliation is funto watch
Get on his good side, he likes people who are enthusiastic.  If you put in the work, you'll get a good grade.

Expect to work very hard and come to lecture prepared. Can be funny and easy going, but most of the time he is intimidating, inacessible, and downright mean. Will rip you to shreds in class if you can't answer when he calls on you. He does make snide cutting remarks. He teaches well, but a lot of people dread his classes.

Get on his good side early. If he likes you and you keep up with the work, you'll have fun. However, if you fumble in class or don't do well, he'll tear you apart in front of the class. Really catty and insulting to students who have trouble with the subject. He can be really impatient and mean but an OK teacher to students he likes.

Totally awesome teacher. Very clear, and easy to understand. He moves a good speed for those who have no experience in Arabic. Hes also really understanding about exam times and will give you a break or reschedule with no questions asked. I definitely recommend Sawaie, as long as you can make yourself come to class every day
Very open to spending one-on-one time to address individual difficulties- his sense of humor will keep you on your toes.

Sawaie is the meanest professor at UVA. Even though I got an A in the class, i couldn't wait for the class to be over. He is not approachable and every time I went to see him in his office, I had to wait in front of the door for like 1 minute bc i was so afraid to go in.Anyhow, be prepared bf going to class bc he will call on everyone.

Arabic 102 is WAY harder than 101, but the class follows the same format and with work decent grades arent impossible to come by. Expect to fail the vocab quizzes...he doesnt tell you whats on them. GO TO CLASS and be prepared- he loves to put you on the spot. Time flies in his class. Recommended.

Sawaie is excellent. He's a native Jordanian, but his accent is very slight and he's easy to understand. He does a good job in breaking down Arabic to its basics. Be prepared to work, this is not a slacker's class. If you do, you'll be well rewarded with a solid base in Arabic grammar.
awesome professor, really clarifies everything he teaches. makes himself accessible to students and is very easy to deal with. but the class itself does get difficult later on.
I love this professor, he knows what he's talking about and cares about all of his students.  He also makes a fairly difficult language easy to understand.
No Comments
Sawaie is great, in a class of 80 he cares about each individual's progress

I don't remember the class number, but out of all of my Classics courses, this was by far the most boring.  The classes weren't well prepared and lacked overall direction.  This course sapped all the fun out of Latin/History for me.

Very interesting class. She knows what she's talking about, and she's nice. But, there's a lot of readings. The class is also disorganized. Still, it's a great class to fulfill humanities requirement!
She's interesting and fun.  Even if you've never been exposed to the Classics, she'll make you love it.
Definitly knows her stuff. Probably would be easy if you have any interest in latin, but if you dont you can still manage by just cramming for tests.
She was very intelligent and sweet. Obviously knew what she was talking about and really tried to share her enthusiasm with the students. Take a class with her, especially one in litterature/poetry.
I enjoyed the class. The pace was just right and I thought Prof. Myers did a great job teaching. She definately knows her stuff.

I was so excited to take the Women/Gender class. Turns out Myers is a TERRIBLE teacher. She doesn't like it when people disagree with her in class (but doesn't mind it in your papers). She has absolutely no personality and no sense of humor. I learned absolutely nothing from this class, which is a crying shame.

Wonderful, but you do have to write down everything she says and read it over later in order to get what the lecture was about.  Overall though she is a great teacher and if you need help, she'll always help.

Ms. Myers is no doubt knowledgable, but her classes have no direction.  Were it not for the title of each lecture on the syllabus I would not have known what the topic was.  Many random tangents, and not fun ones.  I found her teaching style very boring.  I will avoid her like the plague in future.

Ugh, I really dislike this course. I hate attending lectures and never do the reading, there's just too much of it. But I hate history overall, so don't let that deter you. I'm still pulling a C+/B- in the class, so it's not like it's a hard course, if you're interested in Greece, it would be good.
Myers says over a score of times every class "we'll talk about this later" but she never does. Her lectures have no modicum of structure. But her class is quite easy with alot of reading.
Class was not hard but required a lot of memorization; Myers is helpful and definitely knows her stuff but she is not overly approachable.
The class has a butt load of reading. But she is humorour at times and very good at giving lectures. I recomment the class because its quite interesting.

She is reasonably nice. She definately knows that she has a PhD and comes off as a little arrogant. She really knows her Latin well, and can answer almost anything about Romans. Feminist- ask her about Roman Women, wears no makeup, keeps hair pulled tight
Professor Douglas is a life changing professor! He helps you open doors you didn't even know existed. He makes you work for the grade but makes it a journey worth taking. 10/10 recommended
Great Class!!
Doug Muir is highly engaging, intelligent, and an excellent lecturer. He works hard for his students and always relates concepts back to his own experiences with the many companies he has built.
Great guy, fair and honest

How does UVA associate themselves with this man. He has lawsuits all over the place. Most all of his businesses have failed. Got an A, but a waste of my tuition. I guess UVA does not do background checks on professors. Sad that I found this info out, after I paid for the class. Look him up on the internet and you will see the facts. He's a con man!

Muir has the respect of the class despite being (more than a bit) arrogant. He's pretty cool and really knows what he's doing. The class was a lot of work for an STS class and structured as one big group project. The upside is if you do the work you will get an A and there were no tests. Worth taking if you are willing to do the work!
Professor Muir is a great lecturer! I learned practical, useful skills that I can use when I start my own business in the future.  Be sure to participate in class.

Muir's lectures have lots of mistakes and his homework assignments are unclear. He grades on participation in an 80 person class and claims that he is going to cold call on people but, he just calls on the same four or five kids every class. His quizzes are easy because they are straight memorizing but we don't learn anything because of that.
The class is easy if you follow the syllabus, but if you want to learn tangible skills you need to take on the book learning by yourself.
Mr. Muir is very honest and applies real world problems/situations when teaching the class. Overall, I'd say he was one of the best professors I had at UVA.

Professor Muir is an excellent teacher, he is extremely helpful and clear. You MUST however attend all clases. Attendance IS mandatory and if you don't participate you will not pass. Overall, great class.

Professor Muir is a serial entrepreneur who will tell you many stories of his experiences as an entrepreneur. The class is very easy if you do the assignments they way he says, and participate in class.
Very cool guy. Fun lectures.
You sort of have to figure out how to take his quizzes/tests and how to do the homework the way he likes it, but you'll never learn more in a class.

Take this class (if you can get in), it fills up super fast for a reason!! He's an awesome professor, and you will NOT regret taking his class. What's more is that he really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. Probably the most qualified person to teach about entrepreneurship on grounds :)
This professor is awesome!!! :) Take this class!!! I learned so much (probably the most interesting class I've taken here yet). He brings his real-world experience into the classroom all the time.

Love this professor! This is definitely a class to take if you're interested in business and startups. He brings his real -world experience to the classroom which is great. Probably one of the best classes I've taken here yet.

IF YOU WANT TO BE AN ENTREPRENEUR OR EVEN AN INTRAPRENEUR(AN ENTREPRENEUR INSIDE A LARGE COMPANY) YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS CLASS. THIS IS A GREAT CLASS TO LEARN HOW TO COME UP WITH A START-UP COMPANY IDEA, RESEARCH IF IT IS A VIABLE IDEA, AND HOW TO PRESENT TO INVESTORS.
Great teacher!

Worked with Doug- very helpful, knowledgable, and readily available when help is needed. Definitely kept it an interesting class and is super engaging. Moderate reading but interesting case studies given. Always brings his real-world experience into the classroom.

Great class, easy grading, and great professor. Professor Muir is an experienced entrepreneur and a great resource to students. Class is always entertaining and he takes student feedback into account and make subsequent changes to the class.
Great lecturer, fair grader
He's one of the few professors that is super knowledgable and also really great at teaching. Would recommend for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content of this class was sooo boring, but professor Brunelle did an outstanding job at teaching it. His grading policy is clear, giving you an extra opportunity to retake two quizzes out of about six at the end of the semester. His name is under the definition of GOAT.

Amazing! Super understanding and a great lecturer. Not only is he smart, but is very good at teaching, which cannot be said for all professors. He cares about his students and is very kind and approachable.

Brunelle has been the best prof I've had in the CS dept so far. His lectures are engaging and he makes complex concepts easy to understand. The class model was a little annoying at times- you are put into a cohort of 5-7 people based on when you can meet 2x a week and you are stuck with them for the entire class. No tests tho which is great.

Very nice. Learned a lot from the professor and the TAs. 40% of the final grade is programming assignments, so you shouldn't worry about the tests as much. Go to labs often so you can get that 10% participation grade. If you have no coding experience, don't worry. As long as you are good at logic and are interested in programming, you'll do fine.
Nathan Brunelle is an angel sent from heaven to teach algorithms

This was the first class Nathan's taught. He's a really great guy. He has a good grasp on the material, his classes are funny and informative, and he's always willing to help you outside of class. He's very zen. Whenever you put in the effort, he's going to make it worth your while.

She is teaching at UMKC now. The quality is bad. There are lots of papers in her class but only fewer grading units, which results in a high proportion of each assignment. Her grading is strict, and she even feels happy when grading low grades.  Meanwhile, she doesn't reply to students' emails in time, and you have to send her once more.

I took her political science course. The lectures were clear and generated good discussion. The exams and papers are easy if you have been paying attention. Make sure you go and talk because participation counts.
This girl is on fire. Best class I've taken at UVA.
Good TA.

Gwen Nally is a fun TA who definitely has passion for the subject matter and does her best to engage students. This being said, she's a surprisingly tough grader when it comes to essays. Attending class is most definitely optional.
Ms. Nally (She likes to be called Gwen!) was great! Her class was really helpful! (I also like the clothes she wears). Sometimes she looked really tired, but her intellect never faded!

Professor Nabi was a great English professor and really gets you thinking and interested in the topic he is teaching. He has so much knowledge of literature and is willing to help anyone. He does require everyone to participate at least once a week and makes you print out so many papers. Overall great teacher.
Fantastic professor who really cares about improving your writing.
Jason is great and he really helps to bring the text to life
good ta. very approachable and clear. talking about beowulf and chaucer sucks but he did cool things like compare canterbury tales to snoop dogg. grades pretty fairly.
great ta!  discussion never sucked.
Jason's amazing. he is the best ta that i have -ever- had. he works so hard for you in the class and really helps out so much. really, really great guy. check him out =).
Pretty cool guy
very light reading, really awesome open-minded guy, a little too easy but he's really good at promoting class discussion
Professor Newton is great, he is very understanding and funny he seems to really care about his students I would definitely recommend him as a professor!

Jesse is a good and interesting lecturer. He uses personal anecdotes to help you understand the philosophical theories, etc. and sometimes gets off-topic, which is charming. He's a bro kind of guy and not what you would normally expect from a philosophy professor, in a good way.
He is hot and interesting. Great class material and fair grading. I recommend this class!

He's a Nazi grader. The material itself is honestly really not hard, but Jesse for whatever reason feels like everyone deserves a B in the class. He's a good, funny guy and everything, but this is like a kindergarten class that I just can't get an A in. Ridiculous... I think he awards one A- per exam, the highest grade he ever gives.

I can't put two ends together with this guy. He himself seems like a good guy,  but his grading is so skewed. I can't figure out what to do to please him. Overall, he's a good guy, but I just can't get it. He makes a 9 AM discussion easy and entertaining, but not the most worthwhile. Getting him is neither good nor bad, but at least funny.

I didn't really understand his lectures because it seemed like he just rambled during class, discussion attendance is mandatory but I honestly learned more in discussion than in class. Overall there isn't a lot of work but there's a lot of memorization. Reading is recommended but not required to do well in the class, just know the general ideas.

TAKE THIS CLASS, EVEN IF YOU ARE NOT A RELIGION MAJOR. This is my favorite class that I've ever taken at UVa, and it's not even close. Nemec is knowledgeable, funny, and you can tell he really wants his students to succeed inside and outside of the classroom. The class is only graded by 3 papers, but as long as you try, you'll be fine.

Professor Nemec is my favorite professor at Kent. I actually looked forward to attending his class. He had super funny, interesting stories that kept me engaged. As long as you did all of your work and tried, it is an easy A.

John Nemec is one of my favorite professors at UVA. I have taken two of his classes, and I would honestly take a third. He is really passionate about the religions he teaches, and he makes class interesting. I highly recommend him, and it was not very challenging of a course.
Lots of reading that I didn't do all of, learned a lot, lectures get off topic a lot but it's mostly fun.

Lectures are strictly verbal, no powerpoint.  You have to come to class and take notes in order to have what you need for the exams.  He does a pretty detailed in-class review before the exams and often hints at things that will be on the test.  You don't need to do the readings but the paper does require use of one of the books.

Prof Nemec is great. Explains the difficult in a simple, easy way. Exams are straightforward and as long as you attend lectures and read the assigned readings, you will get an A. He is repetitive though..

Nemec should get a promotion if that is possible, as long as that still means he is teaching. Easily one of the best lecturers I've ever seen. He has a passion for Hinduism and India in general. He engaged me in a manner that made me want to learn more.
Amazing teacher! I am always interested in going to class and he gives brilliant fluid lectures that easily convey difficult concepts. He is funny and energized. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Hilarious and will make you want to come to lecture, which you should do anyway to not miss reading checks! Interesting and really easy, especially if you are interested in religious studies. TAs were great too. Only complaint was that you need to write fast on the tests to get the essays done. I would definitely take a class with Prof Nemec again.

He is a very funny guy which keeps the lectures interesting. Tests are easy (2 essays, one long and one short, 5 ID's) because he really only asks you to know the main concepts and use the smaller concepts to define the big ones. Theres no reason to get lower than a B!
HOT HOT HOT. Amazing professor: passionate, flexible, great readings, reasonable exams, class is lots of fun.
RELH 209 - Great class with an awesome professor! I absolutely recommend this class to anyone! It will make you wanna take another class with this guy---and he's funny!
