i am obsessed with this man. literally obsessed. he is so nice and flexible and is willing to change books or take any advice needed. meet with him to discuss paper ideas and write a cohesive paper and you will do well in the class, and he is really cool and has sweet stories and wants to tell you all about his life, so take advantage! the man.

Extremely easy. Almost too easy. I kind of felt like he was teaching a bunch of middle schoolers rather than a college class. Pretty entertaining though and made the material a little more accessible than did Groner. still didnt make me feel the need to go to class though...

John is the awesomest thing ever.  He's my academic advisor and I've taken three classes with him so far, and I have to say, he's just the best.  That's all there is to it.  He's the reason I'm a Religious Studies major.

Probably the best professor I will have in college.  He has the ability to make a lecture class of 400 students seem like a discussion with 15.  A bit technologically challenged, which provides a good laugh every now and then, very engaging and definitely knows his stuff.

Makes you want to come to class in order to see what quirky thing he is going to do next. Once said something like this in class, "Hey, I am a pretty cool guy, I watch the Daily Show." And you also learn some of the context for religion in Asia.
I honestly think he's a little overrated--I heard how great he was and am a little disappointed.  But if you want an easy class that's pretty interesting, this is a good one!

Very entertaining and you learn so much, maks you want to go to class. exciting but you also learn so much and hes very clear.He really makes you understand EVERYTHING in the course.Although you may understand everything, the IDs on the tests are hard because you have to include almost everything there is. not too difficult to pull of an A on tests

I'll second everything that everyone else has said - really charismatic, entertaining, and intelligent professor. A fair amount of reading required, but I think you could skim it and do decently. He does tend to repeat himself, but he's cute enough that I forgive him. Having a guest lecturer is the worst part of the class, haha.
I really liked him, but he definitely repeats himself a lot in class which can get boring.  But he is very funny, usually dynamic, and cute.
a lot of reading but he's the hottest thing ever!  take it.
Great professor!  He really knows what he's doing and makes the class fun to be in!  I would recommend taking any of his classes!  This class/teacher made me change my major to relg studies!

I am a religoion major, so I needed his class for my 3rd concentration.  The sections for the class were virtually pointless; however, lectures were fun and interesting due to the way Prof Nemec teaches.  He is active in getting the students engaged, paying attention, and laughing.  His casual nature is veyr approachable.  He definately knew his material and went at the students' needed pace.  Nemec made sure everyone understood the material.
Nemec is probably the best prof I've had to date, obviously has a genuine interest in what he's teaching, and he tells some slick jokes.
I love this class. John's great, and he's funny. Definitely take this class to learn. It won't stress you out.

Professor Nemec is GREAT.  He's young and lively; class was always interesting.  He was a little bit unconventional in his teaching style that some people might not like, but he gave out really detailed study sheets before the finals; they were really helpful.  Definitely take a class from him.

John is a great prof.  He's extremely passionate about the subject and makes it interesting for the class.  His humor makes it more exciting too.  There is a lot of reading but if you do all your work you should be fine.
SO MUCH READING. Took this for my non-western and I really wish I'd taken something else. She is really passionate, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attacks students in front of the class.

This is a good course overall and I highly recommend it for those interested in understanding pre and post independence India/Pakistan. It also gives context and insight into current issues and they history behind them.

This is a great class if you want to get to understand the intricacies of modern India. Prof. Nair is extremely knowledgeable and since she has lived and worked in India, she brings a lot of real-world knowledge into the classroom.

I thought she had a mastery on India and its neighbors. The course gave me amazing perspective of the subcontinent and it has helped me understand the significance of the region and its importance to the world. I will take another course with her soon.
I am enjoying this class and look forward to taking more of Nair's classes in the future.
Recommended for all social science and business majors looking to understand South Asia.
Good overview of the Indian sub-continent's history and politics. Highly recommended.
I enjoyed this course. For a rewarding experience, be prepared to work hard and engage with Prof. Nair.
It is obvious that Professor Nair is a very intelligent woman. However, she seems to be lacking in social skills, and offers no help if students seek it.
An insightful course. Highly recommended for those who want an insight into the modern South Asian sphere.
I enjoyed this class. Prof. Nair has a good understanding of her subject and makes the class interesting. I recommend it.
I would not suggest taking this class without prior knowledge. Need excellent writing skills. Excessive amounts of reading and lectures are difficult to follow.
Outstanding! I learned a lot from this class. I am enlightened.

This class is great if you do the work consistently. The readings are extensive, lecture is crammed with valuable info, and Prof. Nair does expect a lot. It's definitely a challenging course but also the most rewarding. You learn how to be a good college student: don't write everything down on slides, read consistently and be active in class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Seriously she's impossible and doesn't explain anything - she expects so much prior knowledge that it's impossible to do well unless you already know the map of India and most of the concepts she discusses. She's really hard to understand also. I think it was mostly her, rather than the class - material was OK.

A lot of these comments suggest that this class is an easy A, when it no longer is. Neeti has gotten stricter with her grading style, and doesn't realize that in order for the class to do well she needs to stop packing so much material on a single slide and explain concepts in a succinct manner.Only take this class, if your ok with a B or B+
Such a shame, the class not too bad as a lecture, but Prof. Nair shows a severe lack of understanding when it comes to grading. History majors: Avoid this class!
A great Lecturer with great insights.
Great class overall, I learned a lot. Prof Nair has the unique ability of provoking thought and discussion in class. Highly recommended.
Unlike others in her field, Prof. Nair is a great teacher. She makes her class interesting, and takes a lot of effort to explain the concepts. Look forward to more of her classes.
Easy class, but most of all, EXTREMELY intriguing content. She turned this History major from American to definitely focusing on South Asia for the remainder of college.
Great lectures! She makes the material interesting and reiterates key points.

Prof. Nair really knows her stuff! It's fascinating to listen to her recount stories. Don't be intimidated by all of the foreign names, they start to make sense, and she's very helpful at office hours. Her slides are wordy and it can be hard to keep up when taking notes. She will emphasize what's important, so just pay attention and you'll do well.

She is really nice and really knows her stuff, but her lectures are really boring and hard to follow. Each of her slides have either 300 words o a map that is impossible to read, and she doesnt post the slides. The only pluses are she is a pretty easy grader and simple attendence is 15% of the grade, you don't have to pay attention.

She definitely knows her stuff, though at times the she loses the direction of her lectures.  However, she's very nice and really wants the student to understand the Indian subcontinent and will spend extra time in class to make a particular issue clearer.  The online readings can be very dense but she had us read a book on Cricket, which was cool.

Great lecturer who leads small discussions smoothly and energetically. The readings are often dense so class is a perfect opportunity to come, share whatever thoughts you had, on whatever you COULD understand, and to go from there.  Papers and discussion memos are wide open to indepedent analysis, there is no one right answer.  Highly recommended.
Interesting class. Professor Nair is an awesome lecturer; highly worthwhile because she provides some interesting insights.

Was really disappointed because I actually wanted to learn about International Relations that semester. Ended up getting an A, but learned basically nothing. Frequently showed up late and was more concerned with moving colleges than teaching the course.
Nina was a wonderful professor who was extremely helpful. I enjoyed her class. :)

I enjoyed Dr. Barzachka's class as much as I can see myself enjoying Comparative Politics. THe beginning was a little bit rocky, but I got the hang of her accent and her teaching style. She is very open to students' ideas when it comes to how she should lead the class. I have very few complaints about her.

Nina is a great professor. She really knows her stuff about European political parties and is willing to help you as a student however she can. You have to do the readings before class, but participating will be beneficial for your grade. Nina works very hard and she is extremely helpful. User her office hours she will go out of her way to help you
She is very knowledgeable about the subject. Taking her class definitely cleared up a lot!
No Comments

Take someone else if possible. She frequently shows up late to section, is difficult to get in touch with, and is unclear in class. She appears to be very educated in the subject matter but struggles as a teacher.

Prof. Winter is smart, funny, and engaging (in a nerdy professor kind of way) and talks about research in his field a lot. The lectures are sometimes very detailed and sometimes wander. Grades depend a lot on stuff outside of class: a research project worth 50% of your grade and two exams which draw mostly from readings. Hard but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class. You get to delve more into the "art of research papers".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Amazing professor but this class requires a lot of outside hours. You do a semester-long research project which makes up half of your grade, then the midterm and final were surprisingly difficult; they required awfully specific points from the numerous readings from this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great Professor

I really liked professor Winter! I took him the class for Gender and American Politics, and was really surprised with how much I liked the course. There is a LOT of reading, and participation in discussing it was vital to your grade, but he was super accessible if anyone was unclear on a topic. He's also super enthusiastic which made class fun!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Winter is clearly interested and knowledgeable, and even funny in class. However his course lacks a cohesion, and there is little direction overall and within each lecture. The grades are two tests, based entirely on readings (of which there are many), and a research paper. This paper is 20 pages, and you're left to figure everything out yourself.

Exams are ridiculously hard. The average on the exams were usually 65, then he had to add 15 or 20 points for curve. The research project is a pain, but not hard to do. You must go to lecture to take the exams, but they are confusing and boring. He is a good teacher though.

Definitely take his class, he is honestly one of the funniest professors that I have taken at UVA, always full of energy and willing to answer any questions that you may have. Very funny guy, by the way the freaking tests are online.....
Terrible class by far the worst I have taken at UVA
Worst class in UVA. Prof Winter is unable to explain the theories and there is a lot of work load. Don't take the class
Worst Class ever.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! It is clear Winter means well but the readings don't connect to the lecture and then lecture does not connect to discussion. It feels like separate class material and classes. Seems easy because it is so boring but tests are absurdly detailed. My least favorite class by far.
Awesome, clear, engaging.
Another class that is not too difficult if you prepare. A bit to hard for the subject matter. Should be an easy A, but be ready for a B.
Smarmy and arrogant but you'll pass.
Attending lecture isn't mandatory, but in certain cases can be helpful. Amount of reading assigned is fair. As long as you prepare well, the exams and essays are simple and straight-forward.
Awesome
Waste of a class.
Awesome!
This class was pretty interesting and very easy.
He is a very nice professor who is engaging and interesting.  This class was great.

I don't understand the other comments on this page: Winter definitely does not deserve any "1"s... That is outrageous! He is a competent lecturer and clearly gets the point across in class. Lectures are not boring but they aren't the circus either. The readings are a little heavy, but not outrageous. 227 is not an easy class but it is interesting.

One word~ Painful. Winter is a really nice guy, but lectures have absolutely nothing to do with the tests. Discussion could not have been more boring. I got an A, with absolutely minimum effort, but it was def. not worth the time/effort. I don't think i learned anything. Don't take his class.

I thought the class is interesting. the lecture can be very dry (and so you don't have to go...)but I feel that I learned a lot from the class. i disagree that the reading load was too intense, and is often unnecessary because discussion section goes over each reading anyways. I would recommend this class to someone definitely.

Worst experience of my life. Winter, while knowledgeable, has almost no ability at instructing. For a 200-level class the reading load was insane, with more pages/week than my 400-level seminar. All his lectures came across as a works cited page, with no original ideas. Steer clear of this professor, take my word for it.

PLAP227 was the worst experience of my life. Winter, while knowledgeable, has almost no ability at instructing. For a 200-level class the reading load was insane, having more pages/week than my 400-level seminar. All his lectures came across as a works cited page, with no original ideas. Steer clear of this professor, take my word for it.
Coming into this class, you know it's going to be dry. But Winter did a fantastic job making this class EXTREMELY boring. Beware.

I have never seen lecture halls so empty until I took Rubin's class. About 40 people showed up for a 500 person lecture each week, I counted. Pointless lectures, we talked about absolutely nothing. Discussion was super interesting, easy A, but it made me hate media studies.

Granted, I never took Intro to Media Studies with Professor Rubin, but his class about Music & Broadcasting was my favorite class at UVa -- and also the most challenging. Intro just sucks, no matter what prof. Prof. Rubin's very smart and makes the class relevant. There's reading quizzes and frequent assignments, but they're all worthwhile.
Boring Lecturer, seems to just restate material in readings, and not necessarily a good job at it.  Gives interesting material in relation to music and is friendly/approachable.
really nice guy, very helpful, humorous, engaging, classes go by quickly, very accommodating

nick is an  awesome awesome professor... u can score an easy A in his class and he is really helpful....i dunno why ppl wouldnt think he is good ...but if u get a chance take his class u wont regret it!!

Nick Rubin is just a Musicology PhD UVA student.  He's not an actual professor.  He is mostly unable to convey musical principles to his students.  He of course knows his subject well, but he is not articulate enough to show it.  If you decide to take MUSI 131, make sure that you do NOT get Nick Rubin.
No Comments
Dr. Peter Norton is the greatest professor to have lived and taught at the University of Virginia. Taking one semester with him will change your life forever. He deserves full tenure!
He was extremely disrespectful of students and unprofessional in general. I would avoid taking any classes with him.

The worst professor I had. He lowered my grade for "Behavior" when I brought up that this has never happened to me, he mocked me (I have the email) "If neglect of class policies is fine, maybe I'll save myself some time and have no policies. Or grades, for that matterthey're a hassle. Oh yes, I'd get fired. Never mind."
Was extremely rude to me over an assignment and overall left a bad taste in my mouth.  There are lots of STS teachers, so should be easy to find a different one.
Best professor I've had during the Engineering program at UVA. Doesn't force you to think, but motivates you to do so.
One of the best engineering professors in the E-school. Definitely the best STS instructor.
Dr. Norton's class is thought-provoking and informative.

Took him for STS 2500. Loved the class, so took him for STS 4500 (Thesis). He deserves to be teaching in front of a hundred people. His lectures are well prepared, he connects with almost all students, he encourages participation by asking questions that most people have experiences with, and almost no answer you give him can be wrong! Take him.
Dr. Norton is a highly professional and effective instructor.
No Comments
One of the best professors I've ever had. He always keeps my interest in class.
Best STS ever.

The best prof in E-school, ofcourse.  If you want to do well in your thesis, he'd be the one u'd go for.  Many of his students won the best thesis prizes a lot.  This is the one class I never miss, the best discussions happen here.
Best professor I've ever had, and I'm a 4th year. Most professional, intelligent, and well spoken individual I have ever encountered.
Great professor.  Extremely interesting. You don't have to write long papers but the class still requires work.

Arguably best professor in Engr. school (tied w/ David Evans). Very smart, interesting, but expects a LOT. Gives out only a few A's, but his lectures are so interesting and he really encourages asking questions and coming to talk to him outside of class.

Good teacher... knows his material but expectations are a little too high. I had a tough semester so I found it a little hard to cope with his class. But lectures are very interesting and very well put together.
if youre taking tcc 101, take norton. will probably be your favorite class of the semester. he contacts class regularly by email, knows your name, and you will get the grade you earn
You'll love him and his class.  There are a lot to read and grading is tough (hard to get A or B+), but it is an enjoyable class.

Awesome teacher - will make you love his class. Lots of reading though. Sometimes has sarcastic humor, kinda funny. Knows everyone in the class by name, and treats everyone like a professional. Very nice guy, very down to earth.
cool dude
Great teacher, gives interesting lectures, really helps in office hours.
an excellent professor
One of the best professors at UVa.
Excellent teacher. Makes you work and think. Tough to get a B+/A. Gave mostly B's
way too much reading
Great teacher, very cool guy, interesting and funny classes, but lots of reading
No Comments
No Comments
Prof. Norton is the man.  Cool class, very prepared for lectures.
Best TCC professor, period. Genuinely cares. Lectures incredibly worthwhile.

I love Nora. She is my favorite teacher so far. She is engaging and sweet in class and guess what, she is pretty too! It is always so fun to see her make all kinds of cute faces while having her class. But to receive an A, 96 is required. It is not an easy A class. I am so sad my schedule doesn't allow me to take her class next semester! :(
Profesora is awesome! She is extremely nice and always helpful! She responds promptly to emails and even made me consider becoming a spanish major! Definitely take this class (101) with her!
Best professor I ever had.. super helpful. always ready to assist you. Welcoming, not afraid to visit her. I actually learned something and was excited about it. Not to mention she was fine.
My class with Ms. North was enjoyable. As long as you pay attention and do the work, you will do well. She is my favorite.
She is the most awesome teacher!  Her class rocks my world!
Janice is super nice and very helpful. If you do the work and take the class seriously getting an A isn't hard at all.
Ill be honest, I only took his class because he was on Adam Ruins Everything.

Prof Nosek is awesome! My favorite class of first semester. His lectures are engaging and fun. If you read the textbook and actually study you will do well on the exams and end up with a good grade! Take this with nosek!!
This was my favorite class of the semester!! Very engaging and fun. The tests are based on the lectures and focus questions in the book, if you do the reading tests are EASY! So much fun!!

This class was definitely my favorite so far! Prof Nosek managed to keep my attention throughout the entire class. He was hilarious and incorporated relatable, hand-on examples for everything we learned. The exams could be tricky but you can usually get a pretty good grade if you study. Would recommend this class to everyone!!

He is one of my favorite professors at this university.  His classes were engaging and intellectually stimulating.  He is unusually clear and informative - I still refer to his notes even now.  What's more, I had little interest when I started this course; however, I have taken several additional courses and am considering it as a second major.

If you plan to take Psyc101, go with NOSEK! A stellar, down to earth instructor who knows his stuff! He teaches very well. The only thing I wasn't too thrilled about was the amount of material we had to cover per exam. Alot of reading.And the lectures are only supplementary to the text. Must have a solid studying stragegy that works for you.

This was my favorite class this semester!  Nosek is funny and entertaining, and he shows a lot of good video clips to help explain the material.  I looked forward to every lecture, and reading the textbook wasn't even that bad.  The tests are not easy, though.  Make sure you read and study the study guides that the TA's put out.
I loved coming to lecture. Easily the best professor I've had. The focus questions in the reading are VERY important along with examples he gives in lecture. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.
good teacher really funny, he kept our class interesting with his sense of humor. ALWAYS DO THE FOCUS QUESTIONS IN THE BOOK- i went from a 75 in one exam to a 97 in the next because i did them.

AMAZING TEACHER! he actually makes you want to go to lecture...(almost lol). I personally thought the class was easy however, i love psychology too so... u know how that goes. I heard alot of people say it was challenging...but as long as you read the book you should b good. P.S.- i hate reading and i did fine =]
Best teacher I've ever had.  I looked forward to his lectures every week, and although some found his tests annoyingly tricky, studying and reading the textbook certainly pays off. take him!!!!!!
Amazing teacher!!!  You do have to read the text book though.

Prof. Nosek is a great professor. He is hilarious. Going to class is not neccessary because he puts his slides and notes on the slides online. His curve ensures that 60% of class will get atleast a B. Its a great class to take.
Good teacher but the work is very hard. It seems a bit extensive for a 101 class. If you don't like do read don't take his class. I probably wouldn't take the class over if I had the chance.

Engaging lectures and interesting stories. He's a great professor. To do well on the tests, you definitely have to read the book and sometimes the reading can be extensive. But depending on your TAs, they may type up (very good!) class notes, so if you miss a class, you'll be ok on material covered in lecture. A good 1st semester class!

Best professor I've had at UVA. Makes you want to attend lecture everyday. Tests are challenging but not so bad if you read the book. Overall great class! Recommend it to anyone, even if you're not interested in psychology, you will be.
He is a great professor! lecture s are really interesting, but tests can be difficult!

While this class isn't easy, Nosek is one of the best, if not the best professor in the department. Friendly, approachable, and keeps lectures interesting. Highly recommended if you want an interesting class and are willing to work for the grade.
Great class!  Lectures were always interesting and intellectually stimulating.  However, the tests are hard, so read the book, go to class, and study.

Great class, fantastic teacher! Prof. Nosek is wonderful! He does a good job covering the material and makes lecture interesting and engaging. The tests aren't too bad. Just make sure you do the reading and go to class (a lot of the test questions come from lecture.) Very generous grader! Highly recommended class!!!

He is a great professor, very engaging and interesting lecture...however his tests are HARD. They are based on applying the information not just remembering and memorizing. Do the reading and go to class!!!

Incredible teacher!  He teaches you a lot, and you have to read the book, but he always makes it fun and interesting.  He curves so that at least 60% of the class gets a B- or better, so grading is fairly easy.  Don't take him because he is an easy grader--take him because he is clear, fascinating, and very worthwhile!  Lots of real world examples!

Great class! It's the only class that I've ever looked forward to going to in my life. You definitely need to read the textbook but it's not too bad. He uses lots of video clips in lecture and examples to help the class understand the material. Tests are a little bit tough but the class is definitely worth it!
Interesting material and interesting lectures. He's more funny than not and the tests are fair. Overall a great class.

This guy is great. Lectures are interesting and clear, throws jokes in his slides and tests, plays music before class, and gives really good examples to help understand material. The class is a lot of info though, but its worth taking, especially with him.
Nosek is a great professor. If you decide to go to lecture, it is worthwhile and occasionally fun. If you are going to take psych, definitely take it with Nosek.
AMAZING professor! Makes lectures extremely engaging, using a variety of sources (movie clips, ads, etc). You'll never want to miss his class.
The best teacher I've had at UVA so far.  Also the only class I have ever looked forward to going to in my life.

Having taken his class , I knew that I wanted to major in psychology. Professor Nosek, or Brian as he wants students to call him, is like a stand-up comic slash professor. He rewards you if you improve your test scores for all three tests, which greatly motivated me to do well. TAs were great,too.
Great teacher!  He was funny, interesting, and played music before each class.  Slides and notes from each lecture are online.  I highly recommend this class
INTERESTING CLASS! I looked forward to going bc his lectures were so engaging and fascinating.  Highly recommend
Awesome lecturer...makes class fun.  MC tests are not easy, but class is well worth taking.
He is very engaging, but his test do not relate to lecture.  If you are looking for a class that will make you want to take more psychology this is not it.
Professor Nosek explains everything extremely well and allows you ample opportunities for questions as well as many helpful tools for the tests, such as having all the slides online...oooo yeah!!
Nosek's cool.  He's funny, too.  Also, attendance in his class was never an issue.  People always come--he's that good.
The best professor I've had at UVA so far!

His class was definitely very demanding; lots of reading.  His lectures and the text are both crucial for the difficult exams.  But if you keep up with your reading and especially study the lecture material well, you'll do fine.  ...And he isn't that bad to look at ;)

Come to class & READ! and not the night before an exam either. Coming to class isn't hard, he makes it interesting with demonstrations and videos. Makes a lot of jokes. Reading is easy too, book is actually interesting. Don't slack off though, it's easy to do. Hopefully TA's don't suck (mine did).
Good professor, he keeps the lectures entertaining with video clips and experiments.  The tests are pretty hard but with enough reading you should be ok.

Brian Nosek is a great professor. He keeps his classes light-hearted and entertaining. His main points are usually illustrated by video or some sort of engagement by the students. Lectures are much better than the material itself or the book though.

Amazing teacher. Uses great analogies and makes the class as fun as possible. Good amount of reading but not necessary to do well. Lectures are interesting. He's cute and really wants to help you understand. Take this class.

Very cool professor.  Always has a funny anecdote, and tries to keep things light-hearted during class.  Not a hard prof, as long as you go to class and at least skim the readings.  Really sparked my interest in the field.

I never wanted to skip his class. He is young and always has funny relevant anecdotes.  His tests cover a butload of material but if you do the readings your fine.  If your TA's suck then review sessions will be a joke.  He is hot too.
Fun teacher that others havent compared to as far as maintaining interest.  The tests are hard and the review sessions are as good as your TA's.
It was a fun class and the professor was awesome and very helpful. I loved the class..
An extremely helpful and approachable professor! My interest in Pyschology was definitely sparked off by his enthusiasm for the subject.
A fun, funny guy. Easy to pay attention to and not too bad on the eyes either. Class isn't hard at all, I recommend it.

Brian Nosek is awesome! His class is not that hard, and lectures are fun to attend. Lectures are all posted on Toolkit. He played music before each class and really tried to make the lectures entertaining.
Very funny guy. Knows how to appeal to students, even on tests.
Fun lectures with videos, plays music at the beginning of class, really tries to be the cool guy.  Even puts jokes on the tests, which are hard but reflect the textbook and the lectures.

One of the most useful classes I've taken. Great, laid back teacher who encourages clear, thorough arguments instead of the usual formulaic mumbo-jumbo. Definitely improved my writing skills thanks to this class.

One of my least favorite classes. Critical grader if you have any flair in your writing - advised me to dumb down my style to fit the intelligence of my reader: the average person/soccer mom. Narrow-minded

He is a good teacher. Matt's a grad student, we took him out to lunch, he's cool. Makes himself available to his students (will often be found, regardless of appointments, in the Alderman Cafe). He's fun, has a good sense of humor, and makes for an overall good class atmosphere. I definitely recommend this teacher (and the subject is interesting!)
Overall, he's a pretty laid-back instructor. He makes himself available to his students. I'd definitely recommend him. It's a simple, to the point course.
had her for semester at sea and she is AWESOME!!!!!! I wish she taught at my school!!!

Bear in mind, there were three sections of the same class. Prof. Norris could not deviate from what the other sections were doing. Unlike most professors I have ever had, Prof. Norris actually cares that you learn the material. I highly recommend her for Stats or any other course.

Her mood swings are gone, and she is always happy.  Lectures are not perfect, and her notes handouts are just copys of other books, but she does try to make it easyer, and she cares a whole lot more than the other prob and stat professors.  Keep in mind, the amount of material and number of formulas will eat you alive.

A lot of projects where it seems we only apply the most basic of all the statistical concepts we learned, even later on. She's alright at explaining things, but can make mistakes and things get confusing. She's better than average though, but can be moody.
Pretty good!

She's a psycho...we had a lot of time consuming projects that were worthless. Her TA (rob) was just as bad. They cracked horribly corny jokes at the board every day. And...the mood swings still exist...despite the end of the pregnancy.
a very nice person, tho tests were long and the class wasn't too interesting
Hated the material, and sometimes got frustrated with the writing out definitions on the board but overall definitely a good teacher.
Decent and helpful. I hated the content of the course but she made it tolerable.  Mood swings from pregnancy were a little much, but thats over now.
No Comments
Sometimes boring, but a good teacher and very willing to help outside class

O'Brien is an amazing professor with a LOT of knowledge. He's funny, interesting and entertaining.  I learned a lot in this class although it was very difficult.  My TA was awesome too! See if Charles Aaron Flynn is available

O'Brien is a very funny professor who is also very smart. I felt like I learned a lot in this class. It's important to have a good TA for this class, because that affects your grade a good deal. I feel like his class is a good preparation for those who want to enter law school. The final is a ****, the moot court being a lot of fun.

He completely ruined the class for me and has been by far the worst professor I have ever had. The class material is interesting and I would strongly suggest taking it with a professor other than O'Brien.

By far the most pompous, unctuous, name dropping professor whose class I have had the misfortune to take. Lecture material would be interesting if he didnt pepper it with weak and insipd jokes in an attempt to connect with his audience. His was the most painful class I have ever had to sit through.
Great Person, very humorous, keeps class interesting, makes the supreme court easier to understand. Midterm, Paper, and Final, and of the three the midterm is the hardest.

O'Brien is a very funny man.  Lectures are interesting.  He makes the notes available on toolkit which is nice.  There are a LOT of cases, however, so that part is hard.  The moot court is really fun.  TAs would probably make a big difference: make sure you have a good one.  Join a study group and brief the cases.  You should be fine.  Fun class.

Professor O'Brien is highly knowledgable and a gifted lecturer.  He is also funny.  The class covers controversial issues, and O'Brien gets this positively gleeful look in his eyes when he talks about**** and drugs.  He gets the same look when he talks about the impossible-to-finish midterm and the MC questions only one student has got 100% right.
Quite a bit of reading but still a great class.
No Comments

Very interesting and funny guy, passionate and enthusiastic about his material. He talks about the ongoing current events of the Court in class. Cases can be convoluted to read but he breaks them down well. Has a liberal bias but makes light of it and doesn't interfere much with his teaching.

Good class, knows what he's talking about. Has a sense of humor and often cracks up at his own jokes :P. Good class if you're interested in learning more about the political system and different cases. You MUST read.
This is a really fun course for future lawyers. It totally got me hooked on legal issues. O'Brien is the funniest lecturer there is, he always had the class laughing, and he's really smart.

So smart.  Knows it all.  It's like a law school class (I'm in Law School now), so be prepared to read.  BRIEF THE CASES!  Don't treat it like other classes, it's not.  Test's are not easy.  Great TA's.  Moot Court is awesome.  It really mimics law school in a lot of ways.  He is an imminent scholar
No Comments
Very interesting, passionate about law.  Knows a lot of Supreme Court justices.

She is fun and her class is enjoyable and fairly easy but she is very disorganized. There are 5 graded assignments and she doesn't really give any instruction on how to complete them. She doesn't give information in the syllabus for the assignments either. Wonderful woman, loves teaching, very disorganized
Very caring, I loved her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Vanessa Ochs is an amazing woman, and Jewish Weddings is an amazing course.  Opens your mind to different customs, ideologies that you never would have considered.  Challenges you in the best way.  As a professor, Ochs is kind, considerate, and without a doubt, one of the most intelligent people I've ever come across.  Simply fabulous.
She is very intense at times; I enjoyed herfor the most part but her facial expressions are sometimes a little judgemental

Pfister seems like a great guy. But the whole course is ridiculous. THIS PHYSICS IS ALGEBRA BASED; it doesnt say that in 2010 description. Only take this course if you were terrible in calculus class. Trying to solve physics using algebra makes no logical sense and takes 3 times the amount to solve the problem; it feels like eating noodles w/ spoon

He's a nice guy who wants his students to enjoy the class and learn a lot. The problem was, he was teaching quantum mechanics and we spent 12 of the 15 weeks learning everything but that. He set us back a lot and nobody is really prepared to take QM2, which is poor planning by him.
Enjoyed his class, but sometimes it was difficult to follow the lectures. He's a great professor who cares about his students, just a little difficult to follow...

Professor Pfister is a really nice guy, but for the life of me I never have any idea what he's talking about.  The class is super math intensive, and I would not take it without a good grounding in Calculus.  Exams are always way harder than you think they're gonna be.  Go to office hours all the time, but don't worry too much, everyone makes a B-.

You can tell he is really interested in the subject but is very unclear when trying to explain it. Math heavy but I felt like it was never useful when it came to homeworks and tests. Only take the class if you have to.
Very animated and excited about material. Loves demonstrations and experiments in class. Sometimes is a bit uncear in explaining, but makes up for it with his enthusiasm.

The class was math intensive, but I liked that. However, I think he could have done a better job explaining the concepts. Math isn't a bad thing if it's used to complement an intuitive conceptual explanation. My personal qualm with this class was how the exams did NOT reflect the homework's focus.
Really nice guy, but I felt like I had to learn everything from the book. Lectures heavy in math and so I was so busy focused on following the integration that I lost sight of the concepts.
Funny, friendly, creative.

Obviously well versed in sociology. But I would not recommend. I do not understand why he is so condescending to students. Granted this was a personal occurrence with me. Even though he answered my question, he was so stuck up and unnecessarily critical of my question. I'm not an idiot and just trying to do my own job as a student.

I was really enjoying his class until my TA left, and Olick became both my professor and my TA. Very unfortunate. He is a good lecturer but not good at all in small class discussions. Not terribly difficult, he does have a slightly aggressive way of speaking though.

A very wise professor, Olick keeps the class interesting. The lectures are deep, but he makes the material interesting, even though it already is. If you want to be a sociology major, he is just great.

Prof. Olick is very knowledgeable about his subject and shows enthusiasm/passion when talking. He talks a lot though and bases the test on assigned readings. You need to go to discussions, but you need background lecture knowledge too. I found his talks inspiring, but some don't. Going to TA office hours is helpful (they grade the tests).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olick is not the greatest lecturer. He himself is a knowledgeable sociologist. You get a good grade in the class, but his personality is off-putting - too pretentious for my taste. The information itself is interesting. Generally, an average class if you want to put in the effort to read and try to follow his lectures.

Professor Olick is not a good lecturer. The lectures were pretty necessary to do well on the tests, but I dreaded every one of them because they were confusing and he didn't say much of substance. Lectures are very disorganized. The readings were very good (and reading every one is absolutely necessary for the tests).

Olick is the man. I took his intro to soc. Show up to classes and sections, and skim the readings and you'll be on track for an A. His lectures can seem long but he tries to be funny and incorporate stories. He is approachable to help with complex themes. At one point our class gave him a round of applause for speaking so intelligently. Recommended

Olick is a fairly interesting lecturer when he is actually addressing the content of the class... he tends to go off on tangents that have absolutely nothing to do with the topic. He never stays on schedule with the course either. No textbooks, just a few extremely dull jstor(type) articles each week. Overall, it was an extremely easy class.

Olick is very enthusiastic and presents the material in an interesting way. He incorporates real-world examples seamlessly into lectures to help explain concepts and genuinely values student input and discussion. However, he does tend to assign lengthy readings.

As you can tell, he does like to talk.  His lectures generally tend to be somewhat off the cuff and mildly confusing.  But overall he does a good job of emphasizing what he wants you to know, and the simplicity of the tests reflects this.

Like others have mentioned, he likes to talk. He also likes coming to class 5-10 minutes late. Lectures were repetitive. We'd discuss the readings in section and Olick wouldn't mention them until two weeks later. Easy class, but not organized. Midterm, 5-page paper, and a final.
He likes to talk
He likes to talk.  You will realize after that it wasn't really that helpful.

Class was by no means easy but despite receiving a lower grade than I expected, it was still worthwhile.  He doesn't make you buy a textbook or a lot of books, just has you read bits and pieces of the great philosophical and sociological works from .pdf files.  Though the readings could be dense, he clarifies much of it in lecture.

Olick is one of the most intelligent people i've ever met, and he requires his students to read original texts by all the greats, as opposed to just giving you a dumbed down textbook that spells out everything. If you do the readings and take good notes in lectures, youll be fine. His lectures are extremely helpful in explaining the difficult texts
No Comments

Only take seminar or lecture with him. Oishi has no interests in teaching or helping you. You will be supervised by a grad student who also gets minimal support and functions as his PA and he also doesn't know what he seems to be doing. Not nice vibe. Sketchy research practices in the lab. Go somewhere else, this won't help you get in grad school.

Oishi is so funny and nice, but your grade is based only on 3 tests, and they are all multiple choice. Impossible to get an A unless you are only getting 2 questions wrong on each test. He has interesting lectures and they're fun to attend but not worth the hit to your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved Shige so much! He's an amazing lecturer and very funny. The class is pretty straightforward and test material is from the book and the lectures.

Professor Oishi is such a sweet man, hilarious, and interesting. Fascinating class, almost no studying necessary. One 2 page single space paper. Most test questions are from the lectures, but there are a few from the textbook readings that he doesn't cover in lecture (why some reviewers are whining). Skim it the night before a test, easy A.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Material is interesting and the text book wasn't bad at all. Go to lecture ! Prof. Oishi is funny and test material comes straight from it. Skim the chapters before the test/ review your notes and the class is a breeze. There's 1 paper, not hard. Good course overall.

Prof Oishe is an awesome teacher. He made Social Psych really interesting. His lectures are fun and really helpful for the tests.  There are two midterms, a paper, and a final.  The class is easy as long as you come to class and take notes. Reading the book is highly recommended. I decided to major in psych because of this class, def recommend.

Oishi was VERY funny and definately one of my favortie professors. You'll want to go to class because of him and probably should because 25% of test questions come from lecture. You should read the book for the other 75%(only textbook ive ever enjoyed)...3 tests and 1 paper(which was easy) Simply-put: Take the class =)

Oishi is very funny, makes class fun, and is an overall great teacher. He uses electronic voting, video clips, and other media rather often to make class more interesting and it even goes by faster. This class was pretty fun and I would definitely recommend it to anyone!

One of the Best professors!! I don't know what the other people below are talking about. Really passionate about the subject and VERY helpful. Would DEFINITELY take him for a seminar class. Be prepared to discuss a lot in class. He loves what he studies! He's kind and respects everyone opinions unlike a lot of other professors!!!
i love him! he is super cute, and his lectures are interesting. everyone should take psyc 260; it will probably be the best class i ever take.

Don't go into this class thinking it will be an easy A...it's definitely not. HOWEVER, Oishi was easily my favorite professor. He is HILARIOUS, and i can honestly say that i enjoyed going to his lectures and this class was just a req. filler. If you read thoroughly and take good notes, you'll be okay in tests, but some questions are kinda rando.

The subject matter is incredibly interesting and relevant to everyday life. Tests are NOT hard... read the book and go to lecture (oh, the effort!) and you should be good. Oishi is pretty cool, too. He adds humor into his lecture and elaborates on studies by demonstrating with students. I recommend this class for sure!

He's THE WORST!!! It's impossible to get an A. He puts random questions on the exam that having nothing to do with the material or he'll take one random line from the book and ask a question about the way it was worded. He never gives back old exams and makes you come to class because he'll put questions from lectures that aren't in the book. AWFUL
His tests SUCK.  Sends out a study guide but doesn't put everything on it, so the tests can be surprising.

I Love this class! The subject itself is already very interesting. This man is hilarious and always adds a lot a humour to the lectures which makes them even more interesting. The tests are also not too hard. Just make sure you read the book (which is interesting)and take good notes during the lectures because the tests cover material from both.

Prof Oishi is an awesome teacher!  His lectures are stimulating and entertaining. He uses examples and demonstrations to illustrate complex concepts.  The info in this class is applicable to the real world.  Everyone should take this class.. especially with Oishi! Tests aren't bad, either.

He does a good job of using class demonstrations to emphasize previous experiments, or make a point.  Otherwise the class consists of him reading the slide show he made, which generally reflects the reading of the book.  He can be very helfpul in meetings though, and wants you to do well.

Easy class. Slideshows are sometimes difficult to follow, but his random jokes and sense of humor make the class a little more entertaining and worth attending. Read the book, because he does put questions on the exams that are not discussed during lecture.
This has been my favorite psychology class I've taken at UVA. Professor Oishi is very witty and always makes class entertaining

the info was really interesting but professor oshi's presentation of experiment results are not very clear a lot of the time, and a lot of questions on the midterm and final are taken from the experiments he presents in class. other than that, going to lectures is not really necessary, the book is interesting.  the tests were pretty easy, but do th

this class was easy ... a little bit too much work ... to get an A in the class you had to read the book ... go to class ... and go to a review session before the class ... its a lot ... but i was a worthwhile class ... i think everyone in the university should take it ... it is enlightening

nice guy, sort of interesting stuff i guess. one midterm multiple choice, one multiple choice final, three one-page single-spaced papers. plus up to 12 points extra credit out of 350 total points, helps a lot. worth taking but not a great class overall
He speaks and writes tests in broken english, doesn't proofread his powerpoints, and perpetuates incorrect information.

He read straight from the powerpoints so lectures were pointless and kind of boring.  Reading the textbook suffices and attendence is never needed.  The material itself is very intersting but is taught in a not so interesting manner.

His mild accent seems like it would make it difficult to understand, but he speaks and articulates well. He is quite funny in class and rather laid back. Lectures are quite straightforward and comprehensible. Over all pretty good.

Awesome professor! So smart, accommodating, understanding, and a very reasonable grader. She genuinely cares about your learning and is not out to get you. Only downside is that there arent many assignments, so not much wiggle room in terms of the grade. Regardless, take whatever you can with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: An incredibly engaging and well-paced lecturer. Shes a very intelligent and down-to-earth person, willing to help you out however she can. Her knowledge of English literature and its connections to history as well as the modern day are incredible. Definitely take a course with her!
Prof Olwell is so sweet and caring! Participation is relatively important. Gives great feedback on papers and is always open to help outside of class. Just a nice, thoughtful person overall.

Prof Olwell is the best! I loved her class. She's smart, well-spoken, laid back, and an overall really nice person and great teacher. She's very understanding about students having busy schedules and is a pretty easy grader. If you have to take an English class, take it with her!

Her class is relatively easy. However, she just can't teach.  The majority of the class disliked her and wished they could drop it. She completely controls what is articulated, going so far as to totally ignore a student's ideas. She excels at making students feel simpleminded - as evidenced by her omnipresent disdainful stare. Best avoided.

Transnational Texts and Gender--absolutely wonderful class! Readings were interesting and all Prof. Olwell's comments were very insightful. She's engaging and articulate and gives interesting, short papers. One was even creating writing! Youll learn A LOT--take anything with her!

Women and modernity: Some of the texts were tedious, others were very interesting. She teaches a little too much history for me and not enough literature, but in general I enjoyed the class. She's a fair grader, not easy but she knows what she's talking about usually. You may not get an easy A, but a worthwhile course. Definitely recommend.
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Zunz is a great professor, but he speaks very low and it is sometimes hard to understand him. It is important to do the readings and to attend class! When you can hear him, he definitely makes good points about the topic at hand. There is usually no time for questions so much sure that you get all of that in during your discussion. The re
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zunz is a fantastic guy and VERY knowledgable on the topic of a philanthropy. The class was only three essays and the rest participation, so it wasn't very difficult. Keep up with the reading (about two hours a week), and you will be fine. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Don't bother buying the book full of speeches that he assigns. Most can be found online and few readings come from there. Don't buy the other textbook either! Go go class and listen to the lectures. Also, the TA that you get MATTERS! They grade EVERYTHING (papers and exams)! This class may be boring for non-history majors but Zunz is likable.

Sweet guy, but his lectures are the kind that put you to sleep. Nothing is posted anywhere, so you have to go to lectures to get the information. Not too hard if you do most of the reading and listen to lectures.
His french accent is awesome! He is enthusiastic about history. Not a hard class.

The class is interesting but there is too much reading. It is not an easy class at all and even though lectures are not mandatory if you don't go you're pretty much screwed. I would recommend not taking the class if you want an A.
It has been a while since i took his class - and I have tried to forget it.  Easily the worst class I took at UVa. I hope he has changed.

Zunz is a great professor and very interesting. He ties things together very nicely but focuses especially on the broader connections. Very informative class. Very amusing (sometimes hilarious) professor.

His french accent makes it hard to understand him all the time.  However, he is interesting and approaches the history class from interesting angles incorporating themes across the entire class.  Lots of reading each week!!

People think his accent is hard to follow and he's too into himself. I think he's a nice guy with really engaging lectures. There is a lot of reading and a lot of work, but it's really interesting.  Only complaint--we have to print off our course packet--I used 3 ink cartridges for his class alone.
Graduated many years ago -- but he is a blot on my otherwise perfect impression of the University. He is very impressed with himself, and it is NOT justified.

Urban history was a great class, although it focused on Detroit, Zunz's favorite city.  Zunz is an engaging professor, even funny, and lectures were very organized.  Hey, if he forgot his notes, he'd already written several books on the subject.

Zunz is the man. Urban History was a great class, with a bias toward Detroit and the industrial cities. He chooses three or four books, all of which are excellent. He *does* emphasize structural factors with regard to race problems, so conservatives be forewarned.
I really enjoyed this class.  It was very interesting.  A lot of reading though, and the grading is tough.
Zunz is an entertaining lecturer and his French accent makes him even better. A worthwhile class for anyone interested in urban American history.
really good teacher. i really enjoyed this class and found it to be really interesting and relevant. not terribly easy, though. a lot of reading and the grading is pretty tough.

Graduate some time ago, but I found Zunz to be someone who really had an agenda in approaching history.  Seemed to be rather egotistical and did not respond fairly to student comments unless they fit his preconceived notions.  Basically, a pompous boor.
He genuinely cares about the students, though the course material is at times a bit difficult.
His French accent can be difficult, though some people have blown it out of proportion.

Some professors "have it" and other's just don't. professor Olsen does not. He clearly knows his economics, but does not know how to teach it to others. Often times, his students have to spend more time trying to decipher what he is saying than actually learning. He is also rude and interrupts his students when they are trying to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I implore you to not take this class. It was the worst mistake of my academic career. Nothing is taught. If you are looking for a sure nightmare, this is it. People get 6% on the midterm. All high level econ without anything gained. STAY AWAY

One of the best professors in the econ department. The class was engaging, informative, and easy (if you've taken 301). The bulk of the class examines welfare programs through the lens of microeconomic models, so it's a good preparation for upper-level micro electives.

He's a great teacher. Don't expect much of his personality to come through, unless you're following the class closely and pick up on his sly jokes about bureaucrats and politicians. I don't know if I would have survived without micro. You will leave knowing a lot more about welfare in the US and about how to analyze policy in general.

Really awesome professor. I really like him. He is easy to talk to, very helpful and he makes the class a lot more fun and enjoyable with the jokes he tells during class sometimes. If you get the chance to take his class you should take it and hope that he teaches second semester p-chem also.
No Comments

While he might be old, his class was certainly not boring, and he really stimulated studetns to think about readings. Very intelligent(found out he was a mentor to a director/researcher of Human Genome project). yeah the class was easy, but I think USEMs should be that way.

This is the most boring class you will ever take. He's a nice guy but can't keep anyone's interest with his rambling. It amazingly easy though and he doesnt learn names so you don't have to go to class every week. If you can sit through the class, take the easy A.

I took four Arabic classes with ustetha Omima and I can honestly say that she is brilliant, helpful, encouraging and very interesting. I highly recommend this Professor! It will make your Arabic studies engaging, fun and not stressful at all!
Nice and helpful professor, not too much work but you learn a lot.
Awesome instructor- kind and easy grader.  homework every night, but helpful.  take her class!!!
I heart Omima!
No Comments
Omima is super nice and helpful--even for Sawaie lovers, Omima is most often the good cop, which is a plus for discussion.

Prof Omima is really friendly, i think this is her first year as a professor, but she's very good, im taking her class right now, its not too bad, but she assigns hw every class though, she's egyptian, which is a plus (theyre the best!)

Omar had a very intelligent approach to the material. He is helpful and courteous and expects students to be the same. Even though there is a lot of reading involved yet his summaries and notes make the job much easier.. This class, in my opinion, is for those who are willing to challenge their own preconceived notions of current popular issues.

Omer is a REALLY good teacher.  He expects students to do all reading assigned - and it's A LOT of reading.  He's very helpful, especially if you meet with him during office hours.  It seems as though he has a genuine interest in his students and what they think about the course.If you like discussion and challenges, then he's a good choice.
Omer is a cool guy.  He makes you think about very out there concepts. This class has tons of reading!

Omer has a pretty intense style that some people don't like.  He's anal about attendence and participating in the discussion so be prepared to answer some hard questions.  He really pushes you to think hard, but a lot of times he pushes his own opinions in class.  Overall a pretty good TA, he makes sure discussion goes somewhere and isn't wasted.

This guy is really very smart. He obviously loves what he's studying, and he pushes you hard to think about the things that aren't readily apparent.  I found him very approachable and definitely willing to spend time to help me out. I guess his aggressive style isn't everybody's cup of tea though... He's challenging, that's for sure.

This guy is awful. First day of class he says "I have a reputation for being a really hard grader, I like to tear papers apart." That pretty much sums him up. He is one of those TAs who obviously wasn't happy with how he was as an undergrad and proceeds to take it out on his discussion memebers. Avoid him at all costs!!

I had him as a TA and he was not helpful whatsoever.  He expected too much of students and was not approachable.  I asked him to help me on this paper and he didn't help me but just made me feel stupid and accused me of not trying.  If I wasn't trying, then why would I try to see him for help?

Confusing and uses big words. Tries to make people think but does not realize people want to get good grades and thats it - esp for this intro classes! Difficult grader. Never gives a straight answer! At times very frustrating!!!
Often goes off-topic in discussion. Didn't seem like he cared about teaching the class at all. Wasn't very helpful and almost impossible to seek out help if you needed it.

As an international student, I took this class the first semester I was in the U.S. The reading was a lot; at least more than 250 pages a week. But Prof. Onuf really has passion about what he's teaching and he knows a lot!! I enjoyed going to the lectures :)

Great professor, he knows as much as anyone on the subject. His lectures are funny, but the class is really hard. You can do alright without keeping up with the reading but its still a bit overwhelming.
Awesome class, awesome professor. I learned so much in this class. There's a lot of reading, but it's not completely unmanagable if you keep up.

Another history professor who is brilliant and respected in his field and impossible to follow in the classroom. Spent most of lecture declaring what he was intending to do, and then never getting around to it. A lot of reading (upwards of 200 pgs/wk) and an impossible midterm. Not terrible, but not one of my favorites.

What a great class - I transferred in last minute, taking a huge risk.  The midterm was impossible, but I learned so much and he's a brilliant lecturer.  He's going on sabbatical, but take Age of Jefferson with him.  Greatest class I have ever taken.  I was sad when I finished writing the final paper.  Will teach you to appreciate T. Jefferson!

great class with a great and very knowledgeable professor.  sometimes the lectures were a little over my head, but i learned more in this class then i would have ever imagined.  i highly recommend it.

I took a really dull class - American Wests - but I really have to say that Professor Onuf is probably an amazing professor in any other circumstance. There were three professors for the class, and Onuf was the only one that was passionate and interesting
very eccentric and very excited, makes class entertaining, at least. definitely knows what he's talking about.
Eccentric!  The nutty professor!  Hard to follow, but always entertaining.
Great guy.  Brilliant mind.  Funny.  Will go to bat for you.  Overall, the model professor.
This is one of the smartest professors in the business

Opere has been teaching Spanish for a while and is very good at it. She always makes class discussions actually interactive and is very friendly! Grade in this class mostly comes from 3 exams and 3 papers. There is less annoying busy work in 3010 than other classes, although there are readings most days. Gives good essay feedback.

I switched into Alicias class at the beginning of the semester, and I'm glad I did! Alicia is an amazing professor I would take her class again if I could. Beware though do the readings because she does notice if you participate or not. Other than that its a pretty easy class as long as you do the work and pay attention in class.

Good for 330! I've heard other teachers were much harder.  Alicia made the class fun and interesting (though I like literature) and is helpful outside of class.  She has a spanish accent but is easy to understand
she is great !!
Really nice teacher, really easy class.  She's from Spain, so she really can teach you a lot of random but useful spanish.
makes learning spanish really easy.however, she can be really condescending and gets mad when people don't participate in class.

ROUGH CLASS!!  Lots of busy work, and she tears up your grammar like none other.  She is a great teacher though who wants to help.  As a suggestion:  only take a morning class with her if you are a morning person...she doesn't like a lack of participation--AT ALL!!
No Comments

I can see that she cares about her students success but, in my experience she is very unapproachable. Make sure you are extremely clear when asking questions. I had trouble understanding most of the questions she asked. If you should attempt to answer them be prepared to elaborate extensively. She tends to linger in silence should nobody know.
Not too hard. Fair grading. Many opportunities for revision.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was one of my first classes at UVA, she really made an effort so that everyone gets a good grade. If you do the work, you'll get an A. She allowed me to redo one of the assignments, which made a huge difference

Mr. Ortiz is very tough and strict professor, but he is very kind and humble wants to get to know him outside of classroom. This course requires the students to read a lot and use their critical thinking skills, but you will learn all aspects of the culture. He is a great professor even though some of my classmates would make fun of him.

I have Señor Ortiz currently for SPAN 3020. While it is a challenging course, Ortiz is so helpful and absolutely hysterical. He always makes us laugh in class and I can honestly say I'm learning a lot. He will give pop quizzes if he thinks the class is slacking on readings. Besides that, he gives great feedback on essays and is very knowledgable.

This is my first year at UVA and I was scared to take this course. Spanish 1060 is not a joke and you need to bring your MVP game everyday.  Professor Ortiz is not your typical lecturer at all, but, he will go out of his way to make sure you have a solid foundation of the language.  Great teacher and I hope he teaches SPAN2020 next fall.

Not a good class. One third of lecture time is devoted to David Atenborough videos. Boring lectures regurgitate textbook. Very superficial review of animal behavior. Did not really use grading system prescribed by syllabus. In class ?bonus? points are actually included in the class curve, so if you don?t do them it would be very hard to do well.

Not a good class by any standards. One third of lecture time is devoted to videos--mostly the David Atenborough series. The lectures are quite dull and regurgitate the textbook. The class doesn't seem to do more than survey many animals and their behaviors somewhat superficially. Also did not really use the grading system prescribed by syllabus. In

Great class if you are interested in the subject material, animal behavior.  Probably not a good class if you prefer the molecular realm of biology.  Tests are relatively easy if you study, just like any other class.  He gives extra credit just for attending class.  Videos in class every Friday are a nice break, and they can be pretty entertaining.

One of the most uninteresting and worst classes I have ever taken. Makes his tests cryptic for no reason at all. Intentionally tries to trick students. Unhelpful once asked for clarification and he told me to use the glossary. Spends one class period a week watching a video which are extremely boring and not useful to the class at all.
This class was the most fun i have had in a class at uva because of interesting material and a dedicated professor. tests were not too difficult although you have to remember some frivolous details.

Good class, videos on Fridays are definitely nice. Tests are hard and tricky, uses weird jargon and doesn't focus on the main points. Annotate the textbook and don't miss class if you want to try to get an A.
Best class I took all semester. He's genuinely interested in animal behavior and in the success of his students. Don't skip, he gives in-class quizzes almost every day (graded on effort).
Terrible - what he teaches is not on his exams and he expects you to know the most random details.  Also, test questions usually make no sense.
Great professor-  Very funny, knowledgable and excited about the class!  Easily approachable and his classes were very interesting.  Great guy and a great class all around.

The class was awesome, and the professor was very nice and not boring at all.  We watched videos every Friday, which was a nice break, but they did actually teach us something too.  The tests are a little tricky, but not too much.  OVerall, very worthwile.

Prof. Friesen is a great professor.  He really loves the material that he teaches, and he's more than willing to explain things to you during office hours or after class.  The class is interesting and useful if you plan on taking other upper-level bio classes.
No Comments

Friesen is rude, liked embarrassing a student in my class.  He puts you to sleep & his test was unexpected material (too meticulous) - & hard.  He left the country for our test, tested us on material he forgot to post and did nothing (no curve) to fix his mistakes which shows how much he cares!

Professor Overstreet is far and away the kindest, most sincere, dedicated, well connected Professor at UVA. Bottom line is he loves teaching and loves his students. He is the best teacher I've ever had in my life and I am not alone... all of my other classmates agree. Those who noted that his class was useless are worthless and selfish students.
Memorable professor who truly cares and draws on his relevant business and life experience in his teaching.
the best professor I ever had

Whoever said "he is a useless professor" was pretty likely a useless student. Overstreet is one of the best professors at the University of Virginia. And certainly the best connected comm school professor.
Tough curriculum, nice professor.  You have to speak up and drop by often with good questions to get attention/noticed... which helps with your grades... if you're a wall flower, take another class.
He is a useless professor.  Want a good grade?  Suck up.

George is one of the rare professors who truly cares about his students. I can't say enough about him. Your learning is largely self-directed. You have to want it, and you have to give your all. You'll be hard-pressed to find a better mentor at UVA.

Prof. Overstreet is an incredible teacher.  His  class is not easy though.  Anyone who would give him a poor rating is likely a slacker who was too arrogant to work hard.  Find a group of his past students and ask their opinion.
No Comments
If you want a C or worse, by all means take her section.
Stay away from this TA at all costs!
Great TA!  I don't know how she could have done a better job.  She made things very clear to a point where you really had to ignore her to not get the point.  Four stars!
Great TA!  I don't know how she could have done a better job.  She made things very clear to a point where you really had to ignore her to not get the point.  Four stars!

Sure, she's a bit nerdy, but c'mon she studies the history of English mathematics. Her sections had wonderful flows to them, and were very helpful in understanding extremely dry material. She grades harshly, but she's not unfair. I'm sure one day she'll be a good teacher.
Good TA, very enthusiastic and eager to teach. Discerning grader, but not so much that it makes an A impossible. And her incredible nice-ness makes up for high standards.
She was a good TA overall.  She's smart and professional.  Not a hard grader.
Otis is about as helpful as a solar powered flash light.  Do everything you can to avoid this personification of the word "awkward."
boring sections that made me dread the class.

I thought she did an excellent job in putting the primary sources into context.  She was always on topic and I think her section helped me understand the class.  She was also was willing to help if you had any questions regarding the sources or grading.  If you show up and try to participate you will do fine.
Not that good

Enjoyed lecture, but I dreaded her section.  The sections dragged on forever with the same boring group work that every other TA does.  She grades pretty hard and there is really no getting a good grade.  Take another TA.
If you are looking for a good TA, she is not for you.
Keep away.
Kershaw is a great lecturer, but the subject matter is dry and there is a ton of dry reading.  Otis isn't very good and grades really hard.  Take Whitney's section.
I enjoyed Prof. Kershaw and this class, but did not like Jessica.  She is not a very good TA.  I should have taken the other TA's section.
Get another TA.
Not a good Ta.  Her sections are boring but you have to.  She grades really hard too.  Do yourself a favor and get another TA.  Avoid!
Jessica is the absolute worst TA I have ever had.  Her sections drag on and on, and is not helpful.  Also, she far too harshly, with no helpful comments.  AVOID AVOID AVOID!
I LOVE THIS GIRL! She's the best, take Calc 121 with her!
she's great!  very simply put.

Professor Ozment made transitioning into college a very great time. She was always there when I had questions. There is no question that she genuinely cares about the well-being of each of her students. 

My COLA with her was music video analysis, and the content covered in that class was fun and presented in an easy to understand manner. 10/10.
Dr. Ozment was a bright spot during these tough times with Covid. Her J-term class was super interesting and enjoyable. She gave amazing lectures and the class was great.

She put on a great advising course! During COVID, I appreciated her efforts to have us conduct a hybrid learning structure, since it was my only in-person class. She makes the topic very interesting and you definitely learn a lot about music videos!

This was the most fun class I have taken at UVA so far. Dean Ozment is so nice and approachable and you can talk to her about anything. There were quite a few group projects but they were all fun things like making an informercial. We did a lot of field trips and hands on learning in the classroom
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I personally love Prof. Owen and his class. He is a great guy and very approachable in office hours. Unlike others, I found his lectures to be organized and fairly easy to follow; there was definitely a central and fairly obvious theme to each day's class. It is because of this course and Prof. Owen that I decided to major in the field of IR.

Owen is a friendly and approachable professor, but his lectures and especially the Collab readings tend to be dry. Though he is very knowledgeable, often times he will start a new line of thought mid-sentence, which makes him seem scatter-brained. It's not necessary to have perfect attendance in lecture, but always go to section!

I respect him as a scholar, enjoy his writing, and for the most part like the readings assigned.  However, his lectures are hands down the worst. They're disorganized, have no central theme, and contribute little to the course overall. I've gone everyday just to make sure  I wasn't missing anything but 9 weeks in they've proved to be worthless.

so he rambles during lectures.. impossible to take notes during lectures ended up doodling for most of the time. it's still a good class though because it covers a broad range of theories (realism, national values, etc.) interesting stuff. some readings are just WAY TOO LONG.
Owen is an INCREDIBLE professor! I've never had a professor with such clarity and makes a somewhat theoretical subject completely applicable. An absolute must-take class.
Owen's lecture were somewhat interesting. Readings were boring and long. Two tests and 10 page paper so wasn't horrible. Really depends on your TA
not that interesting.
A wide breadth of material is covered in this class. Owen also has the tendency to ramble during lectures. Overall though, a pretty good class.
Take this class! Even if you think you don't have an interest in IR, it's worth it. You learn info relevant to today's events and he's an all-around good guy.

AMAZING!! He is my fave professor thus far!!! I came into this class thinking "this is going to decide whether or not IR is something I want to pursue" - now I'm going to major in it! He is a great lecturer, modest, and very approachable. He has a true passion for IR. He is a great professor and SO nice!

Spare yourself. The lectures are sometimes interesting but often boring and he rambles. Sure he makes jokes but that doesn't help anyone learn IR. TA does all the grading and grades tough but discussion sections can be very helpful.

LOVE HIM! LOVE HIM! LOVE HIM! my favorite professor so far. very smart, humble, funny, and approachable. he's kinda cute too! interesting lectures, make the crowd laugh hard. tries to have direct discussions in classes even though it is big. grade depends on TA. two 1000 words papers, midterm and final. take it and you will love it

nice guy. lectures not the best but didnt put me to sleep either. very clear and concise; assumes no prior IR knowledge. 340 but went over most IR101 material (made it easier for me). grade really depends on TA. readings boring; i did practically none of them (just key quotes for papers) but still got an A-. take home MT, 10 pg. paper, final- take.

Very basic, easy level class, although suprisingly, the readings were quite interesting. Owen is very knowledgeable and tries his best to give students a useful way to interpret world events both in text books and on the news
great lecturer, but the class seemed gearing towards students who know very little about american foreign policy-- too much emphasis on basics, not enough on critical analysis
