Great teacher, awesome lectures, horrible section and boring readings.  If you are interested in politics take the course, he is by far top two in FA professors I've had.  The papers are graded hard, and the TA made the hour a giant waste of time. But it is tolerable considering the lectures are great.

I loved this class.  The readings were very dry and I ended up not reading them (which harmed my grade - learn from my mistake) but I still enjoyed this class.  Prof. Owen is very easy to understand (and "Southern") and the class just seemed to fly by when he lectured.  If you want to take PLIR101, make sure you wait to take it with Prof. Owen!
Well organized and pretty interesting lectures, if you go to the lectures and do the readings, you'll be fine, but the papers were graded hard.

Owen is clear, direct, and Southern, and he holds your attention, and he repeats key phrases. I thought this course was great, subject matter was very interesting (strategic elements of WWI and WWII, globalization, theories of IR, etc.).
interesting lectures and sections are quite helpful. good starter class to take.
Don't listen to people rant about the subject matter being boring! If you like politics, then the class will interest you. If you don't, then it won't.

This class required too much time for a 101.  The readings were soooooo dry I could not TAKE it.  I think lots of people end up just blowing off the TERRIBLE readings, and that's what I ended up doing.
I dont know about him being the GREATEST professor here at UVA, but he's not bad.  Nice guy.  The class is way to hard for a 101 but hey...talk to your TA about that
Talented professor.  Also challenging, but for 101, its the best.
Great teacher, funny person. Take this class
Owen rocks. Nice guy, funny, good lecture, humble, etc. Definitely take 101...best class I've ever took at uva
He knows his stuff but is hampered by mind-numbingly boring subject matter.
No Comments
Owen's one of the better Politics professors, but if your TA sucks it can really sour the experience.
One of the best classes I have taken
No Comments
Mr Owen is the greatest professor at U.Va. Helpful, kind, super intelligent.

Turker is a great teacher. He really knew the material he was teaching. He gives a lot of effort to help us understand the material; he always answers questions after class and in office hours. He promptly replies to e-mails when questions are asked that way. His grading system is so fair. Although he speaks quietly, you can understand him.

Turker Ozsari is one of the best teachers I have had at UVA. His teaching methods are extremely effective and easy to follow, confirming his grasp of the material. He shows genuine interest in both the topics he teaches along with the well-being of his students. Ozsari makes himself exceptionally available to his students, especially by scheduling

Horrible teacher.  I completely disagree with anyone who said he is a great teacher.  He may be smart, but when it comes to explaining how to do things he is awful.  He is a fair grader and gives a lot of partial credit.  If you decide to take his class make sure you sit in front because he talks very quietly and writes very small.
He's a Genius

great teacher, extremely intelligent and determined that everyone in the class will finish this course with the full understanding of the material. always there for his students. thank you, you have made my semester successful!!!

He is seriously the BEST teacher I have ever had at UVa! I had no interest in calculus at all when first entering the course,but his willingness to help and all his bonus opportunities made it worthwhile. And his grading system is awesome! Even if you do not do well on the test, there is still opportunities to make an A or B. HANDS DOWN the best!

turker is the guy who taught me how to bridge the probability, algebraic geometry and representation theory and I got the fields medal two years ago with his amazing help especially in his office hours.

Turker has the fairest grading system I've ever seen in a class.  He also gives lots of incentives to study more and succeed better.  You'll get a lot of bonus point in his class if you give some extra effort, so you'll end up with an A even if your exams are not so good.
Turker is an exceptionally brilliant and amazing guy, have never seen him coming to class with lecture notes, a chalk is enough for him to teach.

I feel very lucky to take calc class from mr. ozsari.  his main contribution was to provide the motivation and intuition behind the material we were learning, so everything made much more sense when i read the material after lectures.  he was also very helpful with infinitely many office hours, i was able to meet with him whenever i had question ma
I did not enjoy this math class at all (and I am capable of truly enjoying math).  I basically ended up teaching myself everything from the book.  His lectures are incoherent.
No Comments
He's a nice guy but his teaching methods are both ineffective and incomprehensible.

The 40 questions in 50 minutes of it all was crazy, I couldn't manage completing it on time without submitting several guesses. I can't understand how the class averages were so good, HAD to be some quizlets involved. I can't articulate what my problem with the content was - the volume, the specificity, the poor lecturing - probably a combo of all.

Lecture and test heavy class (only graded on midterms). Go to the lecture for the content or watch on Zoom (attendance not recorded) but slides on their own aren't enough. My tests were online and open note but timed and I found the questions not straightforward at all. No curve, but Parichy gives credit back for wrongly graded questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty confused by the negative reviews, Dave was very organized and clear with all of his lectures. The class wasn't easy by any means, but as a non-bio major I was able to come away with an A- by keeping detailed notes and rewatching lectures before each exam. Everything you need to know is in lecture and on the slides -don't bother with the book
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only grade is tests. They are open note, 25 questions, and you have 2 hours to take them. Couple questions are straight up unfair. Hence why the averages would be an 80. I rewatched every lecture recording until my notes were a transcript of his lectures and still couldnt get an A. You can do fine with hard work, but getting an A is just luck.

The worst professor I've ever had. Orgo was easier than taking one of his exams. I honestly recommend not taking this class if you can avoid it. I honestly hope they kick him out because his exams were poorly designed and seemed like he made them last minute because he would always have problems with it and email us about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He won't respond to emails. His exams include answer choices that are ambiguous like "some of the above". Some of his questions don't correlate to what he taught in lecture. Doesn't give you anything to study from besides some useless study questions. He'll email you during the exam and tell you there are problems with questions. Honestly the worst

Dr. Parichy is a great lecturer and makes a lot of references to his own research during his lectures. I really enjoyed having him as a professor this semester. He was very detail oriented in lectures and on exams, but studying hard and paying close attention will ensure success!

Parichy is extremely knowledgeable in genetics but his lectures are difficult to follow, and his exams often require specific details from examples in class. The textbook barely followed the course material and was not much help. The study questions he provided as exam prep were not very useful either. Avoid unless your major requires his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Pace teaches limnology, a topic he has a lot of experience and appreciation for. His lectures are very interesting and tests are not made to trick you in anyway. Not a lot of outside work despite a very small project every now and then and studying for the tests. Make sure to study well for the tests as they count a lot for your grade.
Learn a lot in class

This is my third class with Pace (Ecology, Limnology, Ecosystem Ecology). He is an awesome professor! His classes are easy (he posts slides online), but you learn a lot. He is very helpful with projects and papers that are due.

Algorithms courses are difficult, and I have no doubt that Prof. Pettit knows his algorithms. But when he teaches, for some reason, it feels as though he is just reading what he sees on a powerpoint. The reason is that he can spend 15-20 minutes essentially saying once sentence in multiple ways. He'll read out a new concept without explaining, too.
Very Excellent Professor.

Pettit is great. He makes lecture fun and knows how to teach concepts properly. Before this class, I had little-to-no coding experience, and professor Pettit made it very easy to learn Python. Probably my favorite professor out of all the auditorium lecture style classes I've had. Tip: use Office Hours, they're very helpful.

Pettit is an awesome professor. His lectures are fairly entraining, and tend to be fun/funny; he tries to make them at least. 
The class itself was easy for me since I've used computers all my life, despite not knowing how to code before taking the class. Getting an A is really easy, just do the homework and pay attention in lectures.

He was very charismatic and always tried to engage with and make students laugh. The class isn't too bad in terms of content if you actually pay attention and go to lecture/and or refer to the presentations and the online textbook they offer. In-class quizzes were a bit annoying since its on paper and most students just use trial and error to code.

Coming into this class with no coding experience, this class was not too bad. Professor Pettit is a really nice guy and cares about his students. The lectures are all recorded and he uses a token system for late work. The hardest part of this class is the "in class quizzes" that are essentially exams. These are written and can be tricky.

I liked having Pettit as a professor but my only issue was how unclear the PA assignments were. I felt it was mainly an English test rather than a coding assignment, this can be very difficult as a non-native English speaker. Also, the exams were also really difficult.

Professor Petitt did a great job in teaching the first summer session of CS 1110 in a while. I went from not knowing a word of python to building a makeshift game of sorts in the span of 4 weeks. Professor Pettit is very accommodating and he clearly cares about his students and computer science education in general.

CS2110 professors all have different teaching styles and I don't regret taking Prof Pettit's class at all. He is very chill and approachable. I have actually come to like his dry sense of humor. Don't hesitate to come to his office hours if you have questions about the course material or CS in general, he gives great advice!

Professor Perrot is awesome. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you do the assigned work and study for the quizzes, you will get a good grade for sure.  He makes class fun with videos and music and he also will always schedule office hours if you are struggling or want to practice speaking French.

Mathieu is easily one of my favorite profs on grounds; he really cares about his students and often asks about workload and tries to make sure he isn't overwhelming us. Offers review sessions, extra credit, and isn't a stickler about being a few minutes late or needing a little more time to complete an assignment. He made class 5x a week enjoyable!
A fantastic French professor. Easily one of my favorite professor's on grounds

He's really laid back with homework and projects. He also makes himself available after classes or by appointments if you wanna go over certain things. His French accent is great (he's from Paris) and he's also a stickler on pronunciation in a good way. He makes classes fun with personal stories and french videos.

As a first year who took GSVS 4020, I didn't find the class challenging. The whole semester is dependent upon a group project, so be a good team player. Class could get very boring at times, though. Spencer replies fast to emails and if you ask questions about your project, he'll stop everything to help you. He is super sweet and funny!

I enjoyed the class topics and projects. He was attentive to emails and explained things. He did seem to be a harsh grader at times, but overall, he had interesting topics. I particularly wouldn't retake this, but I did appreciate the feedback.
Overall, wouldn't take a class with him again.
Replys fast to emails and is always willing to listen. The class is on the challenging side but very informative. I will be taking future courses with him.

Even if you're a good student and genuinely confused, he'll still give you a passive aggressive response. Extensions aren't a thing either. You could do everything correctly and still not get a good score. It's an interesting class but not worth the hassle.

Professor Trella is an excellent and caring teacher. He is willing to listen to you and answer all of your questions. He is fair with grading assignments and tests. After the tragedy that happened at UVA in November 2022, he emailed the class and let us know that he wanted to listen and help us. He also gave us cookies that Wednesday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This teacher is very helpful.  HIs lecture was fast but not too fast if you use a laptop.  Keeping up with notes should be enough.  It takes studying but you are rewarded for your work.

Professor Trella is one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. He teaches very well and class is so relaxing and chill.  He grades very very generously. I loved it. Take his class, any of them! You'll love him too!

Oh snap! Trella is the man! His class was sometimes the highlight of my day. Fun class, fun and interesting material, very relaxing because of the lecture structure. I highly recommend that everyone take it regardless of your major.

Good lecturer.  Some of the material covered seemed a little flakey (reading Clan of the Cave Bear), but usually the material was very interesting.  Tests and quizes are very fair if you stay up on the reading and go to lecture.  Highly recommend this course.
I loved this class!  Prof. Trella is great and there's not too much reading.  He's a great guy nad the reading is not too difficult.  And, it's really, really interesting.  He's very helpful.

Mr. Trella is sooo nice and really easy to talk to.  He's extremely clear in lecture, and there really isn't that much reading, except for Clan of the Cave Bear which was a really easy read.  And you don't really have to read Darwin.  His tests aren't difficult at all, very fair.  He's great!
Good class, good teacher.  Just keep up with the reading.  If you go to office hours, he's really helpful
No Comments
Trella lacks the ability to connect with students, and gives too much reading. I don't think he's a fair teacher.
this man is an idiot.  a terrible and incompetent teacher.
Mumtaz is not a bad teacher, but her class is both a lot of work and can feel very, very, VERY long. I didn't like this classit made art boring, and it felt dead to me.
Bad, do not recommend
Aggressively bad, unreasonably hard for an art class
Tought and not worth taking unless you are an art major

In the beginning I did not like her a lot. She does not look very easy to approach. However, as time went by, I liked her more and more, and also for her class. She is kinda an introverted person, and if you try to approach her more, you will find she is really helpful, and very very encouraging. I feel I have made so much progress in this semester

She favors abstract technique, and finds interest in parts of your drawings that you might have overlooked. She's made me more confident in my own work and allowed me to expand the narratives within my pieces. Overall great teacher.

I absolutely loved taking Calculus from Jameson. He was incredibly helpful and was always there during his office hours. This was by far my easiest class of the semester and I attribute that to him. Just do all of the homework and prepare for the quizzes and your grade should be fine.

Mr. Graber did an admirable job of teaching Honors Calc 3, considering all that he had to deal with (cough, Sasha). His first few lectures were a drag, but he really shone once he started teaching multivariable calculus. He definitely has the potential to become a fantastic professor; he just needs a few more years of teaching experience.

Mr. Graber is probably the fairest professor that I've ever had. He is very mindful of concerns that students have and is extremely willing to make changes accordingly. His priority is to make students understand the material; he doesn't want grades to be an issue.
Graber is the best! However, (and I know I'm hijacking the post), if Sasha aka Aleksandr is the TA, under no circumstances should you ever take this class.  But Graber is amazing!

Graber is a very fair professor who is clear in his lectures without being too dry and boring. Very likable because he is so nice and willing to help even the most reluctant math student.He also provides ample opportunities for the students to meet with him to work through problems and answer any questions. Great teacher!!!

Geoffrey is prtty much the coolest person. he's adorable, smart & an excellent music teacher,he's very helpful & obviously loves the subject.  i definitely recommend taking his class. however, his quizzes & tests are extremely long for such a short time period,and even if u know the material thoroughly, ur grade gets screwed up b/c of lack of time!
Simply put, I love Geoffrey. He is hilarious, smart, and very able to relate to you. He grades very fairly, he won't put up with your laziness but if you do your work you are perfectly good to go.
Amazing TA!!! He is hilarious, extremely knowledgeable and very interested in what he is teaching.  Down-to-earth and I enjoyed going to discussion.  It was always interesting!

The most insightful and completely kind professor I have ever had. Waldman will encourage you to think in connections and collages, unlike any sort of linear class. He values improvement is over perfection and is always available in his office. An absolutely genius person who sees the best every living thing.

Very wise and inspirational. It is obvious that you are speaking to someone who interprets the world through the lens of an artist. The only assignment was biweekly letters, which you had full control over and prompts were intentionally left open-ended.

No matter how hard I tried, I could not for the life of me understand anything he was saying. His lectures left me perpetually confused. The weekly essays are the majority of the grade, so put your efforts into those, even though the prompts are incomprehensible.

Waldman is confusing at first, because he uses his own language, but he does provide a glossary. I did not understand ARCH 1010 until having a studio with him. I loved him as a studio professor and I love him as a person. All his classes are interesting, and I love talking with him, inside and outside of class.

Waldman is on another level. It takes a while to get used to his language and to stay attentive in class. At first, the class is confusing and difficult but trust the process. Hang on and the class starts to make sense. Waldman is a genius.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor!
He is one of the smartest, most genuine professorsteachers I've had, though his lectures and assignments can be baffling they do push you to learn about yourself and your environment in new ways.
This class is absolutely awful. Do not ever take it it unless you have to! I REPETE DO NOT EVER TAKE IT UNLESS YOU HAVE TO!!!!

Great professor.If you are unsure whether you want to pursue the Architecture major or not, this class may not be for you.Peter compares architecture to paintings and nature and creates genius connections between them.Only those that try to think deeply on his level will understand him.Others that dont try will just think that the class is  useless

DO NOT TAKE LESSONS OF THE LAWN UNLESS YOU HAVE TO FOR ARCHITECTURE. I missed nothing skipping his class and when I did go, he put me to sleep within 5 minutes. He is semi-comprehensible when speaking about buildings, but 3/4 of the time he tries to relate them to entirely unrelated things. A 3-8 pg paper a week. Teaches you to BS like a pro.

Are these UVa kids rating Peter, or maybe Tech transfers? This class is not for E School or Comm School numbnuts, frat boys, or PreMed type a freakshows. This class lays it down for those entering the creative field of architecture. That means it is ambiguous and difficult and self-directed. No motivation and interest = you will struggle, and do poorly. Don't be fooled by the 101 tag - if you want easy see Anthropology 101, with the jocks and rugby folks. Peter seeks to inspire

This class lays it down for those entering the creative field of architecture. That means it is ambiguous and difficult and self-directed. No motivation and interest = you will struggle, and do poorly. Don't be fooled by the 101 tag - if you want easy see Anthropology 101, with the jocks and rugby folks. Peter seeks to inspire

Are these UVa kids rating Peter, or maybe Tech transfers? This class is not for E School or Comm School numbnuts, frat boys, or PreMed type a freakshows. This class lays it down for those entering the creative field of architecture. That means it is ambiguous and difficult and self-directed. No motivation and interest = you will struggle, and do poorly. Don't be fooled by the 101 tag - if you want easy see Anthropology 101, with the jocks and rugby folks. Peter seeks to inspire
The ratings make him look bad. If you really want to explore the mind of an architect, take this class and get ready to write BS papers once a week. So glad i took it.

The man teaches class with his eyes closed half the time but he is a genius. He's out there but you got to respect everything he says, and the TAs are helpful and are the ones grading your weekly papers. I got an A so it's not impossible.

Well,this guy is indeed controversial.But I would say he is a GENIUS!BEST professor I have ever had.In the first few weeks I didn't know what was going on with the class.He seemed to talk nonsense all the time and enjoyed himself.Thanks to my awesome TAs,I survived.Anyway, the stuff he taught you is extremely useful in you career as an architect

This guy is a genius!! He is absolutely dedicated to architecture, and everything about it. He teaches with passion and desire, and and wonder. He will make you think, draw, and build in the most wonderful of ways. a true educator in the largest sense of the word. Outstanding.

This is not the guy to take if you just want to spit back what is needed to pass. He'll pull your brain out, massage it, and then it's up to you to       put it back in. Folks, isn't this the time to expand your view of this world? Go with an open mind and you'll have memories and concepts for a lifetime. I did.
I loved all of his lectures eventhough at times they made no sense at all.  The only thing bad about the class was the weekly papers.

Waldman is absolutely insane. At times this can be fun and at times it can be infuriating. DO NOT take this class unless you are required to. If you are required then make sure to get good TA's becaue they do all the grading and they can translate Waldman's babbles for you.

This class is useless. If you're not in the A-School or plan on transferring, don't torture yourself by taking ARCH 101 with Waldman. This class is terrible and I hope I don't ever have a class with this idiosyncratic man ever again.

Waldman is incomprehensible and his class is the worst. Most of the TA's are excessively anal about grades and their are no exact set of rules to follow or adhere to when writing papers. This class was completely useless and did not increase my interest for architecture. It's a necessary evil to complete the Architecture major.

Waldman is the craziest teacher I have ever had. He babbles on about nothing and has a knack for putting people to sleep. Basically, he talks a lot, but he generally never says anything. In other words, he just talks about much of nothing. It's all about the TAs for this class. Do what they want and you can get a good grade.

Waldman is an interesting professor to say the least.  However, getting a good (set of) TA(s) is crucial--since they do the majority of the grading.  The concepts and ideas that Waldman presents are generally off the wall and seem outrageous.  But later in your ARCH career, you'll be thankful.

The lectures are boring most of the time. But when the topic is interesting, he is a great speaker. Getting a fun/fair TA is crucial. The assignments are hard to understand but the answers are all on that sheet of paper. Having taken the class, I am a much better writer.

At times you will be convinced that Waldman was on something when he wrote the assignments.  USE YOUR TA!  If you have a good TA and you use them to your advantage, then it is possible to get a good grade in the class.  Otherwise you're screwed, unless you magically understand Waldman's (certainly deep) psycho babble.

I love this man! He is a genius and I find the humor in him. He is very random, but that is what makes the class so great! The weekly essays are annoying, but extremly helpful. I love Professor Waldman and this class.

It's been a few years since I took the class...however, when I took the class...I had no clue what was going on!  He would talk about Ken and Barbie...opera and swimming pools...interesting class...  But looking back I realize how helpful the class was to understanding the diagrams you have to produce later in architecture...and it's also and rite

They guy is definately out there, but give him a chance.  Go talk to him in office hours, you will take on an entirely new perspective on his teachings.  Also, do not miss the trip to his home.  It is amazing, this also give you an entirely new outlook on him.
This class was way out there and pretty boring, and the weekly paper could easily be written without attending all of the lectures.  Expectations for papers completely depended on what the TA wanted.

you might find his 101 lectures boring, but you won't realize until later how much the basic writing and diagramming techniques he teaches are useful. don't take it if you aren't interested in architecture.  as a professor, he's much better as a studio critic, where his seemingly non-coherent ramblings actually inspire your design.

Completely discourages all interest in architecture.  Although with only one paper for the class due weekly, it requires little outside work and often this paper can be done without attending lecture, so little time at all.

The guy is very eccentric, and the first few weeks even maybe the first couple months you will be wondering what is going on and whether you should withdraw and go pass/fail, but in the end you can still do fine you just have to step outside your comfort zone, realize most people are sleeping during lecture, and find awesome TAs.

i had no idea what was going on for the first few weeks until i realized that the point is to be as random and out there as possible.. just like waldman. he even teaches with his eyes closed. learn to think outside the box, get a good TA, and you will do fine
Everything depends on your TA. The class itself is strange, the professor is strange, and the lectures are boring.  If you can successfully BS your way through this class you'll come out alrite.
As much as I hated this class and the paper due every week, once you realize you can make any building seem meaningful if you bs enough (which is all lecture seems to be) its a lot more fun!

Ugh. By far my biggest headache of the semester. Waldman is either absolutely insane, or a genius. He usually leans toward insane. The material is interesting, but basically you just have to pray for a good TA.

Waldman's class is very time consuming. Your grade doesn't really vary with how much effort you put into it the work. You will probably get a B. His lectures are crazy and there is no point in going because he rambles on the whole time with his own thoughts. This class is not worth the time if you don't plan on majoring in architecture.

The class starts out hellishly, but calms down once you realize grades are often unrelated to the amount of effort you put into the paper (varies with TAs). The lectures make no sense whatsoever, and the TAs have no clue what's going on. Not easy, not fun. This class is supposed to weed out the men from the boys.
I took this class as an elective and it because of Waldman's enthusiasm, I transferred into the A-school. He is encouraging, helpful, and downright crazy. I love the man.
In the very beginning he was interesting, then he became just weird, but now that the class is over I definately love him.

i really loved this class once i realized that the assignments are more like guidelines... you can really do whatever you want, provided your TAs appreciate creativity. at first i thought the lectures were awful, but i grew to appreciate them once i started paying attention and sketching during them

This guy is crazy and impossible to understand.  He teaches with his eyes closed.  A good tip: show up to class 30 mins late - that's when he actually starts teaching.  The actual material is pretty interesting, but i wouldn't reocmmend taking it unless you have to.
Bring your pillow to class. It'll help
The class takes time to grow on you.

Amazing. You have to be open minded and somewhat creative to appreciate him and you have to give him a chance. The assignments DON'T get boring because you aren't limited to how you can do them. It's up to you to take that extra step. His ambiguity is what makes this even better. Good ta's help.

As much as I complained about this class 1st year, Waldman's an amazing professor who genuinely takes interest in his students. Anyone who says the workload is cumbersome must be a first year or outside the A-school-it's really nothing once you reach second year. Critical thinking is a must.

This is guy is the man, he may ramble, and he may lecture with his eyes closed, but he's awesome. He subtley allows for you to let go and embrace your intuitions. His assignment maybe rather difficult and the work load tough but it is an experience I have not regreted.

Yeah, yeah, they say the man's a genius...whatever. Let me quote him when I say "I had never seen liver above my head before." What does that MEAN!? Well, if you like having your lifelong ambitions being shot down in a cloud of ambiguity, then this is the class for you. (Peter Waldman=Bilbo Baggins)
You have to be a little crazy to like this class, but the man is a genius
I enjoyed the class.

don't take this class unless you have to or if you're insane.  waldman is really ambiguous about what he wants in your work and the assignments are really confusing--but i hear that it is really helpful in the long run (for a-schoolers especially)
It takes quite a long time to understand exactly what he is talking about.  The projects are very repetative and become quite boring by the end of the year.
This is a very unique course, although very rigorous!
this guy is crazy but by the end of the class you will actually appreciate his insanity- i wouldn't recommend this class to those not required to take it, it is not a class to take "just for fun"
No Comments
No Comments

Peter Waldman is spazzy, odd, adorable.  His class is invaluable to seeing arch as more than just drawings and buildings. He connects architecture to real life (literature, philosophy, culture,art and dreams). You will learn about yourself. He is amazing!
This guy's class is worthless.
No Comments
No Comments
Does not communicate well what he wants for assignments, and isn't always receptive to questions from people who are confused. He also is a really tough grader, so good luck with that.
he leans right (politically). difficult course with lots and lots of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Pitman has a wealth of knowledge on the history of U.S public foreign policy and he will impart that knowledge to you.  Assigned readings were always interesting and coherent. He engages the class and encourages an open forum type class lecture.  There were three papers no more than 5 pages long based solely on the readings. Great class.

He is pretty useless. All he does is go over random problems and does not even finish them. He should be teaching us how to do the problem instead. For tests, he only asks 4 questions so if you miss  even one your grade sinks from there.
Pindera is an amazing guy. Class isn't that important to attend, but statics is a great subject. Test questions are right out of the book. Study the homework and you'll do well

Good professor. Clear & concise. As an advisor, he likes to know all your business and isn't afraid to ask you about your personal life, finances, etc. and tell you what he thinks you should do with the rest of your life.
Easy class. Good professor but go to TA office hours.
He's such a good teacher! You learn a lot and he'll make sure you know everything you need to for the exams. Make sure you go to his review sessions they are extremely helpful!
Prof. Pickett was awesome! I was not a big fan of the subject, but he made it fun and interesting. Great lecturer, very enthusiastic, and coursework is not hard at all if you put effort into it.

Howard was an amazing professor. He challenged each student to speak up about the readings, but was never intimidating about it. I loved this class so much I took another just because he was TA-ing. Do the readings, participate, and you'll do fine.
No Comments

Howard is an excellent TA.  His discussions are thought-provoking and stimulating. Make sure that you have read the material before coming to discussion or it won't go over very well. The TAs grade papers on a check scale, and Howard rarely gives check pluses (he's somewhat of a difficult grader).  He's one of the best in the department!

While Calc 2 is a difficult class, Professor Pisano showed great understanding of the material. Most of her lectures are prerecorded to watch before class. If you need help, she has multiple office hours times a week or is an email away. The tests were difficult, and her grading was strict, but she offered some extra credit for iclicker questions.

Prof Pisano is a great professor who is very knowledgeable about the content she teaches. After every exam, I would sit with her one on one to go over the questions. She never made me feel stupid for making a mistake. Attendance boosts grade so go to class and P2L for extra credit!!

I loved taking Calculus with Professor Pisano. She is very fair with grading and makes tests that reflect the material that was taught in class. She is available for students and amazing at explaining tricky problems. She uses video lectures that must be watched before class, and in class time is reserved for completing the worksheet homework.

Professor Pisano proved to be an effective teacher who shows that she cares about the performance of the students in her class. Her method of teaching, at least for our semester, was for students to watch a 30-60 min Panopto video to learn the material before every class and during class, students completed a worksheet. I was able to learn a lot.

Class was just worksheets, lectures were expected to be watched online before class. Homework due once a week, can be very time-consuming if you don't know how to exploit the system. The work itself can be hard but it works in your favor because tests feel easier.
If you are an A+ math student you will enjoy her. If you are not you will consistently feel like the dumbest person on earth. She is very smart and lets you know that you are not consistently.

I would definitely recommend taking APMA Calc 2 with Professor Pisano. She's a tough grader in that she's looking for specific things but she alerts you before hand. The structure of the class was also really nice (pre-recorded lecture outside of class, worksheet in class that you can get checked). Do the worksheets and you'll be fine on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Almost every class with Pisano is just going to breakout rooms and working on a worksheet with your group. Every lecture was watched online, which might be helpful for some. VERY harsh grader (cannot stress this enough) and gave little to no partial credit for anything. Extra credit? Simply a joke in this class

I have had this teacher twice now for two different classes (prob stat and calc 2). She is a smart lady but she makes you feel stupid when you ask her questions. My biggest issue with her is that she gives almost no partial credit on tests which is especially a huge issue with prob stat. Least favorite teacher I've had since coming here. Avoid her

I enjoyed Pisano's math class. I felt that she really does a good job at explaining the material that helped me understand it a lot better than I previously did. The first 30-35 minutes of the class is usually lecture, and the last 15-20 minutes is spent doing a worksheet with a group. Reasonable amount of homework.

Easily one of the best professors I've had at UVa so far. Anytime I've asked a question about a topic she's answered it directly in a way that's easy to understand. If you can get her, TAKE HER COURSE. Seriously, it will make 1110 so much easier.

Professor Pisano is a great teacher and a very kind lady. She really knows her material and her office hours are extremely helpful if you are struggling with a concept. She makes occasional computational mistakes in class but nothing that indicates a lack of understanding. She will go the extra mile for you if you need help!

I loved Professor Pisano. You could tell that she cared whether or not you did well in her class. She had office hours often and was always glad to answer any questions I had. Calc 2 is a tough class but Mrs. Pisano did an amazing job in my opinion. The grading is harsh in all of 1110 not just her section. I had a 3.5% curve at the end.

Pisano is a great teacher. If you DO THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS, you will get an A. I skipped maybe the majority of classes, but kept up with the practice problems and I have an A going into finals (while many are failing). Just do practice, study for quizzes and tests, and don't listen to the kids who don't do practice as they complain about failing.
good teacher
If you review her lecture slides, spend time doing the "optional" homework problems, and do her review sheets, you'll do fine. I definitely recommend Ms. Pisano.

Considering the difficulty of subject matter, she does well.  Not always the clearest in lecture, but is very willing to help in office hours. Go to office hours, do the extra problems, and ALWAYS ask when you aren't clear on something she says.
Possibly my best math professor at UVA, wants you to succeed, material is tricky though but she explains everything well and posts her slides

Professor Pisano was helpful and an excellent teacher. She made Calculus easy to understand and was readily available to help students during office hours. Would definitely recommend taking APMA 111 with her if you get the chance!
Her quizes and exams are not hard. But her way of grading is TOO weird and you just lost a huge amount of points for god knows what reason. Class is clear but boring to death.

Very nice, always willing to help, pretty fair about grades, approachable. Overall, teaches at a reasonable pace, but not always the best at explaining topics. The class is hard with or w/o a good prof, so study alot on your own and DO THE HW and practice problems she gives even though its not mandatory.

APMA 111 is a tough course but i feel Pisano is an excellent teacher, I was scared to take her at first listening to others but I feel I did great. She's helpful in class and office hrs and her hmwk quizes are GREAT compared to other teacher's requiring hmwk..trust me. I suggest you take her, just my personal opinion

It's just like AP Calc BC. Which makes it easy! But I bombed the final and still got a B+. So I guess that's good. She doesn't always know what she's talking about and doesn't always have anwers to your questions, but she's nice. I recommend another teacher if it's your first calc 2 class.
She was a very sweet woman but does not know how to teach and has the lowest test scores of any APMA 111 teacher.  You do not want to have her as a teacher.

She obviously knows what she's doing, but is really not very good at teaching it. She's a very nice woman, but she skips a lot of steps and is often corrected by the class. Its very clear she understands, but does a poor job of making her students understand. All APMA 111 classes take the same exams, her exam scores are the lowest.

I took this class for a refresher after getting a 5 on the BC exam.MISTAKE!She is clueless and I actually come out of class much more confused than I came in. The only thing more astounding than her position as a prof at UVa is her idiotic quirks that end up taking away from class time.(watch as she cleans the board without looking(takes forever))

I used to love math until this class.  I went from an A+ in 121 to a C in 122.  Pisano is a bad teacher.  She cannot teach well and doesn't give enough explanation and practice on main topics and concepts.  I recommend you find another teacher to teach you math.

Ms. Pisano seems like a nice lady, but she is definitely not the best professor at UVa! She tends to make mistakes at the board that can make a huge difference in how you understand what she's explaining (i.e., putting a negative instead of a positive number.) It was not unusual to have everyone in the class sitting and staring blankly at her.

I checked into AA the other day and our counselor told me "Hey aren't you the guy who had a 3.94 GPA at UVA 1st semester"...well after second semester I found myself in AA--pisano ruined my GPA and drove me to alcoholism
No Comments

She come off as though the class will be all right, but she does not explain things clearly, and is unwilling to help you if you don't understand. she will say "do more practice problems". Her only plus side is that she speaks english, unlike other teachers in the math department
She's not bad at all - just pay attention at lecture and do all the practice problems in the book! the practice problems are the key to her tests.
I really like her, but I had pretty crappy math teachers in high school. She makes mistakes on the board but nothing too crucial. I would recommend her class and I love her outfits :)
Makes far too many mistakes on the board. If I hadn't aced Calc 2 in HS I would have done terrible.

Makes many mistakes on the board and gives the overall feeling that she's not quite sure what she's talking about...which you'll later find out to be true.  Most of your learning (if any at all) will take place on your own making the tests difficult
Reviews for her are horrible, but she's not as bad as they say. Certainly not the best professor, but she wont kill you.
Bad
Just say no!
An all-together good teacher.  She is very clear about everything and makes sure the class understands what's going on before moving on.
Never again!
Single handedly drove me out of the e-school!!
GET OUT OF HER CLASS NOW!
My favorite math teacher thus far, very nice and helpful.  The class is confusing because of the material, not the teacher.  I recommend her highly.
Lecture is confusing
I would avoid her at all costs.  She is very unclear and doesn't explain the material well.  Some people in my class could have taught it better than she did.  Bottom line: she's no good.
Good teacher for APMA212.  She explains things well and genuinely trys to help you succeed in her class.  She is one of the better college math teachers I've had.
No teaching ability, period.
She doesn't seem to want to help in help sessions.  Confusing lectures common as smelly feet.
Worst math teacher I've ever had.  Her lectures are incredibly confusing, and her tests are hard.  Sometimes she even gets confused and puts up incorrect notes.
Our TA knows more, and she's hotter too.

My classmates complain about how terrible she is, but she is not too bad. The tests are very hard, starting with a weed-out test early on of HS cacl topics. Office hours are very helpful, she will explain everything to you. At times I feel lost in lecture
maybe next semester i will find a good math teacher
Possibly the worst teacher that I have ever had. The way that she teaches has repeatedly screwed me over. I am currently failing the class and I am convinced that it is her fault.
Just not a good math teacher. Would be better suited to industry or something.

Nice person...I'm not a bad person at math, and I often walk away from classes more confused than ever. Most of the class is failing the tests. She OFTEN makes mistakes, i.e. writing incorrect formulas or doing bad graphs...also runs over time a lot.

Pilar is an amazing professor. I had her for a class at UVA (3020) and then again in Spain. At first I was intimidated by her because she cold calls a lot. But she appreciates questions and makes an effort to make things as clear as possible. She also gives great feedback in office hours.  Any Spanish major should take her classes!

She goes way too hard on students with more experience.  It is like she tries to show you that you will never speak as well as her.  Accent gets in the way.  However if you look past that, you will actually enjoy the class.

I had her while studying in Spain. She was extremely intimidating at first, I wanted to drop the class, but by the end of the semester she had come to be one of my favorites. She's authoritative, but also helpful and relatable. Don't take her unless you have a strong interest in learning Spanish. I'd highly recommend her!
so help you god
He is cool

The lectures are just a bunch of pictures from his trips and little is actually on the quizzes. He doesn't let anyone use phones or laptops, and he doesn't upload grades. If you get a question partially right, he won't give partial credit if you're not a favorite. He makes you buy his boring textbook and is the most boring professor I have had.

Friendliest professor I have ever had. Brought candy for class on several occasions. Made the subject (archaeology of American southwest) very, very interesting as well. Tests can be a little tricky, but they are graded fairly and are generally not too difficult.
wonderful Professor. He is very knowledgeable and as a result you  learn a lot from him

Wonderful Professor.  You can go into class not knowing or caring about archaeology and leave wanting to do it forever!  You may feel lost at times but in the end you will be amazed at how much you've learned.  Professor Plog is also very approachable so you shouldn't have any problems.

He doesn't give back assignments in a timely manner-you have no idea what you grade is.Did not inform you if you got to take the final exam as take home until a week before it was scheduled- too bad if you had other obligations!watched too many movies. Repeats himself and does not spend enough time on new material that we will actually be tested on
lectures can be monotonous, but the prof. loves the topic and it shows.. projects and tests pretty easy, and the material is interesting.. go to class and you're set

Was intimidating in a small class environment.  Learned a lot, but was totally stressed and spent ridiculous hours studying for class and still felt unprepared.  Most stressful/benificial class at UVA.
great teacher. keeps things interesting. tests and projects pretty straight forward. cares about his students and always in a good mood.
Great Teacher
Good lecturer, makes expectations clear.

Professor Potter is great, she is a great resource and very approachable. However, I would not take her again. Some political science professors are obsessed with having students write research papers like an eng lit class, she is one of them. Having us do actual research and presentations is what I signed up to do- not write literature reviews.

lectures are clear and organized, so are the readings. quiz before every class is overkill. everything is graded by the TAs who all have different guidelines. spent way more time decoding what the TAs wanted from the exams than I did going to lecture or reading. TAs handed out bad grades when there was obvious confusion and poor expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a smart guy but often says incorrect "facts". He made a few ignorant/rude comments and for that reason I wasn't crazy about the professor. I liked the class because of the readings he chose and the way the discussion was set up but i would recommend turning the final paper in early to have him look over it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great guy who really cares about the intellectual well beings of his students but he's a HARD paper grader. Class consisted of 2 reading exams, a class presentation & 2 paper 8-10 pages. He encourages class discussion & gives good feedback through out. He does however tally the times each person speaks each class so beware if you dont like to talk.

Portmann taught this religious studies major seminar on Ritual. Great guy, very nice and understanding. Encourages GREAT discussion in class. Readings are interesting. His classes normally consist of 3 small reading exams, a presentation on one of the readings, and a final 15 page paper. Great class. I'd encourage students to take anything by him.
Intelligent professor, very approachable.  Class structure is a bit different with 50% of your grade coming from the final exam.  No term paper.
John Portmann = awesome.  He is a great guy - the goal of the class is to form your own opinion, not to regurgitate material.  class is interesting, thought provoking, discussion driven - I LOVED IT.

Awesome guy!  He really cares about his students.  His classes are open discussions.  He values everyone's opnion, and wants to make discussions interesting.  Most of the readings are very enjoyable as well.
He is very kind and good at engaging the material. Encourages class discussion and offers interesting insight into the matters discussed in class. Very approachable.

this class was amazing.  discussions were fantastic (portmann is unbiased and very skilled at discussion facilitating), the reading load was heavy but always interesting, and portmann is a kind guy, too.  for me the only downside was coming out of the class painfully critical of how i think about things.

This class was wonderful. Portmann is a great professor. He is very approachable and seems to really care about his students. He assigned a lot of reading, but none of it was too difficult and the discussions were great. If you're looking for a course with lots of fun discussions that generates interesting ideas, take a class with Portmann!
I REALLY enjoyed this class.  Prof. Portmann makes the class really interesting.  Not too much work.  Highly recommended :)

Professor Portmann is very popular: he's funny, the reading is easy(ocassionaly long, but on a 10th grade level at most), and he lets the students do the talking. If you wanta professor who focuses on "actual religion" rather than "popular religion", then take another. If you want an A for talking about who's on the cover of People, take this one.
The best professor I've had at UVA. Great at facilitating discussion. He makes sure to guide the conversation but makes sure the students do most of the talking.
Super easy class. You learn about issues in K-12 education and you hardly have homework
Awesome prof . Was very understanding. Papers were interesting.

Mr. Plaskon  is such an amazing teacher that actually cares about his students. It's the only class that I enjoy going to yet it's the one that makes me think the most. I'm taking one of his class again without a doubt.

Prof. Plaskon is one of the most engaging teachers I've ever had. His class is based on participation. There are a lot of handouts and a lot of grades, but it's easy as long as you pay attention and show up to class. I had a lot of  fun in this class, and in the field experience that went along with it. Good intro to teaching as a profession!

This class was very easy. If you turn your stuff in, then you're good. The deadlines for assignments are not strictly enforced ever. I love Professor Plaskon, but he wastes a lot of time. I didn't learn much about anything.
He is the BEST! Took his course over the summer and I LOVED IT! He made me want to come to school. He really does enjoy teaching and it a WONDERFUL teacher! TAKE HIS CLASS!!! You won't regret it!
Professor Plaskon has some awesome bow ties and raises miniature horses.  He loves a good lunch at the Biltmore Grill.  I heard he was an extra in the movie Bruce Almighty.
Professor Plaskon is extremely passionate about the teaching profession. Very energetic and encouraging.
Great professor.

Great guy.  Took this class over the summer, when everything is a bit more relaxed.  He bought bagels for the class everyday, had all of our names memorized within two classes, and actually taught well.  Even though the material seems stacked against him, I came out of this class really looking forward to teaching.
Nicest guy ever. Essentially no work. Everyone in the class got an A or A-.
Most AMAZING professor EVER!!!  So nice, and so enthused.  Really wants us to succeed.  FAVORITE professor thus far.
His enthusiasm and kindness make you want to succeed. He is wonderful!
he is soooo loveable because he's really enthusiastic, easy-going, and understanding.  and yes, this class was really easy (but pretty interesting as well).
Such a nice guy!! He took the time to learn everyone's name by the 2nd class and he just really cares about the students.  The class was insanely easy, hardly any work at all.

I loved him!! He's so happy and energetic! this class was 3 hours long and it seemed to fly by. He included lots of terrible jokes, anecdotes and media that made the class really enjoyable. Hes also really nice and caring and is definitely willing to help his students.He wants everyone to do get an
No Comments
Sweetest man ever, I loved his class.  He tells terrible jokes and I loved it!
I want to marry this man's son so I can be part of his family. I love him.
So nice and so easy; no real tests or hard assignments; it's really just about introducing you to teaching- what it's supposed to be about
Incredibly energetic and caring man.  Enriching discussions and free Corne lunch

This class is absolutely fantastic and was my favorite course this semester!!! Prof. Pompano is wonderful and does a fantastic job in relating real-world scenarios through her inquiry labs. The TA's can be hit or miss, but you won't do badly if yours isn't great because the grading is standardized for all TA's. To succeed: KNOW THE ACS GUIDELINES!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Lab reports are entirely too picky, and they treat you as if you know nothing, as any facts inputted into lab report HAS to be backed by a source.  Grade depends on TA.

Before you even write your first lab report for lab, go to her office hours; Prof. Pompano is really nice and wants to help, and going to her will save your ass for the rest of the semester. Go to lecture for occasional in-class assignments. Pre-lab and report rubrics are impossible to predict and lab requires actual work. Grades depend on your TA.

It is good to have classes with people from other countries. This is what opens our minds and help us learn about the world. The experiences of South American immigrant refugees are interesting and let us see what they go through in their adoptive environment.
I would not take this prof. again because I feel that I am diminished every time I raise a question in class or outside class. I am not impressed with his publications.
He is not respected, he is not inspirational or funny.  He thinks he is above everyone else in the department, and he thoroughly enjoys the benefits of nepotism.

Prof. Pope is intelligent, however he does not appreciate conveniently the neither intelligence of his students nor their intellectual perspectives on the topics commented. He seems kind, open minded, democratic, but do not believe such appearance. He will not tell you that he does not agree with you, he will simply grade you below your merits.

Professor Pope expects greatness because he wants his students to be strong enough to succeed as competent writers and thinkers. Some students are used to constant codling from professors, but Pope is the kind who will be honest about what is wrong with your work. Wouldn't you rather know? Improved my writing tremendously.

Professor Pope pretends to be a chill and kindly professor. However, do not be fooled. He has a nasty little streak. He seems a little burned out and maybe should consider retiring. He likes to tell students that their work is "poorly written." What type of constructive feedback is that?

Pope is one of those who pretends to care for students making everything easier than it is supposed to be. He is tired of teaching the same stuff for years and has become an entertainer of sorts. Should be on his way out.

Pope is a GREAT professor. Go to his office hours! He cares about improving your written and spoken Spanish and is really interesting. Keeping up with the reading is a must. Small group discussions, daily homework, and a midterm and final.

Professor Pope, unlike many of the Spanish faculty, truly cares about his students. He's Chilean, so his accent is really easy to understand. Pope tries to shake up his classes, so its never boring (he loves small group discussions). He's a really easy grader, which is also nice. Overall, just a great guy

Interesting speaker and lenient grader.  Lots of reading, short weekly responses, final paper and presentation.  Invited the class over for dinner.  Genuinely cares for his students and an overall kind person.

prof. pope is adorable and the who am i? usem was one of my fav classes. medium reading, about 30-50 pgs per week (easy reading though) and 2 written pgs of reponse but they are easy and fun. he is sweet and even had us over to his home for dinner! easy A if you just do the papers--they are just your opinions and not hard.

He ROCKS! Michael is easily my favorite TA I have ever had. You have to do the work and participate in discussion but he makes you want to. He loves what he's talking about and explains topics you don't understand in a really easy way. Plus he's funny and super interesting. HE IS THE BEST

The epitome of passionate; this professor is well spoken, energetic and intelligent. His discussions are stimulating so make sure you read the material! Clever and kind- I'd definitely suggest his course!
Great teacher. Clear, always answers questions and makes sure you got it. Fair grader. Cherry on top: he's really handsome.
He's basically THE BOSS. be sure to do the readings and take notes in order to participate in discussion. fair grader. has a sense of humor which is a plus.
very well

Let's face it, physics isn't the most exhillarating class, but PQ does his best to get people excited about it.  Really nice professor.  His class isn't that hard if you just do lots of practice problems (then it comes naturally).

I took physics201 and 202 only because I had to and I used to hate physics. However, I took his class for both semesters and I did quite well. His lectures were not the best and you had to study hard on your own. Go to his office hour. His a very nice professor and is willing to help his students.
Funny, but not helpful when it comes to learning the material.
hes sweet

Didn't get back to me on any of the questions I had on homework until it was already handed in...never understood my questions when I asked him in person... offered no help other than to work more problems out of the book when I was having problems even working the easy ones.
No Comments
Enthusiastic but not a good lecturer.
Means well but a very poor lecturer.
No Comments

Took this for a science Gen ED because everyone said it was easy. I think he saw this and changed the grading scale so that an A starts at a 95 which is absurd. This class was super time-consuming with tons of homework and labs. Exam averages were all 75%. Office hours not helpful and this guy can be a pretty harsh grader. Interesting Class Tho.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This guy is brutal in a way where he assumes everyone is guilty of cheating until proven innocent. He was previously known as an "easy A" class and was loose and fun, but suddenly turned to trying to trick people into cheating. Do NOT recommend this course unless you love the sky and solar system. Class is interesting, but professor, no thanks.

Note: I took ASTR 1230 (was not an option for post) 

One of the best professors I've had so far. Passionate and wanted us to love astronomy. Assignments included  labs, online quizzes and in-class lecture questions. Fairly graded. Most memorable part of the class was how he made a point to emphasize the beauty and humanity in studying astronomy.

It's a good introduction to astronomy. However, the professor tends to overcomplicate simple concepts. Going to office hours wasn't much help either. There also concern over the professor's professional demeanor towards students. Would not recommend taking with this professor - maybe try a different one.

Prof. Pryal is incredibly enthusiastic about the course and astronomy. He sets clear expectations about assignments that are completely doable if you put in the effort. He is still learning how to improve, but that just means he is very receptive to feedback. Exams are open book, but still pay attention in lecture or you might run out of time.
Awesome dude take his classes.

Lots of things to do, but they're fairly simple and making a good grade in the class overall only requires effort. There are 3 labs, 3-4 tests, and a group project at the end of the class. The rest of the grade is easy participation. Matthew really has a love for astronomy, and that makes his classes much more entertaining and engaging.

Adored him. Never stressed about his class- just enjoyed it. Pryal is passionate about his subject and it shows. He's a great lecturer, and he really cares about his students. He gives lots of extra credit opportunities. Quizzes are open-note and not bad at all. The participation grade was lovely (and easy). Lectures are filmed and put on Collab.

The most frustrating, opaquely worded quizzes and tests I've ever had from any professor.

NOTE: Course code says ASTR1220, but actual class taken was ASTR1270
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Pryal was new, so he was always looking for student feedback. I would recommend to attend class and read the textbook (although both are technically avoidable), but even if you're like me and don't excel at tests there were plenty of classwork and homework opportunities. Astronomy wasn't as easy as I was told, I did math! Still good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Pryal is a young professor, but you can tell he really loves what he teaches and genuinely wants his students to do well. While the tests were decently hard, he offers review sessions and the homework and lab scores make up for any bad scores you might get. It's easy to get an A or a B as long as you go to class and try on the assignments.
quizzes are hard but u can make up for it with labs and hw and participation, i had a 85 average on quizzes but still ended with an A, overall really interesting material

Professor Pryal is someone who you can tell cares about what he is teaching. He is new which makes him care more about his performance. His lectures are very helpful and so are the homework assignments. Definitely recommend taking his class!

Given he is a new professor, I would say he has a way to go in teaching technique. He was not very helpful for me personally in office hours nor did he have much engagement with his students. My personal experience was quite negative but a good grade is certainly achievable in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love this class

Propp was an amazing sign language professor who was very patient and understanding; however, he was very strict when grading (but gave a lot of feedback). The test were usually pretty tough and weighed a lot on your grade. Overall, he was a great professor and was helpful during the Covid times.

Propp is a good professor but he is a very tough grader and gives some feedback. During the Covid era he has been easy to work with but it is a lot of work outside of class. He signed a little fast when we first started, which was a little difficult to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Greg has been so fun! So nice, clear about what he expects, and assignments are interesting but definitely challenging. Fast paced class, quizzes somewhat often, lots of info. Really encouraging, fun activities, helps you absorb the language simply. Online but made it work so well! SAVs and LL's are frequent but simple if you study and watch videos
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Greg is an awesome professor. All of the comments say that he signs too fast, I thought it was manageable. The voice-off policy starts to feel natural after a while. You don't just learn about the language; you also learn about Deaf culture, which is very interesting. I highly recommend this class, but I also recommend the ASL Program in general.

I took ASL in high school, but didn't test out, so the class is pretty easy for me.  But beware, the tests are hard even for experienced signers.  He signs really fast and doesn't repeat.  Not too much homework.  Don't be intimidated by the voice off thing, he's really good at explaining things.  Go to some of the Deaf events, he'll like you more.

Greg is an absolutely AWESOME professor..one of the best I've ever had. He has a great sense of humor, which makes class fun. There is a "voice off" policy..but don't let it scare you. He explains everything as long as you raise your hand. Tests can be tricky, but they aren't bad if you prepare! I highly recommend Greg and this class!
He is a hard professor to work with especially with the finger spelling and the quizzes. I strongly suggest looking for someone else.

He's a good teacher. Class time is cool,it's about the same for all ASL teachers. The biggest difference: TESTS. His are too fast and he makes it HARD to get an A on a test. If you aren't good at ASL,it's harder.

Great professor! The class is hard, but he is willing to help you as much as he can. You will have plenty of homework though he doesn't check it. I would recommend him over the others, his finger-spelling may be quicker than Roco's but the fact that he can talk to you after class makes up for it.

I had Greg for 101 and 102 and I think he's a great teacher. I've heard he's better than Rocco, but not as good at CK. I would take him again though because I thought he graded fairly and he was willing to help all of his students
She is amazing. Would take again.

In a world of inclusion, this, the only special education course for mainstream teachers, should invalidate the so called quality of teacher prep at UVA. You watch whole movies where clips would do, discuss them on a superficial level, occasionally listen to textbook summary powerpoints, and get out early. Grading criteria doesn't ensure learning!

Even though the course claimed to apply to secondary and primary levels, she focused only on primary. Strategies and activities would never work with high school students! Spent bulk of class sessions on her own reading model, instead of exploring a variety in depth. Totally self-serving. Dull lecturer, and doesn't seem to care about students.
The TAs do most of the teaching. She doesn't seem to be interested in the class.

I thought she was sweet. Her lectures aren't thrilling, but I really enjoyed the material. Pullen isn't the best in Curry but I didn't find her as bad as these other raters did. I would take the class again.
Was hard to get in touch with in between classes, and didn't seem to care much about the class.
She knows her stuff and teaches in a clear way with material you can use.  Treats students with respect, will do anything she can to help you learn and do well with the material.
No Comments
Decent researcher, horrible teacher. Very disappointed considering she's teaching future educators. Very rude.
Great class
Very good at giving back feedback. There is quite a bit of reading and listening to do for the class. You write about 4 paragraphs a week. Great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the most brilliant theorists I have ever known.  The content is very difficult, though the grading scheme is very affirming.  The meat of the course was focused on the Mozart piano sonatas, which was pretty cool.  No exams (thank God), just homework (70%) and a final project (30%).
Very enthusiastic and helpful.
Brilliant, interesting teacher with a unique sense of humor. I highly recommend taking any of his classes.
Great guy, good lecturer, very enthusiastic and funny in his own way. Take theory with him!
Hilarious, very intelligent. Definitely knows what he's talking about, but be warned that some of what he says might go over some people's heads.
No Comments
Puri is a great prof and really hilarious.  An excellent new addition to the music deptartment.

Her lectures relied heavily on the readings, and her lecture slides are pretty ambiguous without context, so if you join late or miss a lecture, you're gonna need to borrow notes, especially since she does not provide the lecture slides for studying/reviewing purposes. The only assignments are essays and participation in your TA discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pugh is a big lecturer and loves to assign readings. My advice is do the reading before class and take notes so you're ready for the lecture. It makes a lot more sense this way. You will probably interact with your TA much more than Professor Pugh but the class is interesting and not too intense. It helps if this subject interests you.

Professor Pugh seems to love her sociology, but her setup of the course was questionable. The required readings consisted of her own book as well as her friends' books from graduate school. Had daily iClicker questions and flies through her powerpoint slides. She assigned 5 papers on the weekly (long) readings, a 6-page essay, and an 8-page essay.
Be prepared to read full books and participate a lot.  Her grading is tough and the assignments can be kind of confusing.

This course has been changed extremely from how Pugh used to teach it in the past. There are 19 i-clicker quizzes given in lecture so there is basically a quiz 75% of the time. You actually have to do the reading and read it well to get a decent grade on the quizzes and frequently i would read thoroughly and do poorly.

She is very interactive during lectures, and likes to check what you're doing on your computer, but she really just wants people to participate and doesn't mind a different opinion if you can back it up

She's a pretty average professor. She wasn't always clear and changed the syllabus at times, but it's challenging to teach on Semester at Sea. Her quizzes can be challenging, but if you do the readings, you'll be okay.
Pugh really cared about her students, loved this class and would recommend

Opens her lectures w/ lots of (unnecessary) statistics, but she makes sure to pinpoint the main ideas/arguments of the EXTENSIVE readings. Uses clickers to monitor attendance. Gives exam ?s prior to exam where you can use notes and Internet to prepare. Great readings.  Take-home final that's pretty fair--you can use your notes, too! Skim read

Pugh is so unengaging. The material isn't hard, but she makes things unnecessarily complicated, and often contradicts herself.  The course itself was interesting, just wish I hadn't had to do it with her.

Prof Pugh is not boring but also not that engaging. Her lectures often reiterate what you have already read. There is a lot of reading and many assignments but it's honestly a very easy class! I thought the topic was interesting too.
If you want an easyish A, don't take. If you need to take this class, take it when Will Cox teaches it. He's more interesting. Lectures = boring, says everyone. Unless you LOVE Soc.
Wonderful. Opinionated but as long as you are capable of supporting your argument she's open to it.
loved this class!
Not the hardest, not the easiest, not the most interesting, not the most boring.  Take the class if you like SOC

Pugh was an incredibly boring lecturer. No one paid attention in class, and she was extremely defensive if anyone brought up criticism of her. I found her rude and slightly offensive. I despised the class and would STRONGLY recommend taking any class BUT this one.
Pugh is a great lecturer. Easy class. The midterm is a group project then there is a 7-10 page paper and then a take-home open-book final.

Never ever ever take this class! It's awful; I have never hated a class so much. Pugh is repetitive, boring, and rude. The TAs were absolutely useless, and the group project and huge paper were nightmares. NEVER take this class.
LOVED this class! Professor Pugh is animated and makes lectures interesting. She also tries to involve her students by asking questions, etc. I recommend this class

Professor Pugh was one of the best I've had at UVA. She's really passionate about the subject and tries hard to make lectures enjoyable and tailored to the taste of students. She included lots of videos from youtube, interesting websites, and other sources that made class interesting. She was enthusiastic and very clear! Made me a sociology major.

I would not recommend taking this class from Professor Pugh. She passed a lot of judgement, and was offensive on many topics. My TA was good, but Pugh was unengaging and boring in lecture and managed to be insulting a lot of the time.
If you like Sociology this is one of the best classes. A lot of reading, but getting a good great is not hard at all.

AWFUL class.  There was far too much reading and it was very repetetive.  Her lectures and the material were unfocused and she was defensive when it came to criticism of the class.  This class was disappointing considering how interesting the material is.

This was a bad class. I thought it would be easy and fun but the lectures were extremely boring-hardly anyone showed up to class. There was a lot of reading and we would read entire books and not even dicuss them in lecture or sections. The papers weren't too bad but the final was ridiculous.

Prof. Ramazani is fantastic! He is incredibly kind and very encouraging. Some of the most in-depth feedback I've ever received on an essay in college has been from this course. Show up to class and start your essays a few days early, and you will be fine. Scheduling office hours can be really useful if you need help. Would recommend!

Professor Ramazani is a supportive and intelligent professor. You can tell he really values the voices of his students. He grades papers very quickly and gives extensive feedback on them. No matter your interest in poetry, Ramazani will undoubtedly introduce you to new works and make you appreciate them. I'd take this class again if I could!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Ramazani is an amazing person and very good prof, very respected at the university. However, he gives very little expectations for writing and is a VERY hard grader. Despite my best efforts I think he did not care for my writing style, and I was never able to push into the A range for him, which was very frustrating

Jahan makes poetry very interesting, and tries really hard to make content current and applicable to everyday life. His focus on Black art and artists in Fall 2020 was a huge eye-opener for me (white student).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Robey is fantastic! He makes this course very stress-free and interesting! There are only four tests and a paper at the end of the semester that are not very difficult! He is always willing to help and very funny! Highly recommend!

Prof. Robey was awesome! Easy class, although I still had to pay attention. I read the textbook although optional. I enjoyed the content thoroughly, but Prof. Robey's experience should be independently noted and appreciated and his lectures were so helpful.
I really liked his class as well as him just as a professor.

While the teacher herself was nice, the way she teaches is awful. Be prepared to have to know the smallest, dumbest details from all the 100,000 books and poems we read to do well on the midterm. Unless you are genuinely passionate about old and middle english literature and using dictionaries, don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class! Definitely pick your TA wisely; Rush is excellent but the discussions can be struggles. Also, her exams are brutal but she's very helpful if you seek her out!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved taking Professor Rush at UVA. In the class I took, she had you read various books/excerpts and class is based around discussion of those writings. She is an incredibly passionate and understanding professor and wants you to speak your thoughts, even if they disagree with the rest of the class. I highly recommend taking her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Took this class because i was genuinely interested in architectural history but the professor ruined that. She is very passive aggressive and condescending to students during lecture and not a very effective lecturer. Most relevant content is said during lecture and not found in the slides or resources.
