Grading is harsh, subjective and unreasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall was not a good class to be in. For an intro class I thought it would be a little easier but with the only 3 assignments counting towards our grade being the midterm, paper, and final, there really isn't much room to succeed. Just learn the monuments and terms and you should be able to succeed in this type of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't recommend if you're taking optionally. Mrs. Reilly didn't inspire or improve my understanding of Arch History. She reads from a script and can often be passive aggressive, snappy, and demeaning to students. She's more understanding during OH though. In short, all you need is to research the monument list on your own. Also, no devices allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I skipped most lectures, never did any of the readings, but memorized the monument list and still passed. Reilly's lectures lacked any enthusiasm and my TA for discussion was okay at best, but I did not put much effort into this course either. Definitely not a course I would recommend for people who are not passionate about the subject.

The most important thing is that you show up to lecture. Pretty much all of the material you need to know for the exams will be covered during the lectures. The readings are pretty much optional. There is also a final paper and weekly reading "quizzes." It does not matter what you score on the quizzes because you get full credit for just doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are intriguing and Professor Reilly clearly has so much passion for the subject. Section counts as a huge part of the grade so pray for a good TA, but Professor Reilly is nothing but great. She can be sarcastic from time to time, though when I visited her office hours she was really sweet.

Professor Reilly can tend to be passive aggressive towards students when asked questions. Lectures also are very boring, she reads from a script which make the lectures non engaging. Having a good TA is key for this class as everything is essay based. Be sure to attend sections as those are a huge part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring and you could learn more from the textbook, but go because there are random in class turned in assignments to make sure you attend. Tests are pure memorization and are easy if you study/have good notes/ or read the textbook. She's not super approachable, and class could be so much more interesting than she makes it, but its ok

Not approachable, can be sarcastic and a bit rude. Be careful of falling asleep or asking a stupid question. Lectures are interesting and instructions are clear, do not ask stupid questions. Tests are tough but TA grades them, find one that you like and get to know their grading style. Impromptu in-class check-ins, go to class and section.
She is clear in what she wants you to know and some might say she has a dark sense of humor.
Very good professor, great lecturer. As long as you attend class and memorize your class notes, you should should do fine.

Was in no way as interesting as i expected. bring coffee to class, as lectures are not terrible but verge on boring. attendence a must. tests are extremely difficult, all essey. several times when i basically got the answer right she would put no comments and then just randomly give a B or C+. write as much as you can on each question. tough grader
I attended her course carefully. But I still can't figure out what the point was... bleah
She's super boring and makes you do useless in class group discussions that are a waste of time.  Fill your Medieval requirement some other way.
Great teaching style. Very interested in student's learning and understanding of material.

Professor Reilly makes this one of my favorite classes ever. She is extremely approachable to ask any questions and is very encouraging to all of her students. I haven't missed a class yet and can't see myself missing a class just because she makes her lectures so enjoyable! She does her job well!
No Comments
No Comments

Her lectures are very fun as she is a great lecturer and keeps the class involved through questions and hypotheticals. Since there isn't much that goes toward the grade and it's philosophy, you're more likely to get an A- or below as there is no clear rubric for the papers and exams besides vague information given by the TA's.

Professor Stangl is amazing. Her lectures are not mandatory for this class but they are so captivating and interesting that going is definitely worth it. If you are into ethics then this class is heaven. She has great energy and very passionate about the subject matter. I would take this class again if I could. overal 100/10

Stangl's lectures were really interesting and really useful. Everything she said and put on the board in class was on the tests, so if you don't understand the readings, attend lecture and you'll be set! One of the most thought provoking classes I've had.

She manages to make philosophy fun and interesting! She would sometimes spend the whole class just answering questions to make sure the students really understood everything. I didn't do any of the readings because she explained everything so clearly. Tests and papers were graded pretty harshly, but I feel like I learned a lot in there.

The lectures were very interesting and clear. You could get away without doing the readings because she goes over the information you need very thoroughly. It was not easy to do well in the class because all grades were papers or essay tests that the TAs grade very subjectively. Overall I recommend the class.
The most worthless lecture I have ever been to. Do not take this course. Seriously. It's terrible. The TA saved it for me.

Stangl is phenomenal. She is the best teacher in the philosophy department and  easily one of the best at UVA. I only took this class because another class of mine got cancelled the day before school started and this was the only class open. I couldn't be happier that happened!

Stangl is amazing. I had little interest in philosophy and am now looking to major in it. The lectures AND TOPICS are not only clear, but interesting and the readings are aren't too long or heavy, especially for what you'd expect in a philosophy class. Get Ben Richards as a TA and your semester is made.

Stangl got me interested in Philosophy because she is good at making lectures easy-to-understand and accessible. She's also very helpful at office hours! I was really happy with this class, and Stangl made it fun. There are 3 papers, a midterm, and a final (which are both 2-3 essays).

The Second half of the class is much easier than the first so if you get through the dense Aristotle/ Kant you will be fine.  Some of Stangl's lectures are absolutely unbearable but others are okay.  With that said as long as you skim the readings and are very attentive in the discussions you will be fine.

Definitely my favorite class so far. She does go on the occasional tangent, but overall I think the examples (however trivial or simplistic they appear) are fantastic for making dense theories more relatable. She also posts ultra helpful study guides for the exams. Definitely understand the reading but skimming is sufficient in most cases.

Stangle teaches clearly and thoroughly and uses examples that are often criticized for their simplicity or irrelevance. However, this is untrue. If anything, her examples clarify dense Aristotelian and Kantian concepts. She's a phenomenal professor. I highly recommend taking her class.

Class was really easy but putting up with Stangl's lectures for an entire semester was painful at best. She has a bad habit of going off on tangents that shes convinced are really funny (like talking about her cats for a half hour)

Moderate amount of reading that you should probably skim through before class, though she mostly goes over the important points during lecture.  An interesting class in my opinion and she is rather knowledgeable and personable.  There seem to be only 3 grades as far as written work, so reading is necessary for papers.

lecture is annoying at best; her public speaking gives you that uncomfortable feeling of being embarrassed for someone else. while the topic was interesting, listening to stangl stutter and giggle about it ruined the class for me

Going to lecture is pointless. If you go, you will be bored to tears and put to sleep, she is not the best public speaker. There are 3 papers, a midterm, and a final. The midterm and final are like reading quizzes and she posts a study guide with all possible questions of toolkit. The difficulty level of this class really depends on your TA
Very smart, funny, and good philosopher.  Great lectures, but allows students to take control of discussion too often, in my opinion.
Overall a good class to take.  She really summarizes the reading in her lecture slides and goes over the essentials.  Get a good TA because they do all of the grading.
Very clear, balanced, engaging lectures. Moderate reading load. Very enthusiastic and sweet person. She is my role-model. Very smart too.
Class is incredibly easy. Comprehensive study guides for midterm and final, and neither reading nor attendance mandatory. Papers a big part of grade but are graded easily.

Rebecca is a fun teacher! She's not super awesome, but she definitely loves what she teaches and makes you interested in it too.  She explains things really well and offers lots of viewpoints on everything.  REALLY interesting class!

Excellent teacher - i loved this class! She was very energetic and approachable. Summerizes main points of readings in lecture, which is helpful, but must do the readings for a good grade on papers. Encourages discussion and often uses amusing examples to emphasize her points. I highly recomend taking this or any class by her.
She makes it hard to follow the honor code.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This in-class component of the course is awesome: can't say the same about the labs. They take 4-5 hours ish per week and while not necessarily difficult graders are EXTREMELY nitpicky over just anything and everything and the labs ARE TEDIOUS. Submit in a word doc instead of a pdf: -25%. You didn't phrase something exactly how she likes: pray.

This class has an insane amount of work. For a one credit class, I spend more time on this class than any other class. Many things that are learned in the class can simply be searched on Google, and the questions on each quiz are extremely redundant. If you are a first semester engineering students taking this class, I pray for you.

Fabulous teacher! I loved the online work and the homework that came along with it. I was really pushed to my limits and i dont regret any of the work! I recommended this class to all my friends in chess club!

I think I can summarize the voice of everyone on this. Reimers makes mistakes frequently and doesn't handle admitting or correcting them well. Her research on teaching middle school girls explains her manner of speech - it's belittling. Quote of semester, "I taught this wrong, then wrote this graded quiz question, so remember that when answering."

If you are going to take this class. DON'T. Save yourself the headache of having Ann Reimers try to teach you dynamics. She does not understand the course content and you will go crazy following her thought process. She learns course content as she teaches it but still insists that she understands it to the point of teaching concepts incorrectly.

Apparently Reimers' idea of teaching is making you watch hours of decade-old online tutorials. You don't get to skip the things you already know either because she will have quiz questions that essentially ask 'what did the person say at 1'33" of the video?'. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone but then it's a requirement. So, good luck.

Honestly, this class shouldn't be taught this way. If there was a lecture, then it would be 10x better. Directions in the assignments can be unclear and very confusing at times. Assignments use materials that are irrelevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Absolute trash

Absolutely terrible... The homework assignments are completely absurd. The concepts you're supposed to learn are somewhat useful, but the way it's forced on you ensures that you won't remember anything useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely sassy in emails, especially when you ask her for help. She is also very disorganized and will change the assignment about 3 times every week between when the assignment was released and due. Don't expect to understand the assignments either, they are almost always above the level of a first semester college student.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is decent for figuring out matlab and excel I guess. I also commend professor Reimers for coming up with the assignments from scratch as it's probably not easy. However, the amount of time I need to spend on these assignments is ridiculous for a 1 credit course. She says they take about 3 hours each, but be prepared to work for 6+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class literally has me in tears of laughing at the amount of stupid assignments we are given. Don't bother doing the assignment until the last 36 hours of the week because she'll change the assignment just about every other day. This class is a waste of time and you learn nothing useful or helpful for later engineering classes.

This class has been the bane of my existence. It is supposed to be a one credit class focused on how to become proficient in Excel and Matlab, however, I find myself spending more time in this class than any other. There is extensive prior knowledge necessary to succeed in this class that is far over the heads of the students. Must be restructured

She is a good person and is helpful when you come to her, but the class she runs is extremely unorganized. It started off very easy, but is slowly becoming more and more confusing. Even though this class is only one credit, it's the class I probably have the most work in and spend the most time on. The help sessions run by the TAs are not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class has been an absolute disaster. Students in this class are in their first semester of college. Yet they are expected to have knowledge of linear algebra, advanced material science topics, complex electrical circuits, etc. The instuctions are terrible, and the class is all online and needs good instructions for success to even be possible.

The assignments are hard to follow, and this class is only assignments (no lectures/labs). They're explained poorly, and can't seem to follow any particular pattern. One second you're doing linear algebra, the next material science. The TAs are often not helpful, as they are not shown the assignment before we are, so they're just as confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class focuses on teaching MATLAB and Excell, but it fails on every level to do so. As a one credit hour class, the assignments take 6+ hours on average and sometimes 10+ and require outside knowledge for classes likely not taken yet, such as Kirchhoff's Voltage Law. This class is busywork, and the material could be learned better from YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: An amazing and knowledgeable professor of Chinese history. He made this lecture interesting in a way of telling a story about the materials that I am never bored in his class. Exams are easy since the study guide is provided and it's the same thing. Your paper and exam essays are graded by your TA, this can very impact your score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: My favorite class this semester by far. Professor Reed is a charming professor who is evidently very knowledgeable and passionate about the history he is teaching. His lectures are extremely engaging and he makes history come to life. I looked forward to every lecture and would definitely recommend this class for historical perspective requirement.

Professor Reed is one of the best professor I've had at UVa. Although his assigned readings are quite hefty, his lectures are super interesting. If you pay attention a lot in lecture, you can get away with only skimming the readings. Tests and essays are alright if you've been paying attention in lecture and discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great, Interesting Lectures. Notes are a must. The tests were graded fairly strictly. The TA you have matters a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Reed seems like a nice guy, but lectures are very dry and boring. Uses a lot of complicated definitions and goes fast, making note taking difficult and stressful. Tests/papers graded harshly by TAs with little feedback. The entire class is based on 3 assignment. Dont take just for nonwestern perspective requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No contest the best professor I've had in my life. I looked forward to lecture every single week. He made history come alive.
Best prof. I've ever seen in UVA. Very easygoing, very accessible outside class. Must take his class!
Greatest history professor ever!!!!! Love the way he taught the material and definitely have a deep understanding of Chinese history!

Took Mod China, he is an absolutely engaging lecturer -my favorite professor of the semester. The TAs do all the grading and grade midterms harshly (tip: include dates and the sig/big ideas for maximum points). Th professor definitely knows his material (organized lectures). However they simply skim the surface and reading is essential -& lot of it
Took American history since civil war with prof Reed in Beijing this summer. A great lecturer. Learned a lot.
This guy is an awesome professor. Lectures are organized, clear, and interesting. If you have any interest in modern China, or even if you don't but think you should, take this class!!

Lecture outline is written on the board, but the lectures are often dry and later in the year a little unorganized. For the first half of the semester, will randomly call on people to make them pronounce a Chinese name. Bring his beautiful dog to class occasionally. Overall, fairly interesting material. Helps if you know about socialism.
I HEART PROFESSOR REED!!!!!!!

Engaging lecturer. Didn't know how interested I was in Chinese modern history; definitely captivated my attention. Manageable reading even if you have loads of other work. I'm a science major with little room in schedule, and this was an excellent elective!

He is a great lecturer who articulates very well and definitely knows the material inside-out. However, I have to warn you about the TAs - Zhao Han in particular is very strict and will not give you the grades you want [the downside is that he tends to focus on being philosophical rather than discussing real history]. This class was worth it though

He reads too much from his notes during the lecture and is very repetitive with cliche explanations about how "history is more complicated than a monolithic representation" blah blah blah. Also, not enough time devoted to contemporary China, just one or two lectures. Not missing much by missing lecture.

Sensational! His lectures are very well organized, easy to follow, and very interesting, like he's telling a story. Take notes on your computer because you want to write everything he says down (average 4 pg, 1-space 12 pt on a day!) but if you write it all down, you don't need to read the book - although the book is pretty good. Highly recommended

One of the sleeper best classes at this University.  Even if you aren't interested in Chinese History, its hard nto to be captivated by this class.  Professor Reed is an amazing lecturer and very interesting.
This class was absolutely fascinating.  Reed's lectures, even at 9 am, are captivating.  If you have even a passing interest in the subject, seriously, TAKE THIS CLASS.
Exceptional

Prof Reed is awesome! He is very organized and every lecture of his was interesting. As a science major I could write down everything he said, which for me, was very impressive. =)If you give enough effort to this class you can def get a B or above. Even if you're not a history major, like me, you should try to his class just because he is awesome.
Prof. Reed is a great lecturer, in fact I liked him so much that I took him twice.  If you go to lecture and take good ntoes, you should get at least a B.  He is also very accomodating.
dynamic speaker, easy to get in contact with, invites questions, awesome class!

Interesting professor with a lively personality.  Is an animated professor who is open to questions throughout the lecture and is passionate and very knowledgable about Chinese history. - 2 midterms/1 final that are ID/essay and one 8-10 page paper
Great class. Easy class. Three papers and attendance comprise the grading. He grades really easily. He's a nice guy to. Absolutely recommend.
Wonderful teacher, super helpful and nice.  Helps with writing a ton while being a fair grader and providing great comments for improvement.  He is also really cute!
Awesome dude.
Very good professor

Professor Will is a very knowledgeable professor and the class I took was very easy. However, his lectures were likely the most boring I have ever attended. The majority of the class would be used listening to music and analyzing a libretto of some opera. The class is extremely easy, though, I studied about 45 minutes for the final and got a 90%.

This class is frickin awesome.  End of story.  Very interesting and he tells you exactly what he wants you to know for exams.  Probably my top class I've taken at UVA.  Also, take Michael Bishop for discussion if you can.  He's a riot!
The class covered some very interesting material. The reading was moderate, not too bad. The tests  and papers were pretty easy and related to the class material well.

Richard Will is one of the best professors I've ever had. He's very approachable and funny and really likes the information. 3 papers, midterm, and final. Values your opinions and interpretations. To be honest, the whole semester I was having so much fun I didn't realize how much we had learned when the final came around. If you can, take him!
This guy can jam!
This class is very simple if you do the readings and Rick only lectures for an hour instead of the full class time.
Rick is the man. Just write a little bit and talk. The class is engaging and interesting. He is a kind old man with a big heart.

At first, classes would be really interesting group discussions about death. As the semester went on, it kind of became more of a lecture with very little participation. You could probably get away with skimming readings. Papers were graded in a super annoying way, but were easy to get an A on.

He is a fantastic teacher. Gives great insight to the course and is clearly very intelligent. also funny and sweet in an old man kind of way. 3 papers (pretty short/broad topics) and participation are the only parts of your grade. He is awesome and so is the class. Easy 2 credits!!
Awesome class, awesome teacher. If you go to class, participate, and write decent papers, there's no reason you shouldn't get an A. Easy grader on essays.
Rick is fabulous!

TAKE THIS USEM!  It was basically 2 hours of discussion on Death and Dying, but the time would fly by.  We got into some of the most interesting, totally off-topic discussions and took and amazing field trip to a funeral home.  Easy A too, just a fre easily graded papers.

Professor Ross is approachable and wants his students to succeed. He gave us make-up assignments when we did so badly on the exam. The group project was awful, especially when my assigned groupmates had no idea what we were supposed to do and I did all the work by myself.
On the tests, you get marked wrong for the stupidest things. No partial credit. Homeworks take forever. Don't take this class if you can help it.
Not a good teacher. Does not go in-depth, does not give helpful material, does not give partial credit, and gives incredibly difficult tests.

Professor Rubin was one of my favorite teachers at UVa. Although his classes were often labor intensive  for example, MUSI 4510 required lengthy readings and responses for each class  Rubin was a fair and reasonable grader who always makes himself available if you are struggling with the material.  Definitely a positive educational experience.

This class is absolutely awful. For a 2000 level class, it is far too difficult and Rubin is so scatter-brained. The TA, however, was far worse. If you get Jean, he is completely incompetent in grading, and he can barely speak correct English! I've received A's on 3000 level papers and got my first D. Bad all around.

This is a VERY easy class. He gives you a study guide for the exams. The papers are easy and not graded harshly. In lecture, he's very scatterbrained and it's hard to follow what he's saying sometimes
Ryan was passionate about his subject and made the class fun.   He has a strong grasp of the concepts and teaches them in an understandable way.
I LOVE PROFESSOR NELSON! He's so fun and makes it interesting and fun to come to class

Brilliant teacher and a brilliant class. He is very funny and teaches you everything that you need to know. I would really recommend having him as a professor. He is also very reswponsive to emails (responds within 20minutes usually.) Excellent teacher!
first rate prof!
He's awesome, and he's one of the reasons that Block one is the best in the comm school.
No Comments

Doesn't ever read the assignments you turn in for grades.  Arbitrarily sets grade cut offs.  When you go see him to question his grading system, he tells you that you didn't talk enough about points that were never asked to be discussed in the actual assignment.
Nice guy, does a good job of making IT interesting.

It's the first class that I ever finished auditing from the beginning to the end. Ruth has a very strong background between hardware and software, and she has experienced the whole process from using assembly language to C and she was like an electrical engineer who works in the CS. I'm confident about her knowledge between hardware and software.
She explains very well, but is very strict with grades. (she actually gave me a D, although I got the average on the final and spent an average of 15 hours/weekly labs==>had to retake it)
No Comments
No Comments
bla bla blah
Great lecturer, always prints handouts for us, very well organized. To the point. Knows her stuff! Pays attention to students and really cares about them. The best prof and advisor EVER! :)

Had her for 216, then took 415 again with her. She is just fantastic. One of the best profs I've had at UVA. Even went out of her way to talk with me about grad school and research opportunities. I learned a lot in both classes I've taken with her. Very friendly and nice.

She's the best CS professor in the department. Her lectures are clear, and she will help out any student who doesn't understand the material. Her assignments were fair in difficulty. The course material is pretty interesting and fun sometimes. She's a very friendly and knowledgeable professor too.

Very intersting class. If you start on the labs BEFORE the night before, then you will be fine, I find the labs to be very helpful. Also, do the practice exams and you will do just fine on the real ones. Great class and teacher.

My impression was that her lectures are good, but labs are bad. Labs are just plain too hard; a lot of the later ones are huge projects that most other classes would make long-term assignments (ie: greater than a month), but you have to do them in just a week for her class.
placed too much emphasis (grade-wise) on assembly programming

She is amazing! I learned SO much in her class! She really makes the material interesting and the labs and exams reflect exactly what was in the lecture. Later labs are longer and harder so be prepared! A GREAT professor! One of the best in CS!

Class could have been much worse.Tends to have you do things by hand on tests versus programming.No one does a post/pre/in order traversal or insertion of elements by hand on a tree.Covers data structures well and how to speed up algorithms using them.
Better than other teachers I've had, but not exceptional. Organized lectures.  Boring labs. Helps to have some background in the material.
Doesn't stand out in any one area, but is good all around.
One of the better CS professors at UVA, but that's not saying a lot...
impossible class to get an A in.  Teacher is clear and covers material well.  no matter what you do, you will not end up get perfect on the labs
Good teacher, animated, knows her stuff.
Average teacher, but played games with grades.
No Comments
No Comments
Better to go to Virginia Tech as a CS major, don't stay in UVA
No Comments
worst ever
Excellent professor, knows her stuff.
good teacher; lively
Knows her stuff, teaches pretty well - inher element teaching this course partic
Mrs. Anderson is a mediocre teacher.  She makes cool CS topics boring.
Probably very smart lady,lectures are worthless though,it's here first year here
This class was fairly easy and Saliba is very entertaining. There is a lab component that is very enjoyable and helpful. The grade is not test heavy which is great.

Dr. Saliba can be kind of blunt with more sensitive topics during lecture, but the course itself is straightforward.

Very introductory-level, which can be a nice break & GPA-booster when you have some harder classes paired with it. Lab/discussions are mandatory, but involve some fun and field-specific hands on experience.
This course was generally easy if you have an interest in Kinesiology/medicine. I paired it with BIO 3410 and the course aligned nicely and often overlapped in material.

Really enjoyed this class, though the TAs did most of the teaching, they did a great job! There are several weekly assignments and lots of group work but the material is straight forward and easy to understand. Put in some effort and your grade will be great. Won't kill your grade to miss days here and there either. Never got < 88 on tests

Intro to Kinesiology is a great class, especially if you're looking to major in it. It's a great overview, and pretty easy overall. The TAs are awesome and Dr. Saliba is really cool. I would definitely recommend.

she mentioned entire semester how class would be curved up to the average of B+ but that was completely false. Her explanations were unclear, and both  practice problems and tests had way too many errors, making it difficult to learn. Class was highly theoretical. Tests were confusing, poorly worded, and some questions were unrelated.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know what these people below me are talking about. Professor Schenone is the BEST! Her class really isn't that difficult, but you do have to make an effort. She's great -- my favorite professor at UVA!

Excellent professor!!! Incredibly fair and helpful. She breaks down complex concepts in ways that are easy to follow and understand, and her lectures are really enjoyable! Quizzes and tests aren't too difficult as long as you do the homework. I think her class is pretty fun. Take her! You won't regret it!

Horrible teacher.  She is very unsympathetic, picks favorites, you NEVER know what is going to be on her quizzes.  She's rude and unsympathetic in person.  She says there will be a certain curve and then suddenly changes it.  I have gotten all As and A-s in college, but this was my first B-. Take Smith's class instead!

I dont know what happened between last year and this year, but Prof. Schenone is amazing!  She explains things extremely well and her quizzes/tests are very easy.  People wanted to avoid her class at the beginning of the semester, but people in the other classes now wish they took her section.  One of the most enjoyable classes I've taken at UVA
She seems like a nice person. She's just a very confusing teacher.
Simply Terrible!
possibly the hardest professor to understand and the exams are literally impossible

Carola Schenone is hands down the WORST professor I have ever had. She freaking taught us futures and forwards backwards! At the end of the semester she more or less made up grades--- in fact, there was a petition that at least 50 of her students signed. I cannot believe they kept her for another semester. You will hate life and her Irish accent...
AWFUL exams, very unsympathetic.
Not very helpful, almost never had office hours and not very accomodating.

Absolute queen, she will make you want to learn. Homework after every class but it's not a big deal. If she is an option for your German class, build your schedule around getting her as your professor.

The best professor Ive had at UVA. I had her for german 1010, 2010, and 2020. Truly a caring, kind-hearted woman who wants the best for all of her students. Could never say anything nearly negative about her. Simply, I love her and she made me love German.

She was very repetitive but it in a way that really helps you learn the material. I learned so much German and about Germany in her class. My favorite language teacher ever. Be ready to get called on though!

This class was a breeze. Some of the homework is kind of pointless busy work, but it's easy enough to deal with. She's very kind and willing to help out in any way possible. I honestly can't imagine someone getting below a B+ in her class if they put in at least some effort.
Good teacher.  Going to class and doing the homework prepares you well for the tests.  It got a bit tedious at times having class five times a week and work every night.
This class is like any other language class but at a faster pace. She teaches well and tests are not bad if you stay on top of your homework. She's got no tricks up her sleeves.

Professor Serbulea is a paragon amongst educators. I worked hard and she helped me every single step of the way. Her lectures and her powerpoint are amazing and her ability to disseminate information is unparalleled. I started off my pre med journey with a B- in general chemistry and blossomed in her class with an A+ #Postbacc approved.

The most professional, caring, and excellent lecturer. Initially, she does seem cold, but this is far from the truth. Serbulea cares deeply for her students, but you must show that you care about your grade, her course, and learning. Attend office hours, do the extra credit, meet after exams and see how much she will invest in your success.

What is up with all the negative comments being flagged for Serbulea? Pretty convinced she's flagged them herself geez.
Ex-Serbulea student here. Don't do it. She isn't worth it.
I truly loved serbulea and orgo

Like you will hear from many, Professor Serbulea is very intimidating at first, but she really does care about what she teaches and the students she has. Organic chemistry is not easy, but she does a very good job of setting students up for success. Lectures are great, exams are rough if you do not take the time to study, and homework is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She says "study chemistry every day." This is not a friendly jest. Worst grade I got in college... would take it again 100%. Amazing professor, so eager to teach. It is a rare opportunity to test your limits to the breaking point. She is an amazing professor and, if you put in the work, it will still be paying off years from now. Commit to it.

Serbulea might seem scary at first, but she really cares about each student's success. Her class is very tough, but she is a decent lecturer and if you put in the work, you'll do well in the class. Grading is extremely fair and the feedback you receive on exams is valuable. TAs are great, use the textbook, it is very important.

Serbulea is the best professor I've had at UVA to date. Yes, she's scary at first, but if you work hard in class and spend time learning the course material, she will take note of your hard work and appreciate it. Go to office hours, do the homework, and go to TA review sessions for the best chance at doing well in the course.
she goes on and on in lecture for so long and yet there was so much I had to learn on my own
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Serbulea is by far the best professor I have had in all of undergrad. She seems tough at first, but she offers so many opportunities to improve your grade. Her tests are tough, but fair, and there are always extra credit points available. She explains orgo in a way that makes sense and it is very do-able to get an A or A- if you put the work in

Serbulea seems really cold at the start of the year, but really does care a lot about her students. She is very organized (weekly homework, starts exactly at the same time every day, etc.,) and is good at explaining things but stays on one topic for a little too long. Lectures can be a little dry, but Serbulea is clearly very knowledgable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Do not take the accelerated Organic Chemistry if you're not prepared to commit yourself to learning it -- you've got to spend a solid 15 hours a week outside of class to really have the comfort that you need to succeed in this class. Aloof at first, Professor Serbulea truly does care about the success of her students, but don't waste her time.

Overall, a very good professor. She teaches you all the important things you need to know in lecture but expects you to know everything in the textbook (except for specifically excluded sections). All material listed in the syllabus is fair game for the exam. Although it is important to stay on top of things as she'll teach you stuff day of exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a really great lecturer. She makes everything so understandable in class, but then the exams are like NOTHING you've ever seen before, I mean straight up impossible. She's very structured (mandatory weekly homework) and timely, but she's unapproachable. I would never go to her office hours for help because she's scary. Many clicker questions

Professor Serbulea is probably the worst professor I have had at UVA to date. She is cold and unapproachable. When you go to her office hours, she demeans you for not knowing what you got wrong on a test and makes it seem like you missed the easiest thing in the world. Her lectures are pretty clear, but she still fails to clearly explain everything

The class is overall very well structured and her lectures are amazing. I learn a lot during class and she really helps solidify my understanding of the subject. However, one on one, she is not as approachable as some teachers. She tends to be condescending and impatient, which can rub some people the wrong way.
Expect not to know what you're doing the first few weeks. You will have to work a lot.
Serbulea is an amazing professor who really wants her students to do well. She's funny and engaging. But you do have to put in the effort to do well. Definitely recommend taking her class for orgo
Dry lectures would have more sleeping students if not for caffeine and pre-med anxiety. Presents material deeply and clearly.

She is good at explaining things and her lectures are clear. Her clicker questions are fair, her tests are very difficult, and she does not curve. Serbulea is very mean person. If you try and ask her for help she will knock down everything you say in the most condescending way. Probably the most unapproachable teacher I've had at UVA.

Organic chemistry is hard, but Serbulea does a wonderful job at elucidating the material in lecture and making the chemical logic of reactions make sense. As someone who took McGarvey for CHEM 2410, I ended up with a better grade in Serbulea's class even though she only curved a few points. Reading the textbook isn't necessary, but do the homework!

Professor Serbulea is a difficult but very fair teacher. She goes through the lectures very thoroughly, and her lectures and exams are based off the textbook. She may be intimidating, but if she sees that you continually go to office hours and ask questions, she will remember and appreciate you. Exams were difficult but fair, and I recommend her!

The absolute WORST professor I have EVER had!! Her lectures are useless, but you have to go because of clicker questions. The homework has nothing to do with the lectures and sometimes you can't even find help in the text. She has no clue what she's doing, she stresses the most unimportant things. Avoid her at all costs!

like the previous commenter said she moves very very very fast through all the material. There is no curve ZIPPP NONE at the end so your exam grades are what averages to your final grade = NOT ideal for orgo. I took McGarvey for 2420 and ended up getting a better grade for the same amount of effort because of the huge curve

She moves quickly; there's almost no time during class to recuperate and gather your mind. The average of tests usually was above 70, so she feels like there's no need to curve. However, the tests aren't particularly easy. Some kids are just much smarter than you'd hope (as a cut-throat pre-med). Study LOTS and do the Sapling online homework!

Seidel is not for everyone, but she's very energetic and cares about her students. Might not learn a lot from this class (Mindful Decision Making), but it's the easiest A ever and you're only graded by simple assignments which you all do in class. Not much reading, most of the class is spent doing breathing exercises and listening to her lecture.

I loved Professor Seidel. She is such a kind person and her advice about outlook and mindset were really transformational for my classes going forward. Her office hours were easily accessible. Quizzes were worth 60% but werent too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dean Seidel is an amazing person. She genuinely cares about her students' well-being and how we are absorbing the information. After each unit theres a paper we have to write to make sure we understand the concepts. Each unit last for about 2 weeks. Her lectures can be all over the place, so its important to pay attention, and go to office hours
Roundabout lectures and vague instructions.  Would not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this class to anyone that does not have any interest in the topic. The professor is a really nice quirky lady however, it can sometimes be overwhelming. She teaches big concepts which are easy to understand after you get the hang of it. The lectures tend to be disorganized.
She is disorganized and has a vague way of rambling through her lectures, jumping from topic to topic. I did not appreciate her "quirkiness."

Once you learn her teaching style, this class is great! At first I didn't understand her "conceptual" teaching method, but I quickly picked it up. She and her course materials are accessible to ensure that you learn and succeed. Seidel cares so much about students. Take the class, go to the class, and love the class!

Professor Seidel is awesome. She's very nice and inviting. Ask questions if you need to. Material is easy. I didn't have to touch my book at all, and I haven't once. The book is a good reference if you need to go over something you don't understand. Again, ask her questions if you need to. This class is lecture-based. Go to class!

Don't let the class freak you out at the beginning, it actually turned out to be quite easy. Although most of the information is the same as in AP/IB bio classes, Professor Seidel makes you learn the larger concepts and apply them rather than the minute details. She is very quirky, but definitely wants all her students to succeed.

She's one of those few professors that truly care about her students. Dean Seidel has a quirky, funny personality, and is always willing to help. She remembers your name once you go to her office hours enough too! Class is difficult; she emphasizes understanding and asks you quiz/test questions in her own way. Phenomenal human being. Received a B.

Awesome prof, she genuinely loves biology and it shows in her ability to teach. She cares about her students and is very approachable if you have a problem. Tests are fair and allow for application of knowledge rather than repeating memorized facts. Definitely recommend.

She is an incredible teacher. Not only will she know every students' name but she truly wants them to succeed.  She goes out of her way to make sure that her students are not just memorizing but actually understanding and enjoying the material that she is presenting.  Having her has been an incredible blessing as I am now more prepared for A&P.

I can say that this was the best class I've ever taken. Seidel is  so enthusiastic about what she teaches and it makes you want to learn. It was a bit hard to adjust to, but it really helps you learn to think. She really cares about her students, as well. =)

awesome, awesome, awesome. By maybe the 2nd week she knew everyone's names (56 people).  So passionate and gets really excited when students are excited. Likes to jump up and down to prove a point : )  So interesting and learned much more from her than I had in 4 Bio/ Anatomy classes combined.

Seidel is insane in a good way.  I have heard it said that she is like Miss Frizzle from the Magic School Bus, and I agree. Sometimes her lectures are too disorganized to follow effectively, but parts of her lectures help you understand and remember the material. She cares a lot about her students and the material is interesting.

Professor Seidel is a very passionate teacher. She also cares very much about each and every student. I met her for one on one help every week and she was always glad to extend that extra little bit of assistance. Overall class was very hard. You won't pass without reading the book. Her tests are extremely difficult and hard to understand.

Enthusiastic. Stresses the APPLICATION of bigger concepts, instead of memorization. Provides study guides and offers review sessions prior to quizzes. Would recommend referencing textbook for more detailed information she skips in class.

Ms. Seidel was a very enthusiastic and energetic professor. She was always available for any questions that you had. Her tests are slightly harder as they tend to be VERY wordy. However, overall it gives a good overview of the human body and common diseases (not into the nitty gritty, always the "big picture").  I recommend it.

Remind one of Miss Frizzle from the magic school bus, and is just as enthusiastic.  She is more than willing to aid anyone outside of the classroom. Likes to point out the athletes in the class. :) The quizzes are a bit out there. She intorduces new concepts on the tests (quizzes) that you have to really think about and "think outside the box."

Sandra Seidel is an amazing professor.  Her lectures are always very enthusiastic and very difficult to sleep through.  As said previously, attendance is a huge factor in your grade.  The first quiz seems to be really difficult but once you can see the style of her tests improvement follows.  A very useful class geared to application problems.

This class is not an easy A, you have 3 "pop" quizzes that she tells you about before hand and 3 "quizzes" that are really tests.  If you read the book and attend lecture (which is mandatory and verified by daily notecards) you should do well.  She is a very engaging teacher and always willing to talk to you if you don't understand.

Okay, I never had her as a professor, but i did have her as a dean.  She is, without a doubt, the BEST administrator i have ever had the pleasure of confronting (my grades weren't so great--she did not give up on me as many other "advisors" have. "not college material", my ass.).  She truly cares about students.
lectures are disorganized and impossible to understand.

She is so knowledgeable of the subject. Biology is her passion and she does anything to get students interested and to make them understand the material. It requires reading (if you choose to do it) but reading the book helps. She goes over the material pretty thoroughly. You may find her kind of crazy but you'll never get bored in the class.

She is really passionate about the subject, and this is one of the most useful classes I have taken.  Reading the book before tests and quizzes helped a lot; her questions are sometimes vague, but there are a lot of grades in the class, so messing up on something won't totally ruin your grade.  She is also extremely quirky and knows everyone's name

Awesome professor!  Cares about students, takes time to use various media to make lecture interesting and helpful to all types of learners.  Always available to help students.  visit her office often even if you are doing well.  She helps you think about things in a different way.  approachable.  quirky. makes you interested in the topic

Ok she is really cool and can make the lecture fun.  But beware, she is slightly weird and her tests and quizzes can come from anything!  Do all the reading and know everything because she can ask the most specific, random question, or be really broad.  The material isn't hard, it's just tricky to figure out what she's going to quiz you about.
She makes class so much fun! She's really passionate about biology, which makes the rest of the class really excited about it.

This class was fabulous! Lectures were always so engaging, she knows EVERY STUDENT'S name (even though it's a class of 120 or so), and the material is so interesting.  Hardly ever any homework outside of tests and quizzes, which aren't that bad.  I loved this class!

Seidel is a really passionate about teaching, and about the material. She's really friendly and makes an effort to get to know every student, if they are willing to let her. She is easily approachable and always willing to help. Lectures are very clear and easy to understand, and test are very straightforward critical thinking questions.
He is very passionate about astronomy, and his classes are interesting. He also gives out studying material before each quiz, and it is really helpful. 10000% recommend his class

This class covered some complicated themes but Professor Davis was excellent at covering them in short lectures. He was regularly available if you needed help. There are textbook readings but you did not need to complete them to understand the topics. You do need to pay attention in lectures and do the homework to do well, though (it's not hard).

This class is very lecture-heavy but easy to manage.  Professor Davis was available after class (if he had a minute) or during office hours. I would recommend attending lectures because they are interesting! I found it impressive how Prof. Davis condensed complicated topics into short lectures.

He's the nicest guy and you can tell he's so knowledgeable and passionate about astrophysics. I took this course simply for credit and was so happy that I did. Use the study guide for tests and you're all set. Overall a great class to take!

Easily one of my favorite profs of first semester. Shane gives awesome lectures, is clearly passionate, and quizzes and final are straight from lectures, so make sure you read them. I joined this class two weeks late and copped an A- so for most people if you study well you will do fine. Black Holes is a must-take with SHANE!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Black Holes with him, it was a really easy class but still interesting. He is a great guy, very funny and gives good lectures. Would definitely recommend

Shane is the man!! Material can be complicated at first glance but ur boy Shane will get u through it. I just took this class for the lols as a first year looking to take some interesting classes, and I would def recommend. Not all black holes -- lots of other physics/astr stuff, but all good. Office hours are 10/10, study a bit & ur good.

First things first, this class is the Black Holes class (since ASTR 1559 is the mnemonic for new classes or classes that are irregularly taught).   Prof. Davis is honestly the best professor I have had at UVA. He was able to explain complex topics with ease and made this course very exciting. He was clearly passionate about what he was teaching,

Prof Shutt is a wonderful professor and person, I enjoyed taking a COLA with her. In every conversation we had she always checked in with me on a personal level. She has a lot to contribute to class and she always engaged my thoughts on food and culture. Class wasn't hard, mostly quizzes and a few projects but overall, Prof Shutt is great!

I took Cola 1500 and I LOVED this class. She brings food to almost every class and both the readings and the homework are very interesting. There's an easy quiz before each class, if you have done the reading it's pretty simple. On the last day of class we went to a restaurant! Totally recommend her, she's one of my favourite professors

Lisa's class was amazing! She is an excellent lecturer and is extremely knowledgeable. Discussions and lectures are so interesting you will want to go to class. If you aren't ready to do the reading, then don't take this class! Every day there is a short and super easy homework quiz (easy if you've done the reading!).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shes very friendly and wants to have a relationship with you. I took her Food and Culture COLA and she brought food to class almost every week for everyone and took us on field trips to food festivals. Her readings are interesting and her quizzes on them are super easy. One of my favorite professors

Literally the greatest professor you could ever have. He loves the courses he is teaching, and has so much passion. There's a bit of reading you have to do, but honestly its all enjoyable and easy/fast. If you tell him that you have a midterm coming up and don't have time to write a paper, he'll give an extension. He is the greatest prof I've had!!

Prof Sligh is actually the nicest person on the planet. His class was my favorite all semester. I took his ENWR which is based on Sherlock Holmes, therefore it is very reading intensive. Most of the stories are short stories though so it was manageable. There were 3 essays and a final and they were not difficult. 15/10 would recommend to a friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Sligh is a superb prof who genuinely recognizes and rewards his students' efforts and enthusiasm. He wants us to do well evident through his extra credit assignments, essay revision opportunities, and fairly easy open-book midterm. There's quite a bit of homework reading but he chooses very enjoyable topics, such as the Sherlock Holmes stories!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Sligh was truly an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and brings an energy to the classroom that makes learning fun even at 9 am on Friday mornings. I loved this class and definitely recommend taking a course that is taught by him :)

Charles Sligh is a kind and uplifting professor who is open to help whenever you need it. His essay grading is slightly strict, but he gives you quite a few extra credit opportunities as well as a very easy midterm to help boost your grade. Knows a lot about the subject he teaches and loves hearing different points of views from his students.
I love Charles Sligh. He is a gem in the English dept, and unlike some English professors, he rewards students for what they do well in writing instead of critiquing based on his own writing style.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: After two semesters, Dr. Sligh has been my favorite teacher at UVA, and I don't think that anyone will be able to top him. I actually took his class in the fall, but am revisiting this page to write a review because I don't think he receives enough praise for the passion he brings into the classroom. Would definitely take again if I had the chance!

Wow. Just wow. Dr. Sligh is one of the reasons why the English dept at UVA rocks. He's a genuinely altruistic human being who rewards creativity. Even if he completely disagrees with your interpretation, he will acknowledge what you do well in papers. You won't even know he disagrees! Vastly underrated, under-acknowledged professor!
Fabulous professor! His lectures are thought provoking and purely fantastic. Easily the most fun class I had this semester. There is a lot of readying and a few papers but nothing too crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ghost Stories was one of the most amazing classes I've taken. Professor Sligh is amazing! You will have to read a lot- sometimes more than I could handle from Tuesday to Thursday. I highly recommend him.

I personally found that going to lectures is necessary in order to understand the readings more clearly.  I chose to take notes on my laptop during every lecture, then I used these notes (usually 5 pages for one book) for about half of my paper we wrote.  Basically, cutting my work load in half for the paper.  Your grade is all in the paper!
Charles is an amazing English professor. He really stimulates ideas and discussions in his students and he really knows his stuff. I'd take any english class from him!
Extremely fair, he KNOWS if you haven't done the work.  Loves his subject and is open to new ideas.  What all teachers should be like.
Shes amazing.  I wish all of my TAs were like her!
Jeanine is awesome! One of those very rare TA's that actually is compassionate about teaching and her students.
Jeanine is great!
Jeanine rocks!  She's the greatest teacher I've ever had!  I wish they could all be like her!

Easy class. Tests are easy. The homeworks are so hard u can't do em without going to the TA hours. Make sure u get 90s on the HWs. The hardest part of this class was the huge learning curve for Civil3d.The semester project was annoying, do not fall behind on the deliverable due dates. Smith is a pretty chill guy and i enjoyed his alumni interviews.

Great professor for a great class (if you're interested in construction). Has lots of practical experience with construction processes and management, and brings in guest lecturers from contracting companies. Took it as a 3rd year so the hardest part was competing with the 4th years who already interned at contracting companies (skewed the curve)

Easy professor, keeps everything very practical and interesting. Likes to get class discussion going instead of asking rhetorical questions and immediately giving his own answer (like some profs do). Is very available even though he's super busy (chairman of Civil department), and is very reasonable and helpful.
A nice guy who got stuck teaching a very dry class.  Pretty straight forward and a bit witty, albeit dry.
He is actually the stupidest guy I ever encountered.
Easy class and Smith is pretty interesting.  He presents what you need to know during lecture, so if you pay attention you won't have to read the book.  Tests are easy but long.

PROFESSOR SMITH IS A NICE GUY; HOWEVER HIS LECTURE IS VERY BORING.  HE CRACKS HORRIBLE JOKES IN ATTEMPTS TO RELATE TO HIS CLASS.  THE CLASS WAS SUPPOSED TO BE AN EASY A BUT HE INCORPORATES SO MUCH BS THAT IT IS NO LONGER EASY.  BE PREPARED FOR LONG TESTS.
No Comments

One of the most boring professors and classes ever. The hour and fifteen minutes have the potential to ruin my day. The professor does not even try to make the lectures interesting and the material is completely pointless because it deals with everything that should be hands on not read from a book!
The material is very easy but VERY boring.  Smith seems like a nice guy, but it's really hard to make the class interesting.  It's a long hour and 15 minutes.

Students not enrolled in USingers face a significant challenge taking Slon's classes, as Slon clearly shows preference for students enrolled in his ensemble in class. Slon is more apprehensive at being harsh towards his USingers students than those not enrolled therein.
SHOW UP TO REHEARSALS!!!!!!! That is all that it takes to get an A in the class.
Great person and hold people to a standard that meets their potential.  GREAT all around.
Very fine musician.  Passionate about the music.  High standards.  Approachable and cares about his students.
One of my favorite professors! Quality of music produced is excellent, and rehearsals are typically engaging and fun. I definitely recommend USingers to anyone!
No Comments
USingers- Slon is nice enough, but he is not concerned about any scheduling issues you may have or willing to work with you about them. Very self-focused- expects you to give up a lot.
eh kinda boring but fairly easy
Excellent class
No Comments
Yay! We heart him! (And the hot pepper is for real!)

usingers is fun and slon is very nice and encouraging. lots of extra time dedication during concert weeks and slon is definitely not lenient or flexible about missing rehearsals at all. but i love the class and he is definitely growing on me every rehearsal. :)
great professor~~ very dedicated, yet friendly
Excellent professor. Motivating and a real leader.

If you like to sing join the University Singers. If you don't sing come to our concerts! When I was in high school I did district chorus and All State chorus but none of the conductors was like Slon. He is very polite, very talented and he is a great great great conductor/musician. He brought me closer to music and I made many friends in this choir
The people are cool, but class can be boring and the music can be boring.  He's a good conductor though.
No Comments
Altogether a really nice guy. Unfortunately, he seems to lack control over the chorus. He lets them talk to the point of disrupting rehearsal on a regular basis
EXCELLENT professor, really, not an exaggeration.  But do not miss rehearsals.  Don't do it.
University Singers is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!
Love to sing and Prof. Slon is awesome.
Nice guy, but don't EVER miss a rehearsal for a home Duke bball game

-Feels like she treats her students like children
Talks slow, repeats herself, and gives looks to stop talking I haven't seen since middle school
-Kind, passionate about the subject
-Content chosen is extremely boring
-Assigns a crazy amount of reading for "one of the hardest books in the world to read"
(but you can get away without reading it)
She is a very kind and understanding woman. She cares about her students and is willing to help whenever it is needed. Assignments were easy and she is not a tough grader.
Professor Smith was really nice, and very engaging, which was super important during COVID.

The class was incredible and the workload is very manageable. Her lectures are very engaging but they are very fast paced and she covers a lot of material in one lecture. Therefore, attendance is definitely mandatory! This was by far my favorite class this year! Would recommend this class to everyone! Prof Smith is awesome!
She is very passionate and you can tell in her teaching!! The class is time-consuming but she is very approachable to get help!
not smart enough for how rude she is
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She makes her classes appropriately challenging and always has an amazing attitude!

Dr. Smith is truly a wonderful and inspiring teacher. Even if you are not immediately drawn to the class she is teaching, her great knowledge and witty personality will make the class extremely interesting and worthwhile. Very reasonable in her dealing with students, fair grader and manageable assignments. All around excellent
Amazing! Love her and love her classes!

Absolutely AMAZING professor. She made me want to be an art history major. This was a great class too, very interesting. A lot of memorization, but nothing unmanagable. Tough grading but it's very possible to do well in the class. I recommend ANY class with Dr. Smith!

I learned a lot in this class, and Dr. Smith is a fantastic teacher. Definitely easy to talk to and very helpful. Lots of memorization for the two exams, and the worksheets took a long time. Other than that, reading is not excessive, and it's usually interesting. Tough grader though!

Dr. Smith is seriously one of the nicest teachers I've ever had.  Extremely approachable and helpful even with a really large class.  Not too many assignments (2 exams, 2 large worksheets), but they each require a lot of attention and time.  Definitely impressive resume.  Maybe I have a little crush.
Four open note tests, no final, one quiz per lecture, test and quiz questions taken right from lecture slides, easiest A ever taken
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 4 open note tests, short quiz after every lecture, usually with questions phrased exactly like they were on the slides, all true/false or multiple choice. Slides are posted, take good notes and it's impossible not to get an A. Really easy but also really interesting and enjoyable.
This class was very easy and very interesting, whether you have a background in environmental science or not. Office hours were always very helpful before exams even with the class size being so big.

Do the quizzes so you can get extra credit on the test. Straight forward class, read the lecture slides (which he sends to you) and you will do well on test. Extra credit quizzes also help answer questions on test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE HALLIE. Protect this woman at all costs. I can tell that she genuinely cared about everyone in her class. She kept a running journal of all the things we told her so that she could get to know us better. Her class is rather easy. Honestly just write something and you will get an A. She gives good feedback and never too much homework.

I was really interested in this class coming in, but unfortunately it ended up being a real drag. She doesn't have much to say about the material herself, the discussion is completely run by the students. It's easy enough, because she doesn't enforce that you do the reading, but that also made for a very boring class. Disappointing to say the least
Hallie is a very good teacher. I had her for ENLT. She was extremely fair, flexible on absences and had a great personality. I definately recommend taking a class from her.

So basically ENWR is a BORING class, but if you didn't exempt it oh well, at least it's a GPA booster. Hallie is a fair greater, great personality, and as interesting as can be teaching the course matter. 4 5 page papers and some minor 1 page essays. Not bad at all. Give it some effort and you will get an A.

Professor Smith knows everything there is to know about his subject, cares deeply about human rights, treats his students with respect (although he does expect a high level of dedication from them), and overall is one of the best people I got to know at UVA.

One of the best politics classes I've taken. Smith is an amazing lecturer, and he posts his outlines on his Collab for you to refer back to. Grading consisted of 2 papers, a final, and participation/attendance in section. Final was super easy, I maybe read 1-2 of the books we were assigned and I ended up with an A.

He's great!! Midterm and final were pretty easy. Pretty much a low-stress class. He does amazing lectures, he's an absolute genius--although sometimes this means his lectures are a little difficult to follow because he has a high vocabulary. SUPER nice guy though. grading all depends on your TA. I didn't buy any books all semester and was fine

Professor Smith is very caring and creates a sort of community atmosphere in his class you don't find many other places at UVA. However, his grading rubric is entirely non-existant that can be incredibly stressful. I also really didn't like how he refused to allow modern day references in readings and papers.

If you pay attention in class and pull specifics from the readings, papers are much easier to write. Try not to doze off because lectures can get dry. Get a good TA (April)and do your best to understand the readings (they're dry and somewhat difficult) and you should be fine.

Professor Smith is incredible intelligent and well-read. He has a sharp sense of humor as well. He selected great books for our seminar and led engaging discussions. Also, great adviser because he knows professors all over UVA.

Awesome guy, great teacher, wonderful human being. Very smart, so take advantage of that. No doubt the best teacher I've had so far at UVa. The class isn't hard if you're into morality, human rights, and international relations. If not, don't even take the class.

brilliant professor - possibly the overall most intelligent i've ever had in 4 years of school.  incredible lecturer with an incredibly cosmopolitan knowledge of the subject matter that extends beyond the call of duty.  lots of reading, but if you pay close attention in lectures and discussions, you'll be fine - as long as you can write well.

Great professor who really cares about his students.  He is genuine and kind and really wants his students to succeed.  Take advantage of his knowledge--use office hours to get to know him.  He is one of the best professors that UVA has to offer!
he is like your introverted weird uncle who you always look forward to talking to.  not only smart, but he REALLY, really, truly cares.  kinda reminds me of frasier.

I never thought I would or could love a man as much as I love my father, but that is how much Professor Smith means to me. He is the most selfless, caring, compassionate, understanding, not to mention brilliant professors I have ever had the fortune of having. The course is difficult, but he is instruction and lecture is flawless.

Brilliant. This professor is great if you care about the world, hope it will improve, and care about people.  If you care about money and yourself, you views and his may clash. Classes often involve student discussions centered around the readings. Start you final papers early, read and cite the books from class, and you should do well.

Very intelligent but arrogant. Extremely biased in his presentation. Lectures are his opinion, not the theory of the thinker. He clearly emphasizes one worldview over all others way too much for someone who touts tolerance.

Absolutely the greatest professor I had while attending UVA. Professor Smith was not only a truly wonderful lecturer/instructor, his complete grasp of the Geopolitical landscape was truly something to be experienced. His c.1990 hopeful, yet stark vision of the future has  proven frighteningly accurate. Take anything he teaches, u wont regret it! 8)

Michael Smith is awesome.  One of the best profs I've had.  He is engaging and challenging.  He's also tuned into his students.  One of my roommates tried to kill himself (no 4.0 policy), and Prof. Smith was totally supportive and compassionate without being wierd about it.
this class made me decide to major in foreign affairs- very engaging.  I actually enjoyed reading the majority of the course material, and my TA (Talal Belrhiti) was good

Incredible material, great teacher/lecturer. Has a fabulous reading list, good assignments, and if you're going into anything international related you should definitely take this class. TAs were not so good my year. He believes in primacy of human rights in intl relations, most of his students don't, so classes tend to be very interesting.
No Comments

Like everyone else has said, he's very smart.  Almost too smart, to the point where it's hard to follow what he's saying.  Class is WAY too hard for what it's worth, as the material is highly pedantic and academic, with little applicable relevance to how the world actually works.

Very smart man, knows a lot about the subject.  Very liberal however, and definitely an eternal optimist.  He'll very hard to convert you to his way of thinking.  Don't take this class if you aren't the human rights activist type.
Brilliant!  very intelligent guy who truly cares about the future of politics and human rights.  class was hard, but worth it.
Wonderful material, plus the professor is engaging and dynamic.  Highly recommended - finally there in someone in political science willing to stand up for ethical state action.
zzzzzzzzzzzzzzz

Cross-listed course co-taught w/Childress. Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about subject, but lectures or still kind of boring. He's liberal. Class should be political theory--not int'l. relations.

We can all be a little more like Dave Smith. He is easily my favorite professor by far, and Marine Environments and Organisms is a worthwhile class for any EVSC student with an interest in marine biology. The class is hard, but the tests come directly from the lectures and his grading is extremely fair. Studying for tests is essential and worth it.
One of the best professors I have ever had mostly because of his clarity in lectures.  He is also always willing to help the student achieve their highest potential.
Hard, but fair and clear on what you need to know. Well organized lectures. Friendly, enthusiastic, and incredibly nice. He was also one of the profs on the Bahama study abroad trip- he was my fav.
Very enthusiastic and knowlegable about material.

With everything happening with the pandemic, I believe professor Smith was one of the few who was understandable!! He gave a decent amount of work and recorded all of his lectures. He gave you a decent amount of time to complete everything. Def a great person overall. Would recommend.
Whole class is based off of 3 exams. The lectures are boring. Professor is a good person but his structure of the class is lazy. Very unsatisfied

Awesome lectures-hes very straightforward and the grading criteria is always clear. the class only has 4 grades (multiple choice tests), so not a lot of room for error. No final. He  is very organized and easy to follow. also a super nice guy in general. beware though the multiple choice tests are tricky, not as easy as you'd expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: HE'S MY FAVE!! The Plants People and Culture class was the best. The material is SO interesting and you learn so much. He is super funny and nice and really knowledgeable about the information. The course teaches you about plants and how they are used for food, medicine and alcohol. All tests are multiple choice and no readings or cumulative final!

Professor Smith is a very nice and knowledgeable professor.  Simply, he is a straight-shooter when it comes to tests, and he is a wealth of information in lecture.  With Plants, People and Culture specifically, it definitely is recommended that you attend lecture, but it is not required.
An incredibly nice guy and a great lecturer. Definitely take

Tom Smith is undoubtedly an amazing professor. Every lecture was phenomenal and kept me interested the whole way through.  However, tests can be hard and the study guides can be a bit misguiding.  He didn't quite explain what would be on each test, so the first one everyone did pretty well then the second people tanked. Still a great class though!

Don't buy the textbook! As long as you go to class and study a minimal amount, you should pass with at least a B. Going to class is more important in the end than in the beginning as the tests get harder and harder. Also he'll have opportunities to for you to get extra points on random days, so even though class is boring, GO!

Class is made up of three exams. Exams get harder. Class attendance isn't mandatory but if you want a good grade, you should go. To study, read over his Powerpoints and look at the terms on the study guide. Class is a basic high school science class, so go to class and study a day in advance of exams and you should get at least a B.

Class is boring.  The exams are very difficult and require memorization.  Questions are written in a way to really confuse the students.  There are only 3 exams and he really doesn't care if you do well or not.

Awesome Professor. He is such a nice man and very helpful. Dont buy the textbook he even advises not to buy it ( and he wrote it). The class is very straight forward, most things come from slides others from paying attention.Cool guy :)
COOLEST EVER

Awesome teacher.  Subject matter is challenging but Smith makes it understandable.  NOTE: Lab is VERY challenging and takes a lot of effort crammed into a short amount of time.  Lab not recommended if you don't have to take it. TA's run labs.
Very good teacher.  Excellent explanations. Extremely flexible with office hours. Keeps you up to date and wants students to succeed.  1010 is very easy.

One of the best professors I've had.  Very helpful and flexible.  Attendance isn't required and the class itself isn't very difficult.  All the test questions come right from his class slides and he gives you outlines with the topics that will be on the test.  If you have the opportunity, definitely take a class with him

He is the nicest man in the world. He will help you with anything. You don't have to buy the book or go to class. There are only 3 tests for your grade, based on the slides that he posts online. He makes it easy for those who have to take this class to fulfill a science requirement.
I really enjoyed this class. For a non-science person, the information was interesting and accessible. I definitely learned a lot and really enjoyed Professor Smith's enthusiasm and friendliness.

Horrible class. Horrible professor. He does not teach at all and reads off slides and then tests you on stuff that don't appear on the slides. Much more difficult than it should have been. Never responds to e-mails and I could never get in to see him during office hours. Avoid this class.

EVSC 320 is not THAT easy. 4 exams 25% each. Exam format is all free response and not multiple choice. He doesn't let you write nonsense answers so you have to get them right.
