It's good thing that I only had him for a freshman seminar-type class, because I can't imagine how badly his mumbling and rambling detracts from his science class lectures. He seems to know quite a bit on the subject, and grades fairly easily. It's just that his lectures are boring and not terribly easy to understand.

His USEM is decent. LOTS of reading with a few lectures. the 2 hour class is almost unbearable in length. He has a LOT to say. He has a tendency to ramble and mumble. Not a very good combination. Gives arbitrary assignments. Knows a lot though and is very willing to share. Is a really nice guy too.

He's a nice guy and very approachable. But the tests are extremely hard. They rely heavily on lecture, but he mumbles, and it is hard to understand what he is saying sometimes. He does, however, have many opportunities for his students to meet with him for any questions they may have.
I loved this class and Professor Homyk. He rocks!

Yes he mumbles and yes his tests are hard but he truly enlivens this subject and conveys a deep understanding of the most difficult concepts. Plus, if you know everything from your notes, you will get an A on the tests.
Dr. Homyk is extremly approachable and willing to answer any and all questions.

He mumbles incessantly. His lectures are very hard to follow and even more boring. His tests are hard. This will deff be my worst grade ever at UVA, and not because I didn't know the material. He picks the most random, and non essential, concepts or terms to test on! He seems like a nice guy. But he is an ineffective teacher. booooo

A VERY nice man.  As other students have said, he does mumble a lot, and it is difficult to follow his lectures as a result.  He isn't very direct or clear about explaining concepts, but he is extremely helpful and approachable.
BEST TEACHER EVER!  he is possibly the smartest person at UVA.  He is a mumbler, but he'll repeat anything and he's so awesome that it's ok.  Tests are hard, but everything is from the notes.

Tests are extremely hard, but they only come from lecture material.  Lectures are boring and hard to follow because he mumbles and doesn't use any visual aids.  He's very helpful if you go to office hours with questions, but be prepared to stay a while...he never answers questions briefly!

I like professor Homyk, but I hate his class/exams. I feel like he sometimes picks the most obscure things to put on there and then leaves out huge crucial elements. His lectures are also long and horrible to sit through. But he is a nice man and will try to clarify point and answer questions in office hours.

He's so nerdy he's hot!  I have had Homyk for two semesters of lecture, and he just keeps getting better.  Tests are from lecture material only, so the class tends to be time comsuming only around test dates.  He's always willing to answer questions, and he tries his best to make funny remarks.  Which, just in their nature, usually are hilarious.
No Comments

Made EXTREMELY **** remarks in class the other day..concerning why summer sessions were shortened from 5 weeks to 4 "The girls didn't have enough time to get suntans..." etc.  Also, refers to female professor as "Elizabeth" and male professor of same class as "Dr. Kittlesen."  Old fashioned and NOT with it.  I have no respect for people like him.
This lab is the easiest class I have taken at UVA.  Professor Homyk is a cute funny little guy.  If you need to get rid of a lab requiremnt, take this!

this guy's the embodiment of a nerd, but he does try to make the class interesting, and he knows what he's talking about.  if you're thinking about taking  his usem science fiction and our future - the books are really good.
He knows everything he teaches. Sometimes mumbles but will always clarify any question a student may have. Great to see in office hours.

He mumbles a lot, but if you ask him to slow down or to repeat himself he is very helpful.  I like him - hes a funny man, but don't believe everything he says - I think he likes a lot of science fiction.  :)
Can't stand this guy. All he does is mumble incessantly, about spy cameras. If you take a usem, don't take this one.
impossible to understand, worst tests EVER!
great guy, little goofy but one of nicest people you will meet

I took the fear and anxiety seminar. Moderate amount of work weekly plus a group project and final paper. Grading is very clear and she is always available to help in office hours or by appt. I wouldn't hesitate to take the class if this is your first time taking a seminar.
Excellent Class and Teacher
Abnormal psych - a good class. she definitely knew what she was talking about. tests weren't too difficult, tho doing the reading was important.

She is so interesting and fun! If you do the readings for her class and the work, an A is very easily do-able.  She doesn't just talk about the texts we read, but relates it to real life examples.  This class was very African culture based, and although I am not super interested in African culture, I really enjoyed learning about it.

This was one of my all time favorite classes! Prof. Terni imparts such a wealth of knowledge and encourages students to find their own interest and explore the subject matter, while simultaneously analyzing it critically. She really cares about her students as well, and she makes herself available to students. Amazing class - TAKE IT!!!

So, this is supposed to be the Anthropology of Witchcraft, we barely talk about witchcraft. While her stories of S Africa are interesting, she talks way too much about it & it doesn't relate it to withcraft. The title of the class is VERY misleading. She talks a lot about nothing that relates to w/c. Don't take if you want to learn about witches!

I was first concerned about taking a class from a grad student but it wound up being one of the highlights of my college career.  Prof knows her subject and is able to create on open classroom setting where people are free to talk and learn.  It was a great experience all around
I took this class as a last minute option, it's my favorite class of the sememster. Exams are pretty easy, paper was harder then expected but still not bad.

A genuinely great person and a clear lecturer. Has a good sense of humor and isn't boring to listen to. Recorded lectures are available but he does have iClicker questions so show up to class. 1 weekly quiz & worksheet (open note, easy), no midterms, 1 final. Strongly recommend
No Comments

He is a great teacher to have for such a fast-paced course. It's my favorite class this semester. The information is difficult, but the way he puts things just makes sense. And if you ever miss class, just email him and he'll help you out in any way possible. Try to get into his class if at all possible if you love Latin or just want to know more!

I took this class the Fall of my First Year, and was blown away by the difficulty I had with it. I have received all A's and B's in every other class at UVA, but the structure of this class was dreadful. The multiple choice tests were unfair as they gave you extremely similar answers covering wide ranges - "some are right, choose the most right"

WIlson is by far the best professor I have ever had! I actually got excited to go to lecture..and didn't want to leave when it was over. He is so passionate about social psych, and he teaches it so well! He is super nice, super approachable, very understanding, and just an awesome professor. Such an interesting class! I highly recommend it!

Wilson's lectures are engaging, entertaining, and organized. However, the material itself can often be confusing and contradictory. This makes testing difficult regardless of how effective he is as a lecturer. Be warned for ambiguous test questions and arbitrary grading on the 2 papers. Definitely not boring, though!

Wilson knows what he's talking about. He makes it extremely clear what he is testing you on. Lectures are interesting. He uses film clips and demonstrations to make his point. He's very helpful and always up for answering questions. Tests aren't hard. Papers are graded easily. Overall, it's a good class for someone looking for a psychology class.
Very amazing! Very smart! He changed Social Psychology and he wrote the book!

My favorite class I've taken so far at UVA. Professor Wilson is amazing, he really brings psychology to life with his multimedia examples and his friendly, approachable teaching style. Great class to take for fun. Not too hard and there's a really cool project he assigns near the end of semester.

Class is really interesting (lots of film clips/songs/in-class experiments, which are fun but not distracting). Taking notes and even reading rarely felt like a chore, because the stuff is so interesting. Tests are ok if you study. Pushes his political views hard sometimes, but nice guy. Awesome class! Take it!! (Bloody irritiating TAs though)

Social Psyc was absolutely interesting material, and Professor Wilson was gentle and sometimes humorous to lecture. BUT, i dont know why I got so bad grade on this class. I wrote paper hardly, but never got better than B. And I had to keep up lots of reading, but the test questions were always tricky that I did not do well. Not that easy class.

Tim Wilson is such an enjoyable lecturer. The material is inherently interesting, and not very difficult to understand. Papers were tricky (the TAs look for very specific things and it's hard to do well unless you nail them all) but not unmanageable. And midterms were pretty easy as long as you kept up with the reading. Take this class!
A really good class. Wilson clearly knows what he is talking about and keeps things interesting. Everything is applicable to real life. It will make you interested in Psychology.

I really liked this class, it's by far the most applicable psych class I've taken.  There's a fair amount of overlap between lecture and the book (which he co-authored, so they mesh pretty well), but you will be tested on the stuff that's only in one (like specifics of experiment results, etc.).  show up and read the book, you should do well.
This class is awesome. The information is really interesting and Wilson really makes class fun. It's definitely an easy A and applies to your everyday life.

Professor Wilson is the best! He made psyc so interesting and so applicable to real life. Shows little video clips in class that really add to the lecture. I looked forward to his lectures and even the textbook, which he wrote, was fun to read. Highly recommend taking his class. It will change your world.

Great! I ended up loving Social Psyc and it was my first semester ever taking Psychology! It makes me want to minor in Psychology! Highly recommended! The textbook wasn't a bore and we watched a video in every class!
Professor Wilson is fantastic. Easy to understand, and the film clips keep the class entertaining and interesting. Highly recommended whether you're majoring in psych or not.

Take this class if you are looking for a fun, interesting, relatively easy course.  My only complaint would be that he covers a lot of the same material in Nosek's 101 class--but I don't know, maybe you will want that.  Good professor, take him.

Awesome professor. Loved his class. He has awesome examples and he helped write the textbook, so he knows what he's talking about. He made everything relative and interesting. Definitely take his class. I learned so much!
I LOVE TIM WILSON HE IS AWESOME TAKE HIS CLASS
He is awesome!  Lectures were interesting and pretty fun.  Tests are easy if you read.  You don't need to memorize but need to know concepts.  Really interesting subject!

FABULOUS CLASS AND GREAT PROFESSOR!  Professor Wilson incorporates clips of videos and TV shows to prove certain elements of social psychology.  The class is very interesting and he is an engaging, humble, funny professor.  If you read the material and attend lecture the tests are fine.  TAKE THIS CLASS

Tim Wilson is an awesome teacher.  The class was easy and fun; he included a lot of movie clips during his presentations.  The tests aren't bad and he doesn't have a cumulative final.  I learned a lot without killing myself.  You'll be fine if you do the reading and take notes during class.  My discussion section is worthless, but some were good.
awesome

The material was interesting, and he presented it well. However, it was a tough class. LOTS of reading, which you have to complete if you want a chance of doing well on the test. My TA was great - Patrick Seder - so take him if you can. If you take this class, be prepared to put a lot of time and effort into it. 3 tests, 3 papers, all difficult.
Tim is an amazing prof! His lectures are straight forward.  However, you have to study for these tests to do well on them ... and yes you have to read the book.  But this class is a must-take at UVA!

Great class!  Tests could be tricky, but they weren't impossible--just take them seriously and study.  The lectures were always interesting and Tim Wilson is a very intelligent, cool guy who knows his subject well.  Even the discussion sections for the class are worthwhile and fun.  Highly recommended.

Agreed. A surprisingly not easy class. In fact, I have no idea how I did so poorly in it.  The grading distribution is a little odd - 3 papers, 3 tests, and discussion.  You have to study HARD to get A's on the tests, write damned well to get A's on the papers, and talk a lot in discussion for an A there.  Good luck.  Interesting, but not easy.
Ok, this is not the easiest class in the psych department. Keeping up with the reading is extremely crucial to your success in the class. The tests are really pretty hard.
great class, extremely nice guy. explains in lots of detail and uses great video clips to help. i'd highly recommend taking this class
No.
Great class! Don't expect to get A's on papers though!
GREAT!
Great professor. Very knowledgable and shows a good amount of entertaining videos. Ease of the class depends on the TA you get (ie don't pick Kermer.)
One of the clearest and straight-foward classes in the Psych department
Great prof, nice guy, easy & interesting class
Simply luv this class, prob the only class where watching "Friends" is education

Took this class after reading that it is pretty straight-forward and an easy A if you put in the effort. This was definitely not the case-- it's really difficult to pay attention to his lectures and certainly not an easy class. Many of my friends who took this class ended up taking it pass/fail

While I find him to be a fun and interesting professor, his lectures were rather boring, making note taking a pain. I also took this online, so it's possible that his in person lectures may be better. I found that the class had little direction at times. The tests seemed to bring in curveballs I was not prepared for at all, regardless of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Thuan is such a sweet man! Even though this class is just an intro level course that most of us took to fulfill requirements, he tried really hard to make the lectures interesting and to inspire awe about the universe we live in. People who complain about his accent are just lazy and racist -- his lectures are extremely easy to follow.

The class and material is straight forward. Lots of math and science, but it's all very easy and basic. Attendance isn't required, but his lectures are really important, although they are pretty boring and dry. If you pay attention and take good notes, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pretty straightforward material thats not difficult.  That being said, the class is not very interesting and most people to it to fill requirements.   Thuans explanations not always clear.

He is an incredibly nice man who wants the best for his students. Everything that you need to know he writes on the board, so it is very important to go to class and take notes. He doesn't necessarily test on the book material, so you only need to review the notes to study for the tests. Its a very easy class if you show up and pay attention.
He is very helpful and care for his student. All you have to do is right whatever he rights on the board and study that and you be fine.

Not a bad class, but it gets boring. Take notes in class, and reading the textbook won't be necessary. This class is an easy "B" and a very difficult "A". The way he curves is basically to give 50%-60% of the class a "B". Helpful in office hours.

I barely went to class- just read the chapters the night before the tests and did reasonably well. Thuan's accent is a little hard to understand but as long as you are paying attention it shouldn't be a problem. Very nice guy and kind of funny, but a little all over the place. Lectures were not very focused and some of the math came out of nowhere
pretty easy, straight from the book

Very interesting class. You can tell he is passionate about his subject but it takes a while to get used to his accent. Its not too terribly hard to understand him though. His tests are very very easy if you study both the book and his lectures (which go along with each other.)

This class is pretty boring but fairly easy. DO NOT buy the book. Its very expensive and 100% of the test material is based on the lectures so if you skip ALWAYS make up the notes (if you care that is). So yeah, if you need to take an easy class I definately recommend this. The final was kind of hard so don't completely slack off near the end.
Very passionate about what he does, but it terrible at conveying it. His office hours are helpful, though.
He knows what he's talking about, but he's hard to understand and the tests are based 100% off what he says in lecture. Don't bother buying the book.
Dreadful. That is all. He talks into the board, and his accent makes him completely incomprehensible. Don't waste your time...this class is lethal.
its bad. you can barely understand him. very boring. easy class write what he does and look at him with adoring eyes. very attractive yet don't take the class to get your kicks
i never went to class, never read, and didn't study for tests and i got a C. i'm not complaining. so even with the slightest bit of work you can do better than me!

Honestly, I don't understand why people are complaining. This is not a high-level class. It is an intro course. You learn these things in grade school. Go to lecture, take note, do not buy the book, and you will do fine. You have to go to lecture but on the plus side, when there's an exam, all you have to do is read your note, which is not much.

You can barely understand what he is saying, because of his asian accent. He is VERY dry, & his lectures are painstaking. His tests are ridiculous & even if you study, his questions are so tricky it doesn't matter. Take the OTHER astr professor who teaches 121. For NO OTHER astr 121 class is it required to take a telescope lab except for this one.

Thuan really knows his stuff and he writes everything on the board. Don't buy the book, it's a waste of $125 since you never use it. The tests were a bit difficult, he takes seemingly easy material and makes it difficult with critical thinking questions. I don't recommend this class...it's not easy.

Basically: go to class, only write down things he puts on the board, and bring your laptop to use the internet -- you WILL be bored. Tests are a joke. I never studied and aced the class. VERY easy subject matter.

Hard if you don't want to come to lectures. But seriously, if you go to lectures and write down pretty much everything he says you'll do fine. he doesn't use the book AT ALL. he even tells you that! sometimes hard to understand but it's not like he's teaching quantum physics.

ok..I WILL BE HONEST WITH YOU!! Find another class. Truly, you can miss out on this one. You HAVE to go to class because he doesnt follow the book at all! Be prepared to work MATH problems because he turns even the simplest thing into a complicated math problem. You can barely understand him and he's very boring on top of it all. SKIP IT!!
Sounds like Arnold, the only thing worse than his accent is his horrible handwriting.

This class wasn't that hard; tests weren't that bad at all.  He talks like a miniature Arnold Schwarzenegger, so you have to sit a little closer to understand.  All you have to do is come to class and take notes, the book is COMPLETELY unnecessary.  He's a good teacher though, he knows his sh!t.
he is adorable and funny but kind of hard to understand.  much much much harder than i expected, so be prepared.  however, just read the book and actually study some and you'll do fine.
The class was "sleep-time," i.e. pretty boring.  Test were easy, though.

Its not true that you can just read the book. You HAVE to attend the lecture...the book is unecessary. His accent is NOT hard to understand. His tests are a bit hard, but only because ASTR 121 is 'supposed' to be an easy class. If you go to class and pay attention though, his curve is VERY generous.
This class is easy, the guy isn't that hard to understand if you actually go to his class. I feel bad for you if you can't get atleast a B
did not enjoy class, hard to follow

Seems like a very nice, knowledgeable professor.  However, he does have a tendency to be boring, granted his subject matter isnt the most interesting.  You can get lost in his accent if you dont pay close attention.  If you want to take this class just be prepared to listen to close detail.

Extremely boring and hard to stay awake in. Hard to understand and makes mistakes then corrects them later, making him confusing. Tests are only on what he teaches, no need for book. Not worth taking if you can avoid it

Unlike most of the comments here, I actually like his class. He does have an accent, but he can teach, and if you pay attention, the accent isn't so bad. The tests aren't easy, but I've learned a lot!
It's too bad about the accent, but the class wasn't hard at all.  If you're open to him you realize he's actually an amusing quirky guy.
He was awful...I don't know how else to say it.  The class was torture, his tests were torture.  It is not an easy A...take it with Tolbert if that's what you're looking for.

baaaad, i would be more angry with him if the material weren't so easy. Steps to success: register for the class, don't attend lectures, absorb the textbook the day before the test, and you'll get an A. Or at least a B+

the main challenge in this class is staying awake! understanding what he says is impossible, and he is extremely boring.  on a good note, you don't need to buy the book because his tests come directly from notes.  dont take his class unless you must!!!!!!
extremely boring, lectures all class, hard to understand
I was one of the people actually attending lectures and trying to learn the material and he made me feel like an idiot when I asked him a simple question.
He is probably the worst teacher I have ever had. It's not that the subject is boring, or that he can't speak english well, it's the fact that he can not teach.
So boring! I mean, I read the book and it was more interesting! It takes him 10 years to describe how something happens which he could describe in five minutes! I fall asleep every day!
sure he can't talk well, but it wasn't boring
No Comments
boo
No Comments
Literally the best professor at UVA. Had her for 4 semesters straight. After just 2 years of Chinese with her, I went to China for a summer, and they were astounded by how exceptional my chinese was.
She's not too bad, but expects a lot out of you. She can be a little harsh too. She teaches pretty fast, but if you do the work, not too bad.
very kind, easy weekly tests, wants you to learn
when she makes corny asian jokes, she giggles. it's cute!

Content not too difficult, but challenging- introduces  formal literary language vocabulary- volume/pace of the words/style taught kinda fast.  Good class though, knows her stuff, but always very professional, never come to her with personal problems unless they are serious familial/life-death issues that conflict with Chinese class
B-A-D class is not hard but she operates under the pretense that it is.

Tough tests, good amount of homework. Mylab homework is easy 100, but problem sets are difficult. Utilize office hours. Sometimes Prof Troyan is slightly condescending when I ask questions, but otherwise, he's a pretty good prof. Curves the class at the end.

His tests can be hard but he's very approachable and friendly. Great lecturer and passionate about teaching and making sure his students do well. So go to his office hours and ask for help! (He's also really cute IMHO... Great dresser, too).
Clear and organized lectures. hard tests. Prepare to invest hours in doing HW. Talented and nice person.

The Good: Professor Troyan is one of the nicest and very helpful.  He is good at responding to messages even late night.  He is respectful and open to students. You can talk with him about anything.  He's nice eye candy too ;)! The Bad: He's really smart, which means his tests, HW are super hard, so unless you're really good at econ, it's tough!

Prof. Braun is a very genuine, kind, and charismatic teacher. There is a lott of readings, however they are some of the most valuable pieces youll ever read. There arent many assignment except essays so be ready to write. He works to create a positive, inspirational atmosphere and he does. Try to take this in-person if you can.

I was part of the inaugural cohort that took the Latin American Studies interdisciplinary seminar, back in 2013-2014, over which he presided. Five years later and I'm still thinking of this man's gift for telling a story. Outstanding. Please seek Tico if you're in C'ville. Take a class, go to his office hours, talk to him, listen to what he says.

The Individual and Society was, hands down, the best course I've ever taken. His lectures were entirely improvised, but his teaching was incredibly engaging. There was a LOT of reading, even though he said it would be pretty light, but the readings were interesting. All-in-all, would recommend, even though he's no longer teaching the class.

The Individual and Society for the New College Curriculum. Hes pretty great the first few lectures but then the course seems to be repetitive. Engagement courses are only 7 weeks long and I was over it by week 3. It's only at 8am, and I was contemplating getting out of bed each time. Lots of reading, but you dont have to read in detail to pass

Tico is a gem! If you are taking this class, don't expect a traditional "this happened, then this happened" history class. More about themes and patterns in LA Hist. A lot of reading and hard to judge what grade you will get, but if you go into it with an open mind and you actually care about changing your perspective you will love it!

Doesn't provide a lot of guidance, but he teaches a great class with some wonderful reading material. There is a lot riding on your journal and the final paper, as well as your attendance. This class requires commitment and diligence. Don't expect to coast through the semester even though you only have two assignments to hand in. Its a challenge.

Tico is truly an excellent teacher.  Sure, you may not agree with his ideas, but put some effort in and he really pushes you to think.  I took his small seminar at the beginning of first year, and it's been invaluable to me in terms of teaching me how to write and how to discuss texts in small classes. He's fascinating if you talk outside of class!

If you're looking for an actual history class, DON'T TAKE THIS ONE. Instead of talking about the chronological chain of events taking place in Central America, we talk about coffee, bananas and massacres. Tico is interesting sometimes, but he rants about things a lot, like the war in Iraq, which are irrelevant to the class.

I was so disappointed by this class.  It was been the worst history class I've taken at UVA.  Braun does not lecture; there doesn't seem to be much rhyme or reason to the discussions he attempts to lead.  This class has not been worth the significant amount of time it requires, and I deeply regret taking it.

Coming to class isn't mandatory but it is a factor on your grade and does affect his opinion of you as a student in his class. He rambles but is generally an interesting lector. You don't need to read all the readings but def. most. He is not for the faint of heart or the staunch conservative; he tends to turn off conservatives so watch out for it.

Great class.  Lots and lots of reading, lots of wild discussions.  There's a 20 page paper at the end which is 40% of your grade; your notes constitute 40%; and attendance/whether or not he likes you makes up the rest.  Tico's a riot--you can't not pay attention--and makes coming to class (he takes daily attendance) worth it.

this is an old-fashioned marxist, and thus fun for conservatives... can't find types like that anymore. boring teacher though, and not a serious scholar; hence a waste of time - and only for undergrads if any...

Take a class with Tico if you seek socialist indoctrination.  This man is easily the most radically left-wing prof. I had in four years at UVa.  Historical fact and personal opinion were indistinguishable in his lectures, and the reading material reflected his individual biases.

The most inspiring and enlightening class I've taken yet at UVa.  Tico is really something.  It is a vibrant and dynamic class, the only one I truly enjoy waking up for in the morning.  If you're willing to open your mind, it will be the kind of class that will forever alter your perspective on La, life, everything.
Tico is so great.  He is one of my favorite UVA Professors.  He taught me a lot about what it means to do history and be a historian.

Ok. He's not so bad but not so great either. What happened is that this class, in my opinion, is def not for people that know nothing of Central America. It is for people who already know about the history of Central America and want to expand on their knowledge. That is prob why many people learned nothing and left frustrated. The guy knows a lot
wouldnt take it again if i could....
He's awful. I learned nothing. Class is a random jumble of unclear, abstract ideas, and he doesn't know how to put events in context so they are coherent. A waste of my time.
good class, tico is the man

Don't expect to learn any Latin American history from this guy. His class = him giving opinions on different matters. Some of the readings are interesting, but you can do those on your own time. I'm all for an easy class once in a while, but this one is unbearably boring & truly a waste of time.

Tico = rockstar professor. He will make you question everything you know. He teaches that everything is connected and intertwined, nothing is simple, there is no such thing as absolute truth, and does all of this to give dimension to the actual people of LA, without whom history would be irrelevant.

Braun is fun to listen to, but his class is very hit and miss. Sometimes the discussion is fun, other days he just rants on random opinions trying to show how "nuanced" all our opinions are. But its not very helpful. This is NOT a history class, much more sociological/anthropological.

One of the most interesting professors I have ever had.  His class was a pleasure to wake up early for, and that really something in my book.  Lots of reading but everything was wonderfully interesting.  He made me even more proud to be at UVA.  Caring and helpful as well.
so biased and weird that it's not really worth it, hip with pc second-yearers
A great professor.  Lectures always make you think about issues in new ways and he is very entertaining.  Wants to know his students and help whenever possible.
The best professor at UVA.  Always wants to help and see his students succeed. Take his class even if you have no interest in the subject.  He will remind you why you're here.

Professor Trent is an inspirational teacher. The class is not difficult, he assigns a good amount of reading assignments, but he went over most of them in class, and I rarely read them and did fine. I wasn't sure how I felt about the class at the beginning of the semester, but by the end I absolutely loved it.
No Comments

Best teacher EVER! This was my first class ever in the Ed. School, and it just made me so excited about teaching every time I went to class! He makes the material so simple and useful and he really gets excited when you contribute to class.  He just seems to really love watching everyone learn!

Professor has a pretty heavy accent which takes a little bit of getting used to but overall her lectures are pretty clear and easy to understand.  The course moves fast, we had an exam every week but all of the exams follow the same format so they are easy to study for.  Overall she was very helpful and participation gets you a long way.
Great class, be ready to invest a lot of time though. The work is definitely worth its 4 credits. She's awesome though!

She moves through material very quickly and sometimes does not explain topics.  However she is very nice and will explain anything you ask about.  She will destroy you in class if you get something wrong, but she doesn't mean it malevolently and it won't hurt your grade.

Lilia Saf'yanovna is a very clear and helpful professor. Her Kazan accent makes her slightly intimidating, but she has a good heart. Stay on top of your work and prepare for class; you do NOT want to answer an easy question wrong, she will tear you apart in front of everyone. Lots of homework, but AMAZING TA's

Wow, I really disagree! Prof. Travisano zips thru complicated material and expects you to know it, forever, after one week. This might be ok if you have a TA that drills you, but my TA sucked. The book is unhelpful. If you really want to learn Russian you'll survive, but make it your top priority. Prof.'s poor English makes learning difficult.

She's so nice and explains things really clearly! Classes aren't too big and she's very approachable and makes russian interesting even in 101. quizzes and a chapter test about every other week but she gives you the exact format of the test so it's not too bad if you look over it the day before.
Lilia is awesome! She genuinely wants everyone to pass her class and learn to love Russian :)

One of the most advanced and interesting russian classes i've taken. you're going to learn about stimulating topics and have mature conversations. Be prepared to put in more effort than the one credit is worth though.

She is amazing. If you can, take a class with her. It doesn't even matter what class it is. Ask her questions and don't be let down when she tells you how badly you really did on that essay, she is trying to help you, if you let her. She's funny and knows her stuff!
Very easy class. get to play games or watch Russian cartoons once in a while. sometimes the homeworks are a bit long, though.
The easiest A at UVA.  The exam policy is absurd.  You can retake any test or quiz you want, so there is no real incentive for doing well or studying the first time around.
Simply fabulous!

Great teacher! She's one of the best foreign language teachers around. It's an easy A- guaranteed if you just do your homeworks and follow the assignments. Sometimes course materials can be overwhelming but on the other hand, that's the whole point of 1st year Russian class! YAY~

I view slightly differently. Very nice, accessible individual, clear Russian lectures and you'll do okay if you just finish your homeworks and read some textbook materials. It might be tough for 101 courses, but that's the point of 101. For 301, Mrs. Travisano was a real pleasure. Loved it!

Teacher is very kind and willing to help after school, but the class has a huge load of tests and quizzes -- like at least 2 or 3 a week on extensive vocabulary word lists. I'm talking like..memorize 150 words in one night.
Good.
great
great hands on data science class
Incredible teacher.

Sam can get off subject in but that is mostly because students don't have very much to say so he goes off on tangents. If you actually had any questions and weren't afraid to raise your hand, he'd be more than happy to talk about them. Also, he is extremely helpful on papers with both content and grammar, he wrote a whole page explaining my grade.

Sam Turner's discussion is utterly useless. He's nice, but he really doesn't know how to lead a discussion. You spend the whole session talking about irrelevant speculation on what you read with no textual nor historical basis that won't help you anywhere in the course. On papers he's good at grading them grammatically but not substantively.
great TA...very out there, but somehow it all makes sense..haha He made us cookies and a mix CD too!!! : )
Sam is pretty much the best TA.

sam is an awful teacher. we hardly ever talked about writing, more about the weird dreams and thoughts he has. he won't give you good advice on your paper, just rip on it and give you a B-. he's not constructive. if you want to learn how to write, find someone else.

Sam is a great TA! Anyone who makes his class cookies and CD mixes on the last day of class is worth having. He is definitely fair with grades, and more than willing to look over a paper before it needs to be turned in.
Pretty easy grader and total goof...in a funny way. I found him hilarious-talked about everything under the sun in class but little about writing. Recommended if you want an easy writing class.

He has this awkward way of making random things very funny, yet is very dedicated to writing and therefore focuses on good writing very hard and very well. I would recommend his section, especially if it is the one about monsters.

I had Sam for ENGL 382 Discussion. At first I was taken aback by his irreverant style, but he proved to be a superb TA. He is extremely knowledgeable about many of the texts, but also lets the class take its own direction. For such a phenomenally boring subject, his crude sense of humor and obscene language made disc far more fun than anticipated.
take sam's section for 382 or 383!
Sam is the man. if you get the chance to take this class, do it.

Sam is a crazy guy. Yeh, he's funny at times but it gets old really fast! His class was useless to me, it taught me nothing. He grades pretty easy but if you really want help with your writing do NOT take ENWR from Sam Turner! You never get your papers back on time. He didn't give our last papers back until 2 days before final portfolio was due.

Sam is awesome! The class feels a little pointless..he's obviously very busy with his own work, so if you need a lot of help with writing, don't expect it unless you go to his office hrs. He is enthusiastic about the subject and EXTREMELY encouraging and friendly. Quirky and unusual individual that makes class easy and enjoyable.

OMG this guy makes me laugh every class just because of how crazy he is.  Sometimes his thoughts don't make sense at all so his class is hard to follow.  Overall a nice guy.  Certainly an "interesting" class and I don't really mean that in a good way.
Yeah!!!!
Sam's a great TA. a total scatter-brain but completely willing to work with you if you come to him. Tries to make class fun while getting through the sometimed boring tasks.

Wonderfully nice guy who does make class fun sometimes. Very little work... BUT He is absent minded and slow with returning papers. NEVER returns emails even during his exam/portfolio week. FRUSTRATING TA!
A mean-spirited person.  She had favorites, and only cold indifference or mild distain for everyone else.  I cannot express how much I regret ever meeting her.
Love this woman!

Betsy is mind-blowingly awesome, but you really have to step outside your box and put in crazy effort to get respect from her.  She definitely gets one or two favorite students in each class, though. If your not one, she can come across as judgmental and mean-sprited, but she's just trying to spur you to better things.

I can't begin to explain how much I did not enjoy Betsy's class. She was only wanted to see what she personally liked. It was a class about Betsy, a class about her bragging about the previous shows she has directed instead of trying to help US, the students. It is really ridiculous how awful this class and her teaching style was.

Five years after graduation, I'm still inspired by my classes and conversations with Betsy.  She's one of the best things about that department, because she looks to world theatre and pushes the envelope.  Not everyone digs her.  Being pushed by someone is challenging, and some don't like to be challenged in the way she pushes.  I dig her.
the most mean-spirited person i have met in theater, anywhere.
INCREDIBLE!  Betsy is amazing.  You want to take class from her.
****ed, intelligent, has a crackling laugh.  Throws out eloquent speeches.  She's inspiring, but never sentimental.

Amazing teacher for directing and great for 4th-year seminar as well.  Betsy's classes were the most important ones I took as far as growth and intellectual/artistic development are concerned.  She opened my eyes to amazing things.

Despite being a well cited professor, his lectures are usually a babble of incoherence. I am absolutely shocked by his lack of knowledge of certain books on the topics of cognition Not to mention the blathering contradictions in his content. Would not recommend, felt like I learned nothing.

Wow this professor is a boring lecturer. It shocks me sometimes how poorly structured his lectures are in relation to his slides. He does record his lectures, which is very helpful, but listening to them is painful. There is no homework (only readings) and your whole grade is tests. He is a nice guy but lectures are so so boring.
Turkheimer is the man. This class is kind of confusing and the material is hard to follow, but the curve is pretty generous and its not that hard to get a good grade if you go to lecture.

Although the tests are mostly MCQs, questions and options are worded badly and he tests about random things- I personally never know what he is going to test for and by extension, what to study for. Lectures are amazingly boring and I honestly do not know what I have learnt after a semester of this. Just don't take it.

Turkheimer can be a bit boring in lecture at times but it's only made worse if you keep telling yourself it's boring. Tests seem a bit random at first but then you understand his style and know what to study for. Textbook is actually interesting & I didn't mind reading it. TAs are friendly and helpful too!

I liked this class though the first half was certainly more interesting than the second half. I kept wanting to like Turkheimer though he said some things that became self-fulfilling prophecies like "it will be hard to stay off Facebook" -- well, *now* it is. The MC tests are not as easy as you think they will be.

No personality, unorganized and lacks coherency--as reflected in his lectures and exams. Focuses too much on Freud and includes random ?s on his MC exams (lowest score you can drop) that come from his disorganize PPTS. He never fully covers any material that you are still expected to know for the exam. Take with some other professor!
LOVED This class! Turkheimer was very helpful and made class engaging! One of the best classes I have taken at UVA.
Interesting. Explains everything you need to know very clearly in class. Main terms and concepts from the reading end up on the test but not too much.

I don't know why anyone would have a problem with this class. If you're conscious during lectures the points are spelled out for you very very clearly. Those who don't do well in this class do not belong in college. He's a nice guy and lectures, if you have interest in psychology, are interesting.

Not a great lecturer - though interesting, lectures were disorganized and didn't cover all the slides in his powerpoint (but you're still expected to know them). Tests are always mult. choice & always ask details that you wouldn't think to study. Seemed lazy but very nice. I only recommend this if you really like psych - don't take for an easy A.

Probably the worse teacher I've had here. Came to class late very often, with no lecture planned. Got let out early more than once. Lectures were unorganized, unplanned, slides were from 2006, and his tests were bogus.
This has been my favorite class.  Mr. Turkheimer is super cool and keeps things interesting.  I want to take more classes from him.

He's a very nice guy. I can tell he's passionate about his work and agrees with Freud in a lot of ways and focuses on him a lot. The class is easy, read the book (which is really good) and go to class and you'll do great!
Very nice teacher. makes his lectures interesting (If you cant handle talk about sex dont take it ;)readings are interesting. exams are average and pay attention to lectures.

Pretty ironic actually: a personality teacher with no personality. Talks too much about sex and when lecturing you're never sure what will be on the test. Though if you read the book (which IS really interesting) well you'll fine.

I love this class! He is a very funny guy and his tests are more focused on his lectures. The book is not that hard to study so I think you can get a good grade if you just pay attention in class. Lectures are enjoyable! I'll definitely recommend this class!

He talks a lot about Freud and not enough about other psychologists. Some topics were irrelevant. Exams were between 29-45 multiple choice questions = each is worth almost 1% of your grade. Meanwhile he says longer personality tests are a better sample of personality- that would apply well to exams. Especially when he asks trivial questions.

His tests focus more on his lectures than the book, but it's  good to read the book anyways. Definitely bring a laptop to class if you want to write down what he says...he talks pretty quickly and I don't know how people without laptops took decent notes.

I enjoyed this class a lot; it started out a bit dry, but got pretty good. Turkheimer is very engaging, and when he felt a lecture scheduled in the syllabus was too dry, he would just change it. A very good teacher overall.

Turkheimer is pretty cool guy- his lectures are pretty interesting and good to listen to, although I have fallen asleep a few times here or there.  Some advice- READ THE BOOK!!  His tests come from the book and his lectures.  Exams are hard, but 240 is a worthwhile class.

Terrible teacher, assumes the class follows everything he says and he just babbles on random stuff the whole class. Can never tell what is important and what is not. No class textbook and very lecture heavy. This class makes me want to rip my eyes out, do not take it and avoid van Wincoop at all costs.
One of the best Econ classes I have ever taken.

Professor van Wincoop is one my favorite professors ever! I learned so much from his class. His lectures were super helpful and he gives you the notes ahead of time so you can review what his lectures are going to be about before class. He is clear and concise and I definitely recommend his class if you are thinking about Econ.

I really enjoyed Professor Van Wincoop for ECON 422. His exams are fair, and his lectures follow notes he uploads on Collab, so you can easily prepare ahead of time (no textbook). He really knows his stuff.

I don't know why the guy up here rated him so bad, but I really liked his class. (maybe because the stuff was what I wanted to know the most, but still he is good) I did fairly well, but some people actually seemed like they didn't exactly know the stuff. anyways this Dutch guy is cool.

I came to this site for the sole purpose of warning others against taking VW's class. He is HORRIBLE. I have rated him high in helpfulness, but he absolutely cannot lecture, and zips through the material, writing frantically on the chalkboard without explaining. Worst of all, he makes many mistakes
The worst Professor I ever had.
Horrible

Cooper is a great and passionate lecturer. You learn a lot from this intro class. You do have to put in the time and effort although it is a "1050" class. There are no essays, 3 exams, church visit presentation, and frequent quizzes (depends on TA) that go into your participation grade. The only thing that irked me was that a 95 is an A.
EXCELLENT CLASS AND PROF

While I enjoyed much of the material from this class, my opinion of Professor Cooper steadily declined over the course of the semester. She is biased, accusatory towards the Catholic mass, and as a white student I often felt uncomfortable in lecture. She is a picky, difficult grader. I do not recommend this "preacher." Look for professors.

It's an easy class but I cannot say that I have enjoyed it. She is the most biased and transparent professor I have ever come across (3rd year). God is Black, Blacks still deserve reparations, White churches are not welcoming or fun, and mocks the Catholic Eucharist. Of course I'll seem ****, but I'm repeating things from the source.

Great teacher!  Really nice and a great sense of humor.  Even though her class lasted 2 1/2 hrs long, it never got boring once. Readings are necessary and long, but still very interesting and engaging.  Her class discussions deal directly with the texts.  I learned a lot about Pentecostalism from taking this course and would recommend it to anyone.

Cooper is an awesome teacher at the entry-level classes, but once you get higher into the 300's, 400's and so forth, her teaching style goes down the drain.  She is not very clear, and lets the class direct discussion.  Exams have nothing to do with the discussion, which feels like class is a waste of time.

She is quite passionate about the material... though she deviates from the script a bit and can appear scatter-brained, your grade largely depends on your enthusiasm for the class and the way you're able to engage the material. Readings aren't prohibitive, work isn't oppressive and as a white person, I can say she's anything but prejudiced.

In response to the post about Dr. Cooper's treatment of whites, she is not prejudiced in any way, but explained some extreme position in Liberation Theology.  However she never said she advocated them.  She simply explained how some scholars believed God has a "preferential option" for the oppressed. (Ex. James Cone)

She seemed like an awesome charismatic teacher from the beginning BUT towards the end of the semester she became kind of preachy.  She made seemed to imply that all the white kids in the class were **** and didn't let anyone finish their comment if it wasn't something she agreed with.  Very clear/concise.  Easy tests. Easy A. But kind of rude.

Dr. Cooper is an awesome professor. In contrast to the usual skeptical religion professor, she is a Christian an embaces evangelical viewpoints while continuing to present material objectively. She is awesome and I highly recommended taking her intro to Christian Tradition class.

Dr. Varon is clearly very familiar with her subject, and her assignments, while long, were not too difficult. Although the material is interesting, it's very easy to lose focus during lecture. She was very understanding outside of class, and the TAs were helpful and fair.

I cannot speak highly enough about Dr. Varon. Her HIUS 3071 were so interesting, and you could tell she was extremely knowledgable about the subject material. Do not be intimidated by her; she is one of the nicest professors I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Varon is engaging and the material is interesting. You can tell that she cares about the topic and about her students. Absolutely would take again.

Varon is so kind and really cares about her students (ex: I was sick and she was so nice and willing to give me an extension). Her lectures are super organized and easy to follow if you take good notes! Material is interesting and relates to events today. Shira is an awesome TA, literally the best I've ever had: funny, relatable, fair grader.

I love Professor Varon. She keeps me inspired to learn history and I'm not even a history major! Her class The Coming of the Civil War was extremely interesting. I originally thought that it would be some easy credits because history in high school was easy, but this class was challenging and actually made me think critically. I loved it!

Professor Weaver was fantastic at leading discussion and pretty good at lecturing. The workload for this class was excessive, even after the amount of writing was cut between last year and this year. She was very adept in explaining complex topics or in forcing us to think critically about what we were contributing. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: For the students at Yale who will have the misfortune of Prof Weaver's presence next year, you have my sympathy. Prof Weaver taught one course in my graduate program and was simply horrendous. Attempts to disagree with her views were treated as personal attacks upon the Professor. Dissent was met with either condescension or gleeful repudiation
Amazing.  My favorite professor at UVA, hands down (and I'm a rising 4th year)!  Her energy is infectious.  I'm taking her seminar next semester and am using her as an advisor for my thesis.

One of the best classes I've taken at UVA. She is very smart and extremely charismatic. Very passionate about the subject. Reading load varied, usually about 100-200 pages a week, but very interesting material. Not too much work, especially in comparison to other seminars. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone and everyone.

I had Prof Weaver for racial politics last semester, her first class at UVA, and she was already amazing.  Really passionate about the topic and her research.  There was a good mix of tests and papers, all graded very fairly.

Hands down, the best professor I have had at UVA. She is charismatic, energetic, and extremely intelligent. She goes out of her way to help you with papers and answer your questions. Just make sure you do the reading.
Tests are easy and homework is done in assigned projects. Lecture is confusing but tests are open note and much simpler than class. No previous coding required.
One of my favorite classes at UVA.
Excellent professor.  Homework, quizzes, and tests quite easy because the material is explained so well in class.  She also prints all her slides! bliss
She really knows what she is teaching.  Very helpful in office hours.  Wants her students to succeed.  By the end of the semester, you'll learn a lot!

She presents a tremendous amount of information in class, but it's all very well organized. She's taught the class many times, and it really shows. The class curriculum has obviously been revised many times and is quite well presented. I highly recommend the class to anyone serious about learning networking.

Very willing to help. Cares a lot about how she's doing as a teacher and how she can help you learn better. One of the best in the E-School. Her tests are a bit tough, though, but that's because she knows we're capable.

She was the most unhelpful professor that I have ever encountered.  She tries to cram too much information into each lecture and her tests are very hard and confusing.  I would advise very highly to avoid her and any class that she teaches.
Scribbles all over the board, in all directions until she fills it all up. Lazy with the tests, only mid+final with every point on each test worth a pt/100 on ur raw score b4 curving.
Blathers on endlessly. Uses powerpoint with confusing diagrams. This is a high-level course, it should be general. She takes relatively easy material and makes it difficult. Avoid like the plague.
Great professor. One of the best professors in the department. Her homeworks are very carefully designed to help learn the material. Also, her grade curve is generous.
Sux
Respectable professor.  She knows very well about what she is teaching, but her tests are somewhat very wierd.

I love this man with my entire heart. Easy class (he literally tells you not to study for his exams) with two exams and a paper. Take his classes. Please. Smushiest man ever and he's so obviously passionate about his work.

Vickerman lectures without a powerpoint, so you have to go to class to get notes! There are readings each week which are all interesting, but you don't have to do them to pass. The grade is based on a weekly one page (completion) memo, a 10 page research paper, and a final. Vickerman will make an outline for the paper with you!

Professor Vickerman's lectures were often off topic and didn't relate to the readings or the day's topic. I don't think this class was well designed and I didn't learn much about the "Sociology of Immigration." Personally, would not recommend.

The class was very interesting and was very relevant to modern day stuff; I felt like I really began to be able to converse in a more adult fashion by taking this class. There is one midterm, a 10 page paper, and a final. The midterm is fairly easy if you study the lectures and memorize some key points from the readings. The final was a bit harder.
The class is a little boring and repetitive but he is such a good professor. He's SO chill on assignments and papers. Doesn't mind if you turn things in late. He's so nice and easy to talk to.

One of my favorite professors in the sociology department. Lectures are thought-provoking and he encourages lots of discussion. A lot of reading, but mostly new books and recent news articles. One paper and a final exam. Take this class!
lectures are full of tangents, and he doesn't analyze what we've read for class, just regurgitates it.  Classes felt like a waste of time.
A really great lecturer.  His class was really fun and I learned a lot.  The tests can be difficult especially if you are not very good at essays, but he is very fair.

My favorite class at UVa! Vickerman kept me enthusiastic and interested.  I actually would want to go to class and listen. Classes are varied. Exams are easiest if readings have been done but being attentive in class is fine to pass the exam.

Great class! Interesting, papers have nothing to do with readings (which means you don't have to read them), final essentially has nothing to read them (again - no need to do them), and the lectures are interesting.  He's a pretty easy grader too, and a really nice guy, and lectures in a clear and concise way to make sure everyone gets it.

I had a great experience with Vickerman as both a teacher and advisor. He was helpful, interested, and extremely efficient. I would recommend his classes to anyone who wants to learn and is willing to do some work.
Vickerman is a great professor he really knows his stuff and what he says is interesting, he´s also an easy grader and you dont have to do all the reading to understand whats going on in class

As an advisor, Vickerman is terrible.  He seems annoyed at having to deal with students, loses paperwork, and doesn't respond to e-mails/calls in any timely manner (expect to wait weeks if not months).  Major source of frustration with UVa.
Not a good teacher, way to strict, not for anyone, mean.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: amazing teacher and such a babe

Paloma is a wonderful teacher! She's from Peru but very easy to understand and very patient with her students. There's a decent bit of homework but there is in any foreign language class. She's not a really hard grader, she's very fair. She's also extremely helpful during office hours. One of my favorite teachers I've ever had.

She is a fairly good teacher. Very good in office hours (she will personally give you handouts and study aids that are not given in class) and encourages participation. Returns graded work promptly and there are always ways to make up a bad quiz. Online homework is a annoying, but extremely critical for doing well in the class (especially the final

Professor Kaiser, although a very nice person, did not provide a syllabus until a month into the course and then did not even remotely adhere to the syllabus. We only had two graded assignments: one paper and the final. He also liked to hear himself talk and spent every class talking without caring if anyone understood the concepts.
Nice guy, but what you should try to avoid: to trust him!
He's a nice man. He cares about his students. At times he gets a little carried away and talks too much. He's really easy going. I would recommend him

I love this class and Voker Kaiser; quite frankly, the reason people dislike it is because the material is over their head.  Take this class if you are intelligent (almost extremely so); if not, then yes, you will be bored and confused.  I think this class is wonderful; it is my favorite this semester.
honestly, this was the worst class ever and i changed my concentration after taking it.
EXTREMELY BORING. Nice person, but a terrible professor. I advise: do not take his class.

As stated below, he talks more than he should, and does not answer questions. Don't take the class unless you have to, because the subject matter is pretty intimidating. He is a very nice man, and welcomes visits during office hours, even if you dont want to see him. I didnt think Id do well in the class, but he's an easy grader. Class is confusing
He KNOWS he talks too much, but he doesn't seem to care. He doesn't properly respond to questions, and he almost always holds the class late.
This man loves his own voice and will blatanly ignore your attempts to speak out.
he was a good prof.
No Comments

Professor Wang is a clear lecturer who condenses dense material into concise notes. He keeps class engaging and encourages questions. Though he has an accent, his English is excellent and he clearly knows his stuff. MATH 3351 is tough and test-heavy, but with effort, you'll gain a strong grasp of linear algebra. Prof Wang is just a nice guy too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor gives tests on memorization not on actual math, and he is very hard to understand.

I think he is a very effective teacher overall. His notes are very clear - even if you didn't get everything he taught in class, you can learn by yourself simply by reading his notes. But I still strongly recommend you to go to his class although he has a little bit strong accent. Also, his homework and exams are quite fair.
An alright professor, covers all the material and is clear enough to understand. Tests and homework were fair.
Clear lectures, fair tests and homeworks, great class to take.
An effective teacher. Quite clear. Very well organized.
awful awful awful dont do it, he's not good at explaining things and doesnt understand why no one else gets it

Homework requirements for this class not bad, but don't leave it all until the last minute!  He's willing to help you find solutions to problems (many, many hints) but he won't give you the answer and you do have to ask him.

Goes too fast in class.  Gives unreasonable amounts of homework, and has no clue about either how difficult the homework is or how uncomprehensible his lectures are.  He should have his tenure recinded.

Professor Wattenmaker was a good professor but had an extremely dry teaching style. She really does care about everyone and wants people to pass. Only graded by 2 exams, final paper, and participation and attendance at discussion section. Not an easy A, but it's definitely easy to pass.

Professor Wattenmaker is very knowledgeable in what she teaches and is excited to answer questions. She is very helpful during office hours and is a fair teacher-always asking the class to vote on things (such as changes in exam dates).  Definately take good notes during class because exams are free response and short answer (very fair).

Wattenmaker is a great professor.  She might show up late to class a few times but she more than makes up for it with her interest in her students.  She will do anything to help her students and is so clearly interested in and good at what she does!
Interesting topic but she was a bit disorganized. She really does love what she teaches, though which made it a worthwhile class.

Incredibly approachable. Maybe a bit disorganized, but if you are truly interested in her classes, this does not matter. She will not baby you, she will give you plenty of room to flourish on your own. If you show her you are interested she will love you. Pretty easy A if you put in some effort. Incredibly excited by enthusiastic students.
Loved hearing about fieldwork and the images.  Very helpful.

This class should not have been as much of a hassle as it was. Lectures are not organized at all.  She is very knowledgable but her lack of organization and zeal during lectures makes them a real bore. Yet you still need to go to the lectures to know what will be on the exams.

Perhaps a nice lady, but a horrific teacher. Lectures would span for days without any comprehensible point or theme. Her rants made little sense and were always coupled with late grading and irregular, unfair grading practices. This is one of the worst classes I have ever taken during my entire scholastic career. Avoid like plague!

Awful.  Late to class, utter disorganization! It was VERY frustrating to have her as a professor.  We didn't get the study guide for our Tuesday exam until Sunday at 11pm!  Her lectures have no rhyme or reason.  Steer Clear at all cost!

She is a complete and utter airhead.  Totally not with it, and her lectures are amazingly disconnected and tangental.  The reading is boring, but nothing really important there, and it's not hard to do well... just hard to put up with her!  Avoid her classes.
She's very knowledgable about the subject matter as she is an archeologist herself, but classes are sometimes unorganized and she is often late and/or misses class - its interesting though

I would steer clear.  Very boring class, tests are difficult only because the lectures are no good and therefore do not suppliment the insufferably boring readings.  She is very nice and prob. very smart, just not the best teacher.  Do yourself a favor and take a different class.
Great prof. Usually about 5 minutes late to class. Interesting lectures, and good reading choices. Exams were not too hard.
The course is pretty easy and fulfills the history requirement. But you don't get to anything past settlement patterns and she doesn't seem to have a really good command of the subject.
Very knowledgeable, but lectures get boring fast.  Always runs late to class and leaves early, often just shows movies or slides during class.

Lectures are well put together, and she seems nice.  Her exams are pretty straightforward, and she knows a whole lot about the subject matter.  She doesn't have the best speaking manners; she says "um" a WHOLE lot during lecture.
Late to class sometimes.  Great lecturer, very clear and captivating. Highly recommend.
clear and helpful.  a really nice lady.  sometimes lets discussion get off material.  often runs a little late to class.

I really enjoyed this class, and Professor De Wekker clearly cared a lot about the material. The lectures were clear and the tests mostly followed the slides, but make sure you read the textbook too. I'd happily take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most boring classes I've ever taken in college.  De Wekker is inept and will put you to sleep.  He definitely enjoys the class, but it's no way to learn the (any) material.  By the end of the year I couldn't even go to lectures I was so bored.  I learned everything I know about the material through the book.  I feel  a bit cheated.

Really wants you to understand the material. He's enthusiastic about what he teaches and is very nice. Took mountain meteorology-- interesting class, readings were all from journal articles or modules online, not too much work overall except a paper at the end.
No Comments

If you have any interest in learning more about autism, take this class. Jaswal is a super knowledgeable about the topic and leads some really interesting discussions. Reading is mandatory, but as long as you keep up with it, you'll be fine for the midterm and final.
Great man! Very engaging in lecture and made me want to pursue Psychology as one of my majors.
Really interesting lectures, goes at a steady pace and very approachable. Definitely recommend. Take detailed notes and do all readings to do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Jaswal is amazing. He really tries to make his lectures engaging and understandable and often reiterates that he is available during his office hours for any questions or just to chat. He also offers an optional weekly review session. I would highly suggest doing the reading if you want to do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was enjoyable because of his passion and personal experience with the topics he teaches. Appears nice and approachable, though I only briefly spoke with him for clarification during tests. The essay/interactive assignment that counts for 10% of your grade is enjoyable, make sure you put effort into that essay. Tests harder than expected

Vikram is the nicest professor you can get. There's a ton of reading, but this is a 4000 level seminar, so be prepared. Assignments and questions on the readings are on a weekly basis. One group long project and one essay on a book: it's pretty manageable. Go to class because the discussions MAKE the class. Would take it again in a heartbeat.
Great guy and gives great lectures, but the test are evil. And I mean evil. Make sure to read the book.
the tests are really hard! and the subject matter is not THAT interesting, he's an amazing guy tho! take it but be warned thats there's a LOT of work to get a good grade

Extremely clear professor who is a great lecturer. All exams are multiple choice and are pretty fair if you pay attention in class and read the textbook. You can drop 1 exam out of the 4. Pay attention in  the lecture and make notes b/c he only provides an outline for the day. Very nice and approachable
Genuinely interested in teaching and helping. Corrects inconsistencies in books, offers funny and insightful examples, great disposition.
Very personable and great lecturer. Lectures were interesting as well as interactive, so you didn't feel as though it was a 300-person class. Highly recommended!

Fun, low-key class. Jaswal is a really sweet, approachable guy who knows what he's talking about. Gives a lot of demos that make up for sometimes dry lectures. Tests aren't bad at all and he puts slides online. Take this with Jaswal, he's just a really likable guy teaching a really interesting class.

This class was pretty awesome. You take 3 exams.  Your lowest one is dropped. The Final was SO EASY. Knowing the book is helpful in his class. He covers material very well.  He's a great guy and really cares.  He's emailed students about how to improve their grades-- or simply to compliment them on their improvement.  Great guy and great class! :)

Although the book is very dry, Jaswal explains the important stuff well and gives meaning to the text. Lectures are entertaining. Very approachable. 3 exams with a cumulative final (all multiple choice). Lowest of first 3 exam grades is dropped. Would highly recommend!

He's really nice, genuine and always willing to help. Tries to make the course as interesting as possible and has his own endearing sense of humor. The class is really interesting and wide-ranging; exams test a lot of applications so you have to understand the material. I'd definitely recommend taking the course with him!
Great! He's very approachable and knows what he's talking about! Tests are a mix of reading the book and paying attention in class! I still talk to him now!

Not a bad class at all, and Jaswal was pretty awesome. He definitely had his boring days but I think a lot of that is just the fact that Cognition is not my thing, but overall he is good. Make sure you read the book, or at least skim it, and understand things well enough for an application process since thats mainly what his tests are. Great guy!!

A complete sweetie! He has a genuine interest in his students and tries to teach everything clearly except for when he seems rushed. The book is incredibly boring and the tests are based mostly on the applications of the experiments explained in lecture. He loves to talk about his cat and his niece.

This class is pretty tricky - he likes to test applications, not just memorization. Lectures are interesting and he includes lots of demos and relevant videos. He is an extremely nice guy w/ a genuine interest in all of his students.
He has a very soothing voice.

Lovable guy who really cares about his hundreds of students.  Just quickly read the text; his tests are based on his notes, which are all on Powerpoint on Toolkit.  Interesting topic, but sometimes got boring.  He tries to engage the class in his lectures by interactive activities.  Overall a good class.

Made me major in psychology. Hard but extremely interesting material, and Jaswal is an articulate and appealing kind of guy whose class is well organized. Very good class. If he happens to teach it, I'd say take it from him or Willingham.
No Comments

Extremely nice, energetic, loves students, very prompt with emails. Likes to mention his cat a lot in his lectures. Tests emphasize the notes more than the book (warning: the book will put you to sleep). Interesting lectures, though he lacks the comedic touch of other psyc professors, but he sure does try.

I enjoyed this class, and most lectures were pretty interesting.  Vikram used a lot of videos and funny examples.  Sometimes he would drag out an easy point and fly through more complicated ones but he was very helpful and always open to suggestions. This is a great class for people interested psychology.
I heart Vikram Jaswal!  He makes learning fun and pretty!

One of my least favorite classes this semseter. I heard that UVA had a great PSYC department and this class did not confirm that for me.  I did not enjoy the class. I recomend taking cognition with Willingham (the author of the textbook).  I hear he is much better.
If you attend lectures with any class he teaches, you will do well. The tests are more based on his specific notes, not the book.
Very good.
No Comments
Great class!
I was worried by how young he is, but he's quite good and has entertaining lectures.
The book is very boring and the lectures aren't much better, but the subject material is interesting and the professor is straightforward and a very nice guy.
Boring lectures; skimming the book and reading the PowerPoints will get you a B on the tests.
very poor teacher in comparison to other psyc teachers.

The book is boring but the lectures aren't and it is very important that you do pay attention to his lectures. You can't simply just d/l the powerpoints. He drops one of the three tests. I failed the first one because I didn't paying attention in class but then I aced the next 2 tests and the final
Very coherent, very organized, very eve-paced.  Exams are not easy, but not too difficult either.  Textbook does getting some used to, and I loved the videoclips!
Very good at putting students to sleep.
Always tries to liven up the lectures with film clips, music, and pop culture references.  Energetic lecturer and easy to understand.

Very interesting and straightforward lecturer. Also, he integrates movies or other multimedia into the lectures for variety. The book is horrible, but it's necessary to read it; plus, must go to all the lectures. Great teacher who actually teaches!
great lecturer and very prepared (his powerpoints are very helpful). Textbook is dry, and the tests aren't easy but it's worth it.
an interesting class and a nice guy. as long as you read the textbook and pay attention during the lectures (coz the lectures do help) youll ace the class
the textbook is sheer boredom, but the lectures are slightly more interesting.

Professor Webb has no idea what it means to teach an introductory finance course. The fact that the average was a 70 on the first exam is indicative of just that. The tests are not a measure of how well you know the information, but rather how well you can integrate "there ain't magic in finance" into your essay responses.
Pretty smart professor, the best ever!

He knows and has done everything. Read and study his slides - especially his daily news updates. Great suits. Takes a while to get used to him but my favorite ICE teacher by the end of the first semester

This is class is excellent for those who want to learn about trading and those who've already got their heads into it. Lots of guest speakers, great readings (Market Wizards, NMW and Webb's book) and general news analysis. The class is less structured than the average investments or corp finance class, but you definitely learn tons.

Webb is a really great guy, but he's too smart to be teaching introductory Finance.  I am not a finance person, and everything he said the entire year was way above my head.  He never really goes through the basics-just starts out assuming you know a lot about finance.  If finance isn't your thing, be prepared to be very confused.  tests aren't bad
I love this class and this prof.

interesting class..webb really knows his stuff as he actually worked for many years as a floor trader, gets great guest speakers to come in including paul tudor jones and jerry parker..class has little to no structure and grade is based highly on how much webb likes you..hardly any work tho and def recommended

Fast-paced, difficult course where participation is mandatory for success. Prof. Mattson does an excellent job ensuring students understand general chemistry at a high level. He is a tough grader but is willing to work with students to reach their individual goals and reflects your effort in your final grade. Very devoted professor!
Unclear lectures and too focused on his own methodology
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mattson is one of the most dedicated teachers I have ever had.  If you are willing to put in the effort to learn, he is willing to go above and beyond to teach you.
no comment.
Very good, yet stubborn teacher. Only accepts things done his way.

Prof. Marshall is now teaching at Temple U, and I am currently taking IH2 with her. I think Prof. Marshall is a nice professor and a kind woman, she just has very solid opinions and they do have a lot of influence on the way the class is run. Its not that I disagree with her standpoint, its just that she is very firm with it.

Prof. Marshall is at Temple University now. She was very empathetic towards students, especially during the coronavirus pandemic. She genuinely cares about people and it shows. She definitely has firm opinions and can come off as abrasive but its because she is passionate about social justice and likes to debate.
